incident_description:
While my child was using the bunk bed ladder to climb to the top bunk, the top section of the wooden ladder developed a large crack. The crack is deep and continues to expand, leaving a sharp edge and a gap in the wood. This makes the ladder unstable and unsafe. We stopped using the bed immediately due to the risk of serious injury.
What type of product was being used?
A wooden bunk bed with an attached ladder.
Who was using the product?
My child (a minor).
How was the product being used?
The ladder was being used in the normal way  for climbing up and down from the top bunk.
Were there any injuries that happened or may have happened while using the product?
No injuries have occurred yet, but there is a serious risk of both falls and cuts.
How did any injuries occur (or could have occurred)?
The ladder could break completely while a child is climbing, leading to a fall from height and possible broken bones, head trauma, or other serious injuries.
The sharp split in the wood could cut a childs skin when holding onto the ladder.
A childs toe or foot could get caught in the crack while climbing down, causing tripping and a fall.
justification: No injuries have occurred yet, but there is a serious risk of falls and cuts, making the likelihood of an incident high.

My first instinct was to get out of the chair which constricted that area further and pinched it even more, causing him to be stuck. He was yelping and crying like I have never heard.All three of us were trying to get his paw out. In pain and a panic, he bit my husband  several times on both hands.

incident_description:
I was staying at a [REDACTED], with my husband and two toddlers. The hotel has a (3) drawer dresser in place of a nightstand, which my toddlers started playing with at arrival. They pulled the top drawer fully out, and the dresser then fell onto both of them. We checked them for cuts, bruises, any dizziness or signs of injury, and made sure they were both alright. I called the front desk at about 7:10 pm MST to inform them of what happened, and ask that they mount the dresser as it's not secure and we're staying to two weeks. They told me that they'd file a work order and mount it for me in the morning. Nothing happened Monday or Tuesday, and I called Wednesday morning for an update. They didn't have a work order, had blamed me for the tip over, and refused to do anything. I was transferred to the GM around 9:30 am, who said the same, and that they most they would do is put weight in the bottom drawer. I said that's not enough and doesn't secure it, and he hung up on me. I called corporate shortly after, when my first representative again insisted that they couldn't help me, and that my children should be more careful. They're 1 and 2, and this is the third [REDACTED] person who blamed us for the tip over, when simply pulling the drawer fully out. They tried to hang up on me, but I was transferred to a supervisor who made a report. They then mounted it to the headboard, which is mounted on particle board cleats. I told them it wasn't enough, it needed to be mounted to a stud, and they left. They still haven't remedied it.

It was a (3) drawer plastic laminate finish dresser with particle board construction. I have images of the tags and labels I can share.
justification: The dresser fell on the toddlers but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) as the dresser was not secured and toddlers are prone to such accidents.

incident_description: I have been experiencing repeated issues with the typical Amazon China import product, a clip on book-light that is showing odd charging behavior for what is probably a Lipo (or similar chemistry) battery. I had a previous version dim over time and wouldn't hold a charge, until one day I noticed the case swelling, cracking open, and I dug into it to see what was happening and - woah! the Lithium-Polymer battery had swelled so much it was breaking the case open (I threw the battery out but I kept the actual lamp itself I kept it for possible junk parts use). I was shocked but just tossed the device, thinking I just happened to get a lemon. But now the newer (similar design) I bought more recently on Amazon is displaying similar weird behavior as regards the charging circuitry. It could be they are not properly charging but the issue isn't apparent at first? Anyway, I am abandoning the use of this newer one now. I think they become dangerous if a person really uses it daily. I used it with a [REDACTED] typewriter, it helps my 70-year-old eyes see the screen a little better. But now with these lights from China with strange battery charging behavior--yipes--you do NOT want a lithium fire in the home for sure. Thanks for your help.
justification: The incident describes a battery swelling and cracking the case, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to repeated issues with similar products.

incident_description:
On September 1, 2025, I was burning an Apotheke charcoal Votive candle. The candle was lit indoors on a flat, stable, non-flammable kitchen counter surface, away from other objects or debris, and was being used exactly as intended  for normal household fragrance and ambiance. The entire top surface of the candle ignitednot just the wick. The container split apart during the fire. When I moved it to the sink and poured water on it, a fireball erupted before the flames finally went out. Wax spread across my sink and into the garbage disposal, possibly causing damage.

This incident could have easily resulted in a house fire or injuries if I had not been present. I have photos of the aftermath and the remains of the candle.

I have also experienced abnormal performance with another Apotheke charcoal, petite candle (flame extinguishing after short burns), which I understand may relate to fragrance oil load or wick design. I am concerned this represents a wider safety issue with the brand.
justification: The incident involved a candle fire that could have caused injury or property damage but did not, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the description of similar issues with other candles from the same brand.

incident_description:
I purchases a Casper DRESM MATTRESS IN EARLY July 2025.  The smell from off gassing causes bad headaches.
I tried every way possible to ventilate the room, fans, AC, open windows, standing the mattress on end, etc.
I reported to the company on August 8, 2025 that there was so much off gassing that the room was unusable and they agreed to take it back.

I really wanted to make it work as it looks beautiful, is comfortable from a cushiony point of view and was a descent price so i kept it in a spare bedroom for another month with ventilation.
Everytime i go into the room, the chemical smell is extreme.  I have never had a problem with any product like that as I do not have chemical sensitivities.
I am returning the mattress but think this should be reported.
The mattress label states Date of Manufacture: 06/24/2025
Model #: 880-000074
Prototype ID: CS DREAM CARP V7
justification: The off-gassing caused headaches, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue persisted despite ventilation efforts, suggesting a likely occurrence (4).

incident_description: I was electrically shocked by 277 volts AC while removing a LED U-Tube lamps from the light fixture. The potential for injury and or death is very great. The LED lamps have a metal plate on the top of the U-Tube lamp, maybe for strength, reflectivity or heat protection, The exact purpose is not listed anywhere. While removing the un-lit lamp from the 2x2 recessed light fixture I had to get the lamp out of the holder on the end opposite to the socket/lampholders. My left hand was prying the lamp from the holder with my thumb on the fixture and upon placing my finger onto the metal lamp piece I received 277Volts through my hand between the thumb and finger. Yes I was on a step ladder while doing this . My hand immediately pulled back and had I not been properly situated on the ladder I could have fallen to the ground . I am a New Jersey Licensed Electrician. The product was a RemPhos Technologies Model Number RPT-B-Total Tube-T8-G3-2FTU6-850-A, color 5000K, 15W
justification: The incident involved an electric shock with potential for severe injury or death, but the description indicates no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Incident Description
At approximately 4:00 a.m., we were awoken by the sudden sound of glass breaking. Upon inspection, we discovered that the glass top of our West Elm Jensen Desk (56") had completely shattered across the room. The glass continued to emit popping and fizzing sounds when we entered. There was no impact to the desk or surrounding area, leading us to conclude that the glass top spontaneously shattered. The desk was not in use at the time of the incident. As a result, my husband sustained several minor lacerations on his hands and feet while attempting to clear the broken glass.

Product Information
Product Name: West Elm Jensen Desk (56")
Product Type: Glass-top desk
Retailer: West Elm
Purchase Date: 1/10/22
Approximate Price: $700
Location of Use: home office

incident_description:
On June 11, 2025, my 13-month-old daughter was injured when the melafa365 Bed Rails for Toddlers, 78", Gray, failed to perform as advertised. The product was purchased from Amazon and installed on both sides of a full-size bed exactly as instructed in the manufacturers manual.

The rails were fully extended and positioned flush with the mattress edges, vertical anchor arms were inserted between the mattress and box spring, T-shaped support feet were placed under the mattress, and straps were tightened around the opposite side of the bed. All components were checked for stability before allowing my child to sleep alone.

Despite correct installation, the rail failed to prevent her from falling headfirst off the bed onto a hardwood floor. As a result, she sustained a large hematoma on her forehead, bruising under her right nostril, additional bruises on her arm and leg, and a nosebleed. She was taken to the emergency room for evaluation and monitoring due to concern for concussion.

This product is marketed to prevent toddlers from falling out of bed, yet it failed catastrophically under normal, intended use, causing physical harm to a child.
justification: The child sustained multiple injuries requiring emergency room evaluation, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident occurred despite correct installation, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
On December 26, 2024, I purchased two nightstands through Target.com. After setting them up in my bedroom, I noticed a persistent and unusual chemical odor coming from the furniture. The smell did not dissipate over time, which raised concerns for me, especially because I am currently 36 weeks pregnant and have been exposed to this environment throughout the course of my pregnancy.

To verify the source of the smell, I used an at-home formaldehyde test kit purchased from [REDACTED]. The test, which I conducted on July 6, 2025, indicated a formaldehyde concentration of 0.7 mg/m, a level significantly above the safety thresholds set by regulatory agencies. I am deeply alarmed by this finding, as exposure to elevated levels of formaldehyde can pose serious health risks, particularly to pregnant women and developing fetuses.

The nightstands are located next to my bed and have been used daily as part of my regular living environment. Although I have not yet experienced specific physical symptoms directly attributed to the exposure, I am very concerned about the long-term impact on my health and especially the potential risks to my unborn child. This situation has caused emotional distress and anxiety due to the involuntary exposure to a potentially harmful chemical during a vulnerable time.

Given that formaldehyde emissions at this level may be illegal and hazardous, I believe this product violates indoor air safety standards and should be investigated. I am submitting this report in the interest of public safety and consumer protection.
justification: The incident involves exposure to elevated formaldehyde levels, posing potential health risks, especially to a pregnant woman and her unborn child, but no specific physical symptoms have been reported yet.

incident_description:
Product: Purple brand mattress (model purchased new in July 2023).
Issue: The mattress repeatedly loses support, develops deep indentations, and causes chronic paindespite four replacements in two years.

Details:
Failure Pattern:

Each mattress sagged significantly within months (verified with photos/videos per Purples warranty requirements).

Four separate mattresses (original + three replacements) failed the same way.

Purples customer support acknowledged the indentations but only offered replacements, not refunds.

Safety/Health Impact:

Injuries: Chronic back and neck pain requiring medical attention.

Cause: Mattress lost structural integrity, failing to provide support during sleep.

Near-Misses: Risk of falls due to uneven sleeping surface (deep sagging).

Evidence of Systemic Defect:

[REDACTED] complaints show identical issues (mattresses failing within a year).

Purple presumed sagging was the issue before I reported it (indicating prior knowledge).

How Product Was Used:

Normal use as a primary sleep surface (adults, standard weight range).

Followed all care instructions (proper foundation, no misuse).

Why Reporting:

Purple continues selling mattresses with a known defect that causes injuries.

Warranty process fails to resolve the hazard (replacements have the same flaw).
justification: The incident describes chronic back and neck pain requiring medical attention, indicating injury (severity 3). The repeated failures across multiple mattresses suggest the issue is likely to recur (likelihood 4).

The incident is identical to the problem stated in CPSC Recall #18-724, dated 2/13/2018.
 
 
The product was made in Vietnam.
 
The consumer is extremely concerned that the same exact problem occurred with her table, 3 years after a recall, by this manufacturer.
 
I have emailed and called West Elm. I also submitted a 'claim' (not sure what this actually means) to [REDACTED].
I have not yet heard anything back. 
Note: This product had a safety recall in 2018. This desk was sold to me in 2021 after incidents of this spontaneous shattering glass. Feels irresponsible and so dangerous. The CPSC has this very desk listed on the website.
justification: The consumer sustained cuts to her legs, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident is identical to a recalled problem, indicating a likely recurrence (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description: This is to report the West Elm Jensen Desk (West Elm Jensen rectangular glass table). I own this desk, and its glass top spontaneously shattered around 7pm PST on Sunday, July 13, 2025 at my home. No one was in the room (thankfully) at the time and no other items hit or fell onto the desk. It just spontaneously shattered for no apparent reason with glass exploding all over the room and the few items on top of the desk (1 desk lamp, 1 computer monitor, 2 computer speakers, a keyboard, mouse, small plant and drink coaster) collapsing onto the floor. Fortunately, while my husband, dog and I were home, we were not in the room where the desk is located in our house  it could have been extremely dangerous and injurious should we have been using the desk at the time, which we often do. We were very lucky! Upon research, I found that this West Elm Jensen desk has had a CPSC safety recall in the past (#18-724), but the timeframe for the recall states "from September 2014 through December 2016", BUT I purchased my desk from WestElm.com in September 2020. When I called the Safety Recall number, I was transferred to their regular customer service team and they had no knowledge of the recall and kept insisting they could not help me because I purchased the desk more than 1 year ago. Once I pressed the team more, informing them of the recall and providing them photos of my shattered desk, the representative told me that their supervisor finally admitted they had seen at least 3 other instances of this glass shattering happening to other customers recently and that "West Elm should state on their website that this desk should not be placed next to a window". Based on my experience, and what their customer service team said, the safety recall should really extend past the 2016 date stated as this desk if VERY dangerous. Especially considering that the recall remedy is a glass replacement but all of this indicates that the glass problem has not been fixed and those glass tops issued after 2016 still spontaneously shatter. Additionally, in my conversation with the West Elm team, it took 30 minutes of disputing to get them to rectify the situation, with an initial offer of replacing the glass, but I wasn't willing to risk receiving another defective glass top that could also spontaneously shatter again (and potentially next time hurt someone in my home). The representative told me that the only way to know if the glass was fixed (and would not shatter again) was to find out for myself once I had the new glass top, so essentially, she was saying I should risk seeing if it might shatter again. The whole experience was excruciatingly disappointing. In the end after an hour phone call and lots of insisting, West Elm provided me with a merchandise credit for the desk. So they provided a solution (not one I'm 100% happy with), but it took a lot of time and effort, and yet they never seemed to take the glass shattering issue as a bigger problem and that concerns me especially since the Jensen desk is still being sold on their site, their customer service team is automatically reverting to sending a glass replacement while admitting that the shattering problem has been an issue among customers. This is a very dangerous practice and I'm shocked a big company like West Elm is functioning this way.
justification: The glass shattered spontaneously but no one was injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported instances and the desk still being sold.

incident_description:
I purchased and assembled a Secretlab Magnus Pro 1.5m Motorized Desk. After following all instructions and completing the setup with assistance, I plugged the desk into a standard wall outlet for the first time. Upon touching the metal portion of the desk frame, I was immediately electrocuted  the shock was violent enough to cause my hand to recoil forcefully and trip the circuit breaker, cutting power to the entire house.

No external devices were connected to the desk at the time. The desk was freshly assembled, unused, and had just been powered on. There was a clear electrical fault in the internal wiring or grounding of the desk. After the incident, the desk emitted a strong chemical or burnt odor, indicating internal damage.

I suffered a physical reaction to the shock and was taken to the emergency room, where I was evaluated and monitored for electrical injuries. The incident resulted in muscle soreness and back strain from the involuntary recoil movement, and I was advised to remain under observation. Medical expenses are ongoing. I am now unable to safely disassemble or handle the desk without assistance due to continued pain and concern over further injury.

This appears to be a serious electrical safety failure of a motorized consumer desk, with the potential for severe injury or worse.
justification: The incident resulted in injury requiring emergency room evaluation and ongoing medical expenses, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific and unusual nature of the electrical fault.

incident_description:
FAILURE ANALYSIS REPORT
SITUATION		
On 05/17/2025 at approximately 0720 hours I, Fire Investigator [REDACTED], was requested by DFM [REDACTED] to contact the necessary personnel at the [REDACTED] Mall to investigate a report of multiple lighting failure events.  The purpose of the subsequent investigation was to conduct a failure analysis of the involved lights to determine if any further actions should be taken to ensure the safety of the Mall and its occupants.    

The location of this investigation took place at [REDACTED], in Colorado Springs. 

INCIDENT INFORMATION 
Multiple events are associated with this lighting issue:
[REDACTED] (12/16/2024)
[REDACTED] (2/07/2025)
[REDACTED] (5/15/2025)

POINTS OF CONTACT
[REDACTED]  Fire Investigator, Colorado Springs Fire Department, [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]  General Manager, [REDACTED] Mall, [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]  Maintenance Supervisor, [REDACTED] Mall, [REDACTED]
[REDACTED]  [REDACTED], [REDACTED] 

BACKGROUND
I contacted [REDACTED], who is the general manager of the [REDACTED] Mall.  I met with [REDACTED] and his maintenance supervisor, [REDACTED], to gain context of the events, timeline and equipment involved.  This meeting took place at approximately 0900-1000 hours on location, at the [REDACTED] Mall.

According to both individuals, lighting within the mall common areas was updated starting in 2017, with installation of the new LED lights being completed in 2018.  They stated that in total, they had 57 lights that eventually stopped working, so [REDACTED] contacted [REDACTED] to send out new lights to replace the first batch.  The installation of the second batch started in December of 2024.  After three light failures, two of which resulted in a CSFD response due to smoke/fire production, they were told by [REDACTED] to disconnect all the second batch of lights, and that they would send out a third batch.  [REDACTED] instructions were to connect four of the third batch of lights within a safe area for 30 days to ensure there were no issues with the lights.  Both [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] stated that they had no issues with the third batch of lights, only the second.  [REDACTED] stated that after this mornings CSFD response to a smoking light, he realized that it was one of the lights from the second batch, that he had failed to disconnect.  They both confirmed that no more of the second batch of lights are energized within the mall.  

Both confirmed that while the lights had been swapped out by maintenance personnel, they had a certified electrician confirm that the supply voltage was correct, 120v.  They stated that the power supplied to all four of the failed lights was from three different electrical distribution panels.  [REDACTED] further clarified that two of the electrical distribution panels are supplied by the same transformer, and the third electrical distribution panel was supplied by a second transformer.  They both confirmed that there have been no other electrical issues with any other electrified devices connected to those three electrical distribution panels. 

[REDACTED] provided a second batch undamaged exemplar light, as well as two damaged during failure events.  The lights were photographed and compared to determine potential commonalities in failure.

DEVICES 
Exemplar 
	Brand: Truly Green Solutions
	Model: 881215-RW-TM-CC-90CRI
	Power: 100-277Vac, 60Hz, 15W, 0.14A, WW/NW/CW
	Country of Manufacture: China
	Certification: Intertek ETL Listed
Damaged Light #1
	Brand: Truly Green Solutions
	Model: 881215-RW-TM-CC-90CRI
	Power: 100-277Vac, 60Hz, 15W, 0.14A, WW/NW/CW
	Country of Manufacture: China
	Certification: Intertek ETL Listed
Damaged Light #2
	Brand: Truly Green Solutions
	Model: 881215-RW-TM-CC-90CRI
	Power: 100-277Vac, 60Hz, 15W, 0.14A, WW/NW/CW
	Country of Manufacture: China
	Certification: Intertek ETL Listed

EXAMINATION

All lights are circular, white in color, with a toggle switch on the rear to control the light color emitted from the LEDs.  All three have two wires leading from the main circuit board, out of the light, to be connected to the power supply.  The lights bases are connected to their covers with eight small screws.

The exemplar light base was removed from the cover, with the interior components photographed and utilized as a comparison against the two damaged lights.  Upon examination, the exemplar displayed heat damage to the base of the light upon which it was mounted.  The heat damage displayed was discoloration of the white base as well as multiple electrical components on the main circuit board.

Both damaged lights displayed melting and charring of the plastic bases as well as their covers.  In addition, heat damage was present on the main circuit board of each, as seen while viewing the bottom of the base.  The area of origin for both were approximately 3.5-4 inches from the toggle switch controlling the light color.  This location correlates with the heat damage noted on the exemplar light.  

RECALLS
 
No recalls were located, either past or present, for the appliance involved.

ANALYSIS/RECOMMENDATIONS

The general location of similar fire effects of both the fire damaged lights, as well as the heat effects located on the exemplar, indicate the failure across all three of the lights viewed was consistent with a main circuit board failure.  The exemplar light heat effects indicate a gradual heating event, not a momentary event.  Considering all three lights were of the same model and type, I recommend a recall investigation be conducted by the appropriate agency.  The Mall staff has confirmed that all lights of this model have been removed.  

The opinions expressed in this report are based upon data collected during the investigation process.  I am confident of my conclusions within a reasonable degree of professional certainty.  Any additional evidence or information which may come forth after the preparation of this report may be subject to further review and analysis and may yield modified or additional opinions, conclusions and/or determinations. 

This report will be submitted to the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
justification: The incident involved multiple lighting failures with smoke/fire production, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The Kohler 99007-TLC-MA lighted bathroom medicine cabinet had LED lighting embedded in the door's mirror surface. The lighting is powered by a power cord, which runs from a box inside the mirror (under one of the shelves) to the back corner of the door.  The power cord attaches to the back of the door with an IP68 4-conductor plug.  There are at least two potential failure points in this design: first, the cord flexes at the point where it exits the connector when the door is opened or closed.  Repeated flexing causes at least one of the wires in the cord to break, resulting in flickering and/or loss of power to one side of the mirror. This has the potential to spark internally, eventually wearing through the insulation. At that point, it is a fire and electrocution hazard.  Second, there is no strain relief or chagge guard where the cord exits the box inside the mirror.  As the door opens and closes, the cord moves in and out through the hole in the box.  This has the potential to break the insulation, again resulting in possible fire and electrocution hazard. We've had a wire break on both of the cabinets we have installed. The first occurred soon after installation, the second recently.
justification: The incident describes potential fire and electrocution hazards due to wire breakage, which could lead to injury. The issue has occurred in both installed cabinets, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to file a formal complaint regarding a dangerously defective MAXIM Lighting pendant fixture (Model 39655SHBZ) that I purchased, which posed a significant safety risk. I urge the CPSC to investigate this matter to ensure the safety of other American consumers.

Product Information:
	Product: MAXIM Lighting Pendant Fixture
	Apparent Model: 39655SHBZ
	Weight: 35 lbs 
	Manufacturer: MAXIM Lighting, [REDACTED], Carson, CA 90810 
	Retailer: Lyteworks, [REDACTED], Bradenton, Florida 34208 Purchase Dates (Two Payments): 
o	January 10, 2025 - $2,118.54
o	January 30, 2025 - $2,118.54
	Delivery Date: February 2025 (it took a number of weeks for delivery and electrical box preparation prior to a March 4th installation). 
	Installation Date: March 4, 2025 
	Date Defect Discovered: March 4, 2025 

Description of Defect and Dangerous Situation:

On March 4, 2025, I had two licensed electricians install two MAXIM pendant fixtures. Within an hour of their departure, a suspension cable on one of the 35lb fixtures began slipping . Upon inspection, I determined that one of the "griplocks"the spring-loaded bearing mechanism designed to securely hold the suspension cablewas defective and failing to grip the cable.

This critical failure caused one side of the heavy light fixture to be supported solely by the electrical power wire. This created an immediate and doubly dangerous situation:

1.	The 35lb fixture was precariously suspended approximately 8 feet in the air, at imminent risk of falling, which could cause serious physical injury or significant property damage.

2.	If the fixture were to fall, it would rip out the electrical connection, thereby creating a severe electrical shock or fire hazard.

The local store representative from Lyteworks advised me that the light was dangerous and should be removed. However, I am 69 years old and was physically unable to remove the heavy and awkwardly positioned fixture by myself. 

Compounding this, our area was (and to some extent, still is) in disaster recovery from two named hurricane strikes (Helene, Sep 26, 2024, and Milton, Oct 10, 2024). Consequently, licensed electrical contractors were in extremely high demand and difficult to re-hire on short notice in early 2025.

Faced with a persistently dangerous situation and unable to secure immediate professional help, I was forced to implement a temporary stopgap measure. I cut a piece of wood to carefully prop up the sagging side of the light fixture, thereby taking the weight off the compromised electrical cord and the failing griplock to prevent it from falling.

Manufacturer and Retailer Response:

I immediately contacted the retailer, Lyteworks, on March 4, 2025, the day the defect was discovered. The Lyteworks representative, [REDACTED], was responsive and began trying to get MAXIM Lighting to ship a replacement griplocka minor but essential part for the fixture's safety.

Despite the clear and present danger communicated to MAXIM Lighting via Lyteworks, MAXIM essentially ignored these urgent requests for three weeks. 

Even though an expedited shipment was requested for this critical safety component, the inexpensive replacement part was eventually sent by regular mail from California. 

I finally received it, and the crew was able to rehang the light on March 25, 2025a full 21 days after my initial report of the dangerous defect.

Furthermore, during the reinstallation on March 25, 2025, the electricians discovered an additional defect within the same fixture: a white power wire inside was not securely crimped and had come out. They were able to repair this second manufacturing defect as well.

I have retained the original defective griplock part in a sealed bag as evidence, and have photos of the entire process.

Concerns and Request for Action:

I am deeply concerned that other MAXIM Lighting fixtures currently being imported and sold in the USA may contain similarly defective and dangerous griplock mechanisms or possess other hazardous wiring defects like the ones I experienced. 

The profound lack of urgency and disregard for consumer safety demonstrated by MAXIM Lighting in addressing such a serious hazard is also alarming.

I respectfully request that the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission:

1.	Thoroughly investigate this specific case and the multiple defects found in my MAXIM Lighting fixture.

2.	Examine whether these defects (faulty griplocks, insecure internal wiring) represent a more widespread manufacturing or quality control issue with MAXIM Lighting products, particularly their cable-suspended fixtures.

3.	Take all appropriate actions to protect other American consumers from potential injury or property damage due to these hazardous products.

Thank you for your time and diligent attention to this critical safety matter. 

I am prepared to provide copies of relevant email communications with Lyteworks, photographs of the defect and my temporary solution, and purchase receipts. Please let me know if you require any further information.
justification: The incident involved a defective lighting fixture that posed a risk of falling and causing injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
3.5 years ago, I purchased a couch by Modway. The specific couch is called the Aura outdoor sofa. This sofa was for my backyard in San Diego CA. I loved it so much that I purchased a matching sofa one year later in March and received it in April 2022. Within a single years time, the newer sofa started coming apart. First it started with the cushion covers, which had holes in them that I believe were a factory defect. Then, the wicker started cracking slowly. Now, less than 3 years later, it is completely destroyed and cant even be sat on. It literally crumbled when my child sat on it and she fell through the frame. She was not jumping or doing anything unreasonable - simply sitting. 

I live in California where the weather is temperate and doesnt get too cold or rainy, so I am very disappointed and honestly, mostly confused. I have treated both of my couches the same way: always covering them, rarely using them, keeping them clean As I mentioned, I have two of these couches - the one I bought in 2021 is still in great condition and looks like new. However, this newer one is a disaster. I believe that less than 3 years is an unreasonable amount of time for couchs  lifetime. It is no longer usable even after being consistently covered and barely used. The powder coating is also coming off of the framework as well. 

Since I purchased this couch from Amazon, I reached out to the seller from whom I purchased it from there. I did this in 2024. However, since the couch was past the 30 day Amazon policy, and given the severe defects, the seller suggested that I reach out to Modway since this appears to be a factory defect/warranty issue. Per the Amazon listing, the couch is fade, water, and UV resistant, however, this has not proven to be true with this particular couch. After consulting with an engineer, we believe that this couch fell apart because it was not coated properly in UV coating. Quite simply: we believe this to be a batch defect. Given these circumstances, and because of the lack of safety,  I reached out to Modway looking to replace this product. They basically told me that their return policy was over and that I was out of luck. As this is both a quality AND safety issue, I found this to be totally unacceptable, but they made it clear that they were unwilling to work with me. As such, I am reaching out for help. My family worries that others had a similar experience and we dont want more children or adults to get hurt. 

I am happy to send more photos of the couch, which has been disposed of since due to safety issues.
justification: The child fell through the frame but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

People have asked if the bolts came loose. No, in the attached photo you can see where the wood fractured. I think it's due to so many holes in the wood so close, in a not very thick board, and the fact that it's Manufactured Wood, so glued pieces of wood together. It seems like it came loose at the connection between two pieces that were glued together. 

Other people asked if we had overtightened it. Also unlikely, because there's no evidence of damage to the wood where the bolts were. I hand-tightened and am cautious not to overtighten.
justification: The bed collapsed but no one was injured, though there was potential for serious harm. The likelihood is possible given the structural weakness in the bed.

incident_description: Subject: Safety Concern  Exploding Glass Table Purchased from City Furniture I am writing about a serious safety incident involving a glass coffee table purchased from City Furniture approximately 30 months ago. The table is known as the Mia table and is currently shown on the City Furniture website. On Saturday night, April5, 2025 , while we were asleep, we were startled awake by what sounded like someone shooting out our windows. Upon entering the living room, we discovered that our Mias tempered glass top had spontaneously exploded. . There were no items on the table, and the room was undisturbedyet the glass had exploded with such force that shards and slivers traveled up to 20 feet in all directions. See. Pictures. The photos attached illustrate the extent of the damage. The glass did not merely crack or fallit exploded, leaving razor-sharp fragments and a layer of silicate dust that has settled over furniture and flooring. This dust is hazardous to touch and difficult to remove safely. Thankfully, it did not explode a few hours earlier when we were 3 feet away from it watching television. While no one was injured, the situation could have easily resulted in serious harm. The glass experts with whom we have consulted have told us that a microscopic impurity in the glass (from manufacturing) can expand slowly over time and eventually trigger a sudden shattersometimes months or years after installation. We see that you are still selling the Mia table but do not know if you are still sourcing it with tempered glass. If you are this table presents a significant safety risk to others. We are requesting that City Furniture take this matter seriously, investigate the manufacturing process, and take appropriate action. We are consulting with third parties concerning our next steps regarding our personal situation.
justification: The glass table exploded, causing significant damage but no injuries, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible (3) as it's a known but not common manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
On 03/10/2025, a curtain rod purchased from and manufacturer by West Elm, (parent company Williams-Sonoma, Inc.), fell from it's bracket, hitting my child as it fell down. The manufacturer defect of this product could lead to series safety issues or possibly death. 

Upon closer inspection, the metal bracket has a fundamental flaw with the construction, leading to premature failure. The metal fatigue over years causes the bracket to tear off under its own load. Upon inspection of 10 other curtain rods purchase from the same retailer around the same time, show there was evidence of this failure in each and every other rod. 

I have photos that describe the manufacturing defect of this product. In the attached photos you can see the base of the arm bracket that mounts to the rod holder starts to pull the metal and eventually the metal fails and the entire holder that is mounted to the metal base is broken off from the base. The photos show the manufacturing defect, that the base does not have adequate construction to support the rod, especially as the arm bracket that mounds to the wall is mounted about 4-5" out from the wall, increasing the leverage it as when curtains are hung from the bracket. The metal is not thick enough to support the rods, even with lightweight shear curtains and is poorly designed, as the reinforced thicker metal is only the same diameter as the screw that mounds it to the arm, which is why each and every one of these that fell has failed in the same exact manner. 

Additionally, I have reached out to West Elm support and they did not take the issue seriously as I reported it. Their obligation for consumer safety was not upheld.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child due to a manufacturing defect, and the defect was found in all inspected units, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
I am filing this complaint regarding a FlexiSpot Mobile Standing Desk with Wheels (Order #[REDACTED]), which I purchased through Amazon. The product was advertised as an ergonomic and supportive workstation but instead caused serious wrist injuries and aggravated my existing medical conditions due to its sharp edges and defective design.

What Made Me Want to Report?
I originally purchased the FlexiSpot Standing Desk to accommodate my disability and assist with my daily activities, including working on my nonprofit organization. However, shortly after using the product, I began experiencing severe wrist pain, inflammation, and discomfort. The sharp edges of the desk applied excessive pressure on my wrists, causing pain and possible nerve damage. I have a chronic medical condition (diabetes, magnesium deficiency, and a chest port for bi-weekly infusions), which makes proper ergonomic support crucial for my health.

After reaching out to FlexiSpot for a resolution, they initially offered to replace the product with the same defective design, which does not resolve the safety issue. When I requested a replacement that would accommodate my disability (such as a proper ergonomic chair or adjustable desk that would not cause further injury), FlexiSpot denied my request and refused to acknowledge the harm caused by their product.
justification: The incident describes severe wrist pain and possible nerve damage caused by the defective desk design, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Former L.A. RISE temporary employee at Downtown Women's Center for their MADE by DWC program (madebydwc.org). I have photos and is employee-wide. They "train" us to manufacture their products for their product line to support the program. Candles. Soaps. Bath Salts. (they also sell Coffee). I am aware that the soaps, bath salts, and coffee are FDA jurisdiction, but it's relevant because it might be potential product contamination. I have photos of both the facility and the manufacturing process as much as I could before I resigned.

All candles of all sizes and all scents as listed on the website are manufactured in a way that generates numerous large, deep into the candle cracks, and it happens in double digit times in each lot. It is not tracked. In fact, [REDACTED] all support this process as it has been occurring for years.Tthe production manager, is proud to have a 0 percent candle product rejection rate.  She "repairs" the candles, especially the deep cracks that go deep into the candle, sometimes over an inch deep spanning near the votive glass. She then instructs us to "smash the candle down until the top is flat." Not fill in the gaps, but mash the whole top of the candle down into the cracks, and I know that creates small gaps underneath where the was wasn't smashed into the narrow cracks. So we smash the candle down to "fix" it, then hide the errors with a heat gun to conceal the smashing and thus the gap. We are also instructed to take wicks that are not centered, and we're talking wicks that are adhered to the bottom over to the side if you look at the bottom of the candles, and we are then instructed to "center the wicks," which means, even if the candle wick is over an inch over from the center and completely off, we "center" them by "pulling the wicks through the wax column, mashing it, then heat gunning it to conceal the work. The candles are stored in unwashed racks that share multiple scents together and have been in the same racks for years. No "flammable" "fragile" or "combustibles" signs on any of the transport equipment, storage racks, or wax melters. That entire process is called "Q.C.ing" the candles, short for "quality control." After the mashing and heat gunning, we then stand at a station, with only gloves, no safety goggles or proper PPE because the gloves leach and leave the latex gloves scent on most things they touch. They are FDA approved gloves but they leach. We then are given a spray bottle of mislabeled isoropyl alcohol to then spray near the heat gun to clean the candle. So we spray the towel and then wipe down the votive with the alcohol-soaked towel. While we usually do the cleaning after the mashing and heat gunning, we spray the alcohol near the other unmasked candles during the process...imagine having cracked candles in front of you on a tray and you're spraying alcohol on another in your hand with the others inches away...However, if any part of the process was done incorrectly by participants, considering sobriety and sound mental health is not a requirement for the program, it is clear to me that that is a direct danger of alcohol being caught in the cracks, then mashed into the cracks and sealed off from evaporation, essentially created a type of candle bomb. I complained to them about the process and it was reiterated to me by [REDACTED] that that is the procedure they chose and when I complained, she instead "retrained" me and told me "this is how we do things." [REDACTED] supports [REDACTED] in those decisions, and as stated, has for years. In my time there, often, in 24 candle lots on each tray, often 1/3, or 1/2, sometimes the entire tray, has that cracking and caving issue, and the aforementioned solution is used every time. 

I take issue with the facility having FDA regulation, but has no FDA training, I was told they "have no inspectors," ([REDACTED] told me that they have no inspectors because they don't deal in food, made no mention of knowledge of CPSC jurisdiction over the products), and otherwise think they are exempt from all inspections, safety inspections and such. No OSHA training, no FDA training, no CPSC training for the product line. It's not mentioned, not anywhere, not once. So the candles are thus contaminated in various ways. They're stored uncovered within inches of a regularly used work restroom. They are not labeled correctly; the info is on the box, not the candle, and from what I know, the number of oz of the candle and its contents should be directly on the candle, but they have it directly on the box and not the candle. No Caution label on the outside of the box saying it is fragile and combustible contents. The contents are not shipped in a box that says "combustible" or "flammable." I don't know if they ship with a "fragile" label. The candles are all over the United States because they have been practicing interstate commerce for years. The candles are stored on the same racks as soaps without washing. Candle scents containers, often by the gallon, are stored in the racks themselves with the product. 

Particular incident occurred on 12/17. Photos included in documents. Construction was occurring within 3 feet of where I was working, construction above causing particulates, numerous ones, all over the floor, to fall down. [REDACTED], the Production Manager, did not say anything about it, and I just kept working as the subordinate. My concern is that if this temperature had broken the glass- it could have sent flames out into the couch etc. and the fire wouldn't have been contained.  Separately, I do work for the US Fire Administration- and so this is of particular concern of mine beyond the safety in my own home.

After I got up, I saw that the leg of the chair had cracked and it was only held together by what appears to be light glue (no screw or other reinforcement). We only had these dining chairs for a little over a year (purchased November 2023) and we do not use them everyday or stand on them, they are only used for their intended purpose. After this incident I had a lot of back pain and my elbow was very bruised and sore, I thought I might have had a fracture but did not (confirmed with a doctor), however this could have been much much worse which is why I want to report it. I also want to mention that this product on the IKEA website says it is tested at 243 pounds, but I am less than that. I hope this can help get this product off the market as I feel it is not safe.

incident_description: After purchasing a stegosaurus dinosaur shaped menorah from Target for son, we gifted it to him as a present and proceeded to celebrate the holiday. The menorah was made under Target's Spritz brand. Our menorah started to catch on fire as the channukah candles were burning low. Part of the head and back ended up singed. We used standard channukah candles that and followed the same standard procedures that we do for the menorah. I.e. lighting on the counter away from other items aside from the tray it sits on. The candles have been used throughout the holiday each time and have never been a problem for any other menorah. This menorah was not created to be fireproof, a dangerous reality for an item that is intended to hold anywhere from 2-9 candles each night for a week.

incident_description: The fire alarm went off due to smoke and a burning plastic smell. The fire department searched all over and couldn't find the cause. Their best guess was it was something with the furnace. After some searching, they later figured out that it was the UV light (UV100A 1059) that was installed in our furnace duct. It appears the bulb was fried, and it was still getting sent electricity. That was doing something that was causing the plastic housing unit to burn and melt, sending a thin, steady stream of smoke up. They believe if they had not caught this, it would have intensified and burnt the house down. The product was installed properly and had been used since 2021, changing bulbs of course. (They have photos if that helps).
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard that could have led to a house fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I received an email from Amazon last month concerning a recall for the Medical King Bed Assist Rail Model#7007.  I purchased the product for my Mother who has mobility issues due to Parkinson's disease . Earlier this year her caregiver entered the home and found my mother trapped between the rail and the mattress. she suffered paralysis in her left arm as a result of a compressed nerve. Although the doctors said it could be a temporary condition she has not regained full function after 10 months. I just want others to be aware of this potential hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in paralysis due to a compressed nerve, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the recall and the described incident.

My daughter hurt her foot (nothing bad but it could easily have been much worse). I reached out to the manufacturer who said this product is out of warranty. Thats it; they didnt express any concern about safety.

incident_description: I purchased the Babyletto Sprout dresser in 2023 in preparation for the birth of my first child. After 10 months of normal use, the dresser has started spewing ball bearings at random when the drawers are opened. The ball bearings are small, but absolutely pose a choking hazard for small children, and my child is at the age where he will pick up anything he finds and put it in his mouth. We are gentle with our belongings, but I don't think force has anything to do with when or why the ball bearings come loose, because I watched my tiny 10 month old pull the bottom drawer open gently and saw a ball come flying out. I have found 6 ball bearings around his room so far, two of which I had to pry out of my child's hands. I reached out to Babyletto to ask if they had suggestions for what I could do to fix the issue and ensure that it is safe to continue using, but their customer service team said my product is no longer under warranty, and thus they would not help. I asked them to at least escalate the issue to someone higher up to see if they could fix the design flaw so that future consumers aren't putting their little ones in danger, but it does not seem like they are interested in looking into the issue.
justification: The incident involves a choking hazard for a child, with ball bearings being found in the child's hands, indicating a potential for injury.

incident_description: Biddeford electric blank model TC13W1 controller got hot, smoked and became hotter as long as it was left on. Plastic case was becoming hotter without apparent bounds.  Inspection shows very burned PCB at the site of the fabricated multi-contact switch on the contact. We were lucky that the plastic case did not ignite.

I didn't see that she had gone in there, but I did hear a bump and her whining. My husband flipped the sofa over on its back and I pried the hinge apart enough to pull her out, which took several minutes. Her head and shoulders were trapped between the two sides of the hinge mechanism. I thought she was going to die from being crushed. When we got her out, we noticed injuries on her right shoulder and neck with bleeding (see photos). She is the second animal to get caught in this sofa. Our cat got caught under the motor shortly after we purchased two of these sofas on January 16, 2022. I believe they pose a risk of severe injury or death to small animals, babies, and toddlers.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern

I am reaching out you to express my deep concerns about the button cell battery light string we purchased, especially given that we have a 5-year-old child at home. 

Consequently, we compared the Consumer Safety Commission's standards for such products (UL4200A) and Unfortunately found that the light string we received did not include any warning labels on either the product or its packaging. When we tried to change the battery, the screws fell out directly, It's not an anti drop screw, creating a serious risk of ingestion for young children maybe. Additionally, the battery compartment can be opened manually without removing the screws, leaving the button cell batteries exposed.

I am concerned that this product fails to meet ANSI/UL 4200A and 16 C.F.R.  1263.3 standards. And I hope you to double-check these safety issues promptly to mitigate potential risks.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this urgent matter.
justification: The product poses a potential risk of ingestion for young children due to exposed button cell batteries and lack of warning labels, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

The fiberglass release from the mattress is a clear manufacturing defect that makes the product unfit for use and poses a significant health risk. Furthermore, their attempt to void the warranty based on the removal of the law tag is a deceptive practice prohibited by the FTC.

incident_description: I got an electric shock from a light fixture that has a design flaw that results in the mains voltage being exposed in a place where you can easily touch it. The fixture is a swing-arm sconce, and I have two of them mounted on either side of my bed. The dimmer knob works by raising the voltage of the neutral lead that is connected to the outside of the light bulb. And the light bulb, when fully screwed into the socket, has the outside metal part of the bulb base still sticking up a bit above the socket. When the light is fully bright (no dimmer), the outside of the light bulb is at 0 V. As you dim the light to zero, the outside of the light goes up to 120 V. When reaching up to use the light, I inadvertently touched the outside metal of the bulb with my fingertip and got a nasty shock on my finger, and I felt the current come out of my foot, which was in contact with the floor. I took out my multimeter and found that the outside of the bulb was at 100 V at the time. I called out an electrician who determined that the fault is due to the design of the fixture itself. There is a little cardboard sleeve around the socket, but it does not stick up high enough to protect the metal outside of the light bulb. (Also, that would still be a terrible design choice.) The product is the Visual Comfort S-2000. https://www.visualcomfort.com/triple-swing-arm-wall-lamp-s2000/

incident_description: On April 14, 2020, I ordered an "Olee Sleep 10 Inch Grey I Gel Layer Top Memory Foam Mattress 10FM02Q". Over the last few years, my partner and I have been dealing with dry, itchy eyes, sore throats, occasional rashes, and itchy skin. Recently, I've been developing worsening rashes and itchiness that did not seem to go away. In our attempts to track down what's been causing these issues, we discovered that the inner cover of the mattress we purchased is 100% glass fiber. We then confirmed the source by shining a flashlight on the mattress, foam topper, and sheets with the lights turned off. We saw probably thousands of tiny, perfectly straight, reflective lines on all the surfaces. We confirmed with images and reports online that these reflective "slivers" were, indeed, fiberglass. We have never removed the outer cover of the mattress, nor has it been ripped, torn, or damaged in any way. It seems the fiberglass from the inner cover has worked its way out over the years, contaminating our mattress topper, sheets, blankets, pillows, and clothing. The result of the mattress not only containing fiberglass, but not containing a way to prevent it from escaping, is, I presume, the very health issues I mentioned previously.

incident_description:
WHAT HAPPENED
On April 15th, 2024, I ordered the TribeSigns Overbed Table with Tiltboard and Wheels from Amazon.com (even thought the product page on amazon shows it as another company called LITTLE TREE but that isnt the real company name its tribesigns as its shown on the manual and box it comes in..) This was purchased to help with my disability and being stuck in bed a lot of the time so i could get things done and make appointments without added limitations. 

On July 25th, 2024, the odd behavior of my table when pushing it forward and backward come to a conclusion of why when the caster wheel that is screwed into the frame broke of the frame and my table fell forward and due to unexpected occurance was slow to process this event quick enough to stop it. This lead to the cup of hot tea on my table to fall over and the liquid landed on my leg burning it, knowing proper emergency care being an eagel scout i got an ice pack on my leg within 15 seconds. Though my hard drive had flown off and now is damaged and all my lifes data is unrepairable. All the other objects on my table remained in good condition thankfully. 

Later that night when I clean up myself and the area, I took photos and sent the company an email explaining the issues briefly to the point, and that i need a repalcement of part #9 bc the wheel broke off the frame, they agreeded and i ened up getting a whole new unit (table)

I opened the new sent box and pulled out Part #9 and swaped the broken part of the frame with the new one, put in my csater wheels and 5 days later the wheel broke off the frame but not completely. 

I investigated why this was happening and its bc the company is manufactring the core foundation of the frame using 2 spot welds instead of doing a complete weld around the other part that holds the tread for the wheels bolt. (the frame has a predrilled hole at the bottom and then a seperate part with a internal thread is placed inside the whole and then welded to the frame) The other issue is the metal the thread part is made of is so brittle the it break easily under little resistence or pressure which caster wheels will do.

I can tell you for certain when i took a welding class in high school, spot welding was frowned upon, and consider very unsafe so that fact they are using it is just plain scary. They charge extortion pricing for a product that uses extremely cheap probably illegal manufacturing techniques. 

TYPE OF PRODUCT USED
Table with Wheels

WHO USED PRODCUT
Myself

HOW WERE PRODUCTS USED
positioned over my bed, and moved forward and backward by pushing it and pulling it gently. 

ANY INJURIES THAT DID OR COULD HAVE HAPPENED USING IT
I did burn my leg from the hot tea in my cup that fell over bc the broken caster wheels bolt broke off. furthermore, as for injuries that could have happened are far worse, if there was an infant or child in the room and it fell on them  if a pet was in the way it could have been injured as this table is large. it very easily could have killed anything like a pet or child.

incident_description: Nursery/kids furniture I purchased from Amazon has lead paint. I saw several people tested online and mine has lead paint to. Lead is deadly for kids. This is marketed as kids/nursery furniture. This is unacceptable.
justification: Lead paint is deadly for kids, and the product is marketed for nursery use, posing a severe health risk.

incident_description: My elderly mother's entire right arm became wedged between the rail and the mattress, close to the box spring.  She fell to her knees and died with her face buried in blankets wadded up at the side of the mattress where she had fallen.  The rail basically had her in an arm bar, as her arm was trapped all the way up to her shoulder.  I found her dead with her face stuffed in bedding where the rail met the bed.
justification: The incident resulted in death, as described by the trapped arm and suffocation in bedding.

incident_description:
(06/1/2024) The consumer stated that the furniture has high levels of formaldehyde. There was a chemical smell coming from the furniture. When the consumer did a home test on 6/17, the levels were .126. 

The consumer stated that she had to go to ER because she was having breathing problems. Also, it took about two weeks to get the smell out of the room after removing the furniture.
justification: The consumer experienced breathing problems requiring an ER visit, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to the direct link between formaldehyde exposure and health issues.

incident_description:
have owned a coolsense mattress I bought in biglots. for about 4 years now. and today (7/17/24)  I decided that I would wash the cover because my son toddler had peed the bed. I also have a water proof cover I keep on top of it but he had an accident prior to this and made the cover smell funny. I saw that the mattress had a zipper on the bottom. years ago but never messed with it. 

my dog has been recently over the last 2 weeks has been sleeping underneath the bed but for the last week He has been itching in the middle of the night. I thought maybe mostitoqies or the flies we bothering him. I would check him for flea or ticks and nothing there was nothing that would explain the itching. 

I would also like to add that for the past year and a half my son and I have developed this cough in the morning and night. there's nothing that could just explain why we have a horrible time first thing in the morning and at night. for me at night I am wheezing and coughing  I have been using an inhaler for about a year now.. and my son just now has had to have one kept with him because we could not figure out where this cough was coming from but it's soo bad.  

anyway fast forward to today. I stripped the bed and through the sheets and cover in the washer. and I proceeded to vacuum the blue cover that came with the mattress when I first bought it. and I see some stains. well I finally dared to open the zipper I managed to take the cover and the mesh cover I started to move it and before I knew it I was COVERED in fiberglass.   WHY WOULD A COMAPNY PUT A ZIPPER COVER ON A MATTEESS if there is FIBERGLASS INBEDDED IN THE INSIDE OF THE COVERS?!!?  I freaked out but before I figured out the fiberglass was on me I was researching how to clean a memory foam mattress and then I came acrossed the fiberglass  reviews but as I was doing that my 3 year old came into the room and stepped on to the bed without the cover on.. so he had fiberglass in his feet.  EVERYTHING came full circle as to why my dog is so itchy and why we can't breath!!  I had to throw away all my blankets. the surrounding clothes.. the metal frame is covered in the fiberglass because it had been shedding the fibers. we moved into a new apartment in February and the apartment has new carpet. now there's fiberglass in the carpet. I had to throw out my son's favorite stuffed animals clothes shoes everything underneath the bed was covered in fiberglass.  I'm a single mom this is the ONLY mattress we have. I called my mom and she went to the store and helped me put the mattress in a bed plastic bag and we sealed it so that the fibers can't get out. I got new sheets and a blanket in the mean time. I am absolutely devastated and shocked. I don't know what to do now except I feel so guilty my dog is in so much pain due to the itchiness and how compromised my son's lungs and my own have been compromised because of how long 3 years we have been sleeping in the bed while it's been shedding fiberglass everywhere. nothing on the labels warns you about it containing fiberglass its not even listed as a material used in the bed.
justification: The incident describes prolonged exposure to fiberglass leading to respiratory issues and skin irritation for both the individual and her son, as well as discomfort for the dog, indicating injury.

incident_description: We have a sitting chair that's from Lifestyle Solutions (purchased from Wayfair) that has a very sharp metal spring protruding from the seat cushion. It's in a sitting room that doesn't get a lot of use and is just over a year old.  My wife noticed the issue after it poked her while sitting on it. My kids use this seat and if any of them had moved quickly across the seat, it could've easily caused a laceration. My wife called the company since technically we are out of warranty and they said there wasn't anything they could do. This chair is unusable and we barely used it to begin with. There are several reviews on the Wayfair website that point towards the same hazard.
justification: The sharp metal spring poses a risk of laceration, especially to children, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: We heard a terrible crashing sound. The mirrors mounting hardware (that is glued on) detached and fell off the wall. It hit our tile pieces and broke them off the wall.
justification: The incident involved property damage (broken tiles) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We purchased an LED light compact mirror by impressions vanity partners with hello kitty at Marshalls
In Germantown, TN. The back of the compact mirror didnt close completely, and popped off revealing 4 2032 button batteries. Thankfully I was right there with my 17 month old and grabbed the mirror and batteries before he ingested them. The button batteries were not secured by a small screw only a failed snap enclosure. This is a safety hazard to everyone. It took very little effort to pull the case open and reveal the batteries, especially since the enclosure snaps didnt work properly. I notified impressions vanity company via social media and received no response. They have many many button battery operated mirrors on their website with no screw securing the door that holds the button batteries.
justification: The incident involved a safety hazard with unsecured button batteries that could have been ingested by a child, but no injury occurred due to immediate intervention.

incident_description: Two children were on seat of sofa leaning over back and third child was pulling on back of sofa tipped and fell on third child. Fortunately I had just walked in the room and was able to slow the fall of the sofa and prevent all the weight from crushing the child.
justification: The sofa tipped and fell on a child, but the fall was slowed, preventing injury.

incident_description: Our kitten, [REDACTED], was crushed in an Ashley Next-Gen Classic Power Reclining sofa when my 88 year old mother reclined. We always checked for the location of my toddler granddaughter and pets prior to lowering the recliner. On the day of [REDACTED] accident, he wasn't visible so had likely crawled up into an area we couldn't see. The outcome was grotesque and traumatizing for the whole family. We have since been horrified to learn that children and even one adult to our knowledge have been killed by mechanical/electronic reclining furniture and countless pets have suffered the same fate. I don't think the particular brand of furniture was the issue. I think it is all furniture with mechanical/electronic parts. We have since unplugged all of the reclining furniture we own, as my granddaughter and the remaining pet often play on the floor around and behind the furniture. We have learned that no matter how cautious and aware, there is always that one time....I am writing in the hope that furniture manufacturers would design these reclining pieces with safety in mind for living beings of all species, sizes, and shapes. One accidental and brutal death is one too many. For our part, we will never buy mechanical/electronic furniture again.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a kitten, which is a severe outcome, and the likelihood is possible given the description of similar incidents involving pets and children.

incident_description: I saw this add for a sleep product meant to help acid reflux and it advertises a 15 degree sleep position which is not safe. I am reporting this before something bad happens.
justification: No incident or injury has occurred yet; the report is a preventive measure regarding a potentially unsafe product.

incident_description: Sunlite Lightbulb (092031407)(60A15/FR) separates from base while in socket after use
justification: The lightbulb separates from its base while in use, posing a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: Sunbeam LED 14.5W bulb (model 30414212, E468262, lot 10002) went out, made strange noises, and started smoking. A decent-size cloud, not a little wisp. The base had slightly separated from the bulb body, as has happened with every Sunbeam bulb I "inherited" when buying this house; the only way to remove it from the fixture (with switch off!) was to twist the bulb until the wires inside broke, remove the bulb body, then remove the bulb base. I also removed and replaced the other 3 Sunbeam bulbs in the fixture; while they also had separated bases, the wires didn't break during removal.
justification: The bulb malfunctioned, producing smoke and strange noises, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A 5-month-old infant was found deceased by her mother in her crib when she was sleeping in/on a Turner Sling and Foam Wedge. (Product website: https://tucker-sling.myshopify.com/collections/tucker-sling-and-foam-wedge-combination). This sleeping wedge was reportedly provided to family by the Seattle Children's Hospital after they were born. The product appeared to have been used as intended (the infant was secured by the sling to the wedge), but information on possible injuries is still pending additional investigation and examination.
justification: The infant was found deceased, indicating the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: I received a notice today from Amazon to report a recall on an item I purchased for my mother, the Medline bed assist rail.  In August 2021, the rail malfunctioned and caused her to fall hard. She had to enter a nursing home where her condition continued to deteriorate. In May 2022, she began showing symptoms of sepsis. The physician determined that the fall was hard enough to cause the failure of a mesh sling installed after a hysterectomy to support her bladder. Over the months since the fall, her bladder had descended to her colon where a fistula formed that caused feces to enter her bladder. She died painfully a few days later.
justification: The incident resulted in a death due to complications from a fall caused by a malfunctioning product.

incident_description:

justification: The child was hit by falling shelves, resulting in injury to the foot.

incident_description: Three times in the past three weeks (June 10 -26, 2024) my wife and I have been electrically shocked when touching a "Library Floor Task Lamp" bought from Restoration Hardware in the late-2008-2009 timeframe.  Initially, when my wife reported two shocks, I thought it a short in the outlet and took that apart, finding no problems.  So I looked at the lamp more closely, getting my own shock in the process. Upon removing the weighted base, I discovered that the rubberized insulation on the interior lamp cord had deteriorated to the point of directly  exposing the metal lamp shaft to the copper wiring in literally dozens of locations.  (I am attaching  relevant photos.) I contacted Restoration Hardware (RH) customer service by phone, expressing my concern for the safety of its customers, asked whether it didn't have an obligation to look further into this product's safety and perhaps issue a recall, and inquired about its warranty and restitution.  I emphasized that my primary concern was not replacement/restitution but customer safety.  I was advised to provide a fuller description, receipts and photos by email, which I did to the best of my abilities on June 27, 2024.  On June 29, 2024, RH customer service responded with an email stating that without specific information on the date and location of the original purchase, they are "unable to return or exchange the lamp."  There was not one word of RH's concern for the priority issue of customer safety.  For that reason, I am contacting you in the belief that a serious injury or even electrocution as the consequence of further public exposure to this unsafe product is in the purview and responsibility of the CPSC.
justification: The incident involved multiple electrical shocks but no reported injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the repeated occurrences and the deteriorated condition of the lamp.

incident_description:

Caller stated that she was unaware that her shoulder was broke at the time until she went to Orthopedic the following days after, because she was in so much pain.   Caller stated that she had borrowed the recliner to use.  She stated that she did not purchase the recliner, it is in the home that she is a caretaker.
Caller feels that this recliner is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The caller suffered a broken shoulder and head injury, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The incident involved a faulty recliner, suggesting a possible but not frequent occurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description: I purchased a new set of patio furniture with two swivel chairs. The first time someone sat in one of the chairs it broke off where the chair was attached to the swivel base causing the person to fall over backwards.

The frame cracked where the D-rings connect to the frame, resulting in the D-rings completely separating from the frame. The frame fell onto my couch. Luckily no humans or dogs were on the couch at the time!

The product was sold by VagaryLight on Amazon under the product name: "Neon Signs Lightning Bolt Battery Operated and USB Powered Warm White Art LED Decorative Lights Wall Decor for Living Room Office Christmas Wedding Party Decoration(NELNB)".

incident_description: Turned in my other stool that was apparently unsafe bc the welds could break. Turned my stool in for the new one and the new one broke.
justification: The stool broke but there is no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Received belt strap covers and travel pillow for newborn twins. Pediatrician said to NOT use them, they were a suffocation hazard
justification: The pediatrician identified a suffocation hazard, but no incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a dresser and the business has given me different legs to swap it out but it has not helped. The dresser shakes violently when you open and close it. Every time I open the drawer I fear it will tip over. We took their advice and secured it appropriately but nothing has worked. Before someone gets hurt I want to report the safety concern of the Alto Dresser made by Spot On Square.
justification: The dresser shakes violently and poses a tipping hazard, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Bought from Home Depot, 4 led, 60 watt, daylight, Ecosmart bulbs, # 1006-777-824. Put 4 in our bathroom. All seemed fine. During the night one of the lights exploded. When my wife got up during the night she stepped on the light bulb glass that was all over the counter and floor. Never had a light bulb explode before.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb exploding, which is an incident but no injury was reported despite the glass being stepped on.

incident_description: My client fell off a stool while seated in her kitchen and sustained injuries.

incident_description: Installed Parmida 4FT T8 LED (Type A+B) in standard commercial drop ceiling light fixture with electronic ballast. Several bulbs failed shortly with burnt components and melted plastic. It will become a fire hazard so we will proceed to replace them even though the bulbs are in service for less than 2 months.
