incident_description: I bought a metal bunk bed twin at top and full at the bottom for my 2 boys on April 16th, 2024. At the bottom my 17 year old sleeps and my 14 year old son would sleep at the top, but he is with his mom currently, so he has not used the bed so far, so no load at the top twin mattress yet. Last night at around 11 PM my 17 year old son woke up as the bottom rails of the bunk bed has came out where some rails have come out and also the single middle rail and screws have come out. I have bought this furniture from City furniture considering that I have purchased it from a good store where they have also done the installation. My son is a competitive swimmer and because of this, he has injured his shoulder and could not perform in his morning training this morning at 6:15am. This is extremely disturbing as I can not think of what could have happened if my younger boy was actually sleeping at the top as well!!
justification: The incident resulted in a shoulder injury to the 17-year-old, but no death or more severe injury occurred. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the bed failure was a specific event with no prior indication.

incident_description:
We received information through a child fatality review that a 4-month-old infant died after being placed in her crib on top of a Leachco Cuddle-U  with a blanket that covered the pillow and was tucked under the pillow.
The infant was laid on her back propped and in a swaddle blanket. 
The mother found the baby unresponsive in the crib with her face partially in the pillow
An autopsy was completed on the infant by the District One Medical Examiners Office. The cause of death was undetermined and the manner of death was undetermined.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant, warranting the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is low (unlikely) based on the provided frequency data (72 of 5402).

incident_description: A Simple Living Bradley two drawer filing cabinet was purchased in December 2023  from the  on line Bed Bath and Beyond website for creating a filing system for a 90+ year old woman (my mother in law) to keep her essential papers organized.  The filing cabinet was assembled according to manufacturer's instructions and files were placed in both drawers after assembly.  We recently added more paper files to the drawer and the drawer tipped forward creating a tipping hazard that could cause serious injury.  After contacting Bed Bath and Beyond they assumed no liability for this tipping risk.
justification: The filing cabinet tipped forward, creating a potential hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a platform bed from Wayfair (it is Wayfair's brand - Sand & Stable).  It reports a supported weight of 1500 lbs (the product page is here: https://www.wayfair.com/furniture/pdp/sand-stable-xander-low-profile-platform-bed-stmh2144.html )

Within two months of owning the bed, it collapsed on the side rail.  I left a review about this on the product page.  Wayfair then sent me a replacement box (essentially half of the first shipment).  I installed the replacement side rail and things were ok for awhile.

Today, when I went to sit down on the edge of the bed, the bed collapsed in exactly the same spot.  I am convinced at this point that this is a design defect in the bed and think that the labeled weight capacity of 1500lbs is not actually real.  Wayfair is not providing support because the bed is 20 days outside of the 1 year warranty (even though the replacement parts arrived in July 2023).

I am 300 lbs, my wife is also 300 lbs - with a 100lb mattress and our young daughters sometimes sleeping in bed with us we do not get anywhere near the 1500lb weight limit.

I felt like it was important to report this because my young daughters like to hide under this bed (despite us telling them that they shouldn't be under there).  I am massively concerned now about the potential risk to them had this happened when they were crawling under the bed and one of their parents was on the bed.

I also noticed that Wayfair has an existing recall in place for a similar platform bed that has similar associated risks - I feel like this recall should apply to this bed as well (even though the manufacturer might be different, the potential failure consequences are the same): [REDACTED]
justification: The bed collapsed twice without injury, but there is a potential risk of injury to children hiding under it.

incident_description: Bunk bed is too long and does not fit a standard twin mattress. Because of this, the mattress gets pushed down on both the head and footboard causing feet and arms to get trapped. This morning my son woke up trapped between the headboard and the mattress smashing him.
justification: The description indicates that the son was trapped between the headboard and mattress, which suggests an incident with potential for injury but no explicit mention of injury occurred.

incident_description: We have 4 Herman Miller Eames kitchen chairs. 3 of the 4 have failed at a joint in the metal frame, sending us and guests crashing to the floor. We've asked the company to address this in the past and they say there is no defect. However, we are a household with 2 adults, no children, and we are very easy on furniture. Chairs should not fail in this manner, and we are lucky nobody has been severely hurt when they give way and fall apart suddenly. The 4th chair, the only one that has not failed yet, is starting to show signs of give as well. The company denies any quality issues. But something is wrong and these chairs are unsafe.
justification: Chairs have failed multiple times, causing falls, but no severe injuries have been reported yet.

incident_description: I bought a Hoffree Big and Tall  Office chair from Walmart in July 2023.  The chair was supposed to withhold 550lbs.  I do not weigh more than 250 lbs but the chair started breaking little by little.  On June 3, 2024 the chair broke all the way and almost made me fall to the ground.  I am a 70 year old senior and cannot be falling down.
justification: The chair broke and almost caused a fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: A small candle in a glass jar was burning, when after about 3 hours, I heard a "pop."  I went into the bathroom and saw large and wild flames 6-8 inches above the candle.  It took three attempts to blow the candle out due the size of the flames.  When the candle was out, I saw that the top of the glass  bar had broken at the level of the wax.

incident_description:
I am reporting a significant widespread issue that we have unfortunately encountered firsthand. In 2019, we bought the Lucid memory foam mattress from Amazon. Recently, while spot cleaning the padded outer cover, per the legal white tags, we proceeded to unzip & remove the outer cover  allowing it to  fully air dry at room temperature. However, upon doing so, we inadvertently exposed the fire retardant sock, which consists of 50% fiberglass and 50% modacrylic fibers. These tiny fibers dispersed into the air without our knowledge at first, leading to an extreme contamination throughout our entire home. The situation became so dire that we were forced to vacate our home and everything in it. My family is suffering from various health issues due to the exposure to these synthetic chemical fibers, such as eye infections, lung & sinus infections, amongst other symptoms. It is crucial to highlight the risk associated with exposing the fire retardant layer and the absolute devastating consequences that follow. Moreover, there is a potential risk of the fibers permeating through the cotton cover and becoming airborne without ever removing the cover making anyone with a mattress containing this material at risk. The financial loss and damages well exceed $200,000, all stemming from a simple attempt to clean our mattress cover without prior warning. 
The realization that it is legally permissible in the United States to purchase a mattress without cautionary labels warning against removing the full zipper cover and exposing oneself to hazardous substances is unsettling. The probability of this occurrence affecting countless consumers is heightened due to the widespread use of this "fire retardant" material in millions of mattresses. This issue is not specific to the brand Lucid, in fact there are many brands ranging in price that contain fiberglass and other synthetic fibers posing major risk for respiratory problems to the individuals sleeping on that each night.
justification: The incident resulted in health issues such as eye, lung, and sinus infections, indicating injury (severity level 3). The widespread use of similar mattresses suggests the occurrence likelihood is high (4).

It also stated that fires would be hard to contain! WHY ISN'T THIS INFORMATION VISIBLY PROCLAIMED ON THE OUTSIDE OF THE BOX?

A paper entitled "Important Consumer Information" (copy included with this complaint) states that owners not use heating pads or electric blankets while using the mattress topper-this warning should be on the outside of the box. It so also recommends that owners air out the mattress topper for 24 hours-again this is not something one should discover after opening the box.

Along with ftbromyalgia I have asthma; my asthma had been under control until using the mattress topper. The labeling on the outside of the box or inside the box does not warn users that the toxins in the mattress topper can acerbate an asthma attack. After sleeping on this topper for only two nights, I am still having breathing problems.

I am also concerned with the flammability of this product. Why isn't this information proclaimed on the front of the box in BIG BOLD LETTERING? If this product is so flammable, could static electricity cause a fire? Furthermore, should a fire start in a home and the flames reach the polyurethane foam consider the toxins that would be emitted into the environment and the community at large. And what about the disposal of these foams?

Ollies is not the only store which sells these 'memory foam' mattress toppers under numerous brands. [REDACTED]  sell them along with, I am sure, many other retailers. This is frightening. There is not one brand that proclaims on the front of the box the safety ramifications of their product.

Lastly, I have read that long-term use of polyurethane can cause cancer. This product should be removed from the market.

Thank you for your consideration
justification: The incident describes health issues (asthma exacerbation) and potential fire hazards, indicating injury and significant risk.

incident_description: In 2017 I purchased a mattress from the brand Casper. After moving a few times the cover of the mattress was dirty and I wanted to wash it. There is a tag on the mattress that states it is illegal to remove and I consulted that tag for washing instructions. It says that if you are going to remove the cover to dry clean it or wash in a cold water cycle. Upon removing the cover I found that there was a gauzy fabric layer surrounding the foam which was ripped in many places. Under this fabric was strands and strands of a silvery substance. At the time I did not realize that this was a type of fiberglass. This substance would go on to destroy the physical health and mental wellbeing of me, my partner, and my dog. The mattress cover contains a zipper in addition to the tags that dictate it is safe to remove. The zipper gives the impression that the cover can be removed. No where in the mattress, website, or packaging does it say that this mattress contains fiberglass. At the time of the incident, we noticed the fibers floating in air and settling on our surfaces. We began to feel irritated in our eyes and skin. I ended up washing the the cover, we vacuumed and cleaned and believed we were done with it. I speculated that the fibers may have been fiberglass just by the way they felt on our skin and the way they were behaving in the air. The day after this incident my partner was in a car accident and the whole fiberglass in our mattress thing just ended up taking a back burner.  In the next few months I began to develop debilitating and disfiguring skin rashes and lesions. Painful red itchy lumps and scab like lesions developed on my chin neck arms back and top of thighs (anywhere there was a lot of movement or rubbing of my clothes on my skin. Our dog became ill with bowel obstructions and very itchy red inflamed skin. I also began to notice that all of my belongings, clothes, shoes, pillows, blankets, couches, surfaces, EVERYTHING was inundated with these fibers. My partner and I were sitting on our bed speculating about what was going on with my skin and our dog and I mentioned that I kept finding all this lint in our laundry. I saw his face change when he made the connection between my symptoms, the fibers in our space, and the fiberglass mattress. Since discovering that the fiberglass has contaminated our home we have been living in a nightmare. My skin symptoms persist as well as eye irritation and respiratory symptoms. We have to give our dog an anti itch medication called [REDACTED] that costs us $80 a month. The expense of this experience has been debilitating. We really should throw out all of our clothes, bedding, rugs, furniture, and any soft or upholstered items and we have removed a lot but I cannot afford to replace all these items. We had to cover our furniture and belongings in plastic just to remove the mattress from our home. We have saved the mattress in a mattress bag. We have bought air purifiers (in 4 months we are STILL having to wash the filter every few days because it is absolutely covered in these fibers) it has made it into almost every single item that we own and it is a safety hazard. I am angry that this is allowed to be used in mattresses as a fire retardant. I think it was leeching into the cover of our mattress before I even removed it because the protective layer around the foam was ripped before I even took the cover off. I have photo and video evidence of everything. This is a serious health hazard and safety risk. The fact that we had no disclosure that this product was even in our mattress is criminal in my opinion. It is known that fiberglass is a health hazard and causes irritation but yet it is legal to put it in an item where one spends a significant amount of time. Your bed is a place where you are supposed to feel safe and secure but instead it has made me sick and exposed me to a toxic material. I feel violated and vulnerable. I have reached out the Casper to inform them of our experience and file a claim for financial reimbursement. This is in process. Thank you for reading.
justification: The incident caused skin rashes, respiratory issues, and pet health problems, indicating significant health impacts.

I had a baby in 2021 who wore size large through 2023 and a new baby in 2023 who wore size xs, small, and medium. The threads still came loose with the newer sleep sacks I have owned since 2022. Opened package on 7-20-2023.  Broken glass inside product box and product package. Had eye pain.  Visited an urgent care center.  contacted Amazon Customer Service.  Was told someone would email me, rather than a phone call.

As of 8-10-2023, no emails, and no phone calls.  Amazon order involved [REDACTED].  Emailed Amazon again on 8-10-2023 asking for a phone call from someone at Amazon who deals with customer injuries resulting from damaged products & broken glass in product boxes which then result in medical visits.  Escalating to request help also because the front-line customer service agents at Amazon seem largely useless on this front.  People who can actually help with safety & injjry issues at Amazon appear unreachable.

Later found that the glass from the broken bulb product box had also leaked out into the shipping container.  Disposed of the shipping container.  Examined the other bulb boxes for broken glass powder.  Wiped them off so as to remove such powder (other product boxes which weren't broken, but whcih were in the same shipping box as the bulb box which was broken).

Had to take time out of my workday to visit an urgent care clinic and to deal with this issue also.  One day of personal time regarding impact, resulting and the eye pain.

(03/13/2024): I request that you forward my report to you, not only to the product manufacturer but also to the retailer Amazon.com.
Note that the product manufacturer refused to provide any compensation for my time & trouble and medical visit & time off work. Amazon.com also refused to help. 
In any case, I wanted to ensure that Amazon.com will receive a copy of the report also, as sent to them by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.

incident_description: I purchased 10 pairs of I-Semble heavy duty blind floating shelf bracket (SKU 59434) from Rockler (seen here: https://www.rockler.com/i-semble-heavy-duty-blind-shelfsupport) These are rated for a load of 125# per pair.  While installing these brackets yesterday (per manufacturer's instructions), I noticed that one of the posts was loose and when I applied slight pressure with my hand, the post came off (if possible, will attach a photograph on a subsequent page.) It appears that the post corroded internally. It also appears that the product is assembled by screwing a threaded stud on the post to the flat steel bracket after which it is welded in back; it is not welded around the base of the post and there is a seam where water/humidity can get in and corrode the post internally, causing failure. Thankfully, this occured during installation as opposed to when the product was fully loaded. Such a failure, either initially, or after time as the product continues to corrode internally, could cause serious bodily injury or even fatality.  If you note on the webpage provided, approximately 33% of the one-star reviews report such a failure, including one individual who reports that they incurred a financial loss as items that were on the shelf were destroyed.
justification: The incident involved a product failure during installation with no injury, but potential for serious injury or fatality if loaded. Approximately 33% of one-star reviews report similar failures.

incident_description: The incident occurred May 28, 2023: Serta BeautyRest Black mattress was discovered to be shedding fiberglass through the mattress cover after regular use. No tears or defects were observed. Shiny, glistening fibers were noted on the upholstered bed frame, bedding, and rug under the bed. Immediate mattress removal and removal of all affected items used during clean-up happened within 12 hours. All receipts of professional removal and details were provided to Serta in the official damage claim, and we remain cooperative and responsive to Serta to this day: March 11, 2024. Tangible damages exceed $50,000. Serta refuses to reimburse damages or "admit negligence" because we did not "produce the mattress" or take photos as evidence. The insistence that we should have retained the hazardous mattress for evidential purposes, with minor children and pets in the household, is preposterous and reflects a disconcerting disregard for consumer safety. Expecting us to preserve a product that was actively endangering the health of our household merely to satisfy evidentiary demands is not only unreasonable but also inhumane. The additional request for photographic evidence is equally nonsensical. No photograph could adequately capture the risk posed by fiberglass particles once they have become airborne and infiltrated the environment of our home. Such demands demonstrate a fundamental misunderstanding of the nature of the hazard involved and further illustrate Serta's failure to grasp the seriousness of the health risks imposed by their defective product. The Serta claims examiner assigned to our case continues to drag their feet, sometimes taking over 30 days to respond via email. No mention of fiberglass use anywhere on the Serta website, as evidenced by screenshots we take every month. We would have never bought a mattress with fiberglass had we known. Ongoing respiratory problems since the incident, rash occurred during incident.
justification: The incident involved fiberglass exposure causing respiratory problems and a rash, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described circumstances and ongoing issues.

incident_description: A murphy bed purchased on Amazon callapsed on me.  I am a woodworker, so for me assembling flat pack furniture is pretty easy.  I followed their instructions exactly, but when I got out of bed in the morning. one of the feet that supports the bed slid out, my weight on the bed then caused the case to pull off the wall and fall on me. When the foot slid out, these small screws were not enough to support the weight, allowing it to fall on me.  I found online instructions for some other murphy beds, they had 4 written pages with detailed drawings on how to properly mount it to the wall.  They stateted how you HAD to screw into a stud and used much larger #12 screws that were 3" long.  As currently sold on Amazon, this product is extermely unsafe.  It needs much larger screws to mount to the wall with proper instructions and some way to lock the feet in place so they can't slip out.

incident_description: A mattress we bought in 2020 made of foam had a fiberglass cover unbeknownst to us. When a contractor was here doing work we removed all the bedding and placed the twin foam mattress in question on top of the king mattress in my room so the contractor could work where the mattress in question was usually laying (in our room at foot of bed for our toddler). My daughter and I put a projector on the wall to watch a movie and she jumped all over the mattress while I laid on top of it eating popcorn. We had no idea we were laying directly on a 100% fiberglass cover, we had no idea we were putting thousands if not millions of shards of glass into the air and all over our bodies. I woke up after the movie to go to the bathroom and looked down to see my pants and shirt were like a disco ball. My husband was still awake and ai called him and he said you are covered in fiberglass, how? Why? We went back to the room to find our one year old also covered head to toe and our entire bedroom and closet contaminated. I had to wake her up and shower her at 1130 PM and have been sleeping elsewhere for 10 days. I am exhausted! Zinus is the brand. When I ci tacted them they said take off all extra covers and take a photo of the mattress. So I did. Then they said the warranty was void because I took off the fiberglass cover for the photos! We had to build a new bedroom emergency style onto our house so we have a safe place to sleep. I cannot wear any of my clothes. It's a huge devastation. We are all coughing.
justification: The incident resulted in physical harm (coughing, fiberglass exposure) and significant property contamination, but no death occurred. Such incidents are unlikely but not rare given the product's design.

incident_description:
I purchased the Flexsteel Midway Power Reclining Sofa and Loveseat from Furniture and Appliancemart in Stevens Point, WI. During a visit from my grandchildren in November 2023, I noticed that my 5 year old granddaughter was sitting on the loveseat and her foot/leg naturally slid inside of the space between the seat cushion and the back cushion. When looking further into this I found that the space between the seat cushion and back cushion was 5+ inches and I could fit a spaghetti squash(the size of a child's head) into this space. The power controls to recline the sofa/loveseat are on the inside of the sofa arm, therefore, a child could definitely get a foot/leg or head in that space and also intentionally or by accident hit the control button which would power the couch to go back to original position. This action could crush a child's head.

I have tried to call Furniture and Appliancemart as well as Flexsteel without any reasonable resolution. I first contacted [REDACTED] at Furniture & Appliancemart in November 2023 They added more filling into the cushion which did not make a change in the 5+ inch space between the cushions. I then contacted [REDACTED]  at Flexsteel on 11/16/23 because Furniture and Appliancemart said they could do nothing further to help. [REDACTED] said she will work through Furniture & Appliancemart and will contact Furniture & Appliancemart with recommendations. I have made several calls to Furniture & Appliancemart as well as Flexsteel and have not had anyone address the issue further. I have also requested the safety specifications from Flexsteel and Furniture & Appliancemart, but have not received it. On 2/13/2024 I called Flexsteel again and spoke with [REDACTED]. I asked to speak with a manager. [REDACTED]  said [REDACTED]  would call me back. To date, I have not heard from [REDACTED]  or [REDACTED]. I'm not sure what else I can do to prevent injury or death by this power reclining sofa/loveseat. I have four grandchildren ages 6, 4, 4, and 9 months that visit often. In fact, I babysit them full time in the summer and just don't want them to get hurt.
justification: The description highlights a potential for death (crushing a child's head) with a plausible scenario, and the likelihood is possible given the design flaw and frequent child visits.

incident_description: I purchased a Nectar bed (including mattress and foundation) a few years ago. The Nectar advertises a lifetime guarantee. About 4 nights ago, around [REDACTED], while my wife and I were sleeping, the foundation randomly gave out. Not only did this startle the two of us, but I ended up rolling off my side of the bed and swiftly to the floor. My right shoulder and hip are sore but I have not yet sought medical attention for this. After checking out the broken side of the bed foundation, it appears that the welded part of the metal framework had broken. The mattress has been fine, but this is the second time weve had issues with the foundation. Unfortunately, this time it resulted in mild injury. I contacted Nectar and I was told I was slightly outside of the 3 year warranty window for the foundation. Now I am bed-less  and in pain from the accident.
justification: The incident resulted in mild injury (sore shoulder and hip) but no medical attention was sought, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as this is the second issue with the foundation, indicating a recurring problem.

incident_description:
My wife and child were seated as normal in the Pottery Barn Dream Manual Glider Recliner (https://www.potterybarnkids.com/products/dream-recliner/) and while pressing the manual recline latch, the back of the chair broke off on one side and led both mom and child to tip over and fall.   Both wife and child were thrown to the floor as a result of the part breaking out of its socket.  My wife is 110 lbs and my child is 20 lbs.  Thankfully, injuries were only minor - pulled back muscle and soreness for wife, and temporary pain for child outside of the emotional situation - but could have been significant.  
The product is not made safely, does not adhere to Pottery Ban Kids Anti-Tipping Testing nor their Global Safety Standards.

Upon reaching out to Pottery Barn Kids multiple times verbally (their email is not monitored they said), they have refused to provide any level of satisfactory customer service for the injured consumers.  This includes replacing the furniture given was negligently assembled by the product owner, providing replacement parts for their furniture, or refunding the consumer for the faulty product.  They also showed complete disregard for human injury, particularly to the child.
The company advised that because the product was purchased over 30 days ago, nothing can be done.  In fact, they were unable to even view our original order # [REDACTED] from May 2022 because it was over 1 year old (surely, there must be information record keeping requirements for companies like this?).
The company also advised that they have a one year warranty on furniture products such as this, which they advised is NOT provided explicitly to consumers.  We found this to be very odd that a warranty exists but is NOT disclosed to a consumer?  How is a consumer to know when they are purchasing or even after if there is any recourse?  This seems to be deceptive sales practices at its finest, and surely a regulatory compliance issue.

This is a safety issue for the product that we do not want any other family to go through.
There clearly are policies and standards that Pottery Barn Kids has in place to protect consumers from these issues, yet they are both not clear to its consumers and not followed.
When safety issues do arise, the company is grossly negligent in attempting to resolve them with their consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (pulled back muscle and soreness for the wife, temporary pain for the child), which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the described product failure and lack of customer service response.

incident_description: Zinus mattress was purchased from Amazon in 2019. In 2023, it was discovered that the mattress was leaking fiberglass (ie glass fibers) particles/dust through the mattress cover that had never been removed. It is unclear how long a period of time the fiberglass had been leaking through the mattress cover. Two humans and two dogs have skin, respiratory, and potentially other issues that may be contributed to the long-term fiberglass exposure. At the time of purchase, there was no information on the use of fiberglass/glass fibers in the fire sock of the mattress listed on the Zinus page on Amazon or in the product manual. Since the fiberglass had been leaking from the mattress for an extended period of time, most fabric items including clothing and carpet are contaminated and must be disposed of. All items in the house have to be cleaned and the house emptied to be cleaned by a professional remediation company, following a similar process as mold or asbestos.
justification: The incident involves long-term exposure to fiberglass leading to health issues for both humans and pets, and significant property contamination requiring professional remediation.

incident_description: Both middle support beams of this bed fell off due to stripped screws. One of the outer middle support beams snapped in the middle of the night one night. The bed tilts and sags, collapsing a bit in the middle, and I regularly have to shift it around to get it to sit straight. It is currently propped up by bricks to stay upright and not snap in half or collapse entirely. The product being used was an Andover Mills Part #: W004201266 bed from Wayfair, advertised as the "Aileen Tufted Upholstered Low Profile Platform Bed" on the wayfair platform. The bed is about two years old. I began having issues with it after less than 6 months. I am the only person using this product. My dog also uses it. It is a queen sized bed and the specs say that it should support up to 500lbs. My dog and I combined are under half of that weight, and this is still happening. The product has been used for sleeping and lounging. There have been no high energy activities on this bed, no jumping onto it, no significant moving while in it. I did not get injured because I moved off the bed right when I felt it snapping, and did not use it again until I was able to purchase bricks from the hardware store to stabilize it. However, If I were heavier, was sleeping with a friend or partner in this bed, or continued to use it before purchasing bricks to support it, I am positive it would've snapped and collapsed entirely and potentially caused injury.
justification: The bed collapsed but no injury occurred as the user moved off in time, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) given the recurring structural issues and potential for collapse under normal use.

incident_description: The first concerning symptom about our Signature Design by Ashley (Furniture) Game Zone Reclining Sofa occurred when we tried to use the electrical outlet located in the headrest to charge a USB device. The device not only would not charge properly, but the device (an Internet hot spot) became extremely hot to the touch. Upon discovering this fact, we disconnected the device from the sofa. We charged the hot spot later via a standard, non-couch electrical source and we did not have any further overheating issues. The next cause for concern was the burning, electrical odor that occurs when reclining the sofa. The intensity of the odor has become very noticeable, and nothing else is causing the electrical/burning smell. Every time we power the recliner, the sofa emits this same concerning burning odor. We are extremely concerned for our safety, and we unplugged the sofa from the electrical source. This is a very unsafe product. My husband and I use this couch, and we used this to recline. Now we only recline the sofa manually in the up position on one side and not in the up position on the other side due to our concerns about this product. While no one was injured by the sofa, the electrical, burning odor has made us so concerned that we do not have the sofa connected to an electrical outlet. We wonder what injuries could have occurred if we still used this unsafe product; we are unwilling to take that risk. The symptoms of the Game Zone couch sound too similar to the recently recalled [REDACTED] couch, also made by Ashley Furniture. We should be refunded, as we are unable to use the recliner as it is intended. We spent over $1,400 on this defective product. We are reporting this product to warn others about this unsafe product. The UPC is 024052516333, and the Item Model Number is 3850115. There is also an ASIN number of B07PPWZ2MP.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electrical outlet and burning odor, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description: My husband and I have been sleeping on the Vibe Gel Memory Foam Mattress (purchased from Amazon: https://www.amazon.com/Vibe-12-Inch-Memory-Foam-Mattress/dp/B074ND75P9/ref=sr_1_5?crid=1FFB4WDAJF3Y&keywords=vibe%2Bfoam%2Bmattress&qid=1705866926&sprefix=vibe%2Bfoam%2B%2Caps%2C114&sr=8-5&ufe=app_do%3Aamzn1.fos.18630bbb-fcbb-42f8-9767-857e17e03685&th=1) for about 6 months. We started to notice we were waking up with sinus irritation that didn't improve much with a humidifier or other measures. Then, our cat began having severe asthma flare ups and breathing fits. We investigated and discovered that this mattress has been leaking fiberglass all over. Fiberglass particles are imbedded in every sheet and blanket we own, imbedded in the carpet, and contaminating the air we breathe, causing the asthma flares and illness. The original mattress cover is completely intact and undisturbed, it should be able to hold the fiberglass in but it does not. This is extremely hazardous and has had drastic implications for our health and the health of our pets. This mattress has been used only as usual and has been well taken care of. The protective cover has never been removed as per product guidelines. In addition, nowhere in the product listing or information does this company disclose the use of fiberglass. This mattress is advertised using the CentriPUR-US label, which leads consumers to falsely believe that this product is safe and free from hazardous materials.
justification: The incident describes sinus irritation and severe asthma flare-ups in both humans and pets due to fiberglass exposure, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as it occurred over 6 months of normal use.

incident_description:
I purchased four chairs from Crate and Barrel, called the Anna Dinning Chair  #SKU: 387141. I sat down in one of them to have dinner. After scooting back to sit fully in the chair (with my back against the back of the chair) I heard a crack. I got out of the chair and looked down to find a crack right at the joint where the leg connects to the bottom of the chair seat. I assume if it was my parent, someone heavier than I am, or my niece or nephew jumping to get in the chair, it would have broken off potentially hitting their face on my dining table. 

I'm reporting this because after looking at reviews online at Crate and Barrel, many people have reported experiencing the front legs of this specific chair cracking and breaking off.
justification: The chair cracked but no injury occurred, and online reviews indicate this is a common issue.

incident_description: Seat back of counter height stool broke during normal use, causing the user to lose balance and nearly fall backward. The second occurred some months ago, and the third yesterday 20 January 2024. No injury occurred in any of these three incidents, but this is a serious risk of fall or injury. Stools were disassembled to reveal loose screws in the bracket joining the seat back to the base. In several cases, the screws were partially or completely stripped out of the seat base. To properly secure the bracket, I replaced all screws with longer and stronger screws to at my own expense. We contacted West Elm customer service to report the failure and hazard in January 2023 after the first incident, and were told the product was outside the 30 day warranty, and they would not offer repair or replacement.
justification: The incident involved a stool breaking during normal use, causing a near fall but no injury, and has occurred multiple times with the same issue.

incident_description: They specifically advertise that their mattress does not contain fiberglass but they do. It got all over my home and had to pay for remediation. I purchased an AceSleep King Mattress on 7/9/2020 (Order number [REDACTED]). I purchased this specific mattress because I was looking for a mattress that did not contain fiberglass as a material in the fire retardant layer. This company plainly advertises that their mattresses do not contain any fiberglass. In December of 2020, I removed the outer cover of the mattress which they also claim is removable and washable, only to quickly find out that they do in fact use fiberglass in the mattress. The fiberglass (tiny lightweight strands, very difficult to see without a flashlight) under the outer cover quickly got in the air and spread throughout the room and the entire house. Fiberglass is a contaminant/irritant and can cause health problems including issues with the respiratory system, so naturally I was worried since I was breathing it in. I immediately contacted the company via email and corresponded with "[REDACTED]". She was assuring me that the mattress does not contain fiberglass. I ordered a test kit to test for fiberglass and sent to to a lab for analysis. It came back confirming that it was in fact fiberglass. I let [REDACTED] know about this and she said that they were going to send a sample of their own to a lab and test it for themselves. I have not heard back since then, and I do not know if they even sent the sample to a lab. [REDACTED] agreed to pay "room cleaning fee" if their test came back positive for fiberglass. I replied back stating that I would need to be reimbursed for all costs incurred due to this issue. I have not heard back.
justification: The incident involves exposure to fiberglass, a known respiratory irritant, but no specific injury is reported.

incident_description:
I am writing to bring a matter of critical safety concern to your attention, specifically related to the EQ3 Arie Chair, which has recently been subject to a recall notice by the Canadian Health Department (https://docs.eq3.com/recalls/arie-chair-product-recall-en.pdf).

I am a consumer residing in the United States, and my concern arises from a personal experience with the EQ3 Arie Chair, which mirrors the safety issues outlined in the Canadian recall notice. 

Since our purchase of the chair in 2018, it remained unused in the guest bedroom until May 2023 when my mother, weighing only 137lb, used it for approximately 2 hours each night before bedtime. After just 5 months of light usage, the weld of the metal mounting failed, causing the chair stem to break. This resulted in a fall that, fortunately, did not cause severe life-threatening harm; however, it did twist my mother's lower back, leading to persistent pain for several months. Notably, the breakage was alarmingly identical to the hazard outlined in the recall notice.

Despite being manufactured just one month after the specified recall dates, the chair exhibited an alarming and identical failure in the recall notice. This defect led to a fall, resulting in potential injury, emphasizing the urgency of addressing this matter promptly.

Given the potential risks associated with the observed safety issue and the fact that my experience aligns with the hazards outlined in the Canadian recall notice, I kindly request the United States Consumer Product Safety Commission's intervention in recalling the EQ3 Arie Chair in the United States. This recall extension would encompass products manufactured shortly beyond the initially specified dates, as is the case with my chair.

I believe that extending the recall period in the United States will not only protect American consumers but also prompt the manufacturer, EQ3, to address the concerns promptly and comprehensively. My ultimate goal is to ensure the safety and well-being of consumers in the United States who may be at risk due to this product.

I understand the crucial role that the Consumer Product Safety Commission plays in safeguarding public health, and I appreciate your attention to this matter. Your intervention is vital in preventing potential accidents and injuries associated with the EQ3 Arie Chair.

Thank you for your prompt consideration, and I look forward to a swift and positive resolution.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall causing persistent back pain, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the defect is documented and similar incidents have been reported.

incident_description:
I have been sleeping on this Casper mattress for years, but recently, within the past months at the very least, I've noticed these shiny threads all over the place, they're hard to see unless you shine a light on them, but when you do shine your flashlight onto the sheets, pillows, and yes, even my clothes, you see that these threads are everywhere. 

My mattress tags do not indicate any fiberglass is used, but it is clear from research and from first hand experience and being able to see it visibly, that this mattress does use fiberglass in it's "fire sock" , but none of this is mentioned, and the website and labels even indicate that there is no issue with taking the mattress cover off to clean, which is what I did and I believe that this is the reason it's now more visible than ever. 

When I wake up in the mornings, I have a hard time breathing (asthma) and have to use my inhaler more than usual. I am just so shocked that this is legal in the first place, and that no warnings are clearly labeled anywhere on the mattress. My dog has also been exposed to this and it is my hope that she hasn't suffered any lasting damage, and of course I hope the same for myself. 

In hindsight though, since I don't really know how long I've been exposed, a lot of sinus infections, and respiratory infections and issues I've experienced could have been caused by this exposure. 

I reached out to the manufacturer Casper, and there is a 10 year warranty on the mattress, so I believe they're going to eventually come and pick the mattress up, and even told me they have a "special team" of people who deal with this sort of thing.
justification: The incident involves exposure to fiberglass leading to respiratory issues and increased asthma symptoms, indicating injury.

Fortunately I was standing at the corner that failed and I was able to keep the unit from falling over.  I figured it was just a defective part.  I ordered a replacement part from Trinity.  I again loaded the shelving unit, this time with maybe 150 pounds?  I moved it across the garage once and it was fine.  When I went to roll it back a wheel bumped into a scrap of ÃÂ½ÃÂ plywood.  The caster assembly immediately torqued out of the tubing and this time the unit fell over.  
I took a closer look at the point where the casters connect to the tubing.  The casters attach to the tubes using circular donut shaped pieces pressed into the tube.  The threads are in the hole of the donut.  The donut is tiny, when fully pressed in, it only goes into the tube about 3/8ÃÂ.  To hold the donut in, the tubing is dimpled in the hopes that the donut will also dimple and the two will stick together ÃÂ they donÃÂt.  The donut pieces the failed do not have significant dimples, I assume because of how thick the donut is.
The tubing is 0.06ÃÂ thick.  The combination of the tubing thickness and short length the donut goes into the tube is not adequate for normal use of the unit with 200 pounds.  I believe these shelves are an accident waiting to happen.  If someone relies on the instructions and loads 1000 pounds onto the unit and then moves it, the unit will fail.  If someone is standing in the wrong place, they will have 1000 pounds suddenly falling on them.    
The shelving unit has a high rating on CostcoÃÂs site.  I canÃÂt understand how more people havenÃÂt had this problem and give it such a high rating.  My only guess is that few people actually roll the shelving around, perhaps it just stays in one place.  
Thank you for accepting my report!
justification: The incident involved a shelving unit failure under load, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the design flaw and potential for similar incidents under similar conditions.

Parts 1632-33. The attached document contains images of the law labels for each of these mattresses. As reflected in these images, such as those pertaining to the Molblly 12-inch hybrid mattress in queen size sold under ASIN B0BTV4LHTG, many of these labels appear to lack information that is required under CPSCÃÂs regulations, such as the manufacturerÃÂs name and address, the month and year of manufacture, the location where compliance records are kept, and the specification of the intended foundation.

Similarly, though beyond the scope of CPSCÃÂs regulations, Company has identified apparent attempts by Foshan Aiyi to evade antidumping and countervailing duties enforced by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (ÃÂCBPÃÂ). The Company has filed an allegation with CBP pursuant to the Enforce and Protect Act (ÃÂEAPAÃÂ), and understands that CBP is investigating these apparent attempted duty evasions and potential mis-identification of the country of origin for these imports.

The Company believes that the trade and customs issues, an element of which relates to trans-shipment and mis-identification of the country of origin, are furthered by the lack of identification of the manufacturer on the law label. This creates an overall environment where the consumer cannot be sure of where its product comes from, and undermines CPSCÃÂs ability to trace these products back to the manufacturing source, complicating any potential CPSC investigation or enforcement and potentially frustrating consumersÃÂ ability to pursue remedies in the event of a recall.

The extent to which these apparent labeling deficiencies and customs mis-classifications may be correlated with substantive violations is unclear, but Company does not believe such concerns can be ruled out. incident_description: We bought a dough bowl candle with three wood wicks from Etsy. The wicks all burned differently (the middle wouldn't burn at all, one on the end burned a little and would go out, and the third would burn slightly). This caused the wax to be all uneven across the length of the wood dough bowl. The unevenness of the wax and the low flame on the wick made it extremely difficult to see that the candle was lit at all. One night, only the one wick was lit (the other two wouldn't light) but it wasn't visible due to the unevenness of the wax. The other two wicks were not lit. It was left lit when we went to bed because we could not see that it was lit. The one wick lit the side of the wood dough bowl on fire and the fire spread around the rim of the bowl. The entire bowl did not burn because there was still wax in it due to the unevenness of the candle burning. So the rim turned into a wick burning the wax still in the bowl. We woke up to our smoke alarms going off and saw the entire bowl in huge flames on our kitchen island. The flames were at least two feet high. If the candle had been on a flammable surface instead of our marble island and if there had been anything else around it, there would have been a major fire in the house. My husband used a towel and grabbed the flaming bowl to put it in the sink. He thought the whole bowl was on fire and didn't realize there was still wax in it. The wax spilled over the edge and burned his hand as he was dropping the burning candle bowl into the sink to put it out. This product is inherently unsafe due to the uneven burning of the wicks causing it to be extremely difficult to tell if the candle is still lit, and the wood container that easily catches fire.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury and a significant fire hazard, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the product's inherent design flaws leading to uneven burning and fire risk.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Queen-size Siena Mattress on Amazon.com. Siena is a sub-brand of Resident Home, which manufactures the Nectar mattress. Upon setting up the mattress, I noticed a warning that said, 'Do not remove the zippers. Property damage, etc., can occur if zippers are removed.' It was something along those lines. I knew this mattress contained fiberglass as a fire retardant and had researched numerous articles stating it is safe as long as I don't remove the outer cover. I never removed the cover. After purchasing it, I started having a stuffy nose, and my cat began sneezing occasionally. I attributed this to seasonal changes. Occasionally, my skin itched, which I also thought was due to seasonal allergies. However, the new kitten my housemate adopted likes to run around the house. She went under my bed, and I saw crystal-like sharp material protruding from the bottom barrier of my Siena mattress. I immediately recognized it as fiberglass, having seen enough news and videos about it on social media. I used my phone's flashlight to inspect further and realized that fiberglass was poking through the barrier, with some fibers attached to the metal bed slats, etc. I also found these sharp materials on the fitted sheet, although not as much as on the bottom of my mattress. I contacted Siena but haven't heard back for a few days. They kept asking for my contact information but to no avail. I feel really frustrated. I've ordered a new mattress and will remove this one myself, hoping that Siena resolves the issue and arranges for its disposal. I know fiberglass is safe if the outer cover is well-reinforced, but it seems that's not the case with Siena's product. It appears to be a thin layer of rayon or polyester. It's frustrating that they continue using this material without diligent research and development, especially after class-action lawsuits concerning their sub-brand Nectar.
justification: The incident involves exposure to fiberglass causing minor health symptoms (stuffy nose, sneezing, itching) and property contamination, but no serious injury or death.

incident_description:

The light was not turned on until we had guests.  Within a few minutes of our guests turning the light on, they noticed a strong electrical burning smell.  We searched the room for the cause of the smell and found the EcoSmart light was the source.  We unplugged the light and found the light bulb very hot to the touch.  Once the bulb had cooled down, we removed it and observed the base had blistered and the plastic bulb had begun to melt.

We tested the light using both an incandescent bulb (100-watt) and another EcoSmart (14-watt) bulb and there were no issues, indicating the first EcoSmart light bulb was defective.

While there we no injuries from this event, we were fortunate the light was immediately turned off and the bulb removed before a potential fire occurred.

I tried to contact Home Depot to let them know of the issue with this product, but my attempts to identify a contact point at Home Depot's Atlanta headquarters was not successful; I was referred back to the local store and was not confident the store would elevate this problem to the appropriate personnel.
justification: The incident involved a defective bulb causing a burning smell and melting, but no injuries or fire occurred.

incident_description: In December of 2017 I purchased a Zinus Memory Foam Green Tea 12 inch Mattress from Amazon. This mattress has a 10 year warranty, creating the expectation from me that the materials and supplies it was manufactured with would be safe and functional for that warranty period. I was fully aware that the mattress had a fire retardant fire sock inside that contained fiberglass and that the mattress cover should not be removed. At no point since I have purchased this mattress have I ever attempted to unzip, remove, or otherwise alter or open up the mattress cover. The mattress has been well cared for and has seen standard usage, for sleep at night but is otherwise untouched. The exterior cover at a glance does not visually show any signs of extreme wear, tears, openings, or any other type of large damage that could allow the fiberglass from the fire sock to escape. However, a few days ago I discovered small fiberglass particles on my bedframe, under my bed, on my sheets, pillows comforter, and nearby rug. Upon further inspection it appears that smaller fiberglass particles are breaking down and somehow escaping from the mattress cover. The mattress cover itself is covered in them. This will likely be hours of cleaning, and IÃÂve now been exposed to fiberglass without my knowledge. Over the past year IÃÂve been experiencing unexplained and novel skin and scalp sensitivity. IÃÂve tried different laundry soaps, shampoos, body washes, lotions, etc. to no avail. I now believe it is quite possible this sensitivity could be attributed to unintended and unknown fiberglass exposure over a long period of time as it slowly and unnoticeably escaped from the mattress cover, despite following ALL manufacturer recommendations and warnings. (Again, I have never removed or attempted to remove  the mattress cover.) It should also be noted that I believe it is irresponsible and potentially dangerous that Zinus uses a zipper on their mattress cover. I recognize there are warning tags in place and measures to discourage opening the zipper, but, its a zipper. Consumers recognize zippers as a way to open things. Regardless, I have never opened the mattress cover and was still exposed to the fiberglass inside.
justification: The incident describes unintended fiberglass exposure leading to skin and scalp sensitivity, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
On June 22, 2023, we purchased the Dillon Wall Hugger in Dark Cherry Finish from The Futon Shop and received the frame on July 18, 2023. We put the frame together according to the manufacturer's written and video instructions; however, for a month or so, no one slept or sat on it because we were waiting on a shipment of a specialty futon mattress from another company.

The frame cracked in multiple areas within less than a week of our teenage son of ~160 lbs. sleeping on it. On September 4, 2023, I called The Futon Shop to notify them of the situation, stating that my child could have been seriously injured. I followed up on the call by emailing photos of the defective frame and asking for a refund.

On September 6, 2023, The Futon Shop promised me via email, "I am having the manufacturer ship you a new reinforced queen body for your frame. This will have zero issues and be made stronger. I apologize for the inconvenience and will send you tracking info for this once it ships out."

I understood this meant the manufacturer would fix the problem and send me a new, safe, reinforced frame. They did not.

Instead, The Futon Shop shipped, from their warehouse, the slatted part of the frame only despite the original frame having cracked in multiple areas and not just the slatted ones. The Futon Shop had the manufacturer send me four additional small slats in a separate shipment that I am supposed to attach to the slatted part of the frame to "fix" the problem. The instructions included with the four slats are poorly written, lack sufficient details, and appear hastily written. According to The Futon Shop, I am supposed to remove the original slatted part only from the defective frame and then attach the slatted piece with additional slats to the cracked main bed frame. I never agreed to do this. It does not solve the problem and is, therefore, unacceptable. I asked for a refund, which The Futon Shop refused, and my bank is now seeking on my behalf.

The Futon Shop has admitted in writing to us and the [REDACTED] that the frame is defective. Despite this admission, The Futon Shop refuses to acknowledge that the frame is a potential safety hazard, provide an adequate solution to fix the problem, or recall the product and notify past and future customers of the safety concerns. On October 4, 2023, The Futon Shop emailed me, "I understand your concerns with the frame breaking. This is not a safety hazard it is a warranty issue with the futon frame."

Neither The Futon Shop nor the manufacturer has provided proof that they adequately researched the safety issue and that me adding the four small slats to the defective frame will make it "zero issues and be made stronger." It is not my job as their customer to fix their defective product, and I will NOT risk our son's or anyone else's safety.

Please investigate this situation. It is a safety hazard that neither The Futon Shop nor the manufacturer will address. I will provide any additional details. Thank you for your time and attention.
justification: The frame cracked but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as similar incidents are possible given the defect.

incident_description:
I have a Casper Essential Full Mattress that I purchased in fall of 2017. It had a fire resistant "fire sock" that covers the mattress. This fire sock contains fiberglass, which is supposed to be securely encased so that it does not escape. However, after sleeping on the mattress for 6 years, I discovered that it has begun leaking fiberglass fibers. 

I had it kept in a waterproof anti-bedbug mattress protector for the last 3 years, which I removed on 10/2/2023 in order to wash it. Afterwards, I discovered fiberglass fibers all over my bedroom, and I realized that the fire sock has begun breaking down and that my mattress protector has previously been containing them. The surface of the mattress was covered in shiny strands poking out of it.

There are a few injuries I've sustained as a result of this. My skin is very irritated from where it's been embedded with fiberglass, and even after cleaning I am constantly itchy. I breathed in fiberglass and have developed a sore throat, cough, and sneezing. My voice sounds rough, like I've been smoking (I have never smoked). I've also experienced eye irritation.

In addition to the injuries, I have had to upend my entire bedroom to clean out the hazardous fiberglass. I've also had to throw away all of my bedding and much of my clothing. I am still in the process of cleaning up, but I may need to throw away some upholstered furniture in the room. Of course I am also getting rid of the mattress.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including skin irritation, respiratory issues, and eye irritation, but no death.

incident_description:
Fiberglass Contamination in Casper Mattresses: A Call for Consumer Protection

Introduction:
On Saturday, June 16th, 2023, an alarming incident occurred when an attempt to clean one of our Casper mattresses led to the discovery of fiberglass contamination in our home. The fiberglass emerged from the deteriorated fire sock situated below the mattress cover, unbeknownst to us, as no mention of such material was provided in the product description at the time of purchase. This report details the events that unfolded, the adverse effects we experienced, and the subsequent actions taken to address the contamination, with a specific focus on the concerning emergence of fiberglass from the deteriorated fire sock. Furthermore, it raises concerns about the safety implications and the need for proper consumer protection in the bedding industry.

Background:
Our Casper mattress was purchased on November 7th, 2016, and had been used by both our family members and guests. Little did we know that the mattress contained fiberglass, which was only discovered during the attempted cleaning process.

Discovery of Fiberglass Contamination:
Upon following the mattress tag's instructions for hand washing the mattress cover, fiberglass particles began to emanate from the fire sock beneath it. These particles were found to be widespread in the air and had settled on various surfaces, resembling sparkling fibers.

Adverse Effects and Health Impact:
The fiberglass contamination affected not only our household items but also had adverse effects on our beloved pets. One of our dogs experienced a severe skin reaction, leading to intense scratching and now has large scabs on both sides of his neck. Consequently, it became evident that urgent measures were required to mitigate the contamination's impact on our living environment and health. Additionally, we have scheduled doctorÃÂs visits for our family to see what potential risks we can possibly face down the road from inhaling these fibers in the air. Furthermore, this has affected our mental health as we are now hyper-vigilant of any kind of fiber lingering in the air or on any surface. This is an experience that will forever impact us.

Response from Casper:
Despite promptly reporting the issue to Casper and their quality assurance team, we received no satisfactory response or appropriate action to address the contamination. The lack of accountability and responsibility necessitated us to take matters into our own hands and develop a cleanup plan.

Cleanup Measures Taken:
To minimize further contamination, we employed plastic bags to store our clothes and remove all other items such as rugs, curtains, lamps, bedding, dog beds, porous furniture, and basically anything that canÃÂt be cleaned. Additionally, we hired a professional carpet cleaning company to clean the affected carpets. However, it soon became evident that these measures were insufficient, and the contamination persisted. As a result, we had no choice but to replace the entire carpet, which was also impacting our familyÃÂs and petsÃÂ well-being.

HVAC and Air Ducts Cleaning:
Recognizing the extent of the contamination, we took the additional step of renting and purchasing air scrubbers to contain the spread of fiberglass particles in the air. Furthermore, we have scheduled an HVAC and air duct cleaning to ensure the elimination of any remaining contaminants.

Concerns Regarding Product Safety and Recalls:
Despite, CasperÃÂs knowledge of this problem with mattresses that have tags that offer instructions for removing and how to wash the mattress cover Casper has not issued a recall for their mattresses. Consumers with these tags will not know of the presence of fiberglass until they have removed the mattress cover and thus exposed this material. Although they claim that the Consumer Product Safety Commission deems the "continuous filament" fiberglass used in textiles and fire-resistant barriers as non-hazardous, we firmly believe that such material should not be placed directly below a mattress cover. This issue poses risks to consumers' quality of life and potentially threatens their health and safety.

Conclusion:
The incident involving fiberglass contamination in our Casper mattress raises significant concerns about consumer protection and the need for stringent safety measures in the bedding industry. We advocate for a thorough investigation into the presence of fiberglass in Casper mattresses and a proactive recall process to safeguard consumers from potential health risks with these tags that offer washing instructions for the mattress cover. It is our hope that this report will contribute to ensuring safer products and responsible practices within the mattress manufacturing industry.
justification: The incident caused severe skin reactions in pets and potential health risks to humans, indicating injury but no death.

It is my hope that you can move to quickly have this product removed from the shelves. It would be very surprising if customers have not been injured by this product. Fortunately it did by the next morning and I called to speak with a Manager to ensure that they were aware and to warn others.

incident_description: I received a new leather chair from Wayfair over Christmas. After assemblling and sitting in it the first week of January, my back started burning and blistering. Photos of my back showed the rash matching where my shirted back contacted the leather. I discontinued using the chair, and researched chemicals. Dimethyl Fumarate (DMF) is a common biocide put into dessicant packets by Chinese furniture and leather goods manufacturer to prevent mold. BUT, they don't label the packets as containing DMF, or anything. DMF was banned by the EU in 2009 for this exact chemical allergen problem, which they called 'Toxic Sofa'. DMF also was labelled the 2011 Allergen of the Year by the [REDACTED]. As a Disabled Veteran I contacted my PCP at the VA asking to see a dermatologist and explaining I am reacting to DMF, something of which the doctors aren't aware. They told me to go to Urgent Care. First visit, misdiagnosed as inflamation. Prescription did not solve problem. About ten days later, with a worsening condition, I went to Urgent Care again, misdiagnosis was bacterial infection. Antibiotics didn't help. Problem got worse. Begging the VA for a dermatology consult, their backlog forced me to go to the Emergency Room. Misdiagnosis: Scabies. Prescription made it even worse. Each of the preceding doctors had NOT known about DMF and misdiagnosed me. Only the following dermatologist knew it was a chemical allergen reaction and prescribed correctly (3 weeks after I first sought treatment).  Recovery is still ongoing. Through conversations with others, I have identified two other people who suffered the same allergen reaction to new leather furniture. This isn't just about Wayfair. They took their chair back. It's about ALL leather furniture and shoes being shipped from China using DMF as a biocide and where the chemical use is NOT identified, nor is there any health warning.  Read this: [REDACTED]  and this  [REDACTED]  and this video describes the problem in detail (26:00) [REDACTED}.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (burning and blistering) due to exposure to DMF, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as similar cases are identified but not widespread.

The first box - that came apart was damaged more than the second box. Note that I continued to try to use the second set out of each box but even the male side of the second set will not work so I think the male side may have  some damage somehow too but I can't see it. Bottom line - First box - first set in the box could have shocked me (maybe not super likely but it still could have), second set does not work. Second box - first set had similar (but less) damage to the female plug end, second set worked ok, but I am taking them back at this point because I don't want them. Note - I did not apply any force to these plugs and I did not step on anything. This came out of the box damaged. I have photos. I suspect there are alot more like this at costco and believe it is likely someone could get injured because the female end came just come right apart due to damage. - if it was sitting as mine was in the box. 

To be clear: I did NOT get injured . I did not touch the bare copper copper because it is sort of protected even when apart, but your mind doesn't exactly go to the string being plugged in when you are testing it and the thing totally comes apart in your hand.
justification: The incident involved a potential electrical hazard but no actual injury occurred, and the issue was identified before harm could happen.

I feel that this situation is particular to this curved arm chair and the chair should probably be discontinued or at least have a warning notice of the possibility of a dangerous situation with a serious fall on exiting the chair.

incident_description:
A bedroom set by International Furniture Direct, Rustic Light-Finish Collection was purchased from American Furniture Warehouse (AFW) on Thursday, September 8, 2022. A partial delivery of furniture was made on Tuesday, September 13, 2022, which included a bedframe, tv stand, upright chest of drawers, and two nightstands. We noticed immediately that there were sharp corners on the furniture that were potentially dangerous, especially the chest of drawers that was at eye level for me, the short female, and the bedframe footboard, which sticks out much further than the mattress and rails, to match the headboard. There was also some "distressing" on the tv stand that I felt was too sharp, especially with a newborn in the family who would be pulling up and walking within the year.I immediately called Customer Service about the sharp edges on the tv stand, and AFW agreed to send out a technician on Saturday, September 17 to make an evaluation as to whether that piece was damaged or distressed.  The technician said it was part of the distressing, but said that if I was concerned about my new granddaughter that he could fill in the two sharp "chips" on the tv stand with epoxy, which he expertly did, matching the stone color of the trim. While he was working, I mentioned that I was likewise concerned about the sharp corners on the furniture, because my husband had cut his leg on the footboard the day after the set was delivered, (Sept. 14, 2022), while it was dark in the room. The technician said that this particular set was very popular, and that he himself had one, or a similar set, and had softened the edges of his own footboard. Today, Saturday, September 24, 2022, my husband walked into the corner of the chest of drawers in the dark, and I hurt him say "ouch" and knew from where he was that he had hit the chest, which, if I had done it, would have injured my eye.  We had just put a rubber bumper on the corner of the chest of drawers, thankfully, so it did not cut. I am going to contact customer service and advise them of this issue of sharp corners today, but this is an issue which has potential to injure or ruin an eye, or severely injure another body part on an individual, depending on their height. I am very concerned about my grandchild putting out her eye on the sharp corner of the low footboard or injure her mouth or teeth when she starts pulling up and standing. This popular rustic set has the potential of injuring many others too. Even if the company agrees to modify my set, I believe this to be a public safety issue that AFW, IFD and governing U.S. agencies should look into quickly.
Another issue I noticed is that the Country of Origin tag was attached to my furniture when delivered, but was not attached to the set in the showroom. We had no idea that the set was made in Mexico. The name, American Furniture Warehouse seems to be a misnomer, as it led me to believe the furniture it sold to be made in America, but the IFD website says, "made in North-America," showing the U.S., Mexican and Canadian flags.  The fact that the tag, "Hecho en Mexico" is not on the showroom floor furniture speaks volumes, though.
It seems that most safety rules cover furniture to be used by children, but this set will be "accessed" by children. If the set is already hurting adults, a child who is shorter may suffer even more devastating injuries.
Another issue was the headboard had a crack which went partway through the right top post, and was sharp. I showed this to the technician when he arrived on September 17, and told him it looked as if the post had been previously repaired with epoxy, which split.  He did not believe it had been epoxied, and said the difference in sound when tapped was due to the piece of wood separating from the piece underneath it. The headboard and the rest of the bedframe was replaced on Tuesday September 20. I had reported this issue the day of delivery, September 13, the day before injury to my husband's leg from hitting the footboard in the dark.
The manufacturer does not allow contact with them, but rather refer to the AFW point of sale in the U.S. A problem with complaining to AFW is that they admonish with a 15% restocking fee on any item returned. I am concerned that this will be the issue with this set, because they have so far replaced/repaired any damaged item.
justification: The incident describes injuries from sharp furniture edges, including a cut leg and potential for eye injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to multiple occurrences and the presence of a newborn.

This occurred in an apartment I purchased and have lived in for approximately 3 months, which underwent a full remodel prior to my moving in, so while I am not certain of the exact date of purchase and installation, it was within the last 12 months.
I at first assumed that it must have been improperly installed by the contractor, because it seemed implausible such a dangerous product would be on the market, but when I began doing research I saw scores of reviews and warnings from people who reported the exact same thing, happening anywhere from months to 10 years after installation, with no warning. 
I was particularly alarmed because despite the sizeable number of one-star reviews, often, it seems, this doesn't happen, or hasn't happened yet, the reviews are mostly positive and the product is highly rated on most websites. I am concerned particularly about anyone with small children or pets either purchasing this or having it already installed in their home and not knowing the danger.

incident_description:
My disabled wife got trapped in an electric reclining chair and was unable to get out of it due to a failure of its battery backup system.

The chair is electric powered lift chair/recliner and it provides for a wide range of positions, from tilting forward and lifting up to assist in physically getting out of the chair, to an extreme recline position that allows the user to elevate their feet above the level of their heads.  It only operates electrically, cannot be operated manually, and has an 9-volt battery backup that is meant to provide enough power to return the chair to a normal upright position in the event of a power interuption.  On one occasion the power to the chair was interrupted while my wife was in an extreme recline position.  To her distress, the battery backup failed to provide power to reposition the chair, and my wife, who has very limited mobility, was trapped and unable to get out of the chair.  In my opinion, this constitutes a safety hazard, particularly for the disabled, who likely are prime customers for this chair.

After contacting the retailer, then having a service technician change out numerous components of the chair in an unsuccessful attempt to repair it, I contacted the chair manufacturer.  After speaking with someone in the engineering department, I was told that they were aware that the 9-volt battery backup system didnÃÂt work, but that they would have an improved lithium battery backup system coming out on future models.  I asked about any plans to warn existing owners of the chair and retrofitting them with the newer backup system and was told that they had none.  They said they had notified retailers about the problem, but my retailer said he had never received such notice and was still selling the current line of lift chairs believing that the current battery backup system worked.

Getting trapped in such a chair is frightening, uncomfortable, and potentially dangerous for anyone with limited mobility.  I think the manufacturer should notify each chair owner of the problem and supply them with the new lithium battery backup system.  Alternatively, they could recall all the chairs and issue refunds.

My wifeÃÂs experience seems very similar to that described in Incident Report [REDACTED] from 11/10/2020.
justification: The incident caused distress and potential danger due to the failure of the battery backup system, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:

The 1st chair I received had low power to it, when using the "lift" position the chair elevated and immediately dropped back down to the base
The 2nd chair I received was in a damaged box and had a few marks on it.  Once put together and trying it out, without a person in it.. It functioned properly. However that was only 2 months ago and now there is no power/remote doesn't work. 
Reclining lift chair
I was using the product to sit in
I reclined the chair, watched  TV for a bit and went to get up for bed, no power to the chair.. I tried pushing the foot rest down with my legs after seeing there was no power.. It became obvious that the chair isn't intended to go down manually.. I used my phone to check online for a solution and did not find one.. I could not sit up from the position the chair was in, I sat down in the chair at 8pm and wanting to go to bed around 10:30pm.. I could not get out of the chair until 11am the next morning(today) with the help of my sister and nurses aide.. It was terribly frightening and painful due to my disability.. I cannot stand up without the Lift function of the chair.  I attempted to get off over the side of the chair but was unable to reach my wheelchair from the reclining position.. so for safety i had to stay there..
justification: The incident caused physical pain and distress due to the inability to exit the chair, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred twice with similar products, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).
