incident_description:
At 7PM or so on July 5th, 2022 - I received a package from [REDACTED]. I had ordered a Molblly King Size Mattress, 10 inch premium cooling-gel memory foam from Amazon. As I was following the instructions on how to open up the mattress, which is rolled and air sealed - the instructions advise you to avoid scissors or a knife for opening. Instead they provide a plastic opening tool which contains a razor blade. As I followed the instructions using the tool provided, the plastic shattered and the razor blade went inward cutting my middle finger deeply. I myself was using the product with  a friend who was watching. The product was being used as instructed, and the plastic tool shattered, causing the internal razor blade to cut open the side of my middle finger. The cut was deep - but fairly narrow given it came straight on from the razor blade. I determined that stitches were likely not going to help, so took self care at home. It took nearly 30 minutes for the bleeding to stop enough to apply disinfectant and bandages. 
I was shocked at how flimsy the tool provided was given that it contained a razor. I have kept the broken tool and taken pictures of both the injury and mattress, packaging, and instructions. 
This will certainly happen again if something is not done to improve the quality of the manufacturers tools and I would be genuinely shocked if I am the only one this has happened to. Please take some action to ensure this is resolved with the manufacturer and does not happen again to someone else. While my injury was not serious enough to require a hospital visit/stitches, the next one may be.    

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut requiring self-care, indicating an injury without the need for medical intervention.

incident_description: Our Tuft and Needle Original mattress spread fiberglass all over our home. We unzipped the cover to spot clean as directed on the label. The label did not indicate that any part of the mattress contained fiberglass, however the fire sock under the cover consists of a type of fiberglass that easily spreads once the mattress is unzipped. Using a flashlight we saw hundreds of tiny shards all over the nearby furniture , bedding, clothes, our toddlerÃÂs toys, and almost every surface in the room. There were also shards all over the house including in our toddlerÃÂs room that had spread in the time between when we unzipped the cover and when we realized what had happened. In the weeks since this occurred we have had itchy skin and are concerned about long term effects of breathing the fiberglass dust from our bedding and clothes.  It has taken us over 60 hours to vacuum and wipe down all the affected surfaces. We tried to launder our clothes separately as directed by the company, however we had to throw out many items as they were too contaminated to clean effectively. The company had our old mattress removed and is sending us a replacement of a newer product that does not contain fiberglass. We feel lucky to have found the contamination relatively early and limit the spread and hope this doesnÃÂt happen to anyone else .
justification: The incident caused itchy skin and potential long-term health concerns from fiberglass exposure, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific conditions required for fiberglass spread.

incident_description:

As I moved the cart, the front castered wheel partially collapsed. The unit lurched diagonally forward, dumping any unsecured items to rain down on me or crash on the floor. The castered wheels screw into threaded silver metal caps on the ends of the four legs. The silver caps appear to merely be pressed onto the four legs. So as the front leg began to fail, the silver cap bent and then became dislodged from the leg. There were no injuries to me, although some of my audio equipment may have been damaged.
I contacted the company in City of Industry CA and exchanged several emails with their representative, who now claims to be the owner. She had repeatedly denied that what happened to me was possible. She continually asserts that the silver metal threaded ring is, in fact, merely decorative, and is not a structural element. She has told me the threaded screw which connects the caster threads into the leg of the unit, not the threaded silver cap. I sent her photos demonstrating the opposite. The metal cap is obviously threaded, and it is disfigured by being bent by the weight of my stereo gear.  She continues to tell me I am mistaken. She offered to send me a new base, which apparently has been redesigned, to replace mine. I have not taken her up on that offer. I think the company should contact current owners, inform them of a potentially dangerous situation, and offer to replace their base units as well.
justification: No injuries occurred, but equipment was damaged and the incident involved a structural failure of the rack.

On Thursday, 1/13, I washed the removable zippered cover of our 4-year old Casper mattress, which then resulted in fiberglass covering our sheets and four loads of laundry I subsequently did. We didn't know we had an issue until the middle of the night when we woke up itching and discovered glittering shards of glass all over our sheets, which we had been sleeping in.

Those four loads of laundry included my 3-month old daughter's cloth diapers, our clothes and towels. Our washer and dryer seem to be contaminated and continuing to deposit glass on other loads. We are unable to wash our clothes until we replace the washer and dryer, since it continues to deposit glass shards on our belongings. I have found fiberglass anywhere that our laundry touched, including our couch, coffee table, our bedroom rug, a quilt we lay our daughter down to play, and the route from the bedroom to the laundry, and all over the laundry room. We have thrown out anything unsalvageable, including our sheets and towels, and for the remaining items, we have been lint-rolling painstakingly. The glass on our belongings is one thing -- but it's another thing to know that microscopic fiberglass is floating in the air going into our infant's eyes and lungs. This is a safety issue.

On the Casper website, they "recommend" spot cleaning the mattress topper but there is NO WARNING to not wash it completely. In addition, it should not be removable by zipper if this is a KNOWN ISSUE.

I began contacting Casper on Friday, 1/14, but have had no meaningful response since then.
justification: The incident caused itching and potential exposure to fiberglass, particularly concerning for an infant's health, indicating injury.

incident_description:
[REDACTED]
Thursday, July 30, 2020
Consumer Products Safety Commission 4330 East West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814


[REDACTED]

This is to report the catastrophic failure of a tempered glass and steel table. The table was similar to, but larger than, product T644KOH (Whose instruction I attach). I think I bought the table at [REDACTED] about 10 years ago.

The failure appears to be deterioration of plastic (nylon?) clips that hold the unit together. The top collapsed and the tempered glass shattered. The steel frame remained intact.Fortunately no one was present during the collapse -  there were no injuries. But the danger is obvious.

During the clean up we examined all parts. All the glass was shattered to shards smaller than 2 inches (5 cm). All metal parts and fasteners were intact and tight. All the plastic parts were brittle and often broken. (Ironic twist-the plastic was used for decorative caps over the fasteners and all these declarative caps fragmented when we attempted to remove them. This left fragments blocking the allen-wrench holes, which slowed disassembly). Since most plastic parts broke before, during or after the failure it is impossible to say where the failure occurred. The most likely point of initial failure is one of the plastic clips that hold to the outer steel rim and accept the steel leg. Failure of this clip would allow the glass top to fall inward and strike the steel leg. Since the glass top was under load from objects on the table breakage is to be expected.

The product was exposed to sunlight. The product was used both indoors and outdoors. The product may have been out side during rain, hot sun and freezing. The product was never exposed to chemicals beyond water and household surface cleaner. None of these uses were warned against in any of the packaging.

I own three additional similar products. I am dismantling all of them. I recommend a consumer warning! Imagine a child on or under the table at failure.

[REDACTED]
justification: The table collapsed but no one was present, resulting in no injuries, though the potential for harm is evident.

incident_description:
After product purchase and first use in May 2020, I had a severe asthma attack from the smell deriving form the footwarmer. I let the product sit in the garage for a 1.5 year and tried it again January 12, 2022 in the hope that the product was now 'seasoned.' But again after reuse, I had another severe asthma attack from the smell of the footwarmer after starting it only a few minutes. Note: I did not have an asthma attack for many years. 
It appears the product is made from crumb rubber granulate (CRG) produced from end of life tires (ELTs). 
According to the EPA, benzene, mercury, styrene-butadiene, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and arsenic, among several other chemicals, heavy metals and carcinogens, have been found in tires. Studies have found that crumb rubber can emit gases that can be inhaled. CRGs contain chemicals such as benzene, which has been associated with leukemia, and another carcinogen known as trichloroethylene (TCE), a volatile organic compound that can affect the immune and central nervous systems, liver and kidneys. In addition to asbestos-related illnesses and various types of cancer, medical research has shown links between industrial toxins and respiratory problems such as asthma, emphysema or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); auto-immune conditions such as multiple sclerosis (MS), lupus, or sarcoidosis. 
Source: [REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes severe asthma attacks triggered by the product, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as it occurred twice under specific conditions.

But as I was working to get the cabinet settled into my home, I noticed it was excessively dusty and that the dust was not dirt colored, it was paint dust colored.

I feel that the paint should be tested for lead.  I have found the item on their website as SKU: 563080 - White Stone Wood Cabinet With Drawers.  It is the white paint on the inside of it that is chalking really bad.
justification: The incident involves potential lead exposure from deteriorating paint, which could cause injury if not addressed, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: LED replacement light tube installed to replace a fluorescent 4 foot tube.  The led light burned up at one end four months after replacing a fluorescent tube light.  It reached a temperature that melted the glass tube.  The two prong electric contact end melted off the light tube.  The internal components reached a temperature that evaporated them.     This resulted in the hot light tube connecter end melting off the end of the tube.  The [REDACTED] light fixture connected to the damaged light end melted, plastic and metal.  The connector end along with melted glass and metal rained down on the light diffuser under the light.  Only the diffuser and the fixture itself prevented a fire.  The product has no warning on the light tube of any potential fire hazards.  Another led light tube in a different fixture was found to have overheated at one end at the same time.  My wife bought the tubes while I away and installed the lights.  I can only reference the website since the fire for the installation instructions.  The website does mention that lights must be installed in a fixture with a compatible ballast.  There is an obscure ballast chart with no link to a legible ballast chart.  There is on the website a testimonial of the product being used successfully with a non-compatible ballast.   The website has no mention of a fire hazard with a non-compatible ballast, just the testimonial that non-compatible ballasts will allow the light to work.  I would have expected a warning on the website and the package of a fire hazard.  A warning large enough that someone not familiar with ballasts would recognize that there is a fire hazard.   I will attach a print of the webpage.

I am writing to the CPSC  to help me resolve a situation with a faulty product sold by Home Depot that may have ended in tremendous property damage and loss of my life.

Home depot should not blindly accept a certifier's reaffirmed safety rating when they are liable.
The lamp must be labeled to be unplugged when not in use. A question remains -will the heat of the bulb when plugged in fully evaporate the moisture that comes out if its really humid? At a minimum it must be labeled appropriately.
[REDACTED] was satisfied with the assessment giving no extra thought. Was she not even thinking that Intertek denial was due to conflict of interest? When I explained that the media should know  so that innocent people  are educated about the dangers  she was unconcerned and in the last email told me good luck in my endeavors. Completely unacceptable.
This should be a wake up call to home depot to prevent a catastrophe. Possibly home or life loss? I hope that we can prevent future loss for someone else. incident_description: July 10 we received a cabinet that we ordered from Wayfair.  Its purpose was to a computer cabinet for my husband's computer.   It came assembled.  When we unpacked it, we noticed a scent, but we thought it was from the packaging and it would dissipate.  It was delivered at 10 am that morning.  By evening, it had not dissipated.  We opened three or four windows and already had out ceiling fan running.  The smell continued for days.  I started noticing that I was getting headaches almost every day which was unusual.  My husband began having what we though was a severe allergy attack.  After the second week, we went on vacation.  While at the beach, all our symptoms disappeared.  When we returned that first week of August, my husband's terrible allergies returned within hours.  The smell had filled the house while we were away.  We returned on a Saturday evening.  By Tuesday, I was starting to have the terrible allergies too, my headaches had returned and my 13 year started complaining of having bad allergies.   We all continued to get worse.  We bought an air purifier next day in the middle of the week and while it helped us, it did not resolve the problem.  We put the cabinet outside Saturday morning and by the afternoon, our sinuses had cleared.  I did not have a headache that evening.  I have reported this to Wayfair, but I want someone to know that this product has the potential to do this to others.  I am pretty sure that it was mass produced.
justification: The incident caused headaches and severe allergy symptoms, indicating physical harm, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the issue persisted but may not affect all users.

incident_description: I ordered an "Oily waste can" on Walmart.com from the seller Zoro that was advertised as being OSHA compliant (the listing says "Standards: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.108"), however, when I received it, it was clearly not actually properly designed as an Oily waste can nor could it be OSHA compliant for this purpose, because an actual oily waste can is supposed to be airtight in the receptacle bin (to prevent spontaneous combustion fires from oily rags- that is its main purpose), and this had huge holes at the joints for the lever mechanism in the receptacle area, making it actually even less airtight than a standard kitchen waste can, for example. The listing is https://www.walmart.com/ip/EAGLE-935FL-Oily-Waste-Can-10-Gal-Poly-Red/19272302 It is supposedly by the brand Eagle, but I have no idea if it really is by them, and I would suggest investigating the seller ZORO and Walmart themselves first. However, this kind of Eagle Oily waste can is advertised on other sites like [REDACTED] and Eagle's site, but again I don't know if the problem is that this is a counterfeit product from Zoro/Walmart, or if Eagle's can itself is really made this way and if they are therefore making false (and dangerous) claims.
justification: The product is non-compliant with advertised safety standards, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a sofa from Campaign and it arrived on June 3, 2020. On March 6, 2021, the bottom of the sofa dropped out from under my husband while he was sitting on it. The bottom of the sofa is a steel rectangle that rests on four ~1.5 inch pegs (two in front and two in back). It is held in place by a beam that runs across the front of the sofa. The beam is made out of foam wrapped in fabric. Over time, the foam beam started to rotate forward allowing the steel frame to slide off the back peg on one side, causing my husband to fall through. He caught himself on the arm of the sofa and was not injured, but easily could have been if he were not so quick to catch himself. We also have kittens who sleep and play under the sofa often and they could have been killed (but were fortunately not under it at the time). We use the sofa for sitting/lounging, nothing out of the ordinary. WeÃÂve never approached the weight limit of the sofa (listed as 1,800 pounds on CampaignÃÂs site) with ourselves or the guests weÃÂve had sit on it.

On March 6, I contacted CampaignÃÂs customer service telling them what happened. They never replied. Around 3 weeks later, I detailed what happened in a product review on their website. They never published my review. On March 29, they wrote to me: 

ÃÂ Hi [REDACTED] ,

We just came across your review and are sorry to hear you have had some issues with your sofa.

It sounds like the foam on the front beam has come loose allowing the seat tray to slide out. We are currently redesigning the front beam so that this issue can never happen again. We should have the new front beam available by June and would be happy to send you one then.

In the meantime to avoid another collapse can you please remove the cover and secure the foam to the front beam by using some tape or even zip ties for better hold. 

Hope this helps, please let us know if there is anything else you need.

Best,
[REDACTED]ÃÂ

I replied that I would like the new beam sent to me and provided my shipping address. On June 15, I wrote:

ÃÂ Hi [REDACTED],

Will the replacement front beam still be available this month? 

Thanks,
[REDACTED]ÃÂ

They replied:
ÃÂ Hi [REDACTED],

We apologize again for the issues with your front beam. Unfortunately we probably won't have the new front beam restocked until August. 

As soon as we get them we will send one to you and update you with tracking once it's on the way. Hope this helps, please let us know if there is anything else you need. 

Best,
[REDACTED]ÃÂ
justification: The incident caused the sofa to collapse, but no injury occurred as the husband caught himself. However, the potential for injury or death was present, especially for the kittens.

incident_description:
Using a ceiling light fixture. Semi-flush: Model 5717-EB. Installed for approximately 1 year. All 3, 60 W bulbs blew out simultaneously. Noticed upon removal of bulbs, device was 'hot' to the touch although had not been on for an extended period of time. Removed bulbs. Turned on switch and fixture was 'making noise'. Decided to remove fixture instead of replacing bulbs to trouble shoot the circuit. Removed fixture and turned on switch and circuit was clear. Inspected fixture to find evidence of char on fixture wire. Took fixture apart to investigate damage. In removing parts, it was discovered internal wiring running down the center of the fixture was completely charred. Wiring at very top and bottom, good condition--no damage. While inspecting other lights for exterior signs of damage, as was noticed on failed device (we have another 4 of the same fixture installed),  we recognized that a fixture with the same set of 60 W bulbs were also running 'hot'. This style of bulbs are candelabra type and almost touch center fixture element running the power through the bottom. The fixture that failed is turned on daily for longer periods of time than the other 4 fixtures. I suspect that the permitted 60 W bulbs are generating too much heat and resulted in thermal degradation of the wiring and insulation. Suggest looking into whether or not use of 60 W bulbs should be permitted in this unit. Fixture is UL listed and purchase specifications note that it can use 3, 60 W bulbs.  I still have the fixture and took pictures. Warning to consumers should be issued if necessary to reduce wattage and bulb type.

https://www.crystoramalightinglights.com/product/crystorama-ascott-foyer-lighting-5717-eb.html
justification: The incident involved a fixture overheating and wiring charring, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a toddler bed made of "birch" wood manufactured by Ouef, Inc. and distributed by Fawn & Forest.  The bed was delivered on or about May 12, 2021.  From the moment I opened the box odors emanated from the wood and packaging materials.  This producted is manufactured in Latvia but supposedly is green gold certified with respect to toxity.  My eyes teared and my nose was bothered. I could not believe the odors coming from a product that a child is supposed to sleep in.  I contacted the company and was told that the odors would disappear over time and I should open windows, etc.  While the bed is described as eco-friendly, it has raw wood for the bed slats which I believe is plywood.  Plywood is a manufactured wood that uses resins.  There are also raw wood supports.  This raw wood has an obvious odor if I do not open the windows. The air in the room is very uncomfortable.  Even the "Birch" panels which are finished are made of slices of wood that are glued together which means their are resins in that wood as well. It has been three weeks so far of airing out this toddler bed and while the smell is less, it is still there.  I bought this bed for my grandson who is four  when he will be visiting in July and the bed is in the same room as the bed for my daughter and son and in law.
The room air is notably poor when the windows are closed.  I don't know what to do do as the item is non-refundable (it as 450.00) and more importantly the odors are concerning and, at the very least, unpleasant. I've ordered wood furniture in the past, and nothing like this has occurred.  Lastly, there are no stamps on the furniture indicating it is formaldehyde compliant and meets California requirements.  The manufacturer informed me that the product is green gold certified which I find hard to believe as it has notable odors--still after three weeks.  This is for a child to sleep on!
justification: The incident involves unpleasant odors and discomfort but no reported injury, and similar issues are possible with new furniture.

incident_description:
I purchased a floor lamp in Nov 2015.  I did not assemble and start using it until approximately end of Jan 2016.  I noticed after having it awhile it went thru light bulbs a lot faster than my previous floor lamps.  Over the past year it started blowing even more light bulbs. 
Today I had went to do laundry and came back and the light had turned off.  I assumed the bulb needed replaced so I went and got one.  When I put the bulb in and turned the switch it made an "electrifying noise" and burst at the same time.  Then I smelled burnt stuff.  I quickly unplugged the lamp.  
Upon removing light bulb I seen that it had blown an actual hole in the bottom of the bulb.  I then considered removing the cord and socket and just replacing the components.  Upon removing the top part of the socket I seen that it had even blown a hole thru the socket as well.  I do not feel as though this should have happened.  Had I not been home I feel as though it would have caught on fire.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning lamp that could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I was in the shower when all of a sudden the glass and trim fell on top of my head from the ceiling. Glass shards were everywhere at my bare feet!
justification: Glass and trim fell on the person's head, indicating potential injury from the impact and glass shards.

incident_description: Ordered a children's desk chair for my son at Crate and Barrel (kids' division, Crate and Kids).  It had just gotten delivered by the furniture delivery crew.  When I lifted the chair to take it upstairs, the bottom half (the base) detached from the seat and fell onto my foot.  It is solid metal and I need to get an x-ray to see if I broke my toe.
justification: The chair's base detached and caused a potential toe fracture, requiring medical attention.

incident_description: Pottery Barn Cameron 4 Shelf Bookcase mounting hardware failed. Plastic mounting hardware that was included with bookcase snapped. Mounting hardware was installed according to the directions provided. Luckily, I noticed the bookcase was pulled out from the wall farther than usual and saw that it was not secured to the wall. There were no injuries but there was a possibility of the bookcase falling on my child. Mounting hardware should be metal, not plastic that can easily break under pressure.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the tower linen cabinet has developed vertical cracks in between the drawers and the front left leg of the unit.  She stated that over 3 years it has got worse.   Caller stated that she noticed this incident about 1 year ago.  I first contacted support@wyndhamcollection.com in Oct 2020 & provided shots and didn't get a reply.  I attempted again in Jan. '21' and after emails & calls on Jan 14th I got an email stating it would be replaced.  The NEXT DAY, Jan. 15th I got an email rescinding the offer due to warranty issues.  (it was over 2 yrs old.)  The company was contacted about 6 months ago, they advised that the product was defective and would provide a replacement.  However, 1 day later they rescinded the offer and informed her that due the fact that the product was over 2 years old the offer did not stand.

Caller feels that due to these vertical cracks (especially in the left leg) into the 71 inch cabinet it poses a safety hazard. She stated that if it should tip over where it is located could trap someone in the bathroom or much worse kill someone.

The vertical crack in the left front leg is now 6" long.

incident_description:
Based on store owner's promise that his palm mattress has not used chemical bond and has no chemical smelling, we bought the mattress on 12/15/2020. My wife called her again on 12/17 and asked for talking with her boss however she refused and said boss was not at store and she wanted us to keep it for few days more to let the odour to vapour. On the third day of 12/18 my wife went to store in person and asked to see her boss. The store owner's wife lied and said that her boss was not at store. However a few minutes late, my wife found her boss was arguing with neighbor in the front of store for not shoveling snow on walk way so my wife asked the store owner again for returning and she even offered him $100 reduce in refund but he once more refused and gave my wife a tea set as a gift for compensation and said that chemical odour could go away if we could keep it for another few days more but my wife still insist in return and asked him for a plastic woven bag that can be used for wrapping up the palm mattress when return.

we have been experiencing watery eyes, burning sensations of eyes, nose and throat, coughing, wheezing, nausea, creaking and hoarse voice.

justification: The LED bulb failed and became very hot, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: There was a short in the Allen & Roth Latchbury 9-light chandelier (item 0810101 model  FD19-066-1) I purchased at Lowe's on Feb 1 2021. It caused sparks to fly when I screwed in the lightbulb to two of the sockets, and caused the circuit to trip. I used two different wattages of LED bulbs that were compatible with the fixture, both well below the max wattage requirement, and it happened each time. I reported the issue to Lowe's, who referred me to Lowes Private Brands Customer Support, who then referred me back to Lowe's consumer support, so I was sent in circles. The fixture was very clearly a fire hazard and posed a danger to my and my family's safety. I had to pay extra for the electricians to come back a second day and bring additional scaffolding, and Lowe's has been unwilling and unable to assist.

incident_description: The couch and love seat we purchased in 2018 has decorative furniture pins that line the edges and bottoms and arms of the couch. They come loose and pose a dangerous choking hazard. Not only are they sharp pins that could potentially stab but we have pulled 3 of them out of our baby's mouth! She dropped something on the floor in front of her chair, and when she leaned over to pick it up, the seat cushion, which is designed to aide individuals in standing up from a seated position, sent her catapulting out of her chair, and causing her to land on the floor below (on her face). She bruised her face and nose and had multiple bruises and severe soreness up and down her left side. Fortunately, she did not break anything.

incident_description: For Christmas, I bought my husband a supposedly "high end" chair made by AKRacing.  I paid nearly $500 for it.  My husband recently transitioned to working from home a few weeks before Christmas and he wanted a better chair than the one he had.  Three times now, this chair has tipped right over with him in it for absolutely no reason.  It just happened again about 15-20 minutes ago while I was standing right there.  He went to roll back to grab something off the printer and the chair fell right over.  He slammed his shoulder on our hardwood floor, the same shoulder that he had rotator cuff surgery on about 7 years ago, and now he is in severe pain as this fall caused damage to the repair that he had several years ago.  He is now facing additional surgery for a repair of the repair.  According to some reviews I have been reading, this is a very common issue with this brand of gaming chairs and the company refuses to acknowledge it or do anything about it and they blow every customer off who reports this issue to them. The arrogant little puke from AK Racing ([REDACTED]) who responded to my email accused me of sending "fake photos" and that the photos were not really of my chair, even though I sent about 5 or 6 photos AND sent my proof of purchase that shows my name, address, and the exact chair that I bought and when I bought it.  This guy accused me of trying to "scam" them.  I have never been so furious at a company in my life.

I got a replacement couch from Conn's HomePlus in Raleigh, NC for a couch that had a strong odor, gave me sinus problems, made my nose burn, I could taste it in the air, and it also affected my throat.  It smells bad like something dead.  However, the replacement couch has all the same issues.

My old couch was manufactured by

[REDACTED]

My new couch is manufactured by 

Jackson Furniture Industries, Inc
1014 Sycamore Drive
Myrtle, MS 38650

incident_description: Today I had the back of a gaming chair fail and collapse which caused the chair to topple backwards. This resulted in an injury and some damaged personal property. I bought the chair from Newegg.com (OMEGA-XI Gaming Chair from RESPAWN PRODUCTS by OFM Reclining) on 5/30/2020. I was the only individual using the chair at the time of the incident. The product was being used to sit at my computer desk to operate my computer. The product failure caused injury in the form of a sprained right wrist and hyperextension of the right arm. This also resulted in my beverage being spilled and damaging several computer peripherals (approx. $300 in personal property). The armrests are bolted to either side of the chair and their position is determined by the angle of the backrest. As the backrest reclines or rises the armrests adjust automatically per the orientation of the backrest. My backrest was set at a 100* angle. When the backrest failed it collapsed to almost a full 180* and the chair tipped backwards and to the right. When this occurred the space between the armrest and the seat bottom became very small. My right arm was caught and constricted during the collapse and fall of the chair. This resulted in a pop and sudden sharp pain in my right wrist as the full weight of the chair and myself fell onto it still caught in the armrest. All of this happened within a few seconds. This happened today and currently I still have considerable pain in my right wrist, right arm, right shoulder and neck.  I am consulting this with my physician.  I have sent correspondence to the individual seller and Newegg.com concerning this incident. Thank you for your time.

incident_description: Last Thursday, September 17, my cat got trapped in the power down reclining "feature" of this sofa.    There are three power motors on this sofa.  One operates a headrest, one operates a lumbar support, and another operates the "lean back" and footrest feature.  In addition to the three buttons that allow you to operate these features, there is a "power down" feature that brings everything on the sofa back to a sitting position.   That way you don't have to hold the button down to return to a seating position from laying down, and it brings the headrest and lumbar support back to "home base".    Last Thursday this feature caused my cat to be entrapped.   He was in pain and screaming!  I immediately hit the "up" switch to release him, but he was pretty sore for a few days.   I can only imagine what would happen if a child were playing under there and someone hit that button to power it down.     This power down button works like the old school garage doors, the ones that were trapping children under them and didn't bounce back when they hit something solid.    Luckily my cat is okay.  He's only been inside the house for a few months and is still getting used to everything.  I'm sure he was curious about what was under the sofa and I certainly didn't see him when I went to close it up.   I know this happened to "just a cat" but again, what if it was someone's child.   I really think someone should look into this.   I tried to contact the manufacturer, but the retail store I purchased this product from only said that they would forward my information to the supplier.
justification: The cat was injured and in pain, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) as the incident occurred once but could happen again under similar conditions.

incident_description:
This is the email I sent Rubbermaid on November 9, 2020 that has not received a response.
We purchased two 3' Rubbermaid shelves (#1863232), and appropriate tracks/brackets per the 4 step instructions on the label for the shelving unit.  In the 4 step instructions, the diagrams clearly indicate the use of single hole tracks and single hole brackets for the assembly (see attached photos).  Given the lack of ANY written information, we relied upon the diagrams for our purchase decisions.

After having someone install the units, my significant other began placing items on the shelf, with the result that the shelf fell down and broke her toe.

Upon reflection, I cannot see how you could recommend this mounting system for these shelves or for ANY application for that matter, as this system provides NO WAY to attach the shelves directly to the brackets. 

You do sell a double hole track and double hole bracket system for mounting, which allows for attaching the shelf directly to the bracket, BUT THAT IS NOT WHAT YOU SHOW IN YOUR INSTRUCTIONS!

Your instructions also show placing the track and bracket no more than approximately 1" from the end of the shelf, which is also EXTREMELY DANGEROUS without connections between the shelf and the bracket.  This is in fact what also contributed to the accident, as the single hole brackets are NOT LATERALLY STABLE.  That, in conjunction with the warps in the shelves themselves, led to the accident, as the brackets will shift laterally FAR MORE than the 1" leeway shown in your installation diagram.

After getting her home from the emergency medical center on Saturday, I returned to the Lowe's store where I bought these items and confirmed that Rubbermaid DOES NOT sell a supplemental bracket that attaches the shelf to the single hole bracket, so I had to choose between ripping out the whole system and starting over again, or figuring out a way to solve the problem myself.  I ended up buying some electrical conduit brackets as shown in the photo attached.

The single hole tracks and bracket system is clearly not appropriate for this application, and you are negligent in showing an installation protocol that does not specifically show AND REQUIRE the use of the double hole/double bracket system.  To continue using these installation instructions is materially misleading and is subjecting your company to future lawsuits and liability claims.

We will be sending in medical bills, x-rays, etc. as well as potential worker's compensation claims based upon her potential inability to continue working during her healing process.  Please respond with the specific items you will need, and what you will reimburse for.

I look forward to your prompt response.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken toe, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described installation flaws and potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: I made an online purchase for a chair advertised as "ergonomic" from a company called Autonomous.  They were recommended on some reputable review sites and it looked to be a sound purchase. I already had a slight lower back strain from lifting something too heavy which drove the purchase.  Within 2 weeks of sitting in the chair, the pain in my back worsened to the point that I scheduled an appointment with my physician.  It was pretty severe and I was worried.  I thought it must have been from the injury and maybe the injury was worse than I thought.  We did a quick xray and some bloodwork to rule out anything major.  Then I went to physical therapy and worked on it.  I wasn't using the chair much but thought it interesting that the pain worsened shortly after the purchase of the chair.  Still, I thought it couldn't be the chair that made things worse.  Must be coincidental.  Then, after the therapy helped reduce the pain sufficiently, I spent a full day at my desk, in the Autonomous chair.  By that evening, the pain had escalated severely again.  I was in bed on my back with heat on it for a couple of days and back to physical therapy.  I removed the chair from my office and proceeded to purchase a more reputable brand - [REDACTED].  I've been fine since then.  I deduced that the Autonomous chair is poorly designed and can cause physical problems.  It may have a seatbed that is problematic.  It needs to be examined.  I did reach out to Autonomous with my complaint and the company was not interested in my feedback.  They also refused to allow me to return the item since more than 30 days had passed.
justification: The incident describes a worsening of a pre-existing back injury due to the use of a poorly designed chair, requiring medical attention and physical therapy.

incident_description:
The product in question is a flat-packed sofa that came with separate pieces of seat bottom, back rest, and 2 armrests that use interlocking metal latches to come together without the use of tools.

The product did not arrive with an instruction manual, nor was one available online. The latches (as installed from the factory) permit the seat bottom section to only be able to slot up into the back rest section.

After installing the sofa in this way, during normal usage the seat bottom unlatched itself from the back rest with a load thud. This is because normal sitting will apply downward pressure to the latching mechanism, causing the latches to come undone eventually.

Upon collecting the online PDF instructions from the manufacturer, the correct installation involves installing the seat bottom _down_ into the back rest. The factory-installed latches however did not permit this assembly (one-way latches only allowed the seat bottom to lock up into the back rest), rendering the only possible assembly to be highly unsafe for the product and consumers.
justification: The incident describes a product failure (sofa unlatching) during normal use, posing a safety risk, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
My family has window blinds from SelectBlinds.com installed on almost every window in our home (20+ windows).  All installations used the provided hanging hardware, and followed directions as indicated from SelectBlinds.com.  All of the products were purchased approximately 4 years ago.

On the evening of Monday, September 14, 2020, my husband and I were sitting in our family room when a loud explosive/bang startled us.  A large metal spring (approx. 9 inches long and 1 inch thick) was ejected from the top of the window blind, broke through a plastic end cap on the product, and hit the window trim and opposite wall with great force.  The malfunction resulted in plastic fragments strewn about the room, and of course, a broken window covering.

Upon examination, we surmised that the large metal spring was under tension when the plastic "hook" that was holding it in place cracked and released it.  The potential for this malfunction, and the force at which the spring hit part of our window and wall is a major safety concern.  We have two small children who play in this room often, and we have the same product installed in almost every room of our home.

I immediately contacted SelectBlinds to notify them of the incident, and they replied that their Quality Control department would look into it and get back to me.  I found this response to be lacking and untimely.  

I truly hope that there is a way to quickly notify all customers of the potential for this to occur, the safety risk, and the danger to children for a significant injury.
justification: The incident involved a high-force ejection of a metal spring causing property damage, with potential for injury given the presence of children in the room.

When I felt safe, I brought the chair parts into my house. I proceeded to do some tasks in another room far away from the chair parts, but still began to feel dizzy and disoriented for a time. The symptoms were not as severe as with the first package opening and eventually went away.

I'm contacting you to see why fiberglass is not listed on the label as a content of the mattress or the knit of the mattress covers. I will need to throw this mattress away after using it for only 3 years because fiberglass is getting everywhere and I do not want to breathe it in as I sleep and risk health problems. justification: The incident involves potential health issues from fiberglass exposure, which could lead to injury, and the likelihood is high given the evidence of fiberglass shedding and health concerns.

incident_description: I just received an email regarding the tree we purchased last year. I didn't file a report until now because we ended up bypassing the hazard. The tree had been up and running in our livingroom for a few days and sitting a few feet away, late at night, I smelled something burning. The odor was stong enough that it led me directly to the button portion of the tree's power cord. I was nearly burned disconnecting the power source and noticed a large burn hole in our tree skirt on the floor. I knew I'd probably saved a few lives that night. We decided instead of returning the tree just days before Christmas, we would run it without the button, meaning white lights only and pack it up after the holiday. No issues since but to know that at least 500 people could've been in danger is obviously a reason to recall.
justification: The incident involved a burning odor and a burn hole, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My color changing cord sparked and stopped working. I returned and replaced the tree now the cord is recalled.
justification: The cord sparked and stopped working, indicating an incident with no injury, and the recall suggests such incidents are likely.

incident_description:
I purchased a Kelly Clarkson desk from Wayfair which was delivered last week (July 31,2020).  We had the trucking company bring the desk into the home office room.  We noticed a pungent odor so I decided on Aug.1, 2020 to unpack the desk and remove ALL the packing material from the house.  We still have the pungent odor to the desk.  We had other people come in and see if they could smell it.  One woman had to get out of the room because it was giving her a headache.  We purchased the desk for &1,200.00 and thought, regardless of the product coming from China that it would be a good product since it had Kelly Clarkson's name on it.
     I researched wood products containing formaldehyde on line, prior to the purchase, and discovered the EPA had a law passed to protect people from harmful affects of the amount of formaldehyde that can be used both domestic and foreign. 
     I am looking for a lab qualified and approved by you or the EPA to test the odor being released.  When I talked to your [REDACTED] on the phone she could not give me a lab's name.  I don't think your agency will respond quick enough so, I am willing to hire a lab.  I would rather use a lab that you send me to so I can make sure I am getting the correct test done. I will research the labs in the Erie, Pa. area.
cc:Senator [REDACTED]    /    [REDACTED]   Congressman: [REDACTED]
justification: The pungent odor caused a headache in one individual, indicating an injury, and the issue is possible given the reported symptoms and concerns about formaldehyde.

incident_description: An IKEA 4 drawer MALM dresser tipped over on my two year old daughter pushing her head through an adjacent wall.
justification: The dresser tipped over and caused injury to the child by pushing her head through a wall.

incident_description: immediately upon assembling and using, our Modavari Forrest Live Edge Benches proved to be unsteady unless body positioned directly center of bench. Both my children and my mother tipped on the benches. This is due to base of legs being narrower than bench and top.
justification: The benches are unsteady and caused tipping, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
This product is a light bulb used throughout my home. It installs in a recessed ceiling fixture. While installing the bulb, I twisted the telescoping pole to seat the bulb. The bulb lit momentarily and  exploded into many glass shards that fell down on me. The bulb socket remains in the fixture. Many shards were paper thin and many were very sharp. 

I compared the bulb I removed from the socket initially with another bulb from the same box as the one that exploded and found the original bulb was a little longer allowing it to fit into the fixture easier. Both bulbs are indicated to meet specification BR30, 65 Watts but the shorter one that blew up probably does not.
justification: The bulb exploded into sharp glass shards that fell on the user, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description: Glass globe and ceramic housing with LED light to master bedroom vanity light dropped from fixture into sink scattering the globe. My wife was in the bathroom when this happened. No injuries but when I went to pick up the metal piece which houses the led bulb the item was hot when I went to pick up for discard and had to drop. The  ceramic/metal housing which globe is attached to broke allowing globe to drop. Picture is available of the broken ceramic part which held the globe in place plus picture of vanity light is available. I purchased from Home Depot on November 19, 2016. Model item 73996 made by Hampton Bay.
justification: The incident involved a broken glass globe and ceramic housing with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the event and the product's failure.

incident_description: The chain snapped on our chandelier hanging In Our two story foyer
justification: The chain snapping is an incident, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I noticed that one side of the ceiling light fitting was a lot lower than the other side, fetched a chair to stand on to have a closer look and noticed that one of the plastic clips had snapped and the ceiling fitting was precariously hanging. I took the ceiling fitting out as otherwise it would have potentially fallen and smashed on the floor.
justification: The light fitting was damaged but no injury occurred as it was safely removed before falling.

incident_description:
Northpole Ltd folding arm chair model CF-400-B claims a weight limit of 225 pounds.  The tag warns that the "user must ensure weight is evenly distributed" and should "carefully enter/exit the fabric seating".  No guidance is given regarding how to carefully exit the fabric seating, and I weigh about 210 pounds.  
When I tried to exit the chair by pushing down on the fabric, the plastic fitting that connects the legs at the front of the chair snapped and dumped me off the patio on to our lawn.  Had I been elevated relative to where I landed, the fall could have resulted in severe injury.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury, but the chair failure could have caused severe injury under different circumstances, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: This is in regards to outdoor patio chairs. We purchased a new patio set from Menards. They are Backyard Creations, Farren Falls collection swivel rockers item #272-0962. My girl friend was sitting in one and all of a sudden she fell backwards and hit her head on the cement patio. We inspected the chair and found that all of the welds broke that hold the base to the chair itself.  Then about 10 minutes later I fell while sitting in another chair.  We inspected that chair to find the same issue, broken welds.  We inspected the other chairs and found another one has the same issues starting.  So 3 of the 6 six chairs in the set all have the same issue.  I contacted the company, sent pictures and the receipt over a week ago, still no response.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (head hitting cement patio) and multiple chairs showed the same defect, indicating a likely recurring issue.

incident_description: My 3-year-old son was getting off the bench when the bench suddenly flipped on its side hitting my son's toe.
justification: The incident resulted in a physical injury (hit toe), warranting a severity level of 3. Bench flipping is a possible but not highly frequent occurrence.

incident_description:
In October 2017 I bought a 3 shelf TV stand #NS-HMG 1856 about 56x20 inches, black metal, with a set-in glass top on the top shelf. About two weeks ago I heard a crack in the middle of the night. I got up but could find nothing; but the next day I saw that the glass shelf had splintered, like a windshield that cracks without falling apart.  I ran my fingers over the top and cut myself on very tiny, very sharp glass shards.  I cleaned up ;the top and the surrounding area with wet paper towels and covered it with a sheet so my cat would not get hurt.

I contacted Best Buy where I had purchased the item to report a dangerous situation.  The rep I talked to verified that I had purchased the item, and said the warrantee had run out and the item was no longer being stocked.  He said someone might contact me, but two weeks later I have heard nothing. Nor can I find that it was posted in their recall items. I know this is unusual, but since it happened once it could happen again to someone else.  Also, I have a very large dangerous piece of broken glass to dispose of in the middle of a pandemic.  I am 89 years old and am sheltering in place!
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut from glass shards), and the likelihood of recurrence is unlikely as the product is no longer stocked and the issue seems isolated.

incident_description: I purchased a I10 sleep number bed with flex fit 3 base in Sept 2017 with foot warmer. After working for for about a year the right side of foot warmer seemed to get very warm and seemed warm throughout the day and there was a slight burning electrical odor. An error code F1 occurred on my remote. I tried troubleshooting  by resetting bed which seemed to work but only temporarily. Being now summer of 2019 we didnÃÂt try anything as foot warming wasnÃÂt necessary. Winter of 2019-2020 we tried to reset and called Sleep Support who suggested same reset routine and said a replacement was needed and would cost 299. Since that time , we have looked on support site and learned there was an active recall for similar incidents up thru August 2017. I would like to report this incident as it is identical as reported in the recall but on beds one month later.
justification: The incident involves a malfunctioning foot warmer with a burning odor, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I used a Frogg Togg Chilly Pad around my neck during sports.  I developed a red, painful, papular rash on my neck.   I thought I had shingles.   It resolved in a day.  I washed the pad and used it again.  I developed the same rash on my neck and chest.   I checked Amazon and found reports of multiple people who had the same experience.
justification: The incident describes a painful rash that developed twice, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as multiple people reported similar experiences.

incident_description: Our West Elm Jensen Table, purchased in March of 2019, had a glass top that exploded out of nowhere in the middle of the night.  It sent shards of glass across the entire large kitchen, and into the living and laundry rooms.  Although the table was supposedly tempered, there were many small shards.
justification: The glass top exploded, sending shards across multiple rooms, indicating potential for injury but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The factory-supplied TV stand for our Samsung TV, model UN55JS7000FXZA, is warped and therefore very wobbly, unstable and unsafe.  We first noticed this on June 24, 2020.

We e-chatted with a Samsung customer representative on June 28th, 2020, and explained the faulty stand.  Their response was that this model TV was made in 2015, the one-year warranty has expired, and that we would have to purchase a replacement stand (for $57) on a separate web site.

Since the stand is unsafe to use, we didn't feel that their response was fair.  We expected a free replacement stand from Samsung.  On July 1, 2020 we emailed Samsung executive [REDACTED] with our stance.  In the email we compared our Samsung TV stand to [REDACTED] dressers that have toppled and hurt children.

After one week of no response to our email, we forwarded the original email on July 8, 2020 and marked it "2nd request."  In a couple of days we received a voice mail on our home phone with a message to call the [REDACTED] of Samsung.  When we returned the call on the same day, the representative ([REDACTED]) informed us that we would NOT be getting a free stand.  Her phone is [REDACTED].  We told [REDACTED] we would have to go farther.
justification: The TV stand is described as wobbly and unsafe, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the light bulb was on for about for 30 mins, he heard something that sounded like a gun shot and realized that the bulb had exploded all over the room.  He stated that the incident occurred a few minutes after switching off the light.  He stated that glass pieces shattered everywhere.  Caller is not sure where the product was purchased from.
The  manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that this light bulb is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb exploding, causing glass to shatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The bar stool was being used to sit on. A year after purchase, we started to notice something was protruding from the seat cushion. I reached out to Safavieh back then but did not get a response. We continued to use the stools on occasion and started to notice a sharp metal rod protrude out of the seat cushion. It was unsafe when our son got off the stool and got a cut from the metal sticking out of the cushion.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut injury to the son, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it took a year for the issue to manifest and cause injury.

incident_description: Our child was sleeping in the loft bed when the wood slats gave way and he and his mattress dropped through onto the desk and chair below.
justification: The child fell from the loft bed onto a desk and chair, which likely resulted in injury.

incident_description: I purchased the Furmax Office Mid Back Swivel Desk chair from Amazon.com (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07B7K7N3P/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1), when I leaned back in the chair the back broke and caused me to fall.
justification: The chair broke and caused a fall, but the description does not mention any injury.

incident_description: I removed the mattress cover on my gel infused memory foam mattress to wash it. After washing I put in back on mattress and skerritt on it that night. My partner & I woke up in the middle of the night itching all over. After an internet search, I realized the itching was due to the fiberglass in the removable mattress cover. I washed two loads of clothes before realizing it was fiberglass and now all of clothes, and washer and dryer are covered in it. It's been a cleaning nightmare because it's everywhere and sticks to everything. I have 2 young kids (2v months and 2 yrs), and I'm scared this is going to affect their health. I haven't been able to sleep on the bed since because it's so itchy. I'm afraid that it's in the air and we've been inhaling these fibers. The mattress cover has a zipper with a large puller so one would easily think it's safe to remove.
justification: The incident caused itching and potential health concerns due to fiberglass exposure, especially for young children, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the widespread contamination and ongoing exposure.

incident_description:
6/14 Caller stated that the chairs they purchased have a failure.  His spouse went to sit in the chair and the rear legs broke and where seat meets the back it broke. She fell on her buttocks, there was no injury.  Caller stated that the chairs are made from plastic but they do not appear to be sturdy.  The chairs was on a paved area when the incident occurred. 

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that these chairs are unsafe and should be recalled.
justification: The chair broke causing a fall, but there was no injury reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of the chairs being made of plastic and not sturdy.

incident_description:
On the evening of Friday June 12, 2020 the chandelier fell out of the vaulted ceiling. A scone, 2 light bulbs, and the decorative nub on the bottom (looks like a fancy curtain rod end) shattered. Exposed wires are now hanging out of the ceiling. The ring that was a part of the ceiling plate snapped. The plate is still firmly attached to the ceiling and part of the snapped ring was found on the floor.

Please not that this is not the ring that was recalled before (where the chandelier meets the chain), that ring was replaced with the hardware provided by the company. The ring that broke is where the chain meets the ceiling plate with it being a single unit welded to the plate.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: This chair has a fatal design in its engineering structure causing a child to be ejected forward because the weight distribution is mainly on the two front legs. It is very dangerous for younger children and there is no warning label noting this. They advertise this chair with a mother, father, and son sitting on them in front of a camp fire. This type of advertisement is also dangerous because my child sat in front of the camp fire and got burned because of getting ejected by this chair due to the design. BE WARNED dont let your children on this chair.
justification: The description reports a child being ejected from the chair and burned, indicating an injury occurred.

The chairs were picked up fully assembled 5/29/2020. Because of the type of work that I do, my doctor has told me I can not return to work until she feels it has healed enough and my pain subsides.

incident_description: Muse recliner(Pasadena Ca./HTL Group Singapore purchased from Havertys Furniture in Allen Texas in March 2019 appears to be of poor quality and unsafe design as the metal receclining mechanism is totally exposed on the inside of chair arms at seat cushion.The exposed metal is extremely sharp and if one drops an object such as a tv remote,pen or cell phone etc. reaching into the seat cushion/arm is very dangerous.My wife and have both suffered cuts when retrieving items. I am very concerned with small children setting in chair when we are not in room.
justification: The description reports that both the user and their wife have suffered cuts from the exposed sharp metal, indicating an injury has occurred.

incident_description:
I have an Ikea Brimnes Bookcase in my twin's bedroom and last Wednesday night (6/3/20), it fell over on top of my 2 year old babies. The bookcase was mounted to the wall, and was not overburdened (just children's books and stuffed animals). Luckily the twins were unharmed, minus being absolutely terrified and some bruising a couple days later. 

My biggest concern here is that the bookcase was properly mounted to the wall, with the original mounting material Ikea included with the product. There were two metal brackets attached at the top. One of the brackets pulled out of the wall, the other bracket stayed firmly in the wall but pulled out of the bookcase. 

I have a video of the incident, as well as pictures of the bookcase and mounting material.
justification: The bookcase fell but the twins were unharmed, with only minor bruising and no serious injury reported.

incident_description: The product is manufactured by Hodedah. It is the Hodedah Ribbed PU Leather High Back Swiveling Executive Chair Model #HI-3007. The chair was placed into service on June 1, 2020. On June 10, 2020 the chair fell over while I was sitting in it. The apparent cause is the base that has wheels for all flooring types was bending and eventually collapsed throwing me to the floor.
justification: The chair collapsed, throwing the user to the floor, indicating an injury occurred. The incident suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence due to the product's structural failure.

incident_description: The light bulb was placed into a light fixture to replace another burned out bulb.  It is a two bulb fixture with a conventional bulb on one side and the Everyday Living bulb on the other side.  The bulb lasted one week.  This AM I was sitting on the toilette when the Everyday Living bulb exploded and nearly started a fire.  Glass flew everywhere including my head, shoulders, and arms.  I sustained small superficial cuts which did not require emergency treatment.
justification: The bulb explosion caused small superficial cuts, indicating an injury but not requiring emergency treatment.

incident_description: Sauder office desk shoal creek fell apart two times and injured me and my son. Contacted company but they do not wanna recall faulty desk which has cheap ply wood not holding its weight
justification: The desk collapsed twice, causing injury to two people, indicating a recurring issue with the product's structural integrity.

incident_description:
All 4 legs broke on one of the patio chairÃÂs base, near the heat affected zone of the welds.  A adult was sitting in the chair at time and she sustained some bruises, but no Rx was needed

Early May, 2020, the consumer contacted the firm to participate in the recall, and the rep. (name unavailable) asked for pictures of the broken chair.  There was some back and forth correspondence by email, between the consumer and the firm.  However, he experienced a lot of difficulty with the various links that the firm provided.

The consumer was given a 3rd telephone number to send pictures by text and he said it took 15 attempts to send the pictures successfully..

The consumer spoke with several reps and one of the repÃÂs that was assisting him, has not been available the past few weeks.  The consumer spoke with another rep. in the firm and had to insist that the rep. look up his information, before he finally retrieved it.  That rep. was able to confirm that they had the pictures. justification: An adult sustained bruises from the chair breaking, indicating an injury without the need for medical treatment. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely as the incident is tied to a specific product recall and not a common event.

incident_description: My daughter and her baby were sitting in swingasan chair on swingasan stand and it tipped over, causing them to fall out of the chair.
justification: The incident involved a fall from a swing chair, which could reasonably result in injury to a baby and an adult.

incident_description: My daughter sat on her bed and it collapsed.  I bought 2 of the same beds.  one for each of my daughters.  the first bed, one of the feet snapped in half while my daughter was sitting on it.  I was upset because we had just bought it, but was hoping it was a fluke.  a few weeks later, the second bed we bought, my daughter sat down and it just collapsed.  The bottom fell out from under her, separated from the frame of the bed.   Thankfully it wasn't a big fall, but she could've hit her head, or been stuck.  Now i am just concerned these beds are not safe.  I have emailed the company and they said that they won't refund me, they are working with the manufacturer to try to get me a part.  meanwhile my daughter is sleeping on a mattress on her floor.  I feel like they are only 3 months old and they must be very poorly made.  I bought them from Coleman furniture online.  I am afraid for them to sleep on the beds. https://colemanfurniture.com/kids-white-tufted-full-upholstered-panel-bed.htm
justification: The bed collapsed twice with no reported injuries, but there was potential for harm.

incident_description: Elderly female was using a Carex bed rail and became entangled in it and subsequently died.
justification: The incident resulted in death, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description: Electrically powered adjustable bed when in a raised position will automatically go down (flatten) after any power interruption. I was under head of bed to disconnect power cord to install power strip. When I plugged it back in bed came down. I got out but I am concerned about children. This will happen in a power failure when power comes back on.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with the bed automatically lowering after power interruption, which could pose a risk, especially to children, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: The box lamp was plugged in and sitting on a nightstand. The plastic "cover" in front of the light bulb apparently came unglued and leaned against the bulb. Shortly after, we smelled melting plastic, and noticed the pink plastic was melting/bubbling/smoking - to the point that a hole the size of the bulb was melted into it. We immediately unplugged the lamp, and I  removed the back, and a small piece of melted plastic dripped on my hand. We no longer use it. I believe this item would have caught fire if it had been unattended.
justification: The incident involved melting plastic and a minor burn injury from dripping plastic, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the event.

incident_description: Purchased a desk lamp from amazon, Lampat. Smelled electrical burning throughout the house, was not aware it was the lamp. Came back a few hours later and the panel was burned up. No electrical burn at outlet, just panel of the lamp. Cord was not burned.
justification: The incident involved a desk lamp burning up without causing injury or damage beyond the lamp itself.

incident_description: My child was playing a video game in the chair when he left his room and showed me that his right arm was bleeding. I noticed that he had a laceration on it and he told me it was from the armrest on his gaming chair. Upon inspection, I noted that the chair has three pins or nails poking up through each armrest. The padding is not thick enough to stop the pins from poking through, thus causing injury.
justification: The child suffered a laceration from exposed pins on the gaming chair, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I used the product for less than 3 months and the welding joint connecting the base to the seat cracked. This is the second time my office chair has cracked at the welding joint and I thought the first time was a mistake. Both were purchased from Big Lots and now I believe the product to be lethally dangerous. Death could be caused by an implement or by falling.
justification: The description mentions a cracked welding joint and expresses concern about potential lethal danger, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: Purchased Pottery Barn oval glass finials (decorative ends to curtain rods).  Within an hour of installing the new finials on the curtain rods, the glass portion of the finial separated from the pewter portion of the finial, falling 8 feet to the ground. Upon closer inspection, it appears the glass (which weighs several pounds) came unglued from the pewter, causing it to fall. No one in my home was hurt. However, we hung these curtains in our children's bedroom - directly above a bed and crib. Had these fallen at a different time, our children could have been seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved a falling object that could have caused injury but did not, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the defect could recur but is not certain.

incident_description: We have owned this bunk bed for approximately two years. While my son was getting in bed tonight, the welding on the guard rail gave out completely, causing the mattress to fall from the top bunk while he was on it. He fell through the bottom and hit his head on the way down.
justification: The son hit his head during the fall, indicating an injury, but the description does not suggest a frequent occurrence of such incidents.

incident_description:
I sat down in my patio chair, leaned back, and it immediately fell back and then rolled to the left. I instinctively tried to catch myself but unfortunately was holding a glass of water. I felt the glass shatter in my hand and cut into my finger. I had a neighbor take me to the ER where I received 4-5 stitches. Additionally, I also have a few other minor scrapes and cuts. 

After getting home from the hospital, I saw how the chair had broken and found they had been recalled. To my knowledge I was never notified of the recall even after dozens of trips to the same store since the recall was announced. I believe it was purchased with my [REDACTED] credit card, so they should have my contact info.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention (stitches), which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the chair was recalled, indicating a known issue, but not all chairs may fail in this manner.

incident_description: I was sitting in my Hampton bay swivel chair yesterday eating lunch and the base broke causing me to fall backwards. Thank God I landed on the grass and not the concrete. My furniture was just taken out of winter storage.
justification: The chair broke causing a fall, but the person landed on grass without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she was using her heating pad for approximately three minutes when her husband noticed that there was smoke coming from behind her back where the unit was located. The consumer notes that her sofa has to burn holes about ÃÂ½ inch each, and that she sustained no injuries.
 
The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and left a voice message; she has yet to hear back from a representative.
 
The consumer states that the unit was used approximately once yearly for ten to fifteen minutes.
 
The consumer plans on keeping her heating pad for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The incident involved smoke and burn holes but no injuries, indicating an incident without harm. The low usage frequency (once yearly) suggests the likelihood is unlikely.

incident_description:
I bought a futon at walmart.com on May 4th. It was suppose to be SOME assembly required but when I got it I had to put the WHOLE thing together. I finally finished putting it together on May 8th. The day after we got it. As soon as I sat down I got scratched. I felt around underneath the cushion and I found that the bar going across the frame was scratching me. It was not covered in anything to protect it or me from being a piece of metal.

So I spent HOURS on the phone trying to figure things out and apparently customer service has NO idea what the futon looks like put together because when I explained how it was sitting they said "well just send us a picture so we can see what you are talking about" I sent them 10 pictures and they kept saying " I dont know" 
I made sure it was tight and hope it would keep close to the bar it was attached to. Well I got scratched again, so I realized as long as I tried to sit down and keep my legs bent I would get scratched .
I stopped sitting on it. Then after a day I find that the bar attached to the arm that the frame sat on was coming away from one arm. I looked at the others and I noticed they were all attached with no problem. So I called the company. Their main headquarters is in Canada but they DO have a corporate office in the UNITED STATES so I called.
I got the run around several times and they kept trying to send me to customer service so I decided to do some research on the web and found their executive team. I called and spelled out each person and finally got one guy to call me back but he just said he would have someone call me back. I then dialed the number for the CEO.
I talked to [REDACTED] the CEO and told him what was going on. He did not want to hear it, as a matter of fact he said he took NO RESPONSIBILITY for what HIS product did . So then I sent him pictures. HE said "Ill send them to the president of the engineering department".  He wanted NOTHING to do with it.
I got a call from a guy named [REDACTED] and he said " lets just talk about how to settle this" he did not want to talk about what the futon was doing either. incident_description:
In January 2020, I purchased for my daybed a Zinus Green Tea Mattress, Narrow Twin, through [redacted].  I received the 6" foam mattress a few days later and followed directions to let it expand over a 96 hour period.  During that time I purchased a quilted waterproof mattress protector and a set of sheets, which I put through the wash before putting on the mattress after the full expansion.
All seemed well for a few weeks, but then I began to experience itching and skin irritation, which became worse over the ensuing weeks.  Welts formed on my upper arms and trunk.  They reminded me of the feeling one gets when exposed to fiberglass particles during an insulation installation.
It took me a while to identify the cause, but going back to read negative comments about the product on [redacted], it became clear to me that the problem was with the mattress.  It looks to be that the delay between purchase and symptoms were related to the breakdown of the fire retardant layer and subsequent working of those sharp particles making their way through the Zinus mattress cover, the waterproof cover, the sheets, and, finally, my pajamas and other clothing, the latter three laundered periodically, which delayed or slightly reduced the problem for a day or so.  The symptoms not only included welts and itching, but sneezing and coughing, too, especially right after removing the CPAP mask I wear every night and during naps. 
I have contacted Amazon.com about this and have been issued a refund, although the warranty period expired 30 days after purchase.  I also sent an email to Zinus, but have had no response.

Please, investigate this as soon as possible so that others are not similarly affected.  I have taken the mattress outside in a large plastic bag and will dispose of it next week on our normal trash day.
justification: The incident caused skin irritation, welts, and respiratory symptoms, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described breakdown of materials over time.
