incident_description:
So far I have purchased 2 expensive La Z Boy Leather Recliner Rockers from the local La Z Boy Dealer. As soon as the first recliner was delivered and placed in my living  room my eyes began to burn. After sitting in the first recliner for approximately 15 minutes I began to itch on my legs, arms and back. The itching was most prevalent on exposed skin areas where a red rash started to develop. My eyes continued to burn. I called the La Z Boy Store and asked them to come and described what was happening. They seemed surprised about it and asked if I had included a special coating on the recliner. I said I had purchased it off their showroom floor and didn't know if it had been treated or not. They immediately sent their truck to pick up the recliner and I was given a full refund.

After thinking the first recliner must have been a problem of some kind I returned to the La Z Boy Store and bought a different style of leather recliner and had it delivered. After about 15 minutes I started having the same issues that I had with the first chair. Again I called the store and they sent their truck back, picked up the chair and refunded the purchase price.

I then saw a chair at the local [REDACTED] store that was covered in fabric instead of leather so I bought it and took it home myself. After removing the plastic wrap in my living room and sitting in the chair for several minutes the itching and burning sensation returned. Another person who was with me started complaining about a chemical smell and her eyes began to burn and she hadn't even sat in the chair. I replaced the plastic and returned the chair that evening. 

As soon as all three recliners  were removed from my residence the reactions I/we had were gone and the itching stopped.

1 more try here. I went to a nearby furniture/electronics store to see what they had in recliners. I found an [REDACTED] with a cloth covering that I liked and  decided to sit in it for several minutes prior to buying it. Guess what.....same  issues began to develop. Itching on the arms, back and legs. Needless to say I left the store without making the purchase. 

I have never had any problems with the La Z Boy Leather Recliner/Rocker that I have had for the past 25 years but it's wearing out. I now have it covered to hide the worn out areas. Evidently something has changed in the past few years to create allergic reactions. I have read several articles about dimethyl fumarate (DMF) the chemical used for mold prevention that has been banned in several countries but NOT in  the US which makes no sense at all. Many examples  of people with allergic reactions to their new furniture are posted online so I thought I would add another one. 

Good luck to anyone buying new furniture. I won't be buying anything more.
justification: The incident describes physical reactions (itching, burning, rash) to new furniture, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue recurred with multiple purchases, suggesting a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: A metal-framed barstool, one of three, purchased at Walmart in 2019, suddenly collapsed straight to the floor.  I'm pretty durable, but I was surprised that no bones were broken -- but it was quite a fall which has tremendous potential for harm.  If my chin had been over the bar when the stool collapsed, I can't imagine my neck not snapping with the violent movement.  The weight limit stated on the stool under the seat, is 300 lbs. -- and no one even close to that weight has ever sat on the stools.  I examined the barstool to understand what happened and saw that two welded places had actually torn away from the metal tube they'd been attached to.  I looked at the other two matching stools and saw that one of them showed the same process, as the weld was already partially separated from the tube -- which means that the next person to sit on it would probably be a victim of the poor quality and design.  My 92 year old  mother-in-law, currently recovering from a broken knee, may have been the next person - -and I imagine it would have been tragic.  I took the stools to Walmart and told them about them -- and they clearly didn't care.  I called and left a message, and I emailed Cheyenne Products named on the bottom of the seat telling them about the danger -- and told them that I have no intention of suing them but the stools are dangerous.  I received no response.  I was going to throw the stools in the trash -- but my conscience would not allow me to do that, knowing that people can be very harmed if these are not recalled.  The design is flawed.

incident_description:
An over the fireplace tv wall mount. It failed twice in exactly the same, extremely hazardous way. They will not take responsibility for this, but have only offered store credit. I bought a wall mount a year ago, and after a couple months it developed a clunking sound every time I raised or lowered the tv. Note that raising and lowering the tv is the essential function of this product. Eventually, I figured out that the bolt connecting the gas springs to the wall bracket had come unscrewed. This is extremely hazardous, as the gas springs could fly loose at very high speed and impale someone or break bones. When I wrote to the manufacturer, they said I could exchange the wall mount for the exact same product. They told me I had to have all the original packaging, but I did not have it anymore; it was six months later. They granted me an exception but said they would not do so again. I mailed back the mount in a large box, as safely wrapped as I could. They sent me the same model wall mount in return.

Two months later, the second mount failed in the exact same spot. Looking closely, I saw that the bolt comes under extreme pressure from the gas springs, and it therefore is forced to turn in the direction that the wall mount is moved. Every time you move the tv, you necessarily unscrew the bolt. The bolt just screws into a threaded piece of sheet metal. There is no locking bolt.  Clearly this is an unsafe design.  When I wrote to Monoprice again, at first they said I could exchange it with the original packaging. Yay, I kept that this time, just in case. But I said I donÃÂt want the same product, as it will just fail a third time.  They said I could have store credit. I said I donÃÂt want store credit when your selling unsafe products. They said no, it has been more than 30 days since the original purchase. Well, yeah; the thing failed twice because itÃÂs badly designed, both times more than 30 after receipt! The design could be fixed. They could add a locking bolt, which they have in other locations on this product. They could used a cotter pin that would not be subject to getting unscrewed.  Here are photos of the area that failed. The gas springs on the left is about 1/4 inch past the point where it was originally screwed in. The only thing holding it in place is the fact that it is wedged between the front of the pivot arm and the back of the bracket.
justification: The incident involves a hazardous product failure that could cause injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
Details: Purchase of 12" Novafoam dense foam based mattress with 3" topper and included soft cover
Set up on platform based bed rail
What went wrong:  The mattress and topper do not come with a  totally waterproof type slip into bag cover to cover mattress and topper.  If the mattress or topper accidently receive liquid spills on them in any depth going into the foam mattress topper or mattress itself, or if it is body fluids from accidents or intimate relations, there is no way to retrieve it out of the mattress materials.  It cannot be cleaned out enough and the use of a shop vac - wet/dry is not viable to be able to suck out the liquids.  These types of mattresses to the best of my ability have not been treated with any antimicrobial agents to keep the mattresses from developing molds or souring of the materials.  When this occurs, there is no choice except to cut up and dispose of the mattress and topper and disinfect the bed railing.   Spray on disinfectants do not work either - some cannot be used on the type of foam component the bed is designed from and cause other issues such as degrading of foam materials.  I am asking investigation into the use of any and all foam based mattresses that they redesign them with antimicrobial material and provide a waterproof mattress "sack" to go over both the mattress and topper and zipper closed.  I might add this situation is less of an issue with standard coil mattresses and box springs as they can be cleaned and the use of a wet/dry vac is sufficient enough to pull out liquids and allow for a complete dry out period.   It may also be noted that the traditional beds like this usually have as an accessory to purchase - a waterproof cover of some type well secured underneath a mattress pad cover.   
Result - Attempted disinfecting of mattress, 3rd mattress topper - same issue - no waterproof cover, just regular cover made from cotton/polyester materials with general decoration on it - offwhite in color.   Injury - medical : due to resulting internal contamination/mold interior of mattress, I was having breathing issues and headaches that became problematic which I tried to resolve from cleaning and replacing  and modifying what I could at the time.
justification: The incident resulted in breathing issues and headaches due to mold contamination, indicating an injury. The likelihood is high as the lack of a waterproof cover makes liquid spills and subsequent mold growth likely.

incident_description:
In 2017 I had a new kitchen designed and installed using IKEA SEXTION cabinets.  The two corner wall cabinets on each side of the stove have the UTRUSTA corner cabinet carousels which have two tempered glass shelves each. 

On Friday, December 6, 2019 I was sitting in my living room with my back to the kitchen when I heard an explosion and sound of breaking glass.  There were pieces of broken glass all over the counter and on the floor.  No cabinet doors were open, but when I opened the corner cabinet I saw that the top shelf had shattered and the there was broken glass everywhere.  Some of it was in small cubes, as is common with tempered glass when it shatters, but there were also very small slivers and pieces the size and texture of sand.  (see photos)  I had to clean off food items that were in the cabinet and it took several hours of repeated sweeping and mopping to remove all of the small pieces of glass from the cabinet, its contents, the counters, and the floor. In spite of taking careful precautions,  I received a few small cuts because the edges of the shattered glass were very sharp. (I assume that the cabinet door was blown open with the initial explosion and then retracted by the vacuum inside caused by the explosion because it was closed when I entered the kitchen, although there was glass all over the counter below the cabinet as well on the floor 5-6 feet away.)

The items that had been on the top shelf (the one that shattered) were very light--boxes and small tins of tea, a wooden salad bowl and 8 small wooden individual salad bowls as well as an aluminum vegetable steamer.  I had not used any of those items in several months and had not opened the cabinet that day.  I had not previously noticed any visible evidence of small cracks or damage to the shelf.  The explosion was spontaneous and loud enough so that the HVAC technicians servicing my outside air conditioner on the other side of the house came in to see what happened and to check on my welfare.

My greatest concern about this product is that it seems to have exploded spontaneously and without any apparent cause.  The glass sits on a plastic support and has a "rail" around the outside (see photo).  It is a simple design and installation was simple and done by a contractor.  I see no reason why it would shatter in such a way almost two years after installation.  I am also concerned about the fact that I have two cabinets with these shelves (4 shelves in all) and the regular shelves in my upper cabinets and bar are presumably made by the same manufacturer.  From researching the reasons for sudden shattering of tempered glass, I found that some types, particularly less expensive tempered glass, may contain impurities that over time can cause this type of failure spontaneously.  Glass which has been cooled more rapidly also tends to be more likely to fail.  Therefore, the quality of the glass itself is an important factor in its safety and a less expensive tempered glass is more likely to fail.  Although industry standards in the US are quite high for tempered glass, imported glass has a higher risk of failure.  

When I spoke with a Risk Compliance person at IKEA in Tempe, AZ, I asked if IKEA had any reported incidents of similar accidents.  He said he had no information on that, and that someone would call me from customer service to arrange for shipping the damaged product back to the store.  I was reluctant to do so until I had more information on similar incidents and expressed disappointment that IKEA was not more interested in investigating the incident rather than just replacing the shelf.  During our call, I was disconnected twice.  Although at the time I thought the disconnect was because of spotty cell service at my location, I saw when I checked with CPSC that this had also happened to two other customers who called in about spontaneous glass shattering incidents with IKEA products.  There are no other reports currently filed with the CPSC on incidents with glass shelves in IKEA  kitchen cabinets, but there were over 10 incidents with IKEA tempered glass tables and desks.  I plan to call the national IKEA safety office again to ask if the manufacturer of the kitchen glass shelves is the same as that for the tables and desks cited in the other cases filed with the CPSC.  

I invested a considerable amount in my new kitchen and am concerned about my longterm safety as well as that of my pets.  As the safety officer I talked to in the national office of IKEA said, I need to feel comfortable in my own kitchen.  The fact that the Risk Compliance representative from Tempe failed to mention any similar incidents or to say that he would follow up to find more information was unsettling, particularly when I was able to access the CPSC reports with a simple internet search.
justification: The incident resulted in small cuts from shattered glass, indicating an injury (severity 3). The spontaneous shattering of tempered glass is uncommon but not unheard of, making the likelihood unlikely (2).

There are three light heads in the kit that was purchased, making a total of 3x4=12 fluorescent lamps. Each lamp carton is marked with a warning regarding mercury. Immediately upon applying power, one of the three light heads began making an acrid odor consistent with a mix of hot chemicals. This odor was so bad I opened all the windows of our home for ventilation. It was not clear what the exact nature of the odor was. After an hour or two of operation, one of the four fluorescent lamps in the smelly light head began to make an electrical buzzing sound, then it made a "POP" sound and then one of the fluorescent lamps went dark. The odor, acrid-chemical-solvent-metallic-hot became intense. I felt numb-headed, light-headed, as did my wife. We both don't feel normal now. Neither of us have been the same since, which was on or about NOV 23 2019. Might hazardous chemicals, including mercury, have been emitted by the fluorescent lamp that failed? incident_description:

She heard a crack sound and within seconds the top bunk gave way and she fell completely through to the bottom of the bed. It was then that we discovered that on the top bunk on the side railing in three different places the railing was welded had all snapped. This is noted in the pictures that we obtained. The name of the product is ( Zinus Aileene Easy Assembly Quick Lock Twin over Twin Classic Metal Bunk Bed with Dual Ladders / Quick to Assemble in Under an Hour) that was purhased on amazon.com on March 5th of 2018.

When I got to the Satellite, the firemen were mopping up. I was told me that the flames were shooting out as if a flammable gas was being emitted from the fixture. incident_description:
I purchased several GT-Lite fixtures from a local store.  The model number is GT-SL5000-Link.  I installed two in my garage without incident.  I then installed one in my basement between the discharge and return furnace ducts.  On initial power up, I felt a slight tingle when the switch was cycled.  I then accidentally jostled the fixture and it made contact with the duct work and the circuit fuse blew.  
I contacted the supplier and reported the problem.  They were helpful and I performed several tests but initially I was not able to reproduce the issue.  After further testing I noted that when the ground conductor was missing the problem manifested itself.  I presented this information to the manufacturer and they denied this was the case. (I had sent the original fixture back to them for their testing).  They claim there is no problem with these fixtures-- but since then I have proven it on multiple fixtures and I am still in possession of these fixtures.
The manufacturer says they had the units tested by ETL Intertek and the units passed all tests.  I called ETL and they were not helpful.
Hopefully, you can look into this issue and get these fixtures removed from the marketplace since they could easily harm someone (they tripped a 20 A circuit).  I have much more information if you need.  I have pictures showing the high voltage and a sketch depicting the tests I made. These documents are attached.
justification: The incident involved a slight tingle and a blown fuse, indicating an electrical issue but no injury.

When I finally was helped up, I had severe pain in my right foot, leg, knee, thigh, hip and back; also the right side of my neck and back hurt, as well as my entire buttock area and my left foot. incident_description:
The product is an Aquadom brand.  Toll Free# (800) 654-0016.  Model SR3630.  Signature Royale 36" X 30" X 5" Lighted Mirror Glass Medicine Cabinet for Bathroom, 3D LED Color Temperature Lights Cool/Warm, Clock, Defogger, Dimmer, Electrical Outlet with USB.  Purchased under Aquadom Invoice No. [REDACTED] on 08/09/2019.  I have reported this incident directly to their customer service department.
  I purchased this product as part of a recent complete bathroom remodel which is almost complete.  This project was done under [REDACTED] Illinois Permit.  I am an Illinois licensed and American Society of Home Inspectors Certified Home Inspector.  Therefore I have been trained and am qualified to use basic analytical electrical test equipment.
  Upon completion of the installation including electrical wiring of this product to a Ground Fault Circuit Interrupt (GFCI) protected, wall mounted receptacle upstream to provide the required GFCI protection to the on board receptacle in the medicine cabinet, it was determined by a GFCI receptacle tester that the on board receptacle was reverse polarized (hot/neutral wires crossed).  Further, this receptacle would not trip the wall mounted GFCI receptacle upstream to provide the required, intended GFCI protection to the on board receptacle.  This allows increased potential for shock hazard at a bathroom vanity sink.  It was also discovered that the anti-fog mirror heater in this medicine cabinet was warming continuously weather the internal power button switch for this feature was depressed or not.
  I then asked the electrician to cross the live and neutral connections to the GFCI receptacle upstream while marking the wires to see what would happen.  After that was completed, the on board receptacle now tested as correctly wired, and the tester tripped the wall mounted GFCI receptacle upstream as it should.  However, the anti-fog feature will not work at all now.  
  The reason this occurred is because this electric supplied medicine cabinet which is manufactured in China and listed by ETL, is being improperly wired during the assembly process.
justification: The incident involves a wiring defect that increases shock hazard but no injury was reported. The issue is likely to occur given the improper assembly process.

incident_description:
I have a king size Zinus brand (purchased through Amazon) memory foam mattress that has unleashed fiber glass all over my apartment.  It has a thin zip cover over the mattress.  My husband and infant daughter also sleep on this bed.  My daughter had an accident on the bed and so i quickly removed the bed sheet and also the zip cover that surrounds the bed.  The tag said spot clean only so I set the cover aside for when I had some time to spot clean and let it dry.  In the meantime I put a waterproof fitted sheet over the bed and put clean sheets back on.  I did not notice that on the tag in small print (and not even in the first sentence of 2) that it said not to remove the mattress cover.  Nor does it state for that matter that if the cover is removed it will unleash fiber glass particles all over your house.

Not to mention the tag that states this is not visible when it is underneath the mattress and there is nothing stopping you or alerting you not to remove the mattress cover right where the zipper is.  I was alone with an infant child and was able to remove the cover within a matter of less than 1 minute as I have to move quickly because my daughter will lose patience, and I also did not want the liquid to soak through the cover and into the mattress itself.  We did not discover that there was fiberglass everywhere for 2 weeks.  

My husband was searching for a mattress for my sister in law and was thinking of purchasing the same one and while he was searching online came across a review that there is fiberglass in the bed.  He called Zinus, and they confirmed this and told him to turn off the lights and use a flashlight to see it.  Sure enough it is everywhere.  It has been hot and we have been operating a fan which makes it spread even more.  Since we have discovered this we have had to leave the apartment and stay with at my in-laws home.  We have looked at reviews on Amazon and online searches and sure enough this has happened to ALOT of other people.  We even discovered a news station did a report on this same brand of mattress that ruined a families home. 

 There are also lots of reports about the fiberglass coming through the cover itself.
We know other people with this mattress and we checked their bed and have found fiberglass.  My husband is a firefighter and understands flame retardants are used in mattresses, but to have a flimsy thin cover WITH A ZIPPER is ridiculous for a mattress that contains loose fiberglass just below the cover.  An [REDACTED] Fire Captain came over because he wanted to see what we were dealing with and offer advice and could not believe how bad the situation was,and also thought it was ridiculous and unsafe to have a thin cover WITH AN ACCESSIBLE ZIPPER over all this fiberglass.

This is extremely unsafe and is continuing to unleash fiberglass into many many households.  We have an infant daughter and are horrified she has been exposed to this for 2 weeks and are scared to bring her back home.  We are in the nightmare stage of trying to clean it up. It is EVERYWHERE and we are having to throw a ton of stuff away.  We have heard from other people that this happened to that a professional cleaning service charges thousands of dollars.  We live on [REDACTED] and that is not an option for us. 

 Zinus refuses to help us whatsoever.  Amazon has refunded us for the bed but that does not begin to remedy the situation.  The company advertises this mattress as safe and more natural but is the exact opposite and contains lots of chemicals and fiberglass.  This mattress is clearly unsafe for consumers.
justification: The incident involves exposure to fiberglass, which poses health risks, especially to an infant, and has caused significant disruption and property damage.

She did not hit the grass/ground only because she caught herself with her arms.

She is not using the second chair and she has removed it from her back yard and placed both chairs in her basement.
Not a webbed chair, it is a fabric chair.
There are no injuries being reported
She contacted the retailer's corporate headquarters August 31st, 2019 and their representative provided her with the manufacturer's contact phone number.
She called the manufacturer's contact number, she left a message but she has not as of September 5th, 2019 received a return call.

incident_description: Less than a year ago in October we bought a mattress from Aldi. We had previously purchased a high end mattress from a furniture store and did not have a good experience. We were skeptical at first but when we brought the product home we loved it until yesterday. We recently started having lots of mosquitoes due to the rain here in Oklahoma. For a week now I've been sleeping restlessly because I was getting bites in my sleep. Or so I thought. I was waking to sharp pricks mostly in my legs. Finally yesterday I was awake to feel the pain. 100% alert. After having freshly washed all my linens and putting them back on my bed, I lied down on the bed to chat with my husband when I felt sharp prickles in my arms. I convinced my husband to feel the sheets and he felt it too. I got up and checked the sheets really closely to find small tiny glittery needles all over my sheets. At first I was at a loss to what it could be. But I remembered watching people patch boats as a child and remembered the fibers in fiberglass netting for patches. So I googled it. I found that fiber glass is used to encase beds because it meets the requirements of flame retardant bedding. I know from reading the packaging of fiberglass that it is hazardous to the skin, eyes, nose and lungs. Because fiberglass can imbed, it can cause blindness among many other things. My skin, eyes and throat are irritated as well as my husband's. I wrote an email to Aldi asking for a refund and they have not responded. The mattress was supposed to have a teen year warranty. Fiberglass is known to be hazardous why is this legal?
justification: The description reports skin, eye, and throat irritation from fiberglass exposure, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Monster bran LED light strip. Walmart is selling it for only $5. It Gives off very toxic fumes, which filled the room and made me sick the second I opened the mylar sealed package. I immediately removed everything to the porch.
This is a highly carcinogenic item, packed with at least 7 known causing chemicals, that gives off fumes, and parents are using it around their babies cribs and in homes and giving it to their kids as gifts to decorate their rooms. I purchased it with the intention of gluing it under my kitchen cabinets. Please pull this item from the market immediately! I also don't how to dispose of it properly. It does not belong in people's homes! Thank you!
justification: The description indicates the product caused immediate sickness due to toxic fumes, which qualifies as an injury. The widespread sale and use of the product suggest a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

On 8/14 caller attempted to plug the chair again to the wall to see if the product would work. After a few minutes of being plugged in the remote got extremely hot again so the caller unplugged the chair again from the wall.
justification: The remote getting extremely hot poses a fire hazard (incident), but no injury or death was reported.

The design flaw is the safety strap,which was still anchored to the wall but detached from the back of the bookcase. This could have been a much worse incident and I don't want this happening to someone else.

incident_description:
Approximately 10 months after purchasing a large mirror, the small 1/4" screws pulled out of the MDF board causing the hanger bracket to fail and a 42 lb. mirror fell to floor. Had a person, especially a child, been underneath the mirror when it fell he/she could have been seriously injured or killed.

A short 1/4" screw, especially in MDF board, is obviously not strong enough to hold up a 42 lb. mirror. The fact that the mirror will shatter when it falls adds to the danger of this item.
justification: The mirror fell but no one was injured, though the potential for serious injury or death was present if someone had been underneath.

incident_description:
The T8 LED bulbs were being used in a light fixture in our laundry room.  The LED bulbs were a direct replacement for the original CFL bulbs. They were installed about 1 year ago.

On 9/3/2019  at about 6:30 am the fixture erupted in flames that shot out one end. damaging the ceiling and destroying the fixture. I needed to use a fire extinguisher to put out the fire . The fire dept. was called to be sure the fire had not gotten into the attic. It melted the plastic cover over the floor and scorch the ceiling.  
The fixture was operated by a occupancy sensor.

The product was GT-Lite T8 LED direct replacement bulbs. Model number GT T8 EBIR

It is very obvious that the bulb itself failed in a catastrophic manner. It did not blow the circuit breaker as I had to turn off the power after I put  the fire out.
The house is 13 years old and up to code.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such catastrophic failures are not common with proper usage and up-to-code installations.

incident_description: Bought an adjustable bed frame here that CAUGHT ON FIRE ON ITS OWN. I bought it 8/25/19, delivered 8/28/19. Caught on fire the evening of 9/2/19. [REDACTED] response was "There is nothing that could catch on fire on that corner of the bed." By the way, there is, that's where the USB ports are... I wasn't using the USB ports though. I am still trying to get the adjustable base replaced and hopefully, [REDACTED] will make a note to the manufacturer or warn their clients. I spoke to the Sales Manager, [REDACTED], (or he used to be when I bought the adjustable bed frame and spent over 4000 grand at the store in downtown, Los Angeles) and he said it could have been the wiring in my house (!!!!!). The apartment is new... it's not old wiring. Anyway... THERE IS NO REASON WHY AN ADJUSTABLE BED SHOULD CATCH ON FIRE. I WAS TERRIFIED TO LIE BACK DOWN ON IT. I am still waiting to hear from the [REDACTED] customer service department and the bed frame's manufacturer "HHC." They should warn customers that this could happen ("hey, the bed frame could catch on fire while you're asleep") or they could have a really significant lawsuit on their hands if someone were to get hurt. The one good point the Sales Manager had was that I should have called the fire department... I was just in shock and immediately wrote [REDACTED] to either refund or replace the bed. And yes, there is already a complaint with the BBB. The bed frame is this: Head-Foot Model-Good Queen Adjustable Base - ITEM# - M9X732. [REDACTED] SITE. BUYERS BEWARE. YOUR HEAD COULD CATCH ON FIRE.
justification: The bed frame caught fire, posing a significant hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: When my family moved into our current home in March 2019, we purchased a new tv wall mount (as listed on product itself: company Shaghal Ltd, model ONA16TM011E, manufacture date April 2017. Only warning labeled is to not install a Tv over recommended weight. I think it was purchased from Walmart). It was installed by an amateur, but an informed, experienced one and the product has every appearance of being designed for amateur installation. All installation instructions were followed. It is labeled as able to hold TV's weighing 66 lbs. Mine weighs in the mid 20s. The wall mount functioned well for 5 months. Last Tuesday, without warning and with no seeable cause, the screws holding the wall mount ripped out, sending the tv crashing to the floor. Moments before it happened, my youngest 2 children (1 and newly 4) had been seated on the floor playing where it fell, as it fell into the middle of my living room. In particular, my 1 year old had been seated for an extended period of time exactly where the force of the tv crashed down and only moved perhaps 60 seconds before it fell. Due to her age, she would likely have not moved out of the way in time and obviously would be vulnerable to a much more serious injury than an older person. I don't think saying it might have killed her is an exaggeration, and obviously it could injure even an adult, especially if a larger tv had been mounted at a higher level. I contacted the company through email to alert them to this danger and was simply told that my product could not be replaced for free as it was outside the warranty leading me to believe they have no concerns about the safety of this product. This is not my primary concern, but for what it's worth, my wall was decently damaged during this.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage and posed a significant risk of death to a child, though no injury occurred this time. The likelihood is unlikely as the product was installed correctly and the TV was well below the weight limit.

incident_description: I purchased the mattress only after the sales associate AND store manager told me the mattress did not off-gas. When it arrived, it did. I let it air out for 4 days and 3 nights, then made the terrible decision to sleep on it. Each morning of those 3 nights, I woke with nose bleeding when I blew my nose. The mattress also gave off enough gas to make my pillow smell so bad by the third day that I felt a bit of a panic when I realized that. The smell had soaked through a sheet and comforter that covered the bed (this was a comforter that I had placed over the mattress and underneath me while I slept to try to keep any gas from getting to me- obviously did not work at all). Whoever regulates these mattress materials needs to do a way better job of it. It is very clear that they are toxic. I am sensitive, yes. But, if this mattress caused me to have nose bleeding and allergic type reactions, then I am quite sure others who sleep on them without the symptoms are still being exposed to chemicals that they may not recognize as hazardous but that are hazardous. Please take more care in regulating a product that people spend so much time laying on.
justification: The incident caused nose bleeding and allergic reactions, which qualify as injuries.

incident_description: I bought a candle from Z Gallerie.  We hadn't used it until only recently.  The first time it was lit, and only briefly, the coating on the glass of the holder melted into the candle so the candle was immediately blown out.  I am afraid this could be a fire hazard and has not been used since.  The following day, I called Z Gallerie (the merchant)'s customer service line.  I  explained what happened and asked if I may return or exchange the item and my fear of it being a fire hazard.  They refused to return or exchnage it since I could not produce a receipt. Further, I explained that I don't regularly and didn't keep the receipt for an item for an extended period of time that was not very expensive.  Who knows if this was defective or if this is a fire hazard or how many other people this has happened to.
justification: The incident involved a candle holder's coating melting into the candle, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage occurred. The likelihood is possible as the defect could affect other users but hasn't led to widespread reports.

incident_description:
I bought a children's bunk bed for my young son on Amazon from Mattress Firm with Donoco as the importer. The bed frame was smashed so I had to wait 3 months for a replacement. The wood frame had a very strong stain smell so we left it outside for almost 6 months thinking that it had just been stained prior to shipping. We installed the bed, but he always complained that his room smelled. I did not fully understand the extent of the stain smell until I was lying on his bed one evening and could smell the stain. The drawers also emitted a strong smell when opened. I asked both Donoco and Mattress Firm for a refund and also for them to investigate this hazardous situation. No person, and especially a child, should have a bed with such a strong stain odor. I also invested $300 for assembly and again $300 for disassembly. It is once again sitting on the driveway. I am not sure what to do with it. I am also fearful that other children are being adversely affected by the chemical smell. My son has suffered from headaches since December. I also had been having headaches with a noticeable change since we removed the furniture. By the way, after disassembly, I found  a stamp on the furniture for 2017 which means that the stain/paint utilized is either defective or for exterior use only.

We ask 1. The furniture is investigated for safety or recalled.
 2. We are reimbursed for the furniture and our costs
 Thank you
justification: The incident involves health issues (headaches) linked to chemical exposure from the bed, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description: Product: kitchen table and 4 chairs purchased at Raymour & Flanagan ( Fair Habour is the name of the set) . A chair leg became detached and caused a fall and a deep laceration to hand. Service has been requested on this set four times since it was purchased. All service calls were due to legs  of table loosening or legs of chairs loosening. Chairs have been replaced twice and table legs once by the store. This time an injury and fall occurred on this poorly made and unsafe set. My friend felt the chair wobble, grabbed on to the side of the chair and sliced her finger open when leg collapsed. She bled profusely and finger was purple. Finger bled for more than an hour through a tightened bandage. Today finger is still oozing and badly. bruised. She also hurt her back while grasping on to the side of chair.  went into the store today to complain and The store refuses to accept a return and only offered a 28% store credit since set  was just under 3 years  old. We have removed all chairs and are sitting on folding chairs now. Another of the chairs is now wobbly. This set is an extreme safety hazard and I feel a recall should be started. My husband has tightened screws on these chairs at least 5-6 times. The store has replaced defective parts to this set three times. I have documentation. This time there was a serious I jury.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep laceration, prolonged bleeding, and back injury, meeting the criteria for Injury (severity 3). The repeated failures and service requests indicate the issue is likely to recur (likelihood 4).

Had been living at residential care facility since 2006.  Was last known to be alive at about 0300 hours by caretaker who could hear him breathing in bed.  Was found at about 0745 hours by his caretaker, laying on his left side on the floor, with his back against the bed rail and neck against a bed pole.  When deputies arrived on scene they loosened the bed pole, moved the decedent and assessed him. incident_description:
I incurred a back injury on 07/25/19 as the result of a faulty repair performed on my Volante  Sit-Stand Workstation. The repair was coordinated after I received notice of a *recall due to faulty cylinders, along with instructions for scheduling repair from a qualified technician.

My workstation was working fine before the repair. I was not present when the repair was completed. I returned to my desk to find a note from the technician stating "Desktop Sit-Stand Workstation repair is complete. Your desk has been certified and is ready to use." The technician had left my desk in an elevated standing position. When I attempted to lower the desk by releasing the side handles, it was obvious that there was no support as it started to fall and, on instinct, I attempted to stop or slow the fall with my hands on the side handles. Due to the added weight of dual monitors, a docking station, and laptop, the effort caused me to sustain a back injury which has worsened with each day - and it has been 13 painful days since the writing of this report. I had a coworker from the Facilities department present to witness this injury.

Part of the reason for the growing pain is that I have a serious and chronic back issue which requires me to stand for most of the day. I have not been able to transition between standing and sitting for over a week now, which is exacerbating my back pain and interrupting my work.

I called the technician the following day and went into voicemail to reschedule her return. Her responding voicemail was rather rude. I called Knape & Vogt directly to register a complaint and ask for a different technician, and was told to call back the following Monday. I had to call back the followings week for a status update and just yesterday, 08/07/19, received this email:

"Hello [REDACTED],
We have attached a Multiple Unit Spreadsheet, if you could fill out form and return to sit-stand@kv.com at your earliest convenience, we can work as quickly as possible to complete the repair for you. We only ask to gather the correct information for the repair kit. Thank you for your time and patience."

I am submitting this complaint to register Knape & Vogt's negligence and inadequacy.

*Knape & Vogt Manufacturing Company is voluntarily executing a recall for the Volante Sit-Stand product sold or distributed during the period of October 1, 2016 and February 15, 2019.
justification: The incident resulted in a back injury that has worsened over time, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the context of a faulty repair and pre-existing back condition.

8 year old male has a Hugglepod chair suspended from his bedroom ceiling a few feet from the foot of his bed.  Child goes up to his room and is allowed to play on his own before going to bed.  Mother checks on child and finds that he's hanging by the neck and tangled in the Hugglepod.  Child pronounced deceased, cause of death is asphyxia by ligature, manner of death accident.

The seat portion of the Hugglepod was used for storage and had some weight to it.  Child also enjoyed jumping off the bed and swinging on the Hugglepod.  It is believed that the child jumped from the bed and became entangled in the upper portion of the Hugglepod and asphyxiated.

incident_description:
We purchased a set of 2 zero gravity chairs from Sam's Club in June 2018 (Item # 545111, Model # 80009000152.)  On Sam's website, 3 of the specifications listed for these chairs is "Long lasting outdoor grade fabric, " "300-lbs. weight capacity, " and "Relax with the smooth recline function."  

Yesterday, August 5th 2019 my wife was using one of these chairs in our backyard on a level surface. She is well below the listed maximum weight capacity.  She leaned back in the chair as she has in the past and relaxed. After 5 minutes of laying in the chair something collapsed and she fell backwards, ending up with her head on the ground and her feet up in the air. She is fortunate she did not sustain a debilitating head, neck, or back injury.  

After further inspection of the chair it appears the plastic armrests gave way and allowed the chair's frame to bust through (on both sides.)  Additionally the pivot mechanisms that allow the chair to recline do not look symmetrical any longer - it appears the one on the chair's right side (while seated) shifted into a different position than it was originally in.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall but no injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the chair failed under normal use conditions.

justification: Consumers experienced migraines and sinus infections from the mold/mildew smell, indicating injury.

The product is the "Sloan Dining Table 60" Raw Mango/Glass from West Elm. I bought it in August 2016. In July 2019 the glass top randomly exploded. justification: The glass table exploded, causing significant damage but no injuries, as stated in the description.

incident_description:
The chandelier has been hanging in a stairway for several years.  One night it came crashing down, damaging the wooden stair railings, breaking several globes which left many glass splinters in the carpeting.  No one was injured, and fortunately there was no electrical short in the ceiling.  Upon inspection, the "screw collar loop" to which the chain is attached and supports the entire weight of the fixture, had broken from the ceiling mount.
This loop is not a part that receives any sort of wear and tear, and I feel should never break under any normal usage circumstance.  No one was near the chandelier, which means it simply broke and fell without cause except for the failure of the mounting loop.
There was damage to wooden stair railings.
Also, this is very concerning because we have other Portfolio light fixtures in the house and I am concerned about their safety.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as the mounting loop failure is unexpected but not common.

incident_description: I have 2 Summer Classic Swivel Loungers that were purchased in Mar 2017.  They are the same style as the ones recalled but the exact model is not listed.  The seat snapped off the base.  The metal post that connects the base to the seat literally snapped in an almost clean break.  I have pictures of the base and pictures of the bottom of the seat.  I had no idea the product was recalled.  I was told by the local Summer Classic store that replacement bases were no longer available.  In an effort to find a way to repair this chair (as it is expensive) I sent an email to the company.  The company did not reply.  As I went to the website again to send a follow up inquiry, I noticed the recall.  Again the model I own is the not included in the recall list.  I own two "Summer Classic - Wicker Swivel Gliders".  There were no serious injuries resulting from the event other than a good scare and slight back soreness the following 2 days.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (seat snapping off) causing a scare and slight back soreness, but no serious injuries.

incident_description: I have purchased 2 blue color NOLA 4 drawer chest and one pink color NOLA 4 drawer chest from Wayfair.com on January 14 2019. We loved into our house on February 11th 2019. We assembled them the following week. Have had issues every since. Just last night my daughters whole two drawers fell out when she was getting her shirt. They hurt her leg and foot but she was okay because we harnessed them to the wall or the whole dresser would of fell. The parts are flimsy and easily cracked on the railing. This happened to all 3 of the Zoomie kids dresser products I purchased. Not single one is not defective and was working properly.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the daughter's leg and foot, and the dressers are consistently defective, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Bar Chairs I purchased from Lowes had leg break and almost dumped me while sitting on my deck. I attempted to find a site online to repair or replace the chair legs. I subsequently found a recall from 3i Corporation for these chairs and their use should be discontinued immediately. Unfortunately, I never was advised previously of this recall.  When I called 3i Corporation about the recall, I was put on a record d message that I would receive a return call. I have not gotten a call back. What can I do about the unsafe chairs?
justification: The chair leg broke but no injury occurred, and the recall suggests this is a known issue with possible recurrence.

incident_description: I found an Ikea lamp in the trash dumpster in my 60-unit apartment complex. It had an Ikea LED bulb in it, model # LED1715G3. The bulb was seriously melted down and charred, exposing part of the circuit board. Apparently, in order to melt itself down like that, the bulb had drawn enough current to melt and char the cord and switch on the lamp.  I have retained both the bulb and the lamp and will be happy to send pictures or the items themselves to you. I'm not sure who the lamp belonged to. As far as I know no fire resulted from this incident, but it certainly could have. It is also possible that the lamp and bulb could have been damaged by an external fire or heat source, but there have been no fires in the complex as far as I know.
justification: The incident involved a melted and charred lamp and bulb, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
This report/complaint is about the following office chair I purchased new on amazon on February 1, 2019 - product name and link to amazon page where I purchased follow:

Product Name:  Chairlin Ergonomic Office Chair Mesh Task Chair Mid Back Desk Chair with Lumbar Support Black by CHAIRLIN

https://www.amazon.com/Chairlin-Ergonomic-Office-Lumbar-Support/dp/B07HGP65NP/ref=cm_cr_arp_d_product_top?ie=UTF8

Despite having 4 legs with rollers, the chair is extremely unstable and, being very lightweight, tips over VERY easily (I am a 69 year old male).  On July 1, 2019, I went to sit down and the entire chair slid out from under me causing me to hit my office floor squarely on a shoulder for which I have already received 2 Cortisone injections for rotator cuff problems.  I hit the floor so hard I thought I broke my shoulder and for several days could not raise my right - and dominant - arm above my waist.  I remain in pain  6 days later and, coincidentally, already had an appointment with my orthopedic surgeon scheduled July 9, 2019 who will order MRI and presumably take more xrays at time of appointment to compare with xrays take previously.  NB: I  am 5' 10" tall and weigh 170 lbs and in overall good health.

The chair is made in China, there is no support available in the USA.  Attempts to contact the US importer/amazon seller Aerair Stores were unsuccessful and amazon was not able to provide me with contact information.  NB:  I followed the assembly instructions to the letter.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injury, including severe pain and limited mobility, requiring medical attention.

incident_description:
This consumer contacted the hotline to report an LED light bulb that exploded the morning of June 20th, 2019 around 5:00AM.
The caller's wife alerted  him that she heard a bang sound along with the sound of glass breaking.
They went to investigate the sounds and discovered that one of the lights from a four bulb chandelier light had exploded.
He purchased the chandelier light May 9th, 2019 from a retailer in his area of New York with the four bulbs that were included.
He states that he and his wife noticed that three of the lights were bronze and one was clear but this is how it was packaged do they thought nothing of it.
The clear bulb was the bulb that exploded.
He contacted the place of purchase who offered to replace bulb, however caller states a replacement bulb is not the answer due to this not being a safe incident.
The light hasn't been used in possibly three weeks and was not turned on at time of incident
No injuries are being reported
Manufacturer unknown, caller did contact place of purchase customer support
justification: The incident involved an LED bulb exploding without causing injury, and the light was not in use at the time.

incident_description: My mother is 89 and is in assisted living. Before she entered the facility she had purchased a Southern Motions recliner with power recline from [REDACTED]. Unfortunately we then had to move her but she took her recliner with her to the facility. She has a little difficulty getting up and will sit to the front of the chair and not really rock, but take a couple of times trying to get up before she actually accomplishes the task. Last week she was in the ER two times with cuts and abrasions where the recliner had tipped over (to the front) because of her movement (or so the retailer states). We are really lucky she did not break any bones. One of the injuries was a pretty severe bump to the head. My mom weighs about 120 and her movements were not bouncing but just simply attempts to get up. There is no warning with the chair and I feel it is very unsafe, especially with the elderly or children. The retailer has reached out to the manufacturer (he says) but I feel this should be reported to someone who will test this and see if it is a significant safety issue. Too many elderly people living alone could be seriously hurt trying to get out of this chair. Thank you.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including a severe bump to the head, but no death or broken bones occurred.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting unsafe fabric on a sofa after she broke out in burns and large dark Keloid scars on her feet.
Around the end  of Feb 2019  a candle fell over on a metal tray, she went to put the candle out but somehow her sofa caught fire and she states that the material on the sofa melted then turned into plastic which then dripped onto her foot 
The caller went to Elwood Emergency/St Vincent Mercy Hospital where they diagnosed her with second degree burns on both feet but who she said did not treat her correctly which caused her feet to become infected so she went to Riverview Hospital in Noblesville, Indiana where she is aware that they have a burn center and this emergency room diagnosed third degree burns with some areas at second degree burns.  The medical professionals there have applied a process called Debride which is a painful scraping of the burned skin off to allow new skin to grow.
She is reporting the sofa as an extreme hazard because she states that there is no fire retentive on it which is why she believes that it burned so badly and so quickly which she describes as less than five minutes for the sofa to melt and burn completely.  She will be submitting pictures.

incident_description:
Product: Zinus 12" Green Tea Memory Foam Mattress: https://www.amazon.com/Zinus-Memory-Green-Mattress-Queen/dp/B00Q7EPSHI/
Issue: This mattress has a major design flaw: it sheds fiberglass through the mattress cover, which comes into contact with consumers and causes health issues!  I really believe this product should be banned from sale until it's redesigned. Could be affecting thousands of consumers without their knowledge.

I ordered the Zinus mattress off Amazon after spending a lot of time researching mattresses. It had a lot of positive reviews and was very affordable so I wanted to give it a shot. However, before it arrived I stumbled across a number of concerning reviews from people who ran into severe issues with the fiberglass contained in the mattress. An online search for "Zinus fiberglass" or a search in the Amazon reviews for "fiberglass" returns a significant number of complaints, some which are very startling.

It turns out that in order to give the all-foam mattress some fire resistance, Zinus wraps the foam layers in a fiberglass sock. Zinus acknowledges that they use fiberglass and say that it's an approved material. The issue is that the fiberglass sock easily sheds the glass fibers, and the thin polyester mattress cover does not prevent it from seeping through and coming into contact with consumers and their homes! There are videos on Youtube of people showing just how easily the fibers can flake off the fire sock.

Zinus states that the cover should not be removed, and sure enough a lot of the horror stories online come from people who didn't notice that warning or thought it wouldn't be an issue. When they take the outer covering off, the fiberglass sock is exposed - even the slightest friction can disturb the fiberglass and make it airborne. People reported that fiberglass infested their clothing and bedrooms, causing them to have to spend thousands of dollars after throwing out clothing and paying for remediation. To be fair, the mattress cover has a zipper, almost like it was intended to be washable - most consumers wouldn't know not to remove it unless they read a tiny warning on the tag.

I assumed that I wouldn't have any issues as long as I never removed the outer covering, so I never did. The mattress arrived without any damage and I put cotton sheets on it before using it. But I noticed I was waking up with small skin rashes after I had slept on the mattress for just a couple nights. On top of that, my eyes and throat began to feel slightly irritated like I was allergic to something (and I don't suffer from allergies). After a couple more nights, I started noticing that I would regularly feel small itches just laying in bed, like I was being poked by very small needles. This made me start wondering if the fiberglass could be leaking even though I didn't remove the cover.

Most alarmingly, around this time I started having a sensation like my throat was being constricted or obstructed. It was scary because I didn't know if it would keep getting worse and eventually restrict my breathing. I went to a doctor and mentioned that I wondered if it could be a reaction to the new mattress - he had no way of being able to tell if the mattress was the cause. He told me to come back if the tightness continued over the next couple days. 

I ended up shining a flashlight over my bed sheets since I had started to suspect that my mattress could be causing all the issues. Sure enough, I could easily see hundreds of miniscule glass fibers intertwined with my sheets! They could only be seen when light hit them at the right angle, and they were perfectly straight and clear. Somehow they had gotten all over my sheets and comforter, even the parts that never came in direct contact with the mattress. I also found dozens of fibers inside my pajamas that I had worn in bed! I realized at that point that all the itches and skin irritation had probably been caused by the leaking fiberglass.

I contacted both Zinus customer service and Amazon directly. Zinus only said that the fiberglass shouldn't leak and I probably had a defective one, and I should ask Amazon for a replacement. I strongly believe it wasn't an isolated defective mattress - this is a design flaw by Zinus. There's no way that a thin fabric cover should be the only barrier between a person and a layer of fiberglass, especially when they're moving around on the mattress and causing friction that could disturb that layer! Luckily Amazon took the mattress back because I would not have accepted a replacement. Based on other Zinus product reviews, the fiberglass issues are widespread across almost all of their mattresses. There are so many other reviews warning people not to buy the mattresses due to the fiberglass issues, but most consumers won't see these reviews because they're getting buried under thousands of positive reviews.

I got rid of the mattress thanks to the Amazon return, bought a new one from a different brand made in the USA, and washed my sheets multiple times. All of my symptoms (skin/eye irritation & throat constriction) disappeared within a couple days of me getting rid of the mattress! If I had all that fiberglass leaking and causing issues after only having the mattress for about a week, I can't imagine how bad the issue could get after sleeping on the mattress regularly for a year or more. It seems like Zinus is one of a few mattress companies that uses fiberglass socks as a cost-saving way to meet fire-resistance regulations, but they clearly aren't testing these designs to make sure the fiberglass will be contained inside the mattress.

It's terrible to think that kids and adults could be sleeping on these mattresses and suffering from chronic health issues, not having any clue that the issues are being caused by their mattress. People wouldn't be able to see the fiberglass with the naked eye and wouldn't find out about the issue unless they did their own research. I really hope it can be recalled and redesigned as soon as possible.
justification: The incident describes health issues like skin rashes, eye and throat irritation caused by fiberglass exposure, which qualifies as injury (severity 3). The widespread complaints and reviews suggest this is a likely occurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
The "Bath & Shower Seat" was purchased in Feb 2019 prior to my wife's orthopedic surgery. I assembled it according to instructions. On the second use the legs started to spread and the chair began to collapse while in use. Because I was on hand and able to help her up, she escaped severe injury.
Facts regarding this product failure: 1) The user was well below the maximum weight of 350lbs. 2) The bolts were plenty tight when the chair failed. 3) The legs are light tube aluminum and are subject to shear at the bolt holes. The material and design are inadequate for the intended use. (The attached photo shows the deformed hole of the leg from twisting of the leg under load.) 4) The product was only used two times before it failed. 5) The product was used as intended and not subject to any abuse.
The chair is dangerous as a devise especially made for bath /shower use for those with impaired mobility. Anyone with normal mobility would not need an assistive device. But when such a device fails being used by a person with impaired mobility, the result is dangerous and severe. The chair does not handle side loading. Such is how a person with impaired mobility would use the chair. (Such as gripping one edge of the chair to assist rising or sitting.) When the chair is subject to a moderate side load, the bolt to leg holes shear / deform, the legs begin to spread / rotating out, the threaded inserts in the seat begin to pull out, and the seat flexes. The result is that the legs continue to spread until failure. Now a person with impaired mobility is on the floor (or bottom of their tub) needing rescue / help!
justification: The incident involved a product failure that could have led to injury, especially for users with impaired mobility, and the description suggests such failures are likely under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
The product is called "Redi Shade - Original Pleated Paper Shade". It is a window shade made from paper, with an adhesive at one end that mounts to the top of the window shade. It comes with 2 clips that hold the pleats together to allow the height of the shade to be adjusted.

The problem is that the ends of the paper shade are razor sharp, and the paper is just sufficiently strong enough that it readily gives deep paper cuts. I got two paper cuts while installing the shades.  Additionally, the act of attaching the two enclosed clips is exactly the action that will most likely give the paper cut. That is because the shade had no external structural support, so it flops down when held in one hand. The other hand is forced to run a finger along the bottom of the shade to collect the pleats together so that the appropriate number of them can be clipped. But running the finger along the bottom of the shade is EXACTLY the action that will cause the paper cut.

One solution is to make the edges of the paper shade less sharp. A second solution is to warn the consumer that the paper edge should be made dull with some sort of instrument. I used a small piece of wood with a notch, and I ran it across the bottom edge 2-3 times to make it dull.
justification: The description confirms injuries (paper cuts) occurred during installation, and the design makes such injuries likely during normal use.

For example when the bed moves from elevated to non-elevated position it may crush the dog or cat that's underneath.  

I called Mattress Firm and Rize directly and they both referred me to their warranty and customer service department run by customatic.  I talked to Lauren from customatic but was told two things 1) she isn't willing to escalate the issue to get this looked at or fixed and 2) that its consumers responsibility to spot vulnerabilities and design oversight that may lead to safety issues. incident_description:
Christmas lights were hung along an unused fireplace hearth and worked for several days.  Then the lights quit.

The string was about 50 lamps, each 2.5 volts and 0.425 watts, manufactured by Chia Tsin Electric Co. Ltd. and tagged with the UL Listed Mark E106094.  

I found a burned side in one of the bulb sockets.  Being a Forensic Engineer, I dissected the socket to determine the cause of the failure.   I found one of the brass electrical contacts of the socket seriously bent, making the contact area of one of the wires of bulb a very small point rather than the normal longer contact area.  

The socket did not have any external mechanical damage (other than the melted and burned plastic), so the bent contact was definitely a defect in manufacturing.  

The point contact the subject contact made a high resistance connection to the wire of the bulb.  The heat carbonized the contact which increased the resistance.  Normally, an increase in the resistance of a high resistance connection will increase the heat being generated and a thermal runaway would occur, ultimately resulting in arcing.  In this case, however, the increased resistance lowered (the already low) current and essentially self-extinguished the process.

The lights were cycled daily, and the melting and subsequent re-solidifying of the plastic may have also helped to interrupt the current.  There was no arcing.

I subjected the plastic to a burn test.  The plastic burned and melted readily, but self-extinguished upon removal of the flame.  The melted plastic would drip while burning, but the drops would also self-extinguish.  I can see this could be a problem, however, if the dripping and burning plastic were to land on a present wrapped in tissue paper or other readily ignitable wrapping. 

UL has developed a Two Strike program for decorative lighting strings under which UL samples selected strings for evaluation twice each year.  Any nonconformance is a Strike, and the manufacturer is not allowed to use the UL Listed Mark until the root cause of the nonconformance is identified and corrected.  Two Strikes in a two-year period will result in the termination of its use of the UL Listed Mark. According to UL, Chia Tsin Electric Co Ltd has no Strikes, but its products have not been tested via the Market Survey Program during the past three years.
justification: The incident involved a manufacturing defect causing a high resistance connection and melting plastic, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a Robern recessed medicine cabinet, Model-MT24D4MDCR, 05/2012, and had it installed by bathroom contractor 06/2012.

On Thursday, 01/03/2019, I opened the medicine cabinet door to get some medicine and the large outside/inside mirrored door came loose at the top hinge and feel onto my forehead causing a one inch cut. The cut required "glueing" and bandage at a local urgent care facility.

On inspection of the medicine cabinet after the incident, I found that the door of the cabinet is attached with a two part hinge; part 1, is a small bracket that is attached to the cabinet with a single small machine screw, part 2, is the pivoting portion of the hinge assembly that attaches to the door, part 2 is attached to part 1 with 2 screws and part 2 is attached to the door with 2 screws. The falling door was the result of the small screw holding part 1 of the hinge assembly to the cabinet coming loose, thus disconnecting the door from the cabinet. Once the hinge assembly is put together, there is no way to check the status of this small screw. Looking at the vendor installation instruction (which I still have on file) there is no mention of the small screw being a locking screw, or of the installer having to use "[REDACTED]" to secure the screw.

Without using "[REDACTED]" to secure screws in the hinge assemble, or having a safety cable/strap to secure the door to the cabinet, this unit presents a true danger to consumers, as I can attest to.

My recommendation to the manufacturer would be to include a safety cable/strap attaching the for to the cabinet, and to include "[REDACTED]" with installation parts kit./
justification: The incident resulted in a one-inch cut requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests the issue could recur if the hinge screw is not secured properly, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
I am greatly concerned about a product that I have purchased tonight at Target.
The product is listed as  "bookshelf" and sold in the Target Furniture department.
https://www.target.com/p/9-cube-organizer-shelf-13-threshold-153/-/A-50253268?preselect=17424404#lnk=sametab

QUOTING TARGET WEB PAGE FOR THE PRODUCT:
9-Cube Organizer Shelf 13" - ThresholdÃÂ
"Highlights
Compatible with 13" storage bins and Threshold cube accessories.
Finished front and back.
Weight capacity is 30lb s per cube shelf.
Top shelf weight capacity is 80lbs
Required tools- Hex key (included)
ThresholdÃÂ 9 cube organizer has 9 convenient cube openings for storage and is compatible with 13" storage bins and ThresholdÃÂ cube accessories. This item features a finished front and back to allow for storage access from both sides and has a thick exterior frame. Can be displayed horizontally or vertically. Perfect for organizing any room in the house. This ThresholdÃÂ 9 cube organizer comes with all hardware included. To clean, wipe with a dry cloth.

Weight capacity is 30lbs per cube shelf.
Top shelf weight capacity is 80lbs "
END QUOTE 

I bought this product today and followed instructions to assemble.
The product is entirely unstable and unfit for sales in the United States.
For one, the structural support elements are short 1" x 1/4" wooden dowels that are inserted into pre-drilled holes in six 13" x 13" x 1/2" particle board.

The troubling thing about this unit is that the instructions explicitly state that the unit must be secured to wall studs by two 1 1/2" wall brackets.  However, the instructions also state that the provided metal bracket must be installed less than 1 1/2" from the edge of board "A".  Board "A" is 43" long.  At best, if you install at exactly 1" from the end, you end up with 41" to 40" being the distance between the metal brackets.  That distance does not concur with the spacing of a wall stud in residential construction.

In the US, most residential wall studs are 16" apart from center to center.  This means that it is IMPOSSIBLE to install this "bookcase" correctly.  It is not possible to install these brackets under the bookshelf's shelf as instructed AND simultaneously install into a wall stud 39" to 41" apart.

Therefore, when installed correctly, one or both of the wall mounted brackets will not be installed into a wall stud.  If you are putting this particular unit against a wall, the wall stud can not be located 1 " from the corner of the dry wall.  That's not where a stud would be located.

Even more troubling is that the manufacturer may be overstating the mass capability of the unit.  Upon lateral force (like a child pushing on the side of the product), the product will not withstand significant lateral motion.  There are six 13" square pieces of wood vertically stacked using wooden dowels that are only 1 1/2" inches long.  These dowels barely mate to the adjacent 13" square wooden piece through holes in the two shelves.

I am quite concerned that this particular unit will lead to infant or child death because the wall unit will fall on the child or toddler that is climbing on this unit.  It should not be listed as a "bookcase" at all.  It should be listed as a "wall unit" because the product REQUIRES brackets to securely hold the furnishing against a wall. 

More to the point, if a child begins crawling on the side or front of the unit and if a consumer follows the manufacturer instructions, you could have literally 180 lbs of material falling on the toddler climbing on the unstable "bookcase".

This product needs investigation and I suggest withdrawal from all Target stores nationally.  More importantly, the product needs to be recalled such that no infants or toddlers are harmed by incorrect installation of this wall unit.   It's clear that if a small child (toddler) was to lean against the top of the unit's side, the deflection could collapse the entire bookcase.  If the manufacturer's claim of 30lbs per shelf slot is filled by a consumer, the total mass in the product would be 30 x 9 = 270 lbs.  Plus, the wall unit itself appears to be around 40-50 lbs at minimum and not including any objects on the top of the unit.  

Though I practiced pediatrics for 19 years, I've never submitted a CPSC report until tonight.  This product needs review by CPSC in order to evaluate if other infants and children have been harmed this product.  Also, I'd like to suggest a voluntary recall of the existing sold products by Target because these "bookcases" are not "bookcases" at all.  With the Target instructions clearly stating "must be" attached to wall before use, it's not a bookcase but a WALL UNIT.
justification: The product's design flaws pose a significant risk of injury or death, especially to children, due to potential collapse.

incident_description:
I have been told by Duke University who tests ACMI products for the AP seal that their assumption of "normal use" for a Sharpie alcohol-based permanent marking pen is for one person drawing approximately 10 inches once per day.  However, schools have noted the AP seal on the package and no definition of "normal use" is included on the package.  My daughter's school is using the product as a classroom art supply, to be used by up to 20 students in a session to draw art projects, polluting the air beyond normal use as was tested for in marginally ventilated classrooms (no cross ventilation present for example).  When I called the Sharpie corp. customer service line I was told by three representatives that 20 5 year olds using the pens for art in a classroom is considered "normal use", which is not true and apparently putting children at risk.  

Duke University testing staff sent the following to me.  I see CPSC ran a test with them studying classroom use, but I don't see the study listed on your website.  What are your conclusions regarding classroom use safety per the study?

My daughter, who only gets a headache when she is very ill, had a headache and burning eyes after being exposed to the pens in a Kindergarten classroom art project in September 2018 at White Oak Elementary School in Westlake Village.  Another child also experienced burnings eyes at that time.

Exposure Study Summary 
We evaluated solvent exposure to professional graphic artists who were using both solvent-
containing spray fixatives and xylene-containing markers. The 8 hour time weighted average 
exposures to xylene to 15 artists using these markers ranged from 0.006 to 0.54 ppm. Only those 
artists who used 
solvent-containing aerosols had excessive symptoms of narcosis and mucous 
membrane irritation. 
 
In a second study done in conjunction with the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), 
we evaluated exposures to white board marker solvents from use of markers containing methyl 
isobutyl ketone (MIBK) and n-butyl acetate (NBA). CPSC specifically chose the markers for 
these studies after reviewing generic formulations for whiteboard markers certified by ACMI. 
Two exposure studies were done in poorly ventilated (0.5 air changes per hour) rooms: an 
unventilated 230 m
3
 room and a 237 m
3
 ventilated classroom. Markers were used for 30 minutes. 
Samples were taken for 30 minutes at the breathing zone and for 3.5 hours at a background 
location, 4 m from the work area after marker use had ended. One, 3 or 4 users worked with 
markers in the unventilated room. 1, 2 or 4 users worked with markers in the ventilated school 
room. The dilutional ventilation equation was used to determine background exposures 
associated with use of these markers by 25 users.  
 
In the unventilated room, personal MIBK exposures during 30 minutes of use ranged from 0.87 
to 1.75 ppm and background exposures ranged from 0.37-0.93 ppm depending on the number of 
users. For the n-butyl acetate component, personal exposures during 30 minutes of use ranged 
from 0.21-0.27 ppm and background exposures ranged from <0.06-0.23 ppm depending on the 
number of users.  
 
Using the dilutional ventilation equation to project exposures where there would be 25 users in 
an unventilated room, the expected maximum 4 hour average exposure would be 5.3 ppm for 
MIBK and 2.0 ppm for NBA. In a classroom setting the expected maximum 4 hour average 
exposure would be 4.1 ppm for MIBK and 1.6 ppm for NBA.  
 
 
Reference 
 
([REDACTED]). See Pertinent Toxicological Issues: Solvent-Based Markers.
justification: The incident describes children experiencing headaches and burning eyes due to exposure to marker solvents, indicating injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) given the reported symptoms and classroom usage scenario.

I have informed La-Z-Boy of this condition but they decline any remedy.

incident_description: We purchased a carriage bed for our 3 year old daughter.  She is now almost 5 and we heard a cry from her bedroom about an hour after she had been put to bed.  We ran into the room and found her with her head trapped in the metal frame and the bars pinching her neck as she struggled to get out.  She had climbed up the canopy while sleeping and somehow pushed her head through the metal details of the bed and then slipped down and was unable to get her head back out.  As she struggled she moved further down the canopy/headboard and this caused her neck to be pinned between the metal bars.  If we had already been asleep when this accident occurred there is no doubt this would have been a tragedy and we would have lost our baby girl.  We are very conscientious parents and have childproofed our home. We never thought this bed could be dangerous but now we know it should not be used in childrenÃÂs bedrooms.
justification: The child's neck was pinned between metal bars, posing a life-threatening situation, which indicates a high severity level.
