incident_description:
Merced Glider, Pottery Barn Kids 

On several occasions last spring, as I was reaching towards a nearby side table from a seated position in this glider, I noticed the chair tip sideways and had to shift my balance to make sure it returned fully to the floor. On July 7, 2018, my father was holding my 5 month-old daughter in his right arm and attempted to sit in the chair by reaching behind himself with his left hand (to steady himself on the arm rest), and the chair tipped completely over on its side. My father fell and in the process, dropped the baby. Fortunately, nobody was hurt in the incident. 
I called Pottery Barn and they expedited delivery of a replacement chair while noting that there were no such complaints on file and that hopefully this was an isolated incident. The replacement chair arrived today (September 18, 2018) and as I tested the chair, I was easily able to replicate the tipping over. I am told I will receive a full refund, but the representative again articulated that there were no such complaints on file. I simply cannot be the only person who has had a similar experience with this chair.
Not only is this glider unsafe to sit in, but as it is an item for a babyÃÂs room, it is unsafe for a baby to ÃÂcruiseÃÂ on. It worries me greatly to think of a baby who is just learning to walk try to pull himself up by reaching to the arm of the chair, only to have the chair turn over on him. 
IÃÂve never made such a complaint and my attitude as a mother is a fairly laid-back one. However, I find it unconscionable knowing that this product is in many homes and listed on numerous ÃÂBest Chairs for BabyÃÂs RoomÃÂ articles without acknowledgement of a serious design flaw.
justification: The incident involved the chair tipping over, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is 'possible' as the issue was replicated and could occur again.

incident_description:
Sir/Mam:

     Last Friday I sat on my desk chair, I leaned-back using my back.......and something "snapped".  Now, I knew these "Chinese-made chairs" are made "to see how fast they come off the assembly-line", but Holy Crap !!!!!!

Two weeks ago, this pantry...which weighed several hundred pounds...began to tilt over toward me. before I could react, the unit collapsed straight down upon itself, sparing me from certain injury. incident_description:
We purchased a 3-bulb pack of 40-watt GE Reveal decorative G25 bulbs from a local Lowe's Home Center on 1 July 2018. Later in the month, one bulb failed within 24 hours of being inserted in a bathroom fixture; for a second bulb, the glass fell out of the base and hung by the wires within a day of being inserted, then fell into the sink and shattered when we attempted to remove it from the fixture.

The quick failure of the first bulb was obviously a trait of poor reliability, not worthy of the money paid. The failure of the second bulb was an obvious safety hazard, resulting in broken glass (including some very fine particles of glass) in the sink and on the counter top and floor, as well as the difficulty of removing the empty base with the light switch off and using a pair of pliers while another person held a flashlight in the darkened room.
justification: The incident involved a safety hazard with broken glass but no reported injury.

After further Inspection, what seemed like a sturdy product has now literally EXPLODED all over my living room wood floors. NO, no one burglarized my house. NO, no one smashed into it. NO, NOTHING was on top of the table. We rarely if EVER even SIT in that section of our house but here we are with glass EVERYWHERE!

But hey! I know I purchased extra protection so this will be no problem. I called Bob's customer service at 4:00pmto get this rectified. I was cool calm and collected because I just KNEW, this is clearly a no brainer. Spoke with [REDACTED]- very nice woman, Informed her of the issue. However, to my UTTER DISDAIN, she tells me even though I have extra coverage and even though it IS covered, they will not be able to replace the item because "unless it was accidental damage, goof proof does not cover that".
I beg your pardon??????
Ok [REDACTED], thank you, but let me speak to your supervisor please. After about 10mins of hold time I'm now transferred to [REDACTED], the account manager. [REDACTED] went over all the warranties I had in place with a fine tooth comb only to tell me even though it is covered, it is essentially, NOT COVERED.
Why?
"Well because you cant provide a reason as to why it broke, then we cant replace it. So yes, even though your warranties DO cover your purchase, because its NOT accidental, then we cant send a technician out"
What kinda [REDACTED] is this!??

So you're telling me, if I had called and said, "sorry, I tripped and fell into my table and it broke" THEN, you would replace it but because your product CLEARLY is defective and flimsy, then, you cant? So what is the point of your EXTRA protection? How does that make ANY sense??
CLEARLY Bob's Furniture, doesnt believe its clientele has a modicum of sense. CLEARLY they believe they can insult your Intelligence and get away with it. CLEARLY, even if you're a loyal customer, even AFTER they disserviced you in the past and you forgave them and STILL went back and made purchases and paid your bill on time AND purchase extra protection - IT DOES NOT MATTER!!!! 
I am hurt. I am angry. I am DISGUSTED. I am flabbergasted. I am downright offended. I will NOT stop until my item is replaced or I'm compensated. At this point, I dont even want this despicable excuse of workmanship in my home...and for BOBS DISCOUNT FURNITURE to offer anything less is a disgrace!!!!

Pictures and Video attached.

Friends and family, if you've EVER wanted to help me ever in life, please SHARE, RETWEET and IG this PLEASE.
justification: The incident involves a defective product causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
July 17, 2018

[REDACTED]
Chief Executive Officer
Mattress Finn, Inc.
5815 Gulf Freeway
Houston. Texas 77023

Re: customer 
Dear Mr. [REDACTED]:
In response to your many robo-calls attempting to survey my satisfaction for recent purchases from Mattress Firm, I am requesting a refund of the $107.79 (including tax) delivery charge for buying my second (more expensive no less) mattress, a result of a most unsatisfactory experience.

Because of ongoing back pain issues requiring months of physical therapy, on June 6, 2018 - without performing my usual online due diligence - I walked into one of your stores and purchased a Serta Blue Touch foam mattress. If I ever knew I would be buying something with such a noxious chemical odor that may not dissipate for months (if ever), I would never have made the purchase.

I felt like I was sleeping on a block of carcinogens. In fact, I had to stay on the couch for the first few nights, the smell being that strong. I contacted Serta whose only simplistic and unrealistic advice was to let it air out for a day. I actually stripped off the bedding daily for 14 days with the chemical odor absorbed right into my pillows.

Mattress Firm's salesmen offered two ludicrous suggestions: 1) place cut Granny Smith apples skin-side down on the mattress to absorb the odor (I wasted several good pieces of fruit), and 2) walk on the mattress to release the gasses from the foam bubbles (I injured my foot and almost fell off the bed).

After two weeks of tortured sleep with my throat burning and intermittent coughing nightly, on July 2 - my
bedroom constantly smelling like a [REDACTED] factory - I sent it back and instead bought a Sealy spring mattress.

Having had free delivery for my first purchase, I see no reason whatsoever for my having to pay #107. 79 for
delivery of my second purchase. Though I understand that some consumers want to return a mattress they ultimately may not find completely comfortable (the foam one was actually good for my back), in order to breathe clearly again at night, I had no choice but to return the Serta to safeguard my health.

Who knows what's going into unsuspecting consumers' lungs and into the environment? This mattress should
Immediately be taken off the market. It is a defective product.

Thank you for your prompt attention. I have not yet posted any online reviews of your company or Serta regarding this incident.  Please don't make me regret having done business with Mattress Firm.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The customer experienced physical discomfort and injury (foot injury) due to the mattress odor and subsequent actions, and the likelihood of such incidents is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description:
The LED light bulb in our children's bedroom ceiling fan started smoking A LOT.  I turned off the light switch, which powers the light fixture part of the fan.  When I removed the bulb it was hot and there are signs of melting on the end of the light bulb and in the light socket.  There was a smokey, chemical, smell throughout the house.  The ceiling fan and the other lights on the fan still work, but the fixture is now ruined and the entire fan will need to be replaced.  The light fixture part of the ceiling fan is rated for 3 60W bulbs and is on a dimmer switch and the LED light bulbs are dimmable.  The other 2 light bulbs in the fixture are a different type of dimmable LED bulbs and still work OK.  I do not know the make or model of the ceiling fan.  I had bought the LED light bulbs at our local Home Depot not too long ago (I believe within the last 6 months to a year).  The burned out LED light bulb info is below:

EcoSmart 8.5W (60W replacement), 120V, 4 pack, A19, LED Soft White Dimmable Classic Glass Light Bulb.
SKU#: 1002459588
Model#: B7FA1960WESQD02

I had checked the CPSC website and I do not see any recent recall for this bulb.
justification: The incident involved a smoking LED bulb causing damage to the fixture but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
We converted our toddler's crib into a full size bed using a conversion kit made by the same manufacturer of the crib (Bertini/Dorel Living). During the middle of the night, our son rolled into the space between the footboard and the standard full-size mattress. Our son's head got trapped in this space and he was found in the morning, severely injured and barely conscious. He was rushed to the hospital, and later admitted to ICU. The emergency room doctor concluded the injuries he sustained were due to the trauma caused by the compression of his head in between the footboard and mattress/box spring.  His swelling, due to the compression, became so severe that he was intubated for concern that the swelling would cause his airway to be constricted.  Doctors told us that had we found him later, or if his head had been turned the other way, he would have most likely suffocated and died.  

Main concern with this product is when conversion of the crib with kit to a full size bed results in a gap between the footboard and mattress/box spring that is unsafe for children and can result in a child getting stuck in between, causing serious injury or even death.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries requiring ICU admission and intubation, with a high risk of death, indicating a severity level of 4.

incident_description:

I contacted the retailer in person, Godby Furniture of Noblesville IN, on 8/16/18.  Told them of the incident.  Showed them pictures.  They refused my requests of removing the FLEXSTEEL glass top furniture, cleaning up the shattered glass, and replacing the items with non glass items.  Godby's stand is that the warranty was up on 10/6/17 ( 1 year).
I have pictures of the incident.
I have contacted an attorney.
justification: The incident involved an exploding glass table with no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the rarity of such events but not unheard of.

incident_description:

It was moved so that we can clean under the table and when we slide the table on the floor it collapsed and the two table tops flew down, hitting and damaging the adjacent wall.The table has two tops that when extended can accommodate 10 people. The company is claimed to have compliance with ISO 9001....

incident_description: I purchased a leather kivik sectional sofa from ikea in May 2016. I had not used it on a regular basis until I moved to a new home several months ago. When I started using the sofa on a regular basis, I noticed a painful, burning rash on my elbow and ankle where the bare skin had made contact with the sofa. In addition to the rash, I get headaches & it exacerbates my asthma. The problem was worse when my air conditioner was not working and the indoor temperature in my home exceeded eighty degrees. Upon further investigation, I discovered that the sofa was made in China. I suspect the problem is due to antifungal chemicals.
justification: The incident describes a painful rash, headaches, and exacerbated asthma, which are injuries caused by contact with the sofa.

incident_description:
Had an office chair purchased at Staples break, causing me to fall over backwards.  This chair was manufactured 1/16/12, and I am not sure of the exact purchase date.  Label on bottom describes it as Torrent Chair item #20224 SKU 923571.  Checked Staples Website, and chair is still available at this link.

https://www.staples.com/Staples-Torrent-Bonded-Leather-Managers-Chair-Black/product_923571

When I sat on the chair this morning, the dolly(with five wheels cracked in half and I fell backwards.  I understand this is a 6 year old consumer grade(not commercial grade) product, but the dolly should have not broken in half and this product needs to be recalled.  Also, this chair was only used only by average weight people, and should not have broken.
justification: The incident involved a chair breaking and causing a fall, but there was no mention of injury, only the potential for harm.

incident_description: I bought a couch from Laz-Boy that was delivered this past Saturday. The initial problem was the color was grey and not chocolate brown. I did notice a chemical new couch odor coming from it on delivery but did not realize the extent until I woke up the next morning with a severe headache and then half way down the stairs the couch odor was noticeably overpowering. The couch is in a closed environment and has taken over my 1200 sq ft home including the closets upstairs. I do not have an area to remove the couch to and it is currently in my living room covered with two sheets and two blankets trying to minimize the effects of the chemical odor it is emitting and it is still overpowering. I currently have daily headaches, my eyes and nose sting and have been noticing increasing shortness of breath going up the stairs the last three days. I am limiting my time downstairs where the new couch is and currently staying in a bedroom with the door closed. I have ceiling fans on downstairs and upstairs, I have the AC fan running continuously trying and force the odor out of my place. It is summer time so it is hard to leave the doors open but I have been waking up early in morning with headaches and leaving the front door open but it has to be closed all other times. I have been working with Laz-boy to get the couch out of here asap due to the overpowering odor. It was scheduled for Wednesday pick up but that fell through the cracks and is now scheduled for this Tuesday pick up. I question if that is going to happen. I am very concerned about the current and future toxic effects of this overpowering odor being emitted from the Laz-boy couch. I requested quality control to visit my home to help them understand this issue but they were not interested and I was told that the delivery/pick up crew with do the evaluation.  I am having health issues from the odor being emitted from this couch and I believe that this should not be happening to me (or anyone else) just because I bought a new couch.
justification: The incident involves health issues like headaches, eye and nose stinging, and shortness of breath due to chemical odor from the couch, indicating injury.

I believe the manufacturers should have a 'safety' release lever to prevent injuries such as this.

The type of bed is the Spongebob / Dora the Explore Nickelodeon Loft Bed by Lea Furnitures. I tried to reach out to the manufacturer but found that they went out of business.

incident_description:
A compact fluorescent bulb from Bright Effects, model# L65TN began to overheat and melt causing burning hot plastic droplets to fall from the light.  

The bulb was screwed into a standard ceiling mount glazed porcelain incandescent lampholder and was not in an enclosure.

I happened to be walking through my basement when I saw a little smoke coming from a The Home Depot bag.  Puzzled how a bag could suddenly start smoking I opened the bag to see what was inside when I saw a flash of orange drop into the bag from above.  I looked up and saw this bulb glowing a bright orange and smoking.  I turned off the light switch and moments later the bulb stopped glowing. 

After it cooled I removed the bulb from the lampholder and inspected it to find the bulb was melting from the heat and dripping burning plastic down.

This is clearly a fire hazard as if I hadn't been in the basement at that very moment, the bulb may have caught fire burning the wood the lampholder was mounted to and/or the dripping plastic may have started a fire below.
justification: The incident involved a bulb overheating and melting, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

I weigh 300lbs, the chair and bench are rated for 400lbs.

After using the chair for a few days, I noticed it getting wobbly/unstable, and during one shower, the chair started listing heavily to the left.

I managed to stand without falling or slipping off the chair, but only because of a grab bar. Had I not had a grab bar, I would have fallen.

I unscrewed the bolts from the chair to check if something had gone wrong, and I noticed two things: 1) two of the bolts had bent horribly, making it very hard to unscrew from the underside of the bench. 2) the center piece of the legs had started to bend in the middle.

The same issues were starting to happen with the bench, but not as severe, so I returned both to amazon.com for a refund
justification: The chair became unstable and could have caused a fall, but no injury occurred due to the presence of a grab bar.

incident_description: 2-month old infant being bathed in an adult bathtub by mother while in a Bumbo seat.  Faucet may have been left running. EMS activated, infant transported to [REDACTED] and died later (near drowning).

incident_description: The wall clock fell on the floor and the glass cover shattered to pieces.  It was hung safely on the wall, for five years. The plastic had dripped onto the light lens and also damaged the fixtures at the contact ends.   I worked with Nedco in Mississauga Ontario for the retro fit program.  When looking up the Osram bulbs on line, they are made by Ledvance.  The two models that were recalled were [REDACTED] and [REDACTED]  My model number is 73313-0, which did not have a recall.  The on-line lamp recall information said to call Ledvance.  My contact there has been [REDACTED].  The first bulb that melted was returned for product testing and the second bulb that was discovered on Jan 5, 2018 was not retuned but [REDACTED] was notified.  Ledvance replaced all the LED bulbs at my request.  I was given direction by [REDACTED] to purchase 2 new fixtures from Nedco and have them installed.  I would be reimbursed for the costs.  I had this completed and [REDACTED] had [REDACTED] at XL Specialty Insurance Company contact me.  I sent her my invoices as she requested.  [REDACTED] contacted my and said she would email me the release and when it is returned the cheque would be issued.  A couple emails have gone back and forth regarding the release as this was not disclosed until after I submitted my invoices as instructed.  I feel at this point the company went ahead with instructing me to spend money on the replacements and is now refusing to make payment as they require a release of liability to make the payment. Not only does the product create a huge safety concern but Ledvance would like to remove themselves form the liability.
justification: The incident involved melting bulbs and fixture damage but no reported injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been noted but are not widespread.

incident_description: I purchased a Tempurpedic Mattress direct about 10 years ago. The past 4 months and counting I have suffered from allergic outbreaks of giant hives, chemical burns, lip & eye swelling and close to Anaphylaxis. After months of steroid injections, blood work and pills it was found that I have now an extreme Polyurethane TDI sensitivity due to the long term exposure and break down of the memory foam in the Tempurpedic. Years of off gassing and the foam break down has left me with a hyper sensitivity to the material which is also found in many other products. The major outbreaks landing me in the hospital or doctors resulted at night after laying in the bed. I can no longer take steroids and  it is very difficult to avoid products with PU in it and therefore am suffering and going to start Xoliar injections next. Tempurpedic when contacted and confronted with months of horrific pictures showing the hives and chemical burns on my body, was very apologetic and quick to refund in full the price of the bed purchase 10 years ago. I additionally submitted medical co-pays, medication and time of work due to the damages and they are, a month later, stating it is still under review. I have since contacted a lawyer who is reviewing the information. Incident Description: On 2/11/2018 the following occurred (note that the description that follows is almost exactly what I have written to the owner of the company that made the candle):

When I initially lit the wick, I noticed something different about this particular candle. In most tinned candles, the flame is restricted to the wick, which melts a tiny pool of wax immediately surrounding the wick, while the remainder of the wax body is solid. With this candle, the entire candle wax body liquefied soon after the wick was lit, and this occurred every time I used the candle. I noted it was odd but hadn't heard that this was a concern, so I continued to use the candle. I also noticed that the metal container would become extremely hot while the candle burned, so I began to put the tin on a notepad in case the heat damaged my furniture.On the night of the fire, the wick and wax were about ÃÂ¥.&"high (greater than the recommended W' where you are advised to not bum the candle further) and I noted that I wouldn't be able to bum it for much longer that evening. I placed the metal lid to the container next to the candle.

Initially, the candle burned just as it had been burning whenever I lit it: the wax liquefied and the flame was restricted to the tiny wick. I was watching TV in the bedroom and was not paying attention to the candle when I happened to tum to view the flame and was shocked to see that the tiny flame had become a huge candle wax fire.The entire wax body was on fire, and the previously tiny flame was now a small fireball, about 3" wide and burning about 5 -6" above the rim of the tin. I was shocked and I panicked. In my panicky state, as I was attempting to snuff out the fire, I hit the candle and the metal container fell onto the floor. As the container fell, burning wax splattered onto the carpeting, creating little fires wherever the wax hit the carpeting. The hot metal container fused into the carpeting upon contact. The notebook that I had placed the candle upon was scorched. Aside from the notebook and carpeting, nothing else was harmed.

I immediately began to research what had happened to me and was surprised to learn that the highly reflective interior surface of the container contributed to the liquefying of the entire wax candle, setting me up for a candle wax fire. I've read about causing a wax fire by using water, but this was not my case. There were no warnings on the product that this could happen; in fact the product label states that "Every time the candle is lit, it is preferable to make the wax melt over its whole surface before extinguishing it."Additionally, the instructions state that "Dispose when 1 to 2 mm of wax remain in container." I am perplexed that L'Occitane is recommending procedures that are dangerous and may be setting up customers for candle wax fires.
 
Obviously the highly reflective metal interior of the metal container heated the wax to its flash point, causing a candle wax fire. There were no warnings on the instructions that this could occur - in fact, the instructions  may contribute to a candle wax fire by recommending that:
a) the entire wax surface should melt when in use; and
b) it is advisable to dispose of the container when 1 - 2 mm of wax remain in container.

The consumer was not bodily injured;she suffered property damage.

The consumer stated that she has used other products by the manufacturer but this is the first time that she used one of their candles.
justification: The incident involved property damage (scorched notebook and carpet) but no bodily injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue appears specific to this candle's design but not widespread across all products.

justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including cuts and a gash, but no death or severe injury was reported.

incident_description: This product is a pendant light fixture with several large glass bulbs that was installed above a glass dining table. I want to report that after turning the light on for several minuter one of the glass bulbs fell off and bounced off of the glass table, ten minutes later another glass bulb fell from the fixture and shattered on the glass table. I want to report this as a safety hazard because fortunately this all happened after we had dinner and was not sitting at the table at the time. This was not an install issue, the fixture comes with 40 watt light bulbs and become intensely hot within a minute of turning on so I suspect that the glass and metal base becomes so hot that it expands and therefore the light bulb becomes loose falls off the fixture. I have reported this to the seller (Lampsplus.com) and intend to return the item because it is hazardous and can cause serious injury.
justification: Glass bulbs fell and shattered, but no one was injured as the table was unoccupied at the time.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that he purchased a triple bed bunkbed for his three sons online April 14, 2018 but when they were delivered April 18, 2018 and there was an odd odor emitting from them.
The triple bunkbeds are painted white.
The caller purchased a few lead testers from the nearby home supplies store.
He states that the first test result for lead was 500 the second result of lead test 150.
He then sent the tests to Microlab in Baltimore, Maryland and they returned the tests to the consumer with results of 600 times the amount of lead allowed.
The caller has contacted the online seller, not the manufacturer yet but he does intend to contact the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves a product with high lead levels, posing a potential health risk, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description:
We purchased a Bistro patio set from Home Depot 7/12/17.  We purchased it for our garage the set was never outside in the weather.February of 2017 we were sitting in the garage watching TV my husband leaned his back against the chair the chair snapped and he fell backwards almost hit his head on a table saw.  We took the set back we like it so we thought it was a fluke thing and got another set.
On 3/17/18 it happened again this time my husband leaned froward and the chair snapped and her fell forward on to his knees which one of the knees had been replaced. I told the manager how unsafe this product is and it should be removed the the floor.  I asked for the contact information of the manufacture.  I contacted them on 3/19/17 they said someone would get back with me in 24-48 hours no every contacted me.  I called them 3 more times and was told the same thing again no on contacted me.  The manufacture is Yotio their phone number is [REDACTED their email address is customerservice@yotrious.com.  I emailed them pictures of the chair and the receipts. Yotrio did give me a case # [REDACTED].  I believe that this product is very dangerous and should not be sold and removed from the stores before someone really get injured badly.

incident_description: My adult son was seated in my IKEA Poang chair when the wooden chair snapped, causing him to fall to the floor. The chair was beyond repair (I have pictures). The chair is advertised to hold up to 375 lbs. My son weighs at least 75 lbs less than that. I wrote to the company through their website on 4/15 and received an auto reply that they would respond in 3-5 days. To date, I have had no response from the company.
justification: The chair broke causing a fall, but there is no mention of injury, only property damage and lack of response from the company.

incident_description: An Osram Sylvania halogen bulb attached to a ceiling fan blew out and the lens portion of the lamp separated from the main body of the lamp and fell onto the carpet bellow, melting the surface of the carpet and almost burning my granddaughter's hand. I contacted Sylvania and they sent me a [REDACTED] card with some remuneration towards the bulb but never addressed the burned carpet issue.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned carpet) and nearly caused injury (almost burned hand), but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Company advertises and sells white resin folding chairs that are rated at 1,000 lb. capacity.

In 2016, consumer purchased eight (8) of these chairs.  The chairs were used seasonally and were subject to normal residential use.

In 2017, one of the chairs snapped and broke while an individual was seated.

In 2018, a second chair also snapped and broke while an individual was seated.

Company was contacted and notified of safety concerns and potential for injury. 

Chairs that are advertised and sold as being rated for 1,000 lb. capacity should not break while individuals are seated.
justification: Chairs broke while in use, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was watching TV in the living room. My honey was making bread dough in the kitchen. Out of the blue a light bulb exploded that had been installed in a wall mounted socket near the ceiling. It did not have a cover. Glass went everywhere. Some of it hit my head. Some went into the bread my honey was cooking. The bulb had been working fine... I don't remember when it was purchased. The bulb was not subjected to any trauma or abuse before this happened. It was totally out of the blue! It shattered into many many small pieces of glass. Enough fragments were found to positively identify the bulb.
justification: The incident resulted in glass hitting the person's head, indicating an injury, and the occurrence is unlikely as the bulb exploded unexpectedly without prior signs of failure.

incident_description: I had purchased a 2 pack of GE Lighting 78797 Energy-Efficient Crystal Clear 53-Watt (75-watt replacement) 1050-Lumen A19 Light Bulb with Medium Base on April 18, 2017. I estimate that the bulb was installed in a bathroom light fixture about 3 to 6 months ago. On April 22, 2018, I was cleaning the sink in the bathroom when the bulb exploded showering the entire room with glass that went everywhere. I had bits of broken glass on me and in my hair. I was fortunate that I happened to be looking down at the time otherwise some of the glass particles could have landed in my eye. I was not doing anything with the bulb or the fixture at the time; it just exploded while the light was on. The bulb was not installed in an enclosed fixture so there should have been no issues with heat retention. In all of the years that I have used light bulbs I have never had one explode like this before. I feel that this is an unsafe product.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb causing glass particles to land on the person, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: My husband was sitting in our swivel rocker Memorial weekend when it broke out of thin air.  Luckily no one was hurt; it could have been so much worse. Had it happened any earlier, a new orn baby could have been injured.  Later that weekend I looked online to see if there a replacement base was available, in which I discovered a recall for that very same reason. I'm not sure how we weren't aware; possibly because the patio set was an anniversary gift. We have taken very good care of this patio set, and it's very frustrating to know this could have been prevented.
justification: The swivel rocker broke unexpectedly, but no one was injured. The recall suggests this is a known issue, making recurrence likely.

incident_description:
(03/01/2018) The consumer stated that the industrial-size staples in the seat of the bar stool are sticking up. As soon as her son sat down on the stool, he was scratched on his bottom. The scratch is about 3 inches but the staple did not puncture his skin.

No medical attention was required.

The consumer stated that another one of the bar stools had to be replaced because the staples were sticking up in the seat of the product.

The consumer contacted the firm's corporate office and was advised that they could not help her. She was referred to the place of purchase. After several calls to the store, the consumer had to send an email before she could get someone to help her. She sent the email on 3/8. The store offered to replace the bar stool.
justification: The incident involved a scratch from a staple but no puncture or medical attention was required, indicating no injury. The recurrence of the issue with another bar stool suggests the likelihood is high.

incident_description: I have a Tainoki acrylic office chair that I purchased at Homegoods in 2017.  When I sat on the chair yesterday, the chair snapped in half, rolled away from me and I fell to the ground.  I hurt my left elbow and upper back.
justification: The chair broke, causing a fall that resulted in injury to the elbow and upper back.

incident_description: We have had 5 of the 6 Hampton Bay swivel chairs break over the past three months. Thankfully no one was seriously hurt but 3 people sustained minor scratches and bruises. I would say 5 out of six in a short period of time would constitute a manufacturer defect!
justification: 3 people sustained minor injuries, and the high failure rate suggests a likely recurring issue.

incident_description:
Last night at 4 AM we heard a loud bang in the bedroom where we were sleeping and then what sounded like rain.  
We couldn't figure out what it was - turned on the light and were dumbstruck to see that the glass top on the cabinet that has held our TV for the past  5 years simply exploded into small glass pieces which were continuing to crackle and expand even as we looked at it.
justification: The incident involved property damage (glass top explosion) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased a mattress online from NectarSleep.com because their web site states that the mattresses are Certipur-US certified. Their web site FAQ's also state that the mattresses are certified by 5 other rating groups to be free from known harmful chemicals and gasses, VOC's and many other chemicals as listed on their site. They also state that off-gassing is limited or non-existent and any odor should dissipate within a few days. I have now had this bed opened in a well ventilated bedroom since February 16, 2018 and the out-gassing has made the bedroom unusable due to the toxic odor. If we leave the bedroom door open, the odor permeates the rest of the house making it unlivable as well. I have unzipped the provided mattress cover to allow more air to circulate but that makes the odor even worse. I moved the mattress to the garage hoping that the odor would dissipate. I thought that had worked so I moved the bed back inside, but within a few minutes, the toxic odor had returned. You can smell the bed from outside the house when the bedroom window is open.  It has now been about 6 weeks since opening the bed and everyone who has been in the house has complained of nose, throat, eye and lung irritation as well as a toxic taste in their mouths that won't go away. On March 24, 2018, Nectar removed the bed. We have ventilated the room but the odor has permeated everything in the room including drapes, carpeting, clothing, bed linens and everything else in the room. The bed which I was going to replace with the Nectar had to be removed (which I paid for) because it also was contaminated by the odor from the Nectar bed.
justification: The incident caused nose, throat, eye, and lung irritation to multiple people, indicating injury, but no death was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as such severe reactions are not common with most mattress purchases.

incident_description:
I purchased a wall mount for a TV projector. The mount extends about 30 inches from the wall and consists of two pieces - a metal tube that actually connects to the wall ("wall mount") and a metal bracket that bolts onto the projector ("projector mount"). The projector mount connects to the wall mount via a metal rectangle that sits atop the projector mount. This metal piece slides into a bracket on the bottom of the wall mount.  Within a second of connecting the projector mount to the wall mount, the rectangular piece failed causing the entire projector to fall.  Fortunately I was still holding on to it, so no damage or injury occurred. But, this is a product designed to hole a 15-30 pound object above a person's head, and could have caused a fatality had it failed after installation.  

The metal rectangle is connected to the projector mount via two small bolts. The bolts are barely threaded onto the rectangle - each only goes in to the second thread of the bolt. There is no nut on the other end to secure the bolts, no loctite to secure the threads, and no welds to provide a backup connection. 

This is exceptionally dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that could have caused severe injury or death, but no actual harm occurred due to immediate intervention.

incident_description: Lithonia Emergency Lighting was recalled in 2014 as a potential fire hazard. The Burlington, VT Fire Marshal's Office did a safety inspection at a local business finding several emergency lights that did not work, and the Facilities Manager showed them samples of the recalled lighting that showed no signs of overheating several years ago but now show definite signs of overheating. The Facilities Manager said the firm had told him they would replace any panels that had turned brown from overheating near a potentially faulty resister, and the Facilities Manager worked with the firm to replace approximately 20 units out of a total of 42 in 2015. When the Facilities Manager began to replace the units with newer LED's, he found that many of the panels left unrepaired/ uncorrected in 2015 were now showing evidence of overheating. The Fire Marshal brought the concern to the CPSC's area representative who then contacted Headquarters. Compliance requested samples and an in-depth investigation report.
justification: The incident involves recalled emergency lighting showing signs of overheating, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths have been reported.

incident_description:
The submitter's son was walking to his room when his foot sustained a laceration from the chair. The submitter's son required nine stitches to the dorsum of his foot. One of the wheels on the chair had fell off a few weeks ago, the submitter said his son does not remember how it fell. The laceration was due to the leg, which the submitter said is extremely sharp.  

The submitter contacted the firm and reported the incident. He was told by a Rep. that it's impossible for one of the wheels to fall off. The submitter indicated that the firm was not concerned with the safety hazard of the chair or the incident. 

The submitter said his son is seven years old.

incident_description: In December 2017, I purchased two of the Geneva Glass Globe with marble base task lamps.  On May 22nd, one of them just suddenly caught on fire.  We checked to ensure the bulb was not exceeding the 40w limit and it was not.  There was only a 20w bulb in the lamp.  On May 28th, on the opposite side of the house, the other one caught on fire. I was given a case number and was told a rep from their quality department would reach out to me. I have since called daily and have yet to speak with someone in their quality department.  All I want is to send the lamps back to their quality department so that they can determine if this is a safety hazard.

This was after I put some IKEA corner pads that supposed should hide the sharp corners. You can find similar reports on the Internet.

incident_description:

justification: The incident caused dizziness, sore throat, and cough, indicating injury (severity 3). The persistent odor suggests this issue is likely to recur with similar products (likelihood 4).

When we went into the dining room we saw that the glass table top had exploded into bits and slivers radiating over 10 feet from the table base and leaving some shards of glass imbedded in the walls. As yet, the manufacturer has been reluctant to make good on their warranty.

This is a second home for us.

incident_description:
I hated to take my Christmas Wreath down in January even though the wreath was still green and fragrant. Unlike fresh-cut Christmas trees, which are mounted on a stand with a container of water at the bottom to keep them moist, I never made any attempt to keep this wreath moist. It seemed fine as-is. I decided to conduct a test. I put the wreath in the fireplace to see if it would burn. It lit easily and burned like a torch for the next five minutes. See photos attached, with timestamps in the filenames. I was surprised at the intensity of the flames, much more than my typical firelogs produce there.

I searched the internet, but could not find any significant incidence of wreaths causing home fires. In my house, my wreath is always located away from any source of ignition. However, without application of some kind of fire retardant to the wreath, the potential is there to cause a big problem if it did ignite. Other people might not be as diligent in placing the wreath away from ignition sources in their homes.

As I said, I did not find any significant incidence of wreaths causing fires from my internet search. I'm not trying to cause unnecessary alarm. I just wanted to make you aware. It might be better if the wreath vendor treated them with retardant or recommended a specific approach to minimize ignition risk. Having told you this, now I can sleep better. I didn't want to keep this concern to myself alone.
justification: The incident describes a controlled test with no actual harm, but highlights a potential fire hazard if wreaths are placed near ignition sources.

incident_description:
I purchased a lightweight mirror from Bed Bath & Beyond, whose shoddy, weak materials caused the frame to literally crumble and break off where the hook brackets were attached by two screws. The mirror had been hanging above my bed for over a year,  by a secure screw (see pic),  anchored into the wall, and the mirror came crashing down at 3 a.m. on February 27th, landing behind my headboard, mirror intact.

Luckily I survived. But, had my headboard not protected me, I may not be here today.

I tried to file a claim with the company's insurance company for damages to my wall and baseboard, no more than $400, but it was declined because the company had attached a label on the back of the mirror warning not to use picture-hanging wire.

I have tried to attach some photographs that show how the material of the frame gave way, but this form has no way to attach photographs. The wire is still attached to the brackets, including the one that was dislodged from the frame with a chunk of the frame shoddy, weak, plaster-of-Paris-like material, though the picture wire is still attached, just fine. The wire was in no way compromised, as you would be able to see in the photographs.

My handyman, who attached the wire and safely hung the mirror for me, apparently didn't read the label--nor would I have expected him to because used common sense in hanging the mirror  and hung it the way any handyman might.  In fact, all of my artwork, even the last two prints, with glass, I had framed at two professional frame stores here in Wilmington, have brackets on the back side with similar u-shaped closed hooks, and picture wire attached to each hook. I have at least 10 pieces of artwork hanging in my home, including a 70-lb mirror that had belonged to my grandmother, all hung with wire. Yet this company, MCS Industries in Easton, PA, advises using a separate screw for each u-shaped closed hook--and a leveler.  Totally difficult, awkward, and impractical.  No one hangs artwork in this manner.

I have researched proper hanging of framed art. It is industry standard to use picture hanging wire. Picture hanging kits come with wire.

This company, MCS Industries of Easton, Pennsylvania, is bypassing a common, time-honored practice that most people would not think twice about, and it is insisting consumers use a different method, but only on the label on the backside of the frame, that many people may or may not read.

Thus, if this company uses this similar weak material for all its frames, others like me are in danger of having their artwork fall onto their heads, on to their children, onto their pets, or what have you. It is a dangerous practice. Not to mention glass shards splattering when the frame hits the floor.

I would like to file a formal complaint with the CPSC about this company.
They are not using wood in their frames. They are using a composite like a plaster of Paris. I don't know who regulates the picture-frame industry, but the ability of this company to put warning labels on the backs of their framed works advising unwary consumers not to use picture wire is not only dangerous but unethical. It's just a way for them to cover their you know whats.

I really appreciate your looking into this for me. I have tried to go through the Better Business Bureau, Bed Bath & Beyond, and the company's insurance company, [REDACTED], but I have gotten nowhere. I don't know where else to turn.
justification: The mirror fell but no injury occurred, though there was potential for serious harm.

On Monday night January 29th 2018 at 9PM PT, my 4 year old who weights 43 lbs, and the top board of the guardrail fell of the top bunk and landed with his head on a table.

That night, I have heard a huge bang and my son screaming. Due to the sounds, I knew instantly, that he must have fell out of the bed. It took what seemed forever to console him to be able to examine any of his body injuries and to see if a 911 call or ride to emergency room is necessary. After confirming that my son was able to move and didn't seem to have anything broken, was making sense, did not display any issue with hearing or vision, did not start to throw up, and was no dizzy, I have decided to wait till the morning to call his pediatrician to see if he needs to be seen for a possible concussion. I have given him kids Advil and ice cold pack for his head and ear.

His injuries consist of: bleeding from a cut on his right ear, the ear is swollen, purple, has lots of bruising. On the right side of the head, behind his ear, is a bloody scratch, bump and bruise. The right side of the neck has a red mark as well. There is a big bruise on the right shoulder blade. I have documented all of the described injuries in pictures I have taken with my phone.

The bunk bed was purchased and delivered through Wayfair.com in October 2017, and my friend and I have assembled the bed together. It was a straight forward assembly, and we have followed the assembly directions that came with the bed.

The board from the guardrail that came off still has all pegs attached when it got dislocked. There are no screws to hold either of the two boards that make the guardrail. Both of the boards have just pegs. Those lock into the leg of the bed on one side and into a vertical slat on the other side. That vertical slat is attached by screws only on the bottom which still allows for the movement of the top part allowing for the pegs and rail to unlock.

incident_description:
In mid  2015 I bought 4 dining chairs from Butler Furniture Co in Mountain Home Arkansas and began to use them in my home.  In early 2016 I noticed the chair that my wife was sitting in was at an unusual angle.  When I picked it up the left rear leg was dangling loose and about to come off the chair.

 Had it come off it would likely have thrown my wife backwards through a glass door.  She is on a blood thinner and would probably have bled to death before medical help could arrive or I could have taken her to the nearest ER 15 miles away.
When I turned the chair over I found a tiny 2 line warning in English that indicated that the screws should be tightened by the user when they loosen.  The notice is buried amidst several larger labels, one of which is written entirely in Chinese, and a stamp indicates that it is ÃÂMADE IN CHINAÃÂ. How many buyers look under a chair before they purchased it?  None to my knowledge and the label is hidden under the seat.

I tightened all 32 screws under the chair (all were quite loose) and resumed use of the chairs, but in mid 2016 I found all 32 Screws again loose ( 1 leg dangerously loose).
The chairs are product of Ashley Furniture Co, One Asheley Way, Arcadia WI, 54612.
The label bears D540-402 which is presumed to be a model number. 
That product should be banned from sale as highly dangerous and no longer allowed into the USA.

incident_description:
This is a LED instant-on light bulb made by FEIT ELECTRIC COMPANY. 60 watt replacement uses only 13.5 watts. It was installed in the recess light fixture above my small dining table near the kitchen. We use the kind of energy saving light bulbs (instant-on or not) a lot for a long time. The incident happened at around 8:05 pm on 12/31/2017. The light bulb had been on for several hours before the incident. Suddenly, My wife noticed the light bulb went dark and making noise. The bottom round (glass like) piece and the majority light bulb (the heavy portion) popped out separately and the light bulb went on fire by itself. I turned off the switch right away and the fire stopped. After it cooled down, I removed the small portion of the light bulb that was screwed on the light fixture. The recess light fixture was fine except some burning marks that can be wiped out easily. I changed to another LED light bulb (but not instant-on type) to test the light fixture on the next day. It has been no problem. If we had not been in the house to stop the fire immediately when this happened, this could have been a disaster to us.

We moved to this house in 2006 and the house was inspected and has C/O. We never change the wire and light fixture for the one that had the incident. We bought the light bulbs from Costco.

Other detailed information on the light bulb:
Omni Directional. 
BPCEA19/OM800/LED
13.5W 120VAC 60 Hz 129mA
850 LUMENS UL#E330072

incident_description: Was at home and an LED bulb that has been in a lamp in my home suddenly started making a high pitch whistling noise. I then noticed flames in the lamp shade coming from the opposite side of where the lamp switch was. I then saw thick acrid smoke (dark gray in color) coming from the lamp. incident_description:
I purchased mini blinds online. The mounting brackets are spring steel that are supposed to fasten around the
headrail. Force is used to "snap" them into place. I could not get the headrail to seat with ordinary force and so I
continued to push upward as illustrated in the product instructions. The headrail eventually slipped sideways,
causing my finger to strike the mounting bracket and cut into my flesh. Better quality miniblinds (the ones I was
replacing) use a box-style mount that does not require application of force. If force is required, it should be
minimal, to prevent injury, but these brackets will never positively engage with the headrail no matter how much
force is used.

See enclosures.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as the description suggests the injury was caused by a design flaw that could affect others under similar conditions.

incident_description: Crate and barrel Dakota bench. Was moving it and it tipped over, slamming on my foot. Never went to the emergency department but had a very large bruise and painful movement for a week or two afterwards

The candle burns directly in the tin, it is not possible to take out.  The candle was on my dresser in my bedroom. incident_description: We bought a Fulton bed from an area furniture place. My brother went their first and picked out the futon for my elderly mother.  The furniture place delivered the Futon. I came in from work, and walked around the furniture place. I asked the manager many important questions regarding the safety and sturdiness of the Futon. She fell hard to the ground, thank God I was there, and she only suffered small bruises. She's 85 years old. The Futon is like a seesaw. I called the store and spoke to the same Manager. he stated to me that Futons, you have to lay in the middle of the Futon. You cannot lay at the end. I asked him, what if a person rolls over in their sleep. He stated again you have to lay in the middle. He also told me to call the warehouse for a refund. I called the warehouse. And a woman answered. I explained what happened. She told me the same. You must lay in the middle of the futon, all futons are like that, you cannot lay on either end. I told her, that I have bought futons in the past, and never had to worry about that, and none of the futons I bought in the past flipped over if a person is sitting on it when it is open as a bed. I have never heard of any bed that you must sleep in the middle. The store person lied to me and my family. He stated it is extremely safe and sturdy. The futon they sell are like seesaws. Thankfully my daughter was not standing at the mirror at the time.  This time I'm reporting, the risk for injury was very high.  Something is going on with the quality of the bulbs, they are not supposed to explode.

incident_description:
I purchased two of these cabinets about 4 years ago. I recently placed 2 wine glasses on the top shelf of one of the cabinets and the entire shelf instantly failed in such a way that all of the wine glasses on that shelf (about 13-15 glasses) came crashing out of the cabinet towards me and down onto my floor. Normally, my small child is playing on this floor right where the glass fell, but luckily was not home at the time. The glasses shattered all over my floor, where my dog and I were standing. As this occurred, the edge of the shelf hit the top of my left eye socket and caused bruising and pain to the bone and surrounding tissue for over a week.

Method of shelf failure: The front edge of the shelf dropped past/inside the front 2 shelf supports, much like a ÃÂtrap doorÃÂ would open in a floor, allowing the shelf to fall forward.

Reason for shelf failure: The shelf is not deep enough to ensure it remains positioned on the front 2 shelf supports, and the 2 front shelf supports which extend from the back of the front face of the cabinet (rather than from the traditional location of the side of the cabinet, as do the 2 back supports) do not extend into the cabinet long enough to ensure they hold the shelf.

I checked all 5 other shelves of these two cabinets and this failure mode does not occur with the other shelves because the shelves are sufficiently deep to ensure they remain on the front shelf supports.

I also noticed that the back of the shelving unit "gives" a little behind where the failing shelf sits. This could compound the problem.
justification: The incident caused injury (bruising and pain) but no death, and the failure is unlikely to recur as other shelves are secure.

During the first use of the blanket, a heavy petroleum odor began to permeate the bedroom. Unfortunately, it took a couple days to identify that the odor was coming from the blanket. My search for the origin of the odor was accelerated when my wife awoke one morning feeling dizzy. Her condition improved during the day but I was still concerned for the problem in the first place wondering what could have possible caused the dizziness. I finally homed in on the odor, went to the bedroom and finally picked up a corner of the blanket and sniffed the very strong scent of petroleum. It actually reminded me of the aroma of kerosene. I took the blanket outside, went back to the bedroom, turning on a ceiling fan and within several minutes, the odor was gone. Going back to the blanket, now outside the house, the aroma was still profound. I checked the package the blanket was sold in and there is all sorts of identifying information, but no phone number to call Macy's with concerns.
I'm concerned Macy's is selling a potentially dangerous product, free wheeling manufacturing processes in China being what they are. There is no reason to think the blanket in the package would generate this very strong aroma just waiting to be used. It had to originate with the manufacturer.
I am going to call Macy's tomorrow and voice my concerns to them also.
justification: The incident involved a strong petroleum odor causing dizziness, which qualifies as an injury, but no long-term harm was reported.

It sparked, blew the breaker, and her room filled up with smoke.  We turned the breaker back on, and her room continued to fill up with smoke.  My husband went to unplug the light and was shocked and the breaker blew again.  When we flipped the breaker back again, we realized the cord was melted in many places and the copper wires were exposed. My husband's two fingers were blackened and burned slightly from unplugging the cord.  This could have been a horrible situation!!  This bed is still for sale on RC Willey's website!!!  I contacted a sales person at RC Willey's.  Sent them pictures of the cord and my husband's hand and never heard a word back from them.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns to the husband's fingers and potential for more severe injury due to exposed wires and electrical malfunction.

incident_description:
The evening of 11/24/2017 while myself, my wife, and my in-laws were playing cards at our kitchen table, my wife pointed at one of our can lights and said "fire".  We all looked and observed several flashes followed by a cloud of smoke which registered from the bulb and spread out across the ceiling.  The other 7 can lights which shared the circuit with the defective bulb flickered a little bit during the burn-out of the problematic one, but did not go out (i.e. the circuit breaker did not trip).  We turned off the switch to the lights and watched to ensure no fire spread.  The can which housed the bulb was blackened, but no further flame was observed once the bulb itself had stopped burning. 
 The catastrophic burn-out of the bulb took place over a period of about 5-10 seconds.  I took a couple pictures of the burnt out bulb in place, and then with the power off, I retrieved a ladder and using a silicone oven mitt I removed the bulb and cleaned up the receptacle as best I could.  I took pictures of the burnt out bulb, and removed all bulbs which were of the same type from our home.

The light bulb was a Utilitech LED, model LA19DM/LEDG2.   7W, 79mA, 450 Lumen, UL#E330072.
The flame+smoke exit point is observed to be a hole approximately 1/8 inch in diameter in the plastic at the very base of the bulb, where it transitions from the metal which screws into the socket into the plastic housing of the bulb itself.  The glass portion of the bulb is intact.
justification: The incident involved a bulb emitting smoke and flashes but no injury or fire spread occurred, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
To Whom it May Concern,
 
I am writing you in regards to a LED Ceiling Fixture that I believe could be a potential fire hazard (see attached pictures).  Upon inspecting this fixture, the first things I noticed are:

1.	No heat shielding of any kind on the base plate
2.	Gauge of metal on base plate is very thin, warps easily
3.	Very little heat shielding on the wires

Typically on a E26 base ceiling fixture you would see heat shielding on at least one side of the base and all the way down the wires.  I have to think that other manufacturers would not incur the additional costs of heat shielding unless it was required.

The fixture is certified by ETL to UL1598 standard (see attached Ceiling Fixture portion of UL1598).  I work in the lighting industry and know a little bit about UL1598.  My understanding of UL1598 as it pertains to flush mounted, totally enclosed ceiling fixtures, such as this, is below.

If the fixture has:
1.	GU24 sockets installed to accept GU24 base CFLÃÂs, it is not subject to an additional 90 degree Celsius heat test because the end user cannot install incandescent bulbs into the fixture. 

2.	E26 screw in sockets installed to accept any standard E26 bulb.  Even though the fixture comes with LED bulbs, it is subject to an additional 90 degree Celsius heat test.  If the fixture heats up to 90 degrees Celsius, or above, where it mounts to the ceiling, it will not pass the UL1598 standard.  This additional testing is due to the possibility of the end user being able to install incandescent bulbs, which operate at much higher heat levels than LEDÃÂs, and may become a fire hazard.  The fact that this fixture does not have any heat shielding on the base plate, and very little on the wires, leads me to believe that it definitely would not pass the 90 degree Celsius testing.  

If my understanding of this requirement is incorrect in any way, clarification on your part would be greatly appreciated.

Regarding the ceiling fixture in question; I was able to find the ETL certification on IntertekÃÂs website under the factoryÃÂs name, Bright Lighting and Electric Appliance Co., LTD. ÃÂ Dongguan, Guangdong China.
I understand that Intertek has certified this product to meet UL1598 standards.  

My question is: 
ÃÂ	Is it possible that this fixture could have been certified to UL1598 standards using the requirements for ceiling fixtures with GU24 base bulbs?  Essentially being granted certification while bypassing the heat test requirement.

I ask this because the GU24 CFL version of this fixture has been very popular for the last few years.  However, a manufacturer may not change something on a fixture and use the same certification.  If a manufacturer changes just one item on the fixture (GU24 to E26 sockets), it must go through a new round of testing and receive a new certification stating that it complies with all specs using the new E26 sockets.  

I have seen other ceiling fixtures on the Consumer Product Safety CommissionÃÂs website be recalled in the past due to fire hazard from no heat shielding on wires. (see the below links)

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2013/Ceiling-Mounted-Light-Fixtures-Recalled-by-Dolan-Designs

https://www.cpsc.gov/Recalls/2012/Ceiling-Mounted-Light-Fixtures-Recalled-by-Thomas-Lighting-Due-to-Fire-and-Shock-Hazards

After further review of this product; if, it does not meet UL1598 standards for E26 based LED ceiling fixtures, what steps will the Consumer Product Safety Commission take to rectify the situation?  

I am writing this with the position of safety being the utmost importance.  This fixture is currently being widely used in a major California utility ESA program.  Approximately 30,000 of these units have already been installed in low income homes.  Nobody would like to see damages or injuries come from the use of this product.

Thank you in advance for your time and consideration on this matter.  I look forward to your response.
justification: The description indicates a potential fire hazard due to inadequate heat shielding, which could lead to injuries if the fixture overheats and causes a fire.

incident_description:

I purchased a couch on Wayfair, and after assembling the piece in my home, I noticed that my hands were inflamed and itchy. When I washed them with soap and water the rash went away, so I believe the reaction was caused by an irritant in the furniture. I did some research online and it turns out that this is a common problem for couches originating in China. These companies include the chemical Dimerhyl Fumarate (DMF) to act as an anti-molding agent. Many people have reported having similar reactions tha I have had. I didnÃÂt even touch the gel packets directly, so this tells me the chemical has contaminated the entire piece of furniture. This substance is banned in Europe - it needs to be banned in th USA!

Item specifications:
TRENT AUSTIN DESIGN George ÃÂ78 Track arm sofa. Manufactured in China, sold by Wayfair. Assembly required.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (inflamed and itchy hands) due to exposure to a chemical irritant in the furniture, and the likelihood is high (4) as similar reactions are commonly reported.

incident_description: The table was advertised by Restoration Hardware and subsequently purchased and used by us as a coffee table.  As such, it was used to hold drinks, etc.  What prompted this report was that my infant daughter was tested for lead exposure when she turned 1 as is required in my State.  Her levels were elevated beyond the normal range to the near dangerous level and we were alerted by the State.  In the following month, we began searching around the house for possible lead contamination.  We could not find any potential lead sources until last week when we attempted to clean a white film off our coffee table (seemingly everywhere our daughter touches when she walks around the table).  The film wouldn't clean off, so we searched online for how to clean it and immediately discovered that several other nearly identical tables sold by the same company were recently recalled for causing lead contamination in children when the finish would come off and leave a white residue.  This sounded identical to our problem, so we obtained an at home lead test from Lowe's and it indicated a positive result.  Today we had a professional environmental company come to our house and test the table.  They also found that the table does contain lead.  No other lead sources were found in our living area.
justification: The infant daughter's elevated lead levels indicate injury, and the table was confirmed as the lead source.

incident_description: In the spring of 2017 a bar chair manufactured by 3i Corp. and sold by Lowe's collapsed due to a failure of a weld in the base.  In early July of this year I noticed a recall notice posted near the a Lowe's return location.  I called the number assigned to the manufacturer and reported the problem.  I was promised that four replacement bases would be shipped to me in 6 to 8 weeks.  This was over 4 months ago.  Obviously the manufacturer has no intention of honoring this commitment.  Last week my companion spoke to a manager at the North Charleston SC Lowes and advised of the above situation. He committed to replace all 4 chairs involved in the recall if we would return the recalled chairs to him. Today (Oct. 16) Lowes replaced the four chairs free of charge.  The manufacturer has totally failed to honor its promise to send replacement bases.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (collapsed chair) but no injury was reported, and the issue was eventually resolved by the retailer.

incident_description: I was using an IKEA Glasholm desk with Gerton legs in my office.  It had a laptop, keyboard, microphone, and some papers on top.  As I stepped past the desk, my foot lightly tapped one of the legs.  The table essentially exploded, sending glass throughout the room and onto the floor.

This caused the backs of some the chairs to fall of completely.  The chair company recalled a similar style of chair for the same exact issue, but this particular style was not recalled. I would like to avoid one of the staff becoming injured on a chair that we knew was faulty.  I believe this style of chair is unsafe and should be recalled.

incident_description:
I bought 2  Jackson Furniture Anniston Sofas 2 years ago.  Suddenly, the frame on one of my sofas came apart while I was sitting on it, injuring my back. I removed the cushions to inspect it, and it was obvious that the design was flawed and the manufacturing process was substandard: as you can see in the photos, the horizontal wooden support slats for the cushions have separated from the horizontal wooden support structure of the back of the frame on both sides. These have been fastened with staples rather than more durable fasteners, so this is not only a defect, but it design flaw.

In the time I have had this sofa, I have barely sat on this couch, and I only weigh 170 pounds. No one else even sits on it and there are no kids or pets in the house. When I contacted the store where I bought the sofas (FMO), they spoke with Jackson Furniture's repair agents (a woman named [REDACTED]) after which they informed me that the LIFETIME warranty doesn't cover labor to repair the sofa after the first year of ownership. This is astounding, as the piece was made in such a way that it never could have lasted. These sofas should all be recalled before someone else gets injured. 

I saw numerous similar incidents of frame collapse described for similar Jackson/Catnapper sofas on the website consumeraffairs.com.  I contacted Jackson Furniture through the website, and received a response from the company representative, [REDACTED].  She reiterated that they were not responsible for labor costs for repair of their sofas after 1 year, despite the faulty manufacturing process that makes frame collapse a inevitable outcome with normal use of the sofa.
justification: The incident resulted in a back injury due to a sofa frame collapse caused by a design flaw and substandard manufacturing, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) given the reported similar incidents and inherent product defects.

incident_description: Ashley Furniture Home Store is mixing and matching mattresses and bases, in my case a power base to make sales. They are violating Federal Regulation 16 CFR 1633, and possibly others I am not familiar with. I am sure I am not the only person they have sold mattresses with non compliant bases. It took higher measures to get a full refund and pick up of the items. They were not cooperative, and once I pointed out they were violating the federal regulation, they were quick to return the items. They also use false advertisement to get sales. I feel I should report this as it could be fire hazard under the federal regulation, and want to be sure no one is injured due to this, or has to go through my same ordeal. Two of the same mattresses that are not in compliance with the federal regulation collapsed and bulged in the same spot, as it is not fit for use on a power base. I have included photos of the mattress tag, and receipt showing the adjustable head and foot base sold with my mattress are not the item numbers listed on the mattress tag as bases that are compliant under 16 CFR 1633. I did not realize this issue until I was told the second mattress that collapsed was my fault, and I had to file a complaint with the local consumer protection agency. There are many complaints about the quality of their furniture via review sites and the BBB. Many people also complain about their horrible customer service. I have evidence of them stating the mattress they sold is compliant, and one employee saying it was not due to being innerspring. I can provide any information needed.
justification: The incident involves non-compliant products posing a potential fire hazard and poor customer service, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description: While my daughter was making her bed the wooden side rail split causing the the bed to hit the floor while she was on it.
justification: The bed rail split and the bed hit the floor, but there is no mention of injury, so severity is incident without injury. Wooden bed rail failures are possible but not highly frequent.

incident_description:
IKEA Calypso Ceiling Lamp breaks into razor sharp glass shards when removing the glass shade to clean it or to change light bulbs and has caused lacerations on both my hands. This lamp is a fairly new product and is still on store shelves as of today (10/12/2017). By searching on-line reviews I have found that the glass in this lamp is breaking on it's own without anything coming in contact with it for lots of other people. I believe it is due to stress in the glass from the light going from cold to hot and back again when the lamp is turned on and off, and that IKEA designers may have over compensated in how tightly the glass is held in the metal clips that hold the glass in place, possibly because in a previous ceiling light model, the glass was just releasing and falling to the floor. This lamp DOES NOT have that problem. The problem with this lamp is the glass just spontaneously fractures in one's hands, even if held very gently.

This is a totally separate and new issue from the previously recalled IKEA Ceiling Lamps even though the issue sounds similar at first. This is a newer, redesigned ceiling lamp.

When the glass shade / shroud needs to be removed for either cleaning or changing out light bulbs, this rather large piece of curved glass just spontaneously falls into many razor sharp pieces in one's hands, probably due to stress fractures that develop in the glass from the lamp during use. The real danger here is that if someone is removing the glass from underneath it while looking up, the glass will just fall into that person's face, or will injure children that may be playing on the floor nearby.

As far as I can tell, this seems to be happening to a lot of people who own this product based on some online reviews I've found. I've contacted IKEA, and they appear to me to be unconcerned. They offered me a refund and a $50 store certificate, which I've refused to take.

I have a science and engineering background, and from my perspective there is nothing that can be done to safely remove the glass shroud from this lamp without it breaking in owner's hands causing injury. It is a defective design and uses brittle, non-tempered glass. Someone is going to get seriously hurt when cleaning or changing a light bulb in this Calypso Ceiling Light product, possibly losing an eye in the process. 

This will be a difficult problem to solve for IKEA I predict in that the risk of injury occurs when removing the glass shade. If the product is recalled, then owners will have to do just that, remove the glass, to return it back to IKEA. And it's when the glass is removed that it'll turn into razor sharp shards right in one's hands.

Please please have something done about this dangerous product before someone gets seriously injured. I had received both lacerations and puncture wounds in both hands when removing the glass to clean it, and I was being very very careful with it. I'm quite worried about others have the same or worse outcome.
justification: The incident describes lacerations and puncture wounds from broken glass, indicating injury, and online reviews suggest this is a common issue.

incident_description: I purchased an Omega Chocolate DBL Recliner Power Sofa from Hanks Furniture in Rogers, AR72756.  Also at same time purchased an Omega Chocolate DBL Love seat with power.  When we purchased it no one routed the electrical wires or tied them up.  We were unaware that the wires were loose and could pose a hazard.  After a couple times of plugging them in, my grandson and I were sitting in the floor beside the sofa and someone in the chair pushed the power button.  Fire flew from under the sofa and there was a loud pop.  I quickly moved my grandson to see if he was ok and then immediately unplugged the cord.  After examining the plug I found two cuts in the wiring where it had pinched on the framework of the recliner.  I called Hanks and they replaced the wire, sent someone out to reroute and tie up the cord in different places.  The service person only used wire ties to tie it up.  Again without realizing it had come undone I plugged it in to turn it on but when I saw the excess wire, I decided to check it out first.  Sure enough there were two more cuts in the wiring.  I called them again to tell them this furniture was a hazard and unsafe.  Manager said he would send me a new cord again but I would have to pay for the labor of a service person to rewire and tie up the cord again.  I don't care about the cost of the wire or the cost of the furniture but this furniture is a fire hazard and could have electrocuted my grandson.  When I picked up the cord they were several other cords behind the counter.  Don't think this was the first time this had happened.  I just want someone to check this out.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and potential electrocution risk, but no actual injury occurred.

He has now been informed that the friends who gave him his chair also gifted three others with the chairs because they didn't fit in with their dÃÂ©cor and that all of the other three chairs also were discovered to be unsafe.
