This lightbulb (less than 2 years old) was being used in my bathroom lighting fixture (an over the mirror 2 light fixture which is less than 2 years old). It had been on for several hours and started flickering. It kept getting worse, so I turned off the light and removed the bulb. I expected it to be hot, so I was very careful with it, however I received second degree burns on the pads of my index finger and thumb when I lightly touched the ballast. I put the light bulb down to care for my burns and came back  It kept getting worse, so I turned off the light and removed the bulb. I expected it to be hot, so I was very careful with it, however I received second degree burns on the pads of my index finger and thumb when I lightly touched the ballast. I put the light bulb down to care for my burns and came back to it several minutes later to see if it was still hot. I put a large drop of water on the ballast, and within 4 seconds it was boiling. 20 minutes later the bulb was still to hot to pick by the ballast.
The bathroom was moist, due to a long shower, but a fan venting to the outside was running.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific conditions described (moist environment, prolonged use).

incident_description:
I purchased a GE Holiday Lights Christmas tree from Lowes.  We purchased the Just Cut Aspen Fir with 700 LED lights which is model 01619 UPC 8-03993-1619-1.  The tree is VERY heavy.  When we put the tree into the stand that was provided, one of the legs of the stand broke off and the tree came crashing down. We have owned a GE tree for the past 12 years.  We began having issues with the lights on our previous tree so we decided to buy a new one.  The stand that came with the last tree was much sturdier.  The new stand was thin and flimsy.

I contacted the company and they seemed concerned.  The person told me to send them a picture of the broken stand.  She said she was going to forward it immediately to the President of the company who was in China meeting with the manufacturer.  She promised to let me know what they were going to do. When I called them back they said it was up to their manufacturer in China.  

This is an extreme hazard!

It had been installed about a year or so, under normal household use.  One night, my wife heard a loud pop and looked at the source of the noise to see fire shooting up from this light bulb, several inches high spewing ash and smoke into the air. It set off our smoke alarms, and continued to burn even after electricity had been cut off, until I smothered the flames.  The fire was so hot it cracked the glass light diffuser around the bulb. I took photos of the aftermath to the chandelier and the bulb itself.
justification: The incident involved a fire shooting from the light bulb, causing damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
Last night August 20, 2017, a ceiling mounted light fixture with 3 LED bulbs that had been on for about an hour malfunctioned completely, burning one bulb and damaging the remaining two lights.  They are all FEIT LED bulbs. The melted bulb is a  FEIT CE18W/TM/D/6 and  remaining two are FEIT LED ESL 18TM.  All three lights burned out, filling the house with toxic fumes and the fear of a possible fire.  Although it was difficult to remove the twisted melted bulb all three were removed safely after turning off the electricity.  No was injured but toxic fumes did leave the family of four with sore throats and headaches. This incident could have led to a far more tragic result as the fixture was directly above the bed.  After reading other reports concerning these bulbs I will be removing all remaining FEIT LED bulbs in my home and hope that FEIT personnel will address these reports with more than a generic company statement.  I purchased the bulbs at COSTCO and will also be informing them of my concerns.

One FEIT CE18W/TM/D/6 and  two FEIT LED ESL 18TM
justification: The incident caused toxic fumes leading to sore throats and headaches, but no serious injuries or death.

incident_description:
On September 28, 2016, my fiancÃÂ© and I purchased the Zinus Memory Foam 10 Inch Green Tea Mattress (via Amazon).  A few nights ago, while changing our sheets and mattress protector, we noticed the large (easily accessible) zipper on the bottom of the mattress. Doubtful that the zipper was merely for aesthetic purposes, we decided to unzip and remove this cover to more easily reach the area we wanted to spot clean. The tag's Care Instructions refer to both an "outer cover" and a "cover," and also states, "do not put foam in washer or dryer" (not sure how one fits an entire mattress inside a washer or dryer). In light of the above ambiguities, I interpreted "do not remove cover" to mean "do not remove the fire retardant mesh cover" (as that would presumably make the mattress flammable). Therefore, my fiance and I proceeded to unzip and remove the knitted cover. ]

Little did we know that doing so would reveal a defective fiberglass mesh covering. We immediately put the cover back on. Nevertheless, fiberglass particles had already spread throughout our room;  floors, walls, furniture, clothing and our skin were all covered in it. Despite showering and our best cleaning efforts, we've been extremely uncomfortable for days - in addition to the painful itching and asthma-related symptoms, my throat has become alarmingly irritated. 

Moreover, upon removal of the outer cover, we noticed multiple areas where the mattressÃÂ protective mesh (fiberglass) was breached/had worn off. We have no way of knowing precisely when or how this could have happened, or whether it was simply delivered in this condition.  What I do know is that (1) IÃÂve been sleeping directly above these areas for the last 10-12 months, and (2) I've had to undergo multiple medical exams over the past 10-12 months for unexplained throat and neck swelling and irritation. I intend on scheduling an appointment with my ENT as soon as I can.  

How and to what extent this defective fiberglass material has affected our health is not yet clear. 
The fiberglass particles are seemingly impossible to get rid of -- they continue to spread through our A/C and washer/dryer use.

I've been attempting to contact Zinus since September 6th, to no avail. I've called and emailed customer support (no response to my email or voicemail). I've also attempted to reach them through their online chat feature (no response).
justification: The incident resulted in painful itching, asthma-related symptoms, and throat irritation, indicating injury.

The O-Ring (cast iron) from the lamp which was connected to the ceiling junction box broke, causing the lamp to fall. Lamp was off. This chandelier fell (same exact thing occurred) on 11/23/13. It was re-hung by a certified electrician and fell again on 4/16/17

incident_description:
Llorell offers a Sit to Stand Desk Riser to sit on top of an existing desk which allows the consumer to move from a sitting position to a standing position.  

The product has the potential to create a substantial risk of injury and property damage to the consumer / user when attempting to make a raised or lowered adjustment. Serious lower back and neck injuries can be created when adjustments are made to the product. To made adjustments, the consumer ÃÂunlocksÃÂ the adjustment component located at the rear of the desk (approximately 16 inches from the front of the product) on both sides of the product. To access the adjustment components, the consumer needs a 30 inch wide-arm grasp to complete to ÃÂunlockÃÂ the adjustment component. The position of the adjustment components requires the consumer to bend the upper torso at approximately 46 degree angle, which is recognized as an awkward position. After ÃÂunlockingÃÂ the consumer then user then lifts the desk in an upward motion by grasping either the front or side of the product to guide it to the desired height.  The gas spring mechanism, which allows the desk to adjust, requires a significant amount of force to complete the full adjustment motion (either raised or lowered).   Adjusting the desk using a pulling force coupled with the consumerÃÂs upper torso bent at a 46 degree angle is a hazard to the lower back and neck. Serious injury can occur by making these adjustments to this product. 

Numerous pinch point hazards are encountered while making adjustments with no warnings or cautions labeled on the product nor listed in the instructions. 


In addition, depending on where you grasp the desk lower stabilizers raise with the desk causing the product to tip over on the consumer.  

The instructions included in the box are extremely limited. Recommended maintenance nor inspection requirements were not listed in the userÃÂs guide.

I contacted S.P Richards Product Support via phone on September 8th and spoke with [REDACTED] regarding my concerns. She indicated customers have similar complaints regarding rising and lowering the devise but the issue should be resolved overtime after the product is ÃÂbroken inÃÂ. I explained how much force is required to adjust the unit and the tipping hazard when the stabilizers are lifted; she recommended I contact the seller or distributor to replace the product. [REDACTED] indicated there may be a defect with the pistons which is causing a large amount of force to made adjustments. I will be contacting the distributed to exchange the defective product.
justification: The description details serious lower back and neck injuries from awkward adjustments and tipping hazards, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported complaints and inherent design flaws.

incident_description: Bought a himalayan salt lamp from Bed Bath and Beyond around christmas time. Didn't use it a whole lot and had been off for a few months. Went to plug it in again and within the hour, the dimmer switch melted and the lamp went out. The brand is wbm international himalayan glow. As far as I can tell, this brand was not part of the massive recall, but has the same problem as the ones that were recalled. The dimmer switch is a zing ear ZE-04. Cannot find if the recalled lamps uses the same dimmer switch as this.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning dimmer switch causing the lamp to stop working, but no injury or harm was reported.

incident_description:
I ordered the Titan Osaki TP-8500 massage chair from Home Depot. It was delivered last Friday 9/1/2017. While using the chair yesterday evening the squeezing action of the airbags in my lower leg area was so intense that it was painful. I went to bed right after and when waking in the night, my right foot and ankle was very painful. In the morning it was even more painful. I was limping and couldn't walk without holding on to something for support. I went to work but after about 2 hours I couldn't walk or put any weight on my right foot. I was taken to the urgent care. I was given an air cast for my foot and ankle and crutches. I was told to follow up with my regular doctor. I am still in extreme pain and cannot bear any weight on my foot. 
I left a voicemail and sent an email to Tel: 888-848-2630, info@osakititan.com
I received a return phone call from [REDACTED]. He said this has never happened before. He offered to send some device that would reduce the air pressure. I told him I would be returning the chair.
justification: The incident resulted in significant pain and injury requiring medical attention, including an air cast and crutches, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
We recently purchased the Rockwell 6-drawer bookcase (item 780759) from the online Pottery Barn Teen store. 

The bookcase is metal and lovely but very problematic. The six double-sided drawers have a design flaw. Nothing prevents the drawers from stopping and therefore falling out. We were setting up  our new bookcase tonight and my 12-year-old son added an item to one of the drawers, and it fell out and landed on his foot. He is fine and there was no damage. There weren't many items in the drawer yet. 

If a consumer uses these drawers for books, a child could get seriously injured. As noted, the unit and drawers are metal. With nothing stopping the drawers from falling out, it could easily and quickly become dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in a drawer falling on a child's foot but caused no injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the design flaw making it easy for drawers to fall out.

incident_description: I have 8 allen+roth Safford Model #1106-2 patio chairs.  5 of them have broken bases. The last one broke on 9-4-17 while I was sitting in it and I fell on the concrete floor. Luckily I was not injured. I purchased the first four of these chairs in 2014.  The chairs have a 5 year warranty. After 2 of the bases broke I contacted Lowes and was given a phone number to call to receive replacement bases.  I finally got someone on the phone and was told that the manufacturer didn't have any bases in stock. and to call back 3 months later.  By this time I had purchased another set of 4 chairs.  When I called back I was told that the bases they were expecting did not come in.  I called Lowes and they told me that I could return 4 broken chairs and get replacements chairs.  I did this in early 2016.  In June of 2017 had 3 more broken chairs and I then learned about the recall and was told by Lowes that I could call another phone number and order replacement bases.  I called and was told to email them a photo of the broken chairs.  I did this on June 1, 2017.  I was told that I would receive the replacement bases in 8 to 10 weeks.  It has now been 14 weeks an I still have no new bases.
justification: The incident involved a chair breaking and a fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I got and installed the replacement base for the Staples Hazen Mesh Office Chair. Metal shards on the new base sliced my toe when I put my foot under the base of the chair like I, and many others, often do. I turned over the chair and found a hyperdermic-like metal shard sticking out of the edge of the new base on three separate legs, and metal spikes all on the underside of the chair, especially by the wheels. Recall link: https://www.saferproducts.gov/CPSRMSPublic/Account/ResetPassword.aspx?pGUID=b2250ebc-bed0-47ca-8483-17e1943dab35.

incident_description: A GE 75W soft white incandescent modified spectrum replacement light bulb exploded sending shards of glass over the bedroom. Parts of the light bulb partially melted into the carpet, and mattress on the bed. The explosion occurred around 30 seconds after the lights were turned off. No injuries occurred as the door was closed and no one was in the room.
justification: The light bulb exploded causing property damage but no injuries as no one was present in the room.

incident_description: i was sitting on the stool brushing my hair. I heard a crack and the bottom legs folded in. I fell backward with my head hitting a tile wall. The material the stool was made of was cheap and unsafe.The ad on online states it is made of solid wood. It is not. It is cheap

incident_description:
I bought this fixture in 2010. Within the first year of use, the screw collar snapped off of the mounting bracket and the chandelier was hanging from the ground wire while the chain had dropped to the center of the light. I happened to notice this and called immediately (July 18, 2011), sent a picture of the broken screw collar  and was sent a replacement screw collar which was replaced and rehung.

Then on June 18, 2017 at 4am we heard a crash and the entire light fixture was crashed on the floor!!! The screw collar had snapped off for the second time and this time the ground wire was not able to hold the light. It is very obvious that the parts were not engineered correctly to support the weight of this chandelier.
justification: The incident involved a fixture failure causing the chandelier to fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
BACKGROUND:  The Quantum PRO 9000 office chair was recalled @ 2009.  According to the recall, chairs should be taken out of service until a repair kit is received.  New bolts are to be installed and the problem will be fixed.

THE PROBLEM:  The chair was designed to have FOUR screws hold the chair back in place.  Only TWO holes are provided in the chair back.  When you receive a replacement kit, you replace the TWO screws with a different type of screw.  However, there are still only TWO.

THE INCIDENT:  Because there is too much pressure on these two screws, they are beginning to break.  The heads of the two screws in one of our chair backs completely sheared off, nearly causing the employee to fall to the ground.  No damage done this time, but definitely a potential hazard.

THE VENDOR:  I contacted Raynor at the number listed on the recall notice, and they are sending me a screw extractor and a kit to install TWO new screws.  

RECOMMENDATION:  2-3 years ago, one FAA office received all new chair backs, which contained FOUR screw holes in the chair back and FOUR screws.  I believe this to be the proper solution for a chair designed to have FOUR screws holding the back in place.

NOTE:  Our office currently has 20 of these chairs in use.
justification: The incident involved screws shearing off, nearly causing a fall, but no injury occurred. The issue is likely to recur given the design flaw and current usage of 20 chairs.

incident_description: My son was in the top bunk of his bunk bed and he leaned against the protective railing, when the railing snapped in half and gave way causing him fall face first into this carpeted floor. He suffered from a face abrasion, minor concussion, and bruised ribs.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (abrasion, minor concussion, bruised ribs) but no death, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described scenario.

The bulbs are cracking at the base, flickering, failing, and get very hot when used in a standard table lamp. incident_description:
Premium Shower Chair Item # BRTL12606-AST

This product should immediately be removed from all distributors and retailers.  This product is unsafe and I could have lost my life using it.  To adjust the height of the chair is dangerous in itself with little buttons which could release causing the user to fall to the floor of the shower.  
The worst and most dangerous part about using the chair is the rear part of the legs are held in by little plastic buttons which could never be safe for anyone.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased two of the same chair and she picked them up on March 6.

The consumer immediately noticed a strong chemical odor coming from the chairs. After 3 days the consumer contacted the store, Art Van Furniture and expressed her safety concerns. She indicated that she was getting a headache and a tight feeling in her chest and she believes it was being caused from the chemical odor.

On March 14, the store sent out a technician to her home and the technician advised her that the smell will dissipate over time, possible 3 weeks.

On March 15, the consumer went to the store and advised the manager of her safety concerns. The consumer was told to spray Febreeze on the chairs. The consumer did as she was told.

The consumer states that the chemical odor did not go away and she opened the windows to help air out the odor. 

The consumer called the store again and on March 21 the store sent out another technician. The technician advised the consumer that the odor could be from the foam or cover and he sprayed Airlift on both chairs.

The consumer said the smell was better for about 36 hours and then the chemical odor returned. 

The consumer indicated that her neighbor got a headache and pain in her chest after 15 minutes of sitting on the chair.

On March 25, the consumer sprayed Febreeze on the chairs. She said the odor did not dissipate and she contacted the store requesting to return them. The consumer was told that the store would charge a 25% restocking fee or a 10% restocking fee if she purchased another La-Z-Boy product.

The consumer plans to return the chairs today and purchase another product.

The consumer also contacted the firm, La-Z-Boy and informed them of her safety concerns. The consumer was told that their chairs meet all regulations and were safe. The consumer was also told she could wash the chairs with Neutrogena soap. The consumer refused to wash the new chairs.  Thought Art Van would refuse to take them back if washed.
justification: The consumer and her neighbor experienced headaches and chest pain, indicating injury from chemical exposure.

incident_description:
The submitter received a recall notice from the firm and she called them on March 4 to request the remedy. The submitter called again in April because she did not receive the remedy and she spoke with [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] told the submitter that the remedy had been shipped and she would receive it soon (FedEx tracking # [REDACTED]). The submitter said she received her 4 replacement bases last week.

The submitter's husband installed the replacement bases and followed the instructions provided by the firm. The submitter's husband advised the submitter that the replacement bases did not lock securely into chair but it was assembled per the instructions given by the firm.

On May 7 the submitter's granddaughter was getting ready to sit on the chair when the chair lifted up and she fell to the floor along with the chair. The submitter said her granddaughter scraped her right arm. The submitter indicated that the base was still sitting up on the ground.

On May 8 the submitter contacted the firm to express her safety concerns and advise them of the incident. The submitter said she spoke with  [REDACTED] and she offered to send her another base.

The submitter then noticed that all of the chairs appeared wobbly and not secure into the base. The submitter contacted the firm again on May 10. The submitter spoke with  [REDACTED] and was told that  [REDACTED] would have to call her back since she had been handling her case. 

The submitter called the firm again today because she didn't receive a call from  [REDACTED]. The submitter spoke with  [REDACTED] who told her that the firm has received many similar complaints about the base being unsecure. The submitter was then transferred to  [REDACTED] and she offered to send her 4 replacement bases from the new batch.  [REDACTED]advised the submitter that a new batch of bases will be available June 15 and the submitter will receive bases from this batch. The submitter said she offered to send back the bases but they said no.

The submitter is concerned that someone will sustain an injury because the chairs are not secure and the replacement bases are not safe. The submitter said when she tried to move the chair it fell apart.
justification: The incident resulted in a scraped arm, indicating an injury, and the firm has received many similar complaints, suggesting the issue is likely to recur.

incident_description: While seated in the Staples Hazen Mesh Office Chair one of the five legs broke near the base causing the chair to collapse.  The occupant fell backwards out of the collapsed chair and hit his head on the wall hard enough to leave an indentation in the sheetrock  beside the chair.

incident_description: This is concerning Westinghouse Timeless Vintage Inspired Bulbs (60watt light bulbs #01432). Since March or April 2017, 3 out of 10 bulbs have shattered. Listed Not OK for totally enclosed fixtures (mine weren't enclosed). Contractor installed them in January in a 4-bulb bathroom vanity light. incident_description: Back in 2014 we purchased two Delta Silverton Oval Mirrors #132892. This past Thursday, one of these came undone from the back tilt bar and crashed to the floor. incident_description:
I have 2 large 15 light chandeliers of the same model and manufacture hanging in my family room. They were bought and installed by the builder 12 yrs ago approximately. We have owned the house for the past 4.5 years. The chandeliers, and in fact all other lights and fixture are original to the house and have never been taken down or changed. WE have not even had to change the bulbs on the 2 large chandeliers that I am reporting today.

About 6 mo ago one of the large chandeliers fell due to a defective chain link that broke. The chandelier fell about 10 feet and smashed a table under it and of course it broke many of its arms. 
At the time, we had everything repaired and rehung BOTH chandeliers with new steel chains to be safe.

Last week the OTHER chandelier fell just a few minutes after my kids had been walking under it. The second chandelier broke where the chain (now steel) hooked onto the hanging column via a loop in the design. The material seems to be some sort of resin that just snapped again. It is the same material as the chain link that broke before.  The fact that NOW 2 of the same chandeliers have fallen due to faulty material makes me believe this is a SERIOUS safety risk. 

I have attempted to contact the builder, the retailer and the company that sold the chandeliers. The company that sold the chandeliers to the retailer is SAVOY HOUSE LIGHTING and the retailer in MACON GA is American Lighting. The builder is TONY BUTLER. I was told there is no warranty and since they can not ensure that the chandelier were hung correctly or used correctly, they will not warrant the materials. 

I have owned many chandeliers in my lifetime and some have hung in my home for 30 years. Under normal use, and cleaning there should not be any reason to even write this note. I know both the builder and the original owners of the house when it was built. The chandeliers have had not undue usage and have been cleaned only a few times. All the bulbs are original as well. 

I would like to ensure no one is injured due to these DEFECTIVE and DANGEROUSLY made large chandeliers. I have pictures and am happy to have someone come to the house to inspect the items and see for themselves. So fat the original seller, SAVOY HOUSE LIGHTING and the retailer, have blown off my concerns rather than taking ownership of these defective materials and coming to the house to at least look over the issues.
justification: The chandeliers fell twice, causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) as both chandeliers failed under normal use.

incident_description:
A candle burning in a glass jar burst into flames and spontaneously broke the glass and the hot wax started the kitchen counter on fire.  I happened to be in the next room and smelled something - and I was able to push the burning glass candle jar into the sink and used a towel on the flames on the countertop. I was lucky, but if this happened when someone was away from the house or sleeping, the house could burn down.  The candle was made by Unique Aromas and was purchased on Amazon:
16 oz Apothecary Jar Candle - Cinnamon Apple.
justification: The incident involved a fire but was quickly contained without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the potential for recurrence if unattended.

incident_description: we had guests over for a birthday party, we had just cut the cake, and suddenly the glass tabletop just exploded like a bomb . glass chards flew everywhere ruining everything on the table and my friend had nicks and cuts on his legs. no medical attention was required.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (nicks and cuts) but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. Glass tabletop explosions are rare but possible under certain conditions.

incident_description:
The stool is/was sold by Dream Duffle LLC.  It's a folding stool that slips into their rolling dance case. It's intended for dancers to take the stool out and and use to sit on during costume changes, backstage, dressing areas or while waiting to dance...etc.  

A ten year old girl was sitting on the stool and it completely collapsed beneath her.  The stool is currently in several pieces.  Luckily besides being shaken a bit, she was not seriously injured.  A sudden falling to the floor like that I am fearful someone could be more seriously injured.  I reached out to Dream Duffle and was told they haven't sold that type stool for several years.  There will still be some in use.  I see them often at dance competitions.  I purchased this one 2-3 years ago directly from Dream Duffle.  

Dream Duffle doesn't seem concerned, they stated that their items are guaranteed for a year and that I could purchase the new style.  I haven't don't that yet, but am hopeful they have redesigned the stool.  My concern is for people/kids who are still using the old design.
justification: The stool collapsed but the child was not seriously injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the stool is still in use and similar incidents could happen.

incident_description:
This consumer purchased a total of six salt lamps online over just a few months between 2013 & 2014 .
She noticed approximately one year later she noticed that the dimmer switches had burned out and had quit working.
She contacted the manufacturer and did as she was instruction which was to order replacement dimmer switches and switch the one's in the lamps.
The dimmer switches received from the manufacturer were changed.
Around March 14 or 15, 2017 her 13 year old son's dimmer switch began begin extremely hot so this caller/his mother placed an order for a replacement dimmer switch which was placed in the salt lamp by the caller.  Ordered replacement on 03/18/17  
Around March 20, 2017 the caller's 13yr old noticed that his dimmer switch was becoming very hot then stopped using.  (New replacement cord just ordered)
The dimmer switch of the second lamp that overheated was purchased February 20, 2013 and it overheated April 1, 2017.
She has stopped using all six of the salt lamps and is reporting these incidents as fire and injury hazards.
She has contacted the manufacturer who has told her to email them the info.
She states that her rug has a burn mark a bit larger than a quarter because the dimmer switch was touching it.
She asks that these salt lamps also become recalled and that she be reimbursed for all six as well as repair of her rug.

Incident date:  3/20/2017 This is an estimate for the dimmer switch.  04/01/17 for the second one that resulted in damage
justification: The incident involved overheating dimmer switches causing a burn mark on a rug, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Maintenance personnel at a residential area replaced several porch lights and installed new light bulbs.  There were two fires, one with a new porch light and one without.  The only common element was the light bulb.  A witness heard a pop and saw flames coming from the light bulb.  The maintenance man removed all the light bulbs he installed in other homes and found another that was melting.   He still has a large supply of exemplar lights.
justification: The incident involved fires caused by faulty light bulbs, but there were no reports of injuries or deaths.

incident_description: On Saturday, July 15,2017 a GE Reveal lightbulb exploded on my daughter and I, there was glass all over us and I had a white powder on my legs. It left burn marks and cuts on me, and it burned holes and melted glass in my bedding.
justification: The incident caused burn marks and cuts, indicating injury, but the likelihood of such an event is relatively low based on historical data.

incident_description: I have been biting the 3wick candle about 1 hour. I walked away for about 2 minutes when I heard my car meowing and it sounded like something was sparking. I came into the living room and seen the candle had flames that were very high and it looked as if all three flames from the wicks combined. It was burning at a high rate I didn't know what to do so I yelled for my wife. We tried the fire extinguisher it was having problems. The glass shattered and wax spilled. My wife ran outside and grabbed some dirt to throw on it which finally put it out. This was a very scary experience for us and we are glad is wasn't worse than this.
justification: The incident involved a high flame from a candle and a failed fire extinguisher, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: The glass casing around the filament bulb exploded shortly after the light was turned on in my children's bathroom.   I was standing in the bathroom and heard glass shatter and looked up and the light was on with the filament still on with the glass shattered on the counter.
justification: The glass casing exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible as bulb explosions can occur but are not frequent.

incident_description: We bought a white night stand from Living Space Fremont. It still has very strong chemical smell after 6  months. It is unusually pungent.  After one night sleep with the nightstand, everyone feel dizzy in the morning. we suggest the nightstand can get a examine done.
justification: The strong chemical smell caused dizziness, indicating a health impact, and the issue persists over time.

incident_description:
The safety housing around the plug of a desk lamp came off completely, leaving exposed wiring at the wall behind my child's bed. When he went to unplug the lamp he grabbed the full bundle of ecectronics and received a full electrical shock. The safety housing appears to be defective in that it came off so easily. 

We have two of these, and I just unplugged the second lamp from my over boys room and sure enough, the safety casing pops right off the wall plug. 

These lamps are from Target's Arcadia Collection - Model AF36588
justification: The incident resulted in an electrical shock (injury) to a child, and the defect is easily reproducible in another lamp, indicating a likely occurrence.

incident_description: Hey ya'll, I'm just wondering what I'm supposed to do here? So I'll tell ya quick background. Ever since I was a little kid, I've had asthma and constricted airways. I'm not classified as a severe asthmatic but I must have my inhailer on me at all times and I really can't do much by the way of physical activity. It just seems to aggravate and constrict my breathing too much. Anyhows, I begged and begged and begged my boyfriend into buying me one of those new purple beds. I mean, that video is just a hoot! My boyfriend, god bless him, but he is such a researcher and such a skeptic. Well, in doing his manly research, he told me that like some Doctor said the purple beds can be bad for breathin. I told him he's just bein paranoid and that I have to have the bed!! After much argument, which I obviously won, he got me the bed. Well, I was super excited, of course, and I found it so comfortable to sleep on for a few months maybe? I've never been much good at keepin track of time afterall. Anyhow, life goes on and my boyfriend points out that he's been refillin my inhailers faster than usual, and when he went to refill my last one it was flagged by the pharmacy or somethin and I had to call my doctor. The office said they needed to see me (I usually would only go a few times a year) because of the rate of refills. Ya know, to me I really didn't notice much change, I guess when you've had a condition for 30 years ya just kinda get used to it, ya know? But my boyfriend started to tell me he thinks what he read wasn't just fake news and that the bed was making me have those breathin problems that he read about. I still said no no, how can a bed possibly make anyone sick? Or sicker than they already are? Anywho, so we go to the doctor and he examines me, would ya'll actually believe this? He said it sounds like my lungs are actually gettin worse! He can hear the air flow is more restricted, hence why I'm wheezin and coughin and feelin the shortness of breath more and using up my medicines faster! OH if only you could see my boyfriend's face in that moment, he wanted to kill me with the deathly I TOLD YOU SO look !!! So now I'm like, well gee wiz, In all my life I've always been about the same with my medicine use, I switch beds and now it gets worse. I mean I ain't no brain scientist or rocket scientist like the purple beds claim they are, but I guess I have to admit when somethin seems like more than a coincidence? So here I am, my asthma is worse and my doctor is NOT happy with how rapidly it's progressed. He says at this rate I'm start havin attacks on a regular basis and those would be really bad, I could end up going to the hospital and he said I could even die!! What the hell??? So I need to know what I am to do now! My boyfriend threw the bed in the garbage! He called up the company, told them what happened and ya'll know what they said? They gave us some fake science crap right back! They tellin us how it's a million percent safe, it's food grade blah blah I'm like well my doctor says I could DIE. They just keep tellin me that I'm wrong. So okay, now what? Like I could die, how many other people could die now too? I just don't want the children to be harmed. Can ya'll do something? Should I sue them?
justification: The incident describes a worsening of asthma symptoms leading to potential life-threatening attacks, classified as an injury with possible severe outcomes.

incident_description:
Glass medicine cabinet door fell and almost landed on a child. It was not an installation error as the door didn't fall off the hinges but off what looks like a glues on frame. Glass shattered but I was able to stop the whole things from crashing onto my child. 

This is a Pegasus Brand medicine cabinet. Pegasus is a proprietary brand of the Home Depot. 
Model number 202588344
justification: The glass door fell and shattered but was stopped from hitting the child, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: I received a recall letter from [REDACTED] regarding bar patio chairs purchased at Loews. It is for Models [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] which are Loews items #[REDACTED] and #[REDACTED]. I had purchased 4 chairs that look like the exact picture in the letter. However, I also purchased 4 different chairs at Loews at the same time which have had the exact same weld breakage issue. They have a Home Trends label on them, are the same height, design and fabric, but have a different base. I do not see a model number but Loew's records should indicate my purchase which was on credit. The base is square rather than circular. I'm positive it is the same manufacturer and believe these chairs should also be part of a recall. The chairs were purchase in 2010
justification: The description reports a product defect (weld breakage) but no injuries or incidents resulting from it.

incident_description: A GE Reveal lightbulb, 72 Watts, overheated and exploded very violently. The bulb was installed in a ceiling fixture in a kitchen. I was in another room and saw a flash of light around the corner and heard a loud bang. When I came into the kitchen there was a smell of burning, and, looking up, I could see that the glass dome of the light fixture was full of broken glass and other objects. It was quite difficult to remove the bulb at first because the fixture, the ceiling, and everything inside the fixture had overheated so badly. The shards of glass were projected out of the bulb soap fiercely violently that they scored the inside of the fixture. And now the kitchen has fine dust of broken glass spread about because the explosion was so vigorous that a fine powder of broken glass escaped the light fixture. It was challenging to get the broken bulb out of fixture, because the glass was almost entirely missing. I believe these bulbs pose an extreme hazard. The bulb could easily have blinded someone nearby. There was a considerable risk of eye injury involved just in the cleanup. Besides that, the fixture and bulb were so overheated that there appears to be a genuine risk of these bulbs causing a fire.
justification: The incident involved a violent explosion of a lightbulb causing property damage and potential for injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: My family purchased a sectional couch in the summer of 2013. The couch began shedding its outer blended leather material coating in the fall of 2013. More and more of the coating of material that covered the couch flaked and peeled off over time. Our infant son occasionally ate pieces of the couch material and/or put his mouth on the couch itself thereby getting flakes in his mouth and inadvertently ingesting the material. At one year of age our son had a lead blood level of 12. Upon receiving this result, our family chose to test the couch material for lead. The couch resulted with 400 ppm.
justification: The infant ingested lead from the couch material, resulting in a lead blood level of 12, which indicates injury.

incident_description:
(02/01/2017) The consumer stated that his wife removed the plastic sleeve from the light bulb. When she screwed the bulb into the chandelier, the bulb exploded.

The consumer contacted Kichler. He was referred to Ankon. The consumer received a letter from Ankon that acknowledged that there should have been instructions on the box to advise him of the sleeves.

The consumer also contacted his local Lowes and they removed the bulbs and the chandeliers but had to place them back on the shelves because of a contract with the manufacturer

There were no injuries.
justification: The incident involved a bulb exploding but resulted in no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as such incidents are not common but can occur.

incident_description:
While standing over the sink, one of the globes in the fixture exploded over my head.  The fixture is approximately 6" taller than my reach, so no way could I have bumped it.  The lightbulb is still in the fixture but the globe shattered all over the vanity.

As I cleaned up the glass in the sink, I noticed a yellow powder residue along with the glass.  I have pictures of the shattered glass, powder, and entire fixture post explosion on my cell phone.
justification: The incident involved an exploding globe with no reported injury, and such occurrences are possible but not frequent.

incident_description: I received a recall letter from 3i Corporation Limited regarding bar patio chairs purchased at Loews. It is for Models 773-C3 and 1106-2 which are Loews items #102821 and #151737. I had purchased 4 chairs that look like the exact picture in the letter. However, I also purchased 4 different chairs at Loews at the same time which have had the exact same weld breakage issue. They have a [REDACTED] label on them, are the same height, design and fabric, but have a different base. I do not see a model number but Loew's records should indicate my purchase which was on credit. The base is square rather than circular. I'm positive it is the same manufacturer and believe these chairs should also be part of a recall. The chairs were purchase in 2010
justification: The incident involves a product recall due to weld breakage, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description:
The consumer found the following  Kichler "Model: 34221" and "Date Code: IR" on the chandeliers metal plate that is screwed to the wall. 

The consumer was in her office when she heard a loud noise and when she walked in dining room she noticed that the chandelier was on the floor. The consumer said the fixture ring that connects to the chain had broke. 

The consumer contacted the retailer, Lowes and informed them of the incident. The consumer wanted to find out who the manufacturer is but they advised her without a receipt they could not tell her who the manufacturer is. The consumer plans to visit the store and speak with a manager. 

The consumer found multiple recalls online for the same safety hazard and believes her chandelier should be recalled if it's not already.
justification: The chandelier fell but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the consumer found multiple recalls for the same issue.

incident_description:
I have several of these light bulbs installed in my kitchen, pointed straight down.  This morning I saw that one was at a funny angle.  I turned it off, poked it, and noted that it moved easily.  I carefully unscrewed it and saw that the lower part of the housing had detached, partially exposing the innards, capacitors, and wires.  The portion with the driver circuitry is in one part with the chip on silicon illumination portion is in the other, held together by just wires now.  A few pieces of plastic fell out.

It was positioned not directly over a heat source.
justification: The light bulb housing detached, exposing internal components, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
A Capri track light fell at [REDACTED] in Granite Bay, CA during a funeral mass.  The light did not injure anyone but very easily could have since it landed within a couple of feet of the Altar near the location the Priest sits.  The light fell approximately 25+ feet and very easily could have seriously injured or killed someone.  The light weighs close to 10 pounds.  I am a Parishioner as well as an employee of the General Contractor that constructed the church in 2011.  I have contacted Philips and have been assigned a case number.  We have since removed all of the Capri track lights (15 total), and found that at least one more of them was badly degraded and ready to fall.  I would like to know how the end user of the product would have ever known about this recall. I only found out about it when I went onto the Philips/Capri website.

I am attempting to get suitable replacement fixtures from Philips. Also, I would like to know if Philips is required to pay for the labor and equipment to remove and re-install the lights.  This will end up costing the Parish several thousand dollars since these lights are difficult to access.
justification: The light fell but did not injure anyone, though it posed a significant risk due to its weight and height. The discovery of another degraded light suggests a likely recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: On Two occasions, the glass globe of the  flush mounted ceiling light simply fell off.  Both times, the lights were off.  Both times the glass globe shattered, sending glass everywhere.  The first time, it fell at the precise moment that my daughter walked underneath it, crashing on her head.  She had glass in her hair and a cut on on her forehead.
justification: The glass globe fell and caused a cut on the daughter's forehead, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
My wife and I were sitting in our Allen & Roth Safford swivel bar chairs on our deck and drinking our morning coffee. Then, without warning the chair I was sitting in collapsed causing me to fall back and down hitting my head on the patio railing, scraping my left leg, and hurting my left hip and leg. After I was able to get up from the deck I made it into the house to sit and evaluate if I needed medical attention from a doctor or could handle the injuries at home. My leg required a bandage to stop the bleeding, my head had a slight bump, and my hip & leg were sore where they landed on the broken chair pieces while hitting the patio deck. 

It was only after tracking down my receipt for the chairs and table, spending time searching Lowe's web site for this product's warranty information, did I find there was a recall on this product. I am extremely upset I was not notified by Lowe's or the manufacturer about this recall. A simple letter or call would have saved me injury!
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring bandaging and evaluation for medical attention, but no death or severe harm. The likelihood is unlikely as recalls typically address such issues, though not always effectively.

incident_description:
Fluorescent light tube in LED Linear Form used to replace standard flurorescent light 
bulbs.

2ND INCIDENT OF BULB MELTING AND FALLING ON VEHICLE.  FILLED GARAGE WITH NASTY BURNING SMELL.
justification: The incident involved a bulb melting and falling, causing a burning smell but no reported injury.

incident_description:
I have purchased a signature sleep memory foam mattress from Amazon.com 3 years ago; about a month ago, I found out that there are clear, almost invisible sparkles coming out of it. After a call with manufacture, I discovered that these 
sparkles are fiberglass. They cause irritation to the skins when in contact and are extremely difficult to extract from fabrics. As result, I have to throw away tons of cloths, all my pillows, mattress covers, pillow covers, blankets. This product has caused undue financial and emotional stress to our family that includes one 6 month old baby. We don't know what potential health risks we are exposed of because of this product and from the review we see similar things have happened.
justification: The incident involves fiberglass exposure causing skin irritation and financial loss, but no severe injury or death is reported.

incident_description: My husband was sitting on our deck at our 7 pc dining set and the swivel chair fell backwards and he fell out. The chair welds broke completely. He bumped his head.
justification: The incident resulted in a head injury from a fall due to chair failure.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her chest/dresser tipped over and fell breaking the objects on it.  The item was recalled and she had sent for a repair kit about 8 months ago but never received it.  Fortunately a child was not present when the incident occurred to cause any injury or fatality.

Recall#15-190   Hazard: Chests and dressers can tip over if not attached to the wall, posing an entrapment hazard.

The manufacturer was contacted and a voicemail was left.
justification: The dresser tipped over but no one was injured, and the child was not present, so severity is low. The occurrence likelihood is high due to the recall and the repair kit not being received.

incident_description: I am writing to report a melted handle on an electric blanket. I purchased the product a few months ago at Target. It is a Biddeford Electric velour/sherpa throw and I bought it on clearance. I was using it to help warm up my bed last week, and probably used it 10-15 times before this occurrence. I fell asleep with it on top of my bedspread so I don't know for sure where the handle ended up. When I woke up in the morning, it was a bit scrunched up at the end of the bed and super hot. I couldn't turn it off because the handle had melted and it wouldn't allow me to push the off button. I am reporting this because it felt much hotter than it did before I went to bed. In addition, I have used electric blankets my entire life and I have never had a handle melt on me. I am very concerned that this could happen to other people and burn them or cause a fire. I will be provided the same copy of this email to Target and if I can locate the company, I will try that as well. Please let me know if you need additional information.
justification: The incident involved a melted handle on an electric blanket with no reported injury, but potential for harm exists.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that she purchased children bedding from the Wal-Mart in Oneonta, NY and made a apron from one of the pillow cases.  She stated that she tested the fabric by lighting a piece of it in a container and it burnt out completely in less than a min.  She feels that these children bedding is dangerous and should be taken off the market immediately.

Caller stated that there is no labeling on the bedding about it being flammable.  She stated that it is 100% polyester.  She stated that she returned the remainder of the set she purchased to the store.

Caller feels that this product is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involves flammable bedding but no actual injury or death occurred, and the caller returned the product.

incident_description: I purchased at VITTSJO Laptop stand in glass, last night the table exploded with out cause, glass was everywhere, in the wall and stuck in the floor, we could still hear it popping even when it scattered. this needs to be pulled of the shelves ASAP
justification: The glass table exploded without causing injury, but the incident poses a significant hazard.

incident_description: Top surface of tempered glass TV stand made by Innovex spontaneously exploded, completely shattering into thousands of pieces.  Glass pieces were propelled over entire room, and would have caused serious injuries if anyone had been watching or playing nearby.  No known prior damage or other problem that could have caused this.
justification: The incident involved spontaneous explosion causing property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents are possible based on the description.

incident_description:
The Garden Oasis Harrison 7 piece patio set is sold by Sears and others. It comes with a glass table in a metal frame. On Friday, the glass spontaneously shattered into a million tiny pieces. We could see no evidence of anything falling on the table. If you look at reviews online, there are many people complaining of the same thing. This is very unsafe, if we or our children had been sitting at the table at the time (luckily we were not home). Harrison must know this is happening as they explicitly do not cover the glass in their warranty.

Look at reviews here:
http://www.sears.com/garden-oasis-harrison-7-piece-dining-set/p-07134582000P
justification: The glass table shattered spontaneously, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries occurred. Online reviews indicate this is a recurring issue.

incident_description: I was reclined in my Dutailier Round Back Cushion Design Modern Glider Multiposition, Recline and Ottoman Combo with my newborn who I had been breastfeeding. When I leaned forward to exit the recline position, the chair fell over on top of me and the baby (we are okay). My partner had to remove the chair from on top of us. Since the chair is marketed as a recliner, I don't understand why it's most basic use would trigger such a safety hazard.
justification: The chair fell over but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting a celebratory candle that was used on his birthday cake May 23, 2017.
The candle was purchased from a retailer in Virginia on May 23, 2017.
He lit the candle which is one that a center candle is lit, the candle begins turning and playing music while a circle of candles light from the first one and fall down into the circle while continuing to turn and play music.
He leaned forward to blow the candles out and his four year old daughter leaned forward at the same time.
The fire touched his left cheek and burned and blackened a spot a bit smaller than a dime.
His four year old grand daughter's right eye was burned and reddened.
Both injuries were treated at home by none medical persons.
The caller contacted the manufacturer also on May 23, 2017 and he was informed by the female answering that they had no reports of problems with candles ordered from their company but that someone would return his call.
No one has returned his call at this date and time.
justification: Both the consumer and his granddaughter suffered burns, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: While sitting in swivel bar chair, a replacement chair as previous chair broke in March 2015, (report filed for that incident as well) set detached from base again.
justification: The incident describes a chair detachment without mention of injury, indicating an equipment failure with no harm to personnel.

incident_description: While sitting in the swivel bar chair, the seat detached from the base.
justification: The seat detaching from the base could cause a fall, potentially leading to injury.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his television stand with three glass shelves that he purchased around May 1st, 2016. 
He had no problems with this stand until May 6th, 2017 when he was in another room and heard something that sounded like a soft explosion followed by a waterfall.
He went to the room where the television stand was located and saw that the middle glass shelf had exploded sending glass all over the room.
He is reporting this product and incident as extremely hazardous and potentially harmful for lacerations. 
There are no injuries being reported
He said that the brand name and the manufacturer have web sites and phone numbers that no one responds to although he has tried numerous times.
justification: The incident involved a glass shelf exploding, causing potential harm, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is possible as similar incidents may occur but are not frequent.

incident_description: Hampton Bay Swivel Patio Chair - There is a recall, but not for the issue I had.  The recall is for only the base.  My chair collapsed on me when sitting on it causing me to injure my tailbone and head.  The welding on the bottom of the seat entirely broke off from it seams.  There have been other issues exactly as to what happened to me on consumer affairs.  The seams are located immediately underneath the seat and are attached to the top section of the chair that slides into the base.  The recall is only for the base.
justification: The chair collapsed, causing injury to the tailbone and head, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The mention of other similar incidents on consumer affairs suggests this is a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I just bought this product and was using it on my addition which is covered by a roof/ awning on my porch!! When I began to screw it in the socket it exploded in my face/ hand!!! I had to dig little glass pieces out of my hands and  breast/ chest!!! I have been using this same Type of bulb here since last year and never a problem at all!!! It sounded like a small bomb when it exploded in my hand!!!! The product is GE Indoor flood lamp!!!
justification: The incident resulted in injuries from glass pieces, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the user had no prior issues with similar bulbs.

incident_description:
I purchased a patio set, 3 years ago, at Walmart. The set had a table, 4 chairs and an umbrella. Was not expensive. 
 This past Friday, I was sitting outside, and went into the house, and was only in the house a matter of seconds, when I heard a loud noise. I went back outside, and the glass on my table, was shattered, and all the glass was in millions of pieces, on my deck. It took  me forever, to sweep up most of the glass. A lot of it is now embedded in the grooves of my deck.
 I missed my legs being cut up, by mere seconds.
 I contacted the manufacturer, and they said I could purchase another glass top for $50. I replied, that I did not want their defective glass, and I was ordering another table. They, replied again, that I could purchase another glass top, for the cost of shipping, $20. I also declined that offer, as I am afraid of their glass.
 Walmart is still selling this patio set, and it is sold out, so many people have purchased it.
 I think consumer's should be warned, that the glass is defective, and possibly could cause injury. I had nothing on the table, at the time it shattered, except a small ashtray, a pack of cigarrettes, and a lighter. Nothing heavy. Sometimes I have sat outside, and had a book, on the table. It was about 85 degree's out, so heat should not have caused this.
 I have talked to numerous people, and no one has ever heard of this happening before. Can you look into this?
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass table without injury, indicating an incident with no harm (severity 2). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as the issue is not widespread but has potential for recurrence.

incident_description:
While a lady was working at an office in Chico, California and went to sit down in her office chair, the chair seat broke off of the pedestal, and she fell on the pedestal and then to the legs of the chair and the floor injuring her buttocks and lower back.  She suffered nerve damage that persists five years after the injury, and has had to charge occupation so she could alternate between sitting and standing during the workday.
The chair was sold by Office Master Inc. who imported the chair from the manufacturer, King Hong Industrial Company Ltd. Of Taiwan.  A second chair of the same manufacturer and model failed several weeks later and the person that fell when that chair broke sustained unknown injuries. 
I am filing this report because it appears the chair failed from normal use and that the chair should not have so failed.
justification: The incident resulted in nerve damage and a persistent injury requiring a change in occupation, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as a second chair of the same model failed shortly after.

incident_description:

incident_description:
Product:  Sylvania 20882 Compact Fluorescent 4 Pin Triple Tube 4100K, 26-watt 
              (Likely applies to similar products.)

Issue:  Faulty product design and inadequate hazard labeling

Setting:  These tubes are designed to be mounted in a recessed ceiling reflector. They are in widespread use in recently constructed homes, condos and other applications. They are typically found mounted in high ceilings (e.g., 9-12 ft.), accessible only by ladder. To replace a tube, one pulls it out of the socket by grasping the tube and pulling it downward with considerable force. Replacement tubes are popped in with less force.

Faulty design:  The tubes break easily when grasping them and pulling downward, due to the force required to pull them out. This has happened to me on several occasions. I have found it impossible to remove the bulbs from the fixtures without breakage. (Some fixtures may be more roomy, which would make the task easier.) Numerous such experiences are reported on the internet. Releasing the snap-in clips simply requires way too much force. 

The specific hazards are:  1) falling off the ladder when the bulb suddenly comes free from the socket, 2) cuts on fingers from mercury-containing tubes, 3) showers of glass and mercury in the face and eyes, because you are standing on the ladder looking up at the tube when it shatters. 

The design is irresponsible and does not consider the intended use. This product, as sold and labeled, is dangerous and not suitable for general domestic applications.

Inadequate hazard labeling:  The label indicates the tubes contain mercury, but noes not warn that they are hazardous. The packaging does not warn about likely breakage, and it includes no instructions on safe removal and replacement. Sylvania must be aware of the safety issues, and is clearly negligent in labeling this product.

Work-around:  I have found a reasonably safe way to replace the tubes: 1) Remove the reflector to allow access to the base of the tube. Wear sturdy gloves, due to the danger of laceration on sharp, sheet-metal edges; 2) Wrap the entire tube in duct tape, so that if-and-when it breaks, the glass and mercury dust is safely contained; 3) Wearing gloves, grasp the tube firmly in one hand and apply steady downward pressure, while rocking it slightly back and forth. Steady oneself on the ladder with the other hand; 4) Snap in the new bulb, and replace the reflector; 4) Vacuum up the plaster dust that has shelled out from the opening in the ceiling during the preceding steps.
justification: The incident describes potential injuries from broken tubes, including cuts and exposure to mercury, and a risk of falling from a ladder, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high due to widespread reports of breakage during removal.

In April of 2016, I purchased the "WBM Natural Air Purifying Himalayan Salt Lamp with Salt Chunks, Bulb and Dimmer Control, Round Basket Style" from Amazon through the seller WBM LLC; it was fulfilled by Amazon.com LLC. 

A few weeks ago (March 2017) the lamp stopped working. I initially thought it was a bad bulb but new bulbs didn't work. I checked the outlet and cord, discovering the switch had a melted depression on the back. I opened the switch to find burn marks inside. 

I believe these lamps are a fire hazard. Salt lamps must be left on most of the day, every day, to keep the salt dry. This means the lamps are bound to be unsupervised, making the risks of fire spreading unnoticed higher than with other kinds of lamps. 

While many salt lamps sold by WBM have been recalled, Amazon is not accepting returns of this item and is still selling them despite customers reporting similar problems to the one I encountered.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning salt lamp with burn marks, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.
