justification: The incident involved a chair breaking, causing a fall, but no injury was reported. The recall notice and similar issue with another chair indicate a likely occurrence.

incident_description: We were sitting in our gazebo on may 9 , 2017 when all of a sudden my husband was lying on the concrete slab Apparently the barstool cracked one of the prongs on the b base snapped . I work for lowes , and was talking to my manager about this and he advised me to call garden treasures, and doing some research on my own we came across a recall for our set which we purchased around 2012 with the round table.
justification: The incident resulted in the husband falling due to a broken barstool, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: My neighbor came over and sat down as normal as always and the chair just gave out from under her and she fell straight down and back and she crumbled up like a pretzel! She is in her 50's and definitely felt the aftermath of falling a drop backwards like that for days and days!! I just saw about this recall the other day and looked to see if mine were the same chair sets... I had thrown the bottom piece with the legs away but did happen to save the top part and where you can clearly see where the weld part just came undone and crumbled like! It was very traumatic because my 4yr old saw her fall from where she was playing in the yard and came running to check on her because it was such a hard direct fall backwards and down!
justification: The neighbor suffered injuries from the fall, as indicated by her feeling the aftermath for days, but there was no mention of death or severe trauma.

incident_description:
Individual was leaning back in Haworth X640-0140 chair, at which point the plastic mechanism managing the tension on the back of the chair failed, causing it to abruptly recline several inches and fragments to fly across the room.  Examination revealed three chairs out of a dozen in an identical condition, suggesting former unreported incidents.  A subsequent online search revealed that our experience was not unique (see link below).

https://opexshare.doe.gov/lesson.cfm/2014/3/12/4109/Haworth-Chair-X99-Seminar-defect-requires-recallretrofit
justification: The incident involved a chair failure causing abrupt reclining and flying fragments, but no injury was reported. The presence of similar defects in other chairs and online reports suggest this is a recurring issue.

incident_description: I purchased a Casual Living patio set from Home Depot a few years ago. Las summer my son sat in one for the two swivel chairs and the base snapped and he fell to the ground. I contacted Casual Living and they said this specific chair was not covered under the recall even though this is the same issue as the current recall
justification: The incident resulted in injury (falling to the ground) but no death, and similar incidents are documented but not widespread.

incident_description: This LED bulb was purchased at Lowes and installed into a 3 light ceiling fan in our bathroom approximately 3 months prior to incident date. While my wife was in the shower, she heard a loud pop and the lightbulb fell to the floor. It did not break, but a good deal of smoke was observed in the fixture area when I got into the bathroom. The base of the bulb was exposed with some visible melting noted on the plastic base adjacent to the little diode as well as the plastic covering of the one wire. The base was extremely hot to touch. The metal part of the base remained in the light fixture.
justification: The incident involved a loud pop, smoke, and a hot bulb falling, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
While my wife was using the sink, the hot lens of an overhead light bulb detached and went flying, and hit her in the head.  Fortunately she was not seriously injured.

The bulb is a Philips Par16 Halogen light bulb, 420 Lumens, I believe it is 45W.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb detaching and hitting someone, but no serious injury occurred.

incident_description: Bed collapsed due to side rail support failing.  A screw in the cross supports also broke(head snapped off ) This left a sharp metal clip exposed along with splinters.  The bed is used by a six year old weighing less than 50 lbs..  I have pictures of the failure.
justification: The bed collapse exposed sharp metal and splinters, posing a risk of injury to the child, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I have a set of bar stools purchased from Lowe's between May and October 2015. They are in use on the balcony of our condo at Indian Rocks Beach, which we rent out for vacationers. One vacationer recently reported that a chair 'broke' and they put it in the dumpster. I was angry as suspected it was misused, but then another renter (who is also a friend) reported to me on April 22nd that her husband had fallen to the floor when the chair he was sitting on snapped in two. I contacted Lowe's who have been trying to fob me off asking for a receipt and telling me they were out of warranty. When I explained they were a safety hazzard they began to listen but NO ONE told me they had been recalled - I goggled the issue and came across this website.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall and injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as multiple incidents have been reported.

incident_description: (03/10/2017) The consumer stated that bulb went out in the lamp. Four minutes, later the fire alarm in the condominium went off . It also tripped the circuit breaker. The consumer looked at the lamp and discovered the plastic on the bulb was burned.
justification: The bulb failure and subsequent fire alarm activation indicate an incident with no injury.

incident_description: We have been using fluorescent light bulbs for many years. We have 8 bulbs in our main bathroom. Of the 8 bulbs, 6 are made by GE and 2 are made by Sylvania. Couple of days ago I noticed one of the Sylvania stopped working. Then today, the other Sylvania bulb flickered a few times about 1 minute after I turned them on. Then it went out. But soon I smelled something burning and noticed that the light bulb that just went out was burning. I immediately turned off the electricity. But the light bulb had already burned out at one of the two stems. The bulb is about 3 inch below the ceiling, which has been darkened by the burn. Room was filled with very bad strong odor.
justification: The incident involved a burning light bulb causing damage and a strong odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Turned on the light switch, and the compact florescent bulb caught on fire. Flames shot out of its ballast, but it did not damage anything other than the bulb. The labels on the bulb include "Listed 6G49 UL" also "GE Helical 15W 120VAC 60Hz 230mA FLE15HT3/2/SW FC" and "Y182"
justification: The bulb caught fire but did not cause any injury or damage beyond the bulb itself, indicating a minor incident.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that she purchased eight salt lamps from store online on December 13, 2016.

She had been using the lamps with no problems until Tuesday, January 24, 2017 when her husband got up early for work, he smelled something burning, he looked over at the kitchen counter and saw smoke then realized it was coming from the area of the salt lamp and so he unplugged it.

After unplugging the lamp he inspected the area and saw that it had burned an area of approximately two inches long with one inch wide.  He went around the house unplugging all eight salt lamp and placed them on a bench in the kitchen.

There are no injuries at this time

The caller did send a message to Walmart notifying them of the hazard and requesting a refund.
justification: The incident involved a salt lamp emitting smoke and causing minor property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
We replaced many incandescent lightbulbs in our house with LED lights, including in our bathroom.  We purchased 4 "solais par 30" lightbulbs for our master bathroom see http://www.solais.com/News-65-Solais_Lighting_Selected_for_Final_LED_Test_at_Smithsonian_American_Art_Museum.    They were in place and used extensively for more than one year.  They were purchased from Bethesda Systems http://www.bethesdasystems.com.  

Without warning on or about February 15,2017,  one of the lolais par 30" lightbulbsexploded, scattering glass all over the bathroom.  We reported this to the retailer.  They requested all four of the lightbulbs which we gave to them on March 1, 2017.  We have not heard back from them or from the manufacturer about this extremely dangerous situation.
justification: The lightbulb exploded, causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On 23 January 2017 I purchased a Mainstay Folding Slat Chair from Walmart San Diego, CA.  Today, while leaving a voice-message on my cousin's voice-mail I sat down in the chair, as I had done many times since its purchase and I went straight to the ground.  Closer examination revealed that two welds on the bottom had failed.  I had pre-existing back injury and not sure if this exasperated or not.  Nonetheless, it doesn't hurt to make it a matter of record.
justification: The chair failure caused a fall, and while the pre-existing back injury's aggravation is uncertain, the incident involved potential injury.

incident_description: My wife was sitting in a Fall River Swivel chair when it completely broke off the base causing her to fall backward hitting her head, hand and hip.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the head, hand, and hip, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My kids had their light on for about an hour. A few minute after we turned off the light, I heard a loud noise and my kids screaming. The GE bulb in the ceiling fixture exploded. There was glass all over the room including on my 8 year old. The biggest piece of the bulb says Hungary and 72. There is white dust too.
justification: The bulb explosion caused glass to scatter, including on a child, indicating potential injury risk.

incident_description: I walked into my bedroom and found shards of broken glass over a large portion of my bed and carpet plus several small burn holes in the comforter.  One of the 3 light bulbs in my ceiling fixture had exploded leaving only the filament and base intact.  I immediately turned off the switch and waited for the other bulbs to cool before removing.  Meanwhile, I checked the internet to see if there was a problem with the GE Clear Crystal bulbs and found quite a few reports detailing the same experiences  with this brand....including descriptions of "fire raining down."  Please investigate to determine if they should be recalled.  I had some paperwork laying on the bed and if it had been any closer to the explosion area, my house could have gone up in smoke!
justification: The incident involved a light bulb explosion causing property damage but no injuries, and similar incidents have been reported with the same brand.

incident_description: My children and I began smelling plastic burning, looked all around the house and discovered the dimmer switch in my salt lamp smoking and had melted.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and melted dimmer switch, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My husband and I got the Himalayan salt rock lamp as a gift for our wedding. I love rocks and I love the soft light from the lamp when I fall asleep. Recently though the knob has started to get very hot when the lamp is on. Even when it's on for merely 10 minutes the dimmer knob feels like it is burning. My husband and I are now concerned that it is a fire hazard if we use it as a night light. Breaks my heart. I love this lamp. I don't know what to do.
justification: The dimmer knob getting very hot indicates a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: 5 year old son had bottom two drawers open on dresser and when he went to close them, the dresser fell forward. He was able to back out of the way and was not injured.
justification: The dresser fell but the child was not injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer heard a loud pop noise and when she walked into her dining room she noticed her dining table had small pieces of glass. The consumer realized that one of the globes in the chandelier, which is above the table, had shattered and it had a hair line fracture. 

The consumer indicated that this was the fourth globe that had shattered. The first incident occurred on June 15, 2016, the second incident occurred on August 27, 2016 and the third occurred on October 23, 2016.

The consumer contacted her interior designer and notified them of the incidents. 

The consumer also contacted the firm and notified them of the incidents. The firm told her that the wattage of the bulbs could have caused them to break. However, the consumer said the chandelier can accommodate eight 40 watt bulbs and she has eight 25 watt bulbs. 

The consumer indicated that she hired an interior designer who purchased the chandelier and it was installed in May 2016. The chandelier was ordered in December 2015.
justification: The incident involved shattered glass but no injury, and it has occurred multiple times, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: My daughter received a Plasma Ball as a gift from a friend.  Packaging states "Room2Room", "Distributed by Five Below Merchandising, Inc, 1818 Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103, Made in China, Item # RD4041.  She inserted the batteries, all 4 placed correctly in the battery box and turned it on.  It worked briefly and then the odor of burning plastic/electrical parts stated coming from it.  That is when I took it and turned it off.  I checked the batteries, all inserted properly.  I turned it back on and monitored it.  The plastic inside the globe began to melt, the batteries became warm and the device began to have visible smoke come out of it.  I turned it off and removed the batteries.  At which time it stopped smoking.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device that emitted smoke and had melting plastic, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: The Lighting fixture above the kitchen table houses three bulbs, one of the globes from the lamp fell off and hit table fortunately no one was injured.  It appears the adhesive holding the globe on the lamp failed and release the glass globe.
justification: A globe fell off the lighting fixture but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Burning a candle in a glass holder that was sitting on platform of bathtub.  It exploded sending shards. It appears the wick burned down to the bottom and heated the glass rather than burning out.
justification: The candle explosion caused shards to scatter, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
I ordered Ever Brite solar lights in February 2016.  
I complained to the company twice of the short life of their products within 9 months (Nov). They last less than 6500 hours when they guarantee 5 years or 100,000 hours. I received no response back. 
The near tragedy that just happened was one of the lights exploded and sparked a fire.  My garage almost burned down.  I wasn't home, so I was lucky that it melted off and fell to the ground.  But there was damage to the garage and the garage door.  
I wrote to the company again and attached photos of the damage and the defective product (what was left of it). Still waiting to hear from them.
I'm still pretty shook up at what could have happened. I'm remodeling and everything I own is in the garage.
I want to warn everyone not to buy the product.  Many stores sell them, as does the internet.  They all need recalled because they will eventually burn down someone's house.
justification: The incident involved a solar light exploding and causing a fire, resulting in property damage but no injury or death.

incident_description: I was using an electric throw in the evening and the control panel shorted out. It was sparking and the noise was clearly audible to everyone in the room.  Immediately pulled plug from the wall.  After it shorted out, it was still possible to turn on the control panel although it no longer heated the throw.
justification: The electric throw shorted out and sparked, but no injury occurred as the plug was immediately pulled.

incident_description: Bulb was screwed into outside door light fixture and was not functioning. When I went to unscrew bulb the metal portion of the bulb that screws into the socket portion separated from bulb housing staying in the liight fixture and exposing electrical wires. I had to use needle nose players to remove the product from the fixture
justification: The incident involved a bulb malfunction exposing wires, but no injury occurred, and such incidents are possible with routine bulb changes.

incident_description: While sitting in revolving chair the weld that holds the seat to the base separated and I fell straight down and injured my back.
justification: The incident resulted in a back injury, which qualifies as a severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: We purchased a Barrett PowerRecline La-Z-Time Full Reclining Sofa in August 2016. We had to buy it from a catalog, as there were none in the store. The salesman had us sit in a similar one and stated it would be the same. It is extremely hard to get out of and one needs to push with their hand, which slides down in the back of the cushion. In doing so your hand comes in contact with sharp edged wood, (has cut me several times). The design, while sitting in a normal manor is such that you can reach down in the back of the seat cushion and come in contact with moving metal levers. This is a danger to children as well as adults searching for dropped items, keys, toys, or anything lost while reclining. (Very easy to be pinched between wood and metal moving parts resulting in possible loss of finger), The front under the footrest is wide open to any thing that can walk or crawl into it. There is a thin piece of fabric just hanging in front. All the moving leavers are exposed in there just waiting for a child, dog or cat to crawl in and become mangled. I have complained to La-Z-Boy and they basically say, ÃÂRead the manualÃÂ and gave me a canned reply.  Having been an engineer and designed much more complicated products than this, it is an accident waiting to happen. Note: photos would not upload even with flash installed.
justification: The description reports cuts from sharp-edged wood and potential for pinching injuries, indicating actual injuries have occurred (severity 3). The design flaws and exposed mechanisms suggest injuries are likely to recur (likelihood 4).

incident_description: A resident in the city of Lowell Mass. Called 911 to report a fire in a lamp. When companies arrived they found a Himalayen Glow Large Natural lnoic Salt Lamp, which was purchased at Bed Bath and Beyond. The Deputy found that there had been a malfunction in the switch in the power supply cord. This switch was melted. The elderly woman had the fire department take the lamp from the house.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning lamp causing a fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Product is a rocking chair: https://www.allmodern.com/Viv-Rae-Elsa-Rocking-Chair-VVRO3484.html?refid=TEM_AM_953&mmid=715466995&csnid=820292CD-47C0-40C7-9C2C-39A3AC42776A&libra_c=&libra_d=&libra_g=

incident_description:
I purchased a West Elm Simple Bed Frame with White Lacquer Finish. I unpacked it and brought it into the bedroom to assemble it tonight.

It has a very strong smell. Both my wife and I got light headed, headachy, had difficulty breathing and our eyes started itching after the bed was removed from its packaging.

We decided to move the bed frame out of the bedroom. Now that the bed is out of the bedroom, we experience no further effects.

I love the look of the bed but am concerned about the health effects. It can't be in the house with us.
justification: The incident caused temporary health effects (lightheadedness, headache, difficulty breathing, itching eyes) but no lasting injury, and symptoms resolved after removing the bed frame.

incident_description: A glass shelf on my TV stand spontaneously exploded.
justification: The glass shelf exploded but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
(12/13/2016) The consumer stated that she sat on the bed after she had made the bed. She consumer sat in the middle of the bed at the foot and slipped off the mattress and fell. The consumer stated that the mattress is sagging right in middle and that caused her fall.

The consumer hurt her right arm when she fell. Her entire body is sore. No medical attention was required.  

(12/28/2016) The consumer contacted the Serta Warranty Department and was advised to contact the place of purchase.

The consumer contacted the place of purchased and was advised that she would have to wait 30 days.

The consumer sent more information  regarding the inspection that was done on the mattress on 1/25/17.  A company called "Precise Mattress" called her on 1/16/17.  They set up an appt for 1/25/17 to come out.  The person who inspected the mattress said "its not so much that it was sagging at the foot of the bed.  But, that the whole mattress was defective.  He said, the report would be sent to the store "Howards Appliance" and, that it would be left up to them on how to handle the problem.
justification: The consumer suffered a right arm injury and body soreness from the fall, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description: My son, who is 12 months old, had his head entrapped on the Cracker Barel Rocker between the seat and the seatback, where there is a pretty large gap.  He climbed up on the rocker while I was in the bathroom and then turned on the seat so that his legs went out the back and tried to get down between the seat back and the seat.  His body went through but his head didn't.  Luckily, his older brother saw what happened and got help.
justification: The child's head was entrapped but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident was resolved with help from an older sibling.

incident_description: the glass envelope fell off of a Feit electric LED light bulb, exposing the electronics inside.
justification: The glass envelope falling off exposes electronics, posing a risk of electric shock or injury if handled.

incident_description:
As defined in the attached letter.  Metal inserts broke loose causing chair seat to collapse.
[Letter:]

Dear Sir/Madam,

FACTS: On September 14, 2016 item # 16114959-00-001 consisting of two (2) Tateswood
Cherry Tangle-back Swivel stool- Bar Height chairs were ordered {order# 177242648) from
Overstock.com. They were shipped to [REDACTED] in a timely manner and easily assembled and used.
FAILURE: On Jan 24th of this year, upon swiveling around to exit the chair from the kitchen
counter, the chair seat collapsed backwards. My partner, [REDACTED], age 74, was able to
grab the counter, in time, for support or he would have fallen backwards onto the floor. The
chair was disassembled to learn the reason for the chair failure and pictures were taken.
Copies of those pictures are enclosed.
CAUSE: I also enclosed a copy of the assembly instructions to better define the component failure. The
item labeled "Q" Small Support Ring has metal inserts in four locations for connecting the leg supports
(N) via (4) Allen bolts (part A). The actual failure was the metal inserts pulled out of the support ring
causing the chair seat and back to collapse backwards. (Pictures are enclosed)
ACTIONS: On Jan 27, [REDACTED] called your customer service phone number [REDACTED] to
notify your company of this safety failure and determine what action can be taken to remedy the
problem. He was advised that because it was ordered via Overstock.com, that it was their problem and
he had to call them to seek a resolution. This response seems totally irresponsible when she was
advised that there was a product failure that almost caused personal physical damage.
A call was then placed to Overstock.com and thev said thev would have someone review the problem
(they were provided the same pictures) and respond in 2-3 days. Their email response of Feb. 3, 2017
(see enclosed) was very unacceptable. What do I do with a $75.00 refund to get a matching chair to the
one I am still using when they are out-of-stock?
My Actions: I have copied the Consumer Product Safety Commission on this matter as I believe there is
a probable manufacturing defect in the assembly of the metal insert into the wooden ring which will
lead to other customers suffering similar failures of these chairs. The bore hole was too large, the insert
was not perpendicular to the ring when inserted, or the insert was undersized are just a few of the
possible causes for this safety issue.
At the same time, I kindly request that I be shipped a "Q" support ring which has been through a proper
quality control check at no charge.
Thank you for your consideration on this matter.

[REDACTED]
justification: The chair collapsed but the user avoided injury by grabbing the counter, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Pier One 9 drawer mirrored Hayworth dresser and had the white glove team come out and put the dresser together.  As I was putting my clothing into the drawer the mirrored glass to the drawer spider cracked from the knob outward.  The knob may have been put on too tight.  I love this dresser but it is too unsafe the way it is.

incident_description:
On the evening of February 7, 2017, my wife and I were sitting in our family room.  My wife was on a couch and near her was a torchiere floor lamp rated for a 150 watt bulb in which a GE Reveal HD+ 100 watt, 72 watt usage bulb had been on for a number of hours.  The bulb was surrounded on the sides with a solid composite shade. To the best of our knowledge, the bulb was undamaged and was performing well.  Suddenly without warning, the bulb exploded.  Shards of glass were propelled several feet across the room.  More significantly, a number of projectiles of molten glass were propelled out and fell within 3 feet or so of the lamp where my wife was sitting. Note these were molten, not particles, projectiles of extremely hot glass. They appear to have come out in a liquid, molten form and no longer had a shape they would have had within the bulb.   The molten glass burned several holes in the couch and the carpet, and then it cooled.  One of the holes in the couch was slightly larger than a pencil eraser.  As you can imagine, these holes don't wash out and the couch and carpet are permanently defaced.  Fortunately, the molten glass did not fall on readily flammable material, and a fire was not started in my home.  Even more fortunately, none of the molten glass projectiles landed on my wife.  She could have been seriously and permanently injured.

I am accustomed to reading warning labels and pay more attention to them than most people.  Expecting to see the usual warnings on the label, such as risk of fire and burns if used improperly, I looked at the label on the package and in among some usual warnings I noted that this bulb could unexpectedly break ejecting hot particles of glass.   This was not hot particles of glass that were ejected but was molten glass, i.e., in liquid form.  Besides we followed the warning and the consequences could have still been disastrous with personal injuries rather than just significant damage to property. items.

I do not believe adequate warnings can be put on this product to make it safe for homeowner use.  This product should be withdrawn from the market.
justification: The incident involved property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is possible given the unexpected nature of the bulb explosion.

incident_description:
We purchased a bonded leather sectional from Knoxville Wholesale Furniture, in Knoxville, Tennessee back in March 2013. We were told that the material of the sofa (which was explained to us as performance leather) would hold up better than leather and wouldn't crack or fade. In 2015 the material began peeling off of the sofa. It has gotten worse. Every day pieces of the material can be found on the floor. The foam under the material is now exposed. This has multiple safety concerns to me. 1. I have two small children, ages 7 months and 2.5 years old. If a piece of the material is on the floor and my child puts it in their mouth, they could choke on it. 2. With the foam showing, does the sofa still meet the flammability standards? I'm not sure. 3. What kind of binding material was used to put the sofa together? Since the material is peeling away, is there a concern about toxic material being exposed? I don't know these answers, but I do believe it's concerning.

When I spoke to Southern Motion, the manufacturer of the sofa, they advised that the peeling of the bonded leather is an industry known issue. I believe that this material is defective and needs to be recalled due to the safety concerns mentioned above and also the lack of durability.
,
justification: The peeling material poses a choking hazard to children and potential exposure to toxic materials, indicating a risk of injury.

incident_description: I purchased a Southern Motion Fandango power recliner from Knoxville Wholesale Furniture on approximately August 10, 2016. I previously reported this to a man withCPSC, but cannot find the report. The recliner off gasses formaldehyde and makes my eyes blurry, my head hurt, and/or stuffs me up if I sit in it an hour or more. I did not call the site where I purchased it because my son did not tie it down sufficiently when we brought it home and it flew out of the bed of the truck; but it was not damaged other than one skinned place in the leather. Nevertheless, the recliner did not have any warnings of formaldehyde off gassing from the unpainted man made boards that comprise parts of the chair's frame. I am submitting this report because I strongly feel that Southern Motion should either refund my money or provide me with another recliner, made without the man made fiber board. Additionally, this product emits too much formaldehyde and is a safety issue for,the public, especially for small children. After being I. Our house for over six months, even though I can no longer smell the odor although my husband can, I still get severe headaches and blurry eyes.
justification: The recliner causes health issues like headaches and blurry vision, indicating injury, but no death or severe harm is reported.

incident_description:
Hampton Bay patio furniture from Home Depot.  Two rocking chairs, love seat/glider and 4 tile table.

Both chairs failed catastrophically, without warning.  Was not leaning back hard.  I only weigh about 180 lbs.  The four round, tubular legs that join together under the chair broke completely in half, all at one time.  And both times, I hit the concrete patio hard, getting very stunned both times, taking several minutes to recover.  Again, completely without warning.  I have pictures if I can find a place to upload them.  Both chairs failed within a month of each other.
justification: The incident resulted in the user being stunned and taking several minutes to recover after falling hard on concrete, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The outdoor seating set is used on our patio. We ordered in May 2016. Within 2 months I noticed that one of the swivel chairs was leaning forward & unsafe to sit in.
justification: The chair was unsafe to sit in but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I noticed that a spot in my electric blanket felt very hot, and on closer inspection there was a brown mark on both sides of the fabric. When I touched the fabric, it felt like there was a lump inside. I cut the fabric open to find that the wiring was melted together and blackened and had scorched the fabric.

incident_description:
I purchased a ComforPedic Loft Memory Foam + Cool Gel Classic Bed Pillow made by BeautyRest in November 2016. The reason I bought a new pillow was because I was having some aches and stiffness in my joints as well as trouble sleeping. The other reason is that my cat, [REDACTED], was sharing a pillow with me and there wasn't enough room for the two of us. 

So, I bought this new pillow. According to the statements on the packaging, "great for back, side and stomach sleepers", "premium memory foam cradles your head and neck providing the perfect balance of comfort and support" and "top layer of revitalizing gel keeps you cooler throughout the night so you sleep better and wake up feeling energized".

I put a case on the new pillow and put my old pillow next to it for [REDACTED]. She was happy as a clam. I, on the other hand, had a very different experience to my new pillow.

Within a few weeks of using this pillow my morning aches and pains became progressively worse to the point where I was having trouble even putting on a pair of socks in the morning. I could hardly move. My sleep pattern was terrible, the worse it had ever been. 

Then, I developed an entirely new type of pain. My shoulder and neck areas, both front and back, were painful to the touch. It was like I had a bad sunburn and those were the areas that touch the pillow. 

One night several weeks ago as I was trying to sleep the pain was so intense, not only the 'sunburn' pain but also my neck, back, arms and shoulders. I felt like I had been dropped out of a 5 story window onto pavement. 

I kicked [REDACTED] off my old pillow and swapped it for the [REDACTED] gel pillow. Within a few hours I could literally feel the pain slipping away and was able to sleep. After about 2 days the 'sunburn' pain also dissipated and has not returned. 

An interesting part to my story is that [REDACTED] absolutely refused to sleep on that gel pillow when I swapped it and ended up sleeping with me on my old pillow. until I took another pillow off the spare bed for her to use. She uses that one just fine but the gel pillow she would have no part of. So, even the cat knows something is very wrong / toxic with that BeautyRest pillow!

incident_description: A loft bed by the name LuLu made by Ashley furniture was purchased from Slumberland furniture in Waite Park MN on 8/31/13. It was also delivered and assembled by Slumberland employees. The incident occurred February 26,2014 which led to the death of a four year old girl. The girl was playing in her room. She asked to watch a movie so her mother started the movie and left her in her room. The mother thought things were quiet but thought her daughter may have fallen asleep. A short while later the mother went to check on her to find her stuck in between the wall and her loft bed. The girls mother attempted CPR while on the phone with 911. The ambulance arrived and transported her to the Litchfield Hospital in MN. The girl died. Meeker County did an investigation to ensure no foul play and found it to be a terrible accident. After this incident occurred I examined the bed to see if there was any product flaws that could be noted. I did find that there is a shelving unit on one end that supported the bed frame that stuck out a little bit. After speaking with her mother she said that one time she had gone behind the bed and had her feet on top of the shelving unit for support. Her mother had to help her get out and told her daughter to never do that again because she might not be there to help her get unstuck. I don't know what happened the evening when she got stuck which led to her death but I believe she may have tried doing what she had done before but was to far over that her feet did not catch the shelving unit this time and she ended up being hung by the loft bed. It appears that this is a design flaw as there should not be any space that a child could somehow feel safe to stick there legs between a wall and a loft bed. I would also recommend that in the warnings that come with loft beds that they warn parents to make sure bed is flush against the wall or far enough away from the wall that a child may not become entrapped between the wall and the bed. There should also be a warning that placement should not be by a window. Many parents may not think about these things until something tragic like this happens.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a four-year-old girl due to a design flaw in the loft bed, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description:
Patio Swivel Chair Anselmo was being used during a luncheon. I fell as chair base broke. I received some scrapes, bruises and hit my head on the concrete patio.   I was not able to work on the following Monday because I hurt all over and had bruises. RI statue of limitations for personal injury is 3 years.   I am reporting this on  February 3 2017. 

We disposed  the chair. Now we have only 1. Now that we find out it was defective We Are asking for a chair replacement.
justification: The incident resulted in scrapes, bruises, and a head injury, with the victim unable to work the following day, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with defective furniture.

incident_description: JA Henckels Poultry Shears serrated blade broke off at the pin and flew toward me cutting my hand and foot.  I was using them to cut some soft flower stems. I have photos.  I am very concerned about this - the injury could have been more serious
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the hand and foot, and the description notes the potential for more serious harm, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as the incident happened but is not described as a frequent event.

incident_description: The Serta Motion Perfect Adjustable Foundation comes with a remote control that allows you to select options to raise or lower the head or foot of the mattress.  There is also a button marked FLAT that will automatically return the foundation base to a level position.  When this button is pressed, intentionally or accidentally, the frame continues to lower even if there is an obstruction between the base and the frame.  This could cause serious injury or death if a person or pet gets in the way of the frame while it is lowering.  I became concerned about this when I saw my husband resting in the bed with the head of the bed in the raised position.  Our dog had come into the room and was lying on the floor next to the bed with the top part of his ear laying between the bed frame and base on the opposite side of the bed from my husband.  There is no Pause or Stop button in case of an emergency.
justification: The incident describes a potential for serious injury or death due to the bed frame's inability to stop when obstructed, as evidenced by the dog's ear being at risk.

incident_description:
We bought a Hallmark Peanuts Christmas Time item that moves with a string pull and plays music with button batteries. The product number on the bottom appears to be QX12917.

When we took it out to display it this year, one of the two batteries was corroded. When I tried to remove it, the battery exploded in my hand.

My wife was closely watching.

This could have caused serious injury and blindness.
justification: The battery exploded but no injury was reported, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description: Used an Ikea desk lamp B1201 "Magnarp", with an Ikea LED bulb LED1221. Had lamp and bulb since Oct. 2014 without incident. Tonight (29 Jan 2016) I turned it on. There was a flash and the circuit breaker for the outlet blew. Before using the lamp again, I examined it. The bulb base had partly melted (both plastic and metal parts) and the lamp has a small scorch mark on the contacts.
justification: The incident involved a flash and a blown circuit breaker with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such electrical faults are not common but do occur.

incident_description: We purchased the Sauder Storybook 4 drawer dresser for my 3 year old daughter's room in February 2016. We installed it correctly and used the manufacturer anchor on the dresser to anchor it the wall. This morning, the anchor failed and my daughter  pulled the dresser down. Somehow she managed to get out of the way and was unharmed. Still, the anchor should not have failed.
justification: The dresser fell due to a failed anchor, but the child was unharmed, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I received a Fragrant Jewels Candle as a gift. The candle had been lit this morning for about an hour when my husband blew it out. A few moments later he went to put the lid on the candle and the top part of the candle exploded into pieces. The lid did not explode, it was the glass part that holds the candle that exploded. The lid he tried to put on the candle came with candle when it was new.
justification: The candle exploded but there was no injury reported, only property damage.

incident_description: This morning, I went to turn on my daughter's light in her closet. It didn't turn on and there was a bad smell. The CFL bulb looked like it had melted off of its base and had fallen to the floor. The base was still plugged in and it has black streaks stained going upwards on it. I will be attaching photos.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning CFL bulb with visible damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
While using a Sunbeam electric heating pad on my lower back, I felt a sharp pain. I pulled the pad out (from between the chair and my back) and saw a bright glowing light and smoke. I unplugged the pad and put it in my shower IN CASE it burst into flames. It did not continue burning and I did not put water on it.

I have pictures but was unable to attach them.
justification: The incident involved a sharp pain and visible smoke, indicating potential injury and a fire hazard, though no flames or further harm occurred.

incident_description:
A new office chair snapped apart at the arms (which hold the back to the seat base).  The arms were plastic, and inspection of the broken arm revealed the plastic had air bubbles formed within it, leaving the part hollow in places, instead of a solid as a  structural/weight bearing part should be.  

It's being sold on Amazon by the seller OneBigOutlet out of California.  It's also being sold on eBay and this seller/manufacturer's website.

Numerous others have had the same experience, with the same part breaking within a very short time.  

The seller is aware that customer's are having this defective chair break beneath them, and continues to sell or.  I have the broken item still, as well as images of the faulty part.
justification: The chair breaking could lead to injury, and the defect is known to occur frequently based on customer reports.

incident_description: The Dimmer switch on the lamp melted. this is the same type of lamp from Recall number 17 065, but the labeling and seller of the lamp are different, I believe the source manufacture is identical. It was purchased on Amazon.
justification: The dimmer switch melting is an incident with no reported injury, but the similarity to a recalled product suggests a likely recurrence.

incident_description: Home Depot fan Nassau 52 in. Natural Iron Model 58020 had a short in the  light receptacle. The light bulb was receiving way too much power and you could see the light as a little too bright. The bulb burned my hands even through gloves. After I waited a rather long time to check the bulb. All bulbs that go in this fan come apart. It causes the bulb to become so hot it disconnects from the base. The fan was upgraded to an LED CFL bulb however the model I have is dangerous. It is a different bulb That uses more power. The fan causes the bulb to get too hot and is dangerous to use.
justification: The incident describes a burn injury from a hot bulb, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue with the fan causing bulbs to overheat is described as a recurring problem, suggesting a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Sunbeam LED lightbulb Model 30411617 fell from a ceiling fixture and caught fire.
justification: The lightbulb fell and caught fire, indicating an incident with potential for harm but no injury reported.

incident_description: The helical 20W light bulb overheated and started smoking.  It first started flickering and then 20 minutes it started smoking.  The light bulb is burnt and the fixture it was in  is melted and has burn marks.  Luckily we were home and started smelling smoke, we easily could have had a fire.
justification: The incident involved an overheated light bulb causing smoke and damage to the fixture, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Staying at Doubletree hotel. Alarm clock in the room made a POP noise and then started smoking, with noise getting louder and appeared to be rapidly progressing into a fire (if the clock is replugged in, I have no doubt that it would be on fire in under a minute). Fortunately, my wife and I were awake, and I was able to unplug within 3-4 seconds. Room smelled like burnt plastic. Appears to be the adapter that failed as there are melted plastic spots on the adapter. Building engineer tested/confirmed soon afterwards that the power outlets were fine.

Device is labeled as iHome model HT160, Service Number HT160-A-A.
Manufactured and Serviced by HTI Industries LLC, 12/2015
www.hoteltech.com

Adapter states that it conforms to UL Std 60065, and certified to CSA standard C22.2 No. 60065.

Clock turned in to hotel staff. I retained photos and voice recording of conversation with hotel staff.

We just stayed in a Hilton hotel that also uses the same alarm clock - probably used by all Hilton hotels. I'm a fairly regular guest at Hilton family hotels... these are relatively new alarm clocks.
justification: The incident involved a smoking alarm clock that could have led to a fire, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible given the device's apparent failure and similar models in use.

incident_description: I purchased a Glass desk, the Innovex Fusion Series Delta Collection - Orbit From Fry's electronics a couple months ago. I went to sleep with my door locked and my puppy asleep in my room with the door closed, when i woke Up the bottom shelf of the desk was shattered. my desk literally exploded. there was glass from my desk all the way across to the window. when i contacted Fry's they refused to do anything about it..... so i contacted innovex and they wanted to send me the bottom shelf that exploded and said if you want a refund contact frys. i am horrified by how unsafe this was and how i have been treated by frys electronics management.... This product needs to be discontinued..
justification: The desk shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Just called the company today deciding to put our bunkbeds back together and needed some replacement parts and screws.  Our side rail was cracked.  Customer service notified me that there was a recall on this bunkbed for this reason.   I don't specifically remember how it cracked. It was possible that it was due to rearranging the furniture in the room at the time. No injuries occurred to this incident.
justification: The incident involved a cracked side rail with no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the recall and the mention of furniture rearrangement.

incident_description:
On December 23, 2016 my wife arose from bed complaining of a burning sensation on her lower right shoulder and back.

In examination she had a small 3 x 6 burn area and blister.

On further examination we discovered that the electric  mattress pad had a burn area in the same area where my wife had been sleeping. The sheet, bedding and the top of the actual mattress were also burned and charred.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury (severity 3) from an electric mattress pad malfunction, which is unlikely (likelihood 2) given proper maintenance and usage.

incident_description: GE 53W halogen bulb (model 78797) in an overhead fixture exploded after being turned off and sent glass shards over the bed below it. Luckily, nobody was in the bed and injured.
justification: The bulb explosion caused an incident with potential for injury, but no one was harmed.

incident_description: In June 2016, I purchased a Giatex office desk chair.  The chair's frame just cracked and I fell to the floor injuring my elbow.  The frame looks like it is made of metal but in fact it is made of plastic that is painted to look like metal.  The plastic frame cracked by one of the bolts and made the back of the chair lose causing me to fall.  Had I not grabbed onto my desk, my injuries would have been a lot worse perhaps life threatening if I had hit my head or even fallen backwards through my glass window.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the elbow, and the description suggests potential for more severe injuries if circumstances were different.

incident_description: Today I noticed a CFL light bulb by EcoSmart flickering. I reached in to assure the bulb was tight and while applying pressure I was immediately burned. There was no warning. No heat sensation. Nothing except an immediate sting that register as a burning feeling. When I pulled my finger away the was a burn that immediately showed a blister. This bulb arced and left a blister the size of a large [REDACTED].
justification: The incident resulted in a burn with immediate blistering, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting incident with non slip swivel stool.  He stated that the legs are supposed to snap into the swivel platform.  however, after he followed the instructions and assembled the legs, he noticed that one of the legs was dislodged he snapped it into place again but it did not stay in place.  The box label stated that it is equipped for 400lbs, but the instructions say 300 pounds.  

Caller stated that he was fortunate not to have sat on it before the incident occurred.  The manufacturer was not contacted because they are in China.

Caller feels that this product is a safety hazard.
justification: The incident involved a product defect but no injury occurred as the caller did not use the stool before noticing the issue.

incident_description: The plug on the item is not polarized, and is very slender. It fits so loosely into the outlet that with the slightest touch it shifted and created sparks. I unplugged it immediately as an obvious fire hazard. The item is not UL listed and clearly would not qualify to be.
justification: The incident involved sparks from a loose plug, indicating a fire hazard but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Habersham Candle Co. "White Sand & Sea Salt" luminary candle tried to burn down my home. We no longer have the box, but Amazon.com lists it as model #FGBOT-0238. Between the inner wax (with the wick), and the outer wax (with decorations), is hard plastic shaped similar to a soup can. I assume there is some manufacturing advantage to forming the candle inside the hard plastic "soup can", and then adding decorations in wax around it. The problem is that the hard plastic "soup can" is flammable. The candle starts out being just short of 4" tall. Everything was fine until it had burned down to about a 1" thickness of wax below the wick. The candle was used exclusively indoors, in a bathroom; without open windows or other sources of a draft. We never added any oil, or wood, or anything to increase the burn rate. The wick was kept trimmed. Still, the flame from the wick managed to ignite the hard plastic "soup can", which converted the candle into a torch. 

Before my wife could react, the more intense flame did damage to a wall, the underside of a shelf about 3 feet above the candle, to items near where the candle was sitting (flat surface), and it filled our house with smoke. To the best of my knowledge, there was no prior damage to our candle, or anything unusual about it. We also have a sister candle, in the green "sage" version. It appears just the same, except for a green wax color and flower shaped decorations. 

My wife has burned an awful lot of candles, and this is the first one to ever start a fire. Hopefully, the manufacturer can replace that hard plastic "soup can" with glass, or a plastic which can't burn, or some other alternative. Until an updated version is released, I'd worry about anyone using one of these candles anywhere near anything which could be damaged by flame or smoke. Amazon.com lists many different versions, with different wax colors, and different decorations, but likely the same danger.
justification: The candle caused property damage and filled the house with smoke, but there was no injury or death reported.

incident_description: I purchased a sofa from LazBoy Furniture Gallery in San Diego Ca. 92108 with Ulta  Shield Fabric Protection applied at the warehouse. It was delivered on 12/15/16. On 12/17/2016 I called and talked with [REDACTED]  at the San Diego store and notified her of the strong chemical smell causing skin irritation, sinus reactions; tighten of the chest, headaches, and dizziness. I was told to give it some time as it would dissipate. I was leaving out of town the next day and returning on the 26th. Upon my return my house reeked with the chemical smell and I had to keep the doors and whole house fan on in order to attempt to clear the air. l immediately called the store 12/27 and talked with [REDACTED] again .She would call back and inform me what could be done. On 12/28/16 I called Ultra Shield and wanted to know what the chemicals in the product where and where the warehouse was. I was told by [REDACTED] that information would be delivered to the store. On 12/28/16 [REDACTED] the designer came to my house to check the concern and knowledge the chemical smell and after sitting on the couch for 5 mins. Felt a headache coming on and said she would report this and let me know what could be done. Later that day [REDACTED] called back to tell me that [REDACTED]  would check to see what could be done. i told her that I wanted the couch picked up !On 12/28/2016 I called Laz Boy Comfort Care and reported the continued health problems for me and others in my home and was told a representative would get back to me in 2 days-12/30/16. The next day 12/29/16 I called Comfort Care again and talked with [REDACTED] and once again reported my concerns and urgency about removing this toxic couch from my house. He assured me a rep. would call me the first thing in the morning of 12/30/2016. No call! AII symptoms persist
justification: The incident caused skin irritation, sinus reactions, and headaches, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description:
I purchased a TireRack-branded tire rack from TireRack.com: http://www.tirerack.com/accessories/detail.jsp?ID=164

Upon installing the rack, I noted that the installation instructions are incorrect with regard to the pilot hole that should be drilled for the supplied 1/4" lag screws: http://www.tirerack.com/images/accessories/search/tirestoragerack_instructions.pdf

The instructions indicate using a 3/16" drill bit for the pilot hole; however this will drill-out 1/3 of the good wood that the threads of the lag screws would bite in to and hold in to the wall.  The American Wood Council draws standards for this sort of thing and they indicate a MUCH smaller pilot hole of 7/64" for a soft wood (as would commonly be found in home construction) wall.  http://l-36.com/woodscrewpilot.php

I believe that the included instructions with this product create a critical hazard where this rack may pull out of the wall it's installed to.  This hazard is especially serious in that the rack is designed to store 400 lbs. overhead.
justification: Incorrect instructions could lead to the rack pulling out of the wall, potentially causing injury due to the 400 lbs. load capacity.

incident_description:
I am writing you to tell you about an issue we have had with the TechCraft 72" tv stand we purchased for a new tv we bought in November 2014. On Saturday December 31,2016 the top glass shelf of the stand "exploded" and sent pieces of glass thru our living room and caused our 65"[REDACTED] tv ( which we paid $1000 for) to topple over and now is ruined and does not work. The force of the break also caused damage to our living room wall. Luckily there were no injuries.

I am so glad none of our grandchildren were over when this happened. Someone could have been seriously injured. I have tried to contact the company and their phone number is not working. I have also emailed the company but they refuse to do anything about this issue. (see email below)

Date: January 4, 2017 at 10:55:51 AM EST

Subject: Re: Glass top TV stand

Good morning,

I am very sorry to hear about what happened to your TV stand.

Unfortunately all our stands have a 1-year warranty on them.
Seeing that the stand was purchased in 2014, it no longer qualifies for the 1-year warranty.

Please find attached a copy of our warranty.

I apologize but there is nothing we can do for you.

Regards,

[REDACTED]
Customer Service Supervisor
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, as explicitly stated in the description.

incident_description:
Went to change light bulb in fixture and discovered that coating on white wires was cracked in multiple places. The light fixture is only about 3 years  and we had installed two others in our home. All three fixtures in our home had the  exact same issue. These three fixtures were purchased at different times at two different Wal-Mart locations and none were over three years old. Our concern is that damage to the wire coating could pose a fire hazard in our home or the homes of other families who may have installed them. Wal-Mart still sells these lights:
https://www.walmart.com/ip/Hampton-7320-113-1-Hampton-Bay-15-Diameter-Flush-Mount-Ceiling-Light-Alabaster-Oil-Rubbed-Bronze/21584374
We have replaced the fixtures in our home to be safe but kept them so the issue can be inspected.
justification: Cracked wire coating poses a potential fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: my desk chair seat broke off from it's base and collapsed to the right sending me onto the floor. I am a senior citizen.  I think that it broke off due to metal fatigue.  I have had it at least 5 years.
justification: The incident resulted in the user falling onto the floor, indicating injury, but the likelihood is unlikely given the specific conditions (metal fatigue after 5 years).

incident_description:
(12/14/2016) The consumer stated that she replaced the bulb in ceiling fan around Labor Day. The consumer was sitting in the room and heard an explosion. She smelled burning and was suddenly showered with glass. Shards of glass fused to the fabric in the chair where she was sitting.

The consumer was not injured.

(12/14/2016) The consumer contacted the firm. They are sending her a mailer to send back the unused bulb.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and glass shards, but no injury was reported, placing severity at 2. The likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty bulbs.

incident_description: Purchased FEIT electric LED Dimmable 40 Watt replacement globe 4 pack light bulbs - Item/Article: 1050962 from Costco yesterday, 29 December 2016.  That evening used the 4 bulbs in a bathroom fixture, bulbs pointed downward to give light to the sink area.  Early this morning found shattered glass on the bathroom floor, the sink and around the sink.  Found that the glass globe of one of the 4 LED lights had fallen away from the bulb and had caused the shattered glass.  The LED filament light portion of the bulb was still in the fixture and providing light. Did get a cut on one of my feet from the glass on the floor.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the foot from shattered glass, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such failures are not common but possible with manufacturing defects.

incident_description:
Yesterday afternoon, I had an LED bulb catch fire in my basement. My son said it made a hissing sound and a pop, followed by smoke. The fire appears to have started in the inside of the bulb. The inside of the bulb is burned, the top of the bulb separated from the base and fell to the ground, and the receptacle shows blackening from the fire. 

After searching online, I believe it to be one of the recalled Lighting Science Group LED bulbs from 2010. The bulbs have the marking L4210 (in addition to numerous other markings). I originally purchased at least 15 of these bulbs in early 2011 at Home Depot in Columbia, Missouri.
justification: The incident involved a bulb catching fire and emitting smoke, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Quick warning of a safety hazard to children. The Uncle Milton Star Wars Science Force Lightning Energy Ball appears to have a defect which could potentially seriously harm a child or even cause a fire. We bought one for Christmas at Toys R Us. Within two seconds of turning it on, it caught on fire and started smoking really bad. I was going to simply exchange it, thinking it was a freak thing, but after Googling it, there are reviews on the Toys R Us site, as well as other stores online, that describe the exact same thing happening to others. 

It appears this is a real (potentially dangerous) defect and not a one-off. Hopefully, someone can trigger a recall, in case this causes a really fire somewhere.   I did try calling Uncle Milton several times to give them a heads up, but no one would answer on any extension I tried...:-(.
justification: The product defect can cause fire and serious harm to children, with multiple reports confirming the issue, indicating a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: An incandescent light bulb exploded, raining hot glass and metal. It burned holes in furniture and the floor, but fortunately did not burn the person reading under this light. It was a Philips EcoVantage 72-watt, 120-volt bulb of 1490 lumens, also marked "Mexico."  There were two such bulbs in the lamp, and I have removed the surviving one.  This product should be recalled.  One instance is one too many of this sort of thing, I believe.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as it's a known but not common issue with incandescent bulbs.

incident_description: Welded metal plate on Staples office chair cracked. Chair tipped over
justification: The chair tipped over due to a cracked metal plate, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: Purchased EZ Up 9' Adjustable Christmas Tree Stand from Walmart. installed stand on 7' 5" live Christmas tree. no issue until after tree had been up for 2 weeks. In middle of night my son herd a crack and then the tree came down. My wife and son propped tree until I could get home to fix it. Upon inspection of the tree stand I found the plastic 'Spike" that help keeps the tree centered had completely broken off and allowed the tree weight to shift and caused the tree in the stand to fall over. Luckily the damage was confined to broken ornaments and wet carpet. I have concerns some could have been seriously hurt or could have started a possible fire (son quickly turned off power strip feeding the Christmas lights). I feel poor grade of plastic was used in the molding process which led to stress fracture and equipment failure.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage (broken ornaments and wet carpet) but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as the failure was due to a specific material defect.

incident_description:
Child received a Christmas gift; Ultimate Candle Making Kit.  after creating her first votive candle we lit the wick and in 20-30 minute the glass cracked apart.  this was a large and thick chunk of glass that broke completely off and leaked hot wax  from the candle.  

Injury easily could have been burn from the wax or cuts from the glass or a fire.
justification: The incident involved a cracked glass votive candle that could have caused burns or cuts, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
My daughter & I were working in our kitchen (our dogs were in the room too) on New Year's Day when a light bulb in an overhead fixture exploded for no apparent reason.  The bulb in question was a recent replacement.. Sylvania 60 W replacement 43W A19 halogen bulbs,  extra soft white, Barcode 0  46135 17039  3. 

This bulb was new.  Put in fixture quite recently.  The light had been turned on for an hour or so.  

Through sheer good luck we humans were not facing the direction of the bulb when it burst, throwing shards of glass & whatever else is in halogen bulbs ago over the kitchen.  There were pieces & minute bits of glass on the dogs. 

We were stunned.  We could have been seriously injured. 

I was further stunned to discover that the company, Sylvania,   is well aware that this can happen. In fine print on the end of the box there are warnings in 3 languages about these hazardous bulbs.  This is NOT a prominent warning.  It's on the part of the box the package stands on. There are other warnings on the side where the bar code is.  A reasonable average person like myself could easily assume ( as I did) that the risks were addressed in this caution area . Based on packaging these appear to be simple,  safe,  routine replacements for standard bulbs . The same is true of the marketing in the store. Today's experience shows this simply is not the case..

Research on the Internet & contact with the home improvement store I purchased it from revealed that there is spotty awareness of the risks and special precautions to take installing this type of bulb. 

Bottom line: these are unpredictability dangerous products and consumers are inadequately warned about them. I am furious that a corporation can knowingly get away with pushing this dangerous porridge onto an unsuspecting public .
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb with no injuries, but potential for serious harm, hence severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the description of the product's known risks and inadequate warnings.

incident_description: I purchased a digital electric blanket from JCPenny about a year or 2 ago. The electric blanket hasn't worked properly since the day I got it. Sometimes when I would turn it on, it would immediately display the error code and sometimes it would work for a while and then error out. Since I just used it to preheat my bed in the wintertime, it wasn't a big priority for me to pursue the warranty to have it repaired or replaced. As time has gone on, once the error code came on, I would turn off the blanket but sometimes the wires would continue to heat up making the bed too hot. I then took to unplugging the blanket if this happened. The other night I had turned on the blanket, it errored out so I turned it off. I was busy doing other things when I smelled something awful. I immediately unplugged the blanket and removed it from my bed. It smelled of burned plastic or wires or something. Yesterday I removed the backing from the digital thermostat to discover the circuit board has a burned spot on it. If I had not been in the room at the time this had happened, I fully believe that it would have started a fire, destroying my bedroom.
justification: The electric blanket malfunctioned and could have caused a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Purchased 2 medicine cabinet for our bathroom, Kohler CLC Surface Mount 20 X 26.
The cabinets had mirrored panels that need to be installed on the side of the cabinet for a surface mount. These panels were placed on the sides of the cabinet and double sided tape was included to mount the glass panels.  Approximately 3 months after the cabinet were installed one of the side mirrors came loose and fell on the vanity and the mirrored piece exploded all over the bathroom.
Luckily  no one was standing there or they could have been seriously injured by the pieces of glass. 
Why would the mounting for these be double sided tape and not glue.  Because of the heat and humidity it probably loosen the tape.
justification: The mirror fell and shattered, but no one was injured. The incident could have caused injury if someone was present.

incident_description: Bath and Body Works/ White Barn Candle Company 14.5oz jar candle in French Lavender scent was burning for approximately 1 hour. Suddenly we noticed the candle had caught fire and was engulfed in flames. Flames reached about 5-6 inches high and flames had to be smothered to be put out. Jar was cracked, burned and blackened. This incident occurred without explanation. Candle was near a mirror which was also blackened and burned by flames. Incident caused smoke detectors to go off as well.
justification: The incident involved a candle fire causing property damage (burned mirror, cracked jar) but no reported injuries, indicating a moderate likelihood given the circumstances.

incident_description:
AMAZON GE LIGHT BULBS-FIRE HAZARD
so the EPA in it's infinite wisdom passed a law about higher wattage light bulbs passed by congress in 2007 probably introduced by some dim witted congressman. this took jobs out of the US and these specific lights bulbs are made in Hungary, China or possibly other countries while a lot of people in Texas lost their jobs. these foreign made bulbs can be bought on AMAZON at reasonable prices. i have been buying my 150 & 200 watt bulbs and others on AMAZON. the 150 i use in a pole lamp rated for two 150's. they have been fairly dependable. the last batch i bought on 11/4 and three out of the four burnt out so far. below are pictures of the last burn out. i was sitting right there and heard a pop and sizzle. looking up i saw a foot long flame shoot out of my lamp. the base of the bulb and the socket melted. the previous burnout made a pop when that one blew also, but no flames. These were made in Hungary, my 200's which i use in the garage are made in china. it seems that the GE quality has gone down drastically in the last year since they were working out pretty well having to change them about every six months which was tolerable considering the squiggly ones that cost a ridiculous amount of money weren't lasting much longer, ten years, RIGHT! so i guess i pay an extra .10 per year. you can see by the pictures that even though the sockets were rated for 150 watts that the heat generated from the bulbs melted it. the other socket had a little metal solder point that fell out when i checked it having separated because of the heat. if that lamp had a flammable lamp shade who knows what would have happened. recently when we were away for almost a week we had that light on a timer. i just bought a twelve pack, needless to say they will be going back.

incident_description: Purchase the Spa Sensations 12" Theratouch Memory foam mattress from WalMart.com on 9-20-2014. incident_description: We purchased a Doc McStuffins Pet Vet Table Set from Walmart.com Model # 97324 back in Nov 2016.  We purchased a similar [REDACTED] Table set for our kids previous to that.  Yesterday, our niece for whom we purchased the Doc McStuffin table set fell down and received a serious cut/gash right over her left eye from the protruding leg support that allows the legs to be folded and expanded, and required a hospital visit. I previously wondered if it was just a pinch hazard with our kids when folding the table, but today I realized it could potentially cause a child more serious injury, like to lose an eye.  Thankfully, the loss of an eye did not occur here [only by God's miraculous grace I believe], but it was close enough to her eye that prompted me to request this possible recall and remedy.  I just finished contacting Walmart's Cust. Service Rep to get in contact with her parents and to hopefully recommend a recall and/or re-design.  Rep [REDACTED] stated she will further the claim up to the appropriate Walmart Department.  Still, many of us are aware that the first thing most companies will do is defer blame to another party like the manufacturer.  Hopefully, Walmart will do the right thing here.  The leg support should possible be more self-contained, or a protective covering should be placed above the protruding bracket which visibly does jut out beyond the table's top cover.  It is a potential hazard that can potentially slice and maim despite the rounded edges and I hope you and other product safety watchers will sound an alarm here for the potential risk to other children, especially little infants just learning to walk and so prone to stumbling over at times. And for the record, my niece in question is no longer an infant who stumbles over easily.   Thank you for your time and please feel free to contact us at your earliest convenience if you need additional information.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious cut requiring hospital visit, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
Dear Consumer Products Safety Representative,

On Saturday, December 10, 2016 my wife and I had a scare with a Niagara 20 watt CFL bulb.  This bulb was installed sideways in an open ceiling light fixture in our laundry/utility room.  The bulb base burned so hot that it melted the tube away from base.  In addition, the bulb burned orange where it was affixed to the base, gave off a noxious odor as well as smoke.  The tube shattered as it fell to a carpeted floor.  It was still so hot that it melted a few spots of the carpet.  

I called Niagara Conservation Corp. (800-831-8383) and left a voicemail with two (2) individuals.  Since it was Saturday, I expected to get a response on Monday.  To date I have not heard from the company.

We got the Niagara CFL bulbs at least three (3) years ago from Duke Energy as part of their energy saving promotion.  I called them on Monday, December 12, 2016.  I spoke to four (4) separate individuals all of whom indicated they were unaware of any CFL problems.  Because our carpet had been burned, I was referred to their Claims Dept.  I received a letter from Sedgwick Claims Management Services, Inc. representing Duke Energy denying our claim for carpet damage.  It was recommended that I contact Niagara to file a claim for damages.

I repeatedly mentioned to those with whom I spoke to at Duke Energy,  I was not interested in getting a settlement for the carpet.  The concern I expressed was the possibility of a fire being started due to the failure of CFL bulbs.

My wife and I were unaware of all the failures and recalls that have occurred with CFL bulbs since at least 2011 or earlier.  Where were Niagara and Duke Energy when this was going on?  I found your address and are sending you the information indicated in the document:  http://ceolas.net/#li18ex,  CFL Safety, US Government Energy Star advice.

Product Manufacturer:  Niagara Conservation Corp. Made in China
Model Information:  LKMS 20W (5 photos attached:  the manufacturer name, the date the bulb was installed, the broken fluorescent tube, the burned base and damaged carpet).
Use:  Indoors with sideways base in open light fixture.  Three  CFLs were installed in the fixture.  The plastic light fixture lens shown has not been used since we began using CFLs several years ago.

I would expect that as these bulbs age, they will become more prone to failure.  Due to the fact that I have no confidence that this situation will not happen again, I have removed all the CFLs from our laundry/utility room as well as the unused ones from our storage cabinet.  They will be taken to our local hazardous materials recycling center for disposal.  

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]


This letter was e mailed to cfi@energystar.gov along with pictures of the damaged bulb and damaged carpet.  I was unable to include the pictures in the section below for my files.
justification: The incident involved a bulb overheating, emitting smoke, and damaging the carpet, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We ordered two LED light bulbs from SolarIlluminations.com - Order 10045408. The website pictured the bulbs with E27/E27 bases, which are industry standard 110V to 220V electric light bulb mogul bases.  We ordered two and they were shipped to us in a shipping box.  Inside the two bulbs were bubble wrapped, in no box, with no marking of the voltage required, with no instructions, warnings or other notice that these bulbs were for and voltage intended.  My son received the box from [REDACTED] and opened it, saw the bulbs were standard 110V bases, and installed them.  The bulbs both popped and one blew a breaker and the other one, on another breaker, did not blow the breaker and started to smoke.  My son unscrewed it and stopped the smoking.

We notified the seller and their response was to chastise us for ordering the wrong bulb, which according to their small print on their web site was for 12V, even though the picture showed the industry standard E26/E27 high voltage base.

Our house could of burned down because of this unsafe, unmarked product that does not conform to USA electric code https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edison_screw and they built and market a dangerous product which can injure, kill or cause serious property damage.
justification: The incident involved property damage (smoking bulbs and a tripped breaker) and potential for injury, but no actual injury or death was reported.
