incident_description:
We have been using the Newborn Halo SleepSack Swaddle for our 11 lb daughter (size Newborn listed as 6-12lbs) since we brought her home from the hospital in August. This item is a zip up "sack" that has fabric that attaches in the back via velcro patches that you swaddle around the baby. The purpose of having the removable fabric is to be able to use the sleepsack from the newborn swaddling stage and then transitioning into just the sleepsack.
This morning I woke up horrified when I opened my eyes and saw my baby in the bassinet beside the bed with the removable piece of fabric around her neck and over her mouth and nose. She had wiggled enough to get her hands out and the velcro in the back apparently came lose and allowed the fabric to cover slip up around her neck and over her face. I immediately yanked the fabric off her face and was so relieved to see that she was safe. Once I knew she was safe, I took a quick picture of the fabric around her neck (but I had removed from her face) before picking her up because I knew immediately that I had to share this information to hopefully prevent what could be a fatal accident for another family. 
We are extremely cautions when it comes to our infant's sleeping specifics. She sleeps in a bassinet next to our bed. There is NEVER anything else in the bassinet and she is always zipped into a sleepsack. She is always swaddled in this sleepsack or the fleece version if it's colder. We always swaddle snuggly as recoomended and make sure she is using the correct item for her age/size. We have done everything right. We took every step possible to make sure she has a safe sleeping environment and this is something that should not EVER happen. It's apparent that we swaddled the sack correctly, because the front velcro never broke open. If it would have been a looser swaddle, then  the velcro would have become detached and not wrapped around her neck and covered her face. This item needs to be pulled from the market and replaced with a sleepsack that does NOT have a removable swaddle piece. I know the company is trying to market the item as "versatile" and appealing to the consumer by saying that it will transition with your baby. But it's not safe.
justification: The baby was unharmed but the incident could have been fatal, indicating a high potential severity.

incident_description: Sudden collapse of a less-than-one-year-old swivel rocker patio lounge chair pitched me over backward.  I barely averted striking my head on the patio's tile floor.
justification: The incident involved a sudden collapse of a chair but no injury occurred, only a near-miss with potential for harm.

incident_description:
My concern is with free standing storage shelving (plastic). 

No injury has occurred, but the concern is similar to the problems with flat screen tvs, bookcases and dressers that have caused many injuries in the past.

I believe that this product should be recalled and any future manufacturing of these particular shelving units be done with the original material specified to return these to the original structurally sound formula.  

The shelving was originally rated at a capacity of 150 lbs per shelf, but since they changed the formula to a softer plastic the rating is apparently wrong. Loads of 25 lbs to 45 lbs per shelf cause the shelf to fail or cause the posts to tilt to the point of collapse.
justification: No injury has occurred, but the shelving units are prone to collapse under loads much lower than their rated capacity, posing a potential hazard.

incident_description:
the light bulb in the ceiling fan exploded and melted the glass light cap, causing the glass to explode and glass shred everywhere.  The extreme heat produced by the light bulb melted my furniture (sofa) surface, and also melted glasses burned into the rug underneath.
My toddler son was sitting 6 inches away from where the light bulb exploded and could have been severely burned and injured.
This is not a safe product especially the light bulb exploding could melt through glass and causing it to break and send glass shreds everywhere.  Also the high heat produced by the type of bulb is dangerous when it can severely burn someone.
justification: The incident caused property damage and posed a significant risk of injury to a toddler, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
Tonight, we had a CFL spiral light bulb in a ceiling fixture that began flickering and soon burned out.  A few minutes later, we noticed a foul chemical smell and smoke collecting on the ceiling.  My husband went to remove the bulb carefully, noticed the glass spiral was cool to the touch but the base was extremely hot.  He also noticed that where the spiral glass met the base it was severely burned and had begun to melt.  We had a second bulb (from the same packaging) within the fixture that had not yet burned out, and decided to check on it.  The second bulb had slight discoloration in the same location.  I have pictures of both bulbs available, and will keep the bulbs if needed for your information.  

We are concerned what may have happened if we hadn't been around to remove the bulb when we did, if it would have caught fire.  The concern also is if the mercury within the bulb released and what health issues may arise from this.  We are currently fanning the smoke out of our window in hopes of dissipating the foul smell.  

The information stamped on the base:

FEIT Conserv-Energy
CE18T/D/6    LISTED 56LJ
18W 120VAC 60Hz 300mA
UL#E170906

17-11-19Z    G
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning bulb with smoke and foul smell, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is possible as such malfunctions can happen but are not frequent.

incident_description: I had the chair placed on my front porch which is covered and i casually used it for less than two months before the chair broke at the arm base and it caused my side to get pinched and cut my arm where the chair broke away from base then i fell back and hit my head on the house.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the arm and a fall causing head impact, indicating an injury (severity 3). Chair failure is possible but not highly frequent (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Purchased a twin over twin metal bunk bed for my son from Sears.com.  The bed arrived and my husband and i put it together. this is a metal bed with plastic "clips" to go over the cross bars and clip them to the bed frame. Two of these clips broke from us slipping them over the bars they are meant to go on. there was no force or misuse.  My son is not very heavy or big and the whole family was in the room as he sat down on the bed and two clips broke, As he sat up to get off the bed, two more clips broke. the bed seems like a good solid bed, with the exception of these plastic clips. Sears want to pick up the bed ( for a return )  and continue to sell it to others  I do not want to just return the bed and get a refund while someone else's child may be injured. The manufacturer is American Furniture Alliance and I have spoken with them and they insist they have not had any other complaints. I sent pictures to the manufacturer and have had no other response so far. I hope someone can check into this before an innocent child is hurt. If a child is on the top bunk and these give out one by one, there is nothing holding the mattress up. the child on the bottom will be injured. It is just a matter of when will this happen? I have asked if they might have metal replacements for the plastic and sadly......no.
justification: The incident involved broken clips on a bunk bed, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I came home to a strong electrical burning smell in my bedroom. After searching, I found that the dimmer control on my Ikea basisk floor lamp was sizzling and popping on the carpet. It seems like some sort of liquid came out from inside the control box.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electrical device with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Noticed the smell of an electrical burn and discovered product smoking and crackling. Immediately unplugged the unit and found the small fixture hot to touch, beginning to melt, charred and burned. If not discovered, would have caused a fire.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and charred electrical fixture, posing a fire risk, but was discovered and addressed before any injury occurred.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that the LED bulb overheated, melted and charred the area on the ceiling.  She stated that she smelled an overwhelming odor and discovered that the incident had occurred with the bulb.  This incident could have caused a house fire.

The manufacturer was contacted.

Caller feels that these bulbs are a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The LED bulb overheated and charred the ceiling, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
After sleeping on the new mattress I had red eyes next morning.

Despite of all my attempts to air the room, the mattress still has some chemical odor, causing red itchy eyes, that are swollen. In addition I have scratchy throat and dizziness every time I am around the mattress. The reaction to the mattress is really fast. Whenever I leave the room and stay away from the mattress, I feel significantly better.

I had three visits to ophthalmologists, and none of the specialists found anything wrong with my eyes. They suggested I had an allergic reaction.
justification: The description reports red itchy eyes, swollen eyes, scratchy throat, and dizziness, indicating an allergic reaction, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Portfolio 5 light Lola golden bronze chandelier 34311 chain weld at ceiling has come undone from fixture mount. Hanging by power cord only.  May fall onto table below.
justification: The chandelier is hanging by its power cord and may fall, posing a risk of property damage but no mention of injury.

incident_description: My All-Pro shower light trim model # ERT701 fell from the shower ceiling fixture and both the trim and the glass insert shattered on the shower floor. The date code of the unit is 2002-2-2. I am reporting this incident because it appears that the hazard extends far beyond the original CPSC date code span (347 11 through 119 12) indicated in the original recall notice of August 29, 2012. I will be contacting Cooper Industries to inquire about a free replacement trim and glass for the shower light hoping that they will honor the recall/replacement despite the fact that the date code on my unit preceded the date code range of the recall. I suspect that since this hazard extends further back in time than initially thought, CPSC might consider revisiting this issue to include a broader date range.
justification: The shower light trim fell and shattered, but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I purchased a package of 4 FEIT LED light bulbs from Costco .  They are 5 Watt(40 W equivalent) clear filament globes.  They are all in one multi-bulb fixture over a couch and had not been turned on for a few days.  While sitting and reading nearby in daylight, without the light on, I heard a breakage of glass.  I went to investigate and found pieces of the globe on the couch with the base still in the socket.  I have not been able to remove it yet.  Had my grandchildren been over, they may have been hit by the falling glass or I may have come home from work and sat on the glass.  Again, the bulb was not even lit when this happened.  The bulbs are about 3 months old.
justification: The incident involved a broken bulb with no injury, but potential for injury if someone had been present.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the dimmer switch for the product started to melt and burnt his hutch after it was in use for about 1 hour.  He stated  that this allow the aroma from the rock salts for therapeutic purposes.  Caller stated that if no one had been present this could have caused a house fire.

The retailer was contacted and he was inform that he should return the product so they could review the item.
justification: The incident involved a melting dimmer switch and burnt hutch, but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as it occurred after an hour of use and could recur under similar conditions.

incident_description:
We purchased a Sealy posturpedic hybrid mattress from Haverty's furniture store about 2 years ago.  The mattress has recently been emitting a very strong chemical smell, similar to the smell memory foam has when first purchased. My 2 year old baby sleeps in our bed and began breaking out into hives over
the past month. We left town for several days and the hives subsided. The day after we returned, the smell had worsened significantly, and the hives returned. This time, thr the hives were much worse than previously, covering her entire body and with with her eyes nearly swollen shut.  The pediatrician put her on a course of steroids as a result.  My wife has been having respiratory irritation whenever she enters the bedroom, requiring us to sleep in the guest room. She also suffered from hives twice in the past several months, once requiring her to go on steroids as well. She was pregnant at the time, which made it it even more distressing to be requiring steroids.
justification: The incident involves severe allergic reactions (hives and respiratory irritation) requiring medical treatment, indicating a significant health impact.

incident_description:
My dining room fixture has five Elko G7BR301527SD 15w 1210 lumen bulbs produced by G7 Power. These were provided to me in 2015 as warranty replacements for another discontinued set where the bulbs all failed within 1 year of purchase. The bulbs were advertised as having a 10 year warranty.

Two weeks earlier, the bulb began lightly flickering during use, and continued to do so whenever the bulb was powered on. Today, the bulb completely stopped working. When I went to remove the failed bulb, I experienced a moderate electric shock. I observed that the base had partially separated from the bulb, and additionally the base was also burning hot.

I attempted to contact the manufacturer by emailing support@g7power.com, their main contact email address where I had reached them previously, and the email bounced. Additionally their website is not working.
justification: The incident resulted in a moderate electric shock, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue involves a known product defect leading to electric shock.

incident_description:
(09/06/2016) The consumer turned on the floor lamp that had the 3-way light bulb using the low 50 watts.  After the lamp had been on for about 10 minutes, he heard a loud (booming/bomb) sound. He stated after hearing the noise, he went to check his home. He found debris (little pieces of the  glass bulb) all over the bedroom floor. He unplugged the floor lamp from the electrical outlet. 

There was no damage to the lamp. The consumer did not try another bulb in the lamp because the base of the 3-way light bulb was stuck in the light socket of the floor lamp.

(9/13/2016) The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke with [REDACTED]. He advised the consumer to mail the light bulb to the company. The consumer refused and stated he will send the product to FTC to investigate. 

The consumer stated that the manufacturer sent him a coupon for $12.50.
justification: The incident involved a loud noise and broken bulb debris but no injury or damage beyond the bulb itself.

incident_description:
On 10/7/16 during the evening I observed one of the Led bulbs in the ceiling fan flickering in our kitchen ceiling fan. I turned the light off & tried removing the bulb from it's socket. The bulb cover sealed to the ceramic base separated.  When I attempted to remove the Led from the socket it was very hot & caused slight burning of my left fingers. I finally removed the Led from the socket.  On a previous night one of these bulbs stopped working for several minutes then went back on. This has also occurred in my living room lamps, the bulb would stop lighting & then turn back on. I have changed over 95% of my home to Led bulbs, bulbs in the past year.
I'm concerned about the safety of these bulbs. As I inspected the ceramic part of the bulb it appears that only a bead of silicone is used to attach the bulb cover to the Led base. These bulbs are not reliable.
justification: The incident resulted in slight burning of fingers (injury), and the description indicates recurring issues with LED bulbs, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer turned the light fixture in the bathroom on and one of the bulbs exploded.  This is an overhead fixture in a bathroom and it had 3 bulbs in it.   The bulb shattered and glass flew over the bathroom.  There is a diffuser around the base of the bulb and it shattered as well.  Pieces of the bulb and the diffuser were spread around the bathroom. The consumer was not injured.


The consumer replaced the bulb in the light fixture and it appears to be working correctly without any issues.

The consumer's husband is an electrician and he indicated that the problem was most likely related to the bulb.

The consumer have never had prior problems with this fixture or other bulbs used it.  

The bulb was sold in individual packaging.

The consumer said that she did not notice any UL or ETL symbols on the bulb's packaging.
justification: The bulb exploded causing damage but no injuries occurred, and the issue was isolated to the bulb itself.

incident_description: The glass top of our GRANÃÂS dining table suddenly exploded with an extremely loud sound around 10 am. this Saturday morning. Thousands of pieces of broken glass spread to whole dining room and we were going to have our breakfast! Only three wooden coasters were on the table when the explosion happened and the room temperature was around 70F degree. I cannot imagine what would happen if we were siting at the table when the glass exploded.
justification: The incident involved a glass table exploding, causing property damage but no injuries, and the likelihood is unlikely given the specific conditions described.

incident_description: We have the Select Blinds Select Double Cell Light Filtering Shades (sized 72 W" x 53 H") mounted to our bathroom window with 3 mounting brackets per their instructions.  Although we use it per the instructions, it falls from it's mount and causes problems.  Prior to this product, we had the Select Blinds 2" Faux Wood Blinds (sized 72 W" x 53 H") in the same spot and the magnetically-attached valance fell on multiple occasions- breaking plants and once hitting me on the head.  It's clear that they are not careful with the way that they attach their products to be sure that they won't hit the customer on the head.
justification: The incident describes an injury (being hit on the head) and repeated occurrences of the product falling, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
(07/2016) The consumer stated that the night that she purchased the clock, she plugged it in. She got up the next morning and noticed that the bottom of the clock was hot. The consumer unplugged the unit.

A month later, she plugged the clock in again. When she got up the next morning, the clock was hot again and the bottom of the clock had melted. The consumer unplugged the clock and tried to get in touch with Sharp. When she contacted the firm at 1-800 BE.SHARP,  she was given another number to call but only got voicemail.
justification: The clock became hot and melted, but there was no reported injury or death.

incident_description:
This consumer purchased a standard sized pillow from a retailer in California August 28, 2016 and liked it so much in the beginning that she returned to the store to purchase another.
She began sleeping on the one pillow and noticed that she progressively had a feeling of slight lack of well being but she dismissed it.
Around September 6, 2016 she was visiting with a friend and stated that she didn't feel well at all and so she went home. 
Wednesday, September 7 and Thursday September 8, 2016 the caller was taking her blood pressure and noticed that her blood pressure was rising.  She is a registered nurse and so took her BP Medication but by Friday, September 9, 2016 her blood pressure 227/115 which prompted her to drive to the emergency room.
She was kept at St. Mary's hospital emergency room from 9:30PM on Friday until 10:30AM on Friday to bring her blood pressure back to normal.
She was seen by her physician September 12, 2016 and was provided with additional blood pressure medicine which did not bring her pressure down.
She went to emergency care September 12, 2016 and received a change in blood pressure medicine again.
She returned home and made no changes until Thursday, September 15th, 2016 when she read labels on the pillow instructing her to wash them before using them.
She washed the pillows but has not used them again and her health has been improving progressively since she stopped use of the pillows.
Her blood pressure has been lowering and her doctor has taken her off of the additional blood pressure medicines.
She has not contacted the manufacturer because she states that they are located in China.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant health issue (high blood pressure requiring medical intervention) linked to pillow use, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
09/26/2016 - The consumer indicates that the LED light bulb globe in his kitchen exploded however the light stayed on. The unit had been on for some time. This LED light bulb had been installed for six months or more.

09/29/2016 - The consumer indicates that his wife went into their garage and turned on the LED light bulb. The light bulb globe exploded immediately however the light is still on. The consumer indicates that this LED light bulb was installed approximately two months ago.

The consumer plans on keeping the units for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues. The consumer indicates that the LED light bulbs have a twenty-year warranty on them.
justification: The LED light bulbs exploded but no injuries were reported, and the lights remained functional.

incident_description:
Some years ago I purchased two Sterilite 3 Drawer Units (Part# 2020N-F).  The units consist of a white plastic frame containing 3 clear plastic drawers.

I have used them in my study, always indoors and out of direct sunlight.

In the last few weeks, the white plastic frame on both units has become extremely brittle.  If you contact the surface with even very low force (a pound or two), the plastic fractures into extremely sharp shards, about as sharp as shards of glass.  The plastic remaining in the frame has extremely sharp edges.  Twice I have sustained minor injuries (cuts and abrasions) from these shards and sharp edges.

I contacted Sterilite and received a wholly unsatisfactory response, copied below.

"I'm sorry for the delay.  We do not offer written or lifetime warranties. Plastic is quite durable, but can crack, chip or break during normal use.  We no longer manufacture part #2020 (for item #2023 and other Drawer units), they were discontinued some time ago.

If stored near a window within the household, direct sunlight will eventually dry out the plastic and make it brittle or crack.  To avoid damage, you will want to insure Sterilite products are kept in mostly shade areas indoors.

I'm sorry I cannot assist you in this matter, and encourage you to discard or recycle the unit."

Considering the danger posed to children, adults and pets by the sudden fracturing of these units into dangerously sharp pieces and edges, I suggest and investigation directed towards a recall would be warranted.
justification: The incident describes minor injuries (cuts and abrasions) from sharp plastic shards, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the repeated occurrence of injuries and the brittle nature of the plastic.

incident_description: I bought the Biedermann and Sons "Candle Snuggers" in order to, as the package states, burn my candles more safely by keeping them upright in their holders to prevent excess dripping of hot wax.  They in fact made the burning FAR more DANGEROUS, as the "snuggers" held the dripping wax inside the holders so that it built up too much, and when the flames got down to the snuggers, it set them on fire because they are EXTREMELY FLAMMABLE.  When the snuggers burned away, the entirety of ALL the hot wax at once exploded all over.
justification: The incident describes a dangerous situation where the product caused a fire and explosion of hot wax, posing a significant risk of injury.

incident_description:
The consumer states that the file cabinet poses a tip over hazard. The consumer states the top drawer came loose and noticed that screws were missing. 

The consumer states that she contacted the Office Depot corporate office and has tried to return the cabinet but they will not accept it. The consumer has been told that she could receive screws but the consumer states that the screws will not address the tip over hazard.
justification: The incident involves a potential tip-over hazard with no reported injury, and the likelihood is possible given the missing screws and consumer concern.

incident_description:
Zilotek  48 inch Linear Led Tube  purchased at Menard's.  

Plastic casing caught on fire in light fixture, if I had not been around to see the smoke and flames since it was a ceiling light it could of been very serious.

Tried reporting it to Menards, there Chuck Ochs, pretty much even after I sent them a picture said it was not their concern, never had a complaint, and keeps wanting me to return it.  He told me it was in a correct fixture, so just return it.

Checked Menards and they have discontinued that brand, after stocking them for a short time.

incident_description:
A GE LED bulb (LED14DA21V/827W, 120 VAC, 60Hz, 14 W, 140 mA, 1100 lumens) in a hanging chandelier above our kitchen table caught on fire. Fortunately, I was seated at the table when the incident occurred and promptly turned off electrical power to the chandelier.

The chandelier hangs about 2.5 feet from the ceiling and contains a single light bulb that is well ventilated from all sides. Room temperature during the incident was around 70 F and a window next to the table was open, drawing cool air from outside. Outside temperature was below 70 F. Time of day was around 10 am. The bulb was on for the 1 hour leading up to the incident.

Incident: while seated at the kitchen table reading the newspaper, I heard a sudden buzzing sound from the chandelier. The led bulb then started smoking from the top with sparks and flames following. My first thought was, "is this going to catch my house on fire!" I promptly got up and switched off electrical power to the chandelier, which immediately stopped the sparks and flames. Smoking continued.
justification: The incident involved a bulb catching fire but was promptly controlled without injury, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description:
Village Candle Jar Candle ignited.  
approximately 2 " of wax were remaining.  
Jar Candle.  Was burning for 90 minutes when entire candle ignited.

incident_description:
On Oct 9,2016 I went to brag something out my nightstand top drawer. I pulled open the top drawer and closed it back. I then turn around and all of a sudden the entire nightstand fell forward on the back of my legs pushing me forward. At the time both drawer came open which made everything worst for me to try to get up. It was very heavy for me to get it off me that I had to call my sons to help. Very bad product.

incident_description: A Sylvania Hologen flood light bulb exploded off the glass lense cover narrowly missing my wife and nearly causing serious injury. The bulb was purchased at Lowes. The description: Sylvania Halogen 60 W 120 V WFL, 1100 Lumens, Mexico, J378
justification: The bulb exploded but no injury occurred, narrowly missing the individual.

incident_description: I bought this (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B019NW42EA/ref=oh_aui_search_detailpage?ie=UTF8&psc=1) chair off of Amazon about six months ago and last week the base of it snapped throwing me to the floor. I am 5'8" tall and weigh about 200 pounds. At the time I was sitting in the chair working. There was nothing else on the chair of significant weight and all I was wearing was a pair of shorts (I live near Phoenix). I've never abused the chair, never has two people sitting in it at that same time or anything that would have caused it to fail like that. I'm pretty sure it was a manufacturing defect. These chairs are going to seriously hurt someone if they are not recalled.

incident_description:
We purchased 90 restaurant chairs in 2015 from a company in Canada. Within a couple of months, the seat back of the chair began to break on several of the chairs. This poses a potential risk of injury when the seat back goes back further than it should when someone is not suspecting it to.
We contacted the company immediately but they would not offer us any help. Over the past year, 30+ chairs have broken in exactly the same manner. Frustrated, we again contacted the company but all they would offer was to replace 10 chairs. Since they all appeared to be defective we did not want any more of these chairs as they pose a potential for injury.
We contacted a company and had the chairs evaluated. I am going to send you the results ofthe testing and evaluation.
justification: The incident involves multiple chairs breaking, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description: Fall river Swivel rocker chair recall---2---bad welds
justification: The recall due to bad welds indicates a potential for incidents but no reported injuries, making severity level 2. The likelihood is possible given the recall.

incident_description: We have a Sunbeam heating pad that I was using normally, on my back as I was sitting on our sofa.  The heating pad malfunctioned, burning a 1/2-inch hole through the cloth cover of the heating pad on the side of the pad that was not next to my body, near the end of the pad where the power cord enters.  The heating pad also burned a similar hole through a throw pillow that was next to the pad.
justification: The heating pad malfunctioned causing damage to the pad and a pillow, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Purchased a bed from IKEA in 2014. The bed frame includes a metal center beam. Without notice, the center beam collapsed. If one of my small children were crawling around or under the bed, they would have been injured. Since the part that failed is not visible, there was no way to see the part was bending or breaking.
justification: The bed frame collapsed, posing a potential injury risk to small children, though no injury was reported.

incident_description:
In late August I bought an item through Amazon (Another Vintage World Map Duvet Cover). This duvet cover was for my daughter, and we put it on her bed without laundering. Yesterday and the day before (September 19-20), shortly after touching this duvet cover, I had serious allergic reactions, and the second time a trip to the emergency room. My throat swelled so much that for the rest of the day I had difficulty swallowing. I documented the second incident and can provide a photo of the swelling where I had touched my lip (of course you can't see the swelling that partially closed my throat), and the emergency room report upon request. 

I am deeply concerned that these duvet covers are going out to other people, including children, who may be even more sensitive than I am, resulting in serious illness or even death. I reported this to Amazon and they refunded my purchase price, but Society6 has not responded to my emails and they are still offering the item for purchase. Their website shows them to be a place for artists to sell their products, and the specific artist listed as the maker of this duvet is "beaulac-MJDesigns". I Googled the name and it is [REDACTED]. Her website is in French so she may be in France or Canada.

There is no way for me to be 100% certain that the duvet cover is what caused the reaction because the doctor told me to never touch it again and I am definitely not going to! But both times the swelling began moments after I touched the fabric and then touched the part of my face that swelled up. We have nothing else new in the home, and I am seldom on my daughter's bed so it is easy to backtrack. The doctor said that the plastic it was shipped in may have been coated with a pesticide which was transferred to the fabric (we discarded the packaging as soon as it arrived), or it may be something in the fabric itself. I have had a sensitivity to pesticides on fruit in the past, so this would make sense. I plan to have my daughter put gloves on and place the duvet in a plastic garbage back when she comes home today, because it seems like someone should test it. I have no way to do that and the company won't respond to my emails, so I am asking for your guidance. If you are unable to help, I will simply throw it away and pray that this was an isolated incident.
justification: The incident involved serious allergic reactions requiring emergency room treatment, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it appears to be an isolated case linked to a specific product.

incident_description:

incident_description:
See next page for full explanation.

Pictures of sheared bunk rail support are attached to email. 

On 9/27/12, I purchased a bunk bed for my son from the Room Store in Sterling, VA before the store went out of business. The bed we purchased has two single beds, one on top and one on the bottom. My son always sleeps on the bottom bunk. This past Sunday, my son got into his bed to go to sleep and the metal support rods sheared. I was grateful he was not on the top bunk when this happened. 

Realizing that The Room Store went out of business, I found an identifying sticker on the support that says "Discovery World Furniture PO#X092111-4 Made in China." I researched Discovery World Furniture and found factorybunkbeds.com is the US distributor. I called factorybunkbeds.com to ask about a potential warranty. I spoke to a representative named [REDACTED] and he said the product was no longer under warranty. I asked about the language on the website which states "Discovery World Furniture will replace any components part for 50% of the then prevailing retail price plus freight for the lifetime of the product." He explained that the shipping cost was very expensive and I would need to pay the shipping. Clearly, this warranty is of no benefit to the customer with regard to the metal support rods. He suggested I go to the website and find 'plywood decking modification" and do the repair myself. 

Curious as to why there would be so great a need for a repair of this part to warrant a special link on the website, I asked if the part was perhaps defective. He said the part only broke due to misuse. When I asked him to explain, he said the part broke when kids jumped on the bed and broke them. When I explained that was not possible in my situation as it was the bottom single bunk that broke, and it would not be possible for kids to jump on the bottom bunk from the top or otherwise, he abruptly placed me on hold and never returned to the line.

I am concerned that the metal support rods in these beds are not safe for normal wear and tear. I am also concerned about a company that sells products to children having a dismissive attitude toward a defect that could potentially harm children.
justification: The incident involved sheared bunk rail support but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of occurrence is rated 4 (likely) due to the dismissive attitude of the company and the existence of a repair modification link on their website.

incident_description: I purchased a Besta TV stand from Ikea in early 2015, assembled it according to the packaged instructions, put an appropriately sized TV on it and have been using it without worry ever since. The TV stand is sturdy wood construction with a glass plate on top. At 11:30pm last night, I heard a loud crash, got out of bed and went downstairs to investigate. The glass topper had spontaneously and violently shattered, throwing shards of glass in a five foot radius around the TV stand! There had been no signs of damage when I installed this item, nor had the glass sustained any damage after installation. There is absolutely no reason the glass should have shattered like this. There were no injuries, but only because nobody was in the room when this incident occurred. If my six year old daughter had been awake, chances are she would have been badly injured because we spend much of our family and play time in the room where this furniture is located. I did my best to clean up, but after vacuuming several times, I am still coming across random shards of glass in my living room carpet. We will be wearing shoes in the living room until I am confident all the glass is gone. I picked glass out of my daughter's toys and found some on the couch across the room from the TV as well.
justification: The glass shattered violently, posing a significant risk of injury, but no one was hurt in this instance.

I went to the hospital immediately and there I was informed that my finger had to be amputated. It was half way amputated.

As I was sitting in my living room watching TV around 8:30pm on Tuesday, August 30, 2016, the glass the TV was sitting on shattered for unexplained reason. I bought the TV and stand together at Best Buy on February 13, 2010 as a set. The top shelf of the TV stand was recommended for the size of TV I was buying as the stand can hold up to 300lbs. The TV proceeded to fall forward onto my hardwood floors, which have suffered damage, and my TV no longer works. The two glass shelves below were also damaged. I feel this is a potential hazard to other consumers, especially for small children, pets, and anyone in general. I have my original receipt of purchase from Best Buy, this was the recommended TV stand for the TV I purchased. I also have several pictures of the incident immediately after this happening. I have saved the shattered glass, the TV stand frame, and the TV that does not work anymore. 

What I am asking is that I be reimbursed for replacement cost and for damages to my wood floors. I will submit a claim directly with the manufacturer as well. I have already talked to a store manager at Best Buy on Wednesday, August 31, 2016 and they were not willing to assist in any way. I feel this product should be removed and recalled.

incident_description:
A multipurpose 100W Daytime Heat Lamp (for reptiles) which I purchased from Petco, exploded suddenly on the top of the terranium which I keep my chinese water dragons enclosed in. This has happened once before. The brand ofthe bulb is ExoTerra. l bought this bulb two weeks ago and have kept it in the same place on top of my terrarium since I got it.

Approximately 11 :30pm, the bulb suddenly hissed and then imploded (cracked outward), and pieces of the bulb went in different directions (many pieces landing in the water container that my lizards use for bathing). It made a very loud "pop" sound when it exploded and flickered light briefly. Smoke began traveling out of what was remaining of the bulb. I had to run to it and grab the broken bulb quickly because I was very alarmed that It could create a fire. I had to pull out the power plug to the lamp as well because the main filament of the lamp was still attached and discharging electrical output.

This is very dangerous to my safety, as well as the safety of my pets, and any potential complications this could cause to my house and things. I don't know what would happen if I was not at home in the room when the bulb exploded. IT WOULD HAVE CONTINUED DISCHARGING ELECTRICAL CURRENT. My floor is carpeted and this is a potential ELECTRICAL FIRE HAZARD. This could have also electrocuted my pets and killed them.
justification: The bulb exploded, posing a fire hazard and potential harm to pets, but no actual injury or death occurred. This has happened once before, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
On Sunday, August 14th, my husband and I were in a twilight sleep and were awakened by a loud noise.  After investigating, we found that our TV stand shattered into a thousand pieces.  There are three tiers of glass and the one that shattered was the top one that had the TV and sound bar on it.  The instructions that we still have says that the top shelf holds 120 pounds and there was no where near that on it.  The top piece of glass is thicker then the other two.  I have a bag of glass to prove that we installed the top shelf with the correct piece.  We bought this TV stand from HH Gregg on January 2, 2016 for $319.49.  Thank God that our TV wasn't damaged.  The only thing that did get damaged were two HDMI cables that was $53.47.

On Monday, August 15th, my husband and I stopped at HH Gregg on Colerain Ave. in Cincinnati, Ohio and showed them the pictures and receipt.  All they told us was that they were sorry and that we have to contact the manufacturer, Tech Craft, because it is over 30 days.  I felt like saying that we did not buy the TV stand from the manufacturer, but I didn't.

On Tuesday, August 16th, I called Tech Craft at 1-800-661-7030 and all I got was a voice mail.  I did not leave a message.  I decided to email them instead along with pictures and receipt of sale.  I did not have the receipt at the time for the HDMI cables.  On August 16th, I received an automated reply saying that they have received my email and will normally process it within 2 business days.  As of today, August 28th, I have not heard from them.

I have found 5 other cases of the same thing and just two this year.  This is a serious issue and dangerous.  This company should be recalling all of their TV stands before someone get's seriously injured or killed.  I am afraid that a child or animal will get seriously injured.  This glass shattered with such force that some glass stuck on the wall and blew off a large candle along with other items on the lower shelves.  

I would just like to get the word out to everyone who have this type of TV stand to be aware of the danger especially with children and animals.

I have several pictures and receipt but your tab under product and add files will not open up for me to add them.  Please let me know if you need these and how I can get them to you.  The pictures are worth a thousand words.  Thank you
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered TV stand and HDMI cables) but no injuries, and similar cases have been reported, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: After light was on for 10 minutes, I heard a pop and the bulb shattered, spraying glass everywhere. I was under the light at the time, making a bed, and the glass fell all over my neck and back. It also burned holes in our carpet and we had to cut shards of glass out of it. There was glass everywhere.
justification: The incident resulted in glass shards falling on the person, causing potential injury, and also damaged the carpet, indicating a moderate severity.

incident_description: My 3.5 year old child was getting ready to go to bed and went to unscrew a light bulb  that was in his room by his bed. The bulb is an led light bulb so the bulb wasn't too hot and when he went to go unscrew it the glass shattered. The glass is encompassed in some type of plastic, but it separated from the bulb exposing glass shards to his hands. Fortunately he wasn't injured.
justification: The incident involved a broken light bulb with exposed glass shards, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
(08/11/2016) The consumer stated that his wife noticed that the bulb in the two light ceiling fixture flickered and then it went out.  One shade of the fixture was dark. His wife shut the light  off so that she could remove the bulb. As she was taking the shade off of the fixture, she noticed smoke coming from the base of the coil of the bulb. Immediately, the bulb caught on fire. Flames were coming from the base of the bulb.  

His wife wrapped aluminum foil around the bulb to put the fire out. She also unscrewed the bulb and took it out of the fixture.

The consumer will send pictures of the bulb.
justification: The incident involved a bulb catching fire, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
In early 2016 purchased a Lexington 11 South Urbana King Bed from Exotic Home in Norfolk VA

http://www.exotichomeinteriors.com/
https://www.lexington.com/

After a few days the bed frame collapsed due to a design flaw. The bed platform has support legs but they fold away, placing all the weight on the bed frame, that is only held together by a thin, glued wood veneer.

Luckily I was able to stop the headboard from falling on my children who were sitting on the bed at the time.

I demanded a refund from Exotic Home but they refused. They offered to replace it with a brand new bed, saying there was no design flaw.

After a few days, the new bed too, broke and the headboard fell forward, hitting me on the head very hard. I was lying on the bed at the time so could not catch it in time. If my head had not broken the headboards forward collapse, it would have fallen on my wife's face.

Again I demanded a refund but Exotic Home refused. They said they would modify the bed (thereby voiding the factory warranty). Lexington refused to modify the design of the bed.

Exotic home added extra steel brackets and many additional support legs under the platform, to keep the weight of the frame. But even their supports, and the standard supports fold away if there is a slight sideways movement of the bed. The bed does move on the floor because it is a hardwood/laminate floor and the bed needs to be moved also to clean under the bed.

The bed has a very heavy wood headboard. If that headboard falls on a child, elderly person, or pet, they will be severely injured or worse. This will also happen if a child or pet crawls under the bed and bumps against one of the supports, causing the bed to collapse on them. It could be a severe injury or worse.

I wrote a review of the bed here:

https://www.amazon.com/review/RPTSHOBXUPNOP/ref=pe_1098610_137716200_cm_rv_eml_rv0_rv 

I anticipate with more of the supports folding away, and their mounting bolts breaking because of the repetitive bending, the bed will collapse again in the near future. For safety, we now have to sleep on the floor on the mattress.
justification: The incident describes an injury from the headboard falling, and the likelihood is high due to repeated failures and design flaws.

incident_description:
In 2009 we purchased a [Redacted] LCD T.V. along with an assembled T.V. stand from Frys Electronics in San Jose, California. The T.V. stand has glass shelves and a wood/metal base frame. The top shelf is attached to the base frame using 4 metal mounts glued to the glass. The back two mounts are attached to the base frame. The front two mounts are attached to a hinge liked rods that attach to the base frame. The other night, rear mounts and the detached from the glass (glue failed). Then the glass shelf (due to the front hinge mounts) toppled the T.V. and stand over and landed on the floor. Most fortunately, our two-year-old child nor anyone else was not in front of the T.V. at the time, otherwise serious injury or death would have occurred. 
The design of this T.V. is clearly dangerous, for if the glue fails on the rear glass mounts, gravity takes over and the T.V. will topple over (as ours did).
Thank You,

[REDACTED]
justification: The TV stand failed, causing the TV to topple, but no one was injured as no one was present at the time.

incident_description: In April of 2013, my husband I purchased  the Fall River 7PC dining set. We were enjoying it one day on the patio and he leaned back in his rocker and it fell off its base. He was startled and hit his head and arm on the patio. We did not seek medical attention, but he was quite shaken up and bruised. I immediately contact Hampton Bay for a replacement. I even sent pictures of the chair and its broken base to the initial contact. After several months passed and many, many phone calls we finally received a replacement. I thought it was weird that they didn't want the broken chair back...I thought they would want to see if it was faulty. I was told to simply dispose of it. We still have our 7PC set on the patio.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bruises and being shaken up) but no medical attention was required, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents could happen with faulty furniture.

incident_description: 9/27/11 Caller is reporting that her 2 year old nephew was killed by the MALM dresser after her brother had only purchased it for a month, it was reported to her that her 4 year old nephew was sent to wake up the child and found him under the dresser.  The ambulance was called in and they transported the child to a hospital they declared the child DOA.  There was a police and hospital report submitted.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child, which is a severity level 4. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such fatal incidents are not common.

incident_description: Went into the bathroom at 950am and turned on the light. Shortly after, 5-8 minutes later, I heard a pop and the light went out. I looked up at it and saw it had a faint yellow glow from the lightbulb and noticed smoke and a terrible smell. Immediately turned the light off. Pulled it out and noticed the pop was the lightbulb melted from its base and caused a small fire. This is a safety hazard and am lucky I was in the room while it was on. 13W UL# E170906
justification: The incident involved a small fire and a melted lightbulb, posing a safety hazard with potential for injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: This is a new sectional sofa set (Collinsville model) from Ashley Furniture.  A guest was getting up from the left sided arm recliner, and the chair tipped over.  When there is any amount of pressure on the arm of the chair, the studs on the chair disengage from the bracket on the adjoining chair, and it tips over.  There is no mechanism to keep the chair from tipping over.  We reported it to Ashley Homestore, and a technician came out today, and verified there is a design defect.  However, they offered no repair for it.  I went to the store's showroom today, and their floor model does the same thing.  This is a dangerous safety issue that the public needs to be aware of.
justification: The chair tipping over due to a design defect poses a risk of injury, and the issue is confirmed to occur consistently under pressure.

incident_description: We purchased the Hampton Bay Eastham 7Piece Patio Dining Set, Model # 723.002.000, Internet/Catalog SKU 204411327, on 08/29/2015, which includes a 2-year warranty, for $581.94. Approximately 4 months after receiving the set, we lost our first stationary chair due to the welds breaking. By 05/15/2015, we had lost all four (4) of the stationary chairs, and one (1) of the swivel chairs (due to welds breaking), and by 07/01/16, we lost our last and final chair (swivel); we now have no chairs left to the set.  I filed a claim with Home Depot on 06/01/2016, and to date, I still have not received the replacement chairs (after 50 emails, sending photos, and approximately 10 phone calls).  These chairs broke while we were sitting in them, or trying to get up, and I actually fell to the ground when one of the swivel chairs broke.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall when a chair broke, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Zline Designs desk from Walmart less than a year ago. Today, the tempered glass top exploded all over our guest bedroom. The desk has not been used in months and there was nothing sitting on top of the glass or around it. I feel it is an unsafe product if it can randomly explode and shatter into fragments like that.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploding glass) but no reported injury, warranting severity level 2. The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as spontaneous glass breakage is uncommon but documented.

incident_description: I purchased this lamp about 7 months ago from Urban Outfitters.  It is used infrequently in our apartment.  Every time we have turned it on, the light bulb crackles, shatters and smokes.  This has happened 4 times, with 4 different bulbs (different brands and wattage).  We did not exceed the recommended wattage for the lamp.  Each time, the light bulb shattered within seconds of switching the light on.  We immediately switched it off and unplugged it, thinking that it was another bad light bulb.  But after happening 4 times, there is definitely something wrong with the lamp.
justification: The lamp causes bulbs to shatter and smoke when turned on, posing a hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
Beautyrest Geo-Incline Foam Mattress Pad, King Size

incident_description: My husband was sitting in one of the chairs we were out on the back porch having coffee and he went to sit back in the chair and it completely broke off the hinges falling too the ground no injuries occurred. We had to end up getting it fixed on our own but now we see there is a recall so we wanted to report it just in case someone else he got hurt. We seen on the news that it was recalled and that you guys are offering repair kits and we have 6 of those chairs so not sure how that works but we would need 6 repair kits I'm assuming thank you
justification: The incident involved a chair breaking but no injuries occurred, and the issue is part of a known recall indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Dresser tipped over with a 40inch plasma tv on top of dresser on top of my 2 children ages, my daughter 3 years old and my son 21 months old . This could of been a tragedy. 40 inch TV fell on top of my son corner of dresser cut my sons forehead, drawers fell on top of my daughter while the dresser was caught by the edge of my bed. This was the most terrifying moment of my life. I ran to the room after hearing a loud noise to find both my babies buried underneath the TV and dresser i purchased in IKEA in Carson, CA .
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the son's forehead and the daughter was trapped under drawers, indicating injuries but no fatalities.

incident_description: My 4 year old daughters elbow and mid portion of her arm became entrapped in the mesh cup holder of a foldable child's chair. She sustained petechia from mid upper arm to wrist.
justification: The child sustained petechia, which indicates an injury, but there is no mention of death or severe harm.

incident_description: The Pottery Barn Madison 4-Shelf Bookrack was mounted onto the wall in our toddler's bedroom using the screws provided by Pottery Barn.  It's a very thin, unstable bookrack that needs mounting.  Over time, I guess the books were too much for it to handle and the bookrack came off the wall, out of its mounting system.  No injury was caused, but all the books fell out the back with a loud, forceful fall, and the extremely thin bookcase was standing unmounted, and it is very easily tipped over.  The two screws/mounting system they provide is simply not enough for a bookrack targeted toward kids, who will spend all day taking books in and out and tugging at it.
justification: The incident involved the bookrack detaching from the wall without causing injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the unstable design and frequent use by toddlers.

incident_description:
I depressed the foot pedal to open the trash can and my small toe became caught between the pedal and the bottom edge of the container.  As I removed my foot, my small toe was severely lacerated by the bottom edge of the container.  The bottom edge of the container is stainless steel and extremely sharp. 

It would seem that the bottom edge of the container, at least above the pedal, should have some kind of protection or barrier instead of just an exposed sharp edge.

Product Link: http://www.walmart.com/ip/Better-Homes-and-Gardens-11.9-Gallon-Semi-Round-Trash-Can/34400796

I have also reported this to Walmart.  The Manufacturer, Better Homes and Gardens, does not have an online contact mechanism, however they do have an 800 number will call later.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe laceration, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The sharp edge and lack of protection make this likely to occur again (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Caller stated that her power recliner caught fire and spread to other furniture in the room.  The fire department was called in to contain the fire, there was a fire report.  She stated that this incident occurred during the night while they were asleep, it seems as if the recliner had a combustible fire.

Caller stated that there was an estimated property  damages of about $15,000.00.

(5/2016) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that they were not aware of an incident like that and that someone would contact her in regards to the warranty. However, they have not contacted her or the insurance company.

Caller feels that this recliner is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description:
The consumer and his wife were sitting at the table, when all of a sudden, one piece of glass fell from the table.  Next, all of the glass fell from the table to the floor.  The temperature was somewhere around 90 degrees that day.  After all of the glass fell on the floor, a few pieces of glass shards continued popping and moving around.  This continued with some pieces up to an hour later.

The consumer was not injured and the damage was limited to the table.

The consumer went to the dealer the following day.  Their rep. said that they were not aware of any problems of this nature and suggested that the consumer contact the mfr. 

The consumer checked www.saferproducts.gov and saw that there were other reports of this nature on the site.  However, this manufacturer did not appear to be included in any CPSC recalls.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved glass falling and shattering, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description: My husband and I bought blinds for our entire house but they emitted such noxious, nauseating fumes that they had to be removed the next day.  The odor was so powerful that our eyes, noses, throats, brains, and spinal cords burned.  We had tremors and headache.  The company stored the blinds for two months to out-gas but when they were reinstalled, the same thing happened.  They are currently in our garage because [REDACTED] ruled that there is nothing wrong with the blinds materially. We spent  just short of $4,000 to have our health and immune systems put in jeopardy.  The company refused to give the MSDS to us and are proud that their product is made in the United States.
justification: The description reports physical symptoms like burning sensations, tremors, and headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The recurrence after reinstallation suggests the issue is unlikely but not rare (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
I purchased a tatami room bed a few months ago.

It has a very strong smell. My girlfriend moved in this week and the smell from the bed is making her sick.   If the bedroom Windows are closed during the day she gets a headache when in the bedroom at night.

We decided to move the bed frame out of the bedroom. When we disassembled the bed frame to move it outside the house, we both got a headache. I got a red, itchy rash where my bare arms contacted the wood of the bed frame as I was moving it outside.

Now that the bed is out of the bedroom, we experience no further effects at night.

I love the look of the bed but am concerned about the health effects. It can't be in the house with us.
justification: The incident caused headaches and a rash, indicating injury (severity 3), and the effects occurred consistently when exposed to the bed (likelihood 4).

incident_description: The Messina pillow top, a Brigham collection mattress and box spring that has a 10 year warranty was breaking down after 4 days. Month after month it got worse. It's sunken in completely down to the broken box spring approximately 17 inches deep and a 4 feet circle wide. It also squeaks so loud I can hear her moving through the vents. The noise wakes her up. My daughter has back problems now and has to see a chiropractor. She can't sleep so she failed her second half of the online school year. We contacted the seller 4 times. The first time the first week, the 2nd time,  2 weeks in, and then, months later. This was supposed to be the best mattress in the store.
justification: The mattress failure caused back problems requiring chiropractic care, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue persisted over months with multiple complaints, suggesting a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
We purchased six 100W equivalent CREE LED soft white light bulbs from the Home Depot in May of 2013. One of them burned out and we replaced it thinking it was manufacturing error. When we took that one out, the glass bulb separated from the base.

Another three bulbs have failed recently, and when we rearranged the remaining bulbs, another two glass bulbs detached from their bases. That's three out of seven. If our lighting fixtures were not positioned with the glass shade facing the ground, the detached glass casing could have come loose from the fixture and smashed from the ceiling onto the floor below. We find it hard to believe this is not a design or manufacturing flaw, and with the design of many light fixtures on the market, these light bulbs may be a hazard.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with no reported injuries, but with a clear risk of glass falling from fixtures.

incident_description: 2' fluorescent light fixture started smoking and making a popping sounds
justification: The light fixture smoking and popping is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential fire hazard.

incident_description:
I purchased an office desk for home use In March 2015. Soon thereafter I started having respiratory issues and sore
throat, prompting visits to doctor and hospital Finally, In February, 2016, a series of air quality tests were conducted
in and around my apartment In my senior housing complex. Tests showed that formaldehyde concentration was
very high In my apartment but not elsewhere In complex. Additional testing showed that the formaldehyde was
coming from the office desk.
The desk was removed from my apartment and I was moved to a nearby hotel while my apartment was deep
cleaned, clothing washed/aired, etc. After cleaning, further air quality tests were conducted In and around my
apartment and Indicated that air quality was at acceptable level of formaldehyde.
The desk manufacturer has been contacted and presented with an accounting similar to the forgoing along with an
itemized list of cost incurred for medical, air testing, living relocation, movers, and purchase price of desk.
The Maine Attorney General has acted as my agent. It Is my understanding, that the desk manufacturer denies
using formaldehyde impregnated materials In their desks, will reimburse me for purchase price of desk. pay the
medical bills If I can supply them with the "proper codes", but. will not pay for any other costs that arose from their
desk fouling my living space with such a pernicious carcinogen.
justification: The incident caused respiratory issues and sore throat, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: In July of 2015 I purchased four chairs (Montego Bay Bar Stool) on Amazon.com.  The company that manufactured the chairs is Homestyle-furniture.   The glue in the chairs is defective.  The chairs just came apart.  Last weekend there was a child siting on the chair when the chair just came apart and she sprained her ankle badly.  I have called both Amazon and Homestyle furniture.  They did not appear to care.  When I looked at the review of these chairs it is obvious that this has happened to others.  These chairs need to be recalled and fixed before someone get seriously hurt,
justification: A child sprained her ankle due to the chair collapsing, indicating an injury. Reviews suggest this is a recurring issue.

incident_description:
June 27, 2016 8:20 pm - I was working at my desk - my husband was in the room when my tempered glass desktop exploded. It sounded like a shotgun blast and sent a shock wave through the air. When I had the courage to open my eyes my jeans were covered in blood, the computer was leaning against the wall, there was shards of sharp glass and fine glass dust everywhere - including out the door, the blast was so violent. I had a horrific headache the following day but on Wed June 29, 2016 I took a piece of the glass to the Calgary IKEA store, they returned the purchase price of the desk and said they would contact IKEA Sweden. July 4, 2016 I received a call from the Calgary IKEA store to say this is the normal reaction to a tempered glass table breaking. It is
impossible to believe this is true. I have glass shards imbedded everywhere - I have seen an eye doctor who reports there are no corneal lacerations on my eyes but there is debris in my eyes. I am being treated for that. I play the piano and my hands are of concern. The fine shards of glass in my hands are slowing coming out of the skin - I can still play. At IKEA the item was sold until 2013 - I think! I do not know why it is no longer sold.

____________________________________________________________________________________________

06/29/2016 - The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained the situation. The representative she spoke to informed her that they would have to contact Sweden to report it.

07/04/2016 - The consumer received a call from her local IKEA that Sweden reported that this was the normal way for a tempered glass to break, and hence IKEA will take no further action.

The consumer indicates that she received superficial lacerations to her legs, arms, hands. The consumer indicates that she had to visit her eye Doctor on 06/29/2016 and 07/04/2016 for the debris in her eyes after the explosion. The consumer has another visit scheduled on 07/12/2016.
justification: The incident caused superficial lacerations and required multiple medical visits for eye debris, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description: Purchased a Dining Room Lighting Fixture( portfolio/transglobal nine light fixture) i'd say few years back that fell from the ceiling because of a failed loop which I still have in my posession as well as the fixture. It did severe damage to my wood dining set, the table and one chair which I could not replace as it is not sold anywhere as of this time. I purchased a whole new dining set now prior to seeing the recall for said fixture. It happened while we were was watching TV in the adjacent room and scared the heck out of us. Please if anyone reads this check to see you don"t have one of these fixtures, the fastening loop looks to be made from some cheap material its not even metal, it is very dangerous especially because of the weight of the fixture!!!!!
justification: The incident caused property damage (severe damage to the dining set) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Safety issue. Last night, one of the glass display cases I bought at Ikea, exploded. Nothing touched it. It was the access door. This is a link to some photos in the Microsoft cloud. https://1drv.ms/f/s!ApPoV1nATccFg-gzMM1kW6IejDdhgg  . I think the case is about 5 years old and stands with other identical Ikea glass cases. I think that this is an urgent safety issue. I think the case should be replaced but the safety issue is paramount. The Ikea product code is: DETLOF. The best contact is by return email.
justification: The glass display case exploded without any contact, indicating a potential safety issue, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(7/9/16) The consumer installed the light bulb on the front door fixture. Approximately five minutes later the consumer and his wife went outside to look at the light. Immediately after looking at the light the consumer states that he felt pain in both eyes. 

The consumer indicated that this was the first time he purchased this bulb. 

The consumer believes the brightness of the light bulb caused the pain in his eyes. The consumer states that if he continues to feel the pain he will seek medical attention.

The consumer contacted Walmart's customer service and informed them about the incident. The consumer states that he filed a report (no report #) and he was offered a $5 gift card, which will be mailed to him. The consumer believes Walmart is the distributor of the brand Great Value.

Pain gone 72 hours after injury.
justification: The consumer experienced eye pain from the light bulb's brightness, which resolved within 72 hours, indicating an injury without long-term consequences.

incident_description:
This product sold at Home Depot was installed at a new condo and it fell off the wall and shattered into pieces. The glue on the back of the mirror was not strong and it came unglued.  I thought that it was just one bad mirror and I had a defective product.  However, another mirror did the exact same thing, except this time, I saw that it was tilted and removed it.  On the back of the mirror, the same problem existed, the glue had came undone. 

This is a dangerous product - please do not let Home Depot sell any more of this design.
justification: The mirror fell and shattered, but no injury was reported. The issue occurred twice, indicating a possible defect.

incident_description: I purchased a recliner type piece of furniture from Macy's 2 years ago. Two days ago the steel frame broke in two places causing the recliner to flip backwards and sending me head over heals onto the floor
justification: The incident caused the recliner to flip and the person to fall, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: Taylor glass top scale.  Wife was in the bathroom doing makeup, heard a very loud pop, and turned around to see glass all over the floor.  It broke into hundreds of small pieces.  She screamed and I came in, and we watched the glass continue to break down into smaller pieces for the next 3-4 minutes.
justification: The glass scale broke but no one was injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer's wife was sitting on the chair for about 2 minutes when the chair collapsed and the consumer's wife fell to the floor. The consumer states the chair has one leg in the front, one leg in the back, and one leg on each side. The consumer states that the legs on the side broke. The consumer states the plastic part which connects to the wheel broke in half. The consumer indicated that the plastic is flimsy and cheap. 

The consumer then visited Ocean State Job Lot, where he purchased the chair and informed them of the incident. The consumer was advised that they could not provide any assistance. The consumer then contacted the firm (888-233-7887) and left a voice mail informing them of the incident. The consumer has not received a call back yet.

Injury information:  Sore back
justification: The consumer's wife suffered a sore back from the chair collapse, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Purchased a Sylvania OSRAM LED light bulb from Lowes and installed in a 5 light ceiling light fixture with glass shrouds.  The fixture is open at the top providing access to insert and remove a bulb.  I consider this to be a non-enclosed light fixture.   
The bulb bears the following specifcations: OSRAM 8.5 W LED A19 5000K E26 5000K 800 lumens 8.5 W 120V 60Hz 77 mA.
On Monday 18 July 2016, while seated at our dining table we noticed a flicker or surge from that light fixture.  This was soon followed by a loud and smoke as the top part of the Sylvania LED bulb blew away from its metal screw-in base.   The bulb landed on our dining room table.  The bulb remained intact.  The metal screw-in portion of the bulb was easily removed from the fixture.  The base of the bulb ÃÂ e.g. heat sink (ceramic material ?) remained  very hot for several minutes.
We consulted the following web site: http://www.saferproducts.gov/.  We noted 56 similar complaints filed by consumers.  In our opinion, this product is not safe and may have not been subjected to rigorous testing.  We recommend other consumers contact the manufacturer and file similar reports.  We will not use this bulb in our home.
justification: The incident involved a bulb malfunction causing smoke and a loud noise, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] LED [REDACTED] base bulb exploded. 

I purchased several [REDACTED] base [REDACTED] LED 60w replacement 7w LED light bulbs in late March of 2016. I installed these bulbs in the light kit of a 15 year old Casablanca ceiling fan with Intellitouch controls. That control system uses a wall mounted controller to operate all the functions of the fan and the lights. For the lights that includes on and off and dimming through 6 levels of brightness. 

A few days ago while all four lights in the light kit were on (all four contain LED bulbs) one of those bulbs exploded showering glass and tiny pieces of the base containing the electronics all over the area under the fan. All the pieces were tiny pieces and we swept them up and discarded them in our trash.

incident_description:
I purchased the Jaclyn Smith Addison patio set 6/13.  My children and I were in the house and heard a noise outside. Our table shattered into a million pieces. I am so thankful that we were not eating outside tonight. What a disaster this could have been. Kmart gave me the run around on the phone for 2 1/2 hours. It is a hazard and has been for years. It should have been pulled off the market years before I bought it.

incident_description:
(6/5/16 Estimated) The consumer indicated that the chair is slightly leaned back at an angle. The consumer was in the chair for about 20 minutes when the rear left leg broke and the consumer fell to the floor. The consumer states that she did not sustain an injury. The consumer noticed that the leg broke right under the seat. 

The consumer indicated that the first time she used the chair she felt the chair was unstable. The consumer states that she used the chair 4 other times and each time she used it she felt the chair was unstable. The consumer believes the rear legs were spreading apart when she would sit in the chair.

The consumer contacted the store where she purchased the chair to request a refund but she was advised that it was past the 30 days and she could not receive a refund. 

The consumer weighs 210 lbs.

The consumer believes the chair has poor quality plastic and a poor design which make the chair unsafe.
justification: The consumer fell but did not sustain an injury, and the chair's instability was noted multiple times prior to the incident.

incident_description:
On January 3, 2016 I purchased the McLeland Design Ashdale 5-pc. Patio Set from Fingerhut.  The packaged arrived in the middle of January and was stored inside at the warehouse in my office (Las Vegas, NV) until the middle of April 2016.  In April, I assembled the furniture at my residence where it was stored and used outside.  On June 30, 2016, I was sitting in one of the four chairs (which comes with the set when) when the chair suddenly collapsed.  I fell to the ground striking my head and elbow while landing on my tailbone.  When I looked carefully at the chair, it appears the welds to the chairs had become rusted underneath the chair.  The rust was not visible from the outside, and was only visible from the inside.  

I immediately contacted Fingerhut and reported the damage as well as the fact I was hurt.  Their response was that this fell outside of the refund period.  

The rust on this was concealed, and this seriously is an accident waiting to happen.  The retailer manufactures this furniture themselves, and it is obvious they have no interest in dealing with this problem.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from a collapsed chair due to concealed rust, indicating a potential manufacturing defect.

incident_description:
on 5/25/2016 Sears delivered my Garden Oasis 7 pc Rockford outdoor dining set. We put it out on our deck by our pool. Yesterday, 7/14/2016 I was in the garage and heard a loud pop. I walked out to the pool and the entire glass top of the table had shattered into 1000's of pieces. glass everywhere. I am still vacumming up glass. there was nothing on the table and nobody on the deck except the table and chairs in the sun. I called sears and was transferred around to 4 different people and disconnected twice. Sears told me they will not accept a return and the manufacturer only wanted to sell me a new top for over 200 dollars delivered. I am disputing the charge with my credit card company but that may go nowhere. 
I am done with sears after being a customer for 50 years. And before Sears Holdings replies with their [REDACTED] cut and paste response to call customer care let me reply. I have already done that, it is a waste of time. SEARS does not care about it's customers or their safety. this is not the sears of old. 
I have no choice now but to take them to small claims court to try and recoup my losses. but I certainly wish CPSC will let people know about these dangerous glass tables and make SEARS stop importing them from CHINA.

incident_description:
CFL lamp bulb  in kitchen ceiling installed June 2016. Suddenly, after power returned after loss during thunderstorm the outer glass shell (only) separated from the lamp and fell onto the kitchen center island, shattering the glass envelope all over the kitchen floor.  Small children 5 and 7, were present.

Units fluorescent tube, etc,still intact and working in the ceiling after this.

UL Listed E149698 (File number) Lamp 61Y6

I have the remains and some pieces of the broken glass envelope.
