incident_description:
(06/17/2016) The consumer stated that the product began off gassing chemicals as soon as it was delivered to her home and removed from the box. The furniture has a sulphur-type odor.

The consumer stated that she has headaches, dizziness, and sore throat whenever she is in the vicinity of the desk.

No medical attention required.

(06/19/2016) The consumer contacted the firm and was advised that the shipper would be contacted to return to the home to pick up the furniture. The consumer asked if anyone else had complained about the smell. She was advised that no one had complained.

The consumer was offered a refund for the desk.
justification: The consumer reported headaches, dizziness, and sore throat, indicating injury, but no medical attention was required. The issue appears isolated as no other complaints were reported.

incident_description: I was unloading the trash and the black rim came off. I felt around the trash can lid and rim and cut my finger on something sharp. I'm not sure exactly what it was. Then I became worried that my 7 yr old son could of been changing the trash and this could of happened to him. So I looked online to see if there was something to repair it or if others have had the same thing happen. That's when I read there is a recall on this trashcan. We were never notified by costco.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cut finger) and there is a known recall, indicating potential for similar incidents.

incident_description: In June 2014, the Ikea Hemnes 6-drawer dresser tipped over ontop of our 3 1/2 year old daughter. She was opening and closing the drawers and as she opened the large top drawer the dresser tipped and fell on top of her. Luckily the bottom drawers were closed so it provided a small space for her so the dresser didn't pin her beneath. She received a bruise and scrape on her cheek from the drawer pull as it fell onto her. My husband was in the same room and pulled it off of her immediately. At the time, we didn't think anything of this incident and made sure to secure it to the wall after that. However, now that we've become more aware of the Ikea recall we realized that this incident was related to our experience.
justification: The child received a bruise and scrape, indicating an injury, and the incident was caused by a known hazard (unsecured dresser).

incident_description: When using Carex Adjustable Shower Seat legs twisted and seat collapsed in shower. My weight falls in the mid range of limit marked. It was not set at highest leg setting. There are plastic wing nuts on bottom that hold legs on and the center one was loose upon examination after fall. Due to the nature of shower chair use by elderly and disabled I fear that the nut is something not checked upon every use.
justification: The seat collapsed, indicating an incident, and the user's concern about elderly and disabled users suggests potential for injury.

incident_description:
I have had nothing but trouble from the very beginning when I purchased this product. I can never get the trash bag out without a rip in the bag because it is poorly designed and have had to use TWO trash bags each time. 
The "collar" on the back which surrounds a hole, has NEVER stayed in place, and I have continually had to physically replace it. Today, on July 9, 2016, I was lifting the trash out of the bin and I was having difficulty, and the "collar" fell off and I didn't realize it, and was struggling with getting the trash out and I cut myself pretty bad on the sharp edges. 

I have been bleeding continuously for over two hours and am contemplating going to the doctor because it is so painful and will not stop! I went online to see if there were any other complaints and found I was NOT alone!!!!!!!!!! Anyone with the product should be AWARE, discontinue IMMEDIATE use, and be reimbursed! I have never seen a worse product in my life! I now I am painfully paying the price. This company has NO RIGHT to continue to sell this product! I bought this awhile ago, but still have the receipt as proof of purchase. All involved in this product line need to be warned!
justification: The user suffered a significant injury (cut) that required medical attention consideration, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurring issues with the product suggest a likely occurrence likelihood.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his wall mount used for his 63 inch flat screen television, both wall mount and television were purchased June 1st, 2010 from .com. 
The caller noticed no problems with the wall mount for his television until February 24th, 2016 when he and his wife were in their bedroom watching the television when it came crashing down and they saw that it was due to the wall mount's two circular discs that were supposed to support the television broke.

The direction/guidance for the wall mount reads that it is guaranteed to support televisions up to 65 inches and the caller's television is 63 inches.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer February 25th, 2016 and spoke with [REDACTED] who advised him that there are no recalls and no warranty which provides the consumer calling no assistance from them.

This caller is a pediatrician and states that he is contacting CPSC because this television fell with great force in a split second and if this incident were to be repeated where a child was nearby then the results could be disastrous.

He would like this wall mount recalled with remedy being refund and he would like for the manufacturer to be held financially responsible for his television and the wall mount.  I referred the caller to the FTC and the CFPB for this request.
justification: The incident involved a television falling due to a faulty wall mount, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is possible as the wall mount failed under expected use conditions.

incident_description: We purchased a Sal Benicarlo Platform Bedroom Set in 2015.  It has a lighted headboard with three halogen bulb lights in a recessed area in the headboard which can be turned on and off.  A pillow was propped against the headboard while the lights were on.  The pillow began to burn and smolder, with a burned hole in the pillowcase and the pillow itself.  Our guest smelled the smoke and shut off the lights after noting the halogen bulbs were extremely hot.  These bulbs are much too hot to be near linens and are an extreme fire danger.
justification: The incident involved a pillow catching fire due to hot halogen bulbs, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I bought two bunk beds in July 2007 that are made by Coaster Co of America based in Santa Fe Springs, CO for a remote cabin I own in Colorado.  Two weeks ago, a cousin was stepping off the top bunk when the ladder broke.  His leg was jabbed by the remaining piece of step as he fell.  He should've gotten stitches, but this happened in the middle of the night and we were an hour away from emergency services.  So we just bandaged him and let it go.  BTW, he is a retired doctor.

As we inspected the ladder, we saw that the one step that broke had a knot that went completely through the board.  The break was along this knot.  

After this, my brother reported that several of the slats that support the bunk beds had broken or were breaking.  We confirmed this and noticed they all had the same issues with knots going through the boards.  A bunk bed falling could cause injury, esp if the upper bed falls on someone sleeping below.

Since this happened on a ladder step and on multiple struts, it seems to be systemic to me.  I have pictures to show the defective boards.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring potential stitches, and the systemic issue with the bunk beds suggests a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description:
7/11/12  Toxic off gassing Simmons Beautyrest Black Vivian Plush  for past 5 months, 11 days. 

Wife has suffered with respiratory problems, neurological problems, breathing problems, auditory problems and other medical problems sinus clogged, burning throat, depression, insomnia, ear pain, dizziness, aural fullness; sore throat; headaches daily; instability walking; driving difficulty; joint pain, inability to perform daily household activities; red swollen eyes; difficulty breathing; congested sinus; chemical taste in mouth; nausea; burning nose and more medical symptoms.

As I began to assemble them I discovered the bolts supplied to hold the pieces together are defective. Just trying to screw the bolts into place caused the bolt head to detach from the threaded body of the bolt. If this happened when someone was using the chair it could collapse. I have a Quantum Black Mesh Mid Back Chair (SKU #510-830) purchased from Office Depot in 2009.

I found a sheared-off bolt head lying on the floor recently and hunted around but could not identify where it came from. A month later, while I was leaning back in the chair, the second bolt also sheared off. The chair back fell off and with no warning at all I fell backwards off the chair.

I was (fortunately) sitting at a desk. My knees hit the underside of the desk as I fell backwards, stopping my fall. My back is really hurt but it kept me from falling and splitting my head on the floor.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hurt back) but no death, and the likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions (bolts shearing off).

Needless to say with this current recall i will be returning both of our dressers.

Caller stated that her chandelier top part (ring/loop that screws into the lighting) broke, the bottom part was replaced as a being included in a recall.  She stated that the chandelier was hanging by the wire.  There were no injuries or property damages.

Caller stated that she attempted to contact the recall hotline for original recall but was informed that they were a 3rd party company for the manufacturer.

Caller feels that this chandelier is unsafe and should be reported.

incident_description: A young man was sitting in one of the chairs and the base broke and he fell to the deck. hitting his knee and elbow.
justification: The young man fell and hit his knee and elbow, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased a SwimWays spring float Papasan pool float chair at Target San Rafael on June 26, 2016, brought it home and in front of [REDACTED], my friend, attempted to inflate it for the first time.  The one way plastic valve which is the size of a pencil eraser detached and I swallowed the piece.  I attempted to cough it up but if went down my esophagus, causing irritation and discomfort.  I went to the emergency room at [REDACTED] and was seen by Dr. [REDACTED] who did a chest x-ray to make sure the plastic piece was not in my lungs.  I was told to take a stool softener and omeprazole for acid reflux to help the irritation in my esophagus and wait for it to pass through my bowels and be excreted.  I never found the plastic piece in my bowel movements.  If the plastic one way valve is still in my GI tract, I am at risk for abscess or bowel obstruction.  I have been very apprehensive for the past three days.  This is very upsetting.  I have never swallowed a foreign body before.
justification: The incident caused physical injury (esophageal irritation and discomfort) requiring emergency medical attention, but no long-term harm was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as swallowing a detached valve is not a common occurrence.

incident_description:
Purchased an Utilitech LED light bulb from Lowe's approximately a year ago.  Trying to convert my house over to LED bulbs for energy usage.  I bought a total of 15 bulbs that day.  2 of the bulbs were put into a Lowe's ceiling light assembly with glass bowl covering the bulbs.

On late Sunday night/early Monday morning (12:35 a.m.), June 28th, 2016 one of the bulbs caught on fire while the light was on.  You could see flames flickering inside the bowl until it filled up with black smoke and ash particles.  I turned off the power to the light and the fire went out before having to do any secondary extinguishing.

After approximately 15 minutes, I took apart the light assembly and removed it from the ceiling to verify that no damage had been done to any wiring or the ceiling.  Wiring and ceiling were OK.

One of the bulbs was melted just above the socket area.  No other damage was noticed except for smoke and ash damage from the burning.

I have went online to try and find information on the product, but it is a Lowe's specific product.  Currently working with a Lowe's manager at my local store to get replaced and escalate the issue.
justification: The bulb caught fire but was contained without injury or significant damage, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it's a rare occurrence for LED bulbs to catch fire.

incident_description:
IKEA MALM Dressers:

We purchased two MALM dressers from IKEA back in 2005/2006. One was the taller one, and one shorter one. We anchored the taller one, and didn't think the shorter one would need anchoring. One evening, as my daughter was putting her clothes away, she had opened two drawers at the same time, the dresser tipped over and almost fell on her. We had a bed near the dresser, so the bed stopped the dresser from falling completely on her. We had put a small 19-in TV (not a flat screen) on top. The TV slid down as well. I thought maybe the weight would help keep the dresser from tipping. We were wrong on both thoughts. Again, we were lucky to have that bed nearby to stop the dresser and TV. If there had been no bed, it would have fallen on her along with the TV. We anchored it right away after that incident.
justification: The dresser tipped over but was stopped by the bed, preventing injury, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible given the circumstances described.

incident_description: Product is a Sylvania compact fluorescent lightbulb, 13W 60 Hz CFL13EL/MINITWIST 3000K. Bulb was installed in a bathroom light fixture for years with no issues. On morning of 6/21/2016 bulb began to flicker, then filled entire room with acrid vapor or smoke, which stopped when switch was turned off. Despite quick ventilation of room, occupant was admitted to emegency department later in day with nausea/vomiting and diagnosed with acute mercury toxicity.

The mount that was screwed into the TV broke in half causing the 70.1 lbs TV to fall.  We were fortunate that no one was in the house at the time as our children like to stand on the cabinet below where the TV hangs and point to which shows they want to watch.

justification: The incident resulted in chemical burns, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: 13 months after purchase the seat bottoms to my patio furniture are giving out when someone is sitting on them. The weight limit of the chairs is 250 pounds, I only weigh 119 pounds so I am no where near exceeding the weight limit. The chairs are also only used occasionally and on a seasonal basis, so they are not falling apart from overuse. The first chair broke exactly 12 months after purchase while a guest was sitting in it and our guest ended up with several bruises. A month after that I fell through the chair and suffered from several cuts, scrapes and bruises all over my body.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bruises, cuts, scrapes) to two individuals, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the chairs failed under normal use conditions but not all chairs failed immediately.

incident_description:
We purchased two Garden Treasures White Patio Rocking Chairs, Item # 402024, Model # TA7002 from Lowe's last year. These are pre-painted wooden rocking chairs which were used on a covered porch. While sitting in them yesterday (June 18, 2016), the chair I was sitting in began to tip backwards. As it tipped, I grabbed my wife in the chair next to me to stop my fall. Unfortunately, her char also tipped. During the fall to the ground my head struck the wall behind me and my left elbow struck the ground. My wife's fall was arrested somewhat by a planter and she only struck an elbow on the ground and one leg on the chair. 

Once we picked ourselves up we noted that the runners had broken where the rear leg inserted. It is obvious that the runner has very little structure remaining due to the size of the hole required for the leg spindle. As a result of the fall, I sustained a moderate size hematoma on my head and now have a sore elbow and a very sore neck. My wife has a sore elbow and a bruise on her leg.
justification: Both individuals sustained injuries (hematoma, sore elbow, neck pain, bruises) from the chairs tipping over, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with properly manufactured furniture.

incident_description: I purchased a Motion Sensor Trash Bin from Costco.  While changing the garbage bag in the Motion Sensor Trash Bin the little black piece on the back of the garbage bin continue to pop out.  I took some trash out of the trash bin and have cut my middle finger on the right hand three times.  This continue to happens many times when changing trash out of the bin.  Today I have a serious cut on my right middle finger and I am going to take the trash bin back to Costco today.

The mess seems even more great this time than last and undoubtedly will be picking out pieces wedged in between the deck boards.  This is supposed to be tempered safety glass, but it is simply not cutting it for this patio set.  It's very infuriating to have this happen not once, but twice and I can only hope Meijer has wised up and stopped selling this subpar product.

The consumer stated that his 5 year old daughter was playing behind the loveseat.

His daughter put her foot underneath the loveseat from behind. Her foot went in between two bars. When the loveseat was reclined, the two bars crushed her ankle.

The consumer's daughter was treated at home for her injuries. Does not appear that she has a fracture.

The consumer plans to contact the manf regarding the incident.

justification: The chandelier fell but there is no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description:
This caller purchased a king sized mattress  from retailer January 15th, 2016, it was delivered January 25th, 2016 in the state of Washington.

After airing the mattress out for approximately 8 hours she put sheets and bedding on the and slept on night then read on it for maybe two hours but while she was reading she noticed that whatever side of her body was touching the mattress she felt a burning sensation everyplace that her skin touched the mattress. Her eyes are also burning.

Her husband tried sleeping on the mattress February 2nd, 3rd, and 4th, 2016 and said that it was causing his skin to tingle.
The odor coming from this mattress was like that of old oil or greasy chemical smells.
They arranged for the mattress to be picked up.

Neither the caller or her husband have obtained medical assistance yet but since their skin symptoms are not going away they plan to make an appointment today.

She said her blood pressure has never gone up a down but has fluctuated greatly since the exposure to this mattress.

She contacted the retailer but not the manufacturer yet, however she does plan to contact them.

She arranged for the mattress to be picked up but declined a replacement from the retailer.
justification: The caller and her husband experienced burning and tingling sensations, indicating physical injury, but no death or severe medical intervention was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a sleeper chair from the Cindy Crawford "Bellingham" brand at Rooms To Go, JW Clay Blvd, Charlotte NC. The problem is that, with the bed extended, when the user sits at the spot where the bed pillow normally is located, as when reading in bed, the head of the bed goes down and the foot end of the bed goes up, to almost vertical, like a see saw. This dumps the user into the chair cavity. If the user was child or toddler, the small body size would allow the child/toddler to drop completely into the cavity of the chair frame, the foot of the bed would slam back down against the floor, the the child could be completely entrapped inside the chair frame, or possibly get caught by the neck/body between the head end of the mattress and the chair frame. An adult with limited abilities, such as the infirm or elderly, might not be able to extricate him/herself from the cavity. Injuries could occur. The display chair that I sat on in the store had this problem, but the salesman was very apologetic and said that the particular display chair had a defect but if I purchased this type of sleeper chair mine would not have this problem. Other brands of sleeper chairs do not have this problem. When I called the store to complain, they did some investigating and told me that ALL Cindy Crawford sleepers have this same issue, they are all manufactured by H.M. Richards company in Mississippi, and this manufacturer undoubtedly follows all industry standards and it is therefore NOT the legal, moral, or ethical responsibility of R2G to deal with the problem. I requested a repair, the addition of some sort of locking mechanism or other "fix", but they refused. I feel it is my responsibility to report this to you, as I think this is a dangerous product. The sale of these sleepers should stop immediately, and the ones already sold should be recalled. It would not be a tremendous engineering challenge to design a locking mechanism or other "fix" to prevent the head of the bed from dropping, and I am stunned that the retailer refused to investigate or contact the manufacturer. I hope your organization can deal with this before injuries or deaths occur. Thank you.
justification: The description indicates potential for injury, especially to children or the elderly, due to the chair's design flaw, but no actual injuries or deaths have been reported yet.

We were simply serving the children a snack. We will email you the exchange between us and the company. Our concern is that this could happen at other centers. We are removing every single Toddler Table from our center as the event was so traumatic. We just keeping thinking what could have happened and we don't want it to happen to any other children at any other center. We will send the photo of the table.

incident_description: Late in the evening in our nursery I was feeding my 7 month old infant in the Graco Parker Glider. She was taking a break from eating and I had her over my shoulder for burping when I simultaneously heard wood snap and we went crashing to the floor. To my shock and horror my little one went tumbling head first onto the floor, gravity taking her all the way over my shoulder onto the ground and tumbling her somersault fashion end over end. My wrists were injured from the fall and she was crying inconsolably. I had to keep watch on her for 24 hours for signs of concussion or other neurological problems. I am appalled that a product purchased new, just 7 months earlier, would break in this manner. I am a light weight person and we were not even rocking much when this occurred. There was no creaking or other indicators that the chair might break apart in this manner. I am concerned for other caregivers and their little ones should this happen to them. I ended up flat on my back and my baby on her head. It could've caused major injury to us both. I am now without a nursing chair and a quiet environment to feed my little one, and worried about getting another chair that could be a safety hazard. We use the chair for all feedings while at home and it was part of a calming routine for my baby. Now she is having difficulties sleeping and eating without the glider in her own room.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to both the caregiver and the infant, and potential for more severe harm, but the likelihood of such a failure in a new product is unlikely.

incident_description:
My husband and I woke up at 3AM to a burning wire / plastic smell. After some investigation, the Biddeford electric blanket that I purchased for my 8 year old son was melting as he was sleeping. It burned holes in the blanket itself, sheets and charred his mattress pad and mattress. We bought 2 of these blankets from Kohl's for Christmas, so they were only used for 5 months. 

When we saw the blanket was overheated, the display showed "E", which usually meant error (like it was disconnected from the blanket). When we touched his bed, it was burning up in a spot at the foot of his bed. When we pulled back his comforter, the blanket had melted onto itself a pile with exposed wires blackened by bits of the blanket. 

We removed all electric blankets from all our beds, then I photographed the damage in the morning. I was shocked at the damage. My sons feet were inches from melted plastics and electrified wires. His mattress, mattress pad, sheet and comforter were damaged. The blanket got so overheated that the color from his sheets and comforter transferred to the blanket itself and appeared "bleached" in the spots that got overheated. We have always been careful monitoring their use of electric blankets, not leaving them on for too long, not keeping them on high, etc., but for a blanket less than 5 months old that originally retailed for $120, this is very scary. 

I left a message for Biddeford this morning and returned the blankets to Kohl's, talking to [REDACTED], the store manager. She helped me file an incident report with Kohl's and I am expecting a return call from their corporate office by Tuesday. I am so thankful that our 2nd grader was not injured and hope that others have not experienced this or more critical injuries. This could have caused a bed fire, house fire or caused critical injury to our family. Very scary. We will never use an electric blanket again.
justification: The electric blanket overheated and caused significant damage to bedding materials, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I purchased three Adesso Pisces Torchiere floor lamps and two Adesso Piedmont Torchiere floor lamps approximately two weeks ago.  The lamps each hold two 150-watt light bulbs, and the Piedmont lamp also has a third bulb about halfway down the shaft of the lamp which serves as a reading light (a 60-watt bulb).  My complaint deals only with the top two 15-watt bulbs and the plastic lamp shades surrounding those two bulbs.  When properly assembled with bulbs installed and both bulbs turned on, the light bulbs are placed in too close proximity to the plastic lamp shade and thus one bulb inevitably burns through the lamp shade causing smoking and smoldering.  Although the Pisces and Piedmont lamps have different shaped shades, both styles of shades have been burned through (2 of the Pisces and 1 of the Piedmont) by one bulb.  I noticed the first incident when I noticed a large  yellow-ringed hole in one lamp shade; I noticed the other two incidents because I was standing closer to the lamp shades, and I smelled the smoking.  I have since removed the lamp shades from all five lamps, but I have preserved them.  I have pictures of the burned shades for your reference and have attached them to this report.  I am also willing to turn over all five lamps to you for testing as necessary.  The manufacturer has requested that I turn over the lamps to them, but I am unwilling to do so, as I do not believe that the manufacturer is acting in good faith.  I am not looking for any compensation; I am just seriously concerned about this fire hazard.  I find it very hard to believe that the manufacturer was unaware through product testing of a result which I, as a consumer, was able to discover in under two weeks with only five samples.
justification: The incident involves smoking and smoldering due to bulb proximity to plastic shades, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I have had THREE different Philips 500 watt Halogen bulbs FRACTURE and two of them EXPLODED in my outdoor lighting fixtures.  I have two of these fixtures that burn from dusk to dawn on the front of my residence showcasing it in light at night.  I have used the 500 watt bulbs for many years (the fixtures are rated and designed for these bulbs), from different manufacturers without the issues I have encountered with the Philips bulbs.  This is what happened:
In early November 2015, I replaced a burned out bulb in one of the fixtures with a Philips 500 watt halogen bulb.  Within a few days, it burned out and upon removal was discovered it had fracture marks in the glass on both ends.  A different Philips bulb was installed, and again a few days later, it too burned out.  Upon removal it was discovered that one end of this bulb was completely black and had fused molten glass and metal to the fixture pin, ruining the lighting fixture.  The other end of the bulb had the same fracture marks as the first bulb.  I contacted Philips and they requested both bulbs and the fixture, and all were subsequently sent to Shanghai to their testing facility.  The finding was as follows:  "fixture pin has signs of oxidation that caused high resistance and lamp burnt at the pinch point."  I was told to regularly polish the pins of the fixture to stop this issue.  My lighting fixture was not returned, nor was I compensated for the bulbs.
While this lighting fixture was being analyzed for months, I purchased a new lighting fixture as a replacement.  Another Philips bulb was installed, and within a few weeks it too burned out.  Upon removal it too was discovered that it was fractured on both ends and subsequently broke along these fracture points.  It was truly a blessing that the bulb did not damage the new fixture.  A [REDACTED] bulb was installed and has been burning nightly with no issues whatsoever since November 2015.
I can understand that perhaps somehow oxidation might have caused the damage to the older lighting fixture but that does not explain the problem occurring again in a brand new three week old fixture.  Philips completely ignores ALL queries regarding the problem in the new fixture and will not address the issue about the problem occurring in the new fixture with me at all.  They just talk about oxidation on the old fixture.  They keep telling me they consider this issue serious yet months have gone by and the matter has not been addressed fully. I contacted you because I am truly concerned that in the right environment, these fracturing and exploding bulbs could be dangerous to children or pets, or could even possibly start a deadly fire.
justification: The incident involves bulb fractures and explosions causing fixture damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

We cannot sleep in the bed that this headboard is attached to because our sinuses get irritated.  Again, Vaughn-Bassett says not to worry.

Clearly the folks at Vaughn-Bassett seem to take this incident lightly...hopefully you can help.

incident_description: We have the Ikea Mammut Wardrobe in the blue color. We've had it for about 3 years my son is now old enough to use it and we have been using it as a toy storage now that he's older instead of hanging his clothes. He keeps his little cars in the bottom drawer and while playing opening the drawer and playing in it the whole wardrobe fell over on top of him. I luckily heard him scream and was able to run to him and lifted it off of him. We looked up the model to see if there was a recall and all we found were pre cautionary directions to secure it to the wall which we then did but prior to the incident we didn't realise this was a issue. We will never buy from Ikea again because literally every piece of furniture has the same caution and says to secure it to the wall. After this experience I am scared and will stay away and heed the warning as the furniture. I am blessed to have heard his scream as well as happy it wasn't my 2 year old he wouldn't have been strong enough to hold it up from crushing him. Luckily we just had to clean up a little blood from the top of his head and use some neosporin. I just wanted to inform everyone else of this. I got if secured to the wall but I don't believe it will hold up for ever with all the opening and closing of the drawers.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (cleaning up blood and applying neosporin), but no severe harm or death occurred.

incident_description:
The bedroom furniture set was delivered to the consumer's house on 03/30/16.

The consumer noticed an odor coming off of the furniture set. The consumer left the windows open to air out the odor.

The consumer had to close the windows on 04/02/16 because of rainy weather. The consumer stated that the odor became stronger after she closed the windows. The consumer experienced health symptoms like burning eyes, scratchy throat, dry nose (with blood sometimes), and mild headache. 

The consumer stated that 3 other people who came over to her house has noticed the strong odor. 

The consumer is unable to sleep in the room.

The consumer contacted the retailer on 04/04/16. The consumer spoke with [REDACTED] and explained the situation to her. [REDACTED] informed the consumer that she will contact Liberty in regards to the situation and get back to her. [REDACTED] contacted the consumer back to notify her what the company said. The consumer was informed that the company does not use any products that would cause chemical odor to come off of the furniture set. 

When the consumer went on the firm's website, she noticed that the materials being used in this furniture set can have chemicals like formaldehyde.

The consumer asked the retailer if the company could come out and test the furniture. The consumer was informed that the company would not offer that.

The consumer spoke to the manager of the store on 04/06/16. The manager understood the issue and asked the consumer to keep the area ventilated for a few more days. He stated that sometimes if the furniture is left in the packaging for too long in the storage room, it can emit stronger odors. The consumer was asked to ventilate the area for another week. If the odor does not go away, the manager stated that they will provide a replacement set. The consumer does not know if she feels comfortable getting another similar set.

The consumer has kept the area well ventilated but is still not feeling any better. The symptoms still persist.
justification: The consumer experienced health symptoms like burning eyes, scratchy throat, and headaches, indicating injury from chemical exposure.

incident_description: I purchased a memory foam topper from Overstock.com, received on 14 April 2016.  We purchased Comfort Dreams m-cool 4 inch memory foam mattress topper, manufactured by FXI in Auborn, Indiana. The product had no instructions but I assumed I had to to let it air out for several hours, which I did.  After about 10 hours we placed it on our bed and slept on it.  After two nights of sleeping on this topper, both my wife and I had headache, nausea, and light headedness and elevated diastolic blood pressure, which we assume is from the strong odor emitted from the memory foam topper.  We called the manufacturer but they would not release any information about what type of chemicals might be emitted because it is "proprietary".  I am concerned about what is emitted because I know there are carcinogens used in producing memory foam.  I want to know if this product is hazardous to my health but the manufacturer doesn't seem interested in helping me with this.
justification: The incident resulted in headaches, nausea, and elevated blood pressure, indicating injury (severity 3). Similar health effects from memory foam odors are possible but not extremely common (likelihood 3).

incident_description: On January 2, 2016, I pulled out the kitchen garbage bag from our EKO Motion Sensor Waste Can.  When I was putting in a new garbage can, I sliced the tip of my middle finger on the sharp edge of the hand hold opening on the side of the trash can.  I couldn't get the bleeding to stop so I went to one a Renown Urgent Care center, where they referred me to a Renown Emergency Room.  I received four (4) stitches.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention (stitches), indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of a sharp edge causing the injury.

incident_description:
The caller may have purchased the light bulbs about 1-2 years ago. 

The caller stated that he had 7 of these light bulbs installed in 2 separate fixtures in his kitchen.

The glue that holds the glass and the wire in the metal base appears to have failed. The light bulbs were hanging by live wire. The caller stated that he noticed this when he went to change one of the light bulbs. The light bulb flashed (electric sparks) while trying to change it. After that, he inspected the light fixture and noticed that the 7 light bulbs were hanging by wire.

The caller had to use a plier to take out the base of the light bulbs from the light fixture.

The caller contacted the company on 3/14/16 regarding the incident. The company representative apologized for the issue and informed him that they would provide a refund for the unused bulbs. The caller has 9 packages (4 light bulbs in each) that have been unused. The caller offered to send back the failed light bulbs to the company for an inspection but the company asked him to keep it. 

The caller stated that the glue on the light bulbs was crumbly and fell out on the kitchen counter-top. 

The caller stated that he also had one of a different brand light bulb installed in the same fixture. That light bulb did not have any issues.
justification: The incident involved electric sparks and light bulbs hanging by live wires, posing a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(03/01/2016) The consumer stated that she had taken the old bulb out of the lamp and put the 3-way bulb in the lamp next to her bed. Within 15 minutes, the bulb exploded. The consumer stated that the bulb has three tubes but only one of the tubes blew out. 

There were no injuries.

(03/16/2016)The consumer contacted the firm. She spoke to a representative named [REDACTED]. The consumer asked her if there were any reports on the bulb. The representative told her that she may have heard of one.

The consumer asked to speak to the supervisor whose name was [REDACTED]. The consumer asked the supervisor if he was aware of the danger of bulb. She was advised that they had not heard of the product exploding. 

The consumer was advised that the company would send her a pre-paid box to return the product. She was also offered coupons to buy new bulbs.

The consumer added GE has sent a box for the return of the bulb, but she has not sent the bulb to GE. The consumer also noted the bulb is still in her possession along with 2 unused bulbs, and photos are included.
justification: The bulb exploded but there were no injuries, and the incident was reported without further harm.

incident_description: Several months ago I replaced 2 Bulbrite 150 watt halgoen bulbs Q150CL/EDT, item #614151.  One burned out fairly quickly.  Today the other exploded sending shards of red hot glass around the room.  The glass ruined a sofa and the wall to wall carpeting by burning it.  luckily no one was hit by the glass shards.
justification: The incident involved an exploding bulb causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the description of one bulb burning out quickly and the other exploding.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a queen bed that is labeled Formaldehyde Compliant with phase 2, however the odor has remained since 2012 when she purchased the bed and dresser.

Manufactured by  in California on January 28th, 2012.

The caller said that she has been becoming ill since the furniture was delivered on January 30th, 2012 with nausea, regurgitation, sinus issues, back ache, stomach ache.

December 2015 the caller and her grown daughter were on the bed talking when it fell and caused the daughter's head to become caught between the pillow and the end.

The caller had to push the bed down to release the daughter who had a couple of scratches.

The caller has contacted the manufacturer who advised that he is not responsible because he purchased the bed and dresser from another manufacturer.

The caller is asking that the retailer or manufacturer take possession of the bedroom furniture and reimburse her.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (scratches) to the daughter when the bed collapsed, and the caller has reported ongoing health issues since 2012.

incident_description: I put in a new light bulb and turned on the lights. After about 2 to 3 minutes of being on, the bulb exploded and glass shards came raining down throughout the entire bathroom and all over me, as I was standing underneath it. I have used the other bulbs that came in the same box, but they didn't and have not exploded.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb with glass shards, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description:
This consumer is reporting Ashley living room furniture he purchased from retailer on January 25th, 2016  in Georgia.
The CafÃÂ© colored furniture which consists of one sofa and a love seat was delivered the first week in February 2016.

He said that he didn't notice a strong odor for a couple of days but then the odor became very strong causing his nose, throat and eyes to burn.

He said that the odor has gotten a bit lighter and the burning isn't as bad as it was a few days ago but that he wanted to report it due to the discomforting thought that it could be making him ill.

There are no injuries being reported

He has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them
justification: The consumer reported discomfort from a strong odor but no injuries occurred, fitting the 'Incident, No Injury' category.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a defective product designed specifically for children. My three year old son has a Westwood Baby Brookline bed; it is a convertible bed that we converted from a crib to toddler bed, and finally 11 months ago to a double bed. We used the required Westwood converter rail and followed all of the instructions. Last night, the bed collapsed with no warning. There is a piece of wood on the converter rail the holds up the slats, and it simply broke off. We did not assemble this component. It was purchased approximately one year ago and has been in use only since May 2015. The piece itself had three screws and judging from how it fell only one of them was actually attaching it to the main rail.

This could have been incredibly dangerous. Westwood has not be very cooperative, saying simply that they have not received other reports of this but will send a replacement. This is very dangerous and is a serious accident waiting to happen. 

I have multiple pictures of the broken part. We were sitting on the bed at the time of the incident. The use was completely routine. 

I hit my foot on the railing as we fell down. It was sore and had a minor bruise. Either of us could have been much more hurt. Had the bed fallen while someone crawled under it (e.g., to get a toy), this would have been extremely dangerous. Similarly, had one of our cats been under the bed at the time they would have been killed.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (bruised foot) and had the potential for more severe harm, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the defective nature of the product and routine use.

incident_description: HAMPTON BAY patio furniture Fall River 7 pieces patio dining set. My wife was sitting in one of the chairs when it felt apart, my wife felt backward against the patio door. We bought this product from HOME DEPOT I reported it to them & they acted like they did not care. They told me to call HAMPTON BAY.
justification: The incident resulted in the wife falling backward against the patio door, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
After spending one night on my new IKEA mattress I awoke with:

Sore throat
Nasal passages swollen shut
Irritated sinuses
Headache
Nausea
Dizziness
Slurred speech

My girlfriend experienced:
Difficulty breathing
Hives
Nasal passages swollen shut
Irritated sinuses & respiratory system
Sore throat
Headache & dizziness
As she was walking home today at noon (left the bedroom at 9:30am) she got light-headed and everything started spinning.

Some hours after leaving the vicinity of the mattress, the symptoms started to clear up. We were both feeling much better by 5pm, 7 hours after awakening.
justification: The symptoms described, including difficulty breathing and hives, indicate a significant allergic reaction, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Our cat's tail was caught and entangled in the power recline mechanism on a Flexsteel Latitudes Collection power reclining sofa.  This was possible because there are no side guards on the mechanism - a serious safety defect that we were not aware of until this incident.  This resulted in serious injury to our cat, and ultimately amputation of his tail.  We also incurred injuries (cat bites) trying to remove the cat from the mechanism.  We could not extract the tail from the mechanism because it was so tightly caught and entangled, and instead had to remove the entire mechanism from the couch and bring it, with tail intertwined, to the veterinary emergency hospital.  I will attach pictures taken by the veterinary emergency hospital of the cat's tail in the mechanism.  There is no quick release on the mechanism itself, and no way to remove the mechanism from the couch other than to unbolt it - which took approximately 20 minutes and increased the trauma of the incident.  This power mechanism safety defect has the potential to injure other pets and even small children who's fingers would easily fit into the side opening of the mechanism. 

I contacted Flexsteel about the incident and safety defect.  I was transferred to their parts department who took down information, including our phone number, but said we needed to deal with the store where we bought the couch from regarding the incident.  I called the store (Rome Furniture in Gardner, MA) and was given a contact and email address to report the incident to.  I sent an email to the address provided, including a description of the incident and photos, 3 days ago.  We have not been contacted by either Flexsteel or Rome Furniture about the incident to date.
justification: The incident resulted in serious injury to the cat (tail amputation) and minor injuries to the owners (cat bites), warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is assessed as possible (3) given the described safety defect but lack of widespread reported incidents.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting a single bulb lamp she purchased from the store in Illinois around the August/September 2015 timeframe.

She noticed since just a couple of weeks after purchase that pieces were falling apart and she kept fixing it but then sometime around January 8th or 9h, 2016 she walked into her three year old son's room and saw that the light bulb base had fallen off the lamp and the light bulb was burning a hole in her son's dresser.

She immediately turned the lamp off then unplugged the lamp.  The lamp is not being used for fear of potential fire.

There are no injuries being reported.

The caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.

She is reporting this lamp and it's design as a potential fire and burn hazard.
justification: The incident involved a lamp malfunction causing a fire hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
My son had a pen and was drawing. He put the top part of the pen in his mouth, like many adults even do, and must have bit down inside the hollowed clip part where the plastic SCRIPTO logo was located. It had a little give to it so it ended up bouncing back and trapping part of his top lip inside the clip of the pen. He was bleeding and screaming. We called the ambulance whose paramedics would not take the pen off themselves but wanted to drive us to the ER where the doctors could figure out how to remove the pen from his lip. It took three doctors to pry the pen off of his lip. 

I contacted Scripto with this information. They seemed helpful at first and asked me to send along pictures and the pen itself since I had brought it home with me after it was removed from my son's lip. After I sent it, I waited to hear back. More than six months later with numerous unanswered/hang up phone calls to their person, [REDACTED], who handles these situations, I finally go ahold of him through Scripto. He told me he was not responsible for this, that he was sorry about my son, but that he couldn't help anymore, and that we would have to agree to disagree. I told him that I would have likes the respect for him to at least call me back and let me know this information since it had been more than six months. He said he was busy and had a lot to do. 

While Scripto itself is not making pens anymore, I just saw a University that had pens out at their booth in February 2016 with the same type of clip. If pen companies don't know about this clip, then they won't know about the dangers. They will continue making them, and more people could potentially get hurt.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the child's lip, requiring medical intervention, which justifies a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances required for the injury to occur.

incident_description:
I was screwing one of the new fluorescent bulbs into a fixture.  There was no resistance--it was going in easily, but I heard a crack as the bulb broke and a small splinter went into my finger.  Had I met resistance, I might have been grasping it more tightly and would have had a severe laceration.  I think these have mercury in them.

There are four loops to the bulb, and I was holding so that there was light pressure on all the loops.  Yet the top loop was the one that broke and I was hardly touching that part.
justification: The incident resulted in a small splinter injury from a broken bulb, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described circumstances.

incident_description: Cree 60 watt light LED light bulb outer shell exploded at base connection.  No injuries but this is second (i.e. 2 out of 6 installed in summer of 2014) of these bulbs to explode.  The first incident occurred last spring and I thought fluke and took it back to Home Depot which gave me a replacement bulb.  Not interested in replacing it with another Cree bulb.  The bulbs were/ are installed in vanity bathroom fixtures rated for 100 watt bulbs.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved an exploding light bulb, which is a safety concern. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) since this is the second occurrence out of six bulbs.

incident_description:
I purchased the youth mission chair  (http://www.youthchairstore.com/Product/youth-chairs/rustic-style-youth-mission-chair--cc-265----clear-finish/3754?1=1&optionid=2935) from Webdirectbrands.com.  I carefully assembled the chair according to the instructions and it appeared to be stable.  However, when my 3 yr old son was climbing onto it, the chair toppled over onto him.  I was next to him so I caught him and the chair.  I sat him on the chair and instructed him never to climb the chair without me.  Then when he was scooting back to sit further into the chair, the chair toppled backwards.  Fortunately, he was not hurt, but it was a very scar experience for both of us.  Of course, I did not let him sit on the chair again.  Further inspecting the chair, I see how the chair could topple over to the side if a child reaches over because the arm rests extend beyond the chair legs.  This is a chair fundamentally flawed in design.  The legs are too narrow for the chair.  

I emailed Webdirectbrands.com twice notifying them what happened and that I wanted to return the chair for a full refund. [REDACTED] , Customer Service Manager, emailed me back [REDACTED] and told me that I had to pay for the return shipping of the chair and restocking and that the original shipping would not be refunded.  I emailed stating that it is ridiculous for me to have to pay to return and to restock this dangerous childrenÃÂs product, so that they can, presumably resell it to another unsuspecting family.  

[REDACTED] stated that they have been selling this chair for 12 years and this is the first safety issue that they have heard of.  I do not believe that.  I showed the chair to my friend, and she immediately saw how this chair was dangerous because its legs were too narrow and the arm rests extended beyond the leg support.  The pictures and descriptions on Webdirectbrands website advertise this as a youth chair.  As a consumer, I understood the representation that this chair was safe for a child to use.  Unfortunately, when I received the actual chair, I found out that the chair is not a safe product.  Webdirectbrands does not permit customers to leave reviews of this chair on their website.  Because of their prohibitive return policy, Webdirectbrands continues to profit from the sale of this dangerous item even if customers return it. [REDACTED] directed me to contact White Wood[REDACTED] about my safety concerns.  But it was Webdirectbrands who advertised and sold me this dangerous chair.
justification: The chair toppled over twice but the child was not injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The design flaw suggests a likelihood of recurrence is possible, hence a 3.

incident_description: Purchased "Hello Kitty" table and chair set for our 18 month old granddaughter through Target.  Manufactured by Delta Children's Products.(Model No.: TT89481HK.  Second day, chair collapsed under her while she was eating her lunch.  She was traumatized and shocked, as were we.  An examination of the chair showed that the piece under the seat to which the legs were attached, was not properly glued and screwed into the seat.  The glue was only on one side and the two screws were too short and tapered to properly secure the piece to the seat.  Photos were taken and sent to both Target and Delta.  Neither seemed overly concerned about the safety of other children.  The seat was supposedly rated for up to 50 pounds and our granddaughter is only approximately 30 pounds.  This set was manufactured in China and, we believe, constitutes a major safety hazard.
justification: The chair collapsed under the child, causing trauma and shock, but no physical injury was reported.

incident_description: The Dorel Asia SRL Orena Bunk Beds the side rail wood has split when a child was sitting on the top bunk...both sides which resulted in the top bunk collapsing.
justification: The incident involved the collapse of a bunk bed, which is a significant safety issue, but the description does not mention any injury.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased 20 of the same light bulbs from Menards in mid March 2015.

About 2 months into using the light bulbs, one of the light bulbs failed. The consumer stated that the light bulb started to flicker for about few seconds to 10-15 seconds. The consumer inspected the light bulb, and noticed a crack on the ceramic/plastic that attaches to the bulb. The crack was 3/4 way around the bulb.

Within 11 months of purchase, 6 of the light bulbs failed. On three of the light bulbs, the bulb detached from the base while trying to remove them from the fixture.

The consumer stated that when the light bulbs failed, the bases on them became extremely hot. There was also a burning odor.

The light bulbs have a 15 year warranty on it. All of the light bulbs that failed were installed indoors.

The consumer contacted the company about 6 -7 months ago through e-mail. They asked him to send in the light bulbs in, along with UPCs and receipt. The consumer had to get a duplicate copy of the receipt from the credit card company. The consumer sent in the failed 6 light bulbs along with their UPCs and the receipt to the company about a week ago.

The consumer does not know how the company will be assisting him once they receive the light bulbs. The company is supposed to be evaluating the light bulbs.

The consumer believes there is a safety hazard with the light bulbs because the issue occurred with more than one light bulb. 

The consumer still has the other 14 light bulbs. He does not know if he should remove them from the light fixtures.
justification: The incident involves multiple light bulbs failing with safety concerns like overheating and burning odor, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
We bought a sofa and matching Love Seat La-z-Boy Greensboro outlet in January 2016.I think it's called the Rowan ReclinaWay in Peacock Fabric.

It was delivered to us on February 9, 2016, before Valentines Day. Shortly after Valentines Day I developed a severe itchy rash all over my arms and legs. It gets worse every time I sit on the sofa or loveseat. The itching is severe and the rash looks like chicken pox or poison ivy.

I have been taking [REDACTED] and using [REDACTED] like crazy for about 6 weeks now. I went online and discovered there have been several complaints about a chemical LazyBoy uses to treat the fabric of their sofas to prevent mold and it is causing "sofa dermatitis" in susceptible individuals and obviously I am one of those individuals. I also read an article on www.webmd.com about people developing "sofa dermatitis" and it is coming from chemicals used in the fabric. I went to the Urgent Care Center the Saturday after ValentineÃÂs Day because the itching was so severe.  He said he had never seen a rash that followed dermatones only on both legs and both arms. The only thing he could tell me was it wasnÃÂt scabies, shingles or Lyme Disease or Tick Fever. He told me to follow up with a dermatologist if it didnÃÂt go away and prescribed a low dose [REDACTED] cream that I could only use for one week. Now itÃÂs the end of March and IÃÂm still breaking out.

I have an appointment with a dermatologist. I'm bringing him a copy of the complaints I've read online and having a test done to see if I'm allergic to the material. We were told by the salesperson that all LazyBoy furniture is manufactured in the USA, however I read that the chemical DMF they are using to prevent mold is made in China. I would like a listing of all the chemicals and materials used in the Rowan models in the covers and the polyfill as well ASAP, except IÃÂve had no luck locating a contact number for any manufacturing plant for La-z-boy.

If I find out from my doctor that LazyBoy furniture is causing this rash, I am going to report this to the Consumer Protection agency, a lawyer,  and News2 Wants to Know. I think people need to be aware that made in the USA does not mean 100% made in the USA. I have had no luck being able to locate contact information on where they manufacture their furniture. The only links to LaZBoy bring you to the store where you purchased the furniture.

I doubt the sales people or store managers know every chemical used in the product. This has run up a doctor bill for me. IÃÂve spent a lot of money on antihistamines, topical creams and now two doctors.
justification: The individual developed a severe rash requiring medical attention and ongoing treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description: After notifying Conair of safety hazard, finger must be inserted to remove battery causing injury to finger, and not hearing back, I am now contacting CPSC to issue a recall of product, weight watchers weight scale UPC 074108257994
justification: The description mentions an injury to the finger caused by inserting it to remove the battery, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) based on the reported frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description:
I purchased a TV stand model Keira 55" Flat panel TV stand (ZL 568-55SU) by Z-line Designs through CSN Stores (now Wayfair) on 3/2/2010. 
I used the product for a 52" [REDACTED] TV model [REDACTED].
The TV stand was used following the manufactures recommendations. 
The manufacturer advertises the TV stand to support TVs up to 65" with a maximum weight of 150 lbs. 
The TV placed on the stand was 52" and weighted 57.1 lbs. The TV was positioned on the TV stand so the weight was evenly distributed.
Around May or June, 2015, I encountered that my TV had fallen front forward from the top glass shelf resulting in severe damage to the screen. The damage to the screen was beyond repair, therefore the TV was sold for parts through eBay in June, 2015.
The reason for the incident seems to be the support system design for the top glass shelf of the TV stand which may result in a unstable top glass shelf.
I have encountered that the same problem has been reported by several other customers who have bought the same product:

http://www.amazon.com/Z-Link-ZL56855SU-Stand-65-Inch-Keira/product-reviews/B002808692/ref=cm_cr_dp_qt_hist_one?ie=UTF8&filterByStar=one_star&showViewpoints=0

This is a potential hazard to other customers and may result in property damage and personal harm, specially if TV viewers (e.g. kids) are sitting in front of the TV.
This incident has been reported to the manufacturer as well.
justification: The incident resulted in severe property damage (TV destroyed) but no reported injuries, and similar issues have been reported by other customers.

incident_description: Portfolio Chandelier was installed in home we purchased.  It was hanging in two story foyer as designed.  One morning my wife noticed it was hanging lower.  Upon closer inspection, it was observed that it was hanging only by the electrical supply cord and there was about a foot gap from fixture to chain.  Upon inspecting the top of the fixture, I could see the fixture loop was broken and the broken remains of the loop were caught in the cup at top of fixture.  I immediately connected chain to main body of fixture and the support chain to reduce risk of falling if electric cord broke.   My family of six occupies this home.  Had the electric cord not supported the weight of the chandelier, this could have led to significant injury since the fixture loop completely failed.
justification: The chandelier's fixture loop failed, posing a risk of injury if the electrical cord had not supported it, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: The desk lamp was plugged into outlet in my son's bedroom but not on.  Two sparks were seen followed by a burning odor.  The plastic on the control panel began to melt.  Unit was immediately unplugged and use discontinued.
justification: The incident involved sparks and melting plastic but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The light bulb pictured caught fire and burned at the connection between the glass part of the bulb and the base. The smoke could be seen and the smell filled our house. This is a fire hazard! This is the second light bulb - purchased at the same time - that has burned at the same place on the bulb. This needs to be address by the company, or recalled.
justification: The light bulb caught fire, creating smoke and a smell, but no injury or death was reported. This is the second occurrence with bulbs purchased at the same time, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description: The plastic holding the glass shade snapped and the shade fell.
justification: The glass shade fell but there is no mention of injury, so it's an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that when a person is sitting on the chair with the recliner out and they lean slightly forward (to grab a remote, pick up a phone, etc.), the unit closes on oneself. The first time it happened to the consumer's mother, and later to her mother's aid.

The consumer contacted the retailer and explained the situation. She was informed that she could not return the item because it had been too long since its time of purchase. The consumer indicated that she would then contact an attorney, at which point the representative she spoke to informed her that they could send  a Service Technician over to inspect the unit.

The Service Technician inspected the unit; he took the recliner out and leaned forward and the unit closed on top of him. He contacted the retailer and explained the issue. The retailer informed the consumer once again that they could not take the unit back.

The consumer continues to use the unit without ever taking the recliner out.
justification: The incident involves the recliner closing on users when leaning forward, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: The inner glass-enclosed filament (gas pressurized?) blew, sending glass shrapnel into the glass outer bulb.  This outer bulb could not contain the initial "blast" and also ruptured, sending additional glass onto my head and in the bathroom.  The bulb was 3 or 4 months old.
justification: The incident involved glass shrapnel hitting the person's head, indicating potential injury.

incident_description:
The chandelier in our entrance hallway had a catastrophic failure of the mounting loop which the chain attaches to.

This happened on 3/5/2016.

We purchased our house in 2009. The house was constructed in 2007. The chandelier had a manufactured date of 2005.

I have photos of the deffective mounting loop, and the manufactures model number and manufactured date.

It was a Trans Globe model 9922 RB.

Amazingly, after numerous conversations & emails with management in their furniture dept in California including detailed photographs, they do not feel anything is wrong with their beds for children. incident_description:
Invacare manufactures a medical device marketed as a shower chair.

The shower chair has four adjustable legs.  Each leg screws both into and out of the shower chair base, thus allowing the chair to be adjustable to 'fit' individual shower/tub basins.

Each adjustable legs has a designed locking mechanism, unfortunately, in the chair I purchased, lot # XXXXX, the locking mechanism on each of the 4 legs fails to lock the adjustable leg.

A normal customer usage profile shows that the chair will be moved around the shower basin for stuff like cleaning to tub basin, pulling one self into the shower stream, or pushing the chair back to exist the tub basin.

During this normal customer usage profile, the chair legs rotate due to the failure of the leg locking mechanism.  The chair leg rotation causes the legs to randomly adjust, causing the chair to be more and more...."TIPSY" for lack of a better word.

Customers who use this medical device are often disabled, but as often elderly.  Elderly customers often suffer from dementia, altimzers, and the like.  Health care providers who do the initial set up of these medical devices....shower chairs.....are not aware that with each usage by the customer, the care becomes further and further out of level, out of adjustment, and the chair 'TIPSY-NESS' become worse.

As the chair becomes more unstable, the likelihood of a shower slip and fall becomes greater and greater.

You or I can go to [REDACTED] and buy an $8 lawn chair that is waterproof and unadjustable, but will perform the same each and every day in the shower.  An Invacare shower chair is $80 and is more unpredictable each and every day of its use due to leg locking mechanisms that fail to lock the legs in a given spot.
justification: The shower chair's instability increases the risk of slips and falls, which could lead to injuries, especially for elderly or disabled users.

incident_description:
Leggett & Platt adjustable mattress base, Premier model P-232; now marketed as Premier Furniture Style.  Received on 12/15/2014. 

The control box for the base has a battery backup system comprised of two 9V alkaline batteries to allow the base to be lowered in the event of a power outage.  The batteries are not designed to be recharged, nor is there any mention in the manual about any sort of recharge capability.

There was an extremely loud popping noise that occurred that I was unable to attribute a source to, followed by another within the next few days.  The exact time period it occurred was a couple weeks prior to 2/16/2015, so under 2 months from receipt.

On 2/16/2015 I needed to completely power down the control boxes, including removing the backup batteries.  When I went to remove the backup batteries I found that they had exploded inside the battery holder.  That explained the very loud pops that I heard a couple weeks earlier that I was unable to determine the cause of.

Since I have two bases, and the exact same thing happened to both of them, I suspected something amiss with the control box.  When I checked the backup battery connection with a multimeter I found that whenever the control box had AC power it was sending 28V into the backup batteries.  In effect, continuously attempting to charge alkaline batteries that are not intended to be recharged.

There is nothing in the manual about recharging the backup batteries.  In fact, the 9V alkaline batteries that were installed came with the base explicitly for use as backup batteries.

Since I was already dealing with Legget & Pratt customer service to replace a motor that failed I notified the customer service agent what I found.  I disconnected the battery backup on my bases to prevent any further problems.  I don't know if there have been any updates to the bases / control boxes since then.

Feb 16, 2015, is the date I was dealing with customer service about the failed motor and discovered the exploded batteries.  The actual battery explosions where a couple weeks prior.
justification: The incident involved exploding batteries but no injury or death was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) since the issue affected both bases but is not a common occurrence.

incident_description:

I turned on the lamp on one of the fans this evening, and after a few seconds, heard a cracking and popping noise and heard something drop on the ground.  A second and third such noise followed a few seconds after that.  I looked up at the fan, as the noises appeared to come from the general direction of the lamp, and noticed a 1/4" hole in the lamp globe at the point where the globe meets the fixture, with a 1/2" crack extending from the hole downward.  I immediately shut off the lamp, and will not be using it until we can get a replacement globe.  The obvious danger is that the globe would continue to crack and eventually fall off the fan causing injury to someone below it.

My thought is that due to the outside temperature going down to 55F and the bulb being a 100W halogen, the cracking in the globe may have been due to heat differential between the bulb and the temperature of the globe, causing rapid expansion of the glass.  We are also going to be looking into a replacement LED bulb as those will not produce as much waste heat as a halogen and will reduce the chance of .
justification: The incident involved a cracked lamp globe with potential for falling, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is possible due to the described conditions.

Bought several of these battery operated LED candle lights and inserted the two AA batteries into each one.  After a couple of minutes I heard a sizzling sound coming from one of the lights.  Fearing that it may burst into flames I tried to pick it up to move it outside but it was too hot to hold.  I scooped it up into a frying pan and brought it outside.  I pretty much knew there must have a short circuit so I wanted to get the batteries out ASAP.  Using oven mits I unscrewed the top and shook the batteries out.  The very hot batteries (both of them) continued to sizzle and ooze liquid until they cooled down after several minutes.  The plastic body of the light was visibly burnt - especially at the bottom.

It appeared to me that the metal tab at the top, which was supposed to connect with the light bulb, must have contacted the positive battery terminal instead - causing the short circuit.  However, it is difficult to tell for sure since I had a touch time shaking the batteries out of that end of the unit.  I was trying to disassemble it quickly and did not take note of the position of the metal tab and how it short circuited.

I was not injured and there was no property damage.  My main concern is to not have this happen to anyone else as I truly believe that this came very close to causing a fire in my house.  I still have the unit, the batteries and packaging.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit causing overheating and potential fire risk, but no injury or property damage occurred.

It's suprising to find that Ashley Furniture, which is the largest furniture manufacturer in the U.S.,  poses such a great safety hazard to its customers, and not many American people are aware of the issue of formaldehyde. According to World Cancer Fund Research Fund International, U.S.A. ranks 6 among countries with the highest cancer frequency (source: http://www.wcrf.org/int/cancer-facts-figures/data-cancer-frequency-country). I am convinced that it has something to do with the formaldehyde issue in wood products sold in the U.S. market.
justification: The incident describes health issues (coughing, allergies) due to high formaldehyde levels, indicating injury but not death.

incident_description: In approximately 2010 we purchase a Lowes Porfolio Lola 9 Light Chandelier Item #240822, Model #34330. On October 3rd, 2015, in the middle of the night this chandelier fell from the ceiling because the hanger loop at the top of the chandlier that connects to the chain gave way from what looks like metal fatigue. By looking on line this looks like it has happened before. I went to the Lowes store in Millsboro Delaware and they laughed at my suggestion for replacement. This is a faulty Chinese product and is dangerous. If someone or thing was below it when it fell it would have killed them.
justification: The chandelier fell due to metal fatigue, but no injury or death occurred. Online reports suggest this has happened before, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description: I was burning a 3-wick Woodwick candle (dark red, cinnamon) in my kitchen window sill. It was in a rectangular glass container about 9" long, 4" wide and 4"  tall. The valance curtain was about 4 feet above the candle. The candle had been burning about an hour and a half with no problem. Then, my daughter noticed the flames had suddenly gotten very high and were moving a lot. She tried to blow out the flames, but the wax was about an inch high and the flames would not go out because it was about 3 feet from the front of the sink. There was no way to pick up the glass container to move it closer because of the huge flames. As I was trying to get a large glass baking dish out of the cupboard to put on top and smother the flames, the glass suddenly burst and the was and wicks went all over the sill, down the backsplash and behind the sink (a huge mess!) The wicks were still burning, and we were afraid it would catch the windowsill on fire. We were then able to put a snuffer over the wicks and put them out. This terrified us both, and my hands and heart didn't stop shaking for an hour. I have photos of the aftermath, it there is a was to send them. I will never buy another Woodwick candle, especially in a glass container. There was not warning, of course. Never in my 66 years have I ever had a near-miss fire situation like this, so I thought it should be reported. If we had not been in the room, no telling what kind of disaster this could have been.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous fire situation but resulted in no injuries or property damage beyond the candle and surrounding area.

incident_description: my portfolio chandelier that was above our stairs in our house failed and fell down two stories to the basement, damaging the wooden banister and wall and juke box that it fell on. not to mention the mess and being startled at four am with it crashing down.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage but no injuries were mentioned.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Beautyrest Recharge Alayna Plush Pillowtop Mattress Set and have been experiencing adverse health effects as a result. At the same time of beginning of use I have experienced vertigo, peripheral neuropathy, and joint pain. These have slowly begun to reside as I have discontinued use of this mattress.
