incident_description:
(10/17/2015) The consumer stated that she turned off the power before she took out the light bulb in the ceiling fixture. The consumer then put the new bulb in and turned the power back on. The consumer turned the switch back on for the fixture. The bulb lit then went out. The consumer thought maybe the bulb was not tightened so she reached up too tighten it. The bulb exploded in her hand. 

The consumer turned off the circuit breaker so that she could get the remaining pieces of the bulb out. After removing the pieces she put in a second bulb and a third bulb in the fixture but they would not light. The consumer tried a different brand bulb from another fixture to make sure that the fixture was working. The other brand worked fine.

The consumer was not injured.

(10/18/2015) The consumer contacted the firm via email. She received a response that the information was forwarded to the appropriate department.
justification: The bulb exploded but the consumer was not injured, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
We purchased a Glass Coffee/Cocktail Table from Rooms To Go with many other furniture for the living room. My husband tripped and placed his right hand on this table, which was in front of him, to balance. The glass broke into sharp pieces. He sustained severe lacerations on his right hand and lost lots of blood. He suffered a tendon tear, two arteries cut and nerve damages on his right palm and two fingers (ring, middle). He was rushed to the emergency room by 911 paramedics with acuity level 1. 
At the hospital he was admitted for a reconstructive surgery the following day, after a resident surgeon attended his wounds. The surgery took close to four hours, with tendon, arteries and nerve repairs. He had 27 stitches on his palm and the two fingers. He had to follow up with the plastic surgeon for at least 5 months in two weeks intervals and meet the hand therapist thrice a week. He had his hand in a cast during the recovery. The wound/stitches required cleaning everyday. 
Now even after an year later, his right hand is only 75% functional. This is when I realized that his hand is not going to recover fully and the product needs to be recalled. I reported this incident to Rooms To Go and requested the Glass Furniture products that are not made of tempered glass to be recalled. But I have not got a positive response and the very product is still  on sale.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations, tendon tear, and nerve damage requiring extensive surgery and long-term recovery, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
I installed two Ecosmart 60w replacement LED bulbs in a ceiling fixture on November 11, 2015.  According to the packaging, these bulbs are distributed by Home Depot which is where I purchased them.

Today, even though the lights were not on, the glass enclosure spontaneously on the fixture exploded sending shards of glass to the floor.  Fortunately, nobody was in the vicinity and therefore there were no injuries.

After cleaning up the mess, I looked over the packaging very carefully and found a notice stating the following: "Not for Use in Totally Enclosed Fixtures."  It is not clear to me that the enclosure that shattered is totally enclosed.

While there was a warning on the product, the fact that it is in such fine print should be a cause for concern.  One would think that such an important warning would be displayed in a very visible and noticeable manner.

As a Clinical Engineer, I have dealt with mislabeled and recalled products during the course of my 47 year career.  This would not be tolerated if the bulb were a regulated medical device.
justification: The incident involved an explosion of the glass enclosure with no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the warning was present but not prominently displayed.

incident_description:
My 9 light portfolio chandelier I purchased from lowes under kicheler lighting came crashing down to floor in my foyer. It is a 2 story fall.
No one was injured but damage was sustained to my hardwood flooring and an electrician needed to be contacted as wires were loose and we worked about a possible fire after sparks.
justification: The chandelier fell causing property damage but no injuries, and there was a potential fire hazard from loose wires.

incident_description:
(10/10/2015) The consumer stated that her son was laying on the sofa cushions. The material on the cushion had split over time and the foam on the inside of the cushion was exposed. When her son got up off of the sofa, the consumer noticed a redness on the right side of his face. The redness progressed into hives. The hives spread from right side of his face to his neck and chin and he was wheezing. 

This happened for four days. The consumer gave her son allergy medicine. 

The consumer sought medical attention on 10/13. 

The consumer stated that her son had never had a reaction before so she thinks it is from the foam. 

(10/14/2015) The consumer contacted the store of purchase. She was advised that someone from the store will contact the company. She is still waiting for someone to call her.

Dear Sir or Madam:

The consumers are writing this letter in support of their report (referenced above) that they are respectfully submitting to the US Consumer Products Safety Commission. The consumers are reporting an allergic reaction occurring as a result of exposure to fumes and physical contact with two sofas purchased by them in 2010 from Regency Furniture (manufacturer:Ashley Industries). The registration  number of the product/sofa is: ASH988035.

The consumers purchased two pieces of furniture from Regency Furniture (manufacturer Ashley Industries) in 2010. The two pieces consist of a Dura blend sofa and a Dura Blend love seat The furniture always had a strong smell to it and the consumers assumed the smell would wear off over time. However, even after the several years of having the sofa in the house the smell still remains.  Moreover, their 3 years and 11months old son has developed an allergic reaction to the sofa material and the smell. Over time the sofa began to have some cracks on it in the Dura blend material and the foam inserts from inside the sofa are visible and are exposed. When their son touched the sofa with his face or bands or when he sat on the sofa, be began to develop an allergic reaction  in the form of hives and wheezing.The wheezing appears to increase when he is exposed to the smell emitting from the sofa. The hives do not happen when he touches anything else in our house. Only the sofa produces this allergic reaction.

After extensive research in the field of allergies and immunology, the consumer has found that sometimes it can take months for someone  to develop a particular allergy to a certain allergen. Even though the consumers had the sofas for some time, his allergic symptoms began to appear recently.

On 10/10/2005 he began to develop hives after his face touched the cushions of the sofa. The hives began on his right cheek and progressed down his face to his neck and then the upper body. This has happened for 4 days, every time he came into contact with sofa and until we removed the sofa from the living room. The consumers saw their allergy specialist on October 13, 2015 and even after he took medication he still developed hives from contact on the sofa on the evening of October 13th, 2015.  We removed the sofas from the living room and placed them into the basement. The hives outbreaks stopped since then.

The consumers contacted the Regency furniture customer service. The manager they spoke to, named [REDACTED], was professional and respected the consumers' concerns. However, there is no comfortable solution that the consumers agreed to in regards to this issue at this time.

The consumers have removed the sofa from the living room into the basement and their son's hives stopped.   However, the consumers would like to raise awareness about this situation because there are many people/children who have sensitivities, allergies, respiratory concerns, and weak immune system. The toxins in the furniture and other products can cause allergic reaction when the immune system is overly stimulated. Many furniture items contain flame retardants, chemical ingredients, and have toxic fumes. According to an article by Dr. [REDACTED]: "the toxic chemicals are packed into couches, chairs and many other products... they have been linked to human health risks, including infertility, birth defects, lower IQ scores, behavioral problems in children as well as liver, kidney, testicular, and breast cancers..." People who are sensitive, have respiratory illnesses, asthma, cancers, low immune system, allergies can be effected by these fumes and chemicals. People need to be aware that these products can cause potential harm. However, nothing is mentioned about this in the industry or when you purchase a piece of furniture. When the consumer contacted the customer service, all they could say is that the ingredients are listed on the label inside the sofa. However, what these ingredients can do to our health - no one mentions.

The sofa has caused an allergic reaction in the consumers' son and the consumer wants to warn other customers to read labels, to consider their own special and unique circumstances and health concerns when shopping for any product.  Regency Furniture and Ashley Industries produced and sold us a product that is of concern to their son's health and has caused the consumers to experience significant physical and emotional discomfort due to this incident. No one should feel scared sitting on their own sofa at their own house thinking about toxins inside furniture and seeing their child covered in hives from that particular furniture product   Therefore, we respectfully request a report to be filed with the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). Please see documents attached.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Respectfully,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a child developing hives and wheezing due to contact with sofa materials, requiring medical attention and removal of the furniture to stop symptoms.

incident_description:

One day, a neighbor & I were drinking coffee enjoying the sounds of country living while on the deck.  All of the sudden my neighbor fell backwards in the chair. I jumped up to catch her fall. She was fine, but the chair was not. I flip the chair over to check the bottom of it to be sure it was still safe to sit in. Only to find all four welded pieces on the bottom not bolted together.

I'm no expert, but it looks to me like the part wasn't welded properly.  I've reached out to Big Lots regarding this incident. The set is only five months old and ask them what can I do since it was purchased off the floor and I had no information regarding the manufacturer. Big Lots put me in touch with Garden Best. I left a message, as no one answered the phone during business hours.  I'm currently awaiting a call back from the manufacturer.

incident_description:

incident_description:
A 29-5/8 in diameter, 3/16- 7/32 in thick, round glass coffee/cocktail table top shattered into thousands of angular
pieces and shards on the order of 1/8- 1/2 in without being subjected to any impact and with no substantial load. The glass pieces fell onto the floor and onto the lower level of the coffee table and could have injured anyone who was within a few feet of the table at the time. A young child, not understanding the danger of the small glass pieces, could have walked or crawled into the glass on the floor and been severely cut.

I was the only occupant of the room at the time sitting about 3ft from the table. The glass had about 1 lb of newspaper on top at the time of incident. There were no other items on the top. There was no impact of any kind at the time and there was no shaking from earthquake (we live in Southern California). The room temperature was normal- about 70 deg F, and, to the best of our knowledge, the glass was properly supported around its circumference. I heard a loud noise and immediately noticed that the table top had shattered and was lying all over the nearby floor and bottom coffee table level. I took pictures of the shattered table top and have kept all of the remnants except those which had to be vacuumed. I received a few of tiny cuts from small, nearly invisible, pieces of glass. I then put on gloves in order to clean up the glass. No other glass in the house, windows, mirrors or either of two other glass table tops was affected in any way.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (tiny cuts) and had potential for more severe harm, especially to a child. The likelihood is unlikely as it occurred without any apparent cause or impact.

incident_description:

It's not used as a toy or used roughly. We discovered they have fallen out of the chair where attached at the bottom under the seat to attach the seat top to the wood frame of the chair. In trying to put them back in it is obvious they are stripped and fall right back out of the chair. We have only used the table and chairs for normal child activity so this seems very odd and dangerous. 

The first incident happened roughly 9/2015. Second incident was today, 11/6/2015.
justification: Screws falling out of the chair pose a potential hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her two year old great-niece took the ghost decoration off of the table and started biting on the top of it. The consumer grabbed her niece and took the ghost decoration out of her mouth to inspect her mouth. The consumer put the ghost into her own mouth without thinking too much about it. The consumer was mainly concerned about her great-niece and wanted to make sure there was nothing in her mouth that she could choke from.

The consumer stated that her mouth was burning the next day and the tongue was red. The consumer went to Urgency Center. They examined her mouth and the product. The consumer had red cracking areas on her tongue and her mouth and throat were burning. Urgency Center informed her to contact poison control center about the product.

The poison control center were not aware of any issues with the product. 

The consumer stated that the product had a sweet, perfumed smell.

The consumer contacted her nurse hotline for health partner. The consumer was informed to rinse her mouth and drink lots of water.

The consumer went to her doctor on 9/29/15. The consumer was provided some medication for her mouth. The consumer was informed to contact CPSC and report the product.

The consumer contacted her nephew and asked him to inspect her great-niece for any issues. They are not aware of any issues as of now.

The consumer is worried about the chemical in this product. The consumer stated that kids can touch the decoration, put their hand in the mouth, and expose themselves to chemicals. 

The consumer was informed by the retailer that this product was part of last year's stock. The consumer saw online that Two's Company is no longer in business.

Continue to have mouth issues to date 10-12-2015.  On second medication now!
[REDACTED]

incident_description: "Mainstays Touch Control Mini Dome Lamp" Model No. per Walmart web site: 19.2556 purchased at Walmart (Walmart No. per Walmart web site 1737395) in 2013 has unusual oblong bulb which exploded with a very loud report and spewed small pieces of glass over a wide area. My companion heard the explosion across the house (2500' +/-) and in the laundry room and she came to see what happened. incident_description: During assembly of a 60 inch storage closet (This is a clothes hanging closet that is covered by zippered cloth for attic storage.) the plastic pieces need to be held under high stress as you leverage the covering over an impossible (in my instance) stretch. The warranty includes free replacement parts for the first 30 days. This is to cover the extremely high number of broken parts. The product varies in design from box to box and some have shorter zippers than others, among other differences. I contend that this product is unsafe to the point of being recalled and taken off the market right away.

incident_description: Preschool program ordered Royalco light cube R59601. The cube was plugged in for 2 hours and it exploded. It burst into flames and caused flames to go up the wall. Preschool children had to be evacuated. The wall, phone and floor were damaged.

incident_description: Two drawers from a new chest of drawers continuously fall out if opened. One drawer fell on my foot once and on the floor as my daughter opened it. The chest is also very front heavy and poses a serious tipping hazard.

incident_description: Today, our twenty two year old daughter was going around with something in her hand and mouth, hiding it from us. incident_description: The wooden slats on our bunk bed are defected because of the blemishes in the wood that the manufacturer tried to fill with some type of caulking/ filler to hide them, but you can clearly see them on all the slats. incident_description:

justification: The candle exploded, causing significant damage and potential for injury, but no one was harmed.

incident_description:
I recently bought a memory foam topper and was reminded of a horrible experience I had last year. Last year I bought a memory foam mattress and felt sick for months. I did not realize at the time that memory foam mattresses could make people sick. I had moved into a new house and I did not know the cause of my sickness. It felt like the air was thick, and it smelled. It was a "chalky" smell. I thought it might be the renovation dust, so I spent the next several weeks cleaning for a few hours each day. I wiped down the walls, vacuumed, and even got an air purifier. 

I was so sick that I was in a daze for that entire month. I could hardly think straight. I was just blindly cleaning and trying to purify the air in my spare time. I researched "air scrubbers." I went to other people's houses to sleep. When I spent an entire day away, my head was able to clear and that is when I researched memory foam mattresses and realized their dangers. 

I had put sheets and a mattress pad on the mattress as soon as I unwrapped it, so it had not had time to air out. However once I realized the mattress was making the air in the house like this, I tried to air out the mattress. I left a fan on and the window open to keep the air circulating out. 

However, after a few more weeks, I still felt sick. I had stopped sleeping in that room and slept in a separate room when I found out, on an air mattress. The rest of the house aired out considerably, though not completely. I was able to contain the problem somewhat to the bedroom. But I still felt ill. After a few weeks I gave up. I dragged the mattress back to Ikea and returned it (it was just under their 90 day return policy). 

I had called and emailed the company when I found out, but received no response.
justification: The incident describes prolonged sickness and cognitive impairment due to exposure to off-gassing from a memory foam mattress, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This halogen bulb was installed in an open style overhead fixture above my sink vanity. The fixture had been turned on for a few minutes. I had just stepped a few feet away from the sink when I heard a very loud pop and saw what turned out to be small chards of glass flying through the air. The bulb literally had exploded into hundreds of tiny pieces. I took photos of what was left of the base of the bulb prior to removing it which are available for your review. I also took photos of 4 areas where debris from the inner section of the bulb landed on the cultured marble vanity top and left small burn marks in the marble.

This model of bulb is made with what looks like a bulb within a bulb. The inner bulb appears to have exploded, then causing the exterior of the bulb to explode. Also when I say explode, I am using that word literally. Glass was throw as far as 8-10 feet from the vanity.

This was a very scary experience. I was shaving at the time and if I had not briefly stepped away when I did, I would have been looking right at the bulb when it exploded and there is no doubt that I would at the very least have been cut and burned or perhaps even blinded.

The bulb was a GE Model 78798, 72watt Halogen bulb.
justification: The bulb exploded, causing glass to scatter and leaving burn marks, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: We were in our home and had a candle burning for about 45 minutes when we heard a loud 'bang' from the kitchen, location of the candle. We went to investigate to only discover out countertop was on fire in 3 spots. The candle had exploded and sent shards of glass all over the room and we had to put the fire out quickly. The fire caused irreparable damage to our countertop. This is a HUGE safety concern. If we hadn't responded within seconds or god forbid had we been showering, taking the trash out, or any other activity causing us to be away longer than seconds, our entire apartment would have went down in flames. We were just charged $350 to replace the countertop at our apartment due to the damage this candle caused. The candle was not previously cracked as we had burned it before, and there was nothing even remotely close to the candle to spark the fire or cause the explosion. We could have easily lost our lives that evening, and now to add more stress to us, we are paying for the damage caused by this candle and not any mishandling we had part in at all. This is not ok. We are completely mortified that this product exists and billions of consumers are blindly able to purchase it and believe the candle is safe to burn.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the potential for similar incidents if the product issue is widespread.

The consumer wanted to wait to see if it got better over time. The consumer already has a doctor's appointment scheduled so she waited to see the doctor. The consumer went to the doctor and was informed to go take some tests at the hospital. The consumer went to the hospital for the tests. She received results on 7/16/15. The consumer stated that her results are not good. They will be conducting more tests to check her kidneys, stomach and some other things. The consumer will be going on 7/23/15 for more tests. 

The consumer stated that she did not have these issues before using the pillow. The consumer has had diarrhea and blood in urine. 

The consumer contacted Easy Comforts and they asked her to send the product back to get a refund. The consumer will be holding onto the pillows. The consumer paid about $28-29 per pillow. She ordered two of the same pillows. 

The consumer's Dr. stated she should have X rays, but as she is allergic to the dyes the consumer can not have them,  They would help them see damage to the consumer's liver, kidney, bladder - etc.  The consumer still have blood in her urine is becoming incontinent.  The consumer is going to have a colon check & bladder check.

My name is [REDACTED] the name of my company is US Asian Marketing and Manufacturing. I do consulting work for a number of different Asia based manufacturers my telephone number [REDACTED]. I have been marketing testing products for 25 years and sit on some STP consumer boards at UL. 

Over the last 3 years there has been a mass exodus in China from listing products with UL over to ETL( Intertek). The reason for this is UL stepped up its aftermarket monitoring of off spec products and went to a three strikes you lose your listings law. Meaning, if you products are found to be off spec in the market 3 times your listings are suspended and you cannot use the UL mark. Please note the three companies listed on my testing reports in China all changed from UL to ETL over the last 3 years. These products are in 10,000 Ace Hardware stores Wal-Mart and on line with Harbor Freight and in the 800 stores. 

After many months of presenting my testing data and making complaints at ETL they refuse accept my complaints which should be against the law. They are not investing cheating on products at all and should be suspended as a safety testing agency. These products are below spec making their maximum amperage capacity and everything listed as per spec false and should all be recalled. 

I will send you another few reports also as this is not only being done in extension cords but lighting products too. 

PLEASE TAKE SOME ACTION AGAINST THIS TERRIBLE INJUSTICE TO THE AMERICAN COMSUMER

incident_description:
We bought the California black chair and ottoman from Bailey's approximately 12/2013.  I believe we paid around $1200 for the set.  Approximately 6-9  months ago I noticed slight peeling around the chrome base which at the time I thought was less then desirable but was not overtly concerned.  The chair/ottoman had primarily been in storage until we moved into our newly build home 3/2014, it was kept in heated storage and not overly exposed to the elements.  We followed Bailey's cleaning directions, only dusting the base and using Baileys leather product on the chair/ottoman.  

Never did I realize that peeling chrome would become such a safety hazard until July 30th, 2015 went my 8 month old infant put a small piece of it in her mouth and started choking.  Although she is fine and healthy today, this incidence required the response of paramedics and had I not been there could have been much more disastrous.   Of course following the incidence I moved the furniture to storage and contacted Baileys in the days following. incident_description:

I saw a spray of dust and/or gas as well as shards of glass propelled from the second light from the left.  I turned off the switch immediately and examined the damage. incident_description:
My wife and I purchased our lamp online from Lamps Plus on 12/28/2010. I assembled it as instructed, and it had been in our bedroom since that time. It had not been dropped, placed in water, or misused in any way. On 07/23/2015, I attempted to pick the lamp up by the pole, and the base fell away from the lamp; whatever material the base is composed of had disintegrated. 

I have contacted both the seller (Lamps Plus) and the manufacturer (Lite Source Inc), both of whom dismiss this as a problem of age. We have had two other floor lamps of similar construction, and it was the wiring, not the base, that gave out over time.

The response from a customer service supervisor at Lamps Plus was "the base are [sic] made up of concrete filled with air pockets. This is to give the floor lamp its weight. Overtime [sic] when the lamp is moved, those air pockets cause it to crack and eventually crumble." As the manufacturer cautions "bulb gets HOT quickly!", I am concerned that should the base "crumble" while unattended, the lamp would fall - in our case on bedding or against curtains - and thus, this lamp constitutes a real fire hazard.
justification: The lamp base disintegrated but no injury or fire occurred, though there is a potential hazard if the lamp falls on flammable materials.

incident_description: Last week my children went outside to play in my backyard.  They immediately came back inside.  My 4 year old was bleeding and had a small cut on her foot.  My 6 year said that the patio table was broken into thousands of little pieces.  I went outside to investigate and found that it was exactly how she had described it.  The glass from my patio table had shattered into hundreds of tiny pieces.  I was so confused as to how this had happened.  I googled "shattered patio table and found many links telling stories very similar to mine; glass patio tables shattering randomly, in as little as 2 weeks after purchase up to 3 years after purchase.  Many times the consumers were not a witness and found the resulting mess.  Other times consumers reported the table "exploding into hundreds of pieces."  I was shocked that this is a problem that I am not alone in facing.  I also found from my research that the Martha Stewart table sold at [REDACTED] is often the product affected.  My table is a Martha Stewart table, but was purchased at Home Depot.  I contacted home depot through phone and email and was twice told that they were sorry for the incident, but that because my table had been purchased in March 2013 (2 years ago) that it is not covered under their return policy and the warranty has expired.  I am even more shocked to learn that this product is still being sold at Home Depot.  I was lucky that my family was not outside when my table exploded and we only suffered minor injuries, but I am hoping to prevent a far worse incident from happening to someone else.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury (small cut) to a child, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) based on the description of similar incidents reported by other consumers.

It was unsecured because it was a 3-drawer high version (3 high by 2 wide) and we never imagined that it would tip over because it was a low dresser. She was opening the drawers (not hanging on them or trying to climb) and when she opened the top drawer last, just the act of opening the drawer was enough to tip the dresser over. At the time, we wrote the incident off as a freak accident. incident_description:
The consumer purchased two of the same lighting fixture for two of her bathrooms.They were installed by her son.

The consumer was in the master bathroom for a short time with the lights on. The consumer went outside of the bathroom for about 10 minutes. She left the lights on because she was going to return soon. When the consumer returned to the bathroom, she noticed glass on the bathroom floor and carpet of her bedroom. 

The consumer noticed that the clear glass over one of the halogen lights on the light fixture had exploded.  The consumer stated that the lights were not on for longer than 40 minutes.

The consumer contacted the retailer. The consumer tried to speak to a manager but she was unable to speak to one. The consumer spoke to a sales person in the electrical department. The consumer was informed by the sales person that there have been other reports similar to hers. The consumer was informed to bring in the light fixtures back to the store with packaging and sales receipt for refund. The consumer does not have packaging and sales receipt. The consumer was informed that if she can find the date of purchase and the amount, they can reconstruct the sales receipt. The consumer found the entry in her checkbook for $172.18 (for two of the same light fixtures).  

The consumer contacted a different retailer location and spoke to a store manager. He informed the consumer to go back to the store and have her sales receipt reconstructed. He informed her to fill out a form so that she could deal with the vendor. 

The consumer did not see any reason to deal with the vendor. The consumer filed a complaint with the Attorney General of MN who recommended her to contact CPSC.

The consumer added she purchased the two fixtures on 7/13/14, and she obtained the reconstructed sales slip which does not itemize the sales tax to equal the $172.18.  The consumer also added Menards computer system, in their Electrical Dept, states this product as "discontinued," and it is no longer displayed in their inventory.
justification: The incident involved a light fixture exploding, but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents have been reported but are not widespread.

incident_description:
La-Z-Boy outdoor swivel rocking chairs (model "Peyton") have had welding failures which cause complete separation of the chair seat frame from the swivel/rocker pedestal base.  On two occasions (6/2012 and 7/2015), people sitting in those chairs along w/ the chair frames have fallen backwards, slamming onto our paver patio. 

We immediately contacted La-Z-Boy of the first incident in 6/2012, informing them of the failure  and asking if this model had been redesigned/remanufactured because of the severity of the problem and since we had only used the chairs 4 months.  La-Z-Boy  sent  us a replacement chair frame, but did not respond to my inquiry.  Since my husband wasn't hurt beyond a bruise or two, we assumed this failure was a fluke specific to that single chair.

When this happened again, just several days ago (7/11/2015), as our neighbor tumbled backwards with the chair seat frame having completely peeled off of the swivel base just as it had done in 2011, it was obvious the manufacturing of the chair, ie the welding failure, made it potentially hazardous/dangerous.  We once again contacted La-Z-Boy via telephone and email, and requested that they collect this from our home, as well as refund monies paid.  We are especially concerned about the safety and the liability that these chairs pose--and for that matter, the entire Peyton set!  La-Z-Boy informed us that they would not do that.  Quite honestly, we didn't get the impression that La-Z-boy is too concerned about either safety or liability, especially after it's sold.  We would have NEVER purchased this La-Z-boy set had we known of this severe welding failure and the potential danger/hazard it poses. 

If requested, we will gladly forward pictures of both chair failures (6/2012 and 7/2015), along with available correspondence with La-Z-boy.

Thanks so very much
justification: The incident resulted in injuries (bruises) and poses a clear hazard due to repeated welding failures.

The consumer stated that there was a strong odor in his room that gave him headaches, nausea, sore throat, dry and swollen eyes and congested sinus. The consumer stated that there was also a chemical taste in his mouth. The consumer thought the symptoms were from the new room (he had moved into a new home). The consumer contacted the retailer and was able to return the mattress. They informed him that the odor should go away in a few days. The consumer also moved and purchased a different style of mattress. 

The consumer purchased the same, Beautyrest Black Alexia Extra-Firm, mattress again on 6/1/15. The consumer stated that he smelled the same odor again. The consumer felt the same health symptoms all over again. The consumer will contact the retailer and return the mattress.
justification: The consumer experienced health symptoms (headaches, nausea, sore throat, etc.) due to the mattress odor, indicating injury (severity 3). The recurrence of symptoms with a second purchase suggests a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:

justification: The incident describes a potential hazard with the sleep sack tag, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased three North Star Leather Swivel Bar Stools several years ago from Akinss Furniture in Dogtown, Alabama. During the years I have had these stools, my grandchildren have gotten their feet and hands smashed between the chair bottom and where the base swivels. There is a gap between where the seat bottom attaches to the base of stool. The gap is approximately one inch...just enough for a toe or finger to fit. When someone is getting into the chair beside them the chair turns or swivels and causes the weight of he chair to lean which catches the toe or finger inside this space. This happened today during lunch when I was preparing food for my three grandchildren. I turned around to hear a blood curdling scream from my granddaughter. Her big toe was stuck between the base and seat. It made a very deep depression injury which appeared to look like you had mashed your fingers inside a car door. The entire toe was injuried. I placed ice on the toe for over me hour. When her mom picked her up 4 hours later it was still depressed and very blue in color. The chairs are made by North Star with a serial number of539900045272.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep depression injury to the granddaughter's toe, which was still blue and depressed hours later, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
Product that is UNSAFE is the Frosted Glass Table Top, part of the Room & Board "L- Shaped Portica Desks"

Link: http://www.roomandboard.com/catalog/office/desks/portica-l-shaped-desks

On June 2, 2015, I lifted the 60"x30" frosted glass tabletop and moved it across the room. I held the tabletop in an upright position, slightly angled forward. The lowest corner barely touched the concrete  floor I was walking on and the entire sheet of glass splintered instantaneously from the bottom up. The lower half of the tabletop hit the ground and shattered and the upper portion split into two heavy thick slabs, one in my left hand (positioned higher) and one in my right hand (positioned lower in relation to my left hand.) The EXTREMELY SHARP AND DANGEROUS thick chunk of glass in my left hand instantly tilted downward onto my right hand due to its weight and busted open my right hand, severing the tendon and nerves between my right hand thumb and the back of my wrist. I suffered an extremely deep laceration. In that same second, I pushed the two pieces of glass out of my hands and away from my body, glass crashing down and shattering everywhere. I jumped back and tightly sheltered my hand, putting pressure on the wide open gash now on my right hand. Everything happened shockingly fast. 
Im scheduled for hand surgery to repair my severed tendon and nerves. I have lost the function of my right thumb. I expect to wear a splint for 6 weeks after surgery and months of physical therapy to recover mobility.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury requiring surgery and long-term rehabilitation, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is considered possible (3) given the detailed account of the incident.

The counter has an area that is completely burned and is bubbling up. Had this candle been on a wooden surface (which the rest of my home is) it would have started a fire. The candle itself was completely blackened and covered in ash. When we found it on the table we were horrified. To think that the candle could have burned our place down was terrifying. I am also appalled that hobby lobby was selling the candle to me in April 2015 when the recall happened close to a year ago. It was not a fluke either, there were several of these candles on display for sale at a discounted price. I am furious and concerned for the safety of others.
justification: The candle caused property damage (burned countertop) but no injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) given the recall was ignored and multiple candles were still on sale.

incident_description:
Purchased king size headboard around mid August 2014.
She noticed small incidents with feeling ill but then in October 2014 she began suffering with vertigo, vision changes, exhaustion, headaches , facial twitching and a feeling of ill health.
During the past months the caller has spent thousands of dollars to discover that she has major neurological symptoms and affected her health greatly.

She has not had the headboard tested but her tests showed that she had been exposed to high formaldehyde levels.

The caller has a compromised immune system caused by Lupus and Epstein Bar/adrenal failure.

She and her boyfriend went away for the weekend and she felt better each morning after sleeping elsewhere.

They returned Tuesday, May 12th, 2015 and removed the headboard from their bedroom then placed it away from the area.
In just a couple of days her symptoms have dramatically improved.
The vertigo is gone, headaches and major facial twitching has stopped, sinuses have improved and she is hoping that her vision focus returns soon.

She is asking that these headboard be investigated and the public made aware of the formaldehyde dangers.

She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
justification: The incident caused significant neurological symptoms and health issues due to formaldehyde exposure, but no death was reported.

Further inspection found that the plastic mounting bracket that was installed following directions failed as it cracked, broke away from the screw holding it into the wall which caused it to fall the 3 feet down onto the lower unit.


this is unsatisfactory as the cabinet held no signifant weight only 2 small photo albums and a picture frame.

incident_description:
I purchased Christopher Knight Home Brinkley Backless Barstools from Overstock.com (now called Tate Backless Leather Counter Stool (Set of 2))  on April 2014. on June 17, 2015, I sat on the stool in a normal fashion. My foot made contact with the decorative metal footrest cover on the stool. The metal cover sliced open my left heel. My injury required six stitches, which I received immediately, along with pain medication. I am still recovering, dealing will some pain, swelling and some difficulty walking. incident_description:
Product: Summer Infant SwaddleMe Stage 2 Baby size small/medium.
The swaddle pajamas were being used as intended with the correct size and age of a baby, and followed the directions of how to [fastener] them snugly on the baby.  After using the swaddle for 4 weeks, our baby would get her hands and then arms out of the swaddle due to the material becoming stretched out from normal use.  The hazard was due to when she would wiggle, the stretched out material/swaddle would wiggle up towards her head, giving her hands access to the opening of where the vertical leg sack material and the horizontal material parts meet.  She would stick both of her hands out, then would pull her arms up towards her face in her sleep.  I would find her like this asleep, and the horizontal material would be all pushed and squished up around her neck and partially or completely covering her mouth (still able to breathe out of her nose luckily).   Thinking I was not swaddling her tight enough, I would continue to try using the product, but this same scenario happened 6 times in 1 month (even though I would [fastener] the swaddle so tight that there was no space between the swaddle and her skin, and she was unable to move when I first swaddled her until wiggling and stretching it out over a few hours and the material stretched and then moved).  I stopped using the swaddle when one time I came in to check on my baby and the same scenario had happened again, but this time the material was pushed up over her mouth AND nose (still breathing when found her).  The swaddle would never come undone and still was together, but would become stretched out and move as she slept, which allowed her hands to poke out of the opening (see photo) of where the corners of the material meet, causing a dangerous suffocation hazard.
justification: The incident describes a suffocation hazard that could lead to injury, and it occurred multiple times within a month.

I am hoping you can look into the safety of this product. Surely my little girl is not the only child who messes around on their chair and doesn't sit perfectly like a proper lady :) Perhap, if you find it appropriate, it can be suggested to the company that they make the opening a little smaller so feet and legs can't fit into that area.
justification: The child suffered a bump on the head and bruising from the incident, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I own a family daycare and Thursday June 4th, I had a 9 month old baby in her bumbo multi seat. It is made with 2 seat straps to strap to a chair and a 3 point harness to secure baby in. When I got her out after lunch, I noticed her 3 point harness was unstrapped. I couldn't believe I forgot to strap her in - I am so careful about that. On Tuesday June 9th, I put her in her seat for breakfast and remembering the other day when she wasn't strapped in, I MADE SURE she was strapped and the buckles on the 3 point harness were latched tight and secure. After breakfast, I was washing dishes and the baby was in her seat leaning forward and grabbing her water cup off the table, taking a drink, putting her water back on the table etc. I heard a child fall, and turned around and the baby was on the floor. She was checked out and was thankfully ok with no injuries. I was trying to figure out what possibly could have happened because I was positive she was buckled. I was able to unsnap the buckle with a MINIMAL amount of pressure by pressing it onto the plastic piece that came up between the legs. I firmly believe that by her playing with her cup ( and just wiggling around the other day), she was putting just enough pressure on the buckle to unlatch it. I have emailed the company, but have not yet had a response.
justification: The baby fell but was checked and had no injuries, indicating an incident without injury. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the buckle was easily unlatched with minimal pressure, suggesting it could happen again under similar conditions.

incident_description: At around 4am I was sleeping in my single bed and my son was in the trundle bed that we roll out every night and is stored under my bed.  I heard, "Mommy, I'm stuck.  Mommy, I'm stuck."  I looked over and saw my son's head stuck under my bed.  His head fit through the space between the bottom of my bed and his trundle bed.  My son moves a lot during sleep and his head got under my bed.  His neck was between the side of my bed and the side of his trundle bed.  I jumped up and lifted my bed and said, "Crawl out, baby, crawl out!"  He was able to get out.  I had him get into my bed with me.  I was terrified.
justification: The child got stuck but was able to get out without injury, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible given the child's movement during sleep.

incident_description:
(05/26/2015)The consumer called the manufacturer and left a message.

(05/24/2015) The consumer stated the first time that the topper was used, his wife woke up the next morning with a headache. His wife slept on the topper again and woke up stating that she was seeing things and hallucination. She also had a rapid heartbeat. Each time she would go in the same room as the topper, she would have problems.
The consumer stated that he also had a rapid heart beat and breathing issues just by walking into the same room where the topper was located.
The consumer nor his wife required medical attention.
justification: The incident describes physical symptoms like headaches, hallucinations, and rapid heartbeat, but no medical attention was required.

incident_description:
On 4/30/2015 my husband and I purchased a Lane reclining sofa (model 32739/4148-21) from Mathis Brothers furniture store in Indio, CA.

On 5/17/2015 the sofa was delivered by Mathis Brothers.

On 5/26/2015 my husband and I were both seated on the sofa with the footrests extended in the reclining position.  When we stood up and depressed the footrests, the sofa tipped forward.  My husband caught the sofa before it tipped over on us. This also happened when we were not using the footrests, but merely standing up at the same time. It appears this is safety issue as the sofa starts to tip forward as we shift our weight forward.

Mathis Brothers furniture was advised on 5/27/2015 of this situation.  The store scheduled a technician to come out and inspect the sofa.
justification: The sofa tipped forward but was caught before causing injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Light bulbs exploded in a ceiling light fixture. The bulbs were installed several months ago, last week one exploded with a loud bang, spraying glass across the dining table. The fixture has two bulbs, so I replaced one but left the other, thinking it was a freak accident. Today the other one poped, not as loud and violent but still throwing shards of glass across the room.
justification: The incident involved exploding light bulbs causing glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased an Ikea desk in November 2010 and have been using it daily as my work desk. It shattered /exploded on Monday June 1 2015. There was nothing on the desk, or near it that could have caused it to shatter the way it did. I found a report online of a woman who had a very similar experience as mine, except I was sitting at the desk when it occurred. Also, unlike the report and Ikea's insistence, the glass did not just shatter in safe cubes, it shattered into shards and powdered glass which was everywhere!! 
I have spoken with Ikea as well as their insurance company. I do not want anything in the form of monetary compensation, however Ikea is not accepting this is a safety hazard and the product should be recalled. It is ridiculous that a product that has the potential to do this can be deemed safe and only a quality issue instead of a safety issue. There are small children in the home and i am certain if they were in the room they would have been hurt because of the way height that the glass exploded and that it landed everywhere.

Other reports very similar if not identical to what I experienced. 
http://www.nbcdfw.com/investigations/No-Recall-on-IKEA-Glass-Desks-Following-Scant-Reports-of-Spontaneous-Shattering-189749201.html
http://www.nbcmiami.com/news/local/NBC-6-Investigation-Desks-Spontaneously-Explode-282638411.html
http://bc.ctvnews.ca/customer-upset-after-ikea-desk-explodes-1.2038583
justification: The desk shattered into dangerous shards, posing a potential injury risk, especially to children, though no injury was reported in this specific incident.

incident_description: While sitting in my chair the right arm rest snapped off of the chair and the back of the chair slightly detached. I fell on the ground as a result of the chair malfunction.
justification: The chair malfunction caused a fall, which typically results in injury, hence severity level 3.

incident_description: I was in a small closed in room (bathroom) when one of our GE Halogen 72 watts, 100 watt replacement, A19/67295 bulbs exploded.  If I had been facing the bulb which was over the sink I probably would have lost an eye.  As it is, I was several feet away from the bulb when it exploded and I still had pieces of the bulb stuck in my shirt and in my hair.
justification: The bulb explosion caused an incident with no injury, but potential for serious harm if circumstances were different.

incident_description: We had purchased a Garden Oasis Long Beach outdoor dining set for our patio last July from Sears. The set includes an umbrella ready table with "shatter proof" glass. Yesterday afternoon, as I was sitting inside with a 10 month old baby and my husband was out in our pool, we heard a loud noise sounding like water gushing. I looked out the back door to see the shatter proof glass in a pile on the ground. My husband's hand got cut on the shards of glass as we cleaned it up. Sears was unwilling to help and told me there were not enough incidents to be concerned. I have pictures.
justification: The incident resulted in a hand injury from glass shards, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) based on the description of the event and the lack of widespread reports.

incident_description: My Ikea glass top spontaneously exploded when I was standing next to it. I thought my ceiling was caving in.
justification: The glass top exploded but no injury was reported, only shock and noise.

incident_description: Sitting at my desk at home with my two kids after getting out of the shower we heard a loud crack got up and the candle at the end of the wick got so hot it exploded and wouldnt blow got bigger out so had pour milk over it and look at the heat spot burned into the tablecloth and wood I pulled out the draw and felt hot for 10 minutes Thank Goodness I heard it to catch it otherwise the fire would of spread!!! So scary and the other 5 candles I have are hitting the road because I dont want this to be passed on to my friends!!! No words just wow!!!
justification: The candle explosion caused a fire hazard but was quickly contained without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she entered the bedroom where the light was on.

When she walked in, there was a loud bang and she heard glass falling within 3-4 feet radius of the floor lamp.

The consumer stated that she noticed that the light bulb had exploded. The consumer stated that when she looked at the remains of the bulb, it looks different from usual bulbs. She does not believe it was tested properly.

The consumer picked up and vacuumed the glass, retaining larger pieces for their identifying info.
The consumer bought this in a pack of 2. She still has the second bulb.
justification: The bulb exploded but no injury was reported, only glass falling within a small radius.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased her chairs through Home & Living on Amazon Online.

The consumer stated that the screws on the chairs come loose. The consumer stated that she has to turn the chair over and tighten the screws from time to time. In the past 6 months, the consumer has tightened the screws 2 times.

The consumer stated that on one of the chairs, the front-left leg broke while her husband was sitting on the chair. The consumer stated that the piece of board fell off from the leg where the screw is put in. Consumer's husband was not injured.

The consumer contacted Amazon. The consumer was provided with contact number to Home & Living . The consumer was informed by Home & Living that the 30 day return had expired. The consumer would have to purchase the part.

The consumer contacted Amazon again. The consumer was informed that the manufacturer of the chairs is Coaster Furniture. The consumer contacted them and was provided the base and two legs for free. The consumer was sent the parts for the chairs that she had ordered. The parts did not fit the chair that she has. The consumer found out that she was sent the wrong order either by Home & Living or Amazon. 

The consumer contacted Amazon to inform them that she received the wrong order of chairs. Amazon has contacted Home & Living in regards to the order. Home & Living informed the Amazon that the consumer was sent the correct order.

The consumer stated that she ordered 6 - Parsons Black Leatherette Chair With Cherry Wood Legs by Coaster Furniture. The consumer was sent 6- Roundhill Parsons Chair Black Leatherette with Cherry Finish Wood Legs.

The consumer believes there is a fall hazard with these chairs that she currently has.
justification: The incident involved a chair leg breaking but no injury occurred, and the issue has been reported multiple times with recurring loose screws.

incident_description: The adhesion which holds the mirrored door onto the brackets, which are screwed into the main body of the cabinet, failed. The door just fell off the cabinet and crashed into the floor, missing me by inches, and made a hole in the bathroom floor. The door came adhered to the brackets and were not a part of the product assembly.
justification: The door fell and caused damage but no injury, making it a severity level 2 incident. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such failures can happen but are not frequent.

incident_description:
The light bulb Feit Electric Halogen 65w bulbs that I put into my indoor lighting combusted without warning.  The entire bulb popped and left the middle electrical device screwed into the socket.  I did not think about it to much the first time but when the second one burst with in 24 hours of the first I thought I should warn others.
It can come down on you or your kids in small glass shards without warning.
justification: The incident involves bulbs combusting and leaving glass shards, posing a risk of injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has an implantable defibrillator/pacemaker device (manf: [REDACTED]). The consumer has had the device for about 20 years. He stated that the doctors have always told him that electric blankets are okay to use with the device.

The consumer stated that his medical device was picking up electrical interference since he purchased the blanket. It caused the device to charge up twice in Jan 2015. The consumer related the issue with his device to the blanket about 2-3 months ago. 

The consumer contacted the manf of the blanket. They informed him that their product could not be used with such medical devices. The consumer stated that the blanket does not have any warnings on it.

The consumer also contacted the manf of his medical device. They informed him that a properly working electrical blanket will not interfere with their medical devices. 

The consumer stopped using the blanket and the interference stopped as well. 

The consumer has seen his doctor in regards to this. The doctor informed the consumer that the device charged up twice and that could have led to him suffering from a cardiac arrest.
justification: The incident caused the device to charge up twice, which could have led to a cardiac arrest, indicating a potential for severe harm.

incident_description:
This report involves the CargoLoc Ceiling Mount Garage Hoist.

This product is sold as a device to store large items by hanging them from the ceiling inside a home or garage or other structure. I specifically purchased it to store a kayak we purchased in July 2014. It advertises a weight capacity of 100 lbs, our kayak weighs no more than 75 lbs.

Upon purchasing the product, I followed all the manufacturer's directions and mounted it to the most solid studs in the ceiling of my garage. It held our kayak up all winter long at a height of about 8 feet off the garage floor. It is designed for raising and lowering equipment up to 100 lbs and securing it above the floor.

Earlier today we returned from a trip, and with the assistance of my son, secured our kayak (using the product in full accordance with the directions from the manufacturer) in the product and raised it off the ground to the storage height of 8 feet. Upon completion, both my son and I noticed that one of the brackets looked different from the other and was clearly not flush with the ceiling.

Out of concern for safety and our kayak possibly crashing to the ground possibly hitting a vehicle or child, we attempted to lower the kayak to inspect the product. However, after lowering the kayak just two feet, part of a bolt from the product fell to our kayak. The product became unstable and unsafe, so I asked my son to get away. I tried to grab the kayak to ease it to the ground, but in the process lost control of the ropes that operate the product. With that, the other end of the kayak fell 6 feet to the concrete floor of our garage.

Thankfully it did not hit a person or vehicle. At this time I am still waiting to find out of damage was done to the kayak.

After we moved the kayak to another location for storage, we located the broken bolt. It was approximately one-half inch long, the remaining part of the bolt is still in the stud of the garage ceiling.
justification: The incident involved a product failure causing a kayak to fall, but no injuries or damage to people or vehicles occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a pair of Franklin Iron Works Casa Mirada glass and iron light fixtures in 2008 from Lamps Plus.  They have worked fine for 7 years, but today we happened to be home and saw smoke and sparks coming out of one of them.  It appears that the 3 light bulbs are set so close to the metal center stem containing the wiring that the wiring insulation burned off and the wires touched, sparked, and began to give off smoke.  We immediately disconnected it and checked the other one, which was very close to burning too.  If we hadn't been home, it's probable that my house would have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from a light fixture, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I have purchased multiple CREE LED Light Bulbs from Home Depot in last 3 years. Over those years I have purchased about 10 CREE branded bulbs and of those 10 I have had 4 fall apart. The top dome of the bulb falls off the base exposing the LED array 'filament'. This leads to an electrical shock issue and an overall safety hazard as the top dome of the bulb is a form of glass. One of the bulbs fell to the ground and cracked into pieces. Luckily, I caught the broken glass before one of my dogs ingested it. Since I rarely entered the room the bulb was in, I didn't notice it until I looked in the reflection of an item on the table and noticed the inside was exposed.

I have 4 other bulbs where the sealant on the dome has started to fail and are ready to come apart. I returned the first two bulbs to the Home Depot for an exchange but I still have the most recent two that fell apart. I believe this is a hazard to any living person or animal due to the shock and overall safety hazard of broken glass when gone unnoticed by the user.

I tweeted Cree on Twitter and brought the issue to their attention on there, where I was told I could exchange the bulbs at my local Home Depot. This was just over a year ago when the first two fell apart.

The first incident happened in April 2014. The second incident happened today (May 23, 2015).
justification: The incident describes potential electrical shock and broken glass hazards, with actual harm narrowly avoided (dogs almost ingesting glass), indicating injury is possible.

incident_description:
The consumer states the mattress was delivered to her home on 01/30/15. The consumer began to feel ill on 01/31/15 (symptoms include nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite, hot flash, and respiratory issues). On 04/09/15 the consumer visited a physician regarding the respiratory issues and was prescribed allergy medicine and antibiotics. The consumer has stopped sleeping on the mattress. The consumer states she feels much better after taking the medicine and being away from the mattress. Prior to taking the medicine the consumer noticed that she would feel better once she was away from the mattress.

On 04/27/15 the consumer contacted the store where she purchased the mattress from and spoke with [REDACTED], the store manager in regards to returning the mattress. [REDACTED] did not allow the consumer to return the mattress and indicated that it was past 30 days from the date of purchase. [REDACTED] She did not refer the consumer to anyone.  She offered to file a warranty claim with Serta but not for Comfort Exchange.

On 04/28/15 the consumer contacted the firm (1-888-557-3782) and expressed her safety concerns. The consumer informed the firm's rep (name unknown) that the mattress made her ill and she would like to return it. The consumer asked for a refund but the firm's rep told the consumer that she could do an exchange but the consumer would not be able to get a refund. The consumer does not want an exchange.

On 05/01/15 the consumer filed a complaint with the Consumer Protection Office in VA (confirmation # [REDACTED]). 

The consumer states per warranty instructions the bed needed to have a water proof mattress protector and she picked it up on 01/30/15 from the store.
justification: The consumer experienced health issues requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
Roncer Mesh Back Task Chair (Staples item# 571981) delivered 5/8/15 - upon opening box - very strong chemical odor - which upon assembly the next day seemed to disappear.  Over the past 2 weeks, skin on inner portion of left knee became extremely itchy, red and inflamed - use of cortisone spray seems to have helped the area.  Subsequently have other areas of body developing itch and redness -- today it dawned on me that the chair was the cause.  In doing online research - found there are chemicals used in Chinese products that can cause severe skin conditions - the chair's tag shows it was made by ZHEJIAN HENGLIN CHAIR INDUSTRY - 3 BLOCK, SUNLIGHT INDUSTRY ZONE, ANJI COUNTY, ZHEJIAN PROVENCE, CHINA 313300. 

Having just notified Staples Customer Service of the problem and need to return, was told to call Staple Corporate Office (877-235-9088) tomorrow, which I will do.  

This and any product imported from this China company needs to be taken off the market - it is not safe for use.

If skin condition is not feeling better, will make appointment with dermatologist for treatment - 

Question of Consumer Product Safety Commission: should this chair be tested before it is returned to Staples?
justification: The incident describes a skin condition caused by chemicals in the chair, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: A GE halogen 72-watt light bulb exploded in our dining room light fixture, sending shards of glass all over the room. Some tiny pieces were even embedded in the table and hardwood floor, and they left little scorch marks. Thankfully no one was in the room when it happened - the shards could have lodged in someone's skin or eyes. The light had been turned on for about 2 hours, and the bulb had been in there for a while - probably several weeks.
justification: The bulb explosion caused property damage but no injuries, as no one was present in the room at the time.

incident_description: Heard a loud noise today and went into backyard.  To my surprise, the glass table top on the patio table had shattered into a zillion pieces.  There was nothing around to suggest something had fallen on it.  This was just purchased last year from Home Depot.
justification: The glass table shattered but there was no injury or indication of what caused it.

incident_description:
My daughter was sitting on her bed last night when there was a loud bang. The side rail of the bed had broken in half. Luckily no one was hurt, and luckily we did not have the bunk bed set up as a bunk, we had them set up as 2 separate twin beds.
The bed was purchased 8/17/2014 from Mor furniture store in Murrieta CA. The bed is a BELA bunk bed. The description number on the receipt is 45216 IVY WHT TT BUNK. 
I do have photos available
justification: The bed rail broke but no one was injured, and the beds were not set up as bunks which could have increased the risk.

incident_description:
A few months ago I purchased two OSRAM LED 8.5 watt bulbs at Lowe's Home store.  One
was installed in a reset lighting fixture in the kitchen.  The one in a floor lamp. 

I chose these bulbs as an alternative to incandescent bulbs.  Both bulbs were on for four, six or
eight hours at a time.  Occasionally, the one in the reset fixture was left on over night. Three days ago, the bulb in the reset fixture, exploded, emitting black smoke, causing me to think  a fire may have started.

When I removed the bulb, it was extremely hot to the touch. . .not at the bulb dome which was plastic, but at the metal connection to the socket.  I saw that it had exploded, or separated from its base.

I immediately check the bulb in my floor lamp and it too was overheating at the bulb base.  These
bulbs are a true fire hazard and I don't feel they should be on the market.
justification: The bulb exploded and emitted black smoke, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
This concerns a "Rolling Garden Seat W/TU" Product #41725 purchased from Northern Tool & Equipment store in Davenport, Iowa.  

Item was purchased on 5/18/15 and was first used on 5/23/15.  A weld attaching the seat to a screw which adjusted the seat height broke, dumping me off the back of the cart onto the ground head-first.  

This weld secured a large-diameter acme-type threaded screw to a large circular disk of steel when the seat bolted onto. This was the first use of the item. 

It appears this large steel disk which is similar to a large cut flat washer is not made of heavy or thick enough steel such that a good weld would hold. 

This item was manufactured in China.  A very similar unit with the identical parts is also sold by [REDACTED] as well.

I have photos but cannot upload them to the complaint for some reason.
justification: The incident resulted in a head-first fall due to a broken weld, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a headboard from Pier 1 last June, started using it in July and began having fatigue and sinus issues. By October, I was having massive headaches, extreme fatigue, and many serious neurological issues such as facial twitching, eye spasms, changes in vision, inability to concentrate, mild depression and moodiness. Due to the lack of sleep and the issues I was experiencing, my immune system crashed to the point of not being able to function. During the process of elimination, we mold tested our house (found no mold) and I began daily IVs to try to mitigate my worsening immune issues. I finally figured out it was the headboard based on the fact that whenever I would sleep elsewhere, my symptoms would improve greatly. One of my doctors suspected Formaldehyde.As soon as I removed the headboard from the room, my symptoms improved and within a week, the headaches and neurological issues have cleared up. I am still repairing my immune system but feeling much better already.
justification: The incident caused serious neurological and immune system issues, which qualify as injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a bonded leather sofa for my office so I could take naps at lunch due to my disability status.  I have experienced skin rashes and burns on my face and chest.  I also get itching all over my body when I sleep on the sofa.

I have contacted the manufacturer and they have "pretended" to care.  I sent pictures and all the information they requested back in March 2015 with one follow up and have not heard back from them.
justification: The user experienced skin rashes, burns, and itching, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue persists with continued use, making occurrence likelihood possible (3).

incident_description:
Item purchased: "Flaxa" bed system from IKEA with a pull-out/trundle bed option. The trundle bed is on casters so it can move away from the main unit, however there is nothing to stop the bed from continuing to move as the casters do not lock. This causes the bed to move while a child is on it. The design of the trundle bed includes about an inch and a half of empty space underneath the unit, so when it is moved, it can pinch/scratch toes if someone is standing next to the unit when it is accidentally moved.

My children have suffered minor bruises and scrapes as a result of this unit moving while in use.
justification: The description mentions minor bruises and scrapes from the bed moving, indicating an injury has occurred.

incident_description: Purchased a new Sealy PosturepedicÃÂ® Prichard Ultra Firm King Mattress from Costco. It was comfortable, but the fumes were intolerable. Even with the windows open, I had trouble breathing and had a bad headache every day. I had to retreat to sleep on the living room floor.  I had Costco return to my home to pick up the mattress set.  I have purchased other Sealy mattress sets in the past and never had this type of issue before.  The manufacturer should disclose what type of chemicals are being outgassed.  The manufacturer should reformulate the manufacturing process to reduce outgassing, and/or air out the products at their factory before shipping them to customers.  I wasted a lot of time and money dealing with this and now I am having back pain from sleeping on the floor and I am back to square one trying to find a mattress I can sleep on.  Consumers have a right to know what exactly the risks are when buying a new mattress, and the manufacturers and sellers are not disclosing important safety information.
justification: The incident caused breathing difficulties, headaches, and back pain from sleeping on the floor, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue seems uncommon but not rare, given the user's past experiences with similar products (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
A Cree-type 60watt-equivalent LED light bulb blew apart in an overhead light fixture in my home, with the light switch in the OFF position.  It shattered the fixture's glass protective bowl, spewing glass fragments all over the floor and damaging our laminate flooring.  The bulb itself popped it's glass casing away from the ceramic base, but is pretty much intact.

We're very concerned about the potential for injury to home inhabitants, represented by the possibility of the bulb blowing apart.  It mystifies me why an LED bulb would even blow apart at all when the light switch is Off!  After cleaning up and removing the broken glass and broken light bulb, I personally checked the light fixture and found no flaws. In fact, I screwed in a standard incandescent 60 watt bulb and it functioned perfectly when I turned the light switch to ON.

Home Depot sells these CREE lightbulbs under their house name, but there's no identifying information on the manufacturer. I've written to Home Depot to ask for manufacturer information so i can make a claim for damages.
justification: The incident caused property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such events are possible but not common.

incident_description:
On September 22, 2014 at approximately 5:57am, a light bulb in the Philips Wide-Lite
fixture attached to the [REDACTED] located at [REDACTED] exploded. The heat
of the explosion caused the plastic cover of the Philips Wide-Lite fixture to rupture and
resulting in damage to a student's parked vehicle.

The Clark County Fire Department was called and extinguished the sparks and flames
on the rear fender and right rear light of the vehicle.

The light fixture failed to contain the exploded lamp. The failure caused hot melting
plastic from the fixture to drip down from the ceiling of the parking garage and landed on
the right rear taillight and right rear bumper causing significant damage to the vehicle.

The light fixture lens should be able to withstand lamp rupture per UL 1572.

The ruptured lamp escaped the fixture after only five (5) years operating since the
garage was built. With over 260 same Wide-Lite fixtures in the [REDACTED], 
there is a concern this incident could occur in the future and cause severe
bodily injury or property damage.

The source of the lamp rupture might have been due to loose rivet I crimp connections
on the tail attached to the center lamp socket tab resulting in the failure seen below.
justification: The incident caused property damage to a vehicle but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: On 04/06/2015 a Tempur-Pedic mattress and adjustable frame was purchased to help ease chronic back pain since a failed back surgery . The mattress was taken home first - had to wait until  04/15/2015 before the adjustable frame could be delivered . I slept on the mattress before receiving the frame and there wasn't any odor of any sort . After the frame was delivered , the plastic wrap removed and set-up with the mattress on it , we could immediately start to smell a strong chemical odor permeating the whole house . Thinking it just needed to air out for a couple of days , we opened a few windows just a little bit .  After sleeping on the bed the first night , I woke up with my throat almost swollen shut , the back of my tongue was swollen and irritated , my eyes were burning and was having some issues breathing . I have respiratory problems anyway and in my opinion some type of warning should be given by Tempur-Pedic about these odors - this way a potential customer could be aware of the potential health risk involved by purchasing these mattresses and adjustable bed frames  . If I would have known that the frame was going to emit such a strong chemical odor , we would have never made the purchase . I have made several calls to the salesman at Mattress Firm in Knoxville , Tn. that sold us this set  and he says he is trying to help us but , it's been almost a full 30 days and nothing is getting done . I have asked for a replacement frame early on in this process and , nothing . All Tempur-Pedic wanted to do was , send a T.V. repairman out here to replace some parts on the motor . I told the lady from customer service that it wasn't the motor causing the chemical odor . She said maybe it was the mattress , that's when I told her we had the mattress before getting the frame and it was after getting the frame is when the odor started . She advised me , she would talk to Mattress Firm - haven't heard from Tempur-Pedic since . I kept telling the salesman that we wanted this stuff out of the house , we are tired of having the bedroom closed up with a towel at the bottom of the door to keep the odor from spreading throughout the whole house . I haven't slept on this set since the first night . It almost sent me to the emergency room once , I won't give it a second chance . I have to put my shirt over my face to be able to enter the room to get clothes out . We are at the point now , where we want a refund and they need to get this stuff out of this house or I'm going to put it the yard - I'M TIRED OF BREATHING THIS CRAP !!!!!   THIS IS A SERIOUS HEALTH ISSUE !!!!!
justification: The incident caused severe respiratory issues and swelling, indicating injury, but no death was reported.

incident_description: I recently replace all flourescent light bulbs in my kitchen with new ones that I purchased from my place of employment for Earth day.  When I remove the kitchen bulbs, they literally fell apart in my hands.  Not only were they crumbling, but the base of the bulbs is melted and cracked and toasted brown.  Very scary indeed.  Luckily I was wearing glasses so shards didn't get into my eyes.  These bulbs look like a fire hazard and there was literally no warning that there was a problem.
justification: The bulbs fell apart and appeared to be a fire hazard, but no injury occurred as the person was wearing protective glasses.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her halogen light bulb exploded in her table lamp.  She stated that that glass pieces dispersed everywhere in the room.  Some of the glass pieces were imbedded in the carpet with burnt marks. She stated that she was fortunate not to have sustained any injuries.  

(4/8) The manufacturer was contacted and they informed her to send them the bulb for examination.  She was also advised to provide them with an estimate of the damages.

Consumer feels that these bulbs are a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb causing property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with halogen bulbs.

incident_description:
Caller stated he purchased some foam for his cushions that seems to be off-gassing chemicals which made his wife and himself ill.   Health symptoms are respiratory problems, eyes watering etc.  This has been ongoing for the last 6 months.   He received medical attention and have done some pulmonary test, results were not obtained as yet.
