He stated that the foam cushions were placed outside a few days ago and the health problems started dissipating.  

4/20/15 The distributor was contacted and he was advised that the owner would contact him.

Caller feels that this foam is a health hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident caused respiratory problems and eye irritation, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: An investigation was conducted on similar incidents of light bulbs exploding at this consumer's home in March of 2014. Another incident occurred on 4/9/15. The consumer's husband turned on the kitchen chandelier, and a candelabra bulb exploded. There were no injuries. The consumer stated that the bulb explosion sounded like a gunshot, and pieces of the bulb were found at least 16 feet away. The consumer feels these bulbs are dangerous, and that someone will eventually be injured by one of them exploding.
justification: The incident involved a bulb exploding without causing injury, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a possible likelihood of future occurrences.

incident_description:
(03/11/2015) Each night stand has a halogen light underneath the unit. The light is about five inches from the floor. The consumer discovered that the light gets very hot. If anything touches the light, it could possibly catch fire. The stands have a touch switch on the side of the unit that  turn the lights. The consumer stated that the lights can come on if the switch is touched accidently. This is also a problem because he has touched the switch during the night while he was asleep.

The consumer did not see a UL label for the lights.

(03/12/2015) The consumer contacted the company and advised them of what happened. A representive was sent out to investigate the unit. The representative advised the consumer that the bulb was hot because that is what happens with halogen bulbs. 

The consumer was offered a store credit for the night stands. The consumer advised them that the complaint was not with the stands but the lights under the stands.


The consumer stated to please find the attached picture of the UL label the he thought was not present, and to note that it says, "Caution: Risk of fire, install only in open top cabinet."

The consumer also added Bob's Furniture did replace his two night  stands with new ones the have safe LED lights installed. The consumer noted when he asked if Bob's furniture was going to issue a recall to the other customers that purchased this bedroom set, their answer was not a definite yes. Consumer also noted they [Bob's Furniture]  were going to have to come up with a plan on how to deal with this problem.

The consumer indicated he was told by the contact person at Bob's Furniture, [REDACTED], that the manufacturer of this furniture set has corrected the problem by installing LED lights from this point on.
justification: The incident involves a fire hazard due to hot halogen lights, but no actual fire or injury occurred. The likelihood is high due to accidental activation and proximity to flammable materials.

incident_description:
About 2 months ago, I replaced the bulbs in my children's bathroom fixture with Cree LED bulbs purchased at Home Depot. It's a four-lamp light bar that was installed by electricians when we built our home 8 years ago, and has never malfunctioned in any way before.

Two days ago, my 19 y.o. son had just finished taking a shower and was drying off, standing a few feet away from the vanity area. He heard a pop and something fell onto the counter. He yelled for me to come in to see what had happened (I was in the next room).

The outer bulb part of the Cree LED had burst and fallen off. The base was still in the fixture and was still lit. There were shards of plastic-coated glass on the counter and the floor.

I had him carefully leave the room since he wasn't wearing shoes, and I cleaned up all of the bits of glass I could find. I turned the lights off, then very carefully removed the base from the fixture. I now have the broken, plastic-coated bulb and the base in a bag. I'm not sure if I should call Cree or take it back to Home Depot. I don't have the receipt because it's been a while since I installed the bulbs.

I'm worried because I've already installed about 20 of these bulbs throughout my house, and I see that there are several other online reports of similar incidents.
justification: The bulb burst caused no injury but created a hazardous situation with glass shards, and similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description: My daughter was a going to sit on her bed and when she sat down the side rail split and the metal part that hooks into the headboard came out of the rail.
justification: The incident involved a bed rail failure but no injury was reported, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: My son of 10 yrs old was sitting at his desk reading when suddenly the desk shattered in pieces, and he even cut his finger. The desk was bought last year. We bought two a green and a blue for two sons. We are bit scared that the same thing might happen to the other desk. My wife was lucky enough to come across this website to see that this has happened on numerous occasion for other people and hence the reason for us reporting it. The shattered glass, also damaged my laminated flooring.
justification: The child suffered a cut finger from the shattered desk, indicating an injury, and similar incidents have been reported by others, suggesting likelihood is high.

incident_description: Anthropologie voluspa -a pricey candle with textured apparently thin glass- combusted and cracked in several spots causing a big hole to blow out the side..  It burned my $10k {REDACTED] table that went up in flames.  I had fallen asleep on 4/25/15 around approximately 10:15 PM EST..  I had woken my self up to go up to bed or Else I would have fallen asleep for the night and risked my life to burning in a fire.  I tiredly walked around the corner in my entry way with 30ft high ceilings..the table top was projecting 3 ft high flames..  I have a sprinkler system in my home which had not gone off but fire alarms if had gone off would sounded after the back wall leading upstairs would have already been on fire.  I threw water on it without time to grab an extinguisher in panic..  That candle combusted!!  I am a huge fan of candles abd have owned hundreds!  This has never happened- anthropologies amber textured glass was the cause of this overpriced candle with cheap glass.  My home does not smell like baltic amber but of a horrible burning chemocal smell.  Im left with a ruined $10000 customized charred {REDACTED] table.. Im furious.  When calling anthropologie to report incident they said the store district mgr from where i purchased in RI would call me back.. I requested corporate compliance and legal..
justification: The candle combustion caused significant property damage and posed a life-threatening risk, though no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The glass portion of a flushmount ceiling light fell from the installed fixture 1 day after it was installed.  The glass crashed to the floor shattering everywhere.  I was in the room when it happened, but thankfully, it did not hit me.  We have high ceilings and children.  Someone could have suffered a serious head injury.
justification: The glass fell and shattered but no one was injured, though the potential for serious injury was present.

incident_description:
Stool legs broke apart causing stool to collapse. Injuries resulted in multiple surgeries.

Stool manufactured as RELIUS SOLUTIONS Four-Leg Chrome Base Polyurethane Seating -- 4094500

also Ergocraft Contract Solutions E-13521CBEM-C8.
justification: The stool collapse caused injuries requiring multiple surgeries, indicating a significant impact.

incident_description: I bought a 16' rope light and was trying to figure out if it was going to be enough light for our small laundry room by using painters tape to attach to the wall temporarily. I plugged in the lights and turned to look at the light level in the room when I smelled smoke. I turned back baround and saw the rope light burning in one a spot.I immediately unplugged the lights. I found a burned spot on the wall above the door to the laundry room.
justification: The incident involved a rope light burning and causing a burned spot on the wall, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Last night, between midnight and 1am, I was awakened by the sound of something shattering.  I went looking for what could have caused the sound, and found my scale broken.  It had spontaneously broken/exploded.  There was glass all over the bathroom floor.  The scale had not been dropped (I was asleep).
justification: The scale broke spontaneously without causing injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: I went to sit back into the chair (normal) and the backing and back legs detached from the chair causing me to fall to the ground.  I should mention that I am not obese.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall to the ground, which typically causes injury, but there is no mention of severe harm or death.

incident_description: I decided to see if I could repair a sagging part of the mattress.  I unzipped it and discovered large amounts of mold all over the foam cover that was over the air bladders and under the zip cover.  We bought a different mattress that night.  We called the manufacturer, who said they knew about this problem, but didn't feel the need to do a recall or even inform customers there was a problem.  We got them to come get the bed and refund the purchase amount. As soon as we were rid of the bed, I had relief from an ongoing problem with chest pain and difficulty swallowing at night.  It resulted in severe GERD.  The next night, I had no such problems.  My husband had also slept on this bed for years, and developed sleep apnea which required a CPAP.  I tried to go to my doctor, who laughed in our faces and told us mold could not make us sick.  I have become progressively sicker ever since.  While sleeping on the bed, (without knowledge of the mold,) I developed large fibroid tumors, had my gall bladder removed (it was dead and adhered to my liver,) had to have and recover from a hysterectomy, and developed above-mentioned issues.  Since then, I have developed severe MCS, lost my job because they were spraying chemicals, have developed neuralgia, abdominal pain, PTSD, and MS like symptoms.  I believe the mold exposure was a contributor to these issues.  I cannot get any doctors to admit this is the case because they will avoid litigation at all costs.  Even if it means my life.  When I put everything together, I contacted a toxicologist in [REDACTED] about my worsening health issues.  He verified that the mold was dangerous and could have spurred on the health issues I'm experiencing.
justification: The incident describes severe health issues linked to mold exposure, including GERD, sleep apnea, fibroid tumors, and other serious conditions, indicating significant injury.

incident_description:
At 5:00 AM on Tuesday 14th April, 2015, while preparing to go to work we heard a loud bang coming from my 15 year old daughter's bedroom while she was sleeping. As I dash out, I met her half way in the living area and she said " daddy come and see?".

She lead me into her bedroom and there to our amazement her glass desk top table we bought from Ikea broke into pieces with her books fallen to the floor and broken glasses all over the room. This happened while she was sleeping. She has no hangings on the wall and nothing fell on the desk.
justification: The glass desk broke unexpectedly, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Turned lamp with led bulb in it and it started to make noise then smoke and fire.  I unplug the lamp and it stopped.  The base of the bulb was damaged (melted) and the base of lamp was burned and melted.   Light bulb in ? Feit  BPAG800DM/LED 9.5w/3000k/800lm soft white [REDACTED] e330072 led lamp.
justification: The incident involved a lamp emitting smoke and fire, but was promptly unplugged without injury, indicating a no-injury incident.

incident_description: Three days ago a chandelier purchased at Rooms to Go on Cedar Park, Austin Texas, while plugged to the outlet wall switch overheated and cut fire on the on-off enclosed (plastic) switch. My wife, who is handicap have to run to the second floor and unplug the cable from the outlet before the fire could move further, which could cause a house fire. We reported the incident to Rooms to go, who sent a technician to take pictures and investigate. So far nothing.
justification: The chandelier overheated and caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred, and the fire was contained.

incident_description: 7 piece patio set including table with glass top was purchased from Sears on 5/12/2014. It is the Garden Oasis Harrison set (item #7134582). The glass table top shattered on 1/23/15. There was nothing on the table at the time, the umbrella was not installed at the time and the weather was very mild (central Florida). Thankfully, no one was sitting at the table when it shattered, because glass shards covered my entire patio. This is a design defect and a safety issue (there are many more incidents of this in online reviews). Sears Co and the manufacturer not only refuse to replace the glass, but their only solution is to make the purchaser buy the SAME type of replacement glass, with the same design defect.
justification: The glass table top shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury. Online reviews suggest this is a recurring issue.

incident_description: Bali Exterior Screen shade purchased from Lowes: It was 139" wide, 80" in length so this was quite heavy. The screen was manufactured around a plastic headrail with very small plastic hooks that mounted into a thin metal bracket for hanging.  Both the plastic hooks and metal bracket looked too inefficient to handle the weight of the shade. We followed the instructions for mounting. Two days later the entire shade fell on top of my husband and I.  Upon inspection, the plastic hooks that were mounted into the metal bracket had broke off.
justification: The shade fell on the individuals, indicating an incident with potential for injury, though no specific injury is mentioned.

incident_description:
The Wilson & Fisher rope lights I purchased from Big Lots caught on FIRE!
I installed 3 sets of lights on my back deck (red, white & blue).
They connect end to end.
I noticed the blue lights were not on. When I went to check I realized the white and blue lights were no longer connected.
Then I realized the reason they weren't connected is that they had BURNED apart!
There is a small burn mark on my deck where the fire was.
At the end where the lights were connected they are each completely BLACK & MELTED.
If this had been in someone's house, there would have surely been a fire.
Oddly though, the red & white lights were still burning.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with visible damage to the lights and deck, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
My five month old daughter was on her back on her playmat with the toy suspended above her when my husband noticed she was making a strange choking noise. He pulled the you away from her and noticed that one of the knotted ends of the toy was deep in my daughter's throat and she was choking. If he had been less attentive, or the toy not attached to a suspension bar (which prevented it from lodging even deeper) she may have choked to death as air could not pass by the knot that is the size of a child's esophagus.the toy tag says:
Carter's
FTY#0914
STYLE#L31475H
04/15/2014
PO#3061
It is a bear head and arms with a lovey blanket around it and the four corners of the blanket are knotted.
justification: The incident involved a near-fatal choking event, indicating potential for death (severity 4), but the likelihood is reduced by the specific circumstances (attentive parent and suspension bar).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the mattress and box spring was delivered on 03/03/15.

The consumer stated that there is strong odor emitting from the products.

The consumer stated that she feels tingling in her arms, hands, legs and feet on the left side of her body. The consumer stated that she had the urge to vomit the first two days. The consumer stated that the urge was worse when she is lying on mattress. The consumer felt some burning in her throat and difficulty swallowing.

The consumer stated that the symptoms seem to disappear when she is away from the mattress. 

The mattress is located in her bedroom.

The consumer went back to the retailer to return the products and get her refund. They provided refund but are charging her 15% restocking fee and delivery cost. They contacted Serta for the consumer. Serta will be picking up the mattress and the box spring on 3/21/15. They informed her that they will destroy the products.

The consumer stated that when she was in the store, she felt nauseated and tingling in her body when she laid down on the mattress to try it. The consumer had to get off of the mattress.
justification: The consumer experienced physical symptoms (tingling, nausea, burning throat) linked to the mattress, indicating injury, but the issue is resolved when away from the product.

incident_description: On Thursday 26th March we were just about to go out of the from door when we heard a loud explosion, running back into the house nothing immediate stood out, we then went into a room which we hadn't been in to for 2 days and found that the coffee table had exploded and glass was shattered everywhere.
justification: The incident involved a coffee table exploding, causing glass to shatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
Creations Summers Evening Crib converted into a full size bed using the conversion kit that was sold with the product.  The side rail by the foot of the bed split while my son was sleeping in the bed.  It caused the bed to fall apart and collapse onto the side where the rail split. (bottom right side) We converted the bed to the full size about 2 years ago.  My son does not jump on the bed.  He uses it to sleep or sit and read.  My son was not injured, just a little shook up from his bed falling apart as he slept.  

I tried to call Creations to see about getting a replacement piece and could not get a working number for them.  Called the store I bought the crib and conversion kit from and was told that they have dealt with this several times.  I was told Creations changed from making wood conversion kits to particle board conversion kits without telling anyone.  These kits are the ones that are breaking.
justification: The bed collapsed but the child was not injured, only shaken up, indicating a severity level of 2. The store mentioned similar incidents occurring several times, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description: Problem with red mold on air mattress, no help from Sleep Number Bed.  Mattress is less than two years old.
justification: The presence of red mold on the mattress is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Purchased some Easter Grass from Dollar Tree Stores, Inc. UPC Code# 639277925732.  Imported by Greenbrier International, Inc, 500 Volvo Parkway, Chesapeake, VA 23320.  Made in China

The grass was to be used in a small child's Easter basket.  When the product was opened and grass was pulled out, there is an odor from the grass that smells like burnt wood/ashes and noxious chemicals.  The odor caused coughing and uncomfortable breathing.  After several minutes, the smell remained in the nasal passages.  There is concern that this Easter basket grass could cause health issues to a small child and that food items placed in the basket might absorb the burnt wood/ashes and noxious chemical odors.  This product will not be used in our family's Easter baskets.
justification: The odor caused coughing and uncomfortable breathing, indicating a physical reaction, but no severe or lasting harm was reported.

incident_description: I had purchased two of the twin sized electric blankets from Target store for my children.  The first one stopped working the first night it was used, and we thought it was just defective.  When we went to use the second one, it was plugged in to a household outlet and as soon as it was turned on, we smelled a burning smell.  When we looked at the controller, it was smoking.  We immediately unplugged the unit.  Later, we smelled the other controller, and it also smells of burned wiring.
justification: The incident involved smoking and a burning smell from the electric blankets, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her child, and family pet were within inches of there glass top dining table when she heard a loud pop and then the glass table top spontaneously exploded and shattered outwardly all over 3 rooms.  She stated that the glass pieces on the floor kept popping for almost 3 hours like popcorn.  There were no injuries sustained by this incident but glass landed around and on her child, and pet.  Glass landing where children would be sitting minutes later.  It took 6 hours to clean glass and there were still glass shards embedded in a nearby  hardwood floor.

3/11/15 The retailer was contacted so that they could notify the manufacturer and to halt the sale of it, however, they offered her a replacement for the same product.  She stated that she declined the offer due to the safety hazard it poses.

Consumer feels that this product is unsafe and should be recalled immediately before someone is seriously injured by spontaneously exploding glasstop.
justification: No injuries occurred, but the incident involved a hazardous glass explosion that could have caused harm.

incident_description:
I burned three Gold Canyon Volite candles during a party.  It was about three hours later, and things were winding down when the crowd had gathered in my kitchen.  

The candles were burning on a shelf in my living room.  The smoke detectors simultaneously went off and everyone went to check what was going on.  Sure enough, one of the Volites  was on fire, with a flame over 12 inches high coming off of it.  

Thankfully we were able to smother it with a large ceramic kitchen bowl to put it out!  
The plastic surrounding the candle had completely burned and melted through the little Gold Canyon metal wrap I had purchased with it.  Also, the wick had bloomed out in three places, about the size of a nickel.  Obviously that's what likely cause the plastic to ignite.

This was only the second time these candles had been burned.  The other two did not catch fire, but upon inspection, one of the other candles' plastic was becoming distorted and on its way to the same demise.
justification: The candle caught fire but was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description:
Last night, I turned my floor lamp on and after about 2 hours, the 72w GE Soft White bulb that I put in it exploded and spewed hot glass everywhere. The lamp was simply turned on and was not disturbed in any way, shape or form. The lamp itself ([REDACTED]) has not been modified in any way and was purchased from a reputable retailer (Home Depot). [REDACTED] indicates that this lamp can accomodate 2 100w light bulbs. I believe the bulb that exploded has been in the lamp for about 1 1/2 months and had been operating without incident on a regular basis since it was installed. 
The bulb is one out of a four pack labeled: GE Energy-Efficient Soft White 72w Modified Spectrum General Purpose Halogen Bulbs: UPC 043168662499 PC: 66249 RES: #1223578 CTNHALA194MB72GE66249CJCH-03
I took photos of the bulb and it appears the center glass tube exploded and that is why the bulb shattered. There also was a noxious burning smell when this happened and the glass was hot enough to actually burn my couch pillows.
It was quite an ordeal to vaccum up tiny shards of glass from my woven couch, throw blankets and everywhere within a 5 foot radius of the lamp.
I am reporting this incident because it does not appear that this product is safe for use. Luckily, no one was injured in this incident and only my pillows were burned, but I can see how something worse could happen if a child/infant was close by or if something caught on fire due to the explosion.
justification: The bulb exploded, causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the incident despite normal use.

incident_description:
I bought the Biddeford plush queen size electric blanket with two remotes in the denim color November 2013 from Kohls. A week ago I noticed a yellowish/greenish discolored area on the underside of the cover when I was changing the sheets on the bed, but thought maybe the covers underneath somehow discolored the electric blanket. Tonight I put something down on the bed and it was hot to the touch even though it was off but plugged in. I noticed two big green/brown patches on the cover on opposite ends as well as discoloration throughout the blanket that was all very hot. If I had not been home tonight I'm certain it would have started a fire.

This cover was very lightly used. There is no reason why it would do this. I will call the company but based off of what others said I'm doubtful much will be done.

The model number is OBF03. Tracking number is 06 (written in) N1941T-CDN
justification: The electric blanket showed signs of overheating and potential fire hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I have been using the Biddeford warming throw for two winters, this being the second. 
I was settling down to watch tv and turned on the blanket, within minutes, I felt a burning hot spot. I pulled the blanket away from me sparks flew and an acrid smoke came from the blanket plug in.
The hot spot is on the cord portion that plugs into the blanket. Needless to say, very scary.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased my home in 2010 and this medicine had already been installed in the bathroom. In 2011 the center mirror fell after the hinge broke in half. The same year, the right corner fell hurting my daughter causing lacerations to her head. This past year in December 2014, the left panel cracked as my son opened the cabinet. No one ever sent anything to the house to inform me about the recall, I was not the one who purchased the mirror, but the address of the mirror never changed.

I went to Lowes with a picture of the medicine cabinet and the customer service representative told me about the recall on these cabinets.
justification: The incident caused lacerations to the daughter's head, indicating an injury, and the mirror has fallen multiple times.

incident_description:
Below is the verbiage from the email I sent the company yesterday:

Yesterday 2/10/15; approx 1:00PM EST 
New lamp shades brought home and put in place in first fixture; no problem (see page 2 pic).


Second shade put in place. Installed EcoSmart bulb; turned switch on to test = INSTANT POP AND FIRE!!!
Before fire could spread; unplugged and put fire out.
The entire lamp is now a total loss (see attached pics). FORTUNATELY MY HOUSE IS NOT!!!
There is one bulb left from package (see pic). Knowing we have another one is our house that was from this package and not sure which of the light fixtures has this and now could be another possible fire hazard
is very disconcerting! We do know where the one in our bedroom is recently; replaced and we will get rid of it!!


We will now have to replace both lamps. 

I HAD A FLAMING FIRE IN MY HOUSE DUE TO A FAULTY ECOSMART BULB!!!! (See Page 1)
Is there a recall or safety bulletin out there that the public needs to be aware of???
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a faulty bulb, resulting in property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I purchased a Voluspa brand candle from Anthropologie a couple of years ago. I have never owned any other Voluspa brand before this. However, I do love candles and I have never had a problem with any other brand or type of candle before. That being said: I had the Voluspa 3 wick French Cade scented candle in the tin sitting on the bottom shelf on a built in bookcase in my home. (It sat in the same spot yesterday and burned for a couple of hours with no issue, by the way) The candle had been burning for about 45 minutes, in my sight the whole time. I was in the same room watching TV. I looked over and noticed the whole candle tin was engulfed in flames! I ran to the kitchen to get a cup of water and ran back to douse the tin. The thing was burning from the INSIDE OUT. I extinguished the flame and upon further inspection, the whole tin was charred and when I went to pick it up to move outside due to the smell, it was stuck to my shelf! When I removed it, the wood underneath was scorched and bubbled up. Completely ruined. It's not just a single shelf that I can easily remove as it is the bottom shelf of a built in bookcase. I emailed the company several hours ago to alert them to the problem...we'll see if I end up with a response. I'm thankful that I caught the fire before it spread to anything else but I'm thoroughly pissed off that I'm out the cost of this candle plus whatever it will take me to repair the damages. After some digging, I've discovered I'm not the only person this has happened to with these tins in particular. Voluspa should highly consider repackaging these candles because apparently the tins are flammable. The only warning the product comes with is the standard candle warnings, nothing about their less than mediocre tin that houses the otherwise pleasant candle. It's dangerous to their consumers. This is in no way a case of "consumer misuse", I've been burning varying brands of candles for years and burned the Voluspa the day prior all with no issue. It's not as if I set my shelf on fire and am looking to place blame. This thing erupted in flames out of nowhere. I will never purchase another Voluspa product.
justification: The incident involved a candle catching fire and causing property damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
12/25/2014, 12/26/2014 The consumer's daughter lit her two candles. 

12/27/2014 The consumer's daughter noticed that one of the jars had burnt black, more so than the other one, which appeared to have burned normally. Her daughter told the consumer that her nasal mucus was black. Her daughter did not make the connection that it was possibly due to the candles. 

The consumer's son-in-law was vomiting for a couple of days but the consumer nor her daughter are able to connect his illness to the candles.

01/06/2015 The consumer's daughter lit some candles during dinner, one of which was the second candle in question. 

01/07/2015 The consumer had black nasal mucus as well. When she cleaned her grand child's mucus with cotton swabs, it were also black. The baby nor the consumer took any medications as the consumer decided to let it run its course.

When the consumer went to make the baby a bottle, the white bottle cap was black, as well as all the baby's other bottle caps. Many things in the home were black: bottle caps inside cabinets, utensils, cabinets, toys, portable bath tub, curtains, windows, door corners, chandelier, metal plates for the water sprinkler system that is built into the ceiling, blinds, lighting domes, wood furniture, etc. All in all, most of everything that was plastic or metal on all floor levels. The consumer believes the smoke traveled through the ventilation system, so she decided to change the air filter. The consumer indicates that the filter was completely black.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard. The consumer plans on contacting the manufacturer.
justification: The incident caused black nasal mucus and vomiting, indicating health effects, but no death was reported.

incident_description: The mirror door on my SCS24-(NM) medicine cabinet broke and crashed onto my forehead before hitting the sink cabinet top and breaking.  Both SCS24-(NM) door hinges broke allowing the door to free fall onto my forehead.  I sustained a laceration and nice goose egg as the result of the faulty hinges.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration and a goose egg, indicating an injury, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description:
My bathroom scale was a model made by the Taylor Precision Products company, they are located in Las Cruces, NM. We have owned this item for around one year having purchased it in the local K-Mart. It is model #7506 which had a glass top which was stood on to obtain your weight from a digital readout.

A few days ago when my wife stepped on the unit to get her weight it shattered with such force that shards of glass and small pieces of glass traveled at least 10-15 feet. Glass covered the bathroom and adjacent bedroom. She sustained glass cuts to her feet and legs, has tiny flakes of glass all over her body and one in her right eye. The scale was on the floor, had never been dropped or damaged in any way. My wife weighs approximately 140 pounds, I weigh approximately 190 lbs, neither of us have ever used the scale in any way other than to stand on it barefoot.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including cuts and glass fragments in the eye, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is considered possible (3) given the unexpected nature of the scale shattering under normal use.

incident_description:
A light bulb exploded in my kitchen. The fixture was scorched and burnt. 
The fixture was dry, not a dimmer-type and not enclosed. It was not subject to vibration.
The light bulb was Felt electric Conserv-Energy CE23T2/3(N) 23w 120vac 60Hz 383mA
1600 Lumens- UL #E170906
justification: The light bulb exploded and caused scorching, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: We were using a GE Helical 20 watt light bulb.  It started smoking then flaming at the junction between the glass and the base.  Fortunately we were present and turned it off.  Yhe bulb says 120VAC 60Hz 300mA FLE 20 HT 3/2/SW
justification: The bulb started smoking and flaming, but was turned off before causing injury.

incident_description:
2/23/2015 The consumer was moving the table slightly toward the wall. As soon as he touched the table, the glass top exploded. The only items on the table was a lap top and two phones.

The consumer cut the small finger on his left hand. No medical attention was required.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor injury (cut finger) but did not require medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances of the glass table top exploding upon slight movement.

incident_description:
(02/17/2015) The consumer stated that he turned the light either on or off. He was not sure. There was a bang and the light exploded. The entire kitchen was covered with glass.

The bulb was in an overhead fixture in the middle of the kitchen.

No injuries.


(02/28/2015)The consumer contacted the company to advised them of the incident. The company advised the consumer that they had never heard of anything like that happening before. He was asked to send pictures of the incident.  The consumer asked the company to remove the bulb from the fixture. He was advised that they could not because they were located in California and he was in New Jersey.

The consumer called Costco who offered to replace the product.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb exploding, covering the kitchen with glass, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: For a year or so I get up of a morning just not feeling right. I've never been a sickly person. My husband is also experiencing different symptoms. I finally ask myself... Can your mattress make you sick? I got online and was SO shocked at what I read. You say your bettering our sleep with added flame retardant protection . But we're actually being poisoned every night we sleep on our bed! Using pesticides like arsenic and roach killer! We're breathing this stuff and taking it in through our skin!  I've read all the things this can do to adults, babies, unborn babies...Id rather take my chances with the almost zero percent of my mattress burning than to know we are slowly being poisoned EVERY NIGHT ! Your bed should be a place of rest and peaceful sleep NOT lying down with our potential killer every night.
justification: The description indicates potential long-term health effects from exposure to harmful chemicals, which qualifies as injury, and the likelihood is high given the nightly exposure.

incident_description:
A chair broke causing injury to myself and I Googled for it and found out it had been recalled which was news to me. Reading the recall notice, it says that "bolts attaching the seatback on the recalled chairs can loosen and detach, posing a fall and injury hazard to consumers".  This misstates the problem entirely. The real problem is not that bolts loosen and detach, the problem is that the bolts fail under tension load. That means that tightening them may make the problem MORE likely to occur and one may think that tight bolts would mean that they are safe. The bolts supplied in the seat back attachment are made from pot metal and not hardened steel. The failure mode occurred with bolts fully tight. The recall notice must state that the problem is that the bolts are not strong enough for the task and NOT say that the bolts may come loose. A thinking person may be mislead to believe that he is safe if the bolts are tight and this is not the case. Please have them change this language and keep them from misstating the facts. I have a neck injury as the result of two snapped bolts causing a fall against a filing cabinet.  See below for what I have pasted from the release that I found on line:

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
October 16, 2009
Release # 10-013	Firm's Recall Hotline: (866) 244-8180
CPSC Recall Hotline: (800) 638-2772
CPSC Media Contact: (301) 504-7908
Raynor Marketing Recalls Quantum Office Chairs Due to Fall Hazard; Sold Exclusively at Office Depot Stores

WASHINGTON, D.C. - The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, in cooperation with the firm named below, today announced a voluntary recall of the following consumer product. Consumers should stop using recalled products immediately unless otherwise instructed. It is illegal to resell or attempt to resell a recalled consumer product.

Name of Product: Quantum Realspace PROÃÂ 9000 Series Mid-Back Multifunction Mesh Chair and Multifunction Mesh Chair with Headrest

Units: About 150,000

Importer: Raynor Marketing LTD, of West Hempstead, N.Y.

Manufacturer: Comfort Office Furniture, LTD, China aka Evergood Co. Ltd.

Hazard: The bolts attaching the seatback on the recalled chairs can loosen and detach, posing a fall and injury hazard to consumers.

Incidents/Injuries: Raynor has received reports of 33 seatback detachments and 14 injuries involving bumps and bruises.

Description: This recall involves the Quantum Realspace PROÃÂ 9000 Series Mid-Back Multifunction Mesh Chair SKU # 510830 and the Quantum Realspace PROÃÂ 9000 Series Mesh Chair with Headrest SKU # 690690. The Realspace PROÃÂ Mesh Guest Chair is not involved in this recall.

Sold: Exclusively at Office Depot stores nationwide and on the Web at www.OfficeDepot.com from May 2006 through August 2009. The mid-back chairs sold for about $300 and the chair with headrest for about $350.
justification: The incident resulted in a neck injury due to the chair's structural failure, indicating a severity level of 3. The recall notice reports 14 injuries out of 150,000 units, suggesting an occurrence likelihood of 2 (unlikely).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her husband was sitting in the chair and rocking. The consumer's husband went to pick something up on the left side of him while he was in the chair.

The consumer stated that the plastic bracket that bolts onto the bottom of the chair broke off in two places. The chair tipped over and the consumer's husband fell to the side, out of the chair. The consumer's husband was not injured.

The consumer stated that the plastic bracket that broke off bolts onto two springs. 

The consumer tried calling the retailer but the number was disconnected.
justification: The chair tipped over and the consumer's husband fell, but he was not injured, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: My oldest daughter had my youngest daughter on her back. She knelt down to set her on the bed and as she did lost her balance. She bumped side of bed and the rail snapped in half. You can see the weekness in the rail.
justification: The incident involved a bed rail snapping but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) due to the visible weakness in the rail suggesting it could happen again.

incident_description:
Spring Air mattress was recommended to us. So, we received the bed as a gift.
2,3 days the bed worked the way it was supposed. 4th day. It got stuck on the Up possition" at the headboard.
I would like to know where I can obtain a new "remote control" since this situation is causing a lot of pain to my husband by not being able to move the bed.
[REDACTED]
justification: The bed malfunction caused pain to the husband, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The base shattered when my boyfriend was sitting in the chair ... he leaned back and ended up on the floor bleeding after the plastic base that was holding the caster on, broke in pieces and punctured his leg behind his knee on the way to the floor.
justification: The incident resulted in a puncture wound, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a tempered glass desk from Ikea two years ago. It spontaneously shattered two weeks ago. The shards of glass went everywhere, from large pieces to tiny pieces. I am very thankful no one was in the room at the time. 
Everything on the desk came crashing to the floor, including my computer monitor, hard drive, printer etc. 
I immediately contacted customer service at Ikea with images of the damage and was expecting a timely response and an offer to refund my purchase as well as issue a recall for this item. I was very disappointed with the service I am receiving from them.
After some research, this has happened to many customers with Ikea's glass desks and no recall has been issued. I am still in conversations with Ikea in attempts to work out a solution. I have also requested a professional cleaning allowance, as this room will soon be my brand new baby's room. With shards of glass in the carpet, I do not feel comfortable unless this is professionally cleaned. 
I am most upset that no recall has been issued. This is a major safety issue that could do a lot of bodily harm.
justification: The glass desk shattered, causing property damage but no injuries, as no one was present in the room at the time.

incident_description: At about 9:15 pm I turned on the Sure Fit heated furniture cover and laid down on the couch . I fell asleep and woke up around 11pm and smelled something burning and I felt a little burning on my back. After investigating the burning smell through whole house I pulled back the heated cover and it had burned through to the couch where I was laying. I felt extremely anxiety since I think I may have caught on fire. I have only owned this heat giver for about 2 weeks . I have owned heated mattress pad for years and never any issue.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and minor burning sensation, but no serious injury occurred.

incident_description:
My son plugged in a heated blanket made by Sunbeam.  The control started on fire, then self extinguished, leaving a black soot on a chair and causing a lot of smoke from the control.  Because the nature of the product is bedding, I felt compelled to file a report.  Normally, I would just throw it in the trash, but if I can help someone else so be it.

The control is labeled Style T85A E23623.
justification: The incident involved a fire and smoke but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
12/12/2014 The consumer un-boxed his Christmas tree and put it together bare-hands. The consumer indicates that it was relatively simple to put together. The consumer did not feel any puncture wounds while doing so. The consumer states that it took it approximately twenty minutes to put it together. 

Immediately after putting it together, the consumer proceeded to shower as he states the unit made him itchy all over, indicating that he felt that he had fiberglass in his eyes. The consumer had to use [REDACTED] to clear his eyes. After a couple of days, the consumer states that the all-over itch went away. 

The same evening of the installation, the consumer felt a splinter on his right, ring finger. He was unable to see or take out the object that bothered him, so he left it as is assuming that it would eventually come out on its own. 

12/13/2014 The consumer states that the next evening he noticed his finger beginning. 

12/14/2014 The consumer woke up to a very painful finger and a swelling right hand, as well as slightly swelling knuckles. The consumer spoke to his girlfriend as he was concerned, and they determined that if it did not get any better by the next day, he would have to visit a physician. 

12/15/2014 The consumer contacted his Doctor and unable to get an appointment for that same day, he went to his local hospital. The consumer indicates that he could not wait as his hand was swelling and hurting more, as well as beginning to lose finger movement ability. 

The consumer was seen by the physician in the ER. He was diagnosed with cellulitis and was given a prescription for antibiotics in the form of [REDACTED]100mg twice a day for ten days.  He was told that if his condition did not improve within the next couple of days, that he should revisit the Doctor. 

The consumer fell worse during the next couple of days. Feeling more pain, his hand was getting even more swollen, now including his palm, while his right, ring finger could not move at all. 

12/18/2014 The consumer went back to the ER as he was not experiencing any improvements with his condition. The consumer was immediately admitted to the hospital. The consumer was put on intravenous antibiotics. In the meantime, the Doctor determined he needed hand surgery and so a specialist was contacted. During this time, they did some exams as well as took x-rays which showed no foreign object. 

12/19/2014 The consumer had a successful hand surgery in the evening. The surgeon informed the consumer his hand was filled with pus, which were drained from four incisions.

12/22/2014 The consumer was discharged from the hospital and he states that his hand is still healing. He estimates he can close his hand approximately 3/4 way. As far as nerve damage, the consumer and his Doctor have not really touched the subject but the possibility of nerve damage exists though the Doctor does not know to what extent yet as the consumer has yet to fully heal. 

01/19/2015 The consumer is scheduled for a follow-up appointment. 

01/02/2015 (Approximately) The consumer contacted the retailer and explained what happened. The representative he spoke to informed the Store Manager but all they said was that because it was a product complaint, he would have to contact the manufacturer instead

The consumer contacted the manufacturer and explained what happened with him to a representative by the name of [REDACTED] . The representative informed the consumer that she had never heard a situation like that. SHe also informed the consumer that he would have to submit a formal letter with pictures of what happened. 

The consumer filed a complaint with his state Attorney General under Case No: [REDACTED]. 

The consumer states that he believes the Christmas tree is the source of the ailment as he did not do anything out of the ordinary the previous days before installing it and only became sick almost immediately after he installed the unit. 

The consumer states that he will decide how to proceed once his hand fully heals as he wants to have something to tell to the people he contacts. The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard.
justification: The consumer suffered from cellulitis and required surgery, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident is unlikely (likelihood 2) as the representative had never heard of such a situation.

incident_description: In 2013, Home Depot sold me a Medicine Cabinet.  Yesterday, the large center mirrored door's hinges both simultaneously broke and the door struck and injured my wife.  I believe these hinges are made of 'pot metal' and I believe that is a very poor choice of material for a hinge.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the wife when the cabinet door fell due to broken hinges.

incident_description:
Compact florescent light bulb failed and caught fire.

Just noticed the bulb was blinking. Removed the fixture cover. Checked to see if it was screwed in properly. Went outside briefly and when I returned I noticed descending soot particles. Looked up to see bulb separated from base and flames where the glass seats into the base. Turned off the light switch and removed the hot bulb.
justification: The bulb caught fire, which is a significant incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(01/11/2015) The consumer stated that there is a strong smell in the mattress. The consumer stated she slept on the mattress for the first time. The consumer stated that she had a tight chest and her face was tingling when she woke up the next morning. The consumer stated that she did not sleep in the bed again until Wednesday. When she woke up on Thursday morning, she had to massage her eyes open and her face was also tingling.

The consumer did not require medical attention.

(01/10/2015) The consumer stated that she called the company before she slept on the mattress to advised them of the strong smell.  She was advised to rub baking soda on the mattress to absorb the odor.
justification: The consumer experienced physical symptoms (tight chest, tingling face, difficulty opening eyes) but did not require medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as such reactions to mattress odors are not common.

Metal staples secure the bed slatts into place underneath.  My toddler easily removed a metal staple.    The staple that my child removed was small, sharp and a serious choking hazard.  If a child swallowed one of these it could be fatal.

The consumer stated that she plugged in the blanket and turned it on. The consumer stated that she saw a spark in the wiring and heard crackling sound.

The consumer stated that a fire started in the wire immediately. 

The consumer pulled the plug out of the socket.

The consumer left a message for the manf at 1-800-789-6441 on 1/29/15.

There are no recalls on this blanket.

incident_description:
To Whom it May Concern:

February

I Purchased the TEMPUR - Rhapsody mattress from a Tempur endorsed retailer in Birmingham, AL in the Spring of 2013.  

I immediately began exhibiting symptoms of an allergic skin reaction.  Due diligence requried me to explore every possibility before forming the hypothesis upon which this incident report is founded.  

I have medical records to show that no such skin reactions were present in my medical record prior to owning this mattress.  When I was sold the mattress, no one mentioned nor did any warning labels explicitly state the potential for skin reactions or anything of that nature.

I am confident that the Tempur-Pedic North America, Inc should be held responsibile in part for knowingly selling a product which has the potential to inflict consumers with this infirmity.  

Thanks and kind regards.
justification: The description reports an allergic skin reaction, which qualifies as an injury, but the likelihood of such an incident is deemed unlikely based on the provided context.

incident_description:
In 2012 I purchased a dining room set from The Dump in Langhorne, PA, consisting of one drop-leaf table and six chairs.

Since the purchase I have had two of the chairs collapse while occupied. The first incident occurred while I was sitting on the chair eating dinner. The second occurred as my wife shifted forward preparing to rise from the chair.

In my incident I fell to the floor. I sustained a contusion on my buttock but I did not require nor did I seek medical attention. My wife was lucky enough to be able to grab the table and prevent a fall.

In the first instance the chair was replaced under warranty as it occurred less than one year after purchase. I am now told that the second chair will not be replaced as the warranty has expired.

Inspection of these chairs revealed that the failure point was near where the frame which supports the seat was notched out to accept a diagonal brace. It appears that this significantly weakened the frame at that point. I can supply photos if needed.

I am informed by [REDACTED] of The Dump that they have checked with the manufacturer (which was unnamed) and they will not replace this due to the expiration of the warranty. They further stated that the model has been discontinued.
justification: The incident resulted in a contusion (injury) from a chair collapse, and a near-miss with potential for injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as two chairs collapsed under normal use.

incident_description:
I complained to Jordan's Furniture with the following report:

This is regarding a power sofa recliner we purchased from JordanÃÂs Furniture and was delivered to our home on 9-3-10.  One side had been stalling and not working properly.  While a family member was activating the recliner another family member from across the room saw sparks shooting from underneath.  At least one of these sparks that I observed remained a hot ember for a period of time.  I have since covered the bare wire with electrical tape, but have unplugged and not used this half of our sofa for fear that it will burn down our home.
I have photographs that show that the wire that goes from the switch (on the right side of the sofa) to the motor had been rubbed repeatedly and damaged by the black metal moving hinged arm that opens the footrest, apparently for some time.  The wire insulation had been worn away, exposing bare wire which was arcing with the black metal moving parts.  Your manufacturer had attached this wire with two zip ties.  The wire is routed differently on the left and right sides of the sofa.
Now I understand the motors, wiring and electrical components on this sofa were only warranted for one year (hence no longer covered).  However, the warranty clearly states that ÃÂthe black metal patented parts of the reclining mechanism carry a limited lifetime warranty. The reclining mechanism is warranted to be free of defects for as long as you the original consumer, own the furniture.ÃÂ  When these parts damage wiring, causing electrical arcing, I would call that a defect.
The metal arm began rubbing on the wire at some point in the past, probably as soon as we began using it.  When my wife called about fixing this, she was told it was out of warranty and a service order was written up for:   ÃÂRecliner stalling and making sparks. Need [REDACTED] for wire cover: 290-32-W/290-17.  Finish:TP/323-16   [REDACTED] ÃÂ motor wireÃÂ, and she was charged $79.00 plus tax.
I am absolutely appalled that (1)  A couch that you sold us is sparking in a hidden area, and regardless of the fact that you have sold this piece of furniture to hundreds, if not thousands of unsuspecting consumers, you were not interested in finding out what was going on.  (2)  That you assumed it was the motor, quickly pointed out that it was no longer covered by warranty, and were glad to sell us one for $79.00, and would come and install it for an additional charge.  (I had been expecting a new wire only, not a motor assembly).  (3)  Since we (and how many other unsuspecting customers) opted out of paying for your installation costs, you apparently are not concerned enough to even follow up with a phone call ÃÂHey did that fix stop our couch from sparking?ÃÂ
How many family rooms have been set on fire, or homes burnt down, or God forbid, lives impacted or lost due to this potential fire hazard?  Because of all of the above I am also filing a complaint with Consumer Products Safety Commission.
Has this issue come to your attention before? And is there a fix that we have not been made aware of?
justification: The incident involved sparks and potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the described defect.

incident_description: I lit a Bath and Body works three wick candle in my kitchen, and was doing laundry in the adjoining bathroom, about 30-45 minutes after lighting it, it burst into a huge fireball and exploded all over the place, damaging my stove, counter, and the electronics, with hot wax splattered everywhere.  The flames almost reached to the ceiling.  I have never seen anything like it.
justification: The candle explosion caused significant property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: 12 week old baby in swaddle sure sleep pouch by halo. He was asleep and the Velcro edge scratched his chin and made it bleed when he was being restless.
justification: The baby's chin was scratched and bled, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 8 year old daughter [REDACTED] was using the Disco Ball in her room while playing music on her TV.  She had decided after and hour she was finished and turned the light off.  It fell off of the table when she set it down and the cover came off of the light.  The light bulb base and bulb was exposed and when she grabbed the base her inner wrist bumped the hot bulb and got burnt badly.  She came right in to me and I noticed the skin was blistered and red.  I then took the 1st aid kit and treated the burn.  The burn has continued to cause a great deal of pain to the sight and very well may scar.
justification: The child suffered a burn that blistered and may scar, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: In November 2014, my husband and I received two sofas from Hancock and Moore, which included a Settlement Sofa and Galligher Loveseat. In December 2014, my husband and I received 4 Hancock and Moore Princeton Chairs and ottomans. We were very excited about this purchase, however we were extremely disappointed when the furniture arrived. All the pieces were class 3 leather Gaucho Mocha Burnished. When they arrived they looked beautiful however had an extremely strong chemical odor to them. We had to leave our house for two days because we were getting headaches and sneezing! We were/are very concerned for the quality of our health at this point. We just purchased a $650 air purifier, which will hopefully help! As we are expecting a baby in the summer, you can imagine my fears about the chemicals that we have brought in to our home. We had an air quality specialist come to our home to inquire about testing the air quality in our home. He recommended that we first speak with Hancock and Moore to find out exactly what chemicals were used on these sofas and chairs. Several attempts have been made to reach out to Hancock and Moore to find out the products used on the sofas and chairs that would be releasing these toxic fumes in our home. Hancock and Moore has refused to cooperative and disclose any information on the products used. They stated it is a trade secret. We are extremely disappointed with the chemical fumes that have been brought in to our home from this furniture. This has been detrimental to our health.
justification: The incident caused headaches and sneezing, indicating injury (severity 3), and similar issues have been reported frequently (occurrence 4).

incident_description:
The sofa bed is built with a metal frame, with a canvas upon which the mattress sets.  Part of the canvas contains embedded metal rods.  Metal coil springs are used on the right side of the frame, and attach to the canvas, going over the embedded rods so they do not pull through the canvas.  There is room for tension when folding and unfolding the mattress.

The top frame of the mattress uses solid metal rods, which also rely upon the embedded metal rods to support the canvas.  There is no allowance for tension.  The left side of the frame has open metal rods, with an open fishhook style loop which attaches to the canvas, putting tension on the embedded metal rod.  This has caused a smal flesh wound as the metal rods tore against the canvas and pulled a large portion of the embedded rod, leaving it exposed as a sharp metal spike.


The sofa bed is now unusable due to instability, and the danger created by a spike of metal exposed from the mattress support.
justification: The incident resulted in a small flesh wound due to exposed sharp metal, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Saturday, Feb. 7th 2015, my 6 year old son sat on a WalMart/Mainstay folding chair and it collapsed, causing great injury to his right ring finger.  It's an open fracture between the cuticle and first knuckle.  We (including my son) could see the bone and the break.  We took him to the Emergency Room and they had to do two sets of stitches (one set being THROUGH the fingernail) and we are scheduled to see an orthopedic hand specialist on Thursday Feb. 13th to discuss possible surgery.  

He is now adamant about not sitting on folding chairs and wants us to destroy the ones we purchased in the set.  He is missing school and not able to do homework, as he is unable to write with the splint and the pain.
justification: The incident resulted in an open fracture requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). Folding chair collapses are not common but do occur, making the likelihood unlikely (2).

incident_description:
My husband purchased the Pyros set for our patio from Walmart.  we were keeping it on our outdoor patio when one afternoon while cooking in the kitchen which overlooks the patio with a sliding glass door I hear a huge "blast"!  I was so startled I thought a gun had been fired, to the point I nearly dropped the pan I was cooking in. When my husband came running in to check out the situation we both looked toward the patio at the same time and saw that the entire glass table top had completely shattered to the point there was not any remaining pieces remaining in the frame.  Only thousands of glass shards all over the patio.
I  was grateful that my son who often sits absent wearing any shoes, along with myself and husband who regularly wear flip flops were not sitting around the table at that moment or we would have been cut to pieces if not worse lost a foot.
justification: The incident involved a shattered glass table with no injuries, but potential for severe harm if people were present.

incident_description: I bought a Biddeford electric blanket from Kohl's a couple of years ago for a young friend of my daughter's. It caught fire the other night while she was sleeping! I'm horrified. I'm horrified to see that it's an ongoing problem for many years but that these dangerous products were still for sale not too long ago! I am so thankful she is okay.
justification: The electric blanket caught fire, which is a serious incident, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: In March of 2005, I purchased a set of patio furniture from PatioFurnitureUSA.com, Catamira Patio Set, item #WY155-50104200. Two days ago, I was sitting at my desk near an open window when I heard a cracking noise and looked up and out the window in time to see the glass top on the aforementioned patio table break and crumble into millions of pieces onto the deck. Nothing had fallen on the table, there was no wind, and the temperature was a mild 75 degrees at most. I have no explanation for the spontaneous implosion. Fortunately we were not having lunch at the table and our dog was in the house.
justification: The glass table top broke spontaneously but no one was injured, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she went to bed with the blanket under her bed sheet. The consumer went to pull up the blanket and the sheet and noticed that the blanket was sparking. The consumer stated that the blanket was sparking all over not just in one part. The consumer jumped out of the bed and took the blanket off of the bed. The consumer stated that she unplugged the blanket immediately. The consumer stated that the blanket was running on low (heat setting at 4/5) and had it on for about 2 hours before this incident happened.

The consumer stated that she called the company on 1/23/15 at 800-789-6441. The consumer spoke to a representative about the incident. The representative stated that they have gotten similar complaint about their blankets. The consumer asked if there was a recall on her blanket. The consumer was informed that there is no recall on this blanket. The representative asked the consumer to ship back the blanket for their inspection purposes. The consumer was informed that she would receive a replacement blanket. The consumer did not want a replacement blanket unless it was a different model/style.

The consumer was informed by the company representative that they will have their engineers check the blanket out when they receive it. The representative informed the consumer that they will put a recall on these blankets if they receive more complaints.

The consumer stated that she will hold onto the blanket in case anyone from CPSC wants to see if for inspection purposes. 

P.S.- They never sent the consumer a different blanket
justification: The incident involved sparking but no injury occurred, and similar complaints have been reported, indicating a possible but not certain recurrence.

incident_description:
(01/04/2015) The consumer stated she found that the fingers of the snowman have needle like strands are sharp. The consumer stated that one of the strands pricked her finger on her left hand. One of the strands fell out. It measured about seven inches in length.

The consumer is concerned that the strands can poke out the eye of a child. The strand can also scratch a child or be ingested by a child. 


The consumer did not not require medical attention.

Addendum to report:

The section on Product Detail has  product listed as 24" x 26". This needs to be corrected.  When consumer spoke with the CPSC representative on January 9, 2015 consumer mentioned that the product (pillow) was between 24 to 26 inches in length.

Consumer contacted the manufacturer, Franco Manufacturing Co. in writing since my conversation with one of our representatives.  Consumer heard from the manufacturer on Monday, February 2, 2015. Consumer has enclosed for your information a copy of the letter consumer sent to Franco Manufacturing and a copy of the letter they sent her.

The Frozen character pillow, Olaf, has what appear to be antlers on the top of the head. These antlers are made of the same material as the arms and hands and are also filled with the same plastic filaments as the arms, hands and fingers.

Consumer has enclosed photographs of the pillow and close-up photographs of the hand and filaments.

This product is advertised toward children.

Submitted by: [REDACTED]
justification: The consumer experienced a minor injury (pricked finger) from the sharp strands, but did not require medical attention. The product is marketed to children, increasing the likelihood of similar incidents.

incident_description: I distinguished a 3 wick bath and body candle by placing the lid that was sold with the candle and it caused a vacuum tight seal so that when I opened the candle up using my hands the glass broke  in my hands. I have reported this problem before approximately a year ago  to the bath and body corporate customer service number listed and these candles are still being sold like this. The consumer noticed the light bulb had exploded and the glass was everywhere. The consumer states the light fixture is above the dining table and he found glass approximately 8 feet from the light fixture. The consumer states the glass from the light bulb was moist. The consumer states he would turn the light on daily.

The consumer removed the bulb from the fixture and has all the glass pieces in his possession.

The consumer states there are 2 bulbs in the fixture, however, the other bulb works fine.

incident_description: I have a office chair at my home.  The brand is true innovations and the model is 41832 with ITM. 633882.  While I was leaning back on it 2 of the bolts that secure the upper cushion to the chair sheared about a 1/4 inch below the bolt head.  There are 4 bolt that hold the upper to the lower.  The 2 with the greatest amount of tension snapped.  The shear appears to a almost smooth shear except for one sharp edge that appears to be where the bolt thread was.  I have contacted the manufacturer and I am waiting for a response.
justification: The incident involved a chair failure but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We purchased a new mattress (Stearns and Foster, Cal King) and when it was delivered on Monday, January 26,  the odor was very strong.  We opened windows and turned on fans and left the bed unmade for 8 hours.  That evening we made the bed and tried to sleep in it - my husband only lasted 90 minutes before leaving for the guestroom with a burning throat and headache.  I sleep on multiple pillows, so I made it through the first night, but woke up extremely ill - wheezing, eyes tearing, nose watering, severe heqadache and swollen throat.  I called the store on Tuesday morning and was told to remove bedding and air out mattress every day and it should dissipate in about a week.  We have bought at least a dozen mattresses and never had this issue before. I slept on the couch and  my husband on our futon that night.  My husband was still so ill he missed work half a day on Tuesday and all day Wednesday.  I was having shortness of breath and my chest was tight.  I called the manufacturer of Stearns and Foster and was told IT CAN TAKE UP TO 60 DAYS to offgass. I asked why they weren't aired out before being sealed in plastic and shipped and was told it was their policy to ship as soon as they are made.  I called the store and was told they could have an inspector come on Feb 11, and until then they could not remove the mattress.  I informed them that by then I would be in the hospital and my dog would be dead.  We got an appointment that night.  That afternoon I suffered my first full blown asthma attack in 30 YEARS!  Ended up at urgent care and needed a breathing treatment, and inhalers and steroids were prescribed because of my wheezing and extreme shortness of breath.  The inspector agreed that the odor was strong and recommended it be removed, but the company couldn't send anyone out until at least the following week.  The next day I was in urgent care again because my asthma had worsened and I had to be given antibiotics.  The Doctor wrote a note recommending immediate removal of the mattress, which was faxed to them the next morning.  Still no hurry on the part of Ortho Mattress, and I was told that if we moved it to the garage we would void the warranty.  Finally, after at least a dozen calls, we got an appointment for removal on Saturday, January 31. The fumes released   while packing up the mattress were so strong that as soon as they walked out the door with it, I fainted and needed to use my recue inhaler twice. Today I went to get gas in my car and had to pull over and use my inhaler again and wait for about 30 minutes before leaving the gas station.  I am now having to see my first pulmonary specialist since I was 30 - I am 58.  I am concerned that there has been permanent damage to my lungs, I am angry at the lack of a timely and humane response from Ortho Mattress and the cavalier attitude towards safety shown by Stearns and Foster, who is now owned together with Sealy by Tempurpedic.  I worry about the health of delivery employees who open plastic on new, un-aired out mattress sometimes 100 times a day. There should be a law requiring mattresses be off-gassed prior to shipping.  There should be ventilation holes in the plastic so they can continue to air before delivery.  There should be warnings to all consumers, especially ones who have any history of respiratory illness, to request things be aired prior to delivery.  I did not ask them to do this, as I have never in my life had this problem or known anyone else who has had the same issue.  We're not talking "new car smell."  We're talking mustard gas!  The bed has been gone now for almost 48 hours and I still can't enter my bedroom.  If, as the Stearns and Foster representative stated, this is due to "new mattress technology" than laws and warnings need to be implemembted to protect consumers and workers from these toxins.
justification: The incident caused severe respiratory issues, asthma attacks, and required medical treatment, indicating significant health impact.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the natural log starting emitting black smoke and odor, it caused a burning sensation to her eyes, and she became dizzy.  No medical attention was received. incident_description: I have had a Cree 13.5 watt light bulb on my daughters night stand in a lamp for over a year.  I was reading her a book this evening and noticed the light was smoking.  Upon further inspection I realized the bottom of the bulb had caught fire.  This was of immediate concern and extreme worry to me.
justification: The bulb caught fire but there was no injury reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was in the bathroom was at the sink, when I looked up and the center mirror started to fall out  I caught it before it hit the floor and realized after examining it, the mirror holder rotted and broke off.
justification: The mirror fell but was caught before hitting the floor, resulting in no injury.

incident_description: On 1/17/15, ii purchased 2 velvet flocked ring stands from Ross stores. I placed them atop the dresser near my bed. I became progressively ill and weak and suffered headaches and malaise. On Wednesday, January 28, 2015, I felt so weak, I stayed in bed most of the day. That evening as I lay in bed, my husband asked what was wrong. I told him I felt ill. He said, he smelled an odor like fuel/gas. I traced the smell to the ring stands. He confirmed it. The stands were emitting a gas-like odor. I placed them outside of the house in a plastic storage bench On Wednesday, Thursday and Friday nights. I sat them out during the day for approximately 12 hours to see if they would air out. They have not. I pondered what I should do about it so I am making this complaint. The stands are distributed by Darice, Inc., Strongsville, Ohio. The UPC numbers are 8267626896-0. I purchased them for 9.99 each.
justification: The incident caused illness and weakness, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: After adjusting the bed to desired position, the bed started going up on its on.  It continued to go as far as it could, then I heard this ticking sound as if the bed had reached its stressed level then it just woundn't move anymore. As I attempted to let the bed back down it just would not respond.  It started sparking then I smelled and saw smoke.  I immediately unpluged the unit and then felt it, it was very hot.  I didnt notice the seriousness until the repair guy turned the bed over and it was burned underneath on the surface of the foundation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning bed that sparked and smoked, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: My son, [REDACTED], was almost 7 1/2 months old when he was at daycare napping and a weighted blanket, identified as a a weighted heatable baby shawl from Grampa's Garden, was placed on him.  [REDACTED] had rolled onto his belly from his back before the blanket was placed on him.  Hours later, when they attempted to get him up from a nap, he was unconscious and not breathing.  His face was pressed against the [REDACTED] of the crib and the blanket was bunched around his waist.  [REDACTED] died the next day (8/21/14).  There was no warning or direction on the blanket indicating that such blanket should not be used on a child under the age of one, or should only be used under the direction or prescription by a doctor or therapist.  The blanket weighed almost 5 pounds and my [REDACTED] only weighed about 17 pounds at the time.  There was also no direction or warning as to weight restrictions for such blanket.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to the use of a weighted blanket, indicating the highest severity level.

incident_description:
(12/30/2014) The consumer states that the light bulb in the table lamp started to flicker. The consumer look into the top of the lamp shade and saw flames and smoke coming the base of the lamp. The consumer unplugged the lamp. When her husband got home, he took the bulb out of the lamp and replaced it with one of the old style bulbs. The lamp worked fine.

The consumer has the same bulbs in lights throughout the hose but have not had a problem.
