incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern,
I am extremely upset by the dangerous and deadly Sofia+Sam Deluxe Memory Foam Lap Desk With Light [ASIN: B006L3M882]. My grandchildren have used it every night since Christmas (2 weeks). One night it caught on fire. The battery pack became so hot that it melted and burnt the inside foam of the inner-cushion. My son immediately grabbed it and ran outside where it completely caught on fire. Outside, he immediately reached inside to pull out the battery pack, which caused second degree burns to his fingers and hand. The manufacturer should order a massive recall before they kill a child as a result of this faulty product. It's obvious that the battery pack is very cheaply made and it does not have a safety metal flap to prevent the battery from touching the plastic - a deadly cost saving tactic by an irresponsible manufacturer.  Note also the attached picture of the label attached to the product.  It states that "THIS ARTICLE DOES NOT MEET CALIFORNIA BUREAU OF HOME FURNISHING'S  FLAMMABILITY  REQUIREMENTS - TECHNICAL BULLETIN 117".  The manufacturer should have to pay a significant fine for their lack of safety standards.  Please tell everyone about this dangerous product. Here are a few pictures as evidence:
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns to the user's hand, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the description of the battery pack overheating and catching fire.

incident_description: Item is a weight scale to measure a persons weight. The scale has two thing metal strips that are 1-2 inches wide that span on both sides of the scale to measure a persons weight. The left metal strips adhesive came off the glass scale about 4 inches off the scale is peeling back. I repeatedly have to push the strip back onto the scale. Today after measuring my weight, i stepped back onto the scale, the metal strip lodged underneath my left foot, and left a 2 inch wide gash about 2-3cm deep into my foot. i began to bleed profusely for 2 hours. and was rushed to the emergency room. This weight scale is a health hazard as it can easily cut a persons foot. There is no reason to have such a thin sharp metal piece that is attached with a cheap adhesive to be on here. my foot 12 hours later is still bleeding due to the depth of the laceration. I have been ordered to stay home for a week for recovery and required to get stitches today in the ER.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep laceration requiring emergency medical attention and stitches, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
This form quit on me unexpectedly in the process of filling it out, not sure if you have a partial of this report already- therefore Redoing this form, 
Walmart Great Value BR30 Floodlight, 40 watt, energy Saver Halogen light bulb - installed in my kitchen light recently. The outside glass part of the light bulb just popped and exploded all over the kitchen and eating area with great force, shards of glass everywhere, this is dangerous, as normally my daughter and I would be sitting underneath that very light bulb, eating and doing homework. That light bulb was installed directly over the edge of the kitchen island and chairs where my daughter normally sits.

The halogen light part is still working and in the light socket but there is no glass housing. It is unclear how I will be able to uninstall that light fixture as it was installed with a suction cup-pole as the ceilings are high.

The pop-explosion is dangerous. We could have been injured by the exploding glass -it was very forceful and glass shards were strewn across 2 rooms.

incident_description: Purchased a 5-shelf bookcase from Target. On the instruction sheet, item is listed as Room Essentials, style #411758, and dpci #249-05-0089. The cost was $32.99. The bookcase comes in 2 large sections that are assembled separately, then attached together. The height after assembly is approx 71 inches. The only hardware attaching the two pieces together are one single cam and two small metal 1-inch rods. Instructions caution not to move unit until cardboard backing is nailed on. All instructions were followed.  When we tried to move the unit after assembly, the top section broke away and both pieces overturned onto   the floor. No injuries, but sections are very heavy. Returned to store, and told them of the problem. Worry that item will simply be returned to sales floor.
justification: The incident involved the bookcase breaking apart during movement but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to the design flaw mentioned and the potential for recurrence.

incident_description:

The consumer picked up the candle to blow the fire out. The consumer stated that the fire started because the glass container  got too hot and ignited the wicker on the outside. When she picked it up to blow the flames out, the container was so hot it burned her hands.

incident_description:
I purchased a Safeway candle (store brand) that is a standard wax candle in a glass cup/jar about a year and a half ago.

Today, I finally burned down to the bottom of the candle, and there were severe safety problems.

I noticed a medium flame (not wick!) about two inches above the glass sides (~3 inches) that was producing a lot of smoke.

The candle was sitting on my counter near my kitchen sink, so I went t pick it up and drop it in the sink. I burned my fingers from the heat on the glass. I then used a dry towel to pick it up, and the glass sides separated from the base (cracked!).

Importantly, the heat from the candle slightly melted the poly coating on my counter and left a severe burn mark on the painted wood.
justification: The incident resulted in burned fingers and property damage, indicating an injury and significant safety hazard.

incident_description: LANGLEY EMPIRE CANDLE EXPLODED AND THREW GLASS AND HOT WAX EVERYWHERE.  THE CANDLE WAS PURCHASED AT KOHL'S LAST WEEK. THE CANDLE SEEMED TO EXPLODE FROM THE TOP BASE MID WAY DOWN THE CONTAINER.

We tested the blanket as requested by the manufacturer and the same thing happened again - smelled smoke. This time we were awake so immediately unplugged it.

The consumer contacted the manf. They informed her that there is no issue with the product and that this tends to happen with regular wear and tear. The consumer stated that the blinds are currently with the local dealer for the manf to have it repaired.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the metal hook from the shower curtain fell on the floor and her 17 year old daughter stepped on it without seeing it and the hook got inserted halfway through her foot.  She took her to the emergency room at St David's Hospital in Austin TX, where she was treated and released for followup.

The manufacturer or retailer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that the hook is a safety hazard.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring emergency room treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described scenario.

incident_description:
I use Sylvania Capsylite par20 50watt bulbs in a track lighting fixture to illuminate my office. A few months ago, the glass lens from one of them fell off the bulb and onto the desk. Fortunately it landed on some paperwork, otherwise the desk would have been damaged.
Last night that same bulb burned out. About an hour afterwards the actual halogen bulb inside it exploded with a loud bang. At first I couldn't figure out what had happened until I noticed glass shards on the floor, desk, computer screen, keyboard and in my hair. Fortunately I wasn't injured but feel I could just have easily been blinded had the glass entered my eyes.
justification: The incident involved an exploding bulb with glass shards, but no injury occurred, though there was potential for harm.

incident_description: We used tag tealight candles on a wooden table. When the candle reached the end, a four inch flame shot out of the candle and it took us blowing it out vigorously to extinguish the flame. It charred the table but luckily didn't catch on fire further. Product purchased from Crate and Barrel.
justification: The incident involved a flame shooting out of a candle, charring the table, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Light base melted and blew apart in fixture.  Cree 120E26-1I-00 LED light bulb 2014 2330248.  Started a fire with the lamp shade, melted the base of the lamp fixture as the issue was in the base of the bulb.  Luckily nobody was hurt and the fire was put out.  this happened immediately after turning the table lamp on.  it started buzzing and then blew.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a malfunctioning light bulb, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the glass table top exploded. The consumer heard it in the other room.  The consumer walked into the kitchen and stepped on glass.

The consumer contacted the manf and they informed her that this could happen due to room temperature change.

The consumer had the insurance agent over her house from the manf. The consumer stated that the agent tried to say that this was due to temperature change or the glass was hit with something.The consumer stated that nothing hit the table and no one was in the room when the glass exploded.

The consumer stated that they had the doors open for a while so the house was colder than usual. They then turned on the heater so the temperature fluctuated a little. 

The consumer has pieces of glass in both of her feet.  The consumer stated that she went for a pedicure at a salon and most of the glass pieces were removed by the lady doing her pedicure.
The consumer has seen a foot doctor and gone through x-rays and MRI to find the pieces. The consumer has been going back and forth with the doctor trying to get the pieces removed. The consumer stated that the pieces are too small to take out. The consumer stated that there are about 4 more pieces left in her feet.

The consumer stated that 2 of the 6 chairs that came with the table broke after 2 years of use, so they were only using 4 chairs. The consumer stated that the other 4 chairs would snap so they limited their use. When they contacted the retailer for the incident that happened with the chairs, they informed the consumer that this issue would not be covered under warranty. They informed her that someone would have to fall from the chair for it to be replaced under warranty. 

The consumer has remaining pieces of glass, the table legs and chairs.
justification: The consumer sustained injuries from glass pieces in her feet, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The incident was caused by temperature fluctuations, a known but not common issue (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
Approximately one month ago, I replaced the three 60 watt traditional candelabra light bulbs in my front porch light fixture (a wall sconce affixed to the brick front of my townhouse) with three Great Value brand LED light bulbs from Walmart.  The bulbs are sold in Walmart Stores as "Great Value LED Daylight Deco Light Bulb, 40W equivalent", Walmart #: 551270792.  

When I came downstairs this morning, I noticed that my porch light was not on, which was odd because it is on a timer that turns them on at dusk and off at dawn, and it was still dark outside. 

I opened the front door to inspect the fixture and discovered that one of the bulbs appeared to have caught fire, as it was completely blackened and charred, with the housing cracked from heat.  In addition, the center post was charred and the entire fixture smelled like burnt electrical wiring.  The fixture is now completely inoperable, even with new bulbs, and I have had to purchase, and must install a new wall sconce outdoor light fixture.  I feel fortunate that it did not cause a house fire and was contained within the light fixture.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb catching fire, causing damage to the fixture but no injury or death.

incident_description: We just bought a pack of 4 GE ultra soft white bulbs and put one in a brand new lamp. The light was on for about two hours and the bulb exploded spraying glass all over the bed, nightstand and surrounding area.
justification: The bulb exploded, causing damage but no reported injury.

The consumer stated that the TV was supplied with a poorly designed and weak stand which collapsed. The consumer stated that the TV came out of the screws that were holding the stand's attachment plate onto the TV. The consumer's wife heard snapping sound.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the blanket almost started a fire because the socket that the wires was plugged into melted and started emitting smoke.  He immediately unplugged it to prevent a fire.  The incident occurred approximately 30 mins after it was plugged in.  He has used it several times before and had not experienciend any prior incident.

The manufacturer was not contacted. 

Caller feels that the blanket is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a melted socket and smoke emission, but no actual fire or injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) since the caller had used the blanket several times without prior issues.

incident_description:
I purchased the Bower bed from Room and Board for my daughter.  It is 31 inches high, although from the floor to the base of the platform it is only 29.5 inches and thus does not fall under federal regulations for children's bunk beds.  Nonetheless a guardrail is available for purchase.  
I purchased the guardrail and bed a little over a year ago.  It has cracked on the two pieces that connect to the bed.  The guardrail is very close to cracking completely and falling off the bed.  I am concerned that it could injure one of my children should that happen.  When I sent pictures of the cracks to the company, they responded, "The guardrails are not intended to have weight put upon them or to be used to climb with."  It does not make sense to me that a guardrail for a child's bed cannot have weight put upon it.
justification: The guardrail is cracked and close to failing, posing a potential injury risk to children, though no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: Intended to push the cart 2 to 3 feet thru an opening in my fence. Stepped on the open lid of the cart and was snapped to the ground with the cart. My head was smashed against the ridge of the cart, flattening my glasses and badly bruising my forehead and under both eyes.
justification: The description indicates significant injuries including bruising and damage to glasses, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen but are not frequent.

incident_description:
One evening while we were home, watching television, a lamp bulb EXPLODED -- GE 3 way 50/100/150w Reveal bulb (made in China).  No power surge, no other lights dimmed, everything remained normal in the house except for the bulb exploding.  Glass from the bulb shot in all directions. incident_description:
I purchased a Halogen Torchiere Lamp:  "Curvy Lady Two" from the You Will Remember Collection by the Van Teal Manufacturer at ATGstores.com on November 29, 2014.  The lamp did not come with an instruction manual or a bulb. In the description of the lamp on the ATGstores.com web site, it recommended a 250 W 120V Medium Base Bulb.  I was not able to locate this bulb in my area (Dallas, TX), so I called the Van Teal Company directly and was instructed to purchase a [REDACTED] 250 W Halogen Bulb model # [REDACTED] from [REDACTED].com.  

This lamp is constructed with the Halogen bulb socket on top of the lamp, with a circular shaped acrylic shade positioned under the socket. There is NO protective covering for the bulb and the bulb is totally exposed on the top of the lamp. (See attached photo) 

The back of the [REDACTED] Model # [REDACTED] Bulb packaging has a specific precautionary warning about the safety of the bulb.  It states "Halogen bulbs operate at high temperature and pressure, and they could unexpectedly shatter. Use bulb in an 'enclosed fixture or with a 'protector' in front."  (see attached photo)

Due to the halogen bulb having no protective covering, this lamp is a fire hazard and a risk for causing bodily injury.  The bulb packaging clearly warns that the bulb is capable of shattering and should only be used with a "protector."  In my online research, I found information stating that all halogen torchiere lamps manufactured after 1998 were required to have a protective shield over the bulb.

I contacted  ATGstores.com where I purchased this lamp  and told the Service Representative the safety issues.  I told the representative that this lamp should not be sold and needs to be recalled. When I asked for a return authorization, I was told that I have "buyer's remorse" and would be responsible for the return shipping!!

I am concerned that this lamp is NOT safe for the consumer to use.  It potentially can cause severe bodily injury and/or property damage.  These are the reasons this lamp should be recalled: 
1. The halogen bulb can shatter projecting hot shards of glass.
2. Anything that comes in contact with the hot halogen bulb will burn, i.e.  Kids' toys thrown too close to the bulb, and flying insects will catch on fire if they get too close.


I am also concerned that there may be additional Halogen Torchiere Lamps manufactured by the Van Teal company that also have the same safety issues. (http://www.vanteal.com/index.php/category/view/2/Residential)
justification: The lamp poses a fire hazard and risk of injury due to the exposed halogen bulb, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

On December 3, 2014, we ordered an Elegant Comfort 1500 thread count luxury silky soft, wrinkle and fade resistant, California King sheet (four piece), from Amazon for a new California King Sized bed we had purchased and were waiting to have delivered on Saturday, December 13, 2014.  The sheets arrived via [REDACTED] at our house on December 9. My fiancÃÂ©, waited until after the bed arrived and we were settled in before unwrapping the sheets in order to place them on the bed.  She immediately noticed blue granules that were clearly falling from the sheet.  She shook the sheets and our bedroom filled with what looked like blue sand.  No sooner had she done this, when she began to have great difficulty breathing.  She coughed and choked and ran out, gasping for air and told me had happened.  
I took me into our living room, away from the bedroom and helped me calm down.  She told me she felt as if someone was choking her but she was finally able to stabilize my breathing after about 20 minutes.  During this time, I was preparing to take her to the hospital, located about 40 minutes away in New Bern, where her cardiologist works, however, after her breathing returned to normal and her heart rate also stabilized (she has a diagnosed heart condition), we decided not to go to the hospital.
I proceeded to clean up the blue powder, using a lint remover roller that I attached to a pole.  I went through approximately six of the lint removal sheets before most of the granules and blue dust was removed. She continued to cough a lot the following day, (Sunday) and, as of Tuesday, December 16, 2014, have had intermittent coughing episodes.
Please note that I also put in a call to Amazon late Saturday night in which I informed them, in no uncertain terms, that I would go to press on this entire matter.  The following evening,  AmazonÃÂs Customer Service Department, called in response and took all the information down.  At some point, during the conversation,  asserted that this product was sold to us by a third party, not from Amazon itself.  Therefore, Amazon was not responsible.  I asked whether or not Amazon vetted companies that contracted with them, whether or not there was a review process.  She did not know.
On Tuesday, December 16, 2014, an e-mail offering apologies and a $30 credit (the value of the product) to be used for future purchases.  She also provided the name of the seller, Bespolitan.

1)	The packaging did not contain any warning labels alerting users to the possibility of an anaphylactic reaction to the substances within.  Such as products peanuts or foods that contain peanuts are required to post this warning.

2)	There was no indication on the order form that the product was made in China.  If we had purchased this product in a store, we would have had the opportunity to read on the package itself that the product had come from China.  The catastrophic fall-out from Chinese Drywall underscores the need for customers to know the nation of origin when purchasing any product that is brought into their homes.

3)	This product posed a serious threat.   Question:  Was the product properly tested and approved for distribution in the United States?  ALL RELEVANT FEDERAL AGENCIES NEED TO BE ALERTED.  THIS PRODUCT NEEDS TO BE BANNED.

incident_description:
Please be aware that sofas containing a chemical called DMF (dimethly fumarate, also known as fumaric acid) is causing severe problems in Europe and USA.

The BBC News in the United Kingdom has been reporting that more than 1,600 people have suffered skin rashes and chemical burns from their new Chinese-made leather sofas. Reports say that one person has died. 

After investigation, it was found that the couches were packed with sachets containing dimethly fumarate (DMF), an antifungal agent intended to prevent the leather from getting moldy during storage and shipment from China. The chemical evaporates, penetrating the leather and can transfer to clothing and skin. Even small levels of exposure can cause serious skin sores, blisters, rashes and eye irritation. And some victims have reported that their problems have persisted long after the couch has been put on the curb.

Doctors say a chemical added into furniture shipments from China to prevent the growth of mold has been linked to severe rashes.

The chemical, dimethylfumate (DMF), can penetrate the fabric and subsequently clothing when a person sits on the furniture, says [REDACTED]., MD, clinical professor of dermatology at the University of Louisville, Kentucky.

DMF is also used in the shipping of some clothing and shoes, [REDACTED] says.  And some people are very allergic to the preservative, he tells WebMD.

When they come into contact with DMF, susceptible individuals develop contact dermatitis, a rash that can occur anywhere on the body. Irritated skin becomes dry and chapped and eventually red, scaly, and inflamed.

At the annual meeting of the American Academy of Dermatology, [REDACTED] described what he called "an epidemic of Chinese sofa and chair dermatitis."

[REDACTED] said that the first five cases were reported in Europe in 2008.

"Since then, there have been a good 1,000 cases in Europe, maybe more," he says. Cases have also been reported in Canada and USA.

In 2013, I bought sofas from Jennifer Convertibles, and experienced itchy feeling when sitting on it, and even when entering my house.  A dermatologist told me that it's caused by airborne contact dermatitis.  The chemical evaporates during warm part of the day and goes airborne througout house.  In the evening, it gets cool, so the chemical condensces.  It's heavier than air, so it settles into the carpet and is stored in the carpet pad (acts like a sponge).  I got rid of the sofas and carpetting, and symptoms eventually went away over 3 months.

In 2014, I bought sofas from LA-Z Boy, and within an hour experienced same itchy feeling when entering my house.  I got rid of the new sofas and new carpetting, and symptoms are going away over last 2 months.

Please be aware that this is a big problem.
justification: The incident involves severe skin rashes, chemical burns, and one reported death, indicating significant harm.

incident_description:
On July 21, 2014 we ordered from Hesco Lighting, the Monroe 16 Light Multi-Tier Chandelier by Kichler Lighting. Upon receipt of the chandelier we discovered that the chandelier's rod and its coupling are "standard thread" and our [REDACTED] Light Lift's rod and its coupling are "fine thread." On Kichler's FAQ web page they offer for purchase, via their Customer Service Department, an adapter that would allow their chandelier/light to be hung to an [REDACTED] Light Lift.  

We ordered our chandelier from Hesco Lighting because customers cannot purchase directly from Kichler. We contacted Hesco about the incompatibility issue which they were not familiar with since rods and couplings are generally fine thread based on Hesco's experiences.  Hesco then contacted the Kichler representative and after much discussion among them, it was agreed that we would need the adapter.

Upon receipt of the adapter kit, we proceeded to attach the chandelier to the lift. The attachment of the chandelier to the lift went terribly wrong because our chandelier fell 23 feet to the floor, damaging the chandelier, the wood floor and possibly the lift but we will not know for sure until we attach another chandelier to the lift. Thankfully the four adults present were not injured because none of us were standing under the chandelier.

The adapter kit did not contain specific instructions for the installation of the adapter itself, but it did include a second copy of the instructions that came with the chandelier and those instructions read and depicted the male connector going up into the female connector. 

After the chandelier fell, we contacted Hesco who then contacted Kichler who responded, as we were told, by saying they are not responsible if we hung the chandelier incorrectly. We contacted [REDACTED] Light Lift about the incident and discovered that they are aware of the incompatibility issue with the Kichler chandelier and the [REDACTED] rep immediately emailed us a photo of the installation for the adapter. The photo shows that we needed to remove the fine thread coupling from the [REDACTED] lift, exposing the fine thread male connector, and then placing the female end of the adapter into the male end of the [REDACTED] lift thus changing the original chandelier instructions of male into female. It is our understanding that the adapter is made by Kichler, not [REDACTED].

Kichler was negligent for not including, in the adapter kit, instructions/diagram for the installation of the chandelier adapter to the [REDACTED]Lift.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage, but no injuries were reported.

My husband, [REDACTED], installed the strap and leaned the shelf forward to test it (the bookshelf was empty, and he was still somewhat supporting it with his hand,) and the strap IMMEDIATELY broke.  The eyelet separated from the webbing and the bookshelf came down.  I don't think it was just a fluke or that we had one bad strap because the eyelet in the other side was halfway torn away from the nylon as well.  Luckily when this happened, it was just My husband testing it and not my toddler climbing on the bookshelf full of books because she could have been very seriously injured!  We've all heard the horror stories of furniture falling on toddlers.  I hate to use Facebook to bring attention to this matter, but I have emailed and called Target about this incident with no reply to either attempt to contact them.  I really think it is dangerous to sweep this under the rug, and I don't want to see any children get hurt from this bookshelf falling on them.  It is not unreasonable for parents to expect to trust the safety equipment that comes with their furniture, and the strap that comes with these shelves cannot be trusted!
justification: The strap failure caused the bookshelf to fall, but no injury occurred as it was being tested. The likelihood is high given the defect in both straps.

I lifted her up and removed the swaddle and she was not injured.  Obviously, though, fabric covering the face of an infant is quite dangerous and the outcome could have been different if I had not heard her and checked on her promptly.

incident_description: Had a GE 3-way 50-100-150 incandescent bulb in socket of lamp.  Lamp was on lowest setting.  Without warning, lamp exploded.  I quickly unplugged the lamp and smelled smoke.  Paper on table with lamp was burning.  Parts of bulb melted into couch and were smouldering.  I collected bulb socket and dome was still in tact with writing and identification on it.  There are about 5 holes in a very expensive new couch here and the house could have burned down if I was not there.  I have retained the paper, magazine, and we have the damaged couch available for inspection.

incident_description: Upon coming home from work, I discovered that my patio coffee table with tempered glass top had shattered. Large and small pieces of glass were spread all over the balcony. The patio furniture is located on the second floor balcony of our home. It is covered. Nothing had been touching the glass top, nor was any object set on top of the glass.

incident_description: Just wanted to make note that in the description of the recall on this product your website says that the recall does not include circuit boards with tan coloring on one side-that it only covers the green on both sides circuit boards. incident_description:
I purchased clear plastic tealight candles from WalMart (Better Homes and Gardens brand) and lit two. One of them completely disintegrated, the plastic melted, the hot wax created a puddle on my mantle and dripped down the side onto the floor. I called the company and they asked if I wanted a $25 gift certificate to WalMart. I would rather they determine whether the product is faulty. I don't want anyone to have an unwanted fire due to the failure of the candle. They are having their legal team call me.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (melting plastic candle) but no injury or fire occurred, warranting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as product defects can occur but are not frequent.

incident_description:
On 9/25/14 the consumer purchased the product and when she took the product out of the packaging box she noticed a strong vinyl odor coming from the product. She states the odor became worse when it was inflated. After the consumer pumped the air bed she put it near the window so the odor could air out. She states the bed was near the window for approximately 8 hrs. 

The consumer states the next morning on 9/26/14 the product still had the strong vinyl odor. The consumer states the odor caused her to have difficulty breathing.

The consumer will be returning the product after she files the report (9/26/14). 

The consumer feels the product poses a health problem. SHe is concerned it is especially dangerous to children and those with respiratory problems.

The consumer has not contacted the firm and does not plan to.
justification: The consumer experienced difficulty breathing due to the strong vinyl odor, indicating a health impact.

incident_description:
I recently purchased the Ashley Axiom sofa and loveseat from Ashley Furniture.

After it was delivered it had a terrible chemical smell.  It was making everyone in my family sick.  Eyes burning, throat burning, dizziness...migraine headaches.  We have been working with AAFES to get it returned.  It has been in our home for 7 days  It is still making us sick.  We have had windows open,  air cleaners running.  It is very heavy and we have no way to move it out of our house.  We haven't even sat on it!  The next morning we moved it into another room because we couldn't even be near it.  
  
We can smell the sofa and notice it comes from certain sections.  We thought we were buying a set made of all leather.  After lifting the cushion it states it is 50% leather and 50% leather splits.  The strong odor is coming from the sections of "leather splits".  

These are large heavy pieces and our garage is detached and we have no way to get it our of our house till the merchant gets it removed.  But after 7 days the smell is still there and making us sick.

We have leather furniture upstairs and we never had this issue before.

Also after we started having these issues I found another complaint on this very same website posted in 2012 with the same issues!!
justification: The incident caused physical symptoms like burning eyes, throat, dizziness, and migraines, indicating injury.

incident_description:
Caller purchased two different queen sized sets of mattresses with box springs in the past two weeks and both have a strong odor that it causing the consumer to be ill.
Caller has been nauseous from the delivery of the first mattress which she sold to an expectant mother.

She purchased the second mattress and assured the sales rep that if it made her ill she was going to expect to return it for a refund.
She tried to sleep on the second mattress after putting a mattress pad on it, but she still became ill, she developed a sore throat, began coughing, had problems breathing, her eyes became very red and she began coughing.

She said that whatever this is it literally smells industrial glue.
It has clung to her clothing and her belongings causing her discomfort.

The caller is self diagnosing and self treating,she has not seen a doctor or been to a hospital.
 
The caller has contacted the retailer with the first mattress but has not contacted the manufacture of either and isn't sure whether she is going to contact them.
justification: The caller experienced physical symptoms like sore throat, coughing, and breathing problems, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurred with two separate mattresses, suggesting a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description:
About a week ago, a fluorescent lighbulb exploded in my open fixture, spraying shards of glass below in a wide area, close to the desk where my children do homework. Chemical fumes spread through the house. I recovered whyat remained of the bulb, still in the fixture. The spiral itself had black marks on the outside, as if it had been burned. There were  fabric=like filaments sticking out of the base of the bulb. I gathered hundreds of tiny pieces of glass from the rug, floor and bench below. I called the company, who told me to bag the damaged bulb and to very carefully retrieve all fragments.
The bulb was one of 10 ceiling bulbs in this room. It was the first time I've ever seen this happen.
justification: The incident involved an exploding lightbulb with glass shards and chemical fumes, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
(09/20/2014) The consumer stated that he was sitting in the chair in the backyard. He leaned back in the chair and the back of the chair broke near the seat and at the back of the arms. The consumer stated that he fell on the ground. No medical attention was required. He stated that he was not injured.

The consumer notice that the other Adirondack chairs that he has are showing cracks in the same place.

The consumer stated that he keeps the chairs outside year round

The consumer started using Adam's Manufacturing Company's "Real Comfort Adirondack Chairs" purchased from Lowe's 2years ago. Their design of a outward lumbar support curved arch in the chair's back was very comfortable on my back as compared to the typical straight Adirondack chairs.

Within a few months after the consumer's initial chair purchase the consumer began hearing/seeing fracture cracks in the outer back rails at the base where the back meets the seat. Several chairs have been returned to Lowe's for replacements under Adam's Manufacturing's one year defect warranty (see attachments of purchase receipts and various return receipts at Lowe's).

Currently on 09/20/14, while sitting on a Blue color Adam's Adirondack chair (see blue chair photo), the entire back of the chair gave out and broke completely off the chair without any notice. The consumer tumbled backwards with my feet in the air and landed on my back and hit my head on the ground (no injury sustained other than a bump on the head!) Approximately,1month earlier I had an identical incident with a red (see red chair photo).  Again without any warning, the back of the chair blew out and the consumer tumbling backward onto his back.

The consumer also currently has 3 other Adam's Adirondack chairs with visible cracks in the back rails. Two of the chairs (see chair photo's have identical cracks in the left lower outer back rail and both have plastic fatigue marks on the right lower rails but have not cracked through.  The third chair does not yet have any cracks but the fatigue marks on both sides of the outer rails can be seen closeup, indicating a future chair back failure.

The consumer has a total of 5 chairs, the 3 mentioned above and the 2 completely broken chairs for anyone's review. After contacting the US Consumer Product Safety Commission,  The consumer contacted Adam's Manufacturing (at 800-237-8287) on 9-22-14) @ 2:25PM and advised a customer service representative of the problems the consumer was having. The consumer was transferred and asked to leave a message for Mr. [REDACTED]. As of this date, the consumer has not received a call back from Mr. [REDACTED] nor Adam's Manufacturing.

The consumer believes these chairs with age/and use will end up in complete chair failure as he has experienced. Falling backwards on a hard surface could possibly cause a concussion and even death! The failure points on ailS chairs in his posession indicate a weakness in design.

Hopefully the consumerÃÂs report will result in Adam's Manufacturing correcting these failure points with a heavier design.

 [REDACTED]
justification: The consumer fell but sustained no injury, and similar incidents have occurred multiple times with the same chairs.

Yesterday, about 30 seconds after my wife turned off the bulb, it exploded (imploded?), throwing glass all over - including into my son's high chair, where he'd only been sitting minutes before.

incident_description:
Re:  Elite Modern Victor Glass Table

The above glass dining room table which I had delivered in October 2013 literally exploded on 9/30/14. The cost of the table was approximately $1500 and was purchased from a high end furniture store.  The table can be viewed on the web site of Elite Modern.  The manufacturer is the Elite Manufacturing Corporation in California.

Fortunately, no injuries occurred since I was in another room when this happen.  Glass fragments flew everywhere and the sound was as if a bomb exploded. 

The table was placed a distance from windows (i.e., it was not in direct sunlight) and I keep the temperature of the room in which it was located at around 75 degrees.  The table was not subject to heavy use (I generally eat sitting in front of the TV on the sofa close to where the table is located and I live alone) and the only object on the table was a glass centerpiece (purchased from the same furniture store from which I purchased the table) that I estimate weighed nor more than several pounds.  

I have pictures available of the damage (in the event I have difficulty attaching them to this report).
justification: The table exploded causing significant damage but no injuries occurred as the person was in another room.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a twin mattress set on Saturday, September 20th, 2014.
The retailer had the set delivered to her Sunday, September 21st, 2014.
As the delivery team was taking the plastic off the set she noticed an extremely strong odor of chemicals coming from the mattress and box spring.
She said the delivery team left so quickly she couldn't speak with them about this issue.
She contacted the retailer who advised her that this smell would dissipate, however the consumer is now reporting to the CPSC on Wednesday, September 24th, 2014 that the mattress is still reeking of this odor.

She has tried to sleep on the mattress Monday night 09/22/and Tuesday night 09/23 but noticed that she had a headache on Sunday 09/21th, Monday 09/22nd and then on Tuesday she noticed that she was also developing respiratory problems.

She contacted the retailer to ask for her money back September 21st, was advised that she could obtain a replacement mattress set.. She responded that she wanted nothing from that same company if this set is an example of their selections.
She has not contacted the manufacturer because she does not have contact name anss information.
Sales reps - [REDACTED].

incident_description: On August 7, 2014 a Lighting Science Group PAR 20 LED light bulb caught fire damaging a light fixture,flooring and the towel used to put out the fire and carry It from the house. I was sitting in another room and heard a pop and saw the flaming LED bulb dropping from the ceiling track light fixture in my kitchen. I wrapped the still burning LED light bulb in a towel and took it outside as the smell was very bad. My track light fixture was burned,my vinyl floor was burned,and the towel used to smother the flames was burned. The bulb has been in use for several years. We did not know about the recall until after the incident. I was not injured by the burning bulb.

incident_description:
We purchased Feit fluorescent light bulbs from our Staten Island Home Depot store.  For the second time one of the fluorescent light bulbs we use in our kitchen fixture has burned, filled our home with what smells like poisonous gas and caused our lungs to hurt.  The first time this happened we thought it was an strange occurrence.  But now this second time we know this brand of light bulbs are defective when they fail.  Both lights flickered for awhile before they failed and then burned very hot and caused a lot of smoke.  Smoke should not be coming from a light bulb when it fails.  Lights should just go out, they should not poison us and try to burn down our home.  This is absolutely ridiculous.  As evidence we have saved the light bulb in question and we plan to have it tested.  The air in our home smells like pure poison right now. Melting plastics sometimes let out cyanide gas and we are very concerned.

What's even more shocking is that as we try to contact Home Depot and Feit, there is no way for a customer to quickly and efficiently report a hazardous product such as this one.  They need a link on your website for dealing with dangerous items.  This is purely negligent and irresponsible on the part of Home Depot.   Had we been asleep, this light bulb could have caused a fire in our home.   Only god knows the type of poisonous gases we've inhaled this evening.
justification: The incident caused lung discomfort and potential exposure to harmful gases, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description:
I purchased a glass-topped table from Kmart - item identified as "Jaclyn Smith Addison Dining Table with Lazy susan".  I have owned if for one year, and left it outside on teh porch all winter.  It was covered with a tarp all winter, and never had any snow accumulation greater than 2 inches.

Last week, while I was outside working on the yard, the glass on the table gave a giant pop and it collapsed into tens of thousands of tiny pieces.  After the "explosion" a large numebr of small glass pieces continues to crackle and pop for over 5 minutes.  

Nothing heavy had ever been put on the table, we never put an umbrella in teh stand, did not move the table, and never did anything that could have possibly caused it stress.  I will note that this was very shortly before a storm and I could feel a change in air pressure coming through.

I see on th eKmart website that this table has multiple negative reviews describign the glass breaking.
justification: The glass table shattered unexpectedly but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
(07/16/2014) The consumer stated that the light bulb exploded. He had just got out of the recliner and walked in the kitchen. The sound was like gunshot. The bulbs were in a ceiling fan light fixture which hold four bulbs. Only one bulb exploded. Shards were all over one half of the living room.

(07/16/2014) The consumer called the company. He spoke with someone and advised him of what happened. The person asked about the shards. The consumer asked to speak to an engineer. He is waiting for a call back.

No injuries.
justification: The light bulb exploded, causing shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
I purchased a O2Cool cooling towel about a 10 days ago.  I tried it one week ago following the directions on the package.  After wearing the towel for a day, I broke out in a painful and itchy rash on my neck, chest, upper arms - anywhere the towel touched.  I was treated by a physician with a shot of steroids and given a 5 day prescription for prednisone.  Now a week after the fact, my skin looks like it has chemical burns and is still very painful and swollen.

I recently contacted the company via email, but have not gotten a response.  The packaging does not list any of the chemicals in this product.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful rash requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
CFL Utilitech 18W 1100 Series light bulb used in my bathroom ceiling burnt into scorching and blackening  the metal plate above the light. 
It could have caused a fire if it had got past the metal plate. The light fixture had a plastic cover located just under light bulb that was unharmed. 
The light was used in a very small bathroom with shower, commode, and sink. The light was not to be used where it would come in contact with water. Box said not to use where directly exposed to weather.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb burning and scorching the metal plate, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or damage beyond the immediate area occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased the 5 pcs table and stool set at 
Homestyle Furniture in Laguna Hills on 12/30/13.  On 1/7/14 the 1st stool collapsed under 108lbs weight when a teenager sat down.  All four legs collapsed in different directions.  The child injured her back & wrist but no medical attention was sought.   We noticed the wood on ALL the chairs were cracked in the manufacturing process by the wood screws.   We returned all 4 chairs to Homestyle Furniture and they were repaired with wood glue over the screws and cracked areas.    We were also advised this null and voided any warranty and it would no longer be repaired or replaced in the future.  
On May 15th, the second stool, which had been repaired, collapsed under an adults weight in the same manner.  We have discontinued using the chairs as we don't believe they are safe. 

The stools are Crown Mark Bar Stools (Delia) manufactured 7 of 2012. 

The invoice lists these as:  counter height CM Delia 2793T-3038
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to a teenager and an adult, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the issue with a second stool suggests a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: I have completed two other full reports and have had them get "lost" in the system. On one of the reports, I pushed the "next" button and apparently lost the text. On the second version, I pushed "save" and apparently lost the text. Could you please check and see if either of these reports are still available? My e-mail address and the one I used in filling out the form is [REDACTED]. This product is really dangerous and could cause serious injuries.
justification: Reports were lost in the system but no actual injury or harm occurred, though the product is described as dangerous.

incident_description: Chair collapse and on a another occasion pinch skin off on finger
justification: Chair collapse and pinching skin off a finger both resulted in injuries, hence severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as these are common minor injuries.

incident_description: Glass table top from. Martha Stewart Living Grand Bank edition exploded for no explainable reason.  Company is sending a replacement but I worry about the safety of this product and others using it..
justification: The glass table top exploded but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) due to the lack of explanation and concern about product safety.

incident_description: I was taking down a set of 2" custom cut mini blinds so I could paint the window trim.  You have to push up on the bracket that houses the ends of the blind's headrail in order to open the bracket and slide out the headrail.  I had the right side bracket open and was trying to open the left one when the headrail slipped out of the bracket on the right.  The edge of the headrail landed on my right wrist, causing a 2" long laceration and exposing tendons and my wrist bone.  I received approximately 20 stitches (10 external, I was not informed how many internal stitches were required), and may have nerve damage.  These blinds were custom cut to fit our window and the edge of the headrail is very sharp where thy were cut to size.  One of the EMTs who responded to  my 911 call even commented on how sharp it was.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (laceration exposing tendons and wrist bone, requiring stitches and potential nerve damage), warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the fixture has 2 glass globes. The consumer stated that the left globe exploded.

The consumer was in his bedroom when he heard the glass explode. The consumer stated that part of the globe was still in the fixture and the other part was on the floor and the sink. The glass exploded in multiple sized pieces.

The consumer stated that the light was on for about 15-20 minutes before this happened. The consumer stated that the glass could have exploded while he was in the bathroom and injured him.

The consumer stated that he took the parts into the store on July 5, 2014. The consumer stated the operations manager ([REDACTED]) at the store informed him to call the number on the product for Hampton Bay on Monday. The consumer was not provided any other assistance. 

The consumer contacted the consumer complaint line for the retailer and spoke to a representative. The consumer was called back by [REDACTED] in liabilities. The consumer was informed to contact [REDACTED]. The consumer did not want to contact him. The consumer believes that the retailer did not take any steps to address the safety concerns.

The consumer contacted the # on the product for the manf. They informed him that they will send him a replacement globe in 6 weeks. 

The consumer was informed by the manf that such a thing would happen if the globe was cracked. The consumer was informed that they have 3-5 complaints similar to his.

The consumer was using the light fixture with 60 watt Home Depot light bulb.
justification: The glass globe exploded but no injury was reported, though there was potential for harm. Similar incidents are reported but not frequent.

incident_description: I purchased the Bunjo Chair from Bed Bath and Beyond. This was the first time I sat in it. I sat down (I weigh 125 pounds) Max of 200 pounds. Right after I sat down, the bungees came apart and I started to fall backwards. This is a very dangerous product and its construction should be closely examined. I t is being sold as a seasonal dorm item for college students.
justification: The incident involved a fall due to product failure, which could lead to injury, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The loop that connects the chandelier to the chain broke and the chandelier is currently hanging by the electrical cord. Please help!! Please send a replacement loop ASAP!
justification: The chandelier is hanging by the electrical cord, which is an incident but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
On 9/12/12 my office chair tipped and flipped out from under me. I feel backward to the ground and have suffered injuries and now awaiting my 3rd surgery.  I saw myself , 2 fellow employees with the same office chairs (Humanscale Liberty Mesh Seating) tip and save themselves from falling.  My employer ordered new office furniture just a short time before the incident.  I believe that all the employees have the same chair. 

I sent an email to our then human resources person that I felt the chairs were dangerous and that I saw 2 other employees almost fall and that someone else could be injured as badly as I was , but I received no response. That was probably over a year ago. 

I learned sometime in March or April of 2014 that 2 other employees actually Fell in the same manner as myself and discussed it with my manager, to no avail, I heard nothing about any precautions being taken or research done on these dangerous chairs.  I have no idea if any others have fallen as that information was not given. The other 2 employees that fell told me themselves.

Since there is 3 of us who have now fallen that I know of and 2 other employees tipped and saved themselves , I am convinced that there is a problem with the chairs.  It is not possible that 5 different people would experience the same issue.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring multiple surgeries, and multiple employees experienced similar incidents, indicating a recurring issue.

incident_description: The fluorescent tube stopped working.  Upon replacing the tube, I noticed that the plastic housing had started to melt and showed burn marks on both ends and also near the middle section.  While we did not have a fire or any other damage, the potential for a fire is clearly very high.  Since this is a light we leave on at night while we sleep, it is a concern if other units should start fires.  We have switched to an LED unit, but these low profile fluorescent tube lighting units are still available at Home Depot.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning fluorescent tube with burn marks, indicating a high potential for fire, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Hello,
My mother is 87 and in a wheelchair.  Her OT recommended a PVC pipe  shower chair made by MJM International.  On May 1st one of the chair plastic capped screw fell out.   It caused the chair to become unstable and dislodge from the track, making it almost impossible to move my mom out of the chair.  The company we bought it from came out to repair it.  About 2weeks ago the same bolt came out and completely dislodged the track, causing the chair to fall apart on one side.  Again while my mom was in the chair, 135 lbs without any means to move except for the care of her nurse.  Luckily the nurse is a strong woman and she was able to handle the situation by hooking the [REDACTED] sling in place until she could be lifted out.  Again she soaking wet, slippery, and a risk of falling over or out of the chair while in the bathroom.  I contacted the company three times and they are not interested in finding out why the plastic cap bolt broke.  They were going to send a replacement for me to replace.  I told them they would be foolish to think I would replace it correctly without any knowledge of how it should be properly replaced.  I believe the medical supply company replaced it with a different type of screw and the chair is compromised.  I am concerned about the company's  lack of interest for safety with the handicapped people who are dependent on such a product.  I would like you to find out if this has happened with any other of their chairs.  Hopefully
justification: The incident caused the chair to become unstable and dislodge, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Metal rod for safety rail on side of bed broke off and the rail turned and scratched my daughter.  I had to remove the safety rail and metal rods  from the bed in order to avoid further injury.
justification: The metal rod broke and scratched the daughter, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: We ordered a bunk bed for our kids from Rooms to Go Kids (SKU 3580689P).  Upon inspection on July 23rd (delivered July 22nd), the bunk bed had multiple screws laying in their respective holes, unscrewed and not bolted.  A glaring choking hazard and safety hazard (these are bunk beds that kids sleep in, unattended).  Dowels were missing or half installed.  A child could have easily poked a dowel out and swallowed the dowel.  The safety bar for the top bunk was lose.  Rooms to Go Kids guarantee is delivery professionals will assemble the furniture.  We were not left with assembly instructions to rectify the situation, even after I requested these instructions.  Rooms To Go Customer Service (multiple agents) have pointed the finger at their 3rd party contractor and have basically told me they don't have any control over their quality.  They did send a technician to correct the issue, and he also confirmed it is a 3rd party for the intial delivery, and there is very little oversight over their installations.  A simple [REDACTED] of Rooms to Go Bunk Bed issues led me to multiple complaints across the country with issues similar to mine.  These are beds made for children.  They should be choking hazard free and assembled properly, with no safety problems.  I am glad I caught the issue before my child was harmed, but the quality control should lie with Rooms to Go, not the consumer.
justification: The incident describes a safety hazard with potential for injury but no actual injury occurred, and similar issues are reported frequently.

incident_description: Yesterday I Installed a Phillips 43w echo vantage light bulb medium base A19 in one socket of a four socket bathroom light bar. The bulb was in use about one and half hours today. The light was turned off and I left the room. Five minutes later I heard tinkling of glass. I turned on the light  the bulb was lite but the glass globe had exploded glass on the vanity. The bulb base was extremely hot.
justification: The bulb exploded but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the Night lights using Led bulbs after using them for 3-4 weeks developed scorch marks.  She is concerned that these bulbs are unsafe because they might start an electrical fire, especially when they are being used in children's rooms.  

The manufacturer was not contacted.

Caller feels that these night lights should be taken of the market.

Update from consent form: Please note: Some information I gave when reporting safety issue was omitted on the report.
The products are "Night Lights" that plug directly into electrical outlets to provide low light for nurserys and childrens rooms etc. These lights use an LED bulb and house a sensor that activates bulb when it gets dark at night. After approximately 3 weeks a burn mark appeared on both night light casings indicative of high heat. The numbers on the night lights are: LED Night Light No. A676306  L114534A3 2013 UL LLC  ML053 E344672 120V ac, 0.72W 60Hz made in China
Note: These Night Lights appear to be sold under various brand names.
justification: Scorch marks indicate a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury has been reported.

incident_description: I ordered a desk from Target.com on 6/28/14 and I have had ongoing product issues and concerns since 7/4/14, upon receiving and starting assembly.  After assembling all 3 legs- I was not able to attach them as the built in tee nuts were loose and came out of the main top piece- so that means I could not attach the legs, securely.  I informed Target.com and asked for some new pieces/parts, and they refused.  I went to Home Depot and purchased some nuts, to help with the fastening of the legs, assuming that was a good alternative solution.  Upon finishing the instructions, the last page had a section of care and warning instructions, however, it must have been stamped on, because it was very blurry and the ink had bled.  None of it is legible and there are 9 different warnings that I cannot read.  I informed Target.com on 7/7/14 and they told me I need to buy another desk if I want new instructions.  I asked for the vendor phone number and it was for a different vendor that does not even make desks.  I went back to Target.com and they refused to help in any other way.  Their customer service is in India and they really don't understand the situation or the potential risks.  For the last 2 weeks, I have been trying to escalate this so someone from the US can help, but that has not happened.  During this, Target.com has pulled the product from their website, and they continue to tell me that they can't contact the vendor to get the care instructions clarified.  I am extremely concerned about the safety of this product and the warnings that I am not able to read.  Target.com has been less than cooperative and appears to not understand the situation and potential risks.  I thought it was a legal requirement that international products required labeling and care instructions.  From the box, I do know it was made in Vietnam and there is a purchase order and item number.  I feel like Target.com is hiding something, since they won't share the vendor information with me, ontop of pulling the product- this concerns me and whoever else may have purchased this desk in the past.  Please let me know if you can help me.
justification: The incident involves product defects and lack of proper warnings, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: A tempered glass top patio table exploded spontaneously.  The temperature outside during the day had been over 90 and it had dropped to under 90 by that time.  However, those temperatures are not excessive for this area.
justification: The incident involved a tempered glass table exploding without causing injury, fitting the criteria for severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described temperature conditions are not uncommon for the area.

incident_description:
POTTERY BARN EXPLODING GLASS TABLETOP.

We bought a Pottery Barn "Riviera" outdoor sectional last summer.  It was delivered and assembled on [REDACTED]. We used the sectional and tempered-glass tabletop without incident last summer and fall. However, because the weather has been so wet and lousy this summer in Minnesota, we just got around to putting out the glass tabletop this past Sunday night 7/13/14.

So, around 5:00pm my wife and I brought the glass tabletop out of our house, used [REDACTED] on both sides to clean it, and placed it on the coffee table of our sectional set.  (The glass was NOT cracked or damaged in anyway at that time.)

However, WITHIN AN HOUR, we looked out our window see what seemed like more than a thousand glass shards and pieces all over our patio.  The glass exploded in all directions.  We found glass more than 25 feet away in your yard, garden and pool area.

Luckily, no one was injured!

While temperature fluctuations (between indoor and outdoors) could potentially be an explanation for this exploding glass occurrence, that possibility never would have occurred to us given that this
furniture is made for OUTDOOR USAGE where temperatures fluctuate quite regularly.

Plus, this potential danger of exploding glass is NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE in the product information that accompanied our purchase from Pottery Barn.  (For the record, our indoor temperature was 74 degrees and the outdoor temperature was about 75 degrees when we
placed the glass tabletop on the  sectional coffee table.)

We asked Pottery Barn for a quick remedy to this situation as we did not spend several thousand dollars on this Riviera sectional set to have to deal with this sort of mess, as well as the potential danger of exploding glass.

Pottery Barn has yet to acknowledge the seriousness of this potential safety hazard, in spite of numerous attempts on our part to notify them of the situation.
justification: The glass tabletop exploded but no one was injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the unexpected nature of the event and lack of prior warnings.

incident_description: Our chandelier was installed 5 years ago and has been undisturbed for the life of the product.  Suddenly it fell last night.  Luckily no one was injured.  Our home security system cameras did catch this on camera.
justification: The chandelier fell but no one was injured, which qualifies as an incident without injury.

incident_description: The merchandize was purchased approx. 3mo ago. The back of one of the chairs broke half way off and extremely sharp metal (a tack weld) was exposed. My 5 year old was standing behind the chair with his hand on the (unknown) broken piece when his older brother sat down. The share metal punched his finger and as he pulled his hand back it cleanly slice his index finger from the middle of his nail bed to the tip. The safety instructions and warnings for the set mention nothing about this possible type of injury. The company that manufactures this set is technically China but Kids Only, inc in MA is also listened as a wholeseller.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury to a child's finger, which aligns with severity level 3. The likelihood is considered possible (3) as the description suggests a specific but not uncommon scenario involving children and furniture.

incident_description:
Caller stated that she went in the bathroom and was getting ready for a shower when she heard a popping sound.  She looked up and noticed that the heating and light ventilation system that holds the glass became unhinged and the glass fell out to the floor.  The glass pieces shattered all over the bathroom floor and she feels that it is a dangerous product that poses a safety hazard for consumers.  There were no property damages or injuries.


6/25/14 The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that the product would be replaced.  She stated that she informed the agent that she was not sure that she would like a replacement of that product due to it being unsafe.

Submitter stated that the lamp cover holding a heavy glass came unlatched and swung down. The glass slid out and fell to the floor, shattering into countless shards.

As evidence by the attached photographs, the latching system design is not adequate to hold the plastic frame containing a relatively heavy glass.  The glass is not adequately secure in the frame to prevent it from falling out.

The cover had been opened (with great difficulty) on two occasions to facilitate changing the lamp.  When closing the cover, there is no way of knowing if it latches properly. It is pushed upward until it stops, and one is to assume it is latched. It is feasible that vibration from the motors in the unit could overcome the shallow plastic latches. Even so, the glass should not fall out.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous product failure with shattered glass, but no injuries or property damage occurred.

incident_description:
Polaroid 6 Watt LED bulb. Bulb glass exploded while turned on. It had been installed for a few weeks, with no problems. When it was turned on yesterday morning it exploded and rained glass down on the counter top over where it was plugged in.
  No sparks, or fire thankfully.
 No injuries because I had stepped out of the room, it could have been bad. 
Date or lot number 201310206
Model Number: PLOA17-40-325-6-1S
justification: The bulb exploded but no injuries occurred as the person was not in the room, and there were no sparks or fire.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the table set has a stabilizer leg that holds the leaf in place, however, in folding the sides slams quickly which if a toddler is present could cause severe injuries.  She stated that the hinges that hold the leaf is too small and while it was completely assembled by her son he was folding the legs and the hinges broke.

(6/17/14) The retailer was contacted and no one was able to assist her.
No one would assist.  The consumer was directed to the telephone number originally called 1-866-562-7848

Caller feels that this table set is a safety hazard and should be reported.

UPDATED 6/30/2014
No one would assist. I was redirected to the telephone number originally called 1-866-562-7848.

Hinges on product cannot hold leaf! This is a 2-man lift item. Leaf comes down swifly when stabilizing leg is moved and hinges pop off!!

This is a dangerous product!  The last thing the consumer would want is for someone's child to be injured, struck, beheaded, or have serious injuries due to the weight and force of the leaf side(s) slamming down upon them!!  Please help!
justification: The description indicates a potential for severe injuries, including the possibility of death, due to the table's design flaw.

incident_description:
We own Graco Pack 'n PlayÃÂ® Playard with Twins Bassinet, Model 1812884, and are satisfied with this product.

However, I believe that the sheets for this crib do not fit properly and pose a safety risk for infants.

Graco Pack 'n PlayÃÂ® Twins Bassinet Sheet, Model 1816483, are too tight for the foldable base.  When they are put around the base, it collapses / accordians, causing bumps in the base.  The base also no longer covers the entire bottom of the crib, leaving gaps on the sides which are also unsafe

An infant laid on his back can roll over to his front unexpectedly, or into one of the gaps created at the edge of the crib base.

Neither of my twins have been harmed, but I felt I should encourage the CPSC to look into this situation.

Graco's website has a couple reviews that list the same problem.

My own solution was to discontinue using the Graco sheets and use an alternative from another company which fits properly, so the base can lie flat and fully cover the intended area.

Thank You,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a safety risk with ill-fitting sheets causing gaps in the crib base, but no actual harm to infants has occurred.

incident_description: On June 30 at 4:30 in the morning, I heard a noise.  I went from my bedroom to the Great Room to find the two layer glass cocktail table "exploded."  Had I and/or my husband or any guests been sitting there, we would have been injured.  The broken glass was as far away as the denÃÂapproximately 20 feet from the incident. My husband and I looked up at the ceiling to see if perhaps a bulb has fallen to break the table.  Nothing had fallen.   I took photos and the receipt to the furniture store and asked to speak with THE manager, [REDACTED].  He said he had never seen anything like this before. He advised me that the store's warranty was 90 days, but he took the photos and said he would contact the manufacturer and I should call him in a few days.  I did call back and he told me the manufacturer's warranty was 2 years.  The table was 4 years old.  Of course,we would like to be compensated as this is a defect in the table.  And on the other hand, I wouldn't want this to happen to anyone else, so I told [REDACTED] that I was going to contact Consumer Protection and the Florida Attorney General's office.  I did contact the Attorney General Office, and Attorney General [REDACTED] suggested that I follow up with CPSC as she had forward ed my complaint to you.
justification: The incident involved a table exploding but no one was injured, though it could have caused harm if people were nearby.

incident_description:
Last month I purchased from Summer Infant Inc. (via Amazon) a Sure & Secure Folding Bedrail (Model No. 12524A, Manufacture No. 14040598).

During installation on my 2-1/2 year old's twin-size bed, a plastic clasp on the bedrail snapped. I did not put any more pressure on the bedrail than my daughter's weight would have.

I am bringing this to your attention (and that of the company and Consumer Reports) because I noticed after the fact several similar reviews on Amazon with people reporting the same concern.
justification: The incident involved a product failure (broken clasp) but no injury occurred, and similar issues have been reported by others.

incident_description:
I purchased a patio dining set on 6/22/13 from Sears.  Yesterday (7/13/14) the glass top on the table spontanteously shattered.  No one was near the table at the time and there was only a tablecloth and a small vase on it.  Nothing hit it to cause this shattering, which covered our deck with glass.  So unsafe and since its happened I've read other reports just like this.  The product is manufactured by Garden Oasis, which I understand is based in the UK.  Sears informs me that my warranty was only for a year and that I'll have to take this up with Garden Oasis.  Again, after reading other reports, I don't think I'm going to get any satisfaction.  

I would hate to think what would have happened if my toddler grandson had been close by when this occured, and my dog won't be allowed on the deck for a while.  Although we swept for more than an hour, there's still glass shards in the wood.
justification: The glass shattered without injury, but the potential for harm was significant, especially to a toddler.

incident_description: Purchased a leather chair from HOM furniture in Lakeville, MN.  About one week after having the chair I started to itch on the exposed parts of my body after getting up from use of the chair.  I tried some other items to try and isolate the problem to the chair but it came back to I was reacting to the chair.  I did not at first have a rash or any visual physical indications of the problem so I continued to try other items such as changing the laundry detergent.  I have now removed the chair from the house and the problem is going away.  I believe that the problem is at the chair contains DMF that I am having severe allergic reactions to including a start of a rash on my back and continued skin irritation.  The chair was manufactured in China and they must have sprayed it with the chemical since I do not see any bags that would contain the chemical.
justification: The incident describes a severe allergic reaction and skin irritation caused by the chair, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was sitting on the chair by the computer. The consumer fell when the chair collapsed.

The weld plate snapped. The consumer stated that the weld plate now flops around.  The consumer stated that the chair now leans to the side and he cannot sit on it.

The consumer contacted the retailerÃÂs recall hotline. They informed him that his chair is not included in recall #14-188.  They transferred him to parts department.  Parts department informed him that he would have to send back the weld plate so they can send him the right replacement. 
The consumer was informed that he would have to pay the cost of shipping to ship back the broken part.
justification: The consumer fell when the chair collapsed, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: I am reporting a incident with a folding chair that I got my pinky finger caught in and it amputated the tip of my finger. This is a dangerous folding chair that I don't want to see anybody else good through what I and going through. The incident took place at a dinner I attended at a club we belong to and I just sat down in the chair and I am not sure how but somehow I must have reached to pull the chair forward and there was a gap where the chair was not fully setup or came apart somehow and when I pulled it forward it pinched my finger tip by closing it in the pad against the bar. (Enclosed Pictures)
justification: The incident resulted in the amputation of a finger tip, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description suggests the chair design may pose a recurring hazard, making occurrence likely.

incident_description: i purchased a glass top desk from Z gallery.  I only had a laptop on the desk and one day when I was not home, the glass top shattered into tiny pieces. Most of the glass fell into the desk itself (drawers) and splattered around the desk on the floor.  When cleaning the glass pieces out of the desk, I noticed that there is no real support anywhere under the entire piece of glass to support its weight anywhere int he centers.  The only thing holding the glass top is a 1/4" ledge going around the perimeter of the desk.  After cleaning all the glass pieces in a box, I weighed the box and it weighs about 30 lbs.  This is very unsafe and too much weight for a glass top to be suspended on the thin ledge without any support.  Luckily no one was home when this happened and there were no children or pets around the desk at the time of this happening.  I feel that all desks of this model need to be recalled for safety reasons and have an additional support bar of some sort paced under the glass top to keep this from happening with other desks. The desk is called the Flight Desk and sold at Z gallery ( http://www.zgallerie.com/p-13150-flight-desk.aspx )
justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, indicating an incident with potential for harm.

incident_description:
We had two GE energy-efficient soft white 100watt (GE Halogen Technology) light bulbs installed in a bath room light fixture above the mirror. While my oldest granddaughter (adult) was using the toilet one bulb suddenly exploded raining shards of glass on her and through out the room. 
There were no injuries, just glass all over. These bulbs were purchased recently at our local Lowes store and came 4 bulbs to a package. I have removed both bulbs and intend to return all of them to Lowes.
justification: The bulb explosion caused glass shards to scatter but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2.

incident_description:
My father is 87 and lives with my husband and me.  He is recovering from 07/07/14 surgery of the R leg.
Due to ongoing discomfort at night, my father decided to sleep in his living room-based LAZBOY chair on 07/12/14. We agreed it was safe, would help, and he was sleeping soundly in the full recliner position when my husband and I went to bed. GREYSON RECLINA-ROCKER  010530 C101176 FN 175

The police officers at the scene said that the sliders on the dresser were extremely loose and the drawers came out very fast.  Also the dresser was unstable, not bolted to the wall or floor.
