incident_description:
Dear U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission:

I am sharing my experience with a General Electric (GE) light bulb that is a potential hazard. See enclosed photos for identification.

On Mothers Day, May 11th, 2014 we had three of these light bulbs installed in a fixture in our bathroom. One of the light bulbs exploded sending hot debris all over the bathroom. The expelled debris from the bulb burned a half-dozen spots in the vinyl flooring, similar to a small cigarette burn.

Luckily my wife who was in the bathroom at the time was not injured, but it certainly made a terrible mess with broken glass all over the place. Looking at the bum marks on the floor there was the potential of serious personal injury from the flying hot flying glass chards and possibly molten metal. The bulb was in a fixture that pointed up (see enclosed photos). The force of the explosion ejected the remnants against the ceiling and as far away as 6 feet.

This was no simple popped bulb, but a small explosion. I have witnessed popped bulbs before in applications where they were abused such as rough service applications, dropped, hit with water, overheated and the like. But never anything like this, this was truly scary and a hazard. I immediately removed the other two bulbs and replaced them with different style of bulbs that I have used for years.

There were not a storm lightening event, no voltage surges, and no, water spray was not the cause despite the location in the bathroom. Even if a water drop did manage to touch the bulb, it should have merely broken the bulb, not caused an explosion. There is no warning these bulbs are not to be used in a bathroom, although I doubt that to be the problem.

The problem appears to me to be the very design of the bulb. These bulbs appear to be of a very different design from standard incandescent bulbs, nothing like I have seen before. Normal bulbs appear to have a very small gauge conductors leading from the base to the filament. Inside these bulbs is actually a smaller bulb that appears to be halogen or some other type of light. See enclosed picture. This inner bulb has very thick glass. My theory is the outer shell had some type of leak in it allowing air and oxygen to enter causing the conductors to the inner light to overheat which caused the explosion. Regardless of my theory, the thing is a suspect design and poses a huge risk to anyone that uses it. It didn't just go "pop", it went "boom". It's an 110 volt bomb.

This is a scary product and I'm hoping by sharing my experience I can avoid someone being seriously hurt. If that hot debris struck the floor and melted it struck someones eye that could have caused very serious injuries. We could have spent Mother's Day in the ER. Luckily next year we are planning on replacing the tub and at the same time replacing the flooring, so we will just put up with the burn marks in the mean time thankful no one got hurt. Something like this should never happen ... ever. If someone does not look into this, someone will be seriously injured or blinded.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described event and potential for similar incidents.

incident_description:
A 72 watt halogen light bulb (replacement for 100 watt incandescent as required by federal regulation) exploded in my home this evening.  Fortunately the large lampshade, which sustained damage, contained most of the shards of glass released by the explosion.  However, some glass flew 6 or 8 feet in spite of the shade containment. It was also fortunate that I was the only one in the room and was seated about 15 feet or so from the lamp.  While I have been very unhappy with the government's ill-advised decision to replace incandescent bulbs with halogen due to the fact that these replacement bulbs cost significantly more and have a much shorter life (based upon my own fairly extensive study) and any savings in electricity is more than consumed by the cost of the bulb, I did not realize they were also a potential safety risk.  I am 69 years old and, therefore, have gone through many, many incandescent bulbs in my lifetime, I have never had one explode as this halogen did tonight.  This bulb was manufactured by GE and, according to the printing on the bulb, was manufactured in China.  

I can almost guarantee if someone had been sitting in the chair that is positioned a few feet from that lamp and if the lampshade had been smaller in size, there would have been an injury as a result of this explosion.  I have 3 bulbs remaining from this recently purchased 4-pack and I will not take a chance on using them.  Unfortunately, due to federal regulations eliminating incandescent bulbs, my options for finding a replacement are not great.
justification: The incident involved an exploding bulb with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the event.

incident_description: This is regarding Cree brand LED lamp model number BA19-110270MF-12DE25-1U100 (may apply to other models as well), sold exclusively by Home Depot. The lamps have an outer glass shell, similar to the glass envelope on ordinary incandescent lamps. The problem is that the glass shell is not adequately affixed to the lamp, and can spontaneously separate when the lamp is warm from use. Aside from any danger caused by falling glass, this also exposes the internal electrical connections to contact by the consumer (and this is a line-powered device). This has happened to three of the six lamps I own. I believe that this is a serious product safety hazard, and that the lamps should be recalled.
justification: The glass shell separation exposes electrical connections, posing a risk of injury, but no actual injuries are reported.

It is inherently dangerous to have a table base that only supports a top on two sides.  

I have spoken to the owner, [REDACTED] but he refuses to do anything and I am concerned a child will be hurt.  It is a kitchen top and childen lean on kitchen tops.

Johnston Casuals may have taken down some pictures of the product from its web site recently but at least one JE-133-SET is still up as of this writing.

incident_description: 100 pound 27" CRT TV fell on 7-year-old at a daycare center.  Child suffered head injury and died 3-days later.  TV was on an ACCO Brands Corporation A/V Cart Model Apollo TPDUOEQ.  Product has no safety belt, is advertised as being able to accommodate 27" monitor and weight of 100 pounds.  Cart, by design, has locking casters on front of cart only.  Testing by engineer establishes cart with 100 lb tv is tipped with only 10 pounds of force.  ACCO and CPSC recalled a different Apollo A/V cart in 2006 (Alert #06-548).  That cart actually had a more stable design than the subject model and was recalled because it lacked a safety belt.  The model in this incident also lacked a safety belt and a belt is not offered on new models currently offered for sale.  Also, the manufacturer markets the warnings on the carts as optional and even displays photographs of the product at its own website without the warnings on the product.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to a head injury caused by a falling TV, which meets the criteria for severity level 4. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the historical data provided (72 out of 5402 incidents).

incident_description:
After spending a small fortune on frames to create a gallery wall of 
my children's artwork throughout the years, I decided to go with the command [fastener] picture 
hanging strips. I followed every step, doubling up on strips even when the 
weight of my frames where nowhere near the lowest weight recommended. Less than 
20 minutes of having 12 frames, three large 15 3/4 x 19 3/4 frames leapt off 
the walls from various positions narrowly missing not just my head but my 
children. I have 9 ft ceilings and my gallery wall went the from floor to 
ceiling. Two of the frames went from the very top, those once we tripled your 
recommended strips. One took another one down with it. My husband is currently 
vacuuming out our laundry room and rewashing every thing that was in there as 
glass went everywhere. I myself could only brace myself against the two falling 
picture frames and while I was lucky not to get cut, I have glass dust and 
small particles all over my hair. If either of my children had been standing 
where I was standing I would be in the hospital right now. It is beyond 
irresponsible to sell a product that is as unsafe as this one is. While I 
absolutely hate the holes that nails and screws leave behind at least when I 
hang my pictures from them my life  and health is not in danger. The product is unsafe and the 
trust I placed in Command as a company is shattered along with the glass on my laundry 
room floor.

incident_description: We have these light bulbs all through our home including 6 in the basement. 1 of our bathrooms are in the basement in which my 10 yr old daughter was using at the time. She turned on the light switch to go downstairs into the basement to enter the bathroom and while she was in there the incident occurred. She ran upstairs in a panic to tell me that she smelled something burning and stinky and that the light had went out. I quickly ran down in the dark to find a foggy / smokey basement with a horrible burning and chemical smell which stayed for about 4-6 hrs. I couldn't find where the burning smell was coming from so I inturn also panicked and call the fire dept through 911 because it didn't want our home to burn down not knowing the source. My husband was at work and other daughter wasn't yet home from school. The firemen found it and turned off the breaker cutting off power to that light source until my husband returned home (he's an electrician). The bulb literally burned and charred the fixture in the process. This could have caused our house to burn down and the light which this happened is literally in the path we walk each time we go down stairs right above our heads. My daughter had to travel under that light that was burning to come get me and the chemical smell was so strong it could still potentially cause her problems. The scariest thing I've ever encountered. I am removing ALL OF THESE from my home immediately. See photos.

Immediately after he pushed the setting to recline the seat  he heard a a sound similar to a motor starting and stopping. Afterwards, the motor stopped and a considerable amount of smoke emanated from the left back side of the loveseat. The consumer sensed a burning odor. incident_description:
This morning when my son's "Fluker's" heat lamp for his pet lizard was turned on automatically by a timer, it burst into flames at the point where the cord attached to the lamp.  The flames sent burning rubber into the pet's cage and elsewhere.  The heat completely melted the cord, causing it to detach from the lamp body.  Had we not been at home at the time to unplug the lamp and deal with the problem, it's possible a serious fire could have broken out.

The lamp is a Fluker's Clamp-Lamp.  The product number from the box is 27001.  It was purchased on 8/25/2011 from Petco in Austin, TX.
justification: The incident involved a heat lamp bursting into flames, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
On February 16, 2014, I purchased on the internet, shelves from [REDACTED], Sehorsch Architecture and Design, LLC - 6615 Franklin Avenue Suite 217 - Hollywood, CA 90028. (The item, called Hollywood Franklin Tower, can be viewed at:  www.sehorsch.com  - then click on link labeled FRANKLIN CAT FURNITURE).
 
Upon receiving the shelves on February 28, 2014, and opening the box, I was hit with a very strong chemical smell, and immediately began to sneeze, eyes watering, and sinuses became closed.  I waited several days and these symptoms did not stop.

I contacted the business owner via email telling him about my symptom reactions to the chemical fumes and asked how to this issue could be fixed.  He responded that the product might have been packaged before they were fully dry.   He told me to put the shelves in a warm room and that the odor would disappear in a day or two.  And he concluded with his words - "TRUST ME ON THAT".

I tried what he told me to do and after ONE week (not the one/two days as he said) the shelves were still affecting me, so I wrote back to the business owner.  His response was to write that he uses low vac (sic) stain that is not harmful to the human body.

I wrote back to him with information regarding low VOC stains and that they can cause reactions for people, I asked him how to fix.  His response was to tell me that the product was safe and the there is really nothing he can do.

It has now been three months and this product is still giving off smells and fumes, I have put them in my shed outside while waiting for resolution to complaints I have submitted to Government agencies.  I have an auto-immune disease, and having these shelves in my home have definitely caused a reaction for me.  I would like to know exactly what type of chemical stain this business owner used, or what is in the particle board, or perhaps it is the carpet he put on each shelf.  I want to know what chemical are now in my body so that I can work to remove the toxins.

The business owner told me via email to not contact him anymore or that he would call the police so I don't know where to turn.

I have also submitted a complaint against [REDACTED], Architect, to the California Architects Board, as he has neglected to secure an Architects license and has been running his business and selling products without one.
justification: The incident caused physical reactions (sneezing, eye watering, sinus issues) and exacerbated an auto-immune condition, indicating injury.

incident_description: I purchased this bunk bed from Overstock.com on 4//11/2014 for my 3 year old twin sons. We opted to not stack the beds yet (thankfully), and purchased this set in part because they could be used as two twin beds. On 5/14/2014, as one of my son's was getting into bed, the side rail that connects the headboard and the foot board broke completely in half, making the bed unusable. Had the beds been stacked, and this happened to the side rail of the top bunk, it would/could have crushed the child on the bottom bunk, plus injured the person on top as well. After working with Overstock for over a week they have agreed to refund my money and instructed me to destroy the bed. The rep I just spoke with at Overstock looked at the return reason for others that have returned this bed, and said that there were quite a few issues reported with this bed and that a broken side rail was the primary reason for the majority of the returns. I questioned why they continue to sell the bed and why there has not been a recall. She couldn't answer either question, but agreed that they may need to look into it more closely. I am hoping to have a recall issued before someone is seriously hurt by this known issue.
justification: The incident involved a broken side rail that could have caused injury if the beds were stacked, but no actual injury occurred. The high number of similar returns indicates a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
Two Westinghouse 60w clear candelabra light bulbs exploded within a week of each other. The first explosion happened on 5/16/2014. The bulb was in a small single-fixture desk lamp with a shade. The explosion happened immediately when a family member turned the light on. The person's hair was covered in tiny glass shards, and glass flew across the entire bedroom (~ 9' x 15'). (The light was in one corner of the room--not the middle.)

The second bulb exploded on 5/23/2014. This bulb was in a hanging, 4-fixture chandelier over our dining room table. This bulb exploded just before we would have been turning the lights out for the night--the light had been on for hours. In this case, debris flew even further (the light was higher up) and we found large (~ 1 square inch) shards of glass at least 16 feet away.

Both bulbs were manufactured by Westinghouse. I removed a third Westinghouse bulb that had not yet exploded from the same chandelier the second bulb had been in. I can't remember when the bulbs were installed, but it's probably been around 1 year.
justification: The incident involved glass shards causing potential injury, but no death was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as it happened twice within a week but with no further incidents mentioned.

It seems clear that Tempur-pedic mattresses emit a toxic chemical which causes serious health problems.  Would like to know what fumes are emenating from the mattresses (formaldehyde?) and why they caused us to get sick.

incident_description:

Upon inspection, the bed riser had failed, the mattress frame leg collapsed into the hollow interior, and the three other risers the bed was on showed signs of fatigue and near failure.

incident_description:
The caller is an expert who was called in to investigate the product by the plaintiff.

The caller stated that a male (weight - 205 pounds) was sitting in the chair. The spring on the chair unexpectedly broke. The seat fell to the floor. The consumer received compression fracture to his spine. The caller is not aware of other injuries to the consumer, but they are possible.

The caller discovered that the design for the spring (holds chair to the ceiling) was grossly under designed and could fail at any minute. The caller stated that the spring concentrates stress on a single location. The caller stated that the wire that was formed into the spring may have been cracked due to a very low spring index (which makes forming of the spring difficult and may result in cracking of the spring wire).

The caller stated that the material used to make the spring wire seems to be weak. The caller stated that he has not completed those testing yet. The caller is working on those tests. 

The caller stated that the chair had been used about 50 times prior to the incident. 

The caller has the broken spring and another spring that is not damaged. The caller does not have the chair. The caller has photographs of the spring.

The caller stated that the retailer is aware of this issue as it is a legal matter.

There are no recalls on this product.
justification: The incident resulted in a spinal compression fracture, indicating a severity level of 3. The design flaw and material weakness suggest a high likelihood of recurrence, rated as 4 (likely).

incident_description:
I purchased a Contour Select Tempurpedic Mattress from Sleep Train Mattress Center.  Initially this mattress was delivered opened and setup with an extremely strong chemical odor.  

My home is under 1500 square feet and the odor immediately filled the entire house.  I was instructed by the delivery men and the sales person that the smell would dissipate and go away within a few weeks and ultimately there was nothing to be concerned with.

After the mattress had been in my home for roughly two weeks I began to develop severe headaches I had never had before, exhaustion, coordination issues, memory issues, horrible nightmares in the middle of my sleep, and tingling sensations down both of my arms.

During this time the mattress lost its firmness and became incredibly softer, I contacted the initial seller to see if I could get a replacement and they had me call the manufacturer for a replacement.  During that time I was struggling in between doctors appointments and to maintain my job with all of the symptoms I was experiencing so the replacement was put on the back burner.

After several doctors visits with little to know help, one doctor asked if i had purchased anything new within my home over the past several months, I told him the only thing I had bought was my new mattress.  He recommended that I remove it from the home immediately to see if that might help the symptoms subside.

Since the removal of the mattress my symptoms have subsided significantly although I am still experiencing some residual affects.  I am extremely upset at the fact that there were no warnings given to me at the time of purchase, and concerned for others well being in regards to this mattress.  it is extremely dangerous and has affected my life in a very significant way.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (headaches, exhaustion, coordination issues, etc.) caused by the mattress's chemical odor, but such severe reactions are unlikely for most users.

incident_description:
We purchased several boxes of A19 - 120v - 1200hrs Standard Frosted Bulbs made by Pelican Creations, Inc. (SKU 3530003).
On two separate occasions, the glass portion of the bulb has separated from the metal base of the bulb.  

In the first incident, the bulb fell from a hanging fixture and struck an object below and shattered.  The base remained inside the light socket and appeared to be brown/charred.
In the second incident, the light began flickering and went out. When I went to check if the bulb was tight, I found that the glass portion of the bulb was no longer attached to the metal base.  The glass portion was only hanging by a small wire that was attached to the base.  Again, the base appeared to be slightly charred and a material flaked off of it when I attempted to remove the base from the socket.
This item poses several safety hazards.  The first hazard comes from the dropping/shattering that can occur if the bulb falls from a hanging fixture.  The second hazard is the potential danger that occurs when the light is shorting/charring.
justification: The incident describes bulbs failing and shattering, posing safety hazards, but no injuries were reported.

It turns out the boards holding up the mattress were resting entirely on two very small runners that were held in by long legged staples. They gave all the way out when I was pulling the bedding off of the top after my son got off of the bed because it was slipping. I contacted the company and talked to the general manager. She informed me that I was supposed to contact the retailer that I bought them from. This store has since closed but it was called the Mattress Giant in Little Canada, MN. I am not sure if they are also at fault having sold a bed that's design may have been modified for quality or safety. I am attaching below that correspondence with the company and the pictures of the bunk bed. They said they were going to send the old owner of the store to fix my bed. That was thirteen days ago and no one has followed up. Wnen I wrote back,today, asking a time frame, I was sent an email of the man who is supposed to be coming to my house to fix it. I know very uncomfortable with anyone associated with this company "fixing" a bed that is supposed to be safe for my son. I feel like they have been uncooperative about the seriousness of this situation. I am a person who feels strongly about letting people have a chance to act with honor when mistakes happen and was really hoping that they would do that. Especially since they are supposedly locally owned. I have a bed I can not use and have to have hauled out of here. Even worse, it could have injured a child. I I should have just contacted you to begin with. Product Or Service: Madison Bunk Bed Twin over Twin-White
justification: The bunk bed collapsed but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The design flaw suggests a possible recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: Was attempting to move the cart a short distance, stepped on the lid, and was thrown to the ground against the edge of the cart. Taken by ambulance to hospital. Severed my right temple artery in 4 different places. Was operated on and admitted to the hospital overnight. Stitches and staples needed to close about a 7" gash from forehead / above eye to back of head. Was told at the emergency room that they were not surprised as they see a lot of injuries due to these carts.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting unsafe condition of a black chair that is one of two chairs she purchased August 29th, 2013.
She had no problems the first month or so but then black dust particles from the size of dust to the largest being the size of breakfast grits began coming off of one of the chairs.
Around the end of September the caller began noticing that there was black dusting on her right arm, her posterior and her back whenever she sat in the chair.
As time went on the dust from the chair began showing up in drinks, food then on other piece of furniture.
She noticed around the same time that black dust was appearing in her ears, nose and mouth after she had been sitting in the one chair.
She put a piece of duct tape on the arm of the chair and when she pulled it off it was covered with the black residue.
The second chair was not coming apart as badly but her partner sat in this one there was black on her arm and the backs broke out in a rash which she had treated by Dr. [REDACTED] of Okala, Fl after he diagnosed allergic reaction.
The caller is asking that this chair be inspected, recalled and that she be reimbursed her monies because the store has offered only replacement or $400.00 for two chairs when she paid just $2 short $800. 

Caller has not been seen by a physician, her partner has been and was diagnosed with allergic reaction
She has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them
justification: The incident involves a partner diagnosed with an allergic reaction (injury) and potential health risks from black dust exposure, but no death or severe injury reported.

incident_description: I woke up at 4:45am yesterday morning, and as I was walking to my son's bedroom down the hallway, I saw little black debris on the floor.  As I was getting closer to the rooms down the hallway, I noticed it was coming from my office.  When i turned on the light in my office, I found my desk in pieces along with accessories I had on top of my desk.  The glass looked like it had exploded in that room, it was everywhere!!!  Since I wasn't wearing shoes, I didn't go inside.  I did so after I returned home from work that afternoon.  I found pieces of glass on the recliner that was across from the desk.  A also found the vase across the desk, was also broken into pieces.  The glass was under the recliner, under a piece of furniture I had by the recliner as well.  The closet door was slightly open and glass was in there as well.  Luckily it was I who discovered the glass and not my toddler.  That would have been an unfortunate situation.  This is very dangerous, but luckily we were also asleep when it happened.
justification: The incident involved significant property damage (exploded glass and broken furniture) but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
My husband was the only one home and was in the basement working when he heard what sounded like a tree had fallen on our house.  When he ran upstairs he saw our IKEA glass desk top had completely shattered sending our [REDACTED] Computer, printer and 2 external hard drives crashing on the floor.  It also damaged our hardwood floors.  The two brackets or legs that held up the glass were still standing.  We purchased the product from IKEA in 2010 to hold our new computer.  Since that time it's been in the same place and showed no signs of stress, cracks or scrapes.  The glass was thrown with such force it went from our dining room through the living room and all the way to our front door.  Glass completely covered our dining room floor, was in our plant, blinds, window ledge and every inch of the dining room where it was located. 
We are grateful no one was in the room when this happed.  If they had been they would have had an eye bashed in.  If a child was near that they would have been crushed.  We weighed the items on the desk to make sure they did not exceed the weight limit of 110 lbs and they totalled 46lbs only.
The pieces of glass were mostly pebble size pieces however NOT ALL were.  Some pieces that we picked up had sharp edges and some glass was crushed into tiny pieces of shard glass.
justification: No one was injured, but the incident caused significant property damage and potential for serious injury.

incident_description:
I installed two LED light bulbs which are meant to replace a fluorescent tube (T8-sized).  After powering on the light fixture and observing that the bulbs were functioning correctly, I touched the heatsink of one of the bulbs and was shocked (tingling in arm).

I removed the bulbs and observed with a multimeter that the one which shocked me has 0 ohm short between the live (120V AC) pin and the aluminum heatsink.  I placed the bulbs back in the fixture and powered it on, and observed a 120V AC potential between the heatsink of that bulb and the ground of the fixture.

The other bulb does not have the short between pin and heatsink.  It did show a 20V AC potential over the ground of the fixture though, so its safety seems suspect to me too.
justification: The incident involved a shock (tingling in arm) due to a short in the LED bulb, indicating a potential safety hazard but no serious injury.

incident_description: We purchased the bed from Ikea March of 2014 and I am surprised to see it on the recall list as of January 2014, why didn't Ikea pull these beds if they were a harzard? Also a few weeks ago my husband noticed a screw had fell of, it was from the silver braces underneath the bed. Very dangerous for young children like my son.

Turned lid back over and compartment was smoking & hot to the touch.  Opened compartment to find that spring had bent sideways upon installing pack into compartment & was smoldering. After further investigation, many lamps like this have damaged/melted lens covers which indicates a unsafe product.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burnt table and destroyed lamp) but no injury, and the product's history of similar issues suggests a recurring problem.

incident_description:
On the afternoon of March 31, 2014, I was working in my home office when I heard what sounded like a loud explosion.  When I turned around I realized that the ceiling light fixture had burst, scattering shards of glass in a roughly circular area beneath the fixture.   No one was touching the fixture at the time and, luckily, none of the shards struck me.   The light bulbs were 60 Watt [REDACTED] bulbs and were not damaged.  It had been several months since the last one had been changed.

The fixture is a Quoizel model # ML183Z, with a label stating it was manufactured in China in July 2006.   We did not purchase the fixture; we assume it was purchased and installed by the prior owner who was a contractor who had renovated the property.


I have taken photographs of the scattered shards, the base of the fixture, and the finial which had also burst apart, and would be happy to provide them to you.


Obviously I am very lucky that none of the shards struck me.   I am not making any sort of a claim but I respectfully request that you investigate and determine whether this incident is the result of a defect which could affect other owners of this type of fixture.   I have collected the shards and would be happy to turn them over to you.  We have other Quoizel fixtures in the house which are identical to this one, and want to know if we need to worry about similar incidents occurring with them.

incident_description:
I purchased a glass table top from Ikea about a year ago. (Clear glass with flowers and butterflies printed on it in black, unknown serial or product number) today while I was in the other room I heard a loud crashing noise and discovered that the desk top had spontaneously broken and glass was scattered all over the room. It was like it literally exploded. There was glass on top of shelves and bookcases which are several feet above the table top level, and glass also all over the room in some places about 7-8 feet away from where the desk was located.
Once I purchased the table top, it had not ever been dropped or nicked or damaged in any way so any defects would have been a result of shipping or handling while en route to, or at the store, or a manufacturing defect. The only items on the desk at the time were a pair of pants and a shirt, so it was not a weight issue.
The glass did shatter into hundreds of small pieces and a few large chunks as I believe it was intended to. My concern is if anyone was in the same room when this occurs. Someone could be severely injured if they were any where near this product and it suddenly exploded and sent hundreds of shards of glass flying everywhere. Luckily no one in my family was in the room at the time and the only injuries were some minor cuts to our hands from trying to clean up the glass.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries from glass shards, and the potential for severe injury if someone had been nearby.

incident_description: I bought a Novaform gel memory foam 3 inch mattress topper from Costco three weeks ago. Since having the mattress topper on my bed I have experienced a sore throat, ringing in my ears, extreme fatigue, swollen eyes, loss of appetite and occasional heart pressure. At first I thought it a cold or mild flu but symptoms weren't subsiding. I am typically a very active, healthy woman in my 30's.  I've been exceptionally tired and noticed red cherry hemanginomas suddenly appearing on my abdomen.  I looked into the hemanginomas and bromine came up.  From there I found that mattress toppers often times have bromine and other toxic chemicals. I subsequently found that many other people have these symptoms associated with memory foam.
justification: The description details multiple health symptoms linked to the mattress topper, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the user's report of similar cases.

About 2 months ago I called back after not hearing any word on a replacement unit. 
I spoke with [REDACTED] ext [REDACTED]. He told that that replacement unit was very expensive and that without a receipt  I would not receive a replacement.
Last week I decided to just bite the bullet and buy a replacement unit, and spoke with [REDACTED] in the Cincinnati office ([REDACTED]. I told [REDACTED] I would be sending them the old unit to inspect for areas of concern.
Today I spoke with [REDACTED] at their tech service. He was more intent on telling me what a quality product I had purchased and he was focused on the cracked plastic at the mounting screw area of the grill. I told him I was more concerned about the melting, warping and discoloration of the old unit.

I want to be reimbursed for the new grill. I believe the old grill was defective. OR, it may be that the product is defective. I would like this to be investigated.

incident_description: I bought a Cherry Manchester Conversion Crib from babys r us in December of 2010. My daughter just turned two in January of this year. I decided to convert the crib into a toddler bed. In order to do that you need to remove the front of the crib and the side posts that usually hold up the crib remain. This conversion went well for about three months. On march 12 my daughter went into her bed to take a nap. Upon waking up she stood up to walk over to me and slipped backwards. She hit her head on the side of the post (which is very sharp) and she split her head open. There was blood EVERYWHERE! We brought her downstairs and tried to clean up most of the blood to see how bad the wound was. We took her to METRO emergency room where she had to get stitches. She also had a concussion. She didn't know who I was, or who her daddy was. The following morning I called the manufacturer of the crib and she promised me that I would get a response within twenty four hours. She even sent me a letter stating she made the manufacturer aware of the problem. They did not contact me. I called them again, and they said they were not aware of the situation. I told them I wanted my money back for the crib because I no longer want it in my house. They said they would refund me my money and they still have not. They scheduled a day to pick up the crib and never showed up. Now they are ignoring me. IF my daughter had to  get stitches and had a concussion due to this imagine what could happen to another child? It could be worse. I have contacted an attorney and will be taking this into a legal matter. They say they are all about child safety when they ARE NOT! Or they would not be ignoring this situation.
justification: The child suffered a head injury requiring stitches and a concussion, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the described incident and the potential for similar occurrences with the crib design.

incident_description:
On March 8, 2014, I purchased and installed eleven (11) Utilitech LED bulbs from Lowes. I used these bulbs to
replace ten ( 10) 60W incandescent light bulbs in the kitchen. Four (4) of the bulbs were installed in the ceiling fan in the center of kitchen and six (6) in an over head hanging light over the kitchen table. These light are used
periodically and are never left on overnight or used for any extended period of time. On March 11, 20141 was
working in the garage directly off the kitchen area. I had turned on the ceiling fan light prior to going out to the
garage. The ceiling fan was not on. After about twenty (20) minutes I came back into the kitchen and at that time I heard a very loud cracking sound coming from the ceiling fan light. I looked up and saw black smoke for- 
1 second and then flames shot out from one of the lights. I immediately ran to the garage for the fire extinguisher, shutting off power to the light on my way out. Within seconds I came back in with the fire extinguisher but there were no visible flames only smoke. I watched the light for about fifteen (15) minutes and thought it was safe to remove the bulb from the socket. The top of the bulb was cool to the touch but the base of the light bulb was extremely hot. I placed the bulb out in the garage to cool. About twenty (20) minutes later I checked the bulb and the base was still warm to the touch. l removed all these LED light bulbs I had installed immediately.
The ceiling fan was installed when this house was built in March 2012.
I stopped at the Lowes store that I had purchased the bulbs from got a copy of the receipt and told them what
happened and that I would report this incident to the CPSC and provide them with a copy of the report.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke from a faulty LED bulb, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
SYLVANIA Compact Flourescent Bulb, Model Y529-1, 13 watt, 120 Volt NC, 60 Hertz.

On March 30,2013 at 0500 hours, EST, the aforementioned SYLVANIA compact flourescent bulb, which had been
inserted into a chandelier type lighting fixture for some time, was witnessed to suddenly emit sparks, smoke and
brief flame. The observants immediately turned off the light fixture, allowed the bulb to cool and removed it.
Photos were taken of the defective bulb.

According to Safeproducts.gov, similar model compact flourescent bulbs are experiencing the same defective
hazards as noted by numerous complaints.

However, SYLVANIA continues to repond to these safety concerns in a defensive litigious fashion as follows listed in the follwing link. There appears to be a design and or manufacturing defect with this product that could easily, if not already reported, present a danger to life or property loss via result fire as a direct result of this product's defective design.

www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1382228
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and brief flame but no injury or death, and similar defects have been reported by others.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she woke up from sleep because she felt extra warmth on her leg. 

The consumer stated that the cord that goes into the blanket is stuck. The consumer stated that the cord can come off but overheating caused it to be stuck and turn brown.

The consumer stated that when she stretches the blanket out, the bottom portion (near the cord) of the blanket is wrinkly. The consumer stated that you can see the wires run through the blanket.T he consumer stated that the blanket was not like that before.

The consumer will contact the manufacture to see if the product is covered in warranty. The consumer would like a replacement if possible.
justification: The incident involved overheating and visible damage to the blanket but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Around 02/18/14, the consumer stated that he had an incident occur with the recalled medicine cabinet. The consumer stated that the glass shattered and injured his wife. The consumer's wife suffered a knot and an appx 1/2in cut on her forehead.

The consumer contacted the retailer to find contact information for the manufacturer. The consumer contacted the manf regarding the incident.

The manf informed the consumer that they would send out replacement mirrors. The consumer received his replacement mirrors on 2/26/14.

The consumer stated that the manf never informed him of the recall. The consumer came across the recall while conducting his own search. The consumer stated that he asked the retailer of why he was never informed about the recall but the retailer did not take responsibility.

The consumer has safety concerns regarding the mirrors that are sent out to him as replacement. The consumer stated that these mirrors are thinner than before. The consumer stated that the new hinges are not appropriate for the mirror and don't function well when the cabinet door is opened and closed. The consumer stated that the mirrors shake and rattle when he opens and closes the door. The consumer stated that the mirrors are missing a laminated back panel. 

The consumer stated that when the incident occurred with his old mirror, much of the glass stayed on the back panel. The consumer stated that if these new mirrors were to fall out, the glass would fall all over the place posing more laceration hazards. 

The consumer also plans on contacting the manf regarding his concerns with the replacement.
justification: The consumer's wife suffered a knot and a cut on her forehead, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that her candelabra light bulbs have been exploding.
She purchased candelabra lights possibly in 2012 at a few different retailers and has had three incidents of them exploding since that time.
The first of the incidents occurred February/March 2012; she contacted the manufacturer who sent her a few boxes of replacement bulbs.
It has been over two years since the first incident and it has happened four to five times over this period.
No one has been injured to date however the consumer is reporting as a safety hazard due to the potential for eye damage or other serious injuries from the flying pieces.
There are no known injuries to report at this time
Caller contacted the manufacturer numerous times with the initial call being March 19th, 2012 and ongoing to this date.
[REDACTED] answered this initial call and referred the caller to [REDACTED].
She sent [REDACTED] two email s and received no answer at all.
She was able to speak to [REDACTED] one time on April 17th, 2012 at which time he informed her that he was conducting tests.
She continued talks with other representatives including [REDACTED] but with none following through to a complete explanation or resolution.                                                               
 February 17th, 2014 the consumer spoke with [REDACTED] again who instantly remembered her and her situation.  Informed her that she ([REDACTED]) would call the consumer after a meeting she was preparing to attend.
The caller did not hear from [REDACTED] until February 21st, 2014 when the caller received an email stating that after conferring with the director of quality control it has been decided that what she experienced was normal end of life occurrences as a result of normal wear and tear.
The caller responded that it was not her belief that explosions of product being a normal end of life incident and this is  not an acceptable explanation.
Caller asks if there is any way for consumers reporting these bulbs to be able to meet with one another.
justification: No injuries have been reported, but the exploding bulbs pose a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: We purchased a set of wood bunk beds, the kind with built-on stairs ( no ladder ) from Value City Furniture last year. The stairs have cracked and broken twice in the last year and have had to be replaced. The wood slats under the top bunk have buckled and are not safe. This bed is very dangerous and failure can result in serious injury. I have contacted the store numerous times and they have failed to respond.
justification: The bunk bed has structural failures that could lead to injury, but no actual injuries are reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her 6 year old daughter (weight 55 pounds) was lying for about 2 hours on the top bed of a bunk bed four feet from the floor, her 4 year old son was on the lower bed about the same time. 

The consumer was outside of the childrenÃÂs room when she heard a loud ÃÂbangÃÂ sound. When she entered the childrenÃÂs bedroom she noticed that the top bunk had collapsed over the lower bunk bed leaving only 6 inches of space in between the two, with her daughter on it. Her son had already moved off the bed when she arrived to the bedroom.  There were no injuries sustained by this incident.  She discontinued the use of the beds and dismantled them.

01/30/14- The consumer contacted the manufacturer and the seller through email but has yet to receive a response.

She feels that this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.

This product is not affected by a recall.

incident_description:
We purchased a Cal Lighting Pharmacy floor lamp from Destination Lighting through Amazon.com a little less than 2 years ago.

The lamp has started burning out light bulbs (standard incandescent) at a very high rate.  On examination of the lamp, we saw significant discoloration of the white insulator (indicating overheating) and the black plastic component that screws on to the fixture to hold it in place is disintegrating (it crumbles into pieces when you touch it).

Destination Lighting will not consider the problem and refer us to Cal Lighting.  Cal Lighting will not deal with consumers.

We consider this to be a safety hazard.
justification: The lamp shows signs of overheating and component disintegration, posing a safety hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

incident_description: Ceiling light bronze hook broke suddenly without anyone touching it.
justification: The ceiling light hook broke suddenly, but no one was injured.

incident_description: Installed LED light bulb. After about two hours of constant use, it started to burn. On the bulb, it says "suitable for use in enclosed illuminaries" ours was an enclosed light fixture. My wife heard a popping noise and went to investigate. The ceiling was full of grey and black smoke. If we had not been home, our house would have burned down. This is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard that could have led to severe property damage, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he walked in the room turned on the light and immediately the incandescent 60 watt light bulb in the ceiling fixture exploded sounding like firecrackers, shattering glass pieces all over the bathroom floor.  

The manufacturer was not contacted yet.
Caller feels that this bulb is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb exploding without injury, indicating a minor hazard with possible recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a bed from the company in January, it was devivered in February.  I put in a few service calls to the company I purchased it from after it was delivered, because it did not seem sturdy and it seemed unsafe. After a few weeks, my daughter finally decided to use the bed for sleep.  At 3am on March 14, 2014, one side of the bed completely fell apart , the wood spliting into, and my daughter falling into the area that had fallen in.  The spliting wood almost punctured her to death!  she is now terrified.  The make of this bed is very unsafe and will eventually take the life of a child or children.
justification: The bed collapsed, causing injury and near-fatal harm to the daughter, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
Caller stated that he smelled smoke and noticed that it was emitting from the ceiling fixture where the bulb was located.  He immediately turned off the light and removed the bulb and noticed that there a burnt hole on the side of it.

The manufacturer was not contacted as yet.

Caller feels that the bulb is a fire hazard and should be reported.
justification: The incident involved a burnt bulb emitting smoke, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I bought six fluorescent shop lights from Home Depot for my greenhouse.  When I turned two of the six lights on, they started a flame near the ballast and melt the plastic ballast.  I took them back to home depot.  They were very inexpensive, about $12.96 from China.  They were made by Commercial Electric. 201 462 2-Light Shoplight. I have pictures of the box.
justification: The incident involved a flame and melting plastic but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such product defects can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
We purchased the Graco Sarah Classic crib 2 years ago when our son was born.  We purchased it it to replace a recalled crib because this one was supposedly up to new higher safety standards.  A few days ago, when our son demonstrated the ability to climb out of the crib, we converted the crib to a toddler bed, following the instructions that came with the crib.  There were no problems noted at that time.  The next morning upon waking we discovered that the wooden stretcher/stabilizer bar had SNAPPED during the night.  This created a bed that was structurally unsound and exposed our young child to sharp, splintered, spear-like pieces of wood.

The manufacturer cannot be reached to report or discuss this issues.  Multiple calls are met with the recording "due to high call volume, please try again another time" and the call is then disconnected on their end.
justification: The crib's structural failure exposed the child to potential injury from sharp wood, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought a Mainstays floor lamp silver from a local Walmart yesterday( mar 8 2014).  When I plugged the power plug into a power strip. The safety switch of the power strip was immediately shut down. I reset it and plug it in again. Immediately the plug produced sparks and a burning smell was smelled. One of the prongs of the plug was partially melted. My power strip was damaged. It was scary.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a burning smell with a melted plug, indicating a significant electrical issue but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The caller stated that her 42 year old son sat on the chair and he fell sideways with it.  He received minor bruises to his knees. They noticed that one of the chair legs had sheared off (broke).  

12/28/13 The store was contacted and her spouse was informed that the chair set was not under warranty.  He requested that someone came out and look at the product and they informed him that some would be sent out in 1/22/14.  The retailer called back and reschedule visit for 2/17/14.  They came out and informed her that they would repair the chairs but she declined because of the safety hazard.

Caller is concerned that these chairs are unsafe and poses harm to consumers and should be reported.
justification: The incident resulted in minor bruises, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The chair leg shearing off suggests a possible design or manufacturing flaw, making recurrence likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
(2/2014)  The 61" tall, 149 lbs., consumer had been sitting in the chair for approximately 15 minutes in the reclined position, when she attempted to get up. The consumers' right foot was caught on the edge of the foot recline portion of the chair and she fell forward, landing on a carpeted surface.  The consumer fell on her left knee and her bone hit the floor very hard.  That same evening, the consumer went to Beverly Hospital, ER, Beverly, MA.   X-rays were taken and the consumer was referred to an orthopedic doctor for further treatment.  She was told to apply ice to the injury and to keep her knee elevated.

That same week, the consumer went to her regular doctor [REDACTED], who is an orthopedist.  He advised her to apply ice, keep the knee elevated and he prescribed pain medication.

(2/24/2014)  The consumer went for a follow up appointment this morning with [REDACTED] and x-rays were taken.  He told the consumer that there was no fracture, but that due to the swelling, there was a lot of damage to her knee.  He advised her to apply ice and keep the knee elevated.  Some of her swelling has gone down.


Approximately, 1 year earlier (2013), the consumer was sitting in the chair, in the reclined position and she fell asleep.  The phone rang and the consumer was startled.  She started to get  up to answer the phone, but she forgot to put the foot rest down.  As she got up, the entire chair fell over on  top of her.  The consumer managed to get from underneath the chair on her own and she did not sustain any bruises or injuries at that time.  The chair was in the same location in her home and on a carpet surface, as the 2nd incident.

That same week, the consumer called the retailer and sent a person out (name unavailable) to look at the chair.  The person that came out advised the consumer to nail the chair to the floor.  The consumer was not happy about the response.  She lives in an apartment and could not do what was suggested. 


The chair is powered to recline electrically by a wired remote, which is attached to the chair.  The remote also powers the foot-rest to go up and down.

Overall, the consumer believes that the chair may not be heavy enough on the back portion.

NOTE:  When the recliner was initially delivered to her home, it was in separate pieces and had to be assembled.
justification: The consumer sustained a knee injury requiring medical attention, including ER visit and follow-up care, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident has occurred twice in a year, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description: I was trying to put staples into a Longreach stapler and the head snapped back.  I withdrew my fingers in time so there were no injuries.
justification: The stapler head snapped back but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was using a Bright Effects CFL 9W light bulb when it started to flicker and emit a strong acrid odor. I turned light off and could not touch the bulb for over 5 minutes due to it being so hot. In fact it was so hot it melted the porcelain (?) base and loosened the glass where it was attached to the base. The smell permeated the whole second floor of our home. Had I not been home I believe the bulb would have started a fire. On top of all of this the bulb did not last as long as they say they should. I had bulb for maybe 6 months and it only is used on average 1 hour a day.
justification: The bulb emitted a strong odor and became extremely hot, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Safety First Quick Click bed rail loosens up over night or when any pressure is placed on it this creates a gap between the bed rail and the mattress that is a potential entrapment/strangulation hazard.  This occurs even though the green "lock" indicator clearly indicates that it is "locked"
justification: The bed rail loosening creates a potential entrapment/strangulation hazard, which could lead to severe injury or death, but the description does not confirm any actual incidents or injuries.

incident_description:
Recently heard of the recall regarding the latches on Lane cedar chests. We have a cedar chest that we purchased new in 1983 from Wickes Furniture Store in Minneapolis, MN.  We only recently became aware of the recall as a result of the television show "Inside Edition".  

The serial number and style number on the bottom of our chest were poorly stenciled onto the bottom so we cannot identify the exact style.  We sent photos of the chest to Lane along with the purchase date so they could identify it and received a reply that our chest is a newer one and is okay.  (The recall is for chests manufactured from 1908 to 1987 and since we purchased it in 1983, it obviously was manufactured before 1987 and is within the recall.  The top on ours does latch automatically when the chest is closed.  I communicated and spoke with numerous people at Lane, including a Supervisor named [REDACTED] about the problem.  She is going to check further tomorrow (Mar 12, 2014) but am sending this notice to make you aware that other consumers may have been told that their cedar chest lock is safe when it is in fact not safe at all.  There needs to be a thorough review of the entire recall effort and any consumer that was told their chest was safe, needs to recheck it.  The original recall contained an explanation of how to test the chest but the new recall does not contain that.  This is still a dangerous situation.
justification: The incident involves a potential safety hazard with a recalled product, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: New Serta Perfect Sleeper Highfield Plush mattress gives off toxic fumes. After 10 days of airing it out it still continues to smell really bad. We have had all windows open and ceiling fans on but nothing has helped. Our son even got sick with sinus, ear and upper respiratory infection while the mattress was in our home. Contacting Serta their representative claimed they must have forgotten the carbon packages in the packaging and advised to get the mattress out of the house asap. Despite admitting their mistake Serta still charged us $200 and 15% of the price to have it returned/exchanged. We have owned 4 of these same mattresses before and didn't have a problem with those.
justification: The incident caused a respiratory infection in the son, indicating an injury, and the company admitted to a packaging error.

incident_description: An 87-M was sitting on a white plastic chair when a front leg broke causing him to fall and strike his head on the ground on 01/24/2014.  He did not lose consciousness and did not immediately seek medical attention.  The decedent began c/o headache and demonstrated decreased level of consciousness by the following day.  A head CT taken 1-2 days later revealed an intracranial bleed (subdural hematoma).
justification: The incident resulted in a fatal intracranial bleed, meeting severity level 4. The occurrence likelihood is low (2) as such severe outcomes from chair breaks are uncommon.

incident_description:
The consumer stated she pulled the cabinet out of the box. The consumer picked up the cabinet and moved it to another room. The consumer stated that she discarded the box.
The consumer stated that she was probably in contact with the cabinet for 2-5 minutes. The consumer stated that she started itching instantly. The consumer developed hives on her arms and hands. The consumer stated that she washed her arms with soap and the hives got worse. The consumer stated that the hives spread to her stomach, legs, and face.
The consumer stated that the hives got worse overnight. The consumer stated that the hives were as wide as 3-4in. The consumer took [REDACTED]. 
The consumer stated that few days later she had to pull things out of the cabinet, so she put on gloves to get them. The consumer stated that she touched the cabinet again by mistake. The consumer stated that she developed the hives again. 
The consumer stated that she went back to the retailer to find any warning labels on the box. The consumer stated that the box did not have any warning labels on it.
justification: The consumer developed hives after contact with the cabinet, indicating an allergic reaction, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Purhcased NovaformÃÂ® 12" Valentina Queen Memory Foam Mattress.  My son slept on it the first night and woke up with extreme sore and swollen throat, clogged nose.  He had no fever so I knew this was an allergic reation to the mattress he just slept on. I will be returning this mattress and will never buy anything with memory foam and chemical laden again. I had no idea of the dangers with all the chemicals until he personally experienced it.
justification: The son experienced an allergic reaction with physical symptoms (sore throat, swollen throat, clogged nose), indicating an injury.

incident_description: The plastic housing on compact fluorescent light bulbs manufactured by USHIO in UAE are cracking.  Electrical arching was heard on two of the 7 bulbs that I replaced. The glass blub sections are then very loose and break free from the plastic housing when attempting to replace the bulb.  A lot of particles fall on to the floor or kitchen counter it's unknown if these particles contain mercury.  I contacted the manufacture and they said they were interested in having the bulbs returned but have not sent me a return authorization.  I contacted them on Jan 18th, 2014.
justification: The incident involves cracking and electrical arcing of bulbs with potential mercury exposure, but no reported injuries.

incident_description: I was sitting on the sofa next to a floor lamp.  The lamp is on a timer.  The lamp had been on for about 6 hours.  About 1 second after the timer shut off the lamp one of the light bulbs exploded with a puff of smoke.  There was glass everywhere.  The bulb is a GE 43w 120v 565 lumens RVLL50 bulb.  I believe it is a halogen bulb.  It is not a florescent bulb. These bulbs are dangerous and need to be banned or recalled due to the safety/fire hazzard! I have 2 of these lamps and have removed these bulbs and will be stocking up on incandescent bulbs before they are unavailable.
justification: The bulb exploded causing glass to scatter, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I'm in the market for a new ergonomic desk chair, so last Saturday (2/15/2014) I and my wife stopped at Office Max to test out chairs. The "Work Pro Commercial Mesh Executive Chair" (SKU# 2411-4780) looked great and felt sturdy and I sat rather comfortably in it. But when I placed my right hand over the front edge of the seat and explored one of the adjustment levers on the left side of the chair, I suddenly felt one of my fingers had become locked in the chair's mechanism. Although I tried to work the adjustment lever and slide my finger out, my finger was painfully stuck. My wife tried to manipulate the lever too, but she too could not release the chair's grip on my finger.  Soon the tip of my finger turned white and my wife was calling "emergency, emergency."  A cashier called the manager but the manager did not arrive soon and could not release my finger.  It is hard for me to estimate the time that passed, perhaps four or five minutes, but eventually a shopper worked the adjustment and freed my finger.  This accident could have been prevented by a better design. In particular a plastic guard could be in place to prevent the chair gripping a finger much like a vise.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful injury to the finger, turning it white, which indicates a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
I lacerated my hands three times within the last month on my Ergotron Workfit-S, Dual Monitor with Worksurface+. The keyboard tray has sharp edges and points on the bottom. So, when I pull the workstation down and rest my hand on my lap they're exposed to the sharp edges. My hands were lacerated on sharp edges on the back of the Worksurface+ during install as well and the back of the L-shaped bracket holding the keyboard tray

This is supposed to be a device designed by human factors engineers, and yet they don't follow industry best practices or any guidelines by nationally recognized test labs for product safety. We were expecting a safer product.
justification: The description reports multiple lacerations, indicating injury, and the issue is recurring due to the product's design flaws.

incident_description: We had an explosion of a medium base A19 light bulb that was installed in a kitchen dimmable open fixture base up.  The light bulb was a Philips EcoVantage soft white 29w=40w dimmable mercury free bulb.  The explosion was caused by the inner element, which appears to be a halogen bulb.  No one was in the room at the time, but the outer glass envelope was shattered, sending shards onto the kitchen table and floor.
justification: The explosion caused property damage (shattered glass) but no injuries, as no one was present in the room.

incident_description: The loop at the top of the chandelier (bottom of chain) broke, causing the light to hang by the wires instead of the provided chain.
justification: The chandelier's loop broke, causing it to hang by wires, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We have a Hendredon dining room set that we purchased several years ago at Macys.  One of our dinner guests this week leaned back on the entire back of the chair broke off from the seat.  He hit his head on the wall and fell on the floor.  I contacted Hendredon and they referred to Macys.  Macys no longer carries Hendredon and they referred me back to the manufacturer.  I findally took the broker chair to KELLS Furniture Repair, Roswell, GA today.  The owner inspected the damage and noted that there was no glue used during production and the fasteners were too short and there were not enough to secure the back of the chair to the seat.  I am very concerned about the 7 other chairs with our dining room set.  I am also wondering if this is a flaw that could cause harm to other Henrendon chairs owners.  I have photos of the broker chair and will have a written report from KELLS once the chair is repaired
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hit head and fell) due to a chair breaking, and similar defects in other chairs suggest possible recurrence.

incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED]. I purchased a TV stand that is advertised on walmart.com as: Black Wood TV Stand with Media Storage and Mount, for TVs up to 65". (walmart number 007129694)

Website: http://www.walmart.com/ip/Black-Wood-TV-Stand-with-Media-Storage-and-Mount-for-TVs-up-to-65/14690455

I fully assembled the stand and nearly took four hours doing so. When I was pushing the stand back I noticed the following notice pasted to the back of the unit:

CAUTION: This stand is intended for use with a product that has dimensions that will permit it to sit evenly on this stand. 

It further states

"This stand is intended for up to a 60" flat panel tv"

I brought this stand because it is advertised as being able to hold (presumably safely) a 65" tv, as I have a 65" flat-panel [REDACTED] that I recently purchase. 

I am concerned that it will topple over as it is 5" over the dimensions that the product is listed as being able to hold safely. I am particularly concerned because I have 3 children under the age of 6 and am concerned for their safety. 

When I called Walmart they explained that the "manufacturer" of the product was responsible and that they are not responsible for the advertising on their website. I also note that a "brown" version of the product is advertised similarly on walmart.com

I request that someone check into why this product is advertised on Walmart.com as it is. I also request that walmart contact all persons who have purchased the product to inform them that the product is not to be used with flat-panel TV's greater than 60". I also request that an investigation is conducted to understand if people have been injured with use of this product as advertised.
justification: The incident involves a product misrepresentation and potential safety hazard, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: My master bedroom has a hanging light fixture in the center of the bedroom that is partially enclosed as it is open on top. It is a 3 bulb fixture rated at 60W per bulb. Tonight, one of the 43w light bulbs in the fixture exploded and sent sharps pieces of glass all over my bedroom. The explosion happened within one minute after turning off the light fixture. Fortunately, I was not injured.
justification: The light bulb exploded, causing glass shards to scatter, but no one was injured.

incident_description: The consumer says the blue christmas tree lights hurts his eyes as well as his [son] and wife.  The consumer says the lights radiate ultra violet light.  The glass on it is chemically coded and very harmful.  The consumer says that as soon as he looks at them he had to "squint" his eyes.  He says he never has had eye problems before.
justification: The consumer reports eye discomfort and squinting from the lights, indicating potential injury.

incident_description: We bought a honey-can-do toy storage product at walmart and put it downstairs in my daughters play room. Yesterday, she was cleaning up and bumped her head on the corner. She now has a gash on her brow, and a purple eye. It took 10 minutes to get the bleeding to stop.
justification: The child suffered a gash and a purple eye from bumping her head, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she was outside of her room when she smelled an odor similar to ÃÂburning gasÃÂ. The consumer stated that she inspected her house to locate the source of the smell. The consumer entered her room and noticed that the light fixture on the ceiling was on fire, even though the light switch was off. 

The consumer immediately evacuated her house and contacted the fire department. The firefighters arrived approximately 5 minutes after. They  extinguished the fire and inspected the electrical wiring and gas pipes for the home. The fire department determined that the source of the fire from the light bulb capacitor malfunctioned, setting the base of the bulb and the ceiling on fire. They advised the consumer to remove and dispose of the similar type of bulbs and replace them with LED light bulbs. The consumer estimates $2,000 worth of property damages.

2/8/14- The consumer contacted the retailer. The retailer offered a full refund if the consumer could present a receipt of purchase.

The consumer thinks that this product poses a safety hazard to consumers.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: In my kitchen, I have a lamp above the island.  There are three bulbs in that lamp.  My wife and I heard a popping sound and then a sound of an electrical short.  We went into the kitchen to investigate and approximately 15 seconds after the initial noise, another sound of an electrical short and the light bulb had file coming out of the side and darkened the light fixture.  I turned the light switch off and the fire went out.  There was a significant amount of smoke and visible flame and the house smells like burning/burnt electronics.
justification: There was a visible flame and significant smoke, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Pushing large plastic trash container (wheeled) with lid open. (very heavy, filled with lawn/garden trash). Container tipped slightly back, my foot caught the flopping lid thus pulling the container toward me while tripping me. My forehead was struck by open top of container. Brief unconsciousness, heavy bleeding. Major laceration at hairline. Bleeding stopped by compression and ice: hair cut away near laceration, butterfly bandages applied.
justification: The incident resulted in a major laceration and brief unconsciousness, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
Several years ago I purchased three Voluspa glass container scented candles at Villagio Inn & Spa in Yountville, CA.  Over the years I have discovered that each of the glass containers have cracked, and even burst apart.  Each time the candle remained lit as the melted wax poured out of the container.  In one instance the wax poured out onto a coffee table, lighting the table on fire and causing smoke damage to my home.

I was actually able to witness the last incident.  I was burning a Voluspa "Malayan Coco" candle, which had a pretty solid glass container and I thought was safe to use.  After roughly 1 hour of burning, the candle started to make a "ticking" sound.  Shortly thereafter the top of the candle burst, ejecting sizable glass shards up to two feet away. incident_description: 2/14/10 - Husband put son in bumbo on kitchen island. Bumbo was placed on an unread newspaper, still folded up. No tray or seat belt on bumbo. Husband turned away to make son's bottle. Son wiggled out of bumbo and fell to tile floor. Bumbo remained stationary. Son was visibly shaken, startled, red marks above left eye and left cheek. We rushed our son to ER immediately. ER doctors checked him out, observed him for 4+hours (due to concern of head injury), advised us against cat scan due to age, sent us home. Three weeks later we were back at ER because of wheezing/cold (son was diagnosed with RSV at that visit), they happened to take a chest x-ray, which revealed a single mending rib fracture on left rib. We advised them of fall and ER visit 3 weeks earlier. They sent us home to treat RSV and told us nothing to do for rib except let it heal. ER report goes to pediatrician (standard practice with ER visit), pediatrician calls us to take son for another x-ray to confirm what they see. We do, and then pediatrician calls DCFS. DCFS requires us to take our son to the hospital on a Friday night where we stayed for the next 5 days being threatened by DCFS that they would take our son away if we refused all the tests. He had full skeletal survey + an unnecessary MRI because his head was larger than average, and various blood panels. In all adverse reactions during MRI, 50% are in kids under 1 years of age. No choice but to follow their orders or risk our son being taken away. All tests came back fine except the SINGLE rib fracture on the LEFT side of his body. I thought we were good to check out. They advised mend time was approx to date of fall, no additional injuries, They advised they still thought it concerning for abuse. They had no process in place for a 2nd opinion. Required us to have 24/7 parent supervision  in our home while they did an investigation. Despite investigation coming back no concern with parents or daycare providers they said the injury was not consistent with the fall and indicated an ****unknown perpetrator**** abused our child. Son is now on the state register for abused children because of this. We hired the DIRECTOR of the bio-mechanical engineering lab in Chicago, a phd with 30 years experience. These people are injury recreation experts. The only people who can really offer an opinion based on the reason DCFS gave for indicating abuse. The report came back indicating that rib fracture likely resulted in our son arching back and flipping over the side of the bumbo and the fall to the tile floor worsened the fracture. In summary, it was 100% plausible it happened exactly the way we described. We presented the report to DCFS in the appeal process and despite ALL the evidence they would not dismiss. Over $17k in expenses related to trying to prove that the bumbo is what abused our son, not some unknown perpetrator. The case is now with the Supreme Circuit Court. How does a bumbo accident with EVIDENCE to support what happened turn into this nightmare. And I didn't even include the entirety of the impact this had on our lives/family! The bumbo makers, the doctors, DCFS and yes, my dumb husband are to blame. BEWARE PEOPLE. Thankfully, my son was not as badly hurt as some other cases I am reading about. My heart goes out to those people. Hopefully, they didn't have to deal with DCFS also!
justification: The incident resulted in a rib fracture and required multiple medical evaluations, indicating an injury (severity level 3). Such incidents are possible but not common, hence an occurrence likelihood of 3.

I smelled a burning smell and discovered that the light coming into the window was being refracted through the snowglobe--and that focused light was burning another decoration behind it and starting a fire.  

There have been similar recalls involving other snowglobes, but this one seems to be dangerous.  I still have the other decoration that was being burned.  No one was hurt, since I was home at the time and was able to stop it.

Please note: This happened at the address below, but I do not receive mail at this address, as there is no mail box at the property.
justification: The incident involved a fire starting but was caught in time with no injuries, indicating a minor incident with no harm.

incident_description: Our fire department responded to a reported fire in a business. We arrived and found fire on the ceiling. Fire was extinguished and it was discovered the paper backing on the insulation had ignited. There was a fluorescent light in the area of origin. The light had visible damage and soot on the fixture. Pictures were taken. The light was Eiko SP105/50/MED.  As Fire Marshal, I determined the light bulb was the cause of the fire as there were no other sources of ignition in the area.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was extinguished without injury or death, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such electrical fires are not uncommon but not frequent.
