incident_description:
I am a mother of 2 toddlers currently ages 4 and 34 months.  On 2/17/2013 I purchased a DONCO Kids Honey Mission Twin Bunk Bed from Zulily.com in hopes to have both toddlers use it in the future.  Soon after the furniture arrived, we set up one (1) twin bed alone for our eldest toddler (in Spring of 2013).
On 1/2/2014, we decided to set up the additional twin bed for our 34 mo. old but NOT as a bunk.  We set the twin bed up perpendicular to the first twin bed.  
Tonight as we were tucking our 34 month in for sleep, my husband leaned on the bed and it suddenly made a loud cracking sound and the entire side support beam split apart and the mattress sank down in the middle.  It scared all of us and my 34 mo. old cried and scrambled off of the bed immediately.  What is even more upsetting is I am 25 weeks pregnant and was kneeling with my knees placed underneath the very beam that shattered.  The wood could have collapsed on me or my belly or flew outwards and punctured me/my unborn baby.  
I have taken photos of the broken bed and it is clearly poorly constructed as a screw is visible where the rail/wood split and it is placed very near a knot in the wood, which is never a strong point in the wood's composition.  Thankfully, we did not have this bed placed/installed as the top of the bunk as it is designed to be, or else it could have been even more serious with our child falling out of the bed and to the floor, perhaps being cut or punctured by the sharp wood.  

I would like to note that I tried calling DONCO on 1/6/2014 and spoke with a male rep who answered the phone.  I briefly explained what had happened and who could I speak to regarding the incident and this man actually implied it was our fault because my husband (who is not by any means overweight) caused the bed to break because he leaned onto it.  My husband has slept on the other twin bed belonging to this bunk set several times since March 2013 with no incident.  To imply that an adult cannot lean on a bed that is supposed to be manufactured to hold an adult is ludicrous.  I retrieved the email address of the owner of DONCO Trading Co and he is supposed to respond to my email/complaint which I emailed to him directly 1/6/2014.
justification: The bed broke but no one was injured, though there was potential for harm to the pregnant mother and child.

incident_description:

These health symptoms included rashes, respiratory, headaches, nausea etc.  She discovered the odor when she uncovered it about a month ago.  She stated that the odor was so overwhelming it permeated the entire house and carpet.  

The chair was removed and placed outside and she had her entire home cleaned. Since then she is not having any health symptoms.

(10/2013) The retailer was contacted and a technician sent out 11/16/13, he informed her that he did not smell any odor.  She is concerned that the chemicals in this chair poses a health hazard and should be reported.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
We placed chair outdoors for several weeks before Macy's inspector appointment.  Once outside the home, I no longer suffered a stuffed up nose, cough and my face/around nose and mouth/ healed from blister type sores after about 6 weeks.  Still have a couple of marks on my face from the outbreak.

Since it is not a "nasty smell" hard to describe smell (more like sweet with slight pepper to me). I believe it is easy for the inspector to not acknowledge it or he is used to it, it does not register with him.  [REDACTED]  I believe most people used to the smell in dept stores and not aware it is chemical and dangerous to our health since stores smell this way and so do new cars.  Macy's Inspector told me nothing wrong and they refused to refund my $700. I took back PJs to Macy's when I noticed the smell. [REDACTED]

[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer reported health symptoms including rashes, respiratory issues, and headaches, which indicates an injury level severity. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible due to the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: This evening the mini lamp in my daughter's bedroom almost caught on fire. The lamp was bought in 2007 from Pottery Barn Outlet. It has a lampshade that is attached to the lamp by a metal clamp that fits directly on the light bulb. The lampshade was knocked off of the light bulb when my daughter turned the light on. She did not notice that it was knocked off and the paper/plastic part of the lampshade then rested on the hot light bulb for some time (maybe an hour?). We noticed the smell of smoke when getting ready for bed. At first we thought it was smoke that wafted upstairs from dinnertime. Then, as we approached her bedroom, the smell of smoke became significantly stronger. When I looked at her nightstand, I noticed that the lampshade was askew and that it was smoking. Upon further investigation, the lampshade was slowly burning and turning brown. The lampshade was actually melted onto the light bulb at this point. I immediately turned the lamp off and unplugged it from the electrical outlet.
justification: The lamp almost caught fire but was discovered and turned off before any injury occurred, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:

Seems to me that Westinghouse must have changed suppliers and that its new supplier doesn't meet the same quality standards the company used to maintain.

incident_description:
On November 21, 2013 I heard a noise coming from one of our spare bedrooms.  Upon investigation I opened the closet door in the bedroom and discovered one of the 8 foot fluorescent bulbs from the Lithonia electrical fixture had fallen from the ceiling fixture and was in flames.  The closet was full of clothes, pocketbooks, and other personal belongings, most, if not all of which were flammable.  I reacted by grabbing the bulb and pulling it free from the closet while slapping the flames out with my hand. As this was happening I noticed flames on our wooden floor in front of the closet.  I stomped out those flames.  The charred piece of material that I lifted from the floor was later identified as a piece of the Lithonia plastic protective tube guards used to protect these bulbs from accidental contact or breakage from the bulb.  

I called 911 and the Clermont, Florida Fire Department responded with two trucks.  The firemen were here about 45 minutes and told us that we were extremely lucky that we were home and responded so quickly.  They said that our house would have burned to the ground and all of our possessions with it if we were not home or ignored the noise in the spare bedroom. 

An electrician installed the Lithonia fixture, model C2 96 120 GEB on the ceiling of the closet approximately six weeks earlier.  It was used many times during those six weeks without a problem.  It had two fluorescent 8 foot, T12 bulbs and both had Lithonia Clear Tube sleeves/guards, TGT12 CL 8FT R24 around them.  

We called in a second licensed electrician to inspect the installation job of the installing electrician.  He concluded that there was nothing wrong in how the installing electrician installed or ran the wiring for the fixture.

I contacted Lithonia on December 2, 2013 and reported the incident to [REDACTED] who works in their PMD Post Sales Department.  [REDACTED] requested pictures that showed the burned fluorescent bulb, the burned socket bracket and the identification label.  We sent him the pictures.

Mr. [REDACTED] subsequently responded to us  by email and informed us that, ÃÂthe likelihood of the lamp sleeve causing the problem is quite high.  He further stated in his email, ÃÂIn general, we do not recommend tube guards with fluorescent lamps that are operated on instant-start electronic ballasts, which this fixture has.  There are different types of tube guards, some of which have limited temperature ranges, but they all increase the possibility of poor lamp-to-lamp holder connection.ÃÂ

Our Lithonia fixture did not display ANY language warning us of potential fire if used with any plastic tube protector or with an instant start electronic ballast referred to by Mr. [REDACTED].  I am attaching both the Lithonia plastic Tube Guard literature, and the warning label on the Lithonia electrical fixture box.  As is evident there is no warning in either which addresses the possibility of poor lamp-to-lamp holder connection or fire. If this is really true, Lithonia is NEGLIGENT in not warning consumers and their electricians.  Lives could be lost.

I subsequently sent both a letter, and an email to their Vice President in charge of this product, and have received no response.  His name is [REDACTED], and he can be reached at Lithonia LIghting,  [REDACTED]
It is my upmost hope that you will investigate this.  If we had been asleep we could have died in the fire.  I fear another family may not have our good fortune.
justification: The incident involved a fire that could have resulted in severe damage or death, but was quickly contained without injury or death.

incident_description:
I have tea lights from Ikea - 
info. on package is 100 X GLIMMA
made in Vietnam  
package AA-419673-1

print stamp says 0949

incident_description:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to inform you of a serious concern I have regarding IKEA glass desk tops. I purchased two glass desk tops December 29th 2012 for my kids study room. This past Saturday 12/7/13, when no one was in the room there was an explosion. We all rushed upstairs and to our amazement one of the desk glass table tops had not simply just shattered but had actually exploded and in the process thrown small pieces of glass across the entire room. Note this room is carpeted, so this is not a case where glass fell to the floor and somehow momentum caused it to slide. In order to land where the glass pieces didÃÂ they had to be launched with a decent amount of velocity! After researching on line I discovered that there have been numerous incidents of this occurring; although at this point a recall has not been issued. The question of "safety" vs. "quality" appears to be the pending item. In my case although the "Tempered" glass did break into tiny pieces as it is designed to do... I am so thankful that my kids or any family member was at the desk. This is simply because although the glass broke into smaller peices... the smaller peices still contained very sharp "shards" of glass and glass flakes.  No one could predict the potential harm or danger a single small piece of glass launching into an eye would present. Again, it broke into relatively small piecesÃÂ however I want to be clear. This was not a case of the glass simply cracking and falling to the floor. It was definitely an ÃÂEXPLOSIVEÃÂ event.
justification: The glass desk top exploded, launching sharp shards across the room, but no one was injured.

The lights were plugged into the outlet to enable them to see where they were being placed in tree.

incident_description: I am reporting on a product by Buffalo Snow which is called Frosty Snow.  It is a fake snow for decorating.  As my three year old granddaughter and I were sprinkling it on our Christmas village she accidentally inhaled a piece.  It actually blocked her airway.  Fortunately we had four CPR trained adults because we had to perform the Heimlich procedure and do a mouth sweep several times before she started breathing again.  This product will kill a child. incident_description: The lamp was on the floor, and turned on. The lamp resides next to my bed and a pillow fell off the bed and became wedged between lamp and the side of the bed. Minutes later we noticed a burning smell and realized that the lamp was burning and had burned a hole in both the paper side of the lamp, the pillow case, and the pillow as well.
justification: The incident involved property damage (burned lamp and pillow) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
I purchased a Hanukkah Menorah from the web site 'World of Judaica.com'.

The Menorah item is listed as "Gold Polyresin Hanukkah Menorah with Floral Pattern and Hebrew Text" (Product ID #MNR-TJ-47341).

On the first night of Hanukkah the Menorah not only began melting, but actually started smoke and burn.

After putting out the fire, I looked up the material 'polyresin' on the internet and learned its often used to make candle holders.  However, polyresin is plastic, so shouldn't there be some sort of warning label or protective insert to keep the polyresin from burning?  

No where on the web site or on the product description or packing does it indicate this Menorah cannot be used with real candles nor did the item come with mental inserts or any special instructions.

I took photos of the melted and burned Menorah and have also emailed the web site.

I feel this item is extremely dangerous and could have easily started a fire in our house.
justification: The Menorah melted and started a fire, posing a significant fire hazard, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: I had a CFL melt and scorch the ceiling of my garage, with melted plastic and the shattered bulb on the floor of the garage.
justification: The incident involved property damage (scorched ceiling and shattered bulb) but no injury or death.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was using the electric blanket which was plugged in, on the off position and it started to emit smoke. The consumer stated that he smelled a plastic burning odor. The consumer stated that the electrical blanket was being use in his motor home and he had to pull over and turned off the electrical power to the inverter. 

The consumer stated that he noticed that the control was emitting, had melted plastic and it had burn the carpet where it was laying. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured and he stated that the blanket was no longer usable.

The consumer stated that he returned the product to the retailer and received a full refund. 

The consumer stated that he will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report.

incident_description: We just want to warn people to be careful with their shade cords. We have bali today cellular shades on all our windows in the house, and the kids will find a way to wrap or tie the cords around them. This has happened to two of our children where they climbed up on the back of the couch and someway got the cords around their necks and fell off the back of the couch with one and one was up on the short ledge and both got terrible rope burn gashes on their necks when they fell. luckily i was only a room away when it happened, but it can happen so fast and kids can do things we don't expect them too. my daughter was 2 when it happened and my son 4. we now have a 6 month old and plan on updating all our shades/blinds to cordless due to the scares we've already had w/our other 2 children.

incident_description: A lightbulb exploded showering the office with shards of glass. The bulb was purchased from Topbulb.com and manufactured in China by Bulbrite located in Moonacie, NJ. The lightbulb is item #695100 and the UPC is 739698695105. It is a halogen BR-40 Flood 100W/120V. There is no marking on the packaging or product that it is listed with Underwriters Laboratories or ETL for safety. The office has 3 other identical bulbs installed and no other bulbs were affected or the circuit breaker tripped. I contacted both Topbulb.com and Bulbrite. Topbulb.com did not want to do anything because they only sell the product and have never heard of this happening before and blamed it on an electrical problem. Bulbrite didn't want to take responsibility either. After stressing that I was concerned for the safety of the product and that I had the bulbs installed in other parts of the office they finally said to send an email with the details of the incident and a copy of the receipt of purchase. It appears they are only going to address the monetary issues and not the safety issues.
justification: The lightbulb explosion caused an incident with no reported injuries, and the occurrence likelihood is considered possible given the lack of safety markings and manufacturer's response.

incident_description:
Our Kichler Olympia 1691AP chandelier fell from the ceiling of our two story foyer and was destroyed on impact, which would have seriously injured or killed anyone underneath it. We phoned the electrician who installed it. He came out the next morning to inspect it and told us the "hickey" (he says that is the real term) was defective. This is the metal piece that screws onto the nipple and connects the chandelier to the chain. The metal fractured in a jagged pattern, and is obviously defective. 

After searching on Google we discovered that Kichler has another very similar chandelier that has faulted in what sounds like the same place and manner. Kichler has issued a recall on this chandelier. It is recall number 13-222 and was issued on June 20, 2013. We believe our chandelier has the same defect as the recalled fixture. 

The chandelier was hanging from the ceiling of our two story foyer, and has been there since January 2008. We hardly ever used it as the light from it didn't illuminate our foyer very well. Instead we use installed recessed lighting and two floor lamps. The fixture was connected to a chandelier elevator to make changing bulbs easier. However, since we have misplaced the key to the elevator, it has never been used and placed no stress on the chandelier.

The damage amounted to a complete loss of the fixture, as well as putting dents in our hardwood floor. Anyone who might have been under the chandelier when it fell would have been seriously injured or even killed. My wife and I had passed under the chandelier many times the day it fell, and fell incredibly fortunate that we were in a different room when it broke and dropped.
justification: The chandelier fell and was destroyed, but no one was injured. The defect is known and recalled, indicating a possible but not frequent occurrence.

incident_description: My husband was sitting on the couch with the built-in recliner.  He sat back and we heard a thump.  I looked under the couch saw our 5 month old kitten hanging down from the metal mechanism that retracts the recliner and foot rest.  We didn't move any of the foot rest or recliner and flipped the couch up.  I saw he was caught and her neck was stuck.  I tried to pull him out gently but he didn't come loose.  I pushed on the bar to try and move it and it wouldn't move to release him.  My husband had to push it and then he came loose.  He was unconscious and his throat was cut open.  I could see his neck was cut open and he was breathing through his trachea.  I am 41yrs old and had my first panic attack.  I was hyper ventilating and in a panic.  We rushed him to the Pet ER and they said it was really bad and would cost 2 thousand dollars to get his surgery to repair his neck.  We had to put him down.  I am still crying after a whole week and I can't sit on the couch and use the foot rest or recliner without having anxiety.  I am not going to use it anymore.  When I lay down or wake up, I think of him being stuck and not being able to get him loose.  That picture will never leave my mind.  I have a co-worker that had his dog's toe cut off by the metal mechanism so I know I am not the only one that has had trouble.  A child could have been playing under the couch.  There should be some kind of protective cover over the sharp metal mechanisms that open and close.
justification: The kitten died due to the incident, which warrants the highest severity level. The mention of a similar incident with a dog suggests that such occurrences, while not common, are possible.

justification: The chair tipping incident occurred twice in one day without injury, indicating a design flaw but no harm.

incident_description:

Then, later, it happened again so I took a closer look and found one of the CFLs that had shorted out and looked like a small fire.  I have the light and photographs.  Fortunately, this was a ÃÂporchÃÂ light with nothing flammable surrounding the light and the breaker worked again, shutting off the power to the circuit.

incident_description:
Caller purchased his reclining chair March 12th, 2012 _ Chair was manufactured in 2011.

Caller used the chair to sit in but had not used the reclining position until January 2013 after heart bypass surgery.

After his surgery he needed to use the reclining feature because he had to keep his feet elevated.

The first time he tried to use the chair in the reclining position the chair flipped placing him on the floor with his feet solid on the floor but his body lying on the ground and the chair over him hitting his left hip which he said is still tender to the touch.
He is reporting this chair as a safety issue both as a stabilization safety issue and as a fabric to skin irritation issue.
When he sits in the chair for more than one to two hours his skin becomes extremely sensitive to touch.

He has tried to obtain return or refund through both manufacturers but has had no luck

He said he has tried to work through Consumer Protection within his state in an attempt to return for refund or replacement but this has been unsuccessful.

He is asking for assistance from CPSC because he states that this is not a safe chair by any means.

Caller has not obtained medical assistance for his hip that he believes was injured by the chair tipping over on him

Caller has contacted the manufacturer a few times with the last time being a few months ago.
justification: The caller sustained an injury (tender hip) from the chair flipping, but did not seek medical attention.

incident_description:
After opening two drawers In our Ashley furniture Porter dresser with attached mirror, my three year old son reached up to get something out and the dresser tipped forward. The entire dresser came toppling over.  The mirror snapped off, hit our bed, and shattered.  

Luckily, my husband put his arm out and shoved our son back before the dresser could land on him. When the mirror snapped off, it hit my husbands arm before the glass shattered all over my son's head.  Had the 190 lb dresser (this is the weight listed on the website, before clothes and mirror are attached), had we not been in the room with him, or had my husband not thought fast enough to shove my son out of the way, I am not sure if he would be here with us today.

After the dresser toppled, we noticed that there was a white plastic bag stapled to the back of the dresser.  It contains an anchor.  We NEVER knew that there was a safety anchor attached to this dresser, or that it was recommended that we anchor it to the wall.  We paid Ashley Furniture to deliver and set up this furniture, and in my opinion, they were VASTLY negligent in not letting us know that the anchor existed (let alone offering to put it on).  

We have several pieces of furniture in our home that are anchored to the wall.  This is something that we take very seriously.  Had we known that the recommended safety requirements for this dresser were to anchor to the wall, I can guarantee that we would have done so.  

This was the scariest experience of my life.  I thought for sure at the moment that the dresser fell that my son was underneath.  We are lucky, but not because of Ashley Furniture and their delivery people.  Someone was looking out for us, and it was not the safety concerns of the company who sold us this furniture.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury due to quick intervention, but the potential for severe injury or death was high, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the described scenario and lack of anchoring.

incident_description:
This is a copy of the message sent to Westinghouse:

I have contacted Westinghouse twice in the last 2 months, once on September 29 and again on October 13, related to one of their products (CFL) that literally exploded. I am copying my message I sent to them twice below:

"Last night at about 11PM (PDT) after the kitchen lights had been off for several hours, one of the Westinghouse R-30 Reflector, 15W, 120V, 60Hz, 240mA lamps exploded. Glass shard were spread over counter tops, on the stove and on the floor. We feel lucky that it didn't happen while we were in the kitchen having dinner. It could have created a much worse scenario. In the better light of day, I intend to use our shop vacuum in case I may have overlooked other minuscule pieces of glass.

I can see that several other Westinghouse bulbs are mixed in with another brand that we used as replacements over the years, and I'm wondering if it would be advisable to replace all of the W. bulbs at this time.

As my husband is in a wheelchair, I am the go-to person for these sorts of home maintenance issues, and I am not happy. Please advise."


Each request to them was answered with the same message (below):

"Thank you for your inquiry. A Westinghouse representative will respond to your request shortly.

For more information on our products, visit www.westinghouselighting.com"

To date, we have not been contacted by any representative. Do you have any advice for us? We are hesitant to turn on the overhead lights until there is some resolution.
justification: The incident involved an exploding light bulb causing glass shards to spread, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
On October 11, 2013, at 1:30 a.m., while on the second floor, I heard the loud sound of ta bump and glass shattering 
(as if somone threw a brick through a window). I composed myself for fear that it might be a burglar. I checked my 
daughters' rooms while my mom checked downstairs. One of the hallway ceiling light fixtures (one switch puts on 
two ceiling light fixtures) above the entry door from the garage burst. The glass shade exploded. Various sized hot 
shards of glass was everywhere. The sharp pieces was extremely hot to the touch. I had to use a paper towel for fear 
of getting burned/ cut.
On 10/11/13, around 8:30 a.m., I emailed Crown Communities, to inform them of this dangerous and hazardous 
event. The warranty department responded house closed in 2009 and not under warranty. Although the house 
was built in Nov. 2009, this home was not officially lived in until Aug. 2011. The lights were not used during that 
time. I called them that afternoon to find out the ceiling fixture manufacturer info. They did not respond. Later 
that afternoon I contacted CSPC to get procedure for this issue.
On October 17, 2013, I sent Crown Communities another email requesting ceiling light fixture manufacturer info. 
Their response was: [REDACTED]- two electricians they dealt with during the 2009 construction 
On 10/24/13, Tired, we contacted the electricians. [REDACTED] said Captial Lighting. [REDACTED] 
(Capital Lighting) stated "they do not deal directly with the public, customers have to go through a dealer with any concerns."
justification: The incident involved a ceiling light fixture exploding, causing hot glass shards to scatter, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I removed a functioning standard light bulb from my table lamp.  I installed a Cree brand ÃÂwarm white LED 60W replacementÃÂ bulb purchased at Home Depot.  I turned the knob on the lamp to turn on the bulb. Immediately, there was a pop and hissing noise as the bulb flashed on then off and smoke and flames rose around the bulb.  The computer, which was plugged into the same surge protector, immediately shut off.  I immediately turned the knob on the lamp ÃÂoffÃÂ, unplugged the lamp and took it outside.  The room was filled with a stench of burned rubber or plastic.  I pressed the reset button on the surge protector and restarted the computer, which appeared to function properly.  After a few minutes, I removed the Cree bulb from the table lamp and noticed that the contacts of the lamp were sooty and melted and the base of the bulb had smoke residue stains. incident_description:
During the first part of September, 2013, I installed 3 brand new GE 60W Clear Reveal G25 bulbs in an overhead three-light fixture.  Approximately a month later, one of the bulbs started to intermittently go out and come back on while the other two continued to work properly.

Two days after the one bulb began to malfunction, I switched on the light fixture, (wall mount light switch)  and one of the two "properly" working bulbs literally blew out of the socket onto the floor!  The bulb remained mostly intact emitting a pale gray smoke and did not shatter into pieces.  However, the base and attached filament stayed lodged into the socket and I had to have an electrician remove it.

incident_description:
Several years ago we purchased a kitchen table and four matching chairs from the Ikea Store in West Chester, Ohio.  

This table is made by Salmi (apparently a vender of the Ikea company) and is still sold today.  It is designated as model 20692 and can be viewed on the Ikea web site: 

http://www.ikea.com/us/en/catalog/products/70102298/

As can be seen in the image the TABLE TOP  is clear tempered glass  (41.375ÃÂ diameter) and this TOP weights perhaps 60 lbs (estimated). 

The top is held in place by only gravity, resting on soft plastic pads glued to the metal chrome ÃÂ plated frame and legs ÃÂ i.e., the top was not latched to the frame.

This table functioned well for several years but last Monday (September 23, 2013)  it ÃÂexplodedÃÂ ÃÂ with considerable force and sound ÃÂ sending small jagged bits of glass up to 12 feet from the center of the table.  There is no way to estimate the number of glass shards (mostly approximately  0.25ÃÂ X0.25ÃÂ rectangular bits) but there were hundreds of thousands (literally) of them. The covered the entire kitchen floor some were found on the dining room carpet over 12 feet from the original center of the table.  Most of these shards had extremely sharp jagged sides and edges.  They were extremely difficult to clean up safely.

As luck would have it I had just passed by the table as was standing within 6 ft of the table but was behind a ÃÂkitchen islandÃÂ and did not get hit with glass ÃÂ but I believe anyone in line of the glass trajectory would have been cut ÃÂ perhaps seriously.  

I was not looking at the table at the time of explosion so I can not describe it other than to say it sounded like gun shot or a large fire cracker.

We attempted to call Ikea and report the problem and were immediately told that the table was "out of warranty" but that we could buy a new top from Ikea.  We have no interest in another such table top.

We persisted and insisted that we wanted to report it as a safety concern to Ikea -- at this point we routed for desk to desk (each time with a long hold times) after about 4 or 5 transfers the phone would go dead.  We redialed and the same thing happened -- a series of transfers then the phone disconnected.  But calls to Ikea lasted more than 20 minutes before the phone disconnected.  It seemed like a pattern and if you read the internet you find many making this same complaint.

Clearly there seems to be no person, nor does there seem to be a procedure at the Ikea company for addressing safety issues with their products thus we have filed this report.  Their headquarters are in the Netherlands but the are a Swedish company.
justification: The incident involved a table exploding with potential for serious injury, but no actual injuries were reported.

incident_description:

incident_description:
We purchased about 16 of these lights for use throughout the house.  They have been used for approximately 3-6 months depending upon the bulb (they were purchased at different times). The reason for this report is we had a failure and it was a very bad failure.  The light caused sparks, smoke, and some damage though in this particular case the damage was minor.

The light was located in a recessed can in the bathroom.  The bathroom is divided into two areas: one room with a door holds the toilet and shower (which I would consider a damp room) and the other room has just the vanity (which I would consider a non-damp room).  The light was located in the vanity/non-damp room.  On the basic single-pole switch, there are 3 recessed light (which includes the failed bulb) and the mirror light.  On the circuit, there is only ceiling lights/fans.  It does not combine with any wall outlets, etc.  Of the 3 recessed lights on the circuit, only the one failed.  The others did not flicker or dim during the event.

The actual failure event occurred in the morning.  The lights to the room had been on for approximately 30 minutes.  I was near the vanity mirror getting ready for work, so I witnessed everything.  First it made an audible buzzing noise quickly followed by a shower of sparks coming from the bulb.  The switch was turned off and the bulb emitted smoke for a few moments.  After it cooled down (it felt very hot - much different than the other bulbs), I removed it from the fixture.  The sparks had caused some charring to the plastic trim.  I tried another bulb, of the same type, in the fixture and it worked as a bulb is expected.

The bulb has a burn mark on its side.  In the center of the burn mark there is a hole where you can see inside the bulb now.
justification: The incident involved sparks, smoke, and minor damage but no injury or death, and the failure was isolated to one bulb out of multiple in use.

incident_description: The glass bulb  unglued and internal contacts were exposed.  These were not isolated from power line when measured with ohm meter.

The equipment was purchased at the Lowes store in Stuart, Florida (just south of Indian street) back in November 2006 and since it was place in service we did not observed any signs of straining or yielding that would indicate to us that the chandelier was in imminent mode of failure.
justification: The chandelier fell but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury. The failure was unexpected with no prior signs of strain, suggesting it was unlikely.

incident_description:
On 2 separate occasions, my mother and husband had the Dutailier Multiposition Glider tip forward on them  (base completely leaving the floor) while getting out of the chair with our newborn infant. This chair is unstable and a tipping hazard which should not be marketed to parents of babies. These are very popular chairs that are sold in baby supplies stores all across the country, but they could easily result in injuries for users.
Thankfully in our situation, my mother and husband held onto our infant even as they fell onto the ground, so she was not injured, but the situation could've ended very different quite easily w our baby slipping out of their arms.

Yes, upon closer inspection, I am aware that there is a small warning tag attached to the chair that says it should not be used in recline position w/ babies, and that one should not sit on the edge of the chair. However, I do not think this is sufficient. I am shocked that Dutailier continues to profit from the sales of this chair (costing $500+) without bothering to devote resources to improve such a fundamental design flaw, merely satisfying themselves by attaching the warning tag to protect themselves from litigation should injuries occur.
It is ridiculous to me that I can buy a reclining glider in a baby store, like many other parents do for nursing and rocking their newborns, only to find that one should not use it in reclining position w/ their babies b/c it is so dangerous. Many baby products have been recalled for far less significant hazards.
justification: The chair tipped over twice but no injuries occurred as the infant was held securely, though the potential for injury was high.

My husband found him wrapped up in the crib sheet like a mummy with his arms and hands bound by the sheet and the elastic wrapped so tightly around his neck that he could barely breathe and my husband could not even stick a finger in between the sheet and his neck to loosen it. incident_description:
I purchased a Simmons Lake Street, Pillow top, Queen mattress set from Mattress Barn, 1970 Northwest Federal Highway on 5 July, 2013.  The set was delivered to my apartment at [REDACTED] on July 10.  This is my secondary residence as I work in Orlando area, but my permanent residence is in Port St. Lucie, FL.  Around July 24, or approximately two weeks of use, I began to experience rash like symptoms on my outer thighs, my sides,  and under my arms.  As I sleep on my side with one arm extended above my head, these would have been the areas in most direct contact with the mattress.  The symptoms began to spread to include my inner thighs and across my mid-section.  I began to limit my contact with furnishings in my apartment to my bed and one chair.  I attempted to self-medicate with anti-histamines and eventually to include over the counter hydrocortisone spray.  When I went home to Port St. Lucie for the weekend, symptoms began to finally improve, but return more strongly after returning to my Oviedo apartment and sleeping in the Simmons bed. I also noticed that the irritant began to follow me around as bare skin contacting the chair began to increase the irritation.   This is a chair that I had used the prior three months without incident.  On July 31 I sought treatment at a Port St. Lucie clinic and was diagnosed with folliculitis.  The doctor specifically ruled out chiggers, a local pest, and said it was not an allergic reaction.  She did not rule out scabies, but said that if treatment she prescribed worked, then that would rule out scabies.  She prescribe sulfa antibiotics, prednisone steroids and benadryl  anti-histamine.  Since then my symptoms have greatly improved, though I also no longer sleep on my new mattress.

I contacted Mattress Barn, and spoke to [REDACTED], the salesman I bought the mattress from, on August 1. I explained the diagnosis of folliculitis and wanted Mattress Barn to honor their 30-day money back guarantee.  He said that was only on exchanges.  He stated that if I wanted to return the mattress set it would be subject to a 30% re-stocking fee of $500 and referred me to the back of the sales slip.  That section assessed the re-stocking fee for returns "other than a warranty claim". I asked him if Simmons used chemical flame retardants in the mattresses and what they were.  He said he did not know and suggested I contact Simmons.  I asked him if Mattress Barn had any hypo-allergenic mattresses for people with sensitive skin and he said no.  I explained that since he could not tell me what materials were present in their mattresses and had no hypo-allergenic alternatives that I was offered no choice.  

I do not want this mattress, but nor do I want to pay a $500 penalty for their faulty product.  However, my health is more important than $500 and if I cannot have this mattress tested for likely contaminants and force Mattress Barn to accept the mattress back at full refund, then I will have no choice but to return it and pay the $500.

I fear there is something in this mattress that allowed the infection to take hold.  It is apparently portable and I do not want to be contaminating my family, friends, home, office and other living spaces.  Whatever this is, it suppressed my bodies ability to fight an infection.  I cannot know what long term effects that might have.
justification: The incident resulted in a diagnosed medical condition (folliculitis) requiring treatment, indicating an injury.

The seat back connects to the seat bottom by using two mushroom-head bolts to connect metal tongues attached to each. The failure mode appears to be the heads snapping from the shafts because of metal fatigue. When the heads snapped off (the first snapped off with a "pop" the prior evening but I could not determine what actually had happened) there was nothing to maintain the connection, the seat back fell suddenly and I fell with it, bruising my left tricep I possess the second head which was trapped under the seat back, the other is somewhere among my staged recycling. I also possess the bolt shafts and a section of plastic molding snapped off the seat back by the seat bottom's tongue. In the design the bolt heads appear to be subject to significant, repetitive stress as the seat back flexes during normal posture changes.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (bruised left tricep) due to a chair failure, indicating a moderate severity level. The likelihood is possible as the failure mode suggests repetitive stress could lead to similar incidents.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he experienced problems of Release #12-276 with his chair.  He was sitting in the chair when seat broke off the base and he fell sideways to the floor. Hazard: The seat plate can break, posing fall and injury hazards to consumers.  There was no injury.  He stated that although the chair is called different names they are the exactly the same, which is made by the same manufacturer and he purchased his from a different retailer.

The Sku number is not listed on the recall.

(7/15/13) The manufacturer was contacted and he was informed that they were not aware of any recalls on their chairs.

The consumer feels that this chair is a safety hazard and should be included in the recall.
justification: The consumer fell when the chair broke but reported no injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident suggests a possible defect, making occurrence likelihood 3.

incident_description: We have a Kichler Chandelier and the connecting ring broke.  Luckily it didn't fall on anything.
justification: The chandelier's connecting ring broke but did not fall on anything, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The BrightLight blanket batteries overheated and leaked out of battery compartment. Leaving a white powered residue inside battery compartment and on to the BrightLight blanket. Child touched the leaking battery compartment. 

The BrightLight blanket no longer works and or lights up after a few months this product was gifted to child.
justification: The incident involved battery leakage and a child touching the residue, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: A Philips Marathon mini decorative twister EL/mdT 15W began lighting only intermittently. As I began to replace it to see whether it was the bulb or the wiring of the fixture, I found that something on the bulb was extremely hot -- it caused a painful burn on my finger, where I touched it for an instant. for an instant. The replacement bulb functioned, so the problem was not in the fixture. The bulb was not more than a year or so old, and shouldn't have burned out; but the problem is that the heat generated was painful and conceivably dangerous, and completely unexpected.
justification: The incident resulted in a painful burn injury, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) because the issue was unexpected and not a common occurrence with the bulb.

incident_description: Had installed a bunch of Cree LED lightbulbs - 60W warm white and 40W warm white.  While my daughter, 5, was in the bathroom, a lightbulb exploded.
justification: A lightbulb exploded while a child was present, posing a risk of injury from flying glass or debris.

incident_description:
The consumer says that she pulled out the sofa and slept on the mattress.  Recently she stopped using  it because the mattress was thin.  She said that when the two cushions that you lean on are removed to open the sleeper,  there is a large gap left when using the sleeper. 

She says she was almost sucked into the space when laying on it.  She tries to use the cushions she took out to cover the space while in the sleep position, but they are too large.  The consumer says that two weeks after using the product she developed a rash on her back and her arms.  

She says that everyday appears to worsen and she has gotten scabs from scratching.  When looking at the contents of the furniture she noticed a label that says it contains 57% Polyurethane.    She plans to contact the retailer about her skin irritation.  She has talked to them about the issue of the open space but they were not willing to assist her with that problem. 

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
Sent pictures to Ashlet Furniture about space in sofa sleeper when opened.  I also told them mattress might have been too thin and maybe there is such a large space when opened as a sofa sleeper- a thicker mattress would cover the hole
justification: The consumer developed a rash and scabs from scratching, indicating an injury. The issue with the sofa sleeper design is a possible but not certain recurring risk.

incident_description: I was using a Hampton Bay Floor Lamp (Model #398-505) regularly for lighting in my bedroom.  I have two of these lamps, the other of which is in the living room....both have experienced similar issues but the one in the bedroom is the particular one that prompted me to write this complaint.  I turned on the lamp this morning and left the bedroom for about 2 minutes and when I returned the light was very dim and there was a clicking sound.  The other lamp has occasionally gone dim as well but never with a clicking sound.  I looked at the socket where the light bulb was installed and noticed blue sparks therefore I unplugged the lamp.  There was a foul electrical odor in the air (which has happened on the other lamp when it was dim before as well).  I let the lamp sit for two hours for the bulb to cool down.  When I tried unscrewing the bulb from the lamp, the bulb shattered and cut me because the base of the bulb was actually fused to the lamp socket.  I reported the incident to Hampton Bay as both lamps exhibited the same issue but the response I received did not seem very concerned which prompted me to write this complaint.  I am not sure if it was a bad batch of lamps or if this is a common issue but I believe the product to be very unsafe.
justification: The incident resulted in injury from a shattered bulb and the description indicates recurring electrical issues with the lamps, suggesting a possible defect.

incident_description: The screws on the chairs and table will fall out randomly and pose a choking hazard to children and pets. Also the welds on the chairs fail and will cause the chair to break when its sat on. reviews of the product show that others have had this very same problem with this set if you read the 1 and 2 star reviews you will see it. Mainstays 5-Piece Wood and Metal Dining Set, Multiple Colors. my set is only 5 months old and i have already lost 3 screws on one chair. The screws will not go back in because the wood on the chairs is so cheap that it striped out causing the screws to drop onto my floor.
justification: The incident describes a choking hazard for children and pets due to falling screws, and chairs breaking when sat on, which could lead to injuries.

incident_description: plywood that came with the bunk, cannot hold child of 80lbs. They cracked and my son feel through with the mattress, Very cheap plywood. This company was not thinking, OTHER than saving some money for themselves. Very unsafe bunkbed.  I purchased from a furniture store in my area and they stated that they would contact the company and they have not done so. They said they could replace with better plywood, but no way those bunkbeds are a death trap. Bunkbeds states it holds up to 150lbs not true. The bottom bunk plywood cracking as well. Those bunks need to be recalled.
justification: The description reports that the child fell through the bunk due to cracked plywood, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: This incident involves a dining room chandelier purchased from Lowes.  My husband and I came in one afternoon to find part of a metal ring on the dining room table and discovered that it had come from the chandelier which was still hanging from the ceiling.  It was hanging only by the electrical wire because the ring at the top of the chandelier had broken.  The ring was apparently made of a cheap pot metal and could not support the weight of the chandelier.  The replacement part sent to us appears to be of the same material.
justification: The chandelier fell but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
On February 16th, 2013 Caller went to the curb where the garbage truck had just emptied her 96 gallon can.

She shut the top of the trash can and began pulling the can the 250 feet from the road to reach her garage, she stopped in her garage, on a flat surface she put the trash can upside down to empty the rainwater then turned it right side up again.

The lid was open, she pulled it toward her and very quickly she was sucked into the trash can.

Her left hand was on the handle making it a fist position and causing severe bruising on the left hand and left arm, her right front tooth was knocked out and the left front tooth is slightly cracked.

She states that she always closes the lid to her trash can but since she was only moving a very short distance she diverted from normal behavior and became injured.

She contacted "Rumple" 3700 Struble Road, Cincinnati, OH 45251 - 1(513) 742-2900 February 28th, 2013, informed them of the incident and her injuries.

The trash company who also provides the cans, sent employee [REDACTED] out to caller's house within 25 minutes after receiving her call and caller describes him as pleasant but also said the this person advised her that she is too short to be moving the 96 gallon can, took a report, pictures and provide caller with Claim# [REDACTED].  (Caller is 5'2" tall).

Around  March 26th,2013 caller contacted the trash company again to inquire about the status of what she thought was a study going on to find cause of her accident but was informed that they always take pictures and create a report so that it was on file.

Company informed caller that they had no intention of doing anything because they list her incident as personal responsibility and it was the same as if she had run over the trash can with her vehicle. 

Caller asked company representative, [REDACTED] that if it was such an issue why wouldn't they just put a more visible warning on the cans advising consumers not to move them unless the lid is closed.

She would ask that this be processed.

Company said that there employees always close the lids, caller states that they rarely close the lids.

[REDACTED] also informed caller that "Please" has a definition of danger or caution.
                                   Caller states that the wording Please Close Lid Before Moving should be in red, orange, yellow any color but the black wording on the black lid.

Caller asked to speak with someone over [REDACTED]'s head to which [REDACTED] replied, that she would have [REDACTED] contact the caller.

[REDACTED] contacted caller around March 29th, 2013 and during a forty minute phone conversation where he was during time explained to caller that her incident was personal responsibility.

Caller explained to [REDACTED] that her dentist's receptionist had fallen in her can twice and [REDACTED] told her that they were not talking about the dentists receptionist that they were talking about her and that he had eighteen other complaints but her wasn't focusing on them either.

She asked him if he couldn't just at least place a brightly colored sticker on the cans for the consumer.

He answered her that they had just placed five million dollars worth of trash cans within the city of Cincinnati and if he placed a bright sticker such as the one she described then the city may rethink the contract.

Caller was taken by car to Accudoc, Inc. (Greendale) (812) 577-0092 (urgent care), treated and released.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER: On the can it says in the black imprinted on blank lid in back of lid. Please close lid before moving.   Rumpke told me Please means Caution, Danger! It also says on outside of lid in back to move  bin 1) grasp handle, 2) tilt 3) push or pull.
justification: The incident resulted in severe bruising and a knocked-out tooth, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as such incidents are not common but have been reported before.

incident_description:
tv stand collapsed under 65" plasma set - t crashed to the floor. luckily, no one was home.

design defect - the back of the top shelf is secured by 2 disks that are glued to the glass. no, really!
justification: The TV stand collapsed, causing property damage but no injuries since no one was present.

incident_description:
Purchased the 02 Cool Arcticloth Cooling Towel  on 7/6/2013 at the Rumford, ME RiteAid.  I used this product for the first time on the evening of 7/16/2013 for about 2 hours.  I wrapped the cloth around my neck.  I wiped my face and chest with the towel.  The next morning I had itching burning splotches on my neck and throat that reminded me of poison ivy.  Since then the rash has spread up beyond the hair line, down the middle of my back where the sweat dripped from under the towel, covers my neck, my chest, out my arms.  My face has blotches and it now is effecting my eyes.  

I reported this in a review on Amazon.com where I read of this happening to someone else.  Since my review, I have been contacted by someone else who's child has become very ill from using this product.  She said she was reporting this product to CPSC and suggested I do the same.
justification: The incident describes a severe rash and discomfort affecting multiple body parts, indicating an injury. The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the mention of similar incidents reported by others.

incident_description:
Chandelier model 34330 from Kichler mounting loop broke and landed on the dinning room table.
Shorted the wires and caused circuit breaker to trip. Dented the wood dinning room table.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: One of the 5 legs on the chair broke and the chair fell over with my 72 year old wife
justification: The chair fell over with a person on it, indicating an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I own an adjustable bed that has two bases that lift a king size mattress by head and foot, plus have a massage feature.  The bed is approximately 2 to 3 years old.  The controllers for the bed have a plug that comes from the outlet into a control box (2 boxes total) and out of the control boxes into motors into the adjustable base.  The controllers are controlled by a wireless remote control.  Last week, a ball had rolled under my bed and I reached under to scoop it out.  In the process of reaching for the ball, I had to move wires, which were placed loosely on the floor.  As I moved one of the wires, sparks came out of one of the controller.  I immediately unplugged the bed and contacted the company who sold me the mattress who sent out a service technician.  The technician examined the controller and noted that the wire leading to the bed, just as it exists the controller was exposed.  He explained he would contact the manufacturer, Leggett & Platt regarding the issue.  He called today and explained the company would not cover the part as they did not deem it to be a manufacturer's defect.  I had called the Leggett & Platt myself after being surprised that they would not take responsibility and were not concerned over the safety issue on this and other bed bases they have sold.  The agent explained to me that they carefully inspect the wires before the bed leaves.  I stated that even if that were true, it does not mean one could not wear out.  Her position was that it could only wear out if it were pulled on.  I explained that since the bed was installed, the wire sit there and the only pulling that could occur would be from the lifting of the mattress.  She explained that it would then be the installer's responsibility to properly place the controller.  I explained that if the location was so sensitive for proper and safe operation that there should be a mounting location to avoid the potential problem and allow slack in the wire to properly lift.  Furthermore, even if the installer did located the controller box on the floor at time of delivery, consumers would likely clean or otherwise go under (such as to retrieve a ball) and the wires would be randomly moved without becoming taunt and further there are no warnings to the consumer as to the danger of not having proper amount of slack to allow the bed to adjust up.  Notwithstanding, I am not convinced that the wires became exposed due to improperly designed or manufactured controller.   Leggett & Platt's consumer support division was condescending and dismissive when I called with the issue.  I am deeply concerned over the safety of this defect, whether manufactures, design or information, as the spark could start a fire on the carpet the controller sits on, the wood the base is mainly constructed of on.  Luckily a rare instance of having to reach under the bed disclosed the problem as it could have easily done the same while adjusting the bed when there would be no warning of a likely fire risk while on the bed or sleeping.  I may be reached at [REDACTED] should you need further information or if you'd like to inspect the defective unit.  Manufacturer's contact number is: 800-888-3078 x 2 and the serial number to my bed base is GA652573.
justification: Sparks from the controller indicate a potential fire hazard, but no injury or damage occurred in this instance.

incident_description: We began using a king size Biddeford heated mattress pad in the Fall of 2012.  The pad worked well for a few months, but then one side began to heat only intermittently.  When we removed the pad, we discovered that the cord connecting the power/controller to the pad had a short in it roughly 1" from the mattress pad connector.  The short had melted the plastic around the cord and burned a half inch hole in the mattress pad.  This short developed without the product having been adjusted or manipulated in any since the initially installation.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit that damaged the mattress pad but did not cause any injury or death.

incident_description: When removing mattress pad after using it for several weeks, we noticed the connector from the transformer to the pad was browned and the wiring is charred. The wire itself has nearly broken free. The wire is stranded copper and very few strands remain.
justification: The incident involved damaged wiring and charring, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Capital Lighting Fixture  (model 4108-TS-RS) has been installed in our home for 7 years and 9 months.  Our home was custom built and our lights were installed by a licensed electrician.

Without warning, the part of the light fixture (all one solid piece with the frame) broke and fell from the chain.  No one was in the room at the time and there were no injuries.

This light fixture was hanging over our kitchen table (I estimate weight at at least 30 pounds).  Had there been people present at the table or in the room, there is a high chance that an injury would have occurred from fixture or shattering glass).
justification: The light fixture fell without warning, but no one was present, so there were no injuries.

incident_description: On September 26th, 2012 my 14 month old daughter passed away do to accidental strangulation on an inner cord of the horizontal window covering that was installed in her room. Her death took place in Red Deer, Alberta Canada. The corded window covering was manufactured by Nien Made in 2007 and shipped to Canada from the United States by Home Depot. The window coverings did not have inner cord stops installed on them allowing her to pull several inches of inner cord out. She reached the inner cord from her crib which was placed to the left of the window covering.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to accidental strangulation, which clearly falls under the highest severity level.

incident_description: The product sold at Target stores at the following link is a set of 7 mirrors. It was setup in my house as per instructions. The mount on the larger mirror separated from the mirror and it crashed to the floor. It was an adhesive failure. (Mirror -> Factory glued on mount).
justification: The mirror fell due to adhesive failure, but there was no mention of injury, only property damage.

incident_description: I am the original owner of a Dutailier Glider Rocking Chair.  The chair rocks and the back reclines.  On several occasions the chair has flipped forward onto users, including my elderly mother and my children.  When standing up from the chair, one must move to the front of the seat and when the user does, the entire chair flips forward.  The pieces that serve as the feet are not long enough to provide a stable platform.  The design of this chair is UNSAFE!  The company simply says that I must lock the chair to get out of it but a child IS NOT capable of locking/unlocking the chair when using it.  Nor are visitors and others aware that the chair will flip if not in the locked position.
justification: The chair has flipped forward multiple times, posing a risk to users including children and the elderly, but no injuries are mentioned.

incident_description: I went to pick up my Wexford Bathroom Scale that was purchased at a Walgreens a few months ago and it literally shattered in my hands. It didnt hit anything or drop or bump into anything. It just shattered in my hands.
justification: The scale shattered in the user's hands but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: Chairs purchase in April 2009 started failing the following season.  The base of the chairs breaks off and collapses.  Bought the chairs at Menards. Concord swivel rockers set of 4 was $340.00  thought they would be high quality, ended up being made in China junk.  Bases have 3 spokes of very thin tubes that snap off.  They are from the Woodard Furniture Company.  Tried contacting them for a refund they will not consider it apparently they only come with a 1 year warranty.  Have tried to e-mail several times they will not respond to them.
justification: The incident involves product failure causing chairs to collapse, but no injury or death is mentioned.

incident_description: I was in the family room, two stories high, where the chandelier was installed and hanging from the ceiling.  Suddenly, I heard a noise that came from the ceiling above my head; it was the chandelier falling off the ceiling. It came down and missed my head, when I saw that, I almost had a heart attack. Luckily, it did not fall off completely; it had stopped in the midst of air. The ring, which was connected to the rod and to the chain coming from the ceiling, had been broken. The rod luckily continued holding up the rest of the lights and did not come apart from the ring, which was dangling barely with the ground wire (the copper wire). The ring, which was connected to the ceiling chain and to the rod, had malfunctioned and was not strong enough to hold the weight of the chandelier.
justification: The chandelier fell but did not cause injury, and the incident was due to a malfunctioning component.

incident_description: Ring holding Chandelier to chain to hang from ceiling broke in half causing fixture to drop and hang by electrical cord only.
justification: The chandelier dropped but was caught by the electrical cord, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: Folding chair broke under normal use while on level ground and well in the 225 lbs. weight limit. Fall hazard. Plastic braces cracked metal bolt bent. Metal frame broke on end leaving sharp edge.
justification: The chair broke under normal use, creating a fall hazard and leaving sharp edges, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
Text of the e-mail message dated May 30, 2013:

Subject: Unsafe Child's Toy

Re: ToysRUs child's Resin Chair

Name: Minnie Classic Resin Chair
SKU 039897556048
Price: $9.99

This chair is not stable and has tendency to fall backwards with the child in it causing head trauma.

This happened to my granddaughter so we returned it. I am hoping they can be recalled before a child
is seriously injured. I believe the back legs are made to close to the back of the chair causing the chair
to be unstable.
justification: The incident describes a child experiencing head trauma due to the chair's instability, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that there were name plates attached the lower back of each chair and they were coming off from the chair. The consumer stated that the metal plates were coming off and the sharp prongs (1/2ÃÂ long) were facing up. The consumer stated that she almost stepped on the plate. The consumer stated that she could off stepped onto the metal prongs and they could have been inserted into her foot. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured. 
She stated that this poses a laceration hazard and should be investigated. 
The consumer stated that she contacted the retailer and they informed her that they would notify upper management.
justification: No injury occurred, but the incident involved sharp prongs that could have caused a laceration, posing a clear hazard.

incident_description:
Mattress w/massage feature and head/foot raising feature purchased around February 24th, 2013 but delivered March 4th, 2013

March 5th, 2013 was the first time the caller used the massage feature she believes that she accidently turned it to the highest setting.

Vibration should stop automatically after 30 minutes and the head area did just that but the foot area did not shut off, she couldn't shut it off with the controller so she got up and unplugged it to cut power.

She did not plug it back in but when she returned to bed after unplugging the power to the vibration she states that her body was still vibrating, she could not sleep because of the shaking in her body.

She went to a different bed in her house in the attempt to stop shaking, however it did not stop and it continued through the next day whether she was sitting or lying down or moving around.

She has been to her physician twice because she hasn't been able to sleep because of these tremors.  The doctor on the initial visit prescribed sleep medicine she is waiting for the referral from her physician to enable to be seen by neurologist.

 A contract signed at purchases says the bases are non-refundable. They were $3000 each. 

She did contact the store who advised her that the vibrating bases are not returnable. Total cost of mattress and bases were $9700
justification: The incident resulted in physical tremors requiring medical attention, indicating injury (severity 3). Such malfunctions are unlikely but not impossible (likelihood 2).

incident_description: at 4:45 am while I was sleeping downstairs, my black ikea glass desk top with flowers and butterflies spontaneously exploded.
justification: The glass desk exploded but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My wife and I bought the Martha Stewart Augusta patio set from Home Depot about a year ago.  2 weekends ago, we came home and found that the glass table top was completely shattered all over our deck.  We went to Home Depot to see if they could help and they told us to contact the manufacturer.  Unfortunately, we don't have the sales receipt, but the set is in excellent condition and now we can't even use it.  I took a photo of the broken mess the day it happened if that's needed.
justification: The glass table top shattered, causing property damage but no injuries.

incident_description: I purchased a Regalo Extra long Hideaway Bed rail for my daughter's bed on June 4, 2013. Within 10 days of correctly installing the bed rail, the protective netting zipper closure failed causing the netting to easily separate. The netting is slipped over a tubular open frame and it is the main part of the protection for the bed rail. Without it being secured with the zippered closure there is nothing to keep the netting from sliding down the bed rail frame and allowing an unprotected gap from forming where a child can easily fall from the bed.
justification: The bed rail's netting failure creates a potential fall hazard for a child, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
My daughter was electrocuted and received 2nd degree on her thumb and pincher finger as well her hair singed by touching a bobby pin to the metal cover of a pottery barn kids desk lamp.

The lamp was plugged in with no bulb.  It appears that the was in the metal cover and her touch the cover cause it to arc and blacked the inside of the lamp and welded the bobby pin together while burning and singed my daughter hair.
justification: The incident resulted in 2nd degree burns and singed hair, indicating injury (severity 3). Electrocution from a lamp is uncommon, hence likelihood is unlikely (2).

incident_description: We swaddled our baby using the Summer Infant Swaddle Me wrap and heard a choking sound coming from her room. Her arms had broke through the bottom of the arm wraps and she had lifted her arms over her head causing the upper fabric to become tightly wrapped around her neck. No obvious injury occurred as we quickly unwrapped her and discontinued use of the swaddle following this incident.
justification: The baby experienced a choking incident due to the swaddle wrap, but no injury occurred as the parents intervened quickly.

incident_description: My daughter (age 18 months) got her head stuck in the back of a chair from an Ikea table and chair set called "LATT."  She's fine except the livid red mark on her forehead.
justification: The child sustained a livid red mark on her forehead, indicating an injury, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description:
Manufactured By Master World CO. LTD Target DPCI #249-02-0066 Factory ID #F16815841
Dinning rooms set chairs fall hazard. Three out of four of the chairs in the set legs broke off under normal use. Only had chairs for two weeks. Wood braces attached to legs cracked. Wrong wood used for brace.
justification: Chairs broke under normal use, indicating a defect, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says when the furniture was delivered the odor immediately was present after the wrapping was removed.  

Some days are worst than others. She says that their is a zipper compartment underneath the seating area with pressed particle board with a horrendous smell.  She says the root of her mouth, lips and tongue are all burning.  

She says that it is more than an odor and more like fumes fill the room.  She has tried to properly ventilate the area.  She contacted the retailer yesterday and they are going to have a technician out on Tuesday June 25th.  

She is afraid that this product contains a large amount of formaldehyde.  She gets an overpowering scent as soon as she walks in the door.
justification: The consumer reports burning sensations in the mouth, lips, and tongue, indicating physical injury from exposure to fumes.

incident_description: The glass top of my Martha Stewart patio table suddenly shattered for no apparent reason. It is on a covered porch and was not abused or damaged in any way.
justification: The glass shattered unexpectedly but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I purchased an LED low-voltage light bulb that was being installed in a "niche" wall. On Sunday, June 23, 2013, while the light bulb was on, I noticed the bulb flicker, then smoke began to come out of the wall enclosure. The bulb is mounted in a recessed can-style lighting fixture. I immediately killed the power to the lights. Thinking at first it may have been a wire connection, I began inspecting the connections that were visible to me. The wiring was fine. When I removed the bulb, it was still hot, and a small portion of the bulb's base had begun to melt. The smoke had an acrid smell and was very distinct. Only the bulb had that same smell.
justification: The incident involved a flickering and smoking bulb without any reported injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Hi
We purchased a king sized dual control heated mattress pad from Macys Jan 2012.
The beginning of May 2013 I removed the heated mattress pad from the bed, unplugged and removed 1 of the dual controls.
The second unit was plugged in but not turned on.
On June 3 2013 the dual control caught fire at 4 AM. If we were not home it would have caused a house fire. The unit was on the floor. The fumes and smoke woke us up. The entire upstairs was saturated with the fumes for a week.
Please alert other consumers.
Thanks!
justification: The incident involved a fire and significant fumes, but no injury or death was reported, and the likelihood of such an event is unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: The glass top on our 48" patio table spontaneously broke into a million pieces all by itself.  It has never been hit by a hard object or been subjected to hot items.  The table has been sheltered in a 3 season carpeted porch and never used outside.  In fact, it has rarely been used.
justification: The glass top broke without any injury or external impact, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: We have the Kichler Aztec chandelier shown in the recall.  It hangs high in the stairwell of our house.  It fell at 4 in the morning about a month ago.  As it was up so high, it did not hit the ground.   The electrical wires pulled out if the ceiling and were holding it about 15 feet down from the ceiling.  The ground wire was broken.  Scary at 4 in the morning.  We went to Lowes with it, they would not take it back because we had bought it years before.  They sold us a piece to fix it and we had to hire an electrician to repair the light and wiring.  I didn't know the brand name of the fixture until seeing the recall.
justification: The chandelier fell but did not hit the ground or cause injury, though it was a scary incident requiring repairs.

incident_description: I purchased the Mainstays Woodacre 10-Piece Patio Dining Set from walmart. Brought it home and set it up. after 1 day of use i noticed broken welds on the reclining chairs (brought 2 chairs back to the store for replacement. One week later I noticed two more broken welds (on different Chairs) at the same location (recliner tab welds). Now 3 weeks later, all the chairs well suddenly fully recline without warning. incident_description:
On April 6th, 2013, my wife and I came home to find broken glass on our living room carpet.

The glass, which was the globe surrounding a compact florescent light bulb, had fallen eight feet striking an end table in the living room and shattering. The CF bulb itself remained attached to the recessed light fixture in our vaulted ceiling and to our amazement the bulb was still in working condition.

After removing the bulb from the light fixture we noticed that the coating inside the bulb had pulled away from the glass leaving clear class in places. The light bulb had reached heat levels sufficient to melt the glass and fuse sections of the bulb together.

Compact florescent light bulbs are not supposed to get hot, certainly not hot enough to melt glass. After our discovery we took the bulb back to Home Depot where we originally purchased the bulb and a number of other CF bulbs years ago. We were concerned about the amount of heat that was generated and of the possible fire hazard it presented. The person in the electrical department had never seen or heard of a CF melting before however he was not concerned and when asked did not recommend replacing the remaining bulbs in our house.

Although the Home Depot representative did not seem to be overly concerned about the melted bulb we later spoke to an electrician and electrical engineer who was also amazed by what he saw and was so concerned that he recommended we replace all of the bulbs of this type in our house.

Compact florescent lights are a relatively new technology and do not have the same track record as incandescent bulbs. With any new technology there is always a learning curve and improvements are continuous and numerous as time goes on. Not withstanding the relatively new technology surrounding CF bulbs I am concerned with safety.

My wife and I have decided to error on the side of caution and replace all of the remaining CF bulbs of this type in our house. The circumstances could have been much different if the bulb had caught fire in our ceiling and burned our house down instead of just coming apart and showering our floor with broken glass. 

Although we have taken the steps necessary to eliminate this threat in our home we are afraid that this problem may lurk in other homes across America and felt it necessary to bring it to your attention. The cost of replacing the bulbs is more than offset by the peace of mind we have knowing this threat has been eliminated.

In support of our story I have pictures of the bulb in question including all of the printed identifications and markings. I am also have retained the original bulbs including 4 that have not yet melted as well as the melted one.
justification: The incident involved broken glass from a light bulb but no injuries or fire occurred.
