In November of 2008 I purchased a [REDACTED] ceiling fan, unknown model number (photo attached), which included a three light light package. Within months of installing and using the fan in a breakfast nook, I experienced never before seen light bulb issues.  The glass bulbs in this fan would separate from the base and detach, leaving the glass bulb to hang.  The bulb would stop functioning. 

I soon learned that the only location I could purchase the correct sized bulb was at Home Depot.  Home Depot apparently had special arrangements with GE for the sale of this replacement bulb. The bulb is a 60 watt, "multi use A15 intermediate base" bulb, for use in ceiling fans.

As the glass part of the bulb was no longer attached to the base, I was forced on at least five different occasions over the past 4 years to unscrew the base from the socket using needle nose pliers, in order to replace the broken bulbs. 

On the night of April 7, 2013 I turned the lights on, and immediately began hearing a strange buzzing and humming noise.  The fan was not on.  One of the light bulbs began flickering, and soon started making an arching noise, as the bulb dropped away from the base.  The sound from the bulb was like nothing I had heard before.  Luckily I was in the adjacent room at the time, and was able to get to the light switch and shut off the power to the fan lights.  

The light bulb was smoking.  Pieces of black charcoal debris had fallen to the table below.  The glass part of the bulb had fallen to the table, leaving the base and filament attached to the socket.  This time I had a much more difficult time extracting the base from the socket, as it appeared to have melted to the socket.  

That particular socket will no longer function, as no bulbs work in it anymore.  

I plan on contacting [REDACTED] to see if I can get a replacement light package.  If not, I will just buy one to replace this light package.  If that isn't an option, I will replace the whole fan setup.    I do not want to have to use these GE bulbs any longer, as I feel they are a significant fire and electrocution hazard.   I'm thankful I was home at the time of the bulb failure, and that none of my children, or my wife, was near the kitchen at the time.

The bed frame is too long for the standard twin size mattress.  My daughter became entrapped lengthwise across the end of her bed in this gap, between the end of the mattress and the solid footboard, which compressed her chest and torso.  Her legs and right arm were also trapped, preventing her from extricating herself.  She couldn't breathe.  My older daughter heard the "thump" and gasp from her sister and checked on her.  She immediately ran to me and told me, and we ran to get her.  I could not pull her out by myself, as she was stuck.  My older daughter lifted the mattress up while I got my hands around my younger daughter and lifted her out.  If not for my older daughter, my child could have suffocated to death.  I'm extremely concerned for my child and any other child whose parents have purchased this bed.  It was purchased from Easy Life furniture store from their kids furniture section in Cerritos, Ca.  The name of the bed is "Holland House Chantilly Twin Post Headboard and Footboard Bed" and the bed frame is obviously made much too long for a normal twin mattress.  This bed is NOT an "extra long" twin bed, as confirmed by Easy Life themselves.  I appreciate any investigation and attention to this dangerous product you can give.
justification: The child was trapped and unable to breathe, requiring immediate intervention to prevent suffocation, indicating a high severity incident.

So I started looking for a baseball, golf ball, review the past weeks weather and realized that someone would have had to do that.  Once looking online to try to find a way to replace the glass, I began seeing all of the other complaints reporting the same incident.  Luckily no one was around to get injured but now I have a nice patio set without a table top.  Reading complaints of others it seems like either KMart (which is where I purchased it) or the Martha Stewart company appears to not be doing anything about compensating or at least replacing  the tables.  I too take very good care of my furniture and put it away for the winter, which can be seen by the condition of the chairs but now without a table its worthless.  Please stop this poor standard of manufacturing so other consumers don't waste their money and more important become injured by yet another exploding table.

incident_description:
Cost Plus World Market brand Aiden Coffee Table: this table is a two level coffee table.  It is made of a steel frame with mango wood surfaces and has steel casters on each leg. I was in the process of moving the coffee table towards me while sitting on the couch and one of the casters broke off and the table tilted towards me.  I had a hot dinner I just warmed up on the table and it slid off the table and onto the ground, nearly missing my legs.  

After reviewing the caster that broke off, it appeared that the base plate to which the caster was attached was welded to the leg with only 3 small tack welds.  This appears to be a poor design and a safety issue since the table will tilt when the weld breaks and will cause whatever is on the table to fall off and injure someone if there is something hot or sharp on the table or if someone has the feet or toes under the table at the time of weld failure.    Perhaps a more robust weld that is along the entire sides of the base plate where it meets the table leg would provide more strength and prevent part failure.
justification: The incident involved a caster breaking off, causing the table to tilt and spill hot food, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is 'possible' due to the design flaw described.

The legs are 14 1/2 inches inward from the corner with nothing else to stabilize the unit.
Retailer stated that they were entering this information to the computer and provided her with case# [REDACTED].

In April 8th, 2013 the caller was sitting at the end of the futon when for no apparent reason it flipped over causing the caller to hit her right shin bone.
She states that she cleaned her shin where there was a three inch cut then bandaged it.
She did not require medical attention.

She contacted the retailer/distributor again April 8th, 2013, informed them of her injury and requested that she be able to return the futon and obtain a refund.
She was advised that they were taking the information and would contact her shortly, they still have not contacted her again.

Last Year in our Master Bath we had one fall on its own and shatter the glass. We replaced the Glass and tried to make the tention springs hold up the covers better. Last week we had it fall again. I am concerned that this will fall on our Twin Daughters and cause serious injure.

incident_description: January 31, 2013, we purchased a dual electric reclining couch from Macy's, manufactured by Man Wah (USA) Inc of North Carolina.  On May 3 in the early evening, my wife and baby and I were sitting on the couch; my wife had reclined her side of the couch, and I pressed the button to recline my side.  It began to recline, then started buzzing, then a large fiery spark flew up on the outside of the armrest, barely missing us.  I jumped up and pulled the plug out of the wall.  The couch's motors were dead.  When Macy's delivery staff returned today to pick it up, the delivery man observed that the power cord had actually gotten tangled in the mechanism underneath the chair -- meaning that the power cord was unsecured, slack and loose under the chair.  I shudder to think of the fire or electrocution that could have been caused by literally cutting a live power cord while sitting on the couch that was doing the cutting.  It's a dangerous design flaw, and one that's easily corrected.  Someone in my family could have been killed, or my house could have burned down.

incident_description: Three to four years ago I purchased three 24" cherry saddle seat stools from Chilton Furniture in Scarborough, Maine.  These stools are located under my breakfast bar in my kitchen. In February, my 60 year old sister was visting and she sat on one of the stools. The stool failed catastrophically and she hit her head on my granite countertop as she fell to the floor. Luckily, she was not injured, but was shaken by the incident.  The saddle stools are designed to pivot. When I purchased them I was concerned about the strength of the saddle seats, but I was told they had only experienced a few saddles splitting when very heavy people sat in them.  Nothing like this catastrophic failure, with the saddle completely coming detached from the bottom of the stool was described to me as a possible failure.  I contacted the manufacturer, who admitted they have seen "a few" of these failures and they have changed their design to incorporate longer screws from the pivot plate to the bottom of the saddle seat.  I still have all of the components of the failed seat if you would like to investigate this issue.

incident_description:
I am writing to make you aware of a very scary flaw in a child safety product currently being sold by DreambabyÃÂ®. Based upon information on their web site, it appears that they operate under Tee-Zed Products, LLC throughout the USA. I purchased a gray corner bumper set from Zulily.com in January 2013. I believe the product number to be F810 or L810 and the product description is "Foam Corner Bumpers 4PCS". 

My infant daughter is now at an age old enough to begin crawling and exploring. In preparation for this, I installed the corner bumpers on the ends of our coffee table. The bumpers are installed simply by pulling off the cover to double-sided tape on the underside of the bumper, then affixing the bumper and exposed tape to the corners of the table. The bumpers have not been affixed to our table for more than a couple of weeks and my daughter has now learned to pull herself on the table to learn how to stand. 

However, a very concerning problem arose this past weekend. As my daughter pulled herself up, and as a typical infant would do, she put her mouth up to one of the corner bumpers. With just two small bottom teeth she was able to rip a large chunk of foam material off of the bumper. Please keep in mind that this in an infant who has not yet mastered the art of ripping and chewing with her mouth. I was shocked by how easily such a huge chuck of foam was able to be ripped off the bumper with so little effort. 

Fortunately I was sitting next to her and saw what happened just in time. I dislodged the chunk from her mouth, but am frightened to think of the possibilities of what might have happened, or what could happen to another family if they are not aware of these bumpers. The piece of foam could have easily gotten stuck in her wind pipe. Foam material is capable of expanding when exposed to moisture. This is a very frightening thought, had it gotten stuck in her throat or even if it had made its way to her stomach. This incident had the potential for very severe health implications. 

Upon further inspection, I believe these bumpers to be of an extremely cheap quality and a poorly manufactured product. The entire bumper ripped in half with ease and crumbled to the touch. That is unacceptable. My home is not a very busy household and my coffee table is not subject to constant abuse, and there were no extraneous factors to cause these bumpers to dry out and decay as quickly as they did. This product simply does not meet the standard that it should. 

Needless to say, these bumpers are no longer being used on our coffee table. I would rather run the risk of not having bumpers than continuing to use these poorly configured and extremely brittle foam bumpers. The intent of these bumpers is to minimize the risks an infant my encounter in the average household. In my view, my home is safer without them. 

I urge you to contact the manufacture and distributors of this product and advise of this situation, or provide a warning to other parents thinking of using this product. I would hate for another family to experience a similar malfunction and not have as fortunate of an outcome. I also hope that you can reach out to customers who purchased this product and express to them the danger that this poorly made product poses. 

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED] (Parent)

(I have pictures, however your web site is freezing on me every time I attempt to upload them)
justification: The infant was able to rip off a large chunk of foam, which could have caused choking, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On November 9th, 2012 I bought a plug-in halogen linear, linkable light fixture from the
Home Depot.

This fixture is a trademark of the General Electric Company and is used under a license to
Jasco Products Company LLC. See attached photos for more details, including the store receipt.

On December 27th, 2012 this light fixture caused a house fire where I rent. The fire department concluded that the fire was caused by the light fixture.

The fixture is sold with hardware included to mount it on a wall or under-cabinet location. I
mounted the fixture on a wall in the bathroom to use as a vanity light.

The design of the fixture (see attached photos) is inherently flawed. After taking a closer look
at the fixture I realized how much of a hazard it is.

As I'm sure you know, halogen bulbs get extremely hot, much hotter than incandescent
or fluorescent bulbs. In this fixture the bulb is located about 1/4" from a cheap, plastic
casing. When the fixture is on for any period of time the plastic overheats.

If any object gets near the fixture and there isn't enough air circulating around the casing the
plastic begins to melt, starting a fire. This is exactly what happened in my bathroom, as
evident by the circular hole burnt into my door. The fire was not caused by faulty wiring in
the house as evident from the lack of damage to the outlet that the fixture was plugged into.

Luckily someone walking through the neighborhood called the fire department in time to save
the house. This fire could have started our entire complex of houses on fire, putting
numerous people (and pets) at risk. We are all extremely lucky that no one was injured or
killed in this fire.

I signed the lease for this rental on November 1st, 2012, less than two months before the fire.
I had just moved to Venice from New York so there was a lapse in my renter's insurance.

As a result, I had to pay out-of-pocket for a hotel while the house was inhabitable. In
addition, I had to pay for food while I was displaced and replacement food, toiletries, clothes
and other belongings damaged by the fire and the smoke. I also paid for extra cleaning
products, extra clothes washing and I spent days cleaning once the house was semi-habitable.

This fire also caused disruptions in my work. I am a videographer and video editor and I
spend a lot of time working from home. I had to literally move my large desktop computer to
a hotel in order to try to keep up with work.

This fire has also affected my sense of safety and well-being. I was across the street when the
fire occurred and ran home as the fire fighters were walking out of the house with soot on
their faces. This fire was bad enough that it put their lives at risk too.

I have had trouble sleeping and I am now constantly assessing the house for fire hazards. All
in all, this fire has cost me thousands of dollars in out-of-pocket expenses, and life and work
disruptions.

I am writing Home Depot, General Electric and Jasco Products in order to receive
compensation for my losses, and I am copying various agencies and businesses in order to
increase awareness of this hazardous product.

Thank you all for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
justification: The incident caused a house fire but no injuries or deaths were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible (3) given the described design flaw and overheating issue.

incident_description:
Last week I made a purchase from Walmart on Vine Street in Eastlake, OH.  A simple floor lamp with a reading light.  The floor lamp is 3-way compatible for a max of 150w, the reading lamp is a 1-way with a max of 60w.  I purchased the different bulbs, the floor lamp bulb was a brand name 3-way, [REDACTED] bulb with a max of 150w.  The reading lamp was a [REDACTED] basic type A 60w bulb.  I have used this lamp on and off since I purchased it and have left the reading lamp on for hours at a time with no problem.  Tonight I had both portions of the lamp on, 3-way turned to highest setting, and the reading lamp on.  This lamp is located next to my night stand roughly 2 feet away from my bed.  While just playing on my computer the lamp made a loud pop as it showered me in hot glass.  The glass pieces ranged from sizes as big as quarters to tiny shards and slivers.  There were 2 pieces that melted into my bedspread after noticing them less than 60 seconds after the loud pop.  There was glass all over my pillow, blankets, my hair, my legs and shorts, my floor, and surrounding clothes.  I still have the box for the lamp, we have the broken pieces of lightbulb showing that I did have an accurate bulb in there, pictures of the glass, and pictures of most of the damage.  The only thing I do not have is the receipt from the purchase.

The damages done were melted glass shards into a comforter I received as a Christmas present this last Christmas, shards of glass embedded into my sheets and pillow cases, and (at the time) small red marks all over my lap from where the glass had originally landed.  The glass in the comforter will not come out, as it is melted, and the sheets and pillow cases cannot be guaranteed shard-free due to the nature of how small some pieces were.

The name of the lamp and brand is: Mainstays Floor Lamp with Reading Light--- 3-Way Switch, Silver Finish, UPC: 7 98919 03789 6    - and the item number is HW-F1219SLV.  It was Made in China, but distributed by Wal-Mart-Stores, Inc out of Bentonville, AR 72716.   Intertek # 3160822. 

I purchased the lamp and correct light bulbs March 11th, 2013 around 8:45pm, and the incident happened March 18th, 2013 around 12:15am.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (red marks from hot glass) and property damage, but no severe harm or death. The likelihood is unlikely as it involves a specific product failure under certain conditions.

incident_description:
Dear Sirs,
[REDACTED], Public Information Assistant, Office of the Attorney General of Texas, suggested
I contact your office concerning a matter that I have been trying to resolve since April of this year
regarding a heating pad manufactured by the Sunbeam Corporation.
In April I used their heating pad to relieve an ache in my neck. Though there was some discomfort
it was not until the next morning that the pain began to worsen from a burn the size of a nickel
was burned into my back. After reading the description of varying degrees of burns on WebMD,
my injury closely described of a third degree burn.
After mailing a letter to Sunbeam I received a phone call from [REDACTED], Senior Consumer Care
Specialist with Jarden Consumer Solutions. She asked several questions regarding the incident
and explained that I would be mailed a replacement heating pad as well as instructions on
completing an accident form. At this time I requested written evaluation concerning the defective
product and what steps Sunbeam would take to ensure serious burns from happening to others.
[REDACTED] Agreed, saying this would not be a problem once the product failure was determined
and the department released the information.
On April 26th, I received a letter from Jarden Consumer Solutions stating the procedures for filing
a claim. I immediately followed through with the requested information, even sending two
pictures of my injury rather than the request for one. After what I believed to be a reasonable
amount of time for the company to contact and address my concerns, but was not contacted. On
June 26th, I again wrote a letter to [REDACTED], CEO of consumer Affairs with a copy also sent to
[REDACTED], with Consumer Affairs, requesting information concerning my claim. On July 11,
a message was left on my answering machine from [REDACTED]., stating they had received another
letter from me and would I return her call, which I did at 2:55p.m. that same day. I had to leave a
message on her voice mailbox, which went unreturned. With no other correspondence, on July
20th I called [REDACTED] Again and asked what information she had received from the department
that was investigating the heating pad I had sent. She state she had not contacted that department
yet, but would ind out and call me. On August 11th, at 8:32 a.m., I called [REDACTED]., concerning the
progress of my claim. A representative named, [REDACTED], answered the number and told me that there
was no "claims department" that I could speak with and that, "their lawyers only speak with other
lawyers." I asked who else I could contact concerning this matter and in so many words said that I
should just stop calling.
I contacted a lawyer who told me that attorneys rarely take cases involving Sunbeam because they
keep them tied up for great lengths of time and have many cases already on the court docket. That
the time and expense of dealing with Sunbeam most lawyers felt it was not worth pursuing. He
also suggested that I not try small claims court as Sunbeam could and would most likely bankrupt
me in legal requests, such as paying for specialist to be called to testifY.
It is difficult for me to believe that large companies can cause severe injury and scars to
consumers and because of their unlimited financial means can disregard any responsibilities for
their products. It is my hope that your commission will investigate Sunbeam and Jarden
corporations and their practices when consumers are injured by their products.
Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a third-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such severe burns from heating pads are not common.

incident_description:
I purchased four Hudson Valley Lighting Model 4721 wall sconces from build.com on 24 May 2012.  These fixtures consist of a wall plate, two adjustable arms, and a lamp at the end.  They were unpacked and installed by a licensed electrician.  When the electrician turned them on for the first time, one of them caused an attached dimmer switch to spark and smolder. 

The joints between the arms of the malfunctioning fixture were disassembled by removing the knob normally used to adjust the angle of those joints.  The wiring at the middle joint in the fixture was covered in a cloth wrapping which was worn through, and the insulation on the wiring was also compromised, allowing the wiring to short circuit inside the fixture.

The other lamps were disassembled and showed the same wiring damage.  There is a threaded metal post in the center of the joint over which the wires run and onto the end of which the adjustment knob screws on when the fixture is fully assembled.  The threads on this post are sawing through the cloth wrap on the wire and through the wire insulation as the fixture is adjusted and the wires rub against those threads.  Counting the replacement lamp, we examined five fixtures and found that all were consistently manufactured in this way.

This is a design flaw that leads to a shock and fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a sparking and smoldering dimmer switch due to a design flaw, posing a shock and fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
This morning I awoke to my glass kitchen table top exploding. There were several good-sized shards and many
marble-sized shards that flew all over the kitchen, foyer, under doors, etc. The table had not been used for 17
hours, nothing was on it for that period of time, nothing fell on it, the kitchen is in the middle of my condo, so
sunlight was not the cause and there was not temperature change from either the gas heating system or gas
fireplace. The temperature of the heating system has remained at 68 since it was turned on in early Fall, and the
fireplace had not been on in almost a week.
The table was bought at Raymour & Flanagan in Orange, CT four years ago. I contacted them, and they were
completely disinterested in why this happened. Obviously I have no interest in purchasing another top from
them, but would like to know why this happened. I have learned from the Internet that this has happened to
others, but usually outdoor glass tops.
As far as I know, Raymour & Flanigan continues to sell this table. The explosion happened at 8:15 am, and
luckily I was still in bed. I normally am sitting at that table between 8:30 and 9:00 am and certainly would have
suffered severe lacerations. An even more frightening scenario is the possibility of a child sitting at the table for
breakfast.
I would like to see this product immediately removed from any store selling it. In addition, do I have any
recourse against Raymour and Flanigan for compensation for the top? I found an article on
www.7perth.com.au/view/today-tonight-articles/exploding-tables/ tha.t said that even if the warranty has
expired, there is an implied warranty for a reasonable time period.
I purchased the table in November 2008. My customer number was [REDACTED], and the SKU number for the
top was 700000196. The vendor was listed as RF09, and another identifying number for the table was ODDT-
019T
My name is [REDACTED]. I spoke to [REDACTED] in the "customer service" department of Raymour & Flanigan. The store manager never seemed to be available.
justification: The incident involved a glass table exploding, which could have caused severe lacerations but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
As with other identical stories already summarized on the Consumer Product Safety Commission web page, we purchased a top of the line Tempurpedic Rhapsody Memory Foam King Mattress (approx $3999.00 - tax) and adjustable bases ($2800.00 + tax) plus 69.99 delivery from Mattress Firm.  The mattress felt great at the showroom store (very supportive - no odor), but when the mattress was delivered and removed from the plastic bag, my family's nightmare began.  A very strong chemical odor started filling our bedroom.  Since the store instructed us to expect such an odor (referred to as off gassing and alleged to be non-toxic) and that it would dissipate within 2-3 days, my family stuck it out and lived with the chemical odor for several days.  As instructed by the store, we also walked on the bed daily to progress the off gassing.  During this time, my family all slept in alternative locations (son's room, guest room, gameroom couch) while maintaining an ozone air purification machine, bowls of vinegar, and a window fan in the bedroom as we eventually wanted to enjoy the mattress feel/support we had experienced at the store.  

Fast forward several days, the smell never disappeared (it continued to get worse and spread across the entire house).  My spouse and two young sons as well as myself started having difficulty breathing (we all tasted chemicals on our tongue and could only get relief by remaining outside the home).  After 5 days (having never being able to even tryout the new bed) we paid another $69.99 to have the mattress picked-up and returned to Mattress Firm (thank goodness they had a 100 night money back guarantee).  Once the mattress was removed, we spread baking soda (product which should absorb odors and then be easily vacuumed up) throughout the entire bedroom (carpet, furniture, support bases which couldn't be returned) in an attempt to remove the chemical odor.  However, we were not successful at removing the chemical odor.  

Since the strong chemical odor remained throughout the entire house (now appearing to be a longer term problem and raising questions without answers), I (having a PhD in Chemistry) started researching the off gas odor and discovered the chemicals used to manufacture and fire retard these polyurethane memory foam mattresses (secret formulations due to US patents, etc) are highly reactive, toxic isocyanates, diols, and other reactive chemical compounds, all of which per MSDSs have very low exposure tolerances and create respiratory issues and skin contact problems at very low concentrations.  From what I could locate on the web, I saw no need to contact Tempurpedic as their only response (as expected due to monetary position and size of business) was to provide a generic statement noting they comply with all rules and regs.  I was at this point extremely "[REDACTED]" to say the least since I now had no apparent recourse (just hoping family's health had not been negatively affected due to the short duration).  

Fast forward another week (mattress removed from home for approx. 1 week), the chemical odor still remains throughout our entire home (on the walls, clothing, furniture, etc).  We have had our carpets/curtain/rugs/cloth furniture steam cleaned (another $320.00 out of pocket cost), continue to run the ozone air purification machine, run window fans 24/7, and have changed all HVAC filters in further attempts to remove the chemical odor.  Unfortunately, the chemical odor appears very resistant to removal and continues to remain along with the respiratory health concerns and chemical taste on our tongues.  In addition, we now have purchased a new fully organic/natural mattress and are awaiting its arrival, but are afraid to bring the new mattress into the home concerned that it could pose the same issue and/or absorb the chemical odor prolonging our chemical exposure. 


Please my family asks that the US government or appropriate US agency progress some type of warning or legislation to address this very apparent toxic chemical poisoning problem before it negatively affect any additional tax paying families.
justification: The incident caused respiratory issues and chemical taste, indicating injury, but no death was reported.

incident_description:
The candle is a Voluspa Scented candle and is stored in a tin. I purchased the candle from an Anthropologie retail store. 

I left the candle unattended for about 15 minutes, but was nearby in the next room (about 15 feet away). I noticed the air getting misty and small black flakes in the air, and i began looking around my apartment. I saw a bright light coming from my room, and saw that the entire tin (approximately 4-5" in diameter) had gone up in flames, like a mini-bonfire. 

The flames were so large that i didn't want to snuff the candle out, so i grabbed a cup and sprinkled a small amount of water on the flames. Doing that created a fireball much bigger than the original flames for 1-2 seconds, maybe a foot in diameter, then the fire went out.

Despite immediately doing everything i could to air out my home (a 1 bedroom condo), there was some moderate damage. The candle did major damage to the dresser top it was placed on, destroyed the lampshade on the table, and left extensive smoke damage on the nearby walls. Ash from the small fire got on every surface in my unit, and went through my air ducts to stain laundry in the dryer.

Though I know candles should never be left unattended, I find it ridiculous that this candle can create such a massive flame when only left alone for a very short period of time. Also, a quick google search indicates that this has happened to others.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as similar incidents have been reported by others.

incident_description:
Concern is over a T5 fluorescent light fixture distributed by Good Earth Lighting, Inc., 5260  Capitol Drive, Wheeling, Illinois, 60090.  It has the UPC 5528400408, and is sold by Menards.  It is 110 Volts and designed for under-cabinet use.  It is often used under kitchen cabinets and thus may be near a sink, an electrical ground.  Internally, the fixture has ground (green) wires so the fixtures may be chained by a 3 wire cord.  However, the wall plug for the fixture is only a 2 prong plug so the green wires in the fixture are useless as a safety ground.  

If, instead of being plugged into a wall socket, the fixture is hard wired, the body of the fixture will be properly grounded by the removable part of the fixture that contains the electrical parts is not grounded to the body of the fixture.

If a short circuit  develops in this fixture, an unreasonable risk of electrocution is presented, particularly for someone in a kitchen using the under-cabinet fixture near a sink.
justification: The fixture presents a risk of electrocution, which could lead to death, especially in a kitchen near a sink.

incident_description:
The consumer purchased a 2 inch high, gel foam mattress accessory at the beginning of the year. Consumer stated that within 6 weeks of using the gel foam accessory she started to experience an allergic reaction.  There was a chemical-like odor that emitted from the pad when it was first purchased, but it died down after the consumer allowed it to air out.  Directions said air out for 2 days, they aired out 5 days because odor was so strong.

Consumer started having a sore throat and her eyes were blood red. Consumer saw her Doctor in June, he informed her that it was just allergies. Consumer changed bedding, soaps, shampoos, pillows and her symptoms still worsen. Consumer then tried sleeping on the couch and the symptoms started to get better. we also purchased sleep number which also has flame retardant.

Consumer started to sleep on the accessory and the symptoms began to flare again. So the consumer concluded that while away from the product the symptoms decreased. 

Consumer saw regular doctor on Aug. 21, 2012.  Consumer decided to see a specialist 8/29, 2012, 9/12/2012 and 10/17/2012, where she was given medications to treat the problems.

Consumer stated gel foam is only used on her side of the bed, and her husband is not having same issues. 

Consumer still has product and has not contacted manufacturer as of yet on back of sheet

UPDATE: We contacted Sleep Number and they graciously said we could return bed, but that all beds now (I believe as of 2007) are treated with flame retardant. So we figured a new bed would also cause the same problems.  Besides we liked the bed except for making me sick.  Soft on my side, hard on my husband's side.  We wouldn't be able to have that feature on another bed.  They said we couldn't buy a bed without the flame retardant, it would be against the law.  So, we wrapped all the foam components of the bed in plastic also wrapped all the gel foam mattress pad in plastic and then sealed everything into a plastic mattress cover.  I'm happy to say, my eyes have 99% cleared up and am expecting the other 1% shortly.  The bed though is hotter now, with all the plastic so I put a quilt on the top of plastic mattress pad, then a 1" cotton mattress pad and then fitted bottom sheet. This seems to work.  Eyes clear, throat doesn't hurt and sleeping through the night.
justification: The consumer experienced allergic reactions including sore throat and blood-red eyes, requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
On 1/23/13 we lit a 24 hour memorial candle called a "Yahrzeit Memorial Candle" which was manufactured by a company called "Yehuda".  The other package labeling said "Distributed by HKS Marketing Ltd, Bayonne, NJ 07002 USA, Product of Israel"

The product is a small glass jar filled with paraffin.  The wick in the center is attached to a small metal button located near the center (but not anchored there).  We have burnt many such candles in the past without incident, but we found upon wakening (it is designed to burn 24 hours) that the candle was out and the metal button and wick had slipped to the side of the jar which was cracked and a pool of now solidified paraffin was outside the jar.  Fortunately,we burn these in a shallow pan upon a glass cooktop surface.  But if these precautions were not taken it is reasonable to expect that force of the glass shattering while the candle was buring might lead to a house fire.
justification: The candle malfunctioned but no injury or fire occurred due to precautions taken.

incident_description: I bought my 9 1/2 year daughter the Bright Light Pillow from the retailer Justice on 1/11/2013.  It is a heart shaped pillow with built-in led lights that when turned on, automatically turn off after 15 minutes.  The battery pack is heavy and even though it is placed deep within the pillow (access the battery pack from a side zipper that itself is not well covered), if you are playing around and hit someone with this pillow, the battery pack can definitely hurt you.   There is no warning about this.  Also, my daughter slept with the pillow the first night and woke up with a red raised skin eruption that ran lateral to the right side of her face, close to her ear.  No blistering.  I took pictures of it.  She had no complaints of pain but it was noticeable immediately because of the redness and the texture was raised.  She did not sleep with any other stuffed animals and had slept just fine in her bed without any facial discolorations or eruptions until she slept with the Bright Lights pillow.  On 1/17/2013 the reddened area has changed a brown pigmentation but is still raised when touching it.
justification: The incident resulted in a skin injury (red raised eruption) from sleeping with the pillow, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described scenario and lack of warnings.

incident_description:
Was watching TV in my living room when I heard what sounded like food frying. I realized the soft flicker that had been coming from my bathroom was too bright. When I entered I saw that the candle  burning in there had turned into a torch. The wax and everything was on fire and boiling over.  I immediately cupped water in my hands from the sink and threw it onto the fire, but it reacted like a grease fire and just spit flames and wax higher. My boyfriend attempted to smother it with a towel but it was too hot and was just burning through that as well. Finally I got the fire extinguisher and put it out.  By that time wax had spattered all over the walls and down the shelf it was on. The glass of the candle had exploded. Luckily nothing but bathroom products and the shelf unit were damaged but it could have been much worse.  It took about 3 hours to clear the house out of the smoke/burning smell with all the windows open. 

The candle had been burning for about an hour.  I have no idea why the WAX would have been burning as well but when it was done and over with it looked like the wax was more oil like. I saved the bottom.

incident_description: I recently purchased the Edsal Steel Commercial Shelving Unit Model # UR-245 from my local Home Depot for the Film Studio I run in NJ.  Shortly after assembling the 4 units I bought, I began to stock the shelves which is when I sliced my hand open on one of the support poles.  Thinking it was a fluke and my clumsiness, I and my team continued to stock the shelves after I was all bandaged up.  Not more than five minutes later one of my workers sliced his hands too.  This is when I decided to inspect the unit further.  It turns out that the metal they used for the bars of the shelves and support rods are flat, very sharp and frame each shelf opening.  If you're placing a box in there that comes close to any of the exposed metal framing the shelf opening you must carefully place the box in without your hands touching the metal, like a giant game of [REDACTED].  Instead of breaking the shelves down, taking off the tons of lights we had loaded them up with, and going through the hassle of trying to get our money back from Home Depot, we instead covered each dangerous point (almost the entire unit) with [REDACTED] tape to protect us from anymore injuries and any potential lawsuits.  I felt it was my responsibility to warn potential future buyers of this item's dangers and thus composed a review on Home Depot's website, but much to my chagrin, Home Depot rejected the review.  Please, take action before someone else gets hurt.
justification: The incident describes two injuries caused by sharp metal edges on the shelving unit, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) as the issue is inherent in the product design and affects multiple users.

incident_description:
Email to Regalo Company summarizing incident:

I purchased the Double Hide-Away Bed Rails from Babies-R-Us (Wilkes-Barre, PA) back in August or September of 2011, when we were transitioning my then-almost-2-year-old to a bed.  They have worked pretty well.  The only times I use the hide-away feature is when I change the sheets on the bed - every two weeks or so - so this frequency should not be enough to cause a fatigue failure in the product after less than a year and a half of use.  When I was unlatching one of the rails to slide it under the mattress last week, the metal joint between the rail and the wheel that slides in the piece that goes under the mattress failed - totally broke, leaving a large gap between the mattress and rail as well as two very sharp metal "stubs".  I was very glad the failure occurred when I was adjusting the railing rather than when my son was getting in or out of bed, because this could have caused him to fall, severely lacerate himself, or get caught between the mattess and railing.  
 
I called your customer service number as instructed on the registration card, and the man was absolutely no help.  He repeated that your company offers a 90-day warranty and no more.  He offered parts for purchase.  That was it.  I asked for the name of a supervisor, and he said he could give no contact person for this issue.  
 
I am extremely angered and disappointed by this response from a company whose motto is "For the most important people in the world."  I have notified the store manager where I made the purchase, and she planned to take this issue to her managers.  Depending on the response I receive from Regalo, I am prepared to contact Babies-R-Us on a corporate level to notify them of the hazardous product they are selling and the lack of concern from the manufacturer.  In my opinion, Regalo should replace my product with no questions asked and send me a return label so I can send back the faulty product so you can research the failure and determine if a recall is warranted.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that could have caused injury but did not result in any actual harm.

I slept on this for 3 nights and it has already caused me enough damage that I had to go see a doctor next morning due to acute inflammation of my lungs. PVC material in this bed is so cheap that it releases highly toxic fumes (you can feel that strong new plastic smell). These toxic fumes can damage your respiratory system, cause hormonal imbalance as well as nervous and reproductive disorders. Just Google PVC fumes and you will find many articles describing it.

All 3 mornings when I woke up, my throat was burning and was full of thick mucus/phlegm. I had to clear out my throat and the mucus that I would expel was thick, dark yellowish/brownish. I didn't doubt the bed on the first morning but started suspecting it the second morning. Third morning, I was in a terrible shape and the moment I would enter the bedroom, my throat would start irritating and burning. That night, I could feel my chest fully congested and I had an extremely painful night. I saw the doctor next morning and she has put me on 7 day rigorous treatment to clear out my lungs. Note that I am a non-smoker and am not exposed to any dust or other pollutants whatsoever.

I packed this back in the box but the air inside my home still smells of the cheap plastic. These fumes can cause long term damage to young children.
justification: The incident caused acute inflammation of the lungs requiring medical treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the immediate and severe reaction to the toxic fumes.

incident_description:
My client Mr. [REDACTED] is a yacht captain and yacht broker. On the date of the incident he stopped by the 85 foot yacht belonging to  his friend and client Mr.[REDACTED]. They  were planning future trips aboard the boat. Mr.[REDACTED] had brought several folding deck chairs earlier that morning at West Marine  located at 2401 S. Andrews Ave., Ft. Lauderdale, FL.  The chairs are  wholesaled distributed throughout the United States by a Waterbrands LLC subsidiary, Seateak . The chair is identified as their "Brigantine" model teak folding deck chair.  The chairs have no instructions or warnings of any kind anywhere on them.  

Mr. [REDACTED] invited Mr.[REDACTED] to sit down in one of the chairs that were placed around a table on the aft deck of the boat. As soon as Mr.[REDACTED] sat down the support for the back of the chair broke and the chair began to collapse. The chair has no arm rests so Mr.[REDACTED] attempted to stand up before the chair collapsed completely by using his hands to push himself up from the seat of the chair. His left index finger was caught is a scissoring type of motion created by the legs of the chair as they collapsed. This traumatically amputated a large  portion of the finger.

Further inspection of both the broken chair and the undamaged chairs revealed the following: There is a  small round  piece of brass, 1/2 inch long and 1/4 inch diameter that is attached to the bottom center of the back of the seat. When you unfold the chair this brass piece rests on a horizontal cross piece on the back of the chair and the chair appears ready for use. It is not. The manufacturer intends the chair user to maneuver the brass cylinder behind, around and under the horizontal piece of wood that is attached to the back of the chair. The seat bottom is then "hooked" onto the chair back.This stabilizes the back of the chair and allows the force exerted on the chair back by the chair user  to be distributed  to and supported by the front and back legs of the chair as well as to a second horizontal support piece attached to the lower portion of the legs of the chair . This second support is 1inch by 3/4 inch in width. If the 1/2 inch brass cylinder is not hooked around this horizontal support on the back of the chair but rather is simply placed on the top of the cross piece it is intended to be hooked onto   the entire weight exerted onto the back of the chair by it's  occupant is supported only by  the lower 1 inch by 3/4 inch cross piece. This is a grossly inadequate weight bearing capacity. This is what failed initially, causing the chair to collapse.

There is no way for the chair's users to know what the purpose of the brass knob is. The chair appears ready for use as soon as it is   unfolded, without the seat of the chair  being secured by  the brass cylinder being hooked behind the horizontal piece of wood  There is no instruction or warning on how to properly secure the chair for use or the consequences of failing to do so. The brass "hook" is located on the bottom of the seat and is obscured from view without  very close inspection. Even with close inspection its purpose is not apparent without instruction and warning. For these reason the design of this chair is extremely dangerous and the likelihood of collapse and injury very high.
justification: The incident resulted in a traumatic amputation of a finger, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The design flaw and lack of warnings make the likelihood of such incidents high (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description: While replacing a burned-out light bulb, I discovered that the all three of the light sockets on the ceiling fan in my den/home office had cracked.  The socket material had dried out and cracked in several places, and had begun to crumble.  The ceiling fan was purchased in May 2010, and I have never used light bulbs above the recommended  60 Watt limit.  The fan, which is Hunter Fan's model number 28667, uses the small base light bulbs, which I believe are referred to as "B10" bulbs or "candelabra-base"  bulbs.  Over the course of the two and a half years that the fan has been in use, I have had to replace quite a few bulbs.  In removing the old bulbs, I would say that almost half of the bulbs have broken (the glass portion has separated from the metal base).  I had attributed this to poor quality of the bulbs, and their small diameter at the base of the bulb.  Now I suspect that the metal part of the sockets may have become warped or were not correctly formed.  For whatever reason, many of the bulbs have broken off in the socket.  I have noticed small bits of material falling from the light sockets to my desk below the fan when removing the bulbs.  Not until yesterday did I realize that some of the material was actually part of the light socket itself, not just pieces of the burned-out light bulbs.
justification: The incident involves damaged light sockets and frequent bulb breakage, but no injury or death has occurred.

incident_description:
Summary: No injury.  Manufacturing error could lead to serious injury.  Two Twin beds that can be mounted as a bunk bed.  Construction error makes it likely that the upper bunk is not secured.

Purchasing Details:
   We purchased a bunk bed from American Furniture Warehouse Firestone store [REDACTED]  on Sunday Nov 11th, 2012.  We picked up the bunk bed on Wednesday Nov 14th, 2012 and assembled it that evening.

Design Details:
   The bunk bed design enables the beds to be used as individual beds, or in a bunk configuration.  To secure the upper bunk, the instructions describe placing a 3 and 9/16" long x 17/32" wide hollow metal pin in a hole pre-drilled at the factory in each corner post of the lower bed and upper beds.  The upper bed is then placed on to the metal pin, securing it against lateral movement and ensuring that some vertical motion will keep the upper bunk on the pin.
   As we prepared to stack the beds, it became readily apparent that the pre-drilled holes did not fit the metal pins.  The pre-dilled holes were a touch over 2 and 1/2" deep and 3/8" wide.
   The width is precisely what is needed for 1" by 3/8" wooden dowels provided with the bed set for other joints.  The 1" dowel can go all the way down into the pre-drilled hole.

Problem with the design:
   As the metal pins do not fit in the pre-drilled holes, most installers would likely place a wooden dowel in to each hole of the lower bunk, and then mount the upper bunk.  However, this course of action would most likely push the wooden dowel in to the lower bunk, leaving the upper bunk susceptible to horizontal shear forces and vertical motion.  In best scenario, only a 1/2" length of the wooden dowel is securing the bunk against vertical motion.  Further, if there is vertical motion, this could move the dowel lower, resulting in no stabilization for horizontal motion.  

Likely outcome:
   If the bunk is not secured properly, the upper bunk could fall off causing serious injury.

Notice:
   We notified American Furtniture Warehouse on Nov 15th.  They offered to send a technician on Nov 20th.  We decided to manufacture our own pins.  I purchased a 4 foot by 3/8" diameter steel dowel, and I cut this in to 5" long segments.  These fit perfectly.  Our bunk bed is now secured.  I am concerned about other units of this product in the warehouse or installed recently as these were not likely secured properly.
justification: The incident describes a manufacturing error that could lead to serious injury, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood of the upper bunk falling is high if not properly secured.
