incident_description: I had a person stop by our office with a table lamp that had caught fire. this lamp was on his sons night stand in his bedroom. The father was able to unplug the lamp and remove from the home before there was any damage done to the home. This lamp has a CFL light bulb in it made by TCP. This bulb does have a scorch mark on the base.
justification: The lamp caught fire but was promptly unplugged without injury or property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer says that he sat on the chair and he fell off and hit the concrete.  The consumer says that the four welds snapped.  He says the chairs are aluminum and not very sturdy.  

He purchased the unit at a yard sale.  The consumer says that he contacted the manufacturer and they said that there are no issues with the chair and that they have parts for the unit.  

The consumer says the unit should be recalled.  The consumer says he needed medical attention.  He went to the emergency room.  He scraped his elbow.  They took X-Rays and sent him home saying nothing was wrong.  He says he has a bad back and this incident made it worse.  His Dr. did give him a shot in his lower back. 

The consumer weighs 230 lbs.
justification: The consumer required medical attention, including an ER visit and treatment for a back injury, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) given the chair's reported structural failure under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
I want to report a safety incident that happened on November 18, 2012 while my 22 month old was wearing the HALO SleepSack Micro-Fleece Wearable Blanket Size Extra Large. I woke up at 4am because for some reason I felt the need to check on my sleeping toddler. I found him asleep in his crib and tangled in his sleepsack. He had managed to unzip his sleepsack and was lying face down with his head tightly stuck inside the bottom of the sack that is normally over his feet and the rest of his body tangled in the sack opening. I was alarmed that he could have suffocated and was thankful that he was sleeping fine.

Due to this incident, I will no longer dress my son in sleepsacks which is unfortunate since both my kids wore HALO SleepSacks while they slept in cribs. The sleepsack my son was wearing on Nov. 18th I had bought on Amazon.com in March 2012 for $20, see link below.

http://www.amazon.com/dp/B004G8QN3K/ref=pe_175190_21431760_cs_sce_dp_2_B
 
I suggest a warning label on the sleepsacks that once a child can unzip the sleepsack, they should no longer wear them. There should also be a clasp at the bottom of the sleepsack to prevent a kid from unzipping it. I sent HALO an email to report the incident and shared the incident on Facebook and with my mom friends so that the scary incident I experienced can be prevented.
justification: The child was found tangled in the sleepsack but unharmed, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description: A floating shelf that I purchased at Target falls off the wall if it is bumped into in any way. It's happened three times and I cannot stress how little you have to touch it for it to fall off. The shelf is installed correctly, but the shelf is not secured to the mounting bracket in any way. The shelf holds a decent amount of weight, but if it's moved up at all, the entire thing falls down. It's fallen on my foot without major injury, thankfully,but it has broken a few of my items.
justification: The shelf has fallen multiple times, causing minor injury (foot) and property damage, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The Summer Infant Brayden Glider Chair sold by Babies R' Us, fell apart while my wife was sitting in it with our baby.  The slats on the side are made from press board which is disintegrating. The slats came out and the chair collapsed.  This is a dangerous chair.  My wife ways only 130lb so it wasn't a weight issue and the chair is less than a year old.
Babies R' Us and the manufacturer are unresponsive to my complaints and the product is still on sale on their site and in their store.
justification: The chair collapsed but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I purchased the Gabriella double dresser made by Universal SmartStuff.  This is a children's furniture line.  The dresser fell forward when the drawers were opened.  It fell on my husband and thankfully not my 2 yr. old who was standing nearby.  We tested it with contents inside and without and it fell both ways.  According to ASTM standards a dresser should be able to stand up with all drawers open without it falling over.  The manufacturer recommended affixing the tip restraint hardware.  I was told by someone who sits on the ASTM board that the tip restraint hardware is a last step safety measure but should not be a first solution.  The dresser should be able to stand on it's own however it is recommended that tip restraint hardware be affixed to all children's furniture to prevent it from falling in the event a child tries to climb on it.  Although very beautiful this dresser is very dangerous.  We were able to obtain a full refund from the retailer.
justification: The dresser fell on the husband but no injury was reported, and the child was unharmed. The incident highlights a clear safety issue with the product.

incident_description: An LED light bulb manufactured by Sylvania for consumer use in lamps smoked, charred, and exploded while in use in a conventional stand-up lamp.  The base of the bulb was charred, and the plastic housing for the bulb dome shattered into several tiny pieces.  The bulb had been used without incident in a 5-ft tall stand-up lamp for approximately 18 months.  No fire or injuries resulted with this incident, which occurred in the nursery of a two-story colonial home.  The lamp was the only device plugged into a conventional outlet in a house built in 1968, not known to have experienced any unusual electrical issues.  We have been residents since 2/2011.  Assume the bulb was incorrectly matched to the lamp, but I assumed these were safely interchangeable with conventional and/or CFL bulbs.  Concerned that others use LED bulbs without concern, when there may be a problem.
justification: The incident involved a smoking, charred, and exploding LED bulb but resulted in no fire or injuries, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I purchased a La-Z-Boy Vail XR power recliner on Aug 31, 2012.  I was sitting in the chair in an upright position on Friday, Nov 16, 2012, when I dropped a piece of popcorn in the chair, and reached between the bottom cushion and the arm of the chair to attempt to retrieve the popcorn.  I cut my finger severely.  I turned the chair over and discovered some very sharp edges on some exposed metal.  It seems to be a natural reaction for someone to attempt to retrieve a dropped object.  I dread the thought of a small child attempting to retrieve a toy or other object.  I can easily imagine the possibility of a severed finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe cut, indicating an injury, and the description suggests a plausible scenario for recurrence.

incident_description: My children have the Dorel Asia bunk beds from Wal-Mart. Model No. WM1848R2. The side rail split when my son and neice were sitting in the bed watching tv. Luckily the beds were not set up as bunk beds at the time.
justification: The side rail split while children were sitting on it, indicating a potential for injury, though none occurred in this instance.

incident_description: I purchased a Dunlap auto-shut off, four setting heating pad three years ago.  Last night when I plugged it in and turned it on, it sparked, FLAMED and burnt through the wires!!  This item was purchased at Big Lots.
justification: The heating pad sparked and flamed, causing damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his wife was cleaning the bathroom vanity and she accidently dropped a perfume bottle into the bottom of the vessel. The consumer stated that the bottle chipped slightly at the base of the bottle, but there was no chip on the vessel of the vanity. 

The consumer stated that his wife continued cleaning and she turned to throw a tissue into the trashcan. The consumer stated approximately 2-3 minutes later the complete vanity exploded which was approximately 16ÃÂ wide and 6ÃÂ deep. The consumer stated that there were pieces of glass all over the bathroom. The consumer stated that his wife was not even running water on the vanity. 

The consumer stated that his wife was cut on his left arm. He stated that the laceration was minor and no medical assistance was needed. 

The consumer stated the he contacted the manufacturer through email and was still awaiting a response. 

The consumer stated that he believes this product should be investigated since it poses a laceration hazard to the consumers.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor laceration that did not require medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the plastic chair collapsed when he sat on it and he fell to the floor.  The chair legs buckled under which caused the incident.  The weight requirement is 250lbs which he is not, he is not even close to that amount to cause this failure.  This was the caller first time using the chair.
The manufacturer was not contacted.

The caller feels that this chair is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The chair collapsed but there was no mention of injury, only a fall to the floor.

incident_description:
Office chair purchased in July 2012.
Patient was sitting on chair when one side broke off, resulting in two legs falling off of chair and the patient collapsing with it.
It appears the welding failed on one side of the chair resulting in two legs separating from base of chair.
justification: The patient collapsed when the chair broke, indicating a likely injury from the fall.

incident_description: I purchased a bed frame (the "Narrow-Leg Wood Bed Frame") from West Elm, shipped to me and professionally assembled in September 2012.  Upon placing my mattress on the bed frame, the support beams and rails collapsed.  At first it was suspected that the frame was simply not assembled properly, so replacement support pieces were sent to me.  I put the frame together according to specifications.  All seemed well at first, but within a few days the support beams and rails collapsed again, this time with me on the bed.  Fortunately no injuries were sustained.
justification: The bed frame collapsed twice, but no injuries were sustained, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: The wood base/frame of the glider chair cracked in May 2012 and developed an additional crack in October 2012.  The crack from October is large and goes through where the glider frame is bolted together.  We have stopped using the chair concerned that frame will come apart during use.  This chair looks similar to the chairs involved in the CPSC [REDACTED] recall .  Reading user reviews on the merchant's website (walmart.com) I found other consumers also had the same issue.
justification: The chair's frame cracked, posing a risk of failure during use, but no injury was reported. Similar issues reported by other users indicate a likely occurrence.

incident_description:
I have had two incidents where chandelier holding ring broke.
One of them fall on our glass dinner table (this is a 5 light chandelier).
The other one fall on the floor of our living room (this is a 9 light chandelier).
Thanks God no one got hurt.
justification: The chandelier fell twice but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: My father of 84 recovering from recent back surgery sat down on on a Cosco Model number 37800blk1w Folding stool and collapsed under him giving him a hard fall onto the kitchen floor making his back hurt. I took them back to Walmart where thy were purchased and the only words out of thier mouths was that the stools looked a little dirty. Did not show any concern if anyone was hurt. They refunded the money but offered no concern or compensation for the victim. We are currently seeking a product liability attorney. These stools need to be removed from the market.
justification: The incident resulted in a hard fall causing back pain to an elderly individual recovering from surgery, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Serta Damask Stripe 233-Thread Count Electric Heated Mattress Pad, White

I bought this September 2011.  Nothing out of the ordinary was done with this mattress pad but just over a year of use and the cord has melted.  This could have started a fire!
justification: The cord melting could have started a fire, indicating a significant hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased 3 cases of Sunlite CFL light bulbs through Lightbulbsdirect.com during July 2012.  I have filed a complaint with the state of New Jersey because Lightbulbsdirect.com is located in Eatontown, N.J..  I am filing the New York state because the distributer, Sunshine Lighting.  Their location is Brooklyn, NY 11231.

These bulbs were sold as 8000 hour CFL bulbs.  I installed the first case of twelve in the ceiling can lights in both the kitchen and bathroom of my home.  Within a seconds one bulb quit working.  The following morning my wife discovered a lens laying on an area rug in the kitchen.  It did not break apparently due to falling on the rug.  Soon after, another bulb shed it's lens just above my wife's head.  This one missed a rug and broke into many pieces.  Neither of the rubber like seals or lens glass showed any kind of sealant!

Lightbulbsdirect.com put Shunshine Lighting's representative, [REDACTED], in touch with me.  MR. [REDACTED] suggest that my home's electrical wiring to be defective.  We had just moved in during May but the house was custom built in 1999.

I have presently removed everyone of these Sunshine bulbs.  Before doing so, the entire first case of Day Light Color bulbs were inoperative.  I did have a licensed electrician come to my home and he has certified that the problem was not my electrical system.

My electrician informed me that most of these bulbs are from overseas and do NOT have any testing.  Sunshine's Sunlite bulbs come from China and show no sign of testing or approval.  It was further noted that, for example, Home Depot only sells these type bulbs that are tested and approved.  I bought my replacement bulbs at Home Depot and they are UL certified and from China.

I addition to the falling/breaking glass there is also the mercury hazard.  My living room ceiling is 20 feet high and contains nine light cans!

I wish to be reimbursed for the three cases of bulbs $322.20 plus any return shipping and handling charges.  Also, my electricians charges.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved falling and breaking bulbs, posing a potential hazard, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: It appears that my one year old boy removed the staples from the back of the chair and was eating it.  Fortunately, I noticed it immediately before any harm was induced.  He later tried picking out more staples from the back of the chair.  The chair is now out of harms way.
justification: The child was eating staples but no harm occurred, and the chair was subsequently moved to prevent recurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Quantum Realspace PROÃÂ 9000 office chair.  Leaning slightly back into the chair yesterday evening, the supporting bolts cracked, sending me backwards onto the floor.

I see there is an existing recall on this item but was not aware of it prior to my accident.
justification: The chair collapsed, causing the person to fall onto the floor, which implies an injury occurred.

incident_description:
The product is Quorum International 1353-1-65 Prism Mini Pendant, Satin Nickel
by Quorum International.  We purchased this from Lighting Universe, online.  This is the second time one of these pendants has shorted out.  This time was much worse than the first.  Pink sparks shot out throughout the kitchen, and smoke poured out of the fixture.  I believe that if this had happened when we were not at home, there is a good chance the fixture would have caught on fire.

We will be replacing all of these pendant fixtures.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke, posing a significant risk of injury or fire, and it's the second occurrence, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased 3 of your Bastis hooks ($2.99) each Article Number: 600.953.21 from your Schaumburg Illinois store about 1 and a half years ago.  We used them in our 1 years old son's room and found the hooks dangerous.  We installed 3 of them low enough he could grab them.  He was able to pull them off the wall and pull out a plastic insert inside the hook (used to hang it to the wall) and put it in his mouth.  He did this with 2 of the 3 hooks.  We're very disturbed by the quality of this product and the fact that it comes apart so easily and poses such a risk to children.  After fishing both of the plastic parts from our son's mouth we threw away all 3 of the hooks.  It seems like a huge liability risk on IKEA's part do not design the product so this cannot come apart.

Any product that is clearly marketed towards children (like this) should have a warning label or disclaimer about the possibility of becoming a choking hazard.  We've purchased many products from IKEA in the past but will be much more careful about what we purchase from you in the future.
justification: The child was able to pull out and ingest plastic parts, posing a choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I bought this bed for my 3 year old and it did not last more than a week.  The slats that hold the mattress up fall out and now several have broke when he laid down one night.  It is unsafe for any child in my opinion and wish it to be recalled.
justification: The bed's slats broke when the child laid down, indicating a safety issue but no reported injury.

incident_description:
Well when I first received them  the two klickkack couch futons I was pleased, then not long afterwards about a month, the blue one's spring popped up in the middle. We, my assistant and I,  had to wrap tape around it to keep people from getting stuck by it. As it turned out very few people ever sat on it as I don't have a lot of traffic. I could count on both hands the number of people that have crossed my door step.  About three months after tthe couches arrived I began to get bit as I slept on them every day. I never used my brand new bed until now I'm not a bedroom person, but as I began to get bit we began to investigate the source.  We discounted the couches at first because they were brand new, but we did spray. As time went on the bites became more and more frequent, as they began to be everyday. I noticed every time I slept on the blue couch I woke up with a bed bug on me. I first flicked them away and killed them. Then I threw away my pillows but the biting did not stop. 

So I decided to sleep on the black couch, but I laid my book bag on the blue couch. When I had awakened I saw a big bug on the book bag, as I looked closer I could see several small ones crawling on it. So I immediately threw the book bag away, angry because it had served me well. I decided to pick up the blue couch and check under it, and that's when I saw them embedded into my couch where the under material was stapled on. I then unscrewed the one leg and saw about a hundred or so shell casings where these creatures had shredded their skin. i screamed, immediately I had my assistant throw the blue futon outside. As he got bit by one of the bugs I decided when we went back up stairs we would check the black couch also, and much to my surprise it was just as infested. I threw both couches out.  It's been five days now, and after seeing straggler bugs crawling around the first day Sunday we have not seen any, but I still keep spray handy just in case. 

Proof that it was the couches, is that we have not seen any more, and have not gotten bit since last Sunday. As soon as i threw them out the biting stopped. One of the reasons we did not start getting bit right away, was that the bugs were inside the furniture, until a girlfriend's little girl tore the back of my couch, about three months after I had the furniture.
justification: The incident involved multiple injuries from bed bug bites, but no death occurred. The likelihood is possible as the infestation was contained to the couches and stopped after their removal.

incident_description:
The lamp comes in a box unassembled. I took the parts out of the box and carefully followed the instructions to assemble the lamp. I specifically checked the screws holding the lamp shade to verify that they were tight. As I was lifting the pole to adjust the lamp height, the heavy glass shade and bulb crashed to the floor and shattered into many sharp fragments around my feet. The company says there is nothing wrong with the lamp; it was not assembled properly. My reaction is that a glass shade weighing several pounds in such a precarious position is not reasonable without some safeguard. 

An observation: because of the design of the lamp, it is not possible to actually see if the screws are correctly seated in the shade as you are attaching it. The problem is not self-evident  during the assemblly. An emphatic warning in the instructions combined with an instruction to to loosen knob F and turn the socket head up to see into the socket head so that you can verify that the screws are set in the anchor grove  on the shade would reduce the risk although I still find that heavy glass hanging with no other anchor unacceptable. I am 72 years old in good health, eysight, etc. I have been assembling products all my life. I carefully follow directions. If this traumatic and hazardous experience can happen to me, it can, and will, happen to lots of other consumers.
justification: The incident involved a hazardous situation with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood is high given the design flaws and user reports.

incident_description:
While I have determined that the lime green colored Bumbo purchased at Walmart store #2593, after thoroughly reading the recall notice I have one concern. My concern is with Walmart reselling a defective Bumbo without the agreed safety restraints installed. (Which is the one purchased for my infant son roughly 6-7 months ago). 

I discovered this initially when reading the recall notice which noted the specified information. While looking for this number I was at first worried because the number on the bottom of Bumbo wasn't the one in recall notice. knowing 100% fully we purchased Bumbo very recently I took a closer look.

 Upon doing I found a raised number Polyurethane World Patent No. PCT: ZA/1999/00030 (which appears to be erased). Which brings me back to my concern. My concern is not only that the Bumbo we purchased poses a hazard, but Walmart re-sold such a twice recalled product, putting it back on to the their shelves without the proper restraints. Not to mention for a profit.  I'm disgusted by Walmart's Audacity to do something like this. Who knows how many more situations such as ours there are?

Walmarts #2593 manager ([REDACTED]) was no help whatsoever, and I didn't know who to contact. So thank you for your time in reading and hopefully addressing this issue.
justification: The incident involves a recalled product being resold without safety restraints, posing a potential hazard to infants, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
i was sitting in a chair in front of my PC.
I reached up to scratch the back of my head with my left hand.
With NO warning my chair slowly started to lead backwards.
It kept going and going till I hit the floor.

This was extreemly frighting experience, falling backwards in this chair.
justification: The incident involved a fall from a chair, which is frightening but resulted in no reported injury.

incident_description: My 8 month old daughter was in the seat on our kitchen table.  She was buckled into the seat.  My wife got up from the table to bring some food to the table and before we knew it, she had either rocked the seat off the table or slid it off the table.  She fell to the floor and hit her head.  She had a fractured skull and concussion.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured skull and concussion, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described scenario of a child in a seat on a table.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she purchased a foam mattress and she started having a rash on her skin scattered around her body. The consumer stated that she also experienced itchy eyes, nausea upon waking up, nose bleeds, her right kidney hurts, and bladder infections. The consumer stated that she wakes up during the night and when she wakes up she still feels tired. 

The consumer stated that she decided to move to another bedroom for approximately 2 ÃÂ½ weeks and her symptoms improved. 

The consumer stated that she has been to several doctors and they are unable to find why she was having the symptoms. She stated that she has changed foods and detergents thinking she had been becoming allergic to them. 

The consumer stated that she was researching and found that many reports had been filed online in regards to the foam mattress and the symptoms that they cause. The consumer stated that this product those not provide any labels indicating that it could be toxic to some consumers. 

The consumer stated that she will be contacting the manufacturer to file a report.
justification: The consumer experienced multiple health issues including rashes, nausea, and infections, which improved after discontinuing use of the mattress, indicating injury.

incident_description: We just bought some "RE. Room Essentials" string lights From Target (small glass sphere lights). My girlfriend hung them up, and an hour later we noticed there was two burnt out. Incredulous, she tried screwing one of the burnt out bulbs in tighter in case it was just loose. The glass globe shattered in her hand, cutting her and leaving shards of glass in her hand. She's no brute; she used care and caution. The glass used in this product is cheap, brittle and dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (cuts and glass shards in hand) due to the product's brittle glass, indicating a moderate severity and possible likelihood given the product's quality.

incident_description:
I purchased a  a Kaz Softheat heating pad. After using this product I incurred severe 2nd degree burns and may need skin grafting due to the severity of the burns.The pad has an auto shutoff. I don't know if that doesn't work or if the pad was manufactured in a defective manner. 
I am writing because I do not want someone else  to experience the pain that I had for almost a month now from using a product that is advertised to help relieve pain.
justification: The incident resulted in severe 2nd degree burns potentially requiring skin grafting, indicating a high severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely based on the lack of widespread reports mentioned.

incident_description:
Caller is employee at retail store.
On Saturday, September 8th, 2012 while decorating in store, she was attaching a giant hanging skeleton ghoul.
Ghoul is approximately seven feet long when hanging, while hanging this ghoul, she felt that small particles came off and she breathed them in.
Within the hour caller developed a bloody nose and coughing which kept happening until the following day.
They have been on the Dollar Store and on the shelf for sale since the week of September 4th, 2012.

Caller is asking that these decorations be inspected and investigated before a child or another consumer is injured.

UPDATE: Skeleton ghoul comes in 2 different colors/styles. I was hanging the skull with tan fabric netting over black material.  The particles seemed to come from the tan fabric netting.
justification: The employee experienced a bloody nose and coughing from inhaling particles, indicating an injury. The likelihood is possible as similar incidents could occur with other consumers.

incident_description: Purchased chandelier from Lowes a little under five years ago.  Had the chandelier professionally installed in two-story foyer.  The main solid ring attached to the ceiling broke apart and chandelier came crashing down.  The chandelier was destroyed, along with an area of ceramic tile.  Luckily no one was around when the chandelier fell from the ceiling or someone would have been injured.
justification: The chandelier fell and caused property damage, but no one was injured.

incident_description:
We have a swing arm lamp that clamps to a tabletop, with a single FEIT CFL light bulb that we use to light a work bench in the basement.  On Sunday, Sept 30, 2012, the light was turned on while my husband was in the basement.  After a while, my husband realized that the light had turned off, so he started to unscrew the CFL bulb and it exploded, blowing a 1 inch piece of glass into his hand.  The glass shards made cuts in his finger and thumb, and there was a puff of smoke.  

After this incident occurred, I read on the internet that we should shut down the heating system and crack a window in the basement for ventilation, which we did. However, we are very concerned about contamination from mercury entering into the cuts on my husbands fingers and both of us breathed in the smoke.  I put the broken CFL bulb in a [REDACTED] bag and saved it.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts from glass shards and potential mercury exposure, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description: A glass deck top from Ikea shattered with no warning. This happened at 3:00am, no one was around it. The desk was left shards of glass all over my office.
justification: The glass shattered but no one was present, resulting in no injury.

incident_description:
Dear Members of the National Safety Council,
 
I am alerting you to the potential safety hazard of the Howard Miller Wall Clock. Model# 625-401 
Serial#K 10211. It is a contemporary style wall clock with a class front.  The nail provided with the clock by the manufacturer does not have a pop- open mechanism to secure the screw into the inside wall.
 
I purchased a model of that wall clock. It was installed following the instructions, using the screw provided.
 
Three weeks ago, I was walking by the wall where the clock hung. The clock fell, the lower right side of the glass front cut into my lower right leg at the calf.  I was taken by ambulance to East TX Medical Center in Tyler, TX where an ER physician was able to pull the cut skin from under the skin immediately below the wound and used 13 stitches to close the wound.   Despite antibiotics, the wound became infected.  I have been on three different
antibiotics and have needed to visit an ER a second time as well as my private physician twice.  The third antibiotic has worked and I am looking forward to have the stitches next week.
 
My concern is the safety of this product as it is currently marketed.  A simple replacement of a more substantial, pop open screw would secure the screw to the inside wall and enable it to then securely hold the wall clock in  place.
 
I have notified the manufacturer and am awaiting a response.
 
I felt it necessary  to inform  you of this potentially very dangerous situation in the clock's current hanging mechanism to prevent others from experiencing what I've been through.  What if a child had been the one to be there when the clock fell?
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring medical attention, but the likelihood is moderate as it depends on proper installation and usage.

incident_description:
When we turned on a wall switch, a light bulb in a hanging pendant light fixture exploded, showering glass over an area of many square feet.  Luckily, nobody was close to the bulb when it exploded.  Had someone been nearby, they could have been cut badly or lost an eye (or two).  The only thing left in the socket was the metal base of the bulb.

The bulb was a Phillips appliance 40 watt, medium base, 120 volt bulb made in the Philippines.
justification: The incident involved a bulb exploding without causing injury, but potential for severe injury existed if someone had been nearby.

incident_description: Purchased Tempur-pedic Cloud Supreme mattress set  on 7/21/12. The product produces intense chemical off-gassing, which has caused us to experience burning noses and sinuses, sore throats, chemical taste in mouth, headaches, racing heart, jitteriness, and weak knees.  The fumes are so strong, that I have not been able to use my master bedroom, since taking delivery of the mattress.  After 42 days, Tempur-pedic exchanged the mattress, but the replacement has the same intense off-gassing.  We have tried all the recommendations from Tempur-pedic to alleviate the odor - opening all windows, and running fans, as well as removing the cover and washing it - all to no avail.  The odor is still very intense and sickening, even after another 35 days with the second mattress. The weather is now turning colder and it is more difficult to leave the windows open 24/7.   I am very concerned of the long term health effects of this mattress. I strongly urge you to investigate the toxicity of Tempur-pedic mattresses.
justification: The description reports multiple health symptoms including burning noses, sore throats, and headaches, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue persists despite replacement, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
The consumer stated that 2 weeks ago her chandelier in her entrance way fell out of the ceiling after being installed 11 years. The consumer went to the retailer where she purchased the first one and ordered another one.

(8/2012) After having the new one installed by a carpenter. The consumer was coming down her stairs she looked over to the chandelier and noticed that the wires were protruding from the top and had started to loosen up.

(8/2012) The consumer contacted an Independent contractor to come out and remove the chandelier from the ceiling before another incident occurred.

UPDATE:
In 1998 I purchased the attached chandelier  along with other light fixtures  for my home at the 
Lowe's in Jackson, MI.  The fixture  was installed by the electrician who had done all of the 
wiring in the house. The fixture  was in my entrance way until 2009 when the fixture  broke and 
fell to the floor.  Me; thinking it was a freak accident went to my local Lowe's in Scio Twp. MI. 
hoping to find the same fixture since I really liked the style. I was able to order it through  a special order
catalogue and in a week or so it came and I had the contractor put it back up in my entrance

incident_description: I purchased a glass table top and desk legs from IKEA roughly a year and 9 months ago. When I came home from work I found that the desk had non metaphorically exploded. The only objects on the desk were an LCD monitor(which is now broken), a set of speakers(not heavy ones), mouse ,keyboard, and random papers. There was nothing above the desk so I am sure no object fell on it. The desk was not scratched or damaged in any way that I was aware of. My entire living room is now covered in small shards of glass. The carpet is full of glass as well as some chairs and a few pairs of shoes.  There was an inflatable work out ball beside the desk that was punctured by the explosion. It seems as though if I had been at the desk at the time of the explosion I very likely would have been injured in some way and at least absolutely terrified.
justification: The desk exploded causing property damage but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. Such incidents are rare, hence an occurrence likelihood of 1.

incident_description:

They could not figure out where it was coming from.  About an hour later, the  lights were still on and one of the globes imploded sending hot glass throughout the room. The bulb (a 100 watt halogen bulb) did not break.  The consumer says it was due to the extreme heat from the bulb that imploded the globe.  He went back and read reviews of the fixture.  

Customers were recommending a dimmer switch because of the intensity of the light.  he can only make the assumption that the bulb is being used is too hot for the fixture or there is a defect in the glass of the globe.  The consumer says the implosion of the globe could have caused serious injury to anyone nearby.  The consumer considers it to be a dangerous fixture for reasons to be determined.   

Consumer Added:  Spoke with customer service who told me that the globe imploded because the screw holding the globe was overtightened.  How could they make that statement without seeing the fixture?  I then spoke with the installer who said that was absolutely not the case and he has installed many similar fixtures.
justification: The incident involved an imploding globe that could have caused injury but did not, and the cause is disputed between heat and installation error.

incident_description:
Product is A 4000-INV wall panel lift, manufactured by Auton Company in Valencia, Ca.  The products function is to lift a movable wood panel  thus hiding or exposing a TV behind the movable panel.  

The product consist of a remote controlled motor which powers a bar pulley  attached to three fabric straps which in turn are attached at the bottom of a 50" X 74 1/2" metal frame. A second metal frame is attached the first metal frame and also the wood panel.  Two  seven or eight inch metal blocks containing ball bearings are affixed to the wall.  One of the frames contains two slides which  serves  to keep the  frames  attached to the wall while facilitation an up and down movement.  The metal slides in which the ball bearings roll are not continuous but spliced with a weld at the approximate mid-point.   At that point the slides  are worn which allowed the ball bearing to escape the track. 

In the presence of my two year old grandson my wife  remotely activated the lift to lower it.  When it reached the worn spot in the track,  the metal frames and wood panel escaped the track.  At this point the top of the panel would still be approximately seven or eight feet in the air.  The entire top of the panel flipped 180 degrees,  pivoting on the straps attached to the bottom of the panel,  crashing to the floor and shattering the panel.  At that moment my grandson was less than four feet from being violently hit.  I would estimate the weight involved to be in excess of 150 pounds.

Upon contacting the company I was assured that the product was still under warranty until December 2012 but I had to pay shipping to and from the factory and that none of the labor to repair the panel or other damage the product caused would be considered.   I informed them the only shipping I was willing to incur was to ship the product to your lab for testing but they are not impressed.  

I am an angry man.  I'm angry that this could have seriously injured my grandson.  I am angry that Auton  flaunting their responsibility as defined by the California product liability laws knowing it is not economically wise for me to litigate.  I'm angry at myself because I did not report this to you for product recall consideration until I got angry.  As evidence of how angry I am I am willing to forgo my warranty claim, (the product alone is $4999) and pay for shipping the product to you if you are interested in pursuing. Also if you are interested I can forward you the e-mail correspondence I have had with the company.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure that could have caused serious injury but did not, placing it at severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such failures are possible but not frequent.

incident_description:
On 09/26/2012 I was sleeping and my wife was reading in bed with our King sized electric blanket on.  The Blanket was produced by Biddeford Blankets.  My wife heard a buzzing noise and smelled smoke at which point and time she noticed that the electric controller for her half of the electric blanket was burning. Fire was contained within plastic shell but visible arcing, flame, and smoke were seen. 
She woke me up (firefighter by trade). I was able to unplug and extinguish the controller without any further damage (doused it in a sink.)  The blanket (itself) did not appear to burn just the control unit.  
Due to the fact that the fire did not extend beyond the object of origin, the fire department was not called.  Therefore, I am hoping that this organization can monitor whether this is a freak or common occurence with this device.  
The controller is off white with the number 1-H on a single dial.  It has Biddeford Auto Off on the face.  The lot # was 380910.  There was no visible serial #.
justification: The incident involved a burning controller but no injuries or further damage, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The description suggests this is an uncommon occurrence (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
In August of 2012 we ordered a Simmons Rogers Beautyrest mattress from MacyÃÂs, and immediately it was delivered to our house we noticed a sweet pungent chemical smell that filled the whole room.  We aired out the mattress during the day hoping that the smell would go away but it did not and in fact it spread throughout the house.   My wife and daughter then started noticing eye irritation and sore throats even though we were in another room.  When I tried to sleep on the mattress that night I awoke in the middle of the night with a bad headache at which point I gave up trying to sleep on the mattress.   After contacting MacyÃÂs and the manufacturer, we were told that the smell should go away after airing.  Several people told us different timeframes ranging from 3 days to two weeks.   After one week we contacted the manufacture and were told that it was probably due to ÃÂuncured foamÃÂ in the mattress, and they agreed to replace the mattress.  This time we chose a Simmons Beautyrest Black Kameryn model, but when it was delivered it had exactly the same problem.  After a week of airing it out with a fan blowing on it we gave up and returned this mattress as well.

We found that we were not able to use the mattresses to sleep on.   Much worse, we were very concerned about what chemicals were causing the eye and throat irritation and headaches, and whether these chemicals were harmful.   We repeatedly asked Simmons what chemicals were causing the smell, but they would not answer the question.  I offered to have someone from their company come to our house to look at the problem, but they were not interested.  We did some of our own research and found that one of the ingredients used in making the foams in the mattresses are diisocyanates.  On looking at the MSDS for diisocyanates, they are described as having a sweet aromatic smell and are known to cause eye and throat irritation and headaches.  They are also described as highly toxic.  We have no way of knowing exactly what was causing the problem with these mattresses, but it would seem that one possibility is that excess diisocyanates were left in the foam and were off-gassing.  This possibility would seem to be a significant safety concern.

Simmons claims that their foams have been certified by a group called CertiPUR, and one of the substances they test for are diisocyanates.   However, on the CertiPUR website they state that their testing frequency is only twice a year.  The CertiPUR certification says nothing about the foam produced for the rest of the year, does not address the issue of manufacturing consistency and says nothing about the foam in your mattress.  Additionally, the certification refers only to the foam ÃÂ not the end product that probably contains all sorts of other things that emit chemicals such as glues.  

In the absence of the willingness of the manufacturer to properly address these issues, it seems that a safety organization should.  After all, someone who is sleeping on these mattresses is breathing these chemicals for some eight hours a day at close quarters.
justification: The incident caused eye irritation, sore throats, and headaches, indicating physical harm to multiple individuals.

incident_description:
On the night of Saturday, September 08, 2012, I was awaken by a loud explosion in the computer room where the lights were still on.  The outer shell of the fluorescent lamp in the ceiling fan-light fixture blew up and not only it blew up itself, but it exploded the light fixture on the fan.  The light fixture on the fan is a standard glass shell, shaped like an open-ended cone, and the light bulb can be installed right through the opening, without needing to remove the fixture.  The explosion sent thousands of tiny pieces around, along with about a dozen medium size pieces, and a few large size pieces.  The largest projectile was about 5'x2' with ragged edges.  The force of the explosion was such that projectiles went as far as 5 yards, hitting the wall in the hallway, and reflecting in the opposite direction, so one could see the glass in the hallway, before you even turned the corner into the room.  The glass was all over the couch, carpet, bookstacks, and my husband and I spent two hours cleaning it up late into the night.  Explosion was so powerful that when we lifted the couch pillows, there was glass underneath.  When we moved the couch to clean under it, we found the pieces of glass on the wall behind it.  

It was the matter of big luck that no one was injured.  At the time of explosion, I usually read on the couch, and it was an exception that I went to bed early that day.  This product needs to be taken off the market immediately, because it presents a danger of laceration and puncture.

On Monday, September 10, 2012, I contacted the manufacturer, the Osram Sylvania company.  My report was recorded and my information taken.  I was told that someone from the company will contact me within 48 hours.  Nobody ever called or contacted me in any other way, which makes me suspect that the company is aware of the problems with its light bulbs.  At a minimum, the company has no interest to ensure their product safety by properly investigating the report.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous explosion of a light fixture, but no injuries occurred despite the potential for harm.

incident_description: Phillips flood dim CFL bulb was in a recessed light in my kitchen and the globe fell off and shattered into a million pieces on the floor.  There was no warning noise or blinking before it fell and the bulb was still lit.  Nothing shook the house prior to the bulb falling apart.

After fixing this problem by using L-brackets to fasten the slats directly to the side rail,  one of the upper bunk slats broke under the weight of a 60 pound boy.   

This bed is extremely under designed.  The slats are too small and too few and the side rail design is weak.  This bed, in my opinion, is unsafe for children.

incident_description:
We ordered a new Tempur-Pedic Contour select mattress directly from the company and it was delivered at 5:10 pm on 9/14/2012 by a contractor chosen by the company. The bed was removed from a large cardboard box by the delivery personnel and set in place in the upstairs master bedroom. When they removed the protective plastic a strong chemical odor was immediately noticeable. Shortly after the delivery we left the house for dinner and returned at approximately 7:15 pm. Upon opening the front door we were struck by the intensity of the chemical odor/vapor. I would compare the odor to a petroleum based paint or chemical solvent. We were surprised that it had permeated throughout the entire house so quickly and at how powerful the odor was downstairs.  I immediately consulted the Tempur-Pedic internet site to see if this was ÃÂnormalÃÂ and read the following: 
ÃÂSome people notice a slight odor to their new mattressÃÂthis can come from our TEMPUR material manufacturing process. This smell is normal and usually disappears before the product reaches you. Sometimes, however, this smell may still be noticeable. It usually disappears after a few weeks. It can help to take the steps recommended in ÃÂBreak in periodÃÂ below; that will help the TEMPUR material cells fully open and release the smell.ÃÂ  
And it added: 
ÃÂYou can speed up the break-in period by simply spending time in bed: reading, watching TV or playing with the kids or grandkids. The extra movement will help the cells in the TEMPUR material to fully open (some may have remained closed after manufacturing). As they open, they are able to ÃÂbreathÃÂ and respond to weight and temperature, but they always return to their original shape.ÃÂ
As I was reading this my wife, who is 4 months pregnant and 2 year old son were up stairs. When I went upstairs I was shocked at how strong the odor/vapor was. My wife was complaining of a headache within 15 minutes of being upstairs and is not prone to headaches. I immediately opened all four windows in the bedroom and the window in the attached bathroom and turned on the fan and air conditioner in an effort to dissipate the odor/vapor. The ventilation did little to impact the strong nature of the odor. I decided to try, as the company suggested, to lie on the bed and move around in an effort to speed up the release of the odor/vapor. As I was lying and rolling around in the bed the odor/vapor was extremely noxious and I notices that my eyes were starting to burn. After about 15 minutes I began experiencing an irritation in my throat and an upper respiratory discomfort. I do not have any know allergies and am not easily irritated or oversensitive to odors. It was at his time I concluded that it would not be safe for my pregnant wife and I to sleep on this bed as it was releasing this chemical odor/vapor. I informed my wife that I felt it would be a good idea to sleep in the guest room and let the bedroom air out overnight with the windows open. She agreed and stated that the chemical odor/vapor was very strong throughout whole upstairs, which is where all three bedrooms are located, and could not imagine sleeping in our bedroom on the mattress.
Around 9 pm I went to the grocery store to purchase baking soda in the hope that it might absorb some of the odor. I also purchased moisture absorbent to control moisture in the room since the windows would need to remain open overnight for ventilation. As I returned home and exited my vehicle I detected the odor from the driveway. This is a testament to the strength and noxious nature of the odor/vapor.The smell was clearly present in the driveway and the only open windows were on the second story facing the rear of the house.
I returned to the room to place the baking soda and moisture absorbent inside, upon opening the door I noticed the smell had grown even more intense. As I changed into my sleep wear which was inside the room, my eyes again began to sting and I felt the irritation in my throat return. I closed the door and placed a towel against the gap between the door and the floor to prevent the odor from seeping out. When I opened the door to our guest room my wife was still awake and my son was in the room with her. She explained that he had woken up coughing and was rubbing his eyes so she took him into the guest room since it was slightly further from the master bedroom. She was complaining of a headache and was unable to fall asleep with the odor present. I got into bed and noticed the odor was clearly present in the guest room. After some time I too was unable to sleep and went downstairs to do some further research of the topic on the internet. After searching ÃÂTempur-Pedic odorÃÂ and similar phrases I saw how common this issue is and read many testimonials and reviews by consumers who echoed the same problems and concerns that I was experiencing. Some testimonials stated that they were unable to sleep on the bed for weeks after purchasing and that the odor never really cleared to an undetectable level. I also came across incident reports submitted to safeproducts.gov that mentioned the chemical odor and similar ill effects it caused. I still smelled these odors and after a quick walk around the house it was evident the odor/vapor had permeated the entire home. I went back to bed worried and a bit shocked. I found it difficult to sleep and when I awoke periodically I could feel irritation in my throat and was always conscious of the odor/vapor. I could also hear my son coughing throughout the night.
When I awoke in the morning my throat was irritated and I and I could notice a different tone to my voice. My wife stated that was also experiencing throat irritation and was visibly upset about the situation and possible effects this may have on the child she was carrying.  I instructed her not to enter the room unless it was absolutely necessary and I left the windows open and the fan on and left for work. Shortly after 8 am I called Tempur-Pedic customer service and spoke with representative [redacted]. I explained the seriousness of the situation and the effects that the odor/vapor had caused. He stated that it was ÃÂnormalÃÂ and that some people might notice a ÃÂslight odorÃÂ and he assured me that it was ÃÂsafe and harmlessÃÂ. I took exception this and explained that I did not understand how such a noxious chemical odor/vapor could be referred to as ÃÂslightÃÂ.  I compared it to having an open can of petroleum based paint or gasoline in the house and said it would be nearly impossible not to experience this offensive odor/vapor. I also mentioned that this was far from an isolated incident based on testimonials and reviews, some of which appear on the Tempur-Pedic site. I asked him how long the odor may persist and he stated as I had seen on the Tempur-Pedic site ÃÂIt usually disappears after a few weeksÃÂ. I immediately knew that I could not subject my family to this for weeks. I made the decision that for safety reasons I would exercise my right to return the product within 90 days for a refund as the company promises. I informed [redacted] of my decision and asked that he schedule a return pick up as soon as possible. He stated that I would need to talk to the returns department which was not open on the weekends and that I would need to call on Monday. I was concerned about my continued exposure to this horrendous chemical odor/vapor, and asked if he had any data or studies that show that the product and the odor/vapors it produced are in fact safe. He stated he did not. I asked if he could provide any information regarding the ingredients or materials used in the manufacturing process or any disclosures required by regulatory agencies he said he did have something and that he would send it to me via e-mail. I asked him to please make a notation on my account information about my report of the odor/vapor and he obliged. 
I phoned with my wife around noon and asked If the odor had decreased in intensity. She said that it had gotten progressively worse, that she was still experiencing  headache, and that upon entering the room to retrieve clothing it was basically unbearable. After hearing this I advised that she open all the windows in the house and to try an outdoor activity or spend time away from the home. 
During downtime at work I reviewed the e-mail. The e-mail contained several statements that attempted to reassure that there was no danger. It stated ÃÂBased on the information that we have reviewed and studies that have been conducted, we have no reason to believe any Tempur-PedicÃÂ® product creates a substantive product hazard to consumers.ÃÂ, but provided no data, links to these studies or information and does not say that it is completely safe or non-toxic. It also states: ÃÂTempur-PedicÃÂ® product formulas are a trade secret; however, the raw materials and processes used in manufacturing Tempur-PedicÃÂ® products are similar to those used in the production of a large variety of polyurethane foams used everyday by millions of people in many different applications like furniture, bedding, carpet underlay, packaging and automotive seats.ÃÂ , but does not mention any of the ÃÂcommonÃÂ raw ingredients that are used in manufacturing.
After further searching on studies I came across the following article on the internet http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memory_foam . The article cites all sources and makes the following statement: ÃÂThe HAP [Hazardous Air Pollutants] emissions associated with polyurethane foam production include methylene chloride, toluene diisocyanate, methyl chloroform, methylene diphenyl diisocyanate, propylene oxide, diethanolamine, methyl ethyl ketone, methanol, and toluene however not all chemical emissions associated with the production of these material have been classified. Methylene chloride makes up over 98 percent of the total HAP emissions from this industry. Short-term exposure to high concentrations of methylene chloride also irritates the nose and throat. The effects of chronic (long-term) exposure to methylene chloride in humans involve the central nervous system, and include headaches, dizziness, nausea, and memory loss. Animal studies indicate that inhalation of methylene chloride affects the liver, kidney, and cardiovascular system. Developmental or reproductive effects of methylene chloride have not been reported in humans, but limited animal studies have reported lowered fetal body weights in rats exposed. [10]ÃÂ
In another internet article,  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempur-Pedic the point is made that ÃÂTraditional (not Tempur) memory foams emit as much as 61 volatile organic compounds (VOCs),[17] several of which are commonly recognized as harmful by the California Health and Welfare Agency, the International Agency on Research of Cancer, and the EPA.[18ÃÂ the sources cited here are Toxic Bedrooms: Your Guide to a Safe Night's Sleep by Walter Bader and Integrated Risk Information System (IRIS) US Environmental Protection Agency. While this study does not include Tempur-Pedic products Since Tempur-Pedic did state in their e-mail ÃÂraw materials and processes used in manufacturing Tempur-PedicÃÂ® products are similar to those used in the production of a large variety of polyurethane foamsÃÂ and that ÃÂThe difference between the manufacture of our proprietary TEMPURÃÂ® material and other foam products is a proprietary process resulting in the viscoelastic property unique to our product and a denser, more comfortable material.ÃÂ  Based on this I would assume that Tempur-Pedic products most likely contain emit those same compounds and may have additional chemical emissions due to their unique manufacturing process.
I also concluded if their product was unique and that Tempur-Pedic was concerned with the safety and confidence of consumers they would release and promote data or studies that showed their product did not produce these hazardous air pollutants.
After returning home the odor/vapor was indeed much more intense. In an effort to try to curtail the odor, I took the advice of one testimonial/review that advised removing the outer cover and washing it. I washed the removable cover per the manufacturerÃÂs instructions included with the bed and allowed it to air dry. However, with the cover removed the odor/vapor became even stronger and I began to experience headache and nausea and was forced to leave the windows open and leave the room. I took the family out to dinner and the mall in an effort  to stay out of the house. I noticed that after a few hours of being away from the house the headache, nausea, and throat and respiratory irritation were not present. The fact that they returned about an hour after being home and that all of us were experiencing similar effects, is a good indicator that it was actually the vapor and not just a mere coincidence. Again we were forced to seal ourselves inside the guestroom to minimize our exposure to the odor/vapor.
After another unpleasant night I awoke, my wife complained about the same throat irritation. I went to the bedroom  hoping to find that the odor would have finally started to dissipate, instead I found the odor more established despite having the windows open and fan on high speed all night. By noon the cover had dried and I ventured into the room to replace it. By the time I got it on my eyes were burning and I knew I had to get this mattress out of the living space. I took the family out to the store to get them away from the house. I purchased thick plastic drop cloths and upon returning home sent my wife and son to her fatherÃÂs house to keep them away from the odor. I placed the plastic around the mattress and sealed it with tape. I then moved the mattress into the garage. I then opened every window in the house, turned on every fan and the air conditioning. I called my wife to let her know that she could return. Upon return she noticed that the odor/vapor, while still detectable was a big improvement form that morning. I left the windows open overnight to allow it to air out.
At the time of writing on the morning of 9/18 the odor is still present in the bedroom but is not nearly as potent. The rest of the house is much better. Upon entering the garage, the odor is clearly present, despite being wrapped in plastic and sealed with tape. I will call Tempur-Pedic shortly and arrange for the return. I am very eager to get this product out of my home and try to put this whole incident behind me.
I feel that Tempur-Pedic needs to inform customers about the odor and possible health risk. The headache, nausea, and throat and respiratory irritation we experienced were directly related to their product. A direct warning should be issued to consumers a not just mere mention on their web site that ÃÂSome people notice a slight odor to their new mattressÃÂ. This is truly misleading.
 I was pleased by the level of comfort of the product when I tried it at a local store, and was disappointed that I was unable to ever sleep on the mattress due to the extremely noxious odor. Had I been informed of the potential of experiencing this issue and the health risks associated, I would have never purchased it. This is why IÃÂm sure it is not disclosed, as it would almost certainly discourage sales. 
As a healthcare professional with an extensive background in chemistry, I do not understand how warnings regarding this issue are not required as part of the product labeling. I couldnÃÂt imagine this product being delivered to someone whoÃÂs medical condition would make them more susceptible to the symptoms of inhaling this odor/vapor. I am thankful I was able to remove it from my immediate living space and could not imagine keeping something this noxious in the house for weeks waiting for the odor/vapor issue to resolve.
I have tried to be accurate provide as much detail as possible. I hope that it can be used to prevent others from having similar experiences, especially without proper warning. I have provided my contact information and welcome any further questions you have. I also wish to be contacted by the manufacturer and provided with any and all of the information  pertaining to the chemical components and any research which has been done regarding safety and chemical emissions.
justification: The incident caused headaches, throat irritation, and respiratory discomfort, indicating physical harm, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is rated 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar incidents.

incident_description: Roughly about a year ago I purchased some of these bulbs from Lowe's. These bulbs are marked Bright Effects L18TM6/27K 18W 120VAC 60Hz. In under 24 hours I had two of them fail. incident_description:
I've had, for 6-7 years, an Ott table lamp w/ the original CFC bulb in it.  The lamp is very rarely used, as it's in a guest bedroom.  Yesterday, I was in that BR and noticed the seam on the lampshade was askew, so I turned the shade to straighten it.  Please note that the lamp was OFF and I had not turned it on at all during the time I was in that room.  As I was going out the door, maybe 5-10 secs later, there was an huge popping sound.  Scared the you know what out of me, and when I turned around, there was glass everywhere.  In the bed, all over the pillows and bedding, imbedded in the carpet... and the shards of glass sprayed out over at least 4' of space.  What a freakin' mess - words don't do it justice.  It took me hours, literally, to clean everything up and I'm still not sure I've gotten all the small pieces of glass out of the carpet.  I actually threw out the comforter b/c I was concerned that I'd never properly be able to get the imbedded glass out of it.  More importantly, I shudder to think what might have happened had this occurred while someone was in the bed. When I look at the lamp, there is not one iota of glass left in the fixture - just the ring that contained said bulb. I emailed Ott, shortly after the event, and explained to them what happened and inquired as to whether there was a recall on the product (meaning the lamp) and the reply I rec'd was:  "Hello [REDACTED],  I apologize for the issue with the bulb, however has never been a recall on that bulb.  Best Regards, [REDACTED] |  Customer Service Representative
Exercise and Live Healthy!!"   

Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident involved a bulb exploding without causing injury, but with significant potential for harm if someone had been present.

Within about 3 weeks, while eating dinner, I noticed one bulb flicker and then burn out. I turned the light switch off then on again but the bulb did not light up.  Something seemed odd about it and I took a flashlight to shine on the base of the bulb.  The area looked smokey so my husband tried to remove the bulb and burned his hand. incident_description:
Purchased 6 Instant Pendant Light Conversion Kits in May from Home Depot.  Product #PBN-6012 manufactured by Worth Home Products.  These convert an existing recessed can light fixture into a hanging pendant light fixture.  It's a great easy do-it-yourself item that updates the look of your room, and provides more light than the recessed can fixtures.  The light fixture screws into the existing bulb receptacle and the length is adjusted by winding the cord around a plastic arm in the fixture.  I have photographs attached.  The item is clearly visible on the manufacturer's web page.

At 79 days and at 28 days after installation, on two of the six fixtures, the plastic bracket inside the fixture used to wind excess cord, sheared off from stress.  The fixture then dropped down from the ceiling, hanging about three feet lower than it's original height - the total length of the adjustable cord.  The fixture was still attached to the ceiling by the socket that screws into your existing recessed can bulb receptacle.

Should someone happen to be standing under the fixture when this happened, the fixture would hit them in the head.

The manufacturer needs to provide a repair kit that replaces the plastic braket portion with something capable of bearing the weight of the fixture.
justification: The incident describes a fixture dropping but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given two failures out of six installations.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her 4 years old son was sleep, woke up at approximately 1am and walked into his room. The consumer stated that her son got into her bed and fell asleep on the edge. The consumer stated that she was sleep and unaware that her son was in the bed. 

The consumer stated that she woke up to her son screaming and he was standing up crying. 

The consumer stated that he told her that he fell off the bed. The consumer stated that he was shaking and he told her that his belly hurt. The consumer stated that she noticed blood on sheets and she turned her son over and noticed a puncture wound on his left side above his hip.

She stated that they took him to the pediatric trauma center and they did chest x-rays, and a CAT scan with oral IV and rectal tracing to see if he was internally bleeding.  The consumer stated that the test reveal blood and air in the abdomen.

incident_description:
Home Depot brand, Husky Secure Lock Track Wall, model THD101, Husky 35 lb Vertical Bike Hooks, model THD208, and Husky Track Wall Fastener Kit, model THD 150.
Advertised max capacity is 75 lbs per linear ft, which would be 300 lbs for the 4ft section I purchased.
I installed the track wall according to package directions, using 6 of the fastener kit screws each into studs.  It was appx 7 ft off the floor in my garage, and according to package directions, I counter-sunk the screws "... to be flush with the surface..." of the track wall.
I then attached 4 bike hooks, and hung 4 adult size bicycles from the unit.  Each bike weighs about 30-35 lbs, according to my bathroom scale.
After approximately 10-15 minutes, the entire unit broke free from the mounting screws, and everything came crashing to the floor.  Thankfully, we had just stepped out from under the unit, so no one was hurt.  However, one bike wheel was damaged beyond repair, and several bike components were bent and scratched.
My conclusions are that when this product is installed using the appropriate materials, and following the manufacturer's instructions, and using appropriate accessories, it is unsafe.
In my opinion, the screws do not provide enough distribution of force along the composite material to prevent the material from failing.  The instruction to counter-sink the screws is also problematic, because although this seems necessary to allow adjustment of mounting/hanging accessories along the track, doing so apparently significantly reduces the strength of the composite material, such that catastrophic failure has occurred.
I returned the track wall unit and the 4 bike hooks to the store (in rehoboth beach, del) today, and received a full refund, but I now have a bike with a ruined wheel that I must now replace.
justification: The incident resulted in property damage but no injuries, as the individuals had stepped away before the unit failed.

incident_description: I was almost electrocuted while installing a floor lamp from Cost Plus World Market.  The light bulb base had broke (or came broken).  The jagged edge of the this base was cutting into the power cable for this lamp, energizing the metal casing of the lamp.  Due to the design of the lamp, this seems like it would be a common occurrence.  There is also no grounding conductor run with the current carrying conductors within the power cable.  Fortunately, I noticed the jagged edge cutting into the power cable before plugging in the first time.  The only reason I noticed this was due to wobbly nature of the lamp shade.  This thin piece of metal that makes the base of the light bulb, also is the structural support for the lamp shade.
justification: The incident involved a near-electrocution due to a design flaw, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is high due to the described common occurrence of the issue.

incident_description:
At approximately 5:00PM on 5/15/12, my son was in his bumbo chair on the island counter as my husband was unloading the dishwasher and he bounced himself right off the counter. He had a 5' drop onto a linoleum floor. He was rushed to the emergency room as he fell on directly on his head. At the emergency room, he was given a CT scan and it was determined he did not have a skull fracture but the impact of the fall was so hard that the ear wax that had been inside of his ears was outside and located on his cheek. 

I do not feel this product is safe to put infants in. I would not recommend it to anyone nor would I ever put any of my children in it ever again. Yes, he should not have been on the counter but I do not feel this is stressed enough as a hazard and I do not feel that putting a strap on the product will make it safer in any way. It will not prevent babies from falling over and hitting their heads.

incident_description:
The respondent and 2 of her students were hanging two 65-Q lights and one 360-Q lights in the auditorium.  They were on a catwalk and they were in the process of hanging the lights on a pipe that is attached to the walkway.

The lights had fumes and a smoke emitting from them.  This was a first time use.  There was nothing in the box or any warnings that this type of problem would occur.  The two students went down into the auditorium to work on something else.  The respondent estimates that she had been exposed to these fumes for approximately 60 minutes to 90 minutes, but she did not realize that the fumes were there.  The respondent was talking to a student and she was on her knees, when she fell back on the catwalk.  The respondent indicated that she heard someone's voice and she ended up at the end of the catwalk.  Her face was flush and she experienced shortness of breath.  She could not yell. One of the students had to help the respondent get down off of the catwalk.

After approximately an hour, the consumer felt better.  She was able to walk after about 20 minutes, but she was still disoriented and felt nauseous for a period of time.  The respondent said that she thought that she would be alright the next day. However, approximately 3 days later, the consumer developed lung problems and sought medical attention.

(4/29/2011)  The respondent went to her primary care physician.  The doctor listened to the respondent's lung and administered a steroid shot, steroid pills and an inhaler.  This mediation helped the consumer improve her systems


The respondent was referred to a pulmonologist, who tested her for heavy metals, but she has not found anything as of yet.

In early May 2011, the respondent contacted the firm by e-mail and attempted to get MSDS's for what was in the product and for copies of the problems MSDS sheets, but they would not provide them to her.  One of their rep's said that she did not know what was in the lights or their coating.  Another rep. named [REDACTED] told the respondent that he would provide the information to her, but he never did.

The respondent contacted someone, who referred her to the CPSC.  

The primary symptoms have been dizziness and fatigue.  The respondent has been coughing up a chemical-like substance and she has a lingering metallic taste in her mouth.  Later medical testing showed elevated blood lead levels.  The respondent began having nervous system issues ub late May 2011 that persist today.
justification: The respondent suffered lung problems, elevated blood lead levels, and persistent nervous system issues, requiring medical attention, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Hi,

I bought a 24X36 inch picture frame from AC Moore in Secaucus NJ.  The frame is manufactured by Timeless Decor (see timelessframes.com).  It contains a heavy piece of extremely fragile plate glass.  I attempted to use the frame and discovered the hanging mechanism was simply a sawtooth hanger with two small nails.  Since the sawtooth has to be hammered in to the frame, I attempted to remove the sheet of glass.   With hardly any pressure, the glass broke as I tried to remove it from the frame.  I brought the frame back and exchanged it.  On my second try I was able to successfully remove and then reinstall the glass.  Realizing the danger in hanging such a heavy piece of fragile glass, I hung the frame on two anchored screws.  I quickly discovered that the weight of the frame, however, began to pull the sawtooth hanger out of the frame (I took the frame down after about 1 minute and found the nails had already slipped about 25%).  If left for long enough on my wall, I have little doubt that this frame would come crashing to the ground.  I intend to return the frame tomorrow.

The frame is a hazard.  Asking an average consumer to hang a heavy piece of glass with a simple sawtooth hanger is simply insane.  This product needs to be recalled. The manufacturer needs to install pre-tested hanging mechanisms that will not fail.  

The place I wished to hang this is in a high traffic area in my house.  I suspect a gentle bump would have brought this frame crashing down (due to failure of the sawtooth nails) next to the person who bumped into it.  I don't know what would happen to the glass if this should happen (would it shatter?), but I don't intend to find out.  I will not have this product in my home.

Regards,
[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation with potential for injury from broken glass and a falling frame, though no actual injury occurred. The likelihood is high given the described failure of the hanging mechanism and high traffic area.

incident_description:
I have rheumatoid arthritis and have had several surgeries on my left knee. Because of this I need to use a shower
bench to safely take a shower. I was using a Carex Universal Bath Set that I bought about a month earlier. While I
was showering, I leaned a little to reach for something and the bench slipped out from under me. I fell to the floor
and I bruised my back and arm on the edge of the bench. The feet of the bench are rounded, and I believe the
design of the bench caused it to slip. The rounded bottom of the feet is like balancing on balls, a slight shift and it
will roll.

Because of my condition, I cannot get off the floor without help. Fortunately, my sister and her daughter were
visiting and they were able to help me. If they had not been there, I would have had to call 911 for help.

Photos of my bruises are included
justification: The incident resulted in bruises and required assistance to get up, indicating an injury (severity 3). The design flaw in the bench suggests a likely recurrence if not addressed (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
I have 2 and a half year old triplets and purchased 3 toddler pillows from target.  The pillows have Disney pillow case covers that don't zip, rather they fold inside to secure the pillow.  Similar to some sham type pillows where there is no zipper but the fabric is cut out to fold up inside so the pillow does not fall out.

Our kitchen cabinets have window (glass) inserts. The inserts have a pattern of glass pieces that are soldered in place. My wife and I were checked for high serum lead levels. Fortunately they were normal. We discovered the problem just before our grandchildren visited and we prevented their contact with the lead powder. I am a physician and am concerned about such a product being commonplace. 
The manufacturer is in Canada. The builder has built many homes similar to ours on Marco island, Florida.

[REDACTED]
