incident_description: I had washed the deck (using the hose and water) under my Better Homes and Gardens glass top dining table.  About 4 minutes later while I was standing on the deck the glass table top exploded.   It DID NOT break into a million pieces and fall on the ground-  it EXPLODED and sent projectiles of glass up into the air landing up to 21 feet from the table.  I was hit on the neck, arms, legs and feet with pieces of glass hard enough that the skin was ripped open and bleeding.  I had four small pieces of glass sticking out of me.  I was looking at the ground when this happened and glass ended up in my hair.  (if I had been looking up it may have ended up in my eyes)Glass was embedded in the back of the seat cushions.  The glass did not hit the ground and then bounce since I was looking at the ground and well aware of something hitting me before it hit the ground, it EXPLODED!!!   About 6 years ago I purchased 5 of these sets.  4 were by the swimming pool and one was on a covered deck of the house.  Two years ago one by the swimming pool suffered a similar fate however no one was near it when it broke and none of us saw the explosion (we heard it) and again glass was found 20 feet from the table in places that were too high for it to have bounced.   This set was sold by Walmart under the Better Homes and Garden label.  It is "outdoor" wicker dining sets with glass top tables.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries from glass projectiles, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as similar incidents are rare but have happened before under specific conditions.

incident_description:
I purchased a Lane Glider Recliner in 2005. Since I've owned this chair I thought something was wrong with the base. The chair would tip over backwards very easily when in the recline position. It seemed to me the base was too far forward which forced the center of gravity toward the front of the chair when reclining making it very unstable. I have on many occasions tipped over backward and hit my head on the floor. I did telephone Lane in 2006 and was told it must be my problem they have not had any issues with these glider recliners. 

Now the base is lose and falling off. I searched web sites to determine if anyone else had this same tipping over problem. That's when I found the Safety Alert concerning the glider base possibly being installed backwards. I immediately telephoned Lane to report my problem. Their answer was since the chair was made in 2005 it wouldn't fall under this recall. I asked for an explanation of why my glider recliner did exactly what the recall was issued for (tipping over backwards). They had no answer, but said they would look into it and see if there were any issues reported with glider recliners made before 2008. I have heard nothing from Lane.

I am urging the CPSC to pressure Lane to expand their recall to glider recliners made before 2008 and repair a dangerous problem with their glider recliners.
justification: The incident involves repeated tipping over of the chair, resulting in head injuries, but no death is reported.

incident_description:
We bought a leather sofa from Value City Furniture in Cleveland Ohio (model name Madrid black 2 piece sectional) about three months ago. Ever since we had this sofa both me and my wife started getting very itchy skin rashes all over our body. The rashes appeared mainly on parts of our body that would have contact with the sofa. It also started getting more frequent with the summer months with hot weather. We now have marks all over our arms, back and legs. 

We weren't sure what caused this in the beginning and also pest control to have our apartment checked. They found nothing in our apartment.

Finally, I started researching over the internet and found that leather sofas imported from China (which this sofa was) are shipped with anti-fungal agent called DMF which evaporates to the surface during use and causes skin reactions. These products were apparently banned in the European Union since 2009. I was wondering if these products have been reviewed in the US.

Looking back last three months, all the events with our rashes were too coincidental not to be due to the leather sofa. Both me and my wife had the skin reaction right after we got the leather sofa. The frequency increased with warm weather in summer. The rashes are mild in the morning after we come out of bed, stays the same during the afternoon when we are at work and gets worse in the evening when we are back on the sofa watching TV.
justification: The incident describes skin rashes caused by contact with the sofa, indicating an injury but no death.

incident_description:
In August 2009 I purchased 2 sets of Better Homes and Gardens Mika Ridge 3-Piece Bistro Sets at a cost of $650 from Wal-Mart. Each set consists of two rocker-swivel aluminum framed cushioned chairs and a 30" round glass top table. I use the chairs on my raised outdoor deck. They are always moved inside in the fall and winter and still look almost new. 
Two weeks ago, while sitting in one of the chairs on my deck, I leaned slightly sideways to pick up a can of [REDACTED] I was drinking and had set on the deck along side the chair. Without any warning whatsoever, the aluminum frame broke and I fell sideways onto my right shoulder. I am 69 years old. I was pinned between the seat of the chair and the railing of my deck. The arm of the chair was beneath my right side and I was laying on it so could not easily move. My shoulder hurt badly further restricting my efforts. It took five minutes to finally and painfully push myself to a position where I was able to get on my hands and knees and stand up.
After examining the broken chair, I found that the four aluminum supports had broken at the central column. I examined the other chair sitting next to the one that failed. Three of the four supports on that chair were already visibly failing and one already had a very visible crack. The other two chairs get almost no use, mostly staying inside the house. Consequently there is no evidence of failure on those two chairs.
I called the phone number [REDACTED] listed on the literature I received with the Bistro sets as the number I should call if I had problems with the product and spoke to [REDACTED]. 
After several phone calls back an forth, and sending them an email they requested containing my receipt and several photos of the broken and failing chairs, I was told the chairs only had a one year warranty and there was nothing they could do. They further stated that due to some business transaction they were only responsible for claims years 2010 and later. They gave me a number to call to contact the "original" company, Huayue at [REDACTED]. 
I called that number, talked to [REDACTED]. She said the company was out of business but offered to send me 4 new bases but I would have to pay the shipping and handling but I have to wait until Monday before I get the quote for that. She also told me there was a weight limit for the chairs, 250lbs. I do weigh 250lbs. I told her I saw no such warning in any of the information listed before I made the purchase. She said there is no warning because if there was, nobody would buy the chairs. 
Wal-Mart still sells this exact same product but the price is now $399 per set. I looked at the customer reviews on Wal Mart's web site and there was another complaint about the frames breaking after two years of use, as mine did .  I had already submitted a review after I bought the chairs in 2009 so when I tried to submit another review warning potential buyers about the undocumented weight limit and the fact that the frames could collapse without warning, the web site would not permit this because I had already posted a review. If I could not post a warning review, I strongly suspect other people with frame failures were also prevented from do so because they had left a previous post after purchase.

I do not know if this qualifies for further investigation and subsequent recall, but I shudder to think that if the frame had failed when I leaned backwards instead of sideways, I could have suffered a concussion, cracked my skull, or been knocked unconscious. Remember, these things are still being sold every day and there are multiple examples of the exact same failure point.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (hurt shoulder) and potential for more severe harm, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar failures and the product still being sold.

I returned to the Sears store the next day - May 28, 2012 - and was told that they cannot do anything with returns after 9 days. They directed me to look for the set's owner's manual and to call the 800 number listed.

I found the manual and called the number on May 29, 2012 and reached a company called Numark Industries  [ 800-457-4652  ( http://www.numarkcustomerservice.com ) ]. They stated that glass breakage is not covered under any circumstance. I asked if they knew that this was apparently a common occurrence and that what they were selling was a dangerous product. I was again told that glass breakage is not covered under their warranty. I pressed the issue and explained that according to news reports/videos available on-line detailing a class action lawsuit filed against Martha Stewart Living, K-Mart, and other entities - my table looks identical to the ones that were complained about. Again I was told that the glass was not covered, and then they hung up.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries to three individuals due to the spontaneous shattering of a glass table, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of the event and the mention of a class action lawsuit suggesting this is not an isolated incident.

incident_description: We have a tabletop lamp next to our bed (3-way fixture from Target) and had a 14W CFL bulb installed.  The bulb was only in about 2 weeks.  The lamp was on for about 3 hours last night, and when we reached in to turn it off it made a hissing sound then fire came out from the socket base, with flames scorching the inside of the lamp shade and extending about 2-3 inches about the shade's top (about 10" above the socket).  It lasted maybe 4-5 seconds and was then out.  Fortunately, nothing other than the lamp and shade were damaged.  I have also opened an inquiry with UL and have turned the lamp and the bulb over to their investigators at their Northbrook, IL, headquarters.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or significant damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common with proper equipment use.

incident_description:
The owner of a rental home was called to the residence due to an odor of smoke.  The source of the smoke was attributed to the furnace.  

The owner conducted a safety inspection and found that the electrical insulation on wires in the ceiling light fixtures had deteriorated as a result of heat damage.  The insulation was discolored, cracked and decomposed so bare conductors were exposed on the wires connected to the lamp sockets.  The lamps were fitted with the proper sized bulbs and were installed and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Damage was confined to the lamp fixtures.  There were no injuries.  The lamp fuxture was purchased at a Lowe's store during 2010.
justification: The incident involved smoke and damaged electrical insulation but resulted in no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such electrical issues are possible in older fixtures.

incident_description: I was at my work place using a 3-hole punch when it malfunctioned. Thankfully I wearing my reader eye glasses as I was punching pages for a document when the middle piston of the 3-hole punch exploded out of the unit and hit the left lens of my reader eyeglasses, then bounced of the reader glasses and hit my left eye socket between the eye lid and the eye brow. When I recovered from the initial shock and determined that I was not injured I was able to locate the parts of the 3-hole punch that exploded out of the unit. I found a 1- inch metal piston and spring and discovered that the piston sheared and was forcefully ejected by the spring action.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning 3-hole punch that ejected a piston, but no injury occurred as the eyewear protected the individual.

incident_description: We moved into a brand newly built house on 11/01/06.  Each of the three bathrooms has one of these beautiful Estate Medicine mirror bathroom cabinet with top lights.  Well, on May 24, 2012, I opened one of the medicine cabinet mirror door as usually and it popped out hitting me in my forehead and the bridge of my nose before cutting me under my left nostril.  I am bless that I was able to catch this mirror door before it fell to my the tile bathroom floor because that would have been a bigger mess to clean up broken glass while paralyzed from facial pain.  After nursing the knot on my forehead and the bridge of my nose, and the cut under my nose for over a week we tried to figure out how [REDACTED] after using this same door mirror for years that all of a suddenly it decided to just pop out and hit me on three parts of my face.  After we thoroughly examined this mirror, the cabinet it hung on, and the other medine cabinets in the other two bathrooms, my husband and I decided that this incident comes from a manufacturer defeat in the way the hinges were attached to the mirror doors, so we did some web surfing and found that our medicine cabinets was recalled.  Wow, We had no idea that a recall was in effect for these lovely medicine cabinets because as I said, we purchased our house with the medicine mirror door cabinets already installed in the bathrooms.  I am glad that the maker of these medicine mirror door cabinets took the responsibility to recall these medince cabinets and atleast offer free doors to replaced the old doors.  I hope that people would read my experience with these medicine cabinets and take the responsibility of getting rid of these doors because I do not want this to happen to anyone else.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the forehead, nose, and under the nostril, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) due to the manufacturer defect and recall, suggesting a known issue.

incident_description:
On the Sealy box spring there are 4 thin metal corner guards. While walking to my bed I received a laceration to my left toe. After stitches and surgery it healed. 3 months later the same incident happened and I have received stitches again. These corner guards have caused me more trouble and are very dangerous. Regardless of the guard being polished and buffed they are still sharper than a "butterkife", and there is no rounded edge to help protect consumers from this issue. While taking them off the bed I also almost cut my hand, Therefore they are an issue should not be used.
    
 I would advise everyone to remove these guards or avoid buying this specific box spring mattress with the metal corner guards. This will save you any injuries and some hospital visits. Also see a surgeon if this does happen because It cut through some nerves and I cannot feel one side of my toe.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries requiring stitches and surgery, indicating a severity level of 3. The recurrence of the injury suggests a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
We smelled smoke but could not locate it.  Eventually one of the kids saw the smoke.

The light fixture is marked SUN-LITE and bears a mark "IWI UL 1439" and "Made in China".  The fixture has three glass shades. Each glass shade is held up by no more than a friction fit.  I suspect the friction fit failed, pressing the combustible paper onto the bulb.  The paper then ignited, and later the burning paper dropped to the floor.
justification: Smoke was detected and a fire occurred due to a failed light fixture, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Outdoor patio furniture included 6 chairs, glass table and umbrella.  The umbrella was spinning in the wind so my husband went to adjust it.  As he lifted the umbrella from the stand, the wind caught it and tipped it sideways.  The leverage from the umbrella pole tipping caused the table to shatter into my lap.  I sustained minor scratches as did my husband.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (scratches) to both individuals, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is 'possible' (3) as such accidents can occur under windy conditions with outdoor furniture.

incident_description: I was sitting in my garage in my Coleman Max folding chair. The back of the chair where the bars cross broke under my weight. It broke at the point where the screw holds the 2 bars together. The product was tested for up to 400 lbs. I am 330 lbs. I have only had the chair for approximately a year. It is only used for special occasions. I know have neck pain, a headache, and my back is aggravated.
justification: The chair broke under the user's weight, causing neck pain, headache, and aggravated back, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as the chair was used infrequently and within weight limits.

incident_description: We bought a patio table last year from Target store..It was the Bromley large rectangle one..Yesterday morning with no reason,it shattered all over the place..No one was outside at the time,but 20 mins before we had all been sitting around it..I have 4 kids who i am so grateful were not around when it shattered..There was no wind,nothing..it just shattered..There were some larger shards but for the most part,it was just all over everything..This is an incredible safety hazard..Called target and they just passed me off to the manufacturer who of course isnt anwering their phone..STAY AWAY from this table..Luckily we werent injured(except for the sliced finger cleaning it all up)  SO disappointed at this dangerous product
justification: The incident involved a table shattering unexpectedly, causing a minor injury (sliced finger) during cleanup, indicating a moderate severity with an unlikely recurrence.

incident_description:
On April 28, 2012 the consumers grandchildren were playing downstairs in the recreation room. 

After being downstairs for approximately 1.5 hours the light bulb in a lamp had started to give off sparks and smoke. 
The children immediately went to inform there grandfather and he quickly unplugged the unit. After unplugging the unit the sparks and smoke had stopped.

There were no injuries from the incident and the manufacturer had not been contacted.

The BBB was contacted 5/3/2012 and they advised him to contact CPSC to file a report.

 The consumer was concerned that if he were to leave the home and the light would have been on the home may have caught fire.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke from a lamp, but no injuries occurred, and the situation was quickly controlled by unplugging the unit.

incident_description: Glass Table from Ikea suddenly exploded with no cause at 4:30 AM.  The debris from the explosion covered the entire room.  Luckily no one was in the room when it occurred or there would have been major injuries.
justification: The glass table exploded causing significant damage, but no one was injured as the room was unoccupied.

incident_description: A glass top table suddenly exploded without warning during the early hours. It sounded like a gun shot and glass was shattered every where. There potentially could have been injury but luckily no one was. This was very disturbing and very unsafe.
justification: The glass table exploded, causing a disturbance and potential for injury, but no one was hurt.

incident_description:
I have two Dream On Me toddler beds for my twins. The beds that I have are style 624, manufacturing code "ausy," and date of manufacture September 2010. I purchased the beds in or about January 2011. Several months ago I noticed a serious safety issue with one of the beds. There was a piece of sharp, jagged metal sticking out of the frame underneath the mattress in the direction facing where the child would be sleeping. This piece was coming out directly under the bolt that holds the side rail to the frame (the end of the rail that is halfway down the frame, not up at the headboard side). I pulled the piece of metal out with a pair of pliers and found that it was half of a broken nail, and the broken end had worked its way out through the wood of the frame. This piece of nail was approximately 1 inch long. I did contact the company at that time but only could reach someone's voicemail. I left a message but never heard back from anyone from the company. 

Two nights ago (Sunday, May 20, 2012...actually very early AM Monday, May 21) I realized that the same issue was happening on one side of the other bed. Again, I pulled the piece of metal out and again it was a piece of broken nail of the same size. In addition, I found that the second side of the first bed was starting the same issue, with a piece of metal starting to poke through but not all the way through yet. Yesterday, Monday, May 21, 2012 I called the company again to report this issue. My first phone call was answered by a man who listened to my explanation, said he was going to go check on it and put me on hold where I waited listening to silence for 10 minutes (giving him the benefit of the doubt that I was actually still on hold!) and then hung up. I then called back and a woman answered. I explained to her that I had spoken to someone about an issue with one of the products and had been disconnected, and she offered to transfer me to customer service. I was then transferred to the voice mail of someone named [REDACTED] and left a message explaining the whole issue. I heard nothing from her today.
justification: The incident involves a safety issue with sharp metal pieces in toddler beds, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Consumer reports that her friend was sitting in a wooden chair when the arm and leg assembly gacve way and her friend fell to the floor. She hurt her arm. The chair is not repairable. Another chair of the same model had one of it's wood dowels come off.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (hurt arm) and another chair of the same model showed a similar defect, indicating a possible pattern.

incident_description: We purchased a Martha Steward Living Agusta 7 piece Patio Set and after we had it for about 3 weeks the glass table top exploded in millions of tiny pieces.  ( Made a loud noise)  I do not feel this is save especially since we have a Three Year old and an infant in our home.
justification: The glass table top exploded, posing a potential hazard, especially with young children present, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We had a BAYCO Model #: FL-302NPDQ8  heat lamp securely attached to a sturdy frame in a tack room of a barn warming some baby chicks.  AT 8:25 am on 5/5/2012 smoke was seen coming from the barn.  The fire inside the tack room was concentrated in the area where the heat lamp was located.  Emergency services was notified at 8:27 and by the time the first responders arrived (minutes later) the barn was fully involved. and tumbled to the ground minutes after that.  The ONLY electrical component connected at the time was the BAYCO heat lamp.  The heat lamp was approximately 43" off the floor and the chicks were in a box 18" tall.  This set up had been used continuously for the previous 9 days with the box being changed out on day six to prevent drying out and reduce the combustability.  Both the local fire investigator and insurance arson investigator both determined that the fire's point of origin was in the area of the heat lamp.  

The lamp has since been recovered from the ashes and is available for inspection.   Bayco has refused to talk to anyone except an insurance company.

All indicators point to a fault or short in the heat lamp.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a heat lamp, resulting in significant property damage but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Purchased a glass TV stand on 12/26/2009. Since I have had this product the middle shelf explode twice. The first time was about a year ago, and then again on 5/18/2012. We were actually in the room the first time and were gone the second time. It has the tempered glass but shards of glass flew everywhere. Some at least 6 feet away. Thank goodness no one was injured but some one definitely could be. Besides the fact it's a huge mess.
justification: The glass shelf exploded twice, causing a mess but no injuries, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as it happened twice within a few years.

incident_description:
While standing outside on the  side walk of some retail shops the consumer noticed a very  strong perfume chemical odor. The consumer describes the odor as very strong.

While in the retailer she began to experience uncontrollable shaking, cracked mouth, coughing and heart arrhythmias. She asked the employee of the retailer what the strong odor outside her store was and where it could possibly be coming from.

The consumer was advised that there was a candle retailer located about five doors up.  The consumer asked the employee if she could leave out the back door of the store so that she does not continue to expose herself to the odor.

The consumer exited out the rear of the retailer and noticed that the air outside the back of hte store did not have the same perfume chemical odor - that was outside the front of the store. The incident occurred in the late evening; it was cool and crisp with a gentle wind.

The consumer reports that she has a chemical sensitivity and wears a respirator mask. The consumer states that if she is exposed to the right type of chemical it leads to a immediate reaction.

The consumer contacted the mall security where she was advised that it was indeed Yankee Candle.  The store always has a really strong smell.  Employees have to open the doors and air it out because it is so strong.  

The consumer contacted the retailer and asked if there could be something done about the nonstop burning of the candles. The consumer states that the retailer stated I was welcome to express my concerns but "there was nothing they will do about it."

The consumer states that she would like there to be some sort of legislative where candle stores are required to seal the candles, and not be allowed to burn candles in the store, and not have them open exposing the fragrances, and pollute the public air space .

The scent from burning this candle in the store filled the public air space outside the store & down the sidewalk from the store. 

I would also like our government to check the chemicals in these products for safety before they go to market.

Just like second hand smoke, I as a consumer should have the right to go shopping in air that is not polluted with toxic chemicals.  At a minimum, these products need to be sealed and no store should be allowed to burn these candles and pollute the public air we breathe with chemicals - which for me are toxic and dangerous!
justification: The consumer experienced physical symptoms like shaking, coughing, and heart arrhythmias due to chemical exposure, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased a couch from west elm (http://www.westelm.com/products/blake-sofa-f983) approximately 3 months ago. I started having severe skin allergies and after 2 months of constant visits to various doctors, diet/lifestyle alterations, and ineffective treatments, I realized that it is the couch what is causing me, and most recently, my daughter severe hives. This couch is imported and most likely dimethyl fumarate or a similar anti-mold chemical was used. Please be aware that this chemical is so strong that it seeps through clothing and cannot be cleaned off once it is applied to a surface. The extent of my skin damage is so that the skin pigmentation in the areas affected has changed, most likely permanently.
justification: The description reports severe skin allergies and permanent skin damage for both the purchaser and their daughter, indicating injury.

incident_description:
I had a product donated to me by a local foundation which is supposed to keep my little guy with special needs safe while he sleeps. He has several medical issues along with Sensory Processing Disorder that causes him to not be safe due to jumping out of a conventional crib or toddler bed.  It was recommended to me to look at this bed called The Safety  Sleeper and I spoke directly with the owner and designer of the bed, [REDACTED],  about the design and the purpose for this type of bed. She assured me that this bed would work for My child and we discussed his particular issues for safety due to his special needs. She spoke about several loops specially designed for hanging toys and medical equipment so that you could use those things inside the bed for medical uses. She also described two outlets for electrical cording access as needed for any nebulizer use, like what my child uses and needs, and or catheters or other such tubing that might need to be placed inside for special needs according to individual  needs.

I spoke to her several times and finally placed an order in January 2012 using donated funds specifically meant for this particular  enclosed safety bed. She told me the size of the mattress needed for my bed was a standard twin mattress.  Several weeks later I finally received the safety bed which was delivered on Tuesday March 9, 2012.  My son put it together and the next day I bought a standard size twin and he took it and setup the entire bed in my room. 

The first time I used it for an afternoon nap it seemed fine but it was the following night that I put him in the bed and zipped him in. I got up to use the bathroom and checked on him and everything was fine so I went back to bed. At some point I heard a muffled whine or cry from my little guy which prompted me to get up straight away to check on him.  Upon looking into the sleeper I couldn't really see him well at all so I quickly un zipped the net and looked inside to see him face down, lodged in between the mattress and the tent enclosure. He was not making any further sounds at this time, so I grabbed his foot and quickly pulled him out of the sleeper where he seemed somewhat disoriented and wobbly not holding up his head well.  I spent some time talking with him and rubbing him and he finally started to respond to me.

After some time I took him to my bed so that I could keep further watch on him.

I decided to call the consumer protection place to report this very scarey incident especially when I didn't know how long he had been like that and that probably I had just averted him being suffocated in this safety bed.
justification: The child was found face down and lodged between the mattress and tent enclosure, showing signs of disorientation and potential suffocation risk, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased the 30ÃÂ Sonoma Valley Swivel Top Barstools, imported by Intercon Furniture and sold exclusively by Havertys Furniture in February 2010. There has been a recall for these barstools starting in October 2010 with a potential problem involving the bolt length used to attach the barstool seat to the legs, and could cause the barstool seat to unexpectedly dislodge from the leg assembly. I believe this issue is broader. The seat on my barstools started wobbling after about a year of use and should not. We feel this has to do with the way it is bolted to the legs and may eventually be a safety issue also. We are not sure how to fix it or ensure safety. I think you should expand your investigation / recall on these chairs as they may also be an accident waiting to happen. I have contacted Haverty's but they will not help us based on the purchase date.
justification: The incident involves a potential safety issue with barstools wobbling, but no injury or death has been reported yet.

incident_description: Juno Lighting Group IC22 Recessed 6" light fixture arrived defective.  Hidden from view was a wire that got caught between 2 steel components, which scraped off the insulation exposing the hot lead to the metal housing after installed.  When energized sparks flew and the breaker tripped in time to keep the house from burning down.  It was installed by a licensed GC and the defective part was not exposed or accessible during installation, it was only revealed after uninstalling and inspective of parts.
justification: The incident caused sparks and a tripped breaker but no injury or fire, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it required a specific defect hidden during installation.

incident_description:
Caller purchased 3 IKEA Basisk Floor Lamps _ Solid base, skinny pole with glass shade in December 2011. 

Due to pole size it sways very easily.

She keeps one near the wall but states that her children have accidently bumped two of the lamps with the result being that glass shade shattering and falling everywhere.
The first time in January 2012 and the second time in March 2012.

She did not contact the manufacturer the first time but did contact the manufacturer March 4, 2012 for the second incident when she was told that she could bring the lamps back for refund.

Neither of her children were injured but she notes that they could very well have been with the glass falling.

Caller would like to see these lamps recalled
justification: The incident resulted in shattered glass but no injuries, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of the issue suggests a likely occurrence likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
I purchased a size Queen Room Essentials Style bedsheet set from Target. Color blue. Sku 0621806668 from Target recirpt. UPC 490621806684. Make in Pakistan. 50% cotton, 50% poly from recycled PET bottles. Machine Wash , tumble dry.
I unpackaged the items and washed the items as directed on thier own and placed in my dryer on regular/medium heat. After 10-15 minutes we noticed a burning smell throughout the house and noticed smoke emiting from the dryer door. Upon opening we saw smoke in the drum. We realized the smoke was contained to the drum.
After shutting off dryer, unplugging the dryer and removing sheets we saw singe mark on the interior of the dryer drum. The sheets reeked of a burning, melty, chemical smell. We immediately placed the sheets outside. 
We inspected the dryer lines and lint trap, but we do not believe that we found any evidence of smoke or fire there or at the electrical panel of the dryer or our outlet. The smoke and smell were contained to the drum.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was contained to the dryer drum.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to illustrate that her light bulb is a potential fire hazard as the light began a near fire. The consumer stated that the 100 watt incandescent bulb was inserted into a lamp in her living. The consumer saw that the light bulb began to spark and smoke after the bulb was on for 30 minutes. The consumer unplugged the lamp from the wall outlet immediately after. The consumer is unsure if the light bulb is UL listed. 

The consumer stated that the bulb remained intact but the bulb is blacked at the insertion and the insertion of the lamp is also blackened. The consumer feels that the incident was called by the light bulb. The consumer purchased the light in a pack of multiple bulbs. (exact amount unknown) The consumer stated that there was no extensive property damage. The consumer has not tried to put another bulb in that light fixture as of yet. 

The consumer has not called the firm about the incident. The consumer took the product to the retailer today and will help her file a complaint on these incidents. The store has noticed  245 plus complaints on this matter. The consumer did not call her local fire department at the time of the incident and was not injured.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb sparking and smoking, but there was no injury or extensive property damage, and the consumer was not injured.

incident_description:
The person filing the report was the physician on staff that cared for the infant when she was bought into the delivery room.
The seven month young victim was placed in the seat on a elevated surface when she arched her back causing the chair and her to flip backward. The victim weighs 17 pounds and is approximately 20 inches long.
The victim fell out of the seat and  hitting her head on the floor (type of flooring is unknown). The victimÃÂs mother drove her to Little River health Care in Rockdale Texas.
The victim was  given cat scans and diagnosed with having a right temporal bone fracture. The victim had minor bleeding from the ear as a result from her injuries. The victim was then transferred and transported by ambulance to ChildrenÃÂs Medical Center in Temple Texas.
No further information was provided on the victim since she was transferred to another facility.
justification: The victim suffered a right temporal bone fracture and minor bleeding from the ear, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
Compact Fluorescent light (CFL) bulb purchased from Home Depot failing prematurely.  Unit appears to overheat and melt base casing.  Have smelled burned plastic and find bulb failed with base melted.

CFL's were purchased from Home Depot in packs of 6 or 7.

SKU# 292-460
Model: EDXO-14
120V 60 Hz
14W - 230A
V# 42836
justification: The incident involves a CFL bulb overheating and melting, which poses a potential fire hazard but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: The consumer says the mattress had a toxic odor.  Her and her husband both got sick.  They had burning eyes, and throat was bothering her.  She called the manufacturer to find out what was in it.  She was told it was made with polyurethane.  The manufacturer told her that in order to release the gases they should jump on the mattress and roll around.  The consumer's concern is that they claim the order would dissipate.  She feels that this would make it more dangerous.  She complained about it to the retailer and got a refund.  Her husband and her feel that this product should not be sold without a warning label and full disclosure of what its made of.  The manufacturer told her she should pour baking soda on the mattress.
justification: The consumer and her husband experienced burning eyes and throat irritation, indicating physical injury from the toxic odor.

incident_description: This is Menomonee Falls Fire Department.  Had a bedroom, room and contents fire.  Cause was traced down to a electric blanket that was on at the time of the fire.  Then occupant stated she got out of bed and pushed the sheets, regular blanket and electric blanket to the floor off of the bed.  She went to the living room, then stated 12 minutes then  she heard the cat whining from her bedroom.  Opened the door to see fire at foot of her bed by the blankets.  We got the call for a house fire.  First in crew was able to hold it to the bedroom and hall.  Pictures were taken of the origin area and of another electric blanket same brand but bigger size.  We did not collect the remains of the blanket or the controller.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by an electric blanket, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says the socket exploded in flames and started a fire inside the lamp shade with flames about a foot and a half tall.  He says the bulb was on for approximately 30-45 minutes prior to the incident.  The consumer says about a year ago he realized if the three way bulb was on it wouldn't turn on or off so they replaced the 150 watt bulb to a 100 watt bulb. The consumer contacted the manufacturer and left a voice mail today.  He took the lamp outside and poured water on it.  

UPDATE:
Please note:
1) Lamp returned to uttermost 4/17/12 for inspection
2) I contacted Uttermost 4/16/12
3) Bulb lodged in socket and returned to Uttermost, what remains of it
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injury was reported, and such events are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description:
Caller and his disabled wife purchased a Queen sized mattress and box spring set March 25th, 2011.
On April 25th, 2012 caller's wife was sleeping when all of a sudden the mattress gave way and she fell to the floor.
Caller states that the edge of the mattress just "gave way" and acted as a chute forcing her to the floor. Approximately 9 - 10 inches in from the edge is collapsed.
She contacted her husband her took her to the hospital emergency room where she was diagnosed with a slight concussion with contusions to the ribs and she was prescribed muscle relaxers and pain killers.
She is being sent to surgeon for follow up due to her already have back problems to be sure this fall hasn't worsened her condition.
Caller returned to retail store and was informed that "Warranties mean nothing, we don't give money away & neither does the manufacturer"
Caller has not yet contacted the manufacturer but does intend to contact them.
Caller states that he is not asking for his money to be returned, he and his wife would like to have the mattress replaced with a different model at manufacturer/retailer expense.
justification: The incident resulted in a slight concussion and rib contusions, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the specific circumstances of the mattress failure.

incident_description:
Sylvania led light bulb exploded and caught fire.  We were in the room at the time and able to immediately turn the light off and avoid further damage.  Light fixture was scortched black.

Markings on light bulb:

39Pr
E327386
LED8A/DIN/F/827
75 mA 8W L0111CH
120VAC 60 Hz
A19L6A1A03
justification: The LED bulb exploded and caught fire, causing scorching to the fixture, but no injuries were reported and the situation was quickly controlled.

incident_description:
I am concerned with the safety of a twin sized headboard made by Fashion Bed Group in Chicago. 
I bought a twin bed (mattress, box spring, base support etc, and headboard) from Sleepys here on Long Island. The problem is with the headboard - a 'Hamilton Twin' headboard. The fasteners keep falling out. With any slight movement, they just fall out. They're small enough that a child could swallow them, and it's very likely that a child would be the one using a twin bed. 
I noticed it the day I got the bed. It continued to happen with any movement of the headboard. I called Sleepys - they replaced the headboard. But the problem happens with the replacement also! I suspect that it is a design flaw. I wrote to the Fashion Bed Group explaining this, and asking if they had a 'fix' for this problem, but have not heard back from them. Their info is: Fashion Bed Group 5950 W. 51st Street Chicago Illinois 60638 800-825-5233.
I am concerned with the safety of this product - if the fasteners simply fall out, and, as I mentioned, a child swallowing the fastener itself. Hope you can look into this matter. Thank you.
justification: The incident involves a design flaw causing fasteners to fall out, posing a potential choking hazard for children, but no actual injury has been reported.

incident_description:
Caller is Workers Comp Carrier for Nursing Home reporting that Office Depot Desk Chair has broken with injury to worker.
This chair is recalled on release# 12-146

March 19th, 2012 victim was placing a patient's chart back in the rack while seated in office chair when chair broke causing her to fall down or backward injuring her upper and lower portion of her back. 
Victim is from Alabama and has been seeing doctor for medical help and is being considered as a pain management candidate.

She has been diagnosed with L4-5 herniation and annular tear as well non displaced fracture of the distal sacrum.
Repeat tests have been requested.

Caller is requesting reimbursement for salary lost and for personal indemnity, also requesting reimbursement for medical paid due to chair breaking.

incident_description: These counter stools (Belleview Swivel Counter Stools from Ballard Designs) are very top-heavy and easily tip over if you do not center your weight while sitting on them. My 82 year old mother tipped over in one of these shortly after I got them. Luckily I was sitting next to her and caught her, although the stool went over with a crash and damaged my wood floor. I thought it was a one time incident but a stool tipped again yesterday with a 3 year old on it. These stools are extremely heavy and I am lucky it didn't land on top of the child. They are so top heavy that it is even difficult to right them after they have tipped over. The problem is dependent on how a person is positioned in reference to the legs of the stool: if you sit so that your legs are on each side of a leg of the stool, the chair is stable. But if you are sitting so your legs hang in the wide area between any of the stool legs, the stool will easily tip over if you slide forward or even lean your body forward.  Since the seat swivels, you really can't be sure where you are positioned in reference to the legs of the stool.  The diameter of the seat is so large (19") children(or smaller adults) will have a tendency to sit more off center so their legs can hang down.  If they have swiveled to the wrong area, any sudden movement can cause this stool to tip over if the occupant is already off-center.
justification: The incident resulted in no injury but had the potential to cause harm, especially to vulnerable individuals like children and the elderly.
