incident_description: My child has REPEATEDLY fallen out of this chair despite all of the precautions I have taken. He has suffered many bumps on his head although he has not broken or fractured any bones. With the slightest arch of the back or if he leans to far to a side to pick an object off of the ground he is either out of it or STUCK IN IT as it is rolling/flipping/tipping. I cannot believe this product is still on the market.
justification: The child has suffered repeated bumps on the head, indicating injury, and the chair frequently tips or flips, making incidents likely.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed that the task light protective coating cracked at the transformer exposing the cooper wires. 

The firm was contacted and was advised that the 90 day warranty had a expired. However since she showed a great concern about their product they would be willing to mail a new light out. 

She is responsible to mail the facility light in and pay for the shipping for both hers and the new one.

The consumer estimates using the light for  12 days or more day for the almost two years that she has had it.
justification: The protective coating cracked, exposing wires, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I purchased clip-on LED lamp Model F3044-AC-02 at a Lowes store in Hadley Massachusetts about 6 months ago. In normal use the power cord broke off of the lamp where it enters the lamp body, exposing the uninsulated and electrified wire inside.

Upon further inspection I see that the lamp cord has an incredibly poor design. The cord makes a soldered transition to a different type of wire at the exact point where it is expected to flex the most, and that solder joint was simply concealed beneath short lengths of heat shrink insulation. This lamp design is very likely to cause a fire or electrocute someone.
justification: The incident involved a broken power cord exposing electrified wires, posing a risk of electrocution or fire, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Opened new air bed and installed batteries into built-in air pump. It could only partially fill up the bed. Got 4 new D batteries, and the same thing happened. After 10-15 minutes of waiting for the bed to fill up, I touched the battery compartment and it got very hot. Potential to burn hands and create a fire hazard. After cooling down, batteries could not be removed, since something must have melted inside the compartment.
justification: The incident involved a potential burn hazard and fire risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We purchased an expensive Martha Stewart Lazy Susan Glass Patio table and the glass shattered into a billion pieces while sitting on our deck.  Nothing hit the top.    The lazy susan piece was intact.  I have tried to find a replacement glass through them but am now seeing that this is happening to others.
justification: The glass shattered without any impact or injury, indicating an incident with no harm but potential for concern given reports of similar occurrences.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the seat and back of the children's chair are made from nylon mesh and are attached with staples. After several uses the staples break and are exposed which caused the staples to lacerate his 3 year old child's leg (not sure which one).  No medical attention was needed. First aid was administered at home.

The consumer contacted the retailer in 2011 and was advised that he could not return the product.

The consumer feels that these chairs are a safety hazard for children and should be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration to a child's leg, which required first aid but no medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of the issue with the staples breaking after several uses.

incident_description:
LED night light bulbs, after about a year or more, easily separated from their base with the minimum of turning effort.  One bulb was in use in my garage for approximately a year and another was unused but stored in the garage.  It appears the plastic dried out or became brittle where the bulb meets the base over a period of time.  

See picture.

If the separation occurs while the bulb is still screwed into a night light fixture and power is on, there is a risk of an electrical shock, sparks or fire.
justification: The incident describes a potential risk of electrical shock, sparks, or fire, but no actual injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: I replaced a halogen bulb in the light fixture on my ceiling fan over 3 months ago. I used the Feit Electric Halogen bulb. The bulb says it doesn't have to be replaced for 2000 hours.  A couple of days ago, we were in the kitchen eating lunch. I heard an explosion come from the spare bedroom. When I went to see what had happen, I found the halogen bulb had exploded, it shattered the glass that surrounds the bulb. The pieces had flown all over the room. The drippings from the bulb melted into the carpet. I tried calling the company that made the bulb to see why this happen. My grand kids play in this room all the time. If they had been in there, they would have been showered with glass and burnt from the bulb. The company asked me how I replaced the bulb. I told them by hand. The bulb has two prongs that slip into the electrical fixture. There is no other way to change the bulb. The lady from the company wanted to send me a replacement bulb. She told me I shouldn't have changed it by hand. How else do you change a bulb? I asked an electrician the same question and he said I changed the bulb correctly. I was so frustrated with the company, I just hung up. What if it had injured a child? The company didn't seem interested in finding out what caused the bulb to explode. I gave them the UPC Code because I happen to keep the package in case I needed to replace a bulb again. I'm still using the fan, but I wouldn't dare turn the light on again. I'm going to replace the fan with regular lighting as soon as I can buy one.
justification: The bulb exploded, causing potential harm, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the product's behavior.

incident_description: The consumer says that at 9 months old her baby was found with lead at a level 3.3 in his blood.  Her home was tested for lead by a lead program in her community.  The only items that had lead in the home was the furniture.  The consumer says she contacted the retailer by phone in December.  They told her they may offer a reimbursement of the product.  She was also told by the manufacturer that she was making all of this up.  She then sent copies of all her reports and the proof that she purchased the furniture.
justification: The baby had lead in his blood, indicating injury, but the likelihood is unlikely as it's a specific case linked to furniture.

incident_description:
I put my two year old in his crib for a nap ten minutes later I heard him crying in distress well when I  walked in the room to see what was the matter, his fitted sheet,the elastic part and sheet was twisted around his neck and over his head and wrapped around his arm tight but not tight enough to choke
him but still tight enough that I had a little difficulty unwrapping it.
justification: The child was in distress with the sheet twisted around his neck and arm, indicating a potential for injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: The consumer says that she was inside her home when she heard a loud boom when she noticed the glass top exploded.  She contacted the retailer who told her they would contact the mfr.  Also, she saw a website (consumeraffairs.com) of other reports similar to the incident she has.  She says that the reports are all of the same manufacturer.  Their were 117 pages of reports on the website.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded glass top) with no reported injury, and multiple similar reports suggest a likely occurrence.

incident_description: I have a lamp on an end table that is on a timer and comes on prior to me coming home after work. When I came home a couple of weeks ago, I noticed that the litght was not on and assumed it had burned out. But as I came into the kitchen (which is open to my den) I noticed something on the counter.  When I walked over to it, I noticed it was the top of the screwy 3 wayk Chinese light bulb I had in my lamp. When I tgo another light on, I noticed glass as gar as 6 feet away from the lamp, small pieces.  the end table was covered and it was covering about half of 2 couches that we sit on most of the time.  I had to vacuum it all up. The end table also had a white powder all over it that I could not vacuum, but had to get a damp cloth and wipe it up. I am glad no was sittig on the couches when this bulb, as I understand, emploded because it sure would have hurt them..I had another of these bulbs do the same thing when they first came out, but I did not think too much of it then, I guess. I have grandchildren and if they had been there I'm sure it would have gotten in their  eyes. I still have the base to the bulb and the numbers on are E137657 3G01 FCC ID: KQP09. It is a Sylvania 3 way made in Taiwan.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb exploding, causing glass and powder to spread, but no injuries occurred.

incident_description:
The lamp was turned off but plugged in. I set a ball chain necklace on the base of the lamp that
happened to connect to two metal telescoping parts of the lamp. It had evidently completed
some sort of circuit because the metal super-heated and the plastic base started smoking (really
noxious brown-black smoke) and started to catch fire. After I unplugged the lamp, removed the
superheated metal, and patted out the base of the lamp I noticed the part of the ball chain
necklace I had set on the lamp was still blazing hot and the base of the lamp had burned into my
bedside table and the ball chain had burned an impression into the base of the lamp.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard and property damage but no reported injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Simmons Matira Plush Firm queen-sized mattress and a Simmons Grace Bay Plush firm twin-sized mattress from Sears that were finally delivered on October 20, 2011.  The queen and twin mattresses were manufactured by Simmons in Charlotte, NC on 10/17/11 and 9/10/11, respectively.

The pungent odor from the mattresses was severe and overpowering, so we aired them for a week in a closed room running a fan on and leaving the windows open.   Over the course of the next many months, my child and I began to have strange health symptoms.  I did not make the bed connection until symptoms improved when we stayed elsewhere for vacation and one of my work trip'sÃÂ.and especially when I laid in my childÃÂs bed. 

My symptoms:  insomnia and extreme sweating at night; mild coughing.  I am an exceptionally healthy and athletic person with no serious stress in my life.  I have never had any symptoms like this before and typically sleep 8 hours straight.  On this new bed, I would wake up wide awake after roughly 3 hours of sleep.  Some nights the sweating was so severe it seemed like I had run a marathon and my body odor was terrible.  I do not have any body odor issues that I know of.

5 year oldÃÂs symptoms:  chronic cough (dry cough every minute) that forced me in March to take her to the doctor.  My child has NEVER been to a doctor for any illness ÃÂ extremely health.  The symptoms are pointing to asthma or some environmental irritant.

A few weeks ago, when I laid on my childÃÂs bed for a night time story, after about 20 minutes, I began to violently dry hack as though I had an allergy (I have ZERO allergies).  I had never laid on her bed for any length of time before this.  Then, more recently, I laid in the twin bed again and after 30 minutes, my throat began to tighten up.  Later that night, I had an ÃÂa-ha moment.ÃÂ  After rethinking what could be causing my childÃÂs potential asthma conditions, I realized the beds could be the culprit.  

So, we slept on an old queen futon in the house in another room and the VERY next day, my childÃÂs coughing decreased by more than 90%.  This first time no severe coughing in MONTHS.  I am so relieved to see her coughing disappear and now understand why her coughing decreased considerably after she stayed at a friendÃÂs house.  I am now able to sleep through the night in the same house without waking at all and without sweating.  When I slept back on the queen bed, my symptoms returned.  

These mattresses are toxic, dangerous, and clearly unsafe.  I am having them removed immediately.  I am hoping that the CPSC will be able to test the fumes emanating from these two beds ÃÂ they are clearly unhealthy.

More than anything, what concerns me most is the thousands of people who unknowingly sleep on these beds and might never know that newer health problems are caused by the very product that they sleep on 7-9 hours a night.  It took us a while to connect the dots to then prove the source of the health problems.   I am hoping, more than anything, that the safety of these beds, as well as other beds, get more carefully tested to determine the volume and toxicity of the offgassing that occurs.  Also, I wonder if any entity has considered how much these products contaminate a home that is not ventilated, especially during the winter.  

We need better testing and better protection.  When we discovered that these beds were the cause of our health problems, I did some research on the internet and was shocked to see reams and reams of postings by people with all sorts of terrible symptoms caused by their new beds.  Our government should do more to ensure public safety.  There needs to be more comprehensive testing by our government or an independent entity to measure the toxic levels of offgassing over at least an 8-hour period (and prolonged periods) so that toxicologists and epidemiologists can evaluate the full impact on human health.
justification: The incident describes health symptoms including insomnia, extreme sweating, and chronic cough in both an adult and a child, indicating injury due to toxic mattress offgassing.

incident_description:
I purchased 4 barstools from the Centennial IKEA in September.  One of the stools appeared to have some warping of the wood, but I assumed that it was cosmetic in nature and kept the stool.  4 months later, stool became very unsteady and when I attempt to tighten the bolts I can hear the wood splintering.  Due to the unsteady nature of this stool, we have has several near falls and have now removed it from our kitchen.  
I believe that the stool is defective stemming from the manufacture of the stool and using inferior or damaged wood.
justification: The stool's defect led to near falls but no actual injuries, classifying it as an incident without injury.

incident_description: My three-year-old son was at my sister's house and climbed into an empty laundry hamper.  The design of the laundry hamper and my son's height are such that his weight in the cloth bag forced the top of the hamper that consists of two parallel wood rods to snap shut around his neck.  He was unable to breathe or even make noise.  Luckily, his six-year-old brother and five-year-old cousin were in the room and were able to call for an adult to help.  The hamper had to be fully lifted out of the corner where it stood in between a dresser and toy chest in order to get him out - not easy to do.  He did not require medical care as he was extracted very quickly, but I am deeply concerned that this particular design that several manufacturers produce could be lethal for other children.
justification: The child was unharmed but the incident could have been lethal, indicating a serious risk with the hamper's design.

incident_description:
After sleeping on the mattress on the third night the consumer noticed that mattress had a very pungent chemical odor. She began to experience symptoms of fatigue, cold/allergy like symptoms, itchy hands, and minor hip pain.

Around 2/10/2012 the consumer decided to open the windows in the room with a fan inside. She closed the door and sealed the bottom so no air could get in. She tried that method for two days.

 Around 2/11/2012  while sleeping in the bed the consumerÃÂs husband began to feel numb on his left side and  experienced swelling  on that side as well.

On 2/13/2012 the consumer and her husband decided to sleep in another room in the home on another mattress. She indicated that they both feel better. 

She contacted the retailer on 2/13/2012 and was advised that she would have to hold on to the mattress for thirty days before she could exchange it.

The consumer indicated that she would try to air the mattress out again on 2/14/2012. She did not indicate if she would discontinue the use of the mattress. 

She or her husband didnÃÂt not seek any medical attention but she indicated that  she would if her symptoms do not clear up within 24 hours.

She does not plan on contacting the firm.  Consumer ADDED:  Saw a Serta Response to a consumer, which was not favorable to consumer.   America's Mattress Store removed mattress Feb 16th 2012.  Was still lingering odor in house for days after removal.  Had severe back pain and numbness on left arm and leg after sleeping on mattress also developed cough and cold symptoms. Other Victim developed upper respiratory problems, lost sense of smell.  Saw Dr. at Urgent Care.  Received Prednisone for allergic reaction.  I no longer have mattress so there is no pictures, I found hundreds of illness complaints about these memory foam mattresses.  I have printed over 50 pages.
justification: The consumer and her husband experienced physical symptoms including fatigue, numbness, and allergic reactions, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) given the described symptoms and the need for medical attention.

incident_description:
The consumer set the temperature at 120-124 degrees  for approximately an hour. The heating pad is in a cotton flannel cover and she placed a towel on it to sit on. Within a  matter of minutes the consumer noticed that the heating pad got extremely hot.

The consumer unplugged  the heating pad and removed the cotton flannel cover and noticed that there were scorch marking on it. When she examined the heating pad and the cover that was stitched on it she noticed an exposed pink wire. There was also scorch markings around the wire.

On 3/8/2012 the firm was contacted and the consumer was advised that there was no longer a warranty for her model. The consumer indicated that they were not willing to offer any other assistance.

The consumer stated that she has intermittently used the heating pad since she saw the scorch markings on it. As of 3/8/12 she stated that she will discontinue the use of it.

The consumer indicated that the heating pad poses as a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved scorch marks and exposed wiring but no injury was reported, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with potential for property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his small table lamp caught fire Wednesday February 29 2012. The consumer stated that the product might have been for about 8-10 hours before the lamp began to catch fire. The consumerÃÂs wife was standing four feet from the product. She put out the fire by unplugging the lamp and fire burned itself.  The consumer stated that the product did not cause any injury or extensive property damage. 

The consumer did not find it necessary to call the fire department or his home insurance company. The consumer mentioned that the product is all burned and unusable. The product sustained the most damage. The consumer called the retailer today and advised that he should contact the firm. The consumer has not called the firm.  The UL number is E211937.
justification: The lamp caught fire but was quickly extinguished without injury or extensive property damage.

incident_description:
The consumer was using the heating pad on her feet  in bed for 15 minutes when it began to smoke. 

She immediately jumped up to unplug the heating pad from the wall outlet and threw it onto a tile floor in the bathroom.  The consumer noticed that there were holes burned into heating pad in which she was able to see the flames contained inside. 

She used a pillow to put the fire out The heating pad was used on top of the comforter and  burned through cotton sheets and a king size mattress. 

She contacted the firm on 2/20/2012 and  they sent back and paid postage envelope for her to send back in the heating pad. She indicated that they also offered to send out a replacement electric pad. She declined and indicated that she would hold onto the heating pad.

The consumer indicated that she received a minor burn to the heel of her foot and she did not seek any medical attention.
justification: The consumer received a minor burn but did not seek medical attention, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident involved a heating pad catching fire, which is a rare occurrence.

incident_description:
In January 2012 I purchased the Printer's desk from Pottery Barn. I noticed right away that something was volatilizing off of the desk. The bedroom where the desk is located had such a strong odor that we could no longer use the room.  I tried opening windows, baking soda in the drawers, air filters in the room, and even putting house plants in the room to filter the air.  I love the desk size and design and really hoped the odor would dissipate  

Last Sun I could not avoid working at the computer on this desk any longer. I spent 45 min working on taxes. In that time my throat started to ache, my eyes started to burn and even my face stared to burn. After this I called Pottery Barn and demanded they take thy desk back. They agreed and said I would be contacted on Monday. I have not yet heard from them. 

I am a PhD Organic chemist. I have worked in college and industrial labs for many years and have never had such an acute reaction to a chemical. It is clear that the coating or resin is not adequately cured and VOCs are being released.  I am really afraid to find out what the voc's are. 

I just want this desk out of my house before we really get sick.  Please warn others to be ware of this issue. 

Thank you.
justification: The incident caused throat ache, eye and face burning, indicating injury from VOC exposure.

incident_description:
On Wed March 1st,  I sat down to read e-mail and lit a Yankee Candle that had a stained glass shade option attached to it.
After some length of time (30-45 minutes) the shade shattered in a loud pop, once the adrenalin subsided, I noticed my right eye was burning.
I proceeded to flush out my eye and cleared a 1/4 inch long piece of glass from my eye.
After several days, I had my eye looked at by a Dr. due to continued irritation. Fortunately there was no sign of additional glass or deep cuts.
After the incident, I [REDACTED] the incident to see if there were any other incidents reported and sure enough, minus the eye injury, it seems to happen quite a bit.
My injury could have been more serious and it is probably only a matter of time before some little kid sitting by one on Christmas Eve looses an eye
justification: The incident resulted in an eye injury requiring medical attention, and similar incidents are reported to happen frequently, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: Delta Soho 5 drawer chest does not have any type of support mechanism for its drawers!  I was standing in front of the chest going through the contents of the top drawer, my toddler playing around my legs.  All of a sudden the drawer and its contents fell through!  This top drawer was holding keepsakes that my wife stored up there including but not limited to albums, silver spoons, and glass decor.  The glass decor shattered!  I barely caught it with my body and shielded my son from what could have been a disaster.  I then examined the drawer and realized there was no support on any of the drawers!!!  NOTHING was holding it up except a tiny 1/4 inch indent on the side.  NOTHING supporting the center!  I couldn't believe what I was seeing!!  This item is a deadly accident waiting to happen.  Had my toddler yanked at the drawer when I wasn't there he would be DEAD!!!  I glued the bottom to the indent but then my wife had a similar incident and scraped her arm trying to capture it.  My wife contacted Delta Enterprise  but to no avail.  They do not have anything to repair it or anything to replace it with!  This item needs to be RECALLED!  And the manufacturer needs to be held responsible for putting our kids in danger!  My wife and I are trying to contact other owners to form a joint law suit.  PLEASE HELP and recall this item!!!
justification: The incident resulted in injury (scraped arm) and potential for severe harm (death to toddler), with a high likelihood of recurrence due to the faulty design.

incident_description: I purchased a Wilson & Fisher White Cast Bistro Set Item # XG-1015-23 from the Big Lots store in Colorado Springs. I assembled the pieces per manufacturer directions.  I sat on the chair.  I experienced castastrophic failure of the chair.  Two legs broke away from the seat and I fell on the floor.  It appears the seat itself failed, as the legs were still bolted to the rim of the seat.
justification: The chair's catastrophic failure caused a fall, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased the Guidecraft Multipurpose 24" storage units with red shade and the latch that turns to lock it has broken off all but one of the cabinets.  I called and they sent me replacement latches and they have also broken off.  This leaves a metal piece sticking out that the children could hurt themselves on.
justification: The broken latches pose a potential injury risk to children due to exposed metal pieces, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: Since purchasing our tempurpedic bed 5 years ago, within 2 months of sleeping on it, I started having respiratory, ear, sinus and allergy problems and severe sweating. I would wake up every night with an itch in my throat and eyes which would cause me to wake up several times a night and cough uncontrollably. I was constantly clearing my throat through out the day, and my ears have been congested and ringing every day for 5 years. Every year seemed to get worse and the beginning of 2011 everything became severely worse. I started seeing an allergist in the summer of 2011 and was told to stop sleeping on the tempurpedic bed after I was tested. I was told they are made with harsh chemicals that release toxins and gases. After just the first couple of nights, I was sleeping through the night. It has been over 3 weeks now and all my symptoms are improving dramatically. My doctor told me to do some reading on the memory foam to find out more information. I never imagined this would be causing my health issues until I stopped sleeping on the bed, found out what these mattresses are made of, and all the other people who have went through similar problems from sleeping on memory foam.
justification: The incident describes severe respiratory, ear, sinus, and allergy problems caused by the mattress, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: An office chair that I own began wobbling on its' mounting stem and I fell on the floor. The chair can no longer support anyone sitting on it.
justification: The incident involved a fall due to a faulty chair, which could cause injury, but the description does not mention any actual injury.

incident_description:
I have three table lamps in my living room all of which contained GE Reveal Halogen 50-100-150 bulbs model #71367. They were approximately 1 month old, purchased from Walmart. Out of nowhere a bulb in one of the lamps exploded like a bomb. Luckily everybody that was home at the time was in the dining room and not in the living room. The scariest part of this ordeal was not the explosion itself but when we started cleaning we had found that the inner halogen bulb pieces were so hot and flew with such force that they burned multiple holes in the floor, couch, lamp shade, throw pillows, blankets, my babies play mat and even the wooden top of the end table that the lamp was sitting on. I have two small children, one is an infant that has a play mat beside the end table for her to play. This play mat got multiple holes melted through it, which imbedded the glass in it. Had she been on it she would have been burned or worse blinded by these burning hot shards of glass.
   I had some extra bulbs in the basement and upon examining the boxes after this incident, GE states on the back, ÃÂPressurized lampÃÂunexpected rupture may cause injury, fire, or property damage.ÃÂ This is totally ridiculous, itÃÂs a light bulb, people sit around these things everyday. They shouldnÃÂt have the potential for this kind of injury; this is not acceptable. I am returning these to Walmart, I also documented the damage the best I could with my camera.
justification: The incident involved property damage and potential for serious injury, but no actual injuries occurred. The likelihood is low as it was an isolated event with specific conditions.

incident_description:
I installed a new ELCO ET547 track lighting head on an existing section of track. When I turned the sestion of track on at the dimmer switch, there was a loud pop and puff of smoke from the dimmer and the dimmer was destroyed. I removed the track head and confirmed that the bulb that the bulb was compatible with the track and a working bulb and tested the track head on another section of track that had a standard light switch. When I turned the switch on, the circuit breaker protecting that circuit immediately tripped.

The track head is obviously defective and is a fire hazard.
justification: The incident involved a defective track head causing a loud pop, smoke, and a destroyed dimmer, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: On September 25, 2010 I purchased a package of two Westinghouse 60w light bulbs from an Ace Hardware store here in Scottsdale, AZ. The Item No. is 03793. I installed the bulbs in the outdoor fixtures on either side of our garage door. Ten days ago, one of them burned out and I reached in from below to remove the bulb, thinking I would take it to the store to use as a sample when buying a replacement bulb. The glass portion came out in my hand while the metal socket remained. I decided to unscrew the working bulb since I thought that would make a better sample, and again the glass portion came loose from the socket, with only a thin wire connecting the two parts of the bulb. I did not force either bulb or give them a hard twist--the bulbs came apart with just a gentle touch. Perhaps these bulbs are not designed for the hot summers here, although you can see the bulbs were in use for only one summer so that is no excuse. I believe these bulbs are a safety hazard so I wanted to report them. The Ace store still carries the same bulbs. Please let me know if you need additional information. I will save the bulbs for awhile.
justification: The incident describes bulbs breaking easily but no injury occurred, indicating a minor safety hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to report that his bed is unsafe as he has impressions of the bed on his person from the bed when he wakes in the morning. The imprints are in the shape of a spring on his bed. The mattress is a coiled full sized mattress. The consumer has owned this bed since November of 2008. The consumer suffers from preexisting nerve damage and his right arm and shoulder go numb from sleeping on this bed.

 The consumer stated that lately he is experiencing the same problems in his leg. The consumer called the retailer about the issue in July of 2011. The retailer agreed to send a person to inspect the mattress and the retailer stated that the mattress is perfectly and will not exchange the mattress. The consumer has not called the manufacturer. The consumer has filed a complaint with the CPO in DE and the FTC. The consumer stated that the impressions are not immediate and happen gradually over the course of one night's sleep.
justification: The consumer reports numbness in arm, shoulder, and leg due to the mattress, indicating injury.

incident_description: In the last two months (approx) two light bulbs melted on the ends. Consumer has a plastic cover on the bulbs.
justification: Melted light bulbs with plastic covers indicate a potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I bought a bed for my 8 year old daughter through Art Van Furniture in Warren Michigan. The bed was made by Legacy Classic Furniture and was delivered on March 8, 2012. The next day my three kids and a friend were playing underneath the bed. The kids evidently pushed up on the mattress and the bed collapsed on them. The cause of the collapse was due to the design of the bed. The boards that connect the headboard and the footboard simply clip into position and depend on the weight of the mattress to hold everything together. There are no screws or safety catches to prevent the bed from collapsing if the mattress is lifted up from underneath. I understand that a bed is not a play structure, but kids are kids and love to climb underneath things. When they pushed up on the mattress, the footboard became disconnected from the bed and the wooden frame snapped off of the headboard and fell onto the children. Although the kids were unharmed, they were very frightened.

I looked at our other beds in the house and saw that one of them used the same type of clip-in construction, but added screw-on angle brackets in each corner to prevent this problem. Our other child bed has the sideboards screwed on which also prevent this problem. I do not understand how such an inherently dangerous design can be sold when the problem can be easily and inexpensively solved by adding simple corner brackets or retaining clips. I took pictures of the collapsed bed if you need them. Thank you for your time. [REDACTED]
I also sent this to another section of your website as I did not see this area to report the problem.
justification: The bed collapsed on the children, but no injuries were reported, only fright.

incident_description:
After lighting a candle for approximately a half an hour she heard a crack. She noticed that the glass candle holder cracked. The consumer noticed that the wick is formed on the side of the candle instead of the center of it.

The consumer indicated that this is the third failure that she has experience with the same brand candles.  The failure has occurred week apart from each other in 2/2012.

She contacted the retailer the week 2/20/2012 and bought the hazard to their attention. The consumer indicated that the retailer only offered to replace the candle.

The consumer has not contacted the  firm and does not plan on contacting them. The consumer stated that the candle could pose as a fire hazard.

incident_description:

I didn't realize what had happened until I re-entered the house, approximately 5 minutes later. The consumer stated that the bulb did not break and did remain intact but the metal base did get destroyed in the process. The base of the bulb is blackened and burned. 

The consumer stated that no one was injured by the product. The consumer feels that the bulb was the cause and not the light fixture. The consumer stated that this incident may have been caused by the transformer of the light bulb. The consumer has not had this problem before with these type of light bulbs. 

The consumer is not sure how long the light bulb has been in the light fixture. The consumer believes he bought the light bulb in a single packet. The light bulb did damage his light fixture and the socket had to be repaired. incident_description:
Directed by [REDACTED]  Television Station to contact CPSC and report VOC's 

Caller purchased a full size memory mattress in December 2011 because she was having surgery in January 2012 and she wanted a comfortable sleeping area for recovery.
The mattress was delivered to her home January 9th, 2012.

She came home for recovery January 9, 2012 and began using the mattress.

The first night she didn't notice problems but she attributes that to possible post surgery general anesthesia recovery.

The second night she noticed odor compared to nothing she had smelled before this time, she began noticing the same odor but a bit stronger (she believes this may have been due to general anesthesia wearing off or possible off gassing from the mattress) her throat was beginning to become sore, she had a headache that had no relationship to her physical procedure recovery.

These first two nights she was on the mattress most of the day and night due to being bedridden.

The third night as she was sleeping on the mattress she had to have it moved away from her by the middle of the night because the odor or whatever was causing the odor coming from the mattress was increasing the headache and sore throat symptoms.

Due to the conditions with this mattress she had to switch to an full inflatable bed to recover from surgery.

She had to have bedding used on foam mattress washed repeatedly before she had all the odor out of it.

Since she has switched out of her new mattress and into the inflatable bed she has had no sore throat and no headaches.

Caller would like to have this mattress investigated and possibly recalled.

She contacted the retailer within the week of January 12th, 2012 and was referred to the manufacturer.

She contacted the manufacturer January 2012 (she doesn't remember which date)

She faxed claim form January 21, 2012, she hasn't been given a claim form number at this date.
justification: The caller experienced headaches and a sore throat due to the mattress odor, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as similar incidents are not uncommon with new mattresses.

incident_description:
A "Cartwright" medicine cabinet manufactured in China for Restoration Hardware fell on my wife.  It appears that the mounting bracket is flimsy.  Restoration Hardware repleaced the cabinet wityh the exact same model, but we noticed that the mouting bracket design had changed.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a new leather sofa and love seat which has a noxious chemical odor that is causing my eyes to burn, making me nauseous, irritating my sinuses and giving me headaches.  This odor is not a natural, earthy leather smell.  It is a toxic, chemical smell similar to glue, paint, or varnish and it permeates and transfers onto anything in contact with the furniture such as clothing, pillows or blankets.  I am working with the retailer, Ashley Furniture, to remove the furniture from my home.  The Furniture Series is Axiom Walnut and the Model # is 4200035 and 4200038.  I am very concerned about the health consequences of exposure to this chemical smell.  I am also concerned for other consumers who may not be so wise.  How can a consumer be sure the products they purchase are free of harmful chemicals?  Is there some way to test this odor?
Thank  you, [REDACTED]
justification: The description indicates physical symptoms (eye burning, nausea, headaches) caused by exposure to toxic chemicals, which qualifies as injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents are not uncommon with chemical off-gassing from new furniture.

incident_description: The back of the chair suddenly gave way and I fell back over the chair and on the now separated back of the chair. The bolts holding in sheared off entirely in the holes

WHILE IN USE ABOUT 1 MONTH AGO I COULD SMELL SOMETHING BURNING AND SOON AFTER A LITTLE SMOKE, AND THEN REALIZED WHAT IT WAS.  I UNPLUGGED IT BUT THEN NOTICED THE CONTROLLER WAS MELTED.  I TRIED TO CONTACT THE COMPANY DIRECTLY, BUT THEY ARE IGNORING ME.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and a melted controller, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: Product ordered from Amazon.com.: "SE Table Magnifier Lamp - 5X - Fluorescent Light (White)" Sold by: Micro-Tools.  I received the product Feb. 29, 2012.  Product packaging box says:  "LJJ Liang Jing Jing The Lamp of Illumintion (sic) Magnifying Glass.  139   Made P.R.C."  UPC # B000X7AHEY  I plugged lamp into socket and turned on the switch.  The fluorescent light flickered momentarily, then went out.  I touched switch to try it again, but when I touched the switch, I heard a "poof" sound, saw a small cloud of smoke discharge, and immediately smelled a burnt electrical smell.  I then immediately unplugged the lamp from the socket.  Definitely defective!  Truly unsafe!  In my opinion, a piece of junk.  No injury or harm took place to me or my surroundings.  However, I wonder the result if it had been handled by a child, or to have continued to have been left plugged in. incident_description: Harbor Breeze ceiling fan light kit fitter model CS42WW5C malfunctioned when I turned on the lights.  One of the three light sockets exploded.  The light bulb and the metal light socket threads from the light kit fitter burst out of the unit during a flash electrical fire.  The molten metal from the bulb and socket singed the carpet where it landed, but the fire did not spread.  The light kit fitter was permanently damaged.  Soot was left on the inside glass of the ceiling fan light fixture.  No one was hurt.  The Litex fan company agreed to send the consumer a new light kit fitter as a "one time courtesy."  The ceiling fan and included light kit had been used under normal household conditions for approximately one to two years.
justification: The incident involved an electrical fire and damage to property, but no injuries were reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) given the specific malfunction described and the company's response as a 'one time courtesy.'

incident_description: Compact fluorescent bulb malfunctioned.  Heard an electrical noise coming from one of rooms.  Sounded like a sizzle.  Saw a small flash from the room and then smelt a very distinct electrical burning smell.  Very disturbing sound and smell and the brown scorch marks on the base of the bulb indicate this is an unsafe product.  It didn't last anywhere near the rated life either.  CPSC should do a complete investigation on this product.  The internet (e.g., [REDACTED], CPSC) is riddled with reports of these bulbs malfunctioning and catching fire.
justification: The incident involved a bulb malfunction with electrical noise, a flash, and burning smell, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
I want to make you aware of a very serious safety concern involving HALO SLEEP SACKS for infants that recently occurred with my 8 month old daughter.  The Halo Sleep Sack is a wearable blanket designed for babies to wear in their cribs to prevent SIDS (Sudden Infant Death Syndrome).  The Halo Sleep Sack has a tag that is attached to the back.  My daughter managed to pull it off while she was in her crib for her nap and then put it in her mouth.  By the time I got up to her room, the entire tag was lodged in her throat.  Thank god she made some noise and I went up to check on her and saw that she was gagging.  The tag was in the back of her throat, halfway down her airway.  I pulled it out and she was alright, but I shutter to think what might have happened if the tag had gotten into her mouth earlier in her nap and I had not gone upstairs to check on her.  She could have choked to death.

When you are dealing with products that are designed for infants to sleep in, knowing they will be unattended while in their cribs, anything that could be a potential safety hazard should be removed.  I have three kids and have used the halo sleep sack with all three, and nothing like this ever occurred before, so I never even thought twice about cutting off the tags.  However, I would highly recommend that Halo go "tagless" and instead simply print a label on the back of the sleep sack itself.  I would hate to hear of any baby suffocating or choking on a tag they managed to dislodge while in their crib when their parents believe they are sleeping.

Thank you for your attention
justification: The infant was unharmed but could have choked to death, indicating a high potential for severe injury or death.

incident_description:
I was sitting in my kitchen at the table on Sunday afternoon, the light overhead was on. I started smelling a terrible burning odor.Looked up and smoke was pouring from my overhead light. I switched it off quickly. after a little while it quit smoking, It cooled of and I removed the bulb. the bulb was a Sylvania 40W  CF40EL/TWIST  It is one of the new energy type bulbs that if I understand correctly we will be forced to purchase instead of the incadesent type. Five minutes after pulling the chair from the box, she tripped and hit her forehead on the corner of the chair. The injury required a trip to the emergency room and five stitches. Saw smoke coming from my candle warmer. After turning it off and removing wax holder, it smells like melted.burnt plastic. Inside where the electric cord attaches to the halogen lamp unit, it has a black burnt area. I contacted candle warmers Etc. company and I was told there is no chance of a fire from a candle warmer. I was then told to pick out a new product and return this one to be inspected. I chose one but was told it cost more ($3.00) so I chose another. After hanging up the phone that evening I thought it over more and it angered me first that I was told there was no chance of a fire and secondly, they were more concerned the new product I chose cost $3.00 more.
I emailed the company over the weekend and told them how I felt and that the halogen lamps are not safe as they get too hot. I received a call today from the customer service manager [REDACTED] or [REDACTED] (?) and she also said theres no chance of fire. incident_description: In one of the homes that I am a maintenance person for there are 50 can lights on tracks that were using Sylvania 75Par16 Halogen lights (Sylvania item #59042-3). We have had a very high rate of failure from a design or manufacturing defect in which a metal ring that holds a glass lens cover in place falls off allowing the hot lens cover to fall out as well. We have had cases of the hot lens exploding on impact with coffee tables and countertops, posing a risk of severe eye injury. Fortunately we have replaced all of the bulbs with another brand without anything worse than singed carpet and minor finger burns. Upon replacement we noted that out of the 45 Sylvania bulbs we removed 14 had already had a failure as described above. We are not sure of how many we replaced one at a time before we realized that there was a serious problem with the product.
justification: The incident involved hot lens covers falling and exploding, posing a risk of severe eye injury, though only minor injuries like burns were reported. The high failure rate (14 out of 45 bulbs) indicates a likely recurrence.

incident_description: On 12-9-2011 I was called to a nail salon by the local fire dept. A customer at the salon had been receiving a pedicure on a massaging pedicure spa chair, and her long hair became entangled on the masssaging rollers that were inside the chair back. The seat back fabric had to be cut away and a significant amount of the victim's hair was cut off to release her from the entanglement. It appears that the only way her hiar could have been entangled on the massaging rollers was if there was a tear in the seat back fabric. Upon further investigation of the fabric material that covers the rollers, it appears the thin foam backing was worn and pushed out of position by the up and down movement of the massaging rollers, and the remaining thin fabric could be easily torn. It was not possible to distinguish if there was a tear from the rollers due the cuts made to release the victim. The operator of the salon indicated that the seat back fabric had been replaced previously by a service techinician due to a tear. My concern is that this is a faulty design that could lead to more such incidences of hair entanglement or other injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a customer's hair being entangled and cut off, indicating an injury (severity 3). The worn fabric and previous tear suggest such incidents are possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description: Bought a Power Reclining sofa and loveseat in Sept 2011. They ALL have the same issue of the cord being rubbed as recliners move back & fourth and is wearing as well.  This is a fire hazzard.

incident_description:
On 11/2/2011 I purchased 80 boxes of Holiday Time LED C7 Light Sets from Wal-Mart in Grove, OK.  They are 14 feet long and contain 25 LED lights each.  Each LED element is enclosed with a plastic globe.  The box is marked "indoor/outdoor use", and there is an Underwriters Lab label on each string.  I hung the lights around the outside of the house using plastic mounting hooks made to fit the lights (same brand).

Problem:  After a rain, I noticed water inside the plastic globes.  Then after a freeze, the globes on many of the units popped off, exposing the LED elements.  Within a few days of water in the globes, several of the strings of lights shorted out and quit functioning.  My concern, in addition to the inconvenience, is that the water in the globes and the exposed LED elements presents a risk of electrocution and fire.  I know that water and electricity do not mix.  They are definitely NOT suitable for outdoor use.
justification: The incident describes a product failure (lights shorting out and globes popping off) but no actual injury or death occurred, hence severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue occurred after specific weather conditions.

incident_description:
Re: Tea Light Candle flare up

I am forwarding this information on for your review and appropriate action.

Recently my wife and I were en route to an arson conference and we stopped to enjoy an elegant meal at
an upscale restaurant. Across from us sat five people at an adjoining table. All of the tables in the
establishment had two tea light candles in glass cup containers in place. The five people left and a few
minutes later we saw one of the candles flare. There was a two-inch wide base of flames at the top of the
glass container with erratic flames over 12 inches high and about eight inches wide at the top.

Had a witness at a fire told me what had happened I would have found it had to believe. However, my
wife and I were the witnesses.

A waitress quickly smothered the flames. I asked for and received the errant candle remains. We let one
of our candles burn completely out with no event. The waitress said that they have used these same
candles for some seven years with no problems; however, in the last batch they received, six candles have
flared. In each instance an odor of kerosine was observed.

I have attached images of the candles and a container.

Common to both candles, the errant one and ours, is that the wick disk base was not centered and instead
was against the side of the aluminum cup, allowing the flame to impinge on the side of the glass
container.

The owner said she purchased the candles through her restaurant supplier. They are called Five Hour
Tea Lights, supplied by the Sterno Group Division of Candle Corporation of America, [REDACTED]. She said the item number on the box is #505TIL. The box indicates they are made in Thailand. She has called Sterno several times, but has
received no real response. (Note: Sterno web site lists the number as 505TL)

It appears the main problem is that the disk that holds the wick is not secure in the aluminum cup when
the wax is melted. The melted wax allows the disk holding the wick to travel to the edge ofthe cup when
tipped or disturbed. The wax is melted at the time the candles are extinguished by staff and, if tipped
before the wax is cooled, the disk can be displaced. This can also occur during the time the table is being
reset by staff for the next guest and the candle is still lit.

I have reviewed some research on the laboratory work on these candles, but this is my first field
experience of how things happen in the real world.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact me. I still have the remains of both candles
and the glass container.

Very truly yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a candle flare-up that was quickly controlled without injury, but poses a potential fire hazard.

Within days of receipt of product, I noticed that at least one of the two wires out of inserted into the female plug was separated resulting in a bare wire being exposed in 30+ of the 60 strings of light. incident_description: I purchased a Luna 4 piece entertainment center a little over a year ago. Since purchasing the product I've had many incidents happen mainly because the right end piece of the entertainment center scoots away from the tv stand. When this happens it causes the pegs that hold the shelf above the tv to give away and then the whole shelf falls down onto the product below. The last time it fell the shelf hit my daughter in the leg causing a very minor cut on her leg as well as major property damage to the tv stand and our hardwood floor. The shelf has enough force when it falls to cause major damage or injury to the consumers. I have 2 small children that if they were to be near the product during a time it falls it can either kill them or do serious damage. The pegs that connect the shelf to the right side of the entertainment center does not even touch the bottom of the shelf meaning there's not much stability. Something really needs to be done about this before it does kill or seriously injure someone.
justification: The incident caused a minor injury to a child and major property damage, with potential for more severe injuries or death if the issue is not addressed.

incident_description: Automated Recliner with remote was sold to my elderly mother 70 years of age, She needed a chair to help come to a stance, she is suffering from stage 4 terminal cancer. She is mobile, and just needed help with getting up out of the chair. A commerical offering this product sold her on this product, it showed an elderly lady being propped up to a full stance. Our family visited the El Cajon store (Jeromes) and the sales person also exlained the uses of the chair and it would be of great help for our mom. She purchased in full payment on her credit card. She also has another chair from the same store, and uses this regulary, but decided to use the new chair yesterday and today. The chair remote does not have a kill switch, or stop mode or any modes listed. She pressed it to stand up and it literally pushed her out onto the floor. She was able to pick herself up, but with some bruising and scratches from the fall. My brother was home today, she wanted to use the chair with his assistance. Again, they tried to stop the chair, they were not able to stop the chair and he barely caught her before she fell all the way to the ground. She was bruised from my brother trying to catch her. The chair is not safe, and the commerical is misleading and other elderly people could receive more extensive injuries. We reported to our BBB locally, and call the store. The customer service reprsentative was nto helpful and not courteous and rude. I escalated to the manager, and she listened to our full complaint. She said they are not the manufacturer and only the retailer and they have no way of offering a refund, but a store credit. I told her my call was to inform them of the potential hazards of the remote feature, and they need to address ASAP. Other consumers need be aware of this chair and potentail hazards, My mother will be seen my her physician today, and we will have full medical exam. Her condition is terminal and has about 6 months per her oncologist. We are saddened by the misleading information advertised by this company and there mishandling of this serious issue.
justification: The incident resulted in bruising and scratches from falls, indicating an injury severity level. The likelihood is high given the product's design flaw and potential for repeated use by elderly individuals.

incident_description:
I purchased some candles at Target, the product name is the Fresh Lilac / Pure, Clean, Soy /Natural Soy Wax & Essential Oils Designed for CLEAN LIVING. I purchased a couple of them in the glass jar (10 0z.) presentation and a couple of them in the metal tin presentation (14.1 oz.).
I really like these candles since I have bought them before in the metal tins. The smell is wonderful.
So after I started using them at home, after about 35-40 minutes lit, one of the glass jars exploded and smeared hot wax all over my bathroom! Glass pieces flew all over and the wax was very hard to remove from all the surfaces that were smeared. Luckily no one was in it the bathroom when the candle exploded at the time! While I thought that it might have been my fault for the candle exploding, like maybe I sat it in a place where there was a breeze or maybe I sat it over a wet surface, not sure what to make of it. I still had 2 more glass candles,  so I lit up another one days later and placed it on my bedroom night stand.  It was lit fine until I noticed, that after about 30 minutes burning, the jar was getting "deformed", like "melting" and was extremely hot to the touch!.   I got scared, cause it looked like it had this big bump on one side in the glass!!! I thought it was about to explode too, so I blew it off and let it cool off for good.  I never lighted up my jar glass candles again, only my metal tins, which I never had a problem with and they still burn fine!!

I do believe there is something wrong with the glass they are using for these candles. It is either not tempered or they are just defective. I am a candle person and have been buying candles for years! Different brands, and never had an incident in which a candle would explode due to the glass getting too hot! I always use my "[REDACTEd] Candles" until they are gone!! I would burn them constantly until there is no more wax left in the jars and never had a problem like this ever.
justification: The glass candle exploded and caused property damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I'm attaching a review I posted on Amazon regarding the Progress Lighting 300W transformer and Illuma Flex track system that describes the issue we had w/ this product.  I also have some pictures of the burned area on the track that I can send to you at your request.  Thanks,  Bought this system w/ the supposedly 300W transformers in brushed nickel and installed in house in March of 2011.  The lighting systems were quite expensive and when they arrived we were surprised at how cheap the whole system looked (a lot of cheap plastic and didn't seem very well made). (We actually have 3 of them that we ordered at the same time to install in our kitchen/family room area-2 w/ spot lights and one w/ the wine bottle pendant lights/globes).  Within 4 months of installation, one of the flex track units started intermittently turning off and on.  The system was not overloaded if it was in fact a 300W transformer like we paid for and as the unit was labeled.  (We had 6, 50w bulbs w/ the suspension arms that we purchased all at the same time from Progress Lighting as recommended=300w total).  Now I'm finding out that the transformer that was advertised and sold as 300W was actually probably only 250W even though it was labeled as a 300W. (Read other person's review under the 300W Progress Lighting transformer).  I was also told by Customer service at Progress Lighting today that they only carry a 250W transformer now, but she couldn't tell me when they discontinued the "300W" that we paid extra for and trusted it to power 6, 50W bulbs.  This unit completely quit working and when we took down the flex track, we discovered that it was completely "burned-out" where the track connects to the transformer and the plastic connectors on the transformer were melted!  We are so lucky that our house didn't burn down and that no one was injured or killed!  Progress Lighting sent us another transformer and is in the process of sending us another flex track to replace the "burned-up" one, and recommended that we only us max of 250w instead of the 300w that it was rated.  Honestly, we are scared of this system now and thinking of replacing all of them w/ something different!  The wine bottle pendants look nice and we haven't had a problem yet w/ them probably b/c we only have 250W (5 hanging pendants) on this flex track.  Flex track is a great idea, but now I'm scared of this system. Wanted to insert a picture of the burnt flex track w/ this review, but didn't see where to attach it.
justification: The incident involved a burned-out transformer and melted plastic connectors, posing a fire hazard, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a twin size bed for my 5 year old from The Land of Nod.  After having the bed delivered and professionally put together, I purchased a twin size mattress.  There is approximately 3 inch gap from where the mattress ends and the bed frame.  I honestly didn't think anything of it and first, as in hindsight I should have.  My daughter, as 5 year olds will do, was jumping on her bed and got her foot caught in the cap and twisted her ankle.  She could have been much more seriously hurt.  I went onto the The Land of Nod webiste and pulled up the bed description for the Petite Marguerite bed.  Upon looking at the dimensions of the bed and where it was made I was able to determine that the bed was made in Vietnam and the dimensions of the bed are 43.25 W x 78.75 D x 44 H.  Well, a twin size mattress, even the ones that Land of Nod sells are 38 inches W.  This explains the gap!  I then went to a website that tells me international matress sizes (link below) where it listed Twin measurements in the USA/Canada 39 inches, Europe 36 inches and Asia 42 inches!  That also explains a great deal.  The bed frame would be fine if I lived in Asia/Vietnam where the bed was made.  I have called Land of Nod and they said that there products are made for US specifications, but this is clearly not the  case.  I am awaiting a call from a supervisor, but the bottom line is a child could get seriously injured.  I have resorted to jamming towels in the gap between the bed and the mattress so my daughter doesn't get hurt again.  This was not a cheap piece of furniture and I am hoping that something can be done about this, but I think consumers should be forewarned.
http://www.mattresssizes.info/mattress_dimension_chart.html
justification: The incident resulted in a twisted ankle injury to a child due to a gap between the mattress and bed frame, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the potential for similar incidents with children using the bed.

incident_description:
I recently purchased the Easy Riser 25" Air Bed w/ 4" Built-In Pillow & Pump from shopnbc.com.  /This air mattress is manufactured by Lion Sports.  We received it 11/17/11 and used it the following weekend when we visited my son who is away to college.  My son is now how visiting for winter break and has been using the air mattress in our spare room.  This mattress is about waist high. incident_description: I purchased a Disney Fairy Bedroom suit from Rooms to Go in Greenville, SC.  The chest has fallen over 3 times.  The first time it fell on my 4 year old granddaughter, the only thing that saved her from injury is that it hit another piece of furniture in her room and kept it from going all the way to the floor.  She was able to crawl out from under the chest. The second time it fell over I was putting clothes away in the drawers and caught it and was able to push it back up.  The third time I pulled the chest away from the wall to sweep behind it, the drawers came open and it tipped and fell and again it hit the bed and the entertainment center, so it kept it from hitting the floor. I called reported to Rooms To Go in Greenville the incidents and they siad to call and report this to thier Customer Service department.  I called and was told by [REDACTED] that there had been complaints of this happening and that it had been fixed and they would send a service representative out to the house to look at the chest and see if I had the correct piece.  She asked me if when the furniture had been delivered if they had informed me that the chest needed to be anchored to the wall and if a wire had been delived with it.  The answer was no to both of these questions.  The people who delivered the furniture spoke only broken english.  The service rep came out to the house and I asked him if the Fix for the problem was anchoring the piece to the wall with a wire and he said yes.  But that it was up to the buyer to do this. This chest will tip over 100% of the time if the bottom 3 drawers are open and you go to open the fourth drawer. This is a child's piece of furniture and is marketed for children.  It is unsafe.  The design of the chest lends it to tipping over because it is narrower at the bottom and wider at the top. The answer that I get from the company is that all chests tip over when the drawers are opened.  I have never owned a chest that has tipped over, even with all drawers opened.  This one tips over when all drawers are empty.  The drawers have metal sliding mechanism to open them very easily, which also makes them very easy for a child to open them.  You cannot tell a young child to only open one drawer at a time.  At no time, in the show room or at delivery were we ever informed that it would be necessary to secure this piece of furniture to the wall, nor did we receive any paperwork where it was stated that this was important to do.  Again 100% of the time, this chest will tip over.  It is very heavy and if this chest had fallen on my granddaughter without having been stopped by another piece of furniture, I know without a doubt that she would have sustained a serious injury and possible death.  I am a [REDACTED] and have worked with the Greenville Hospital System for the past 36 years and take this very seriously.  We have a duty to protect our children and I am deeply concerned that this chest is being marketed for children to be placed where they will be using it.  My granddaughter is at the independent stage and wants to dress herself.  We have removed all of her clothes from this chest to keep her from going to it and we are requesting from the company that they come and take the chest back because it is unsafe.  Even if they tell the consumer that it should be anchored and it is up to the consumer to do so, not everyone is going to do that or have the ability or know how to do it.  The chest is so heavy that if anchored to the drywall it would probably pull free, it would have to be anchored to a stud and it would need to be done correctly.  The customer service department of this company only tells me that anyone should know that all chests should be anchored to the wall. They have been slow in responding and I am receiving conflicting information depending on who I speak with.  I have asked to speak with a supervisor and was informed that she had 48 to 72 hours to return my call.  The three times I have called and asked to speak with her I am told she is unavailable. It does not seem to matter to them that this is a safety issue.  Also, not all configurations of a room lend it to placing a chest against a wall to be anchored.  Our chest is placed under a window because that is the only place for it.  Again, this chest is unsafe and has a high risk of causing injury or death.  This chest should not be on the market to be placed in a child's room and place that child under significantly high risk of injury or death.  I am disappointed that the retailer has been so uncooperative, especially as it was their customer service department that informed me that they already knew of the risk of this chest falling over and had put a FIX in place.  Whether that was the retailer or the manufactuer I do not know.  Their disregard for safety is unacceptable.

She was leaving to go home tonight and barely bumped the globe on an upholstered chair and it broke into hundreds of pieces. The glass is almost as thin as a piece of waxed paper! Had this been dropped on her foot, it would have cut it to pieces. She fortunately only received a small cut on her hand where a piece of glass fell. We have had a hard time cleaning up the glass because it is so thin and have received several small cuts to fingers

This product was purchased from Things Remembered. This globe and all others made by Danbury Falls Water Globe Co. need to be recalled immediately! They are extremely dangerous!
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (small cuts) from broken glass, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) given the fragility of the product and the ease with which it broke.

incident_description: The infant room teacher was leaving on Monday, 12/12 at about 5:30 when she stopped me and told me that the glider rocker in the baby room was feeling weird, like it was loose and going to fall apart. She then left for the day. About 10 minutes after that I got a phone call from one of the parents in the baby room, she proceeded to tell me that when her boyfriend picked up their child and went to put her in the car that they found a bolt in her mouth. They took the bolt, checked to make sure she was fine and put her in her car seat. They then drove home and called me to tell me what had happened. I told the mom I would call her right back after I went into the room the check things out. I then went into the infant room and checked all the cribs, swings, bouncy chairs and the glider rocker. I took the glider rocker and tipped it upside-down when I did that two washers and a nut fell onto the floor. I look at the underside of the rocker and could tell where the washers were from but I couldnÃÂt see where a bolt was missing. I then removed the rocker from that classroom and swept the floor. I returned to my office and called the mother back and explained to her that I thought it was the rocker that had lost a bolt because of what had fallen out onto the floor. I also explained to her that this was the second glider rocker we had gotten from this company and it was only about 6 months old. I told her that the first rocker we had was taken out because the springs fell out of the bottom if it. I also explained to her that this glider rocker was purchased for us as part of a materials grant we received in 2010. I made sure that the infant was fine and that the parents were at ease with what happened but I did assure that them that I was going to report this incident to the Environments Company as well as the people that we received the grant from.
justification: The infant was unharmed despite finding a bolt in her mouth, and the incident was promptly addressed by staff.

incident_description:
Illuminating Experiences ELF1 Bath Fixture

We have ordered 8 of these Illuminating Experience ELF1 fixtures for our new house.  They came equipped with two different kind of Zenon double contact bayonet style bulbs rated at 60watts each.  There are two bulbs per fixture.

Six of the eight came with bulbs that had a longer shaft of insulating material between the socket and the bulb.  

The other two came with bulbs with no insulating material.  Within a few weeks these fixtures began to have a burning smell and then within another couple of weeks, the top bulbs burned out.  Actually what happened was the heat from the bulbs began to attack the wiring insulation but before it damaged the insulation, the bulb base welded itself into the socket.  Eventually this caused a short circuit at the base and the fixture had to be replaced on warranty.  

When we got the replacement fixtures, after complaining about the apparent faulty bulb, the new units came with the same non-insulated bulbs.  Again, within a couple of weeks we had the same burning smell and when I tried to remove the top bulbs, they were once again welded into place.

Illunimating Experiences has more that a warranty problem with these lamps.  At some point they will be given a Consumer Product recall.

Buyer beware
justification: The incident describes a recurring issue with bulbs welding into fixtures and causing a burning smell, but no injury or death is mentioned.

We contacted our fire department so they could forward the info on to the State Fire Marshals Office and I have also contacted the Sylvania.  They just got back with me today and I have sent the info on the bulb to them.  Here is the info on the bulb.  It is a Sylvania 13W 120V 60Hz 190mA CF13EL/Minitwist 3000K.

incident_description: I purchased the Bumbo Sitter around October 2010 when my daughter was born. I didn't use the Bumbo until she was only enough to hold her head up by herself - basically it was used 5 to 10 minutes  a day 3 to 4 days per week from age 3 to 4 months (approximately January 2011- February 2011).  The Bumbo would be placed on the floor in the middle of room.  I would give her a toy and if she would drop it, she would look at it, but as she got a little older she would try to reach for it, reaching out to the side and sometimes trying to reach forward or behind her. I would usually hand it to her. I caught her almost tipping over backwards once, so after that I always made sure I was no more than 2 to 3 feet away at all times. But one time she couldn't reach her toy, and I was momentarily distracted by another child, even though I was sitting on the floor only 2 feet away from her, and the Bumbo fell over sideways, causing her to hit her head. Somehow or another she hit forehead first, causing a huge egg-sized hematoma in the middle of her forehead. This occurred approximately in February 2011.   I am a medical professional and didn't see need at the time to rush her to the ER, there were no visual signs of concussion or loss of consciousness, but to this day December 14, 2011, she still has a bluish/purple discoloration to her forehead, approximately 1 inch in diameter and located 1/4 inch above the bridge of her nose.  It is most noticeable on cold days or if she has been crying or when her face turns flushed/red for any reason.
justification: The incident resulted in a hematoma and persistent discoloration, indicating an injury.

incident_description:

The flame flared up 12 inches when blown on and I finally extinguished it with water, causing a huge flare-up that almost caused a house fire.  

When I examined it,  I saw that the metal wick holder had a large pool of glue around it, which was the cause of the toxic smoke.  THESE CANDLES HAVE WICKS THAT ARE GLUED IN PLACE WITH FLAMMABLE AND TOXIC GLUE.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous flare-up and toxic smoke, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The fluorescent bulb was placed in an open  vanity light  for approximately 11 to 12 month total .The light fixture was put  in the on position estimating 10-15 minutes when suddenly she smelled smoke and saw smoking coming.  While the light bulb was smoking she noticed that the light bulb was still operating.

The light fixture was powered in the off position and the bulb was carefully removed (the item used to remove the bulb is unknown) and she noticed that the plastic casing had burned through. 

The bulb was placed in a guest bathroom that is rarely used. 

She experienced the same hazard with three other fluorescent bulbs manufactured by the same firm that were also placed in various different fixtures in the home. The bulbs were placed in the home all at the same time and the last three incident occurred a week after the original hazard occurred.  

She noticed  that the casing at the bottom were brown and scorch looking and emitted a burning smell  but they did not catch fire. Around the later part of 2010 she returned all the bulbs to the retailer ad received a full refund to purchase another brand of bulbs. 

The firm and was contacted the month 7/2010 and asked the consumer to mail the light bulb in so that they could evaluate the light bulb. The consumer decided not to mail the light bulb back because she does not believe they take her concerns seriously. 
CONSUMER ADDED: Manufacturer provided inadequate packaging to protect the bulb in transit (an envelope!)
justification: The incident involved smoking and burning of bulbs without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The recurrence with multiple bulbs suggests an occurrence likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
Heavy and unendurable chemical smell came out of a room. I and my wife found that smoke came from a light bulb. We turned off the power switch immediately and opened all windows. A 23-watts compact florescent light bulb whose model number is CD23TM/4(N) from Feit Electric burnt and melted significantly by itself. After the incident settled down, I found that the lighting-up part of the light bulb was dangling from the the socket body due to the burning and melting on the junction between the two parts. When I softly touched it, it came separated from the socket body.

We were lucky enough to act fast and to have good wind flows from outside so that the fire alarm did not come on. We turned on scent candles and sprayed scents every day, but the disgusting chemical smell all over the room lasted a good week. 

The burnt light bulb was one out of four that came together as one package. We took down and replaced rest of them with regular light bulbs because we did not want to burn our home by the light bulbs from Feit Electric.
justification: The incident involved a burnt and melted light bulb causing a chemical smell, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description: Thursday evening, we noticed a smell of burnt plastic in our livingroom, but could not locate where the smell orginated.  We turned off the lights, TV, Christmas Tree and proceeded to go to bed.  The next morning upon rising, we turned on the Christmas tree.  A short time later we notice the Christmas tree was not lit.  Checking the switch, we found that the power was okay.  So we tried the plug in other sockets, but upon closer inspection we found that the plug was warped, bulging, and smelt burnt.  Thinking it was maybe the fuse, we open the plug to find that it had caught fire inside and melted.  We were grateful that we were home and did not have any presents or material around the plug at the time or we may have had a house fire.
justification: The incident involved a burnt plug with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or property damage occurred.
