incident_description:
I purchased the following item from a Walmart
http://www.walmart.com/ip/Nickelodeon-Dora-All-Together-Micro-Raschel-Throw/15223351
The tag bears a manufacture or distribution date of August 2010 along with a Batch# 020810.
 
My two year old daughter was put in bed at 8pm last night with this blanket.  At around 9pm I heard banging like I have never heard before and a noise resembling a wild animal in her room.  I went into her room and discovered about two feet of the pink border of the blanket wrapped around her neck and she was purple and choking.  I removed the blanket from her and inspected her neck.  The only thing I saw were normal pink marks associated with this kind of accident.  Normal breathing returned almost immediately and she required no medical attention nor does she seem to have suffered any long term ill effects.  Once my husband and I knew our daughter was alright, my husband went to the store and found the same product.  He did notice at that time that the original packaging indicated that the blanket should not be used in cribs.  My education tells me that is due to a possible risk of SIDS and not due to the fact that a toddler would be able to find a defect in the craftmanship of this product and it could cost his or her life.
 
After this incident, we removed the entire pink border because we realized that the blanket was still usable and wouldn't be able to cause further harm.  However after more thought we returned the item because we realized that the store needed to look at its inventory and determine if this was an isolated incident or if this product should be pulled from the shelf.  I think it should also be noted that when the border was removed, all three tags that were sewn into the product came along with it.  Also, on the tag that contained the batch #, those numbers are obviously printed on a sticker---or at least on my particular product, they were as the bottom of the first three numbers of the batch were in the middle of the tag instead of being where they were supposed to be.  My husband placed the bottom of the first three numbers where they needed to be.
Even though we returned the product I still wanted to write to you regarding these three safety issues----my child being able to remove two feet of the border by herself, the 3 tags coming off simultaneously once the border over the tags is removed, and a sticky adhesive label that was able to be placed and removed with ease.  We feel very fortunate that our daughter made enough noise to alert me that something was wrong but if these matters are not investigated and remediated, another little one, another family may not be so lucky.
justification: The child was choking but recovered immediately with no long-term effects, indicating no injury occurred.

incident_description:

incident_description:

incident_description: I just noticed the recall on the bumbo chair while on my sisters facebook page.  I wanted to write in with my own incident.  Not only is the bumbo chair a hazard while on a table or counter top (which I never did), but my daughter fell out of one and received an injury while the bumbo was on the floor!  She is 2 yrs old now, but when she was a baby and using the bumbo, I sat her in it on the bathroom floor while I was looking in the mirror and putting on makeup. I would recommend that the bumbo be used ONLY with the tray on it to possibly prevent a baby from being able to push forward and fall out.

incident_description: The Fisher Price Laugh & Learn Musical Learning Chair was purchased for our 1st child (2005/2006) and after the inital recall of possible strangulation, we did get the repair kit and it was installed. Our 2nd child (18 months) was trying to sit on it today when his thigh was wedged between the lamp and repair part (the table and arm of the chair)...over the area where the replacement part is.  He screamed because he was unable to free himself.  He was left with pretty bad marks on his leg that are very tender to the touch. I have not heard of any other problems with this product, but wanted to make it known that it does still pose a risk to small children.

incident_description: While me, my wife and daughter where out-of-town the Air Pump on our Select Comfort Sleep Number Bed caught on fire by itself. Our neighbor was out in his garage and heard our smoke alarms going off and entered our house through our garage using our garage code to see why the smoke alarms where going off and he found the smoke was coming from under our bed in our master bedroom. Once he pulled our bed out from the wall a few feet he saw the Air Pump smoldering into our carpet which was burned completely through to the carpet pad. He immediate unplugged the electric cord and cut the air tubes from the pump and immersed the air pump in water in our bathroom sink to contain the fire inside the pump. It blew out of the wall and the prongs are melted.  I left the house with the tree plugged in and I came home to the plug blown out of the outlet.  There was black soot on the outlet. incident_description: When I opened the packaging I immediately smelled a very strong chemical odor on the garland, similar to a combination of garden fertilizer and pool chlorine. After handling the garland for about 5 minutes (I was hanging it in a well-ventilated space) I began to feel quite dizzy and nauseous. My symptoms stopped within 10 minutes of stopping exposure to the garland, washing my hands thoroughly, and seeking fresh air.
justification: The incident caused dizziness and nausea, which are symptoms of injury, but no long-term harm was reported.

incident_description:
Hi, 

Late last summer (2010... I could find the receipt with the exact date if you need it) I bought 1 Birch Veneer Malm 3 Drawer Chest and 1 Birch Veneer Malm 6 Drawer Dresser from IKEA at my local Ikea store in Charlotte. I also bought 2 Black Billy Bookcases. I bought the furniture to go in my 2nd house at the time... not my permanent residence. 

I only stayed the night at that location 5 times when I first bought the furniture, then I didn't stay there anymore for over a year. At that time I realized furniture initially had a strong smell... particularly the Malm, but I thought it would go away with time, but it didn't. When I would go to that residence to get belongings every once in a while I was surprised to know that my room still smelled strongly of fumes. I didn't think much about it since I was not spending much time there.

Move forward... in August of this year I moved out the furniture out of that residence and put it in storage. Then about two weeks ago moved the furniture into my bedroom at my new residence. IThe first thing I noticed was that the place where I had the furniture stored smelled like the strong fumes associated with the furniture, and then my new bedroom begin to smell like that as well once I moved the furniture in. I also began having some respiratory symptoms and a general feeling of malaise when spending any significant amount of time in the room. It is also making any of my clothes that I keep in the furniture smell like some sort of chemicals. When I slept in the same room as the furniture all the next day I felt extremely bad. 

I felt so sick I have decided that I don't think it's safe, or pleasant to keep the furniture in my room any longer. I am going to be moving it to storage until I hear back from you guys. 

I really like the way the furniture looks and functions, but obviously I can 't keep it around because of the fumes. It's really quiet unbelievable how strong they are. Anyone who has been in my room has noticed it, and once I let them smell the inside of the furniture drawers they can't believe it is so strong. 

 I think this may be a consumer safety issue Ikea may want to look into. I fear that if it makes me feel like this it could make children very sick... and possibly be dangerous to anyone.
justification: The incident describes respiratory symptoms and malaise linked to chemical fumes from the furniture, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the unique circumstances described.

incident_description:
My girlfriend and I live together and both went to our respective homes for the Thanksgiving holiday.  I came home to find our Crate and Barrel Mix Coffee Table completely shattered. The alarm was still set so I knew that no one had entered the apartment and caused the damage. It seemed as though the table had exploded as I was finding glass shards as far as 30 ft away in all directions from the table. There was a dusting of fine glass pieces everywhere in the apartment, including our counter tops, couches, rugs, and pillows. We felt extremely lucky that we were not home when this occurred, as we could have been seriously injured. However, we were baffled by why and how this could have happened, until we saw other examples of this listed here:

http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1203429
justification: The incident involved property damage (shattered table) with no injuries, and the rarity of such events is indicated by the need to reference external examples.

incident_description:
Bought a prelit Xmas tree last year.  Stored it in a great location, inside a padded storage bag, in a temperature controlled environment.  It was used for maybe 60 days.  Half the lights don't work now.  I replaced the fuzes, and bulbs with extras included.  Unfortunately, I needed more bulbs.  Garden Ridge, does not carry replacements, they told me " buy a light string at home depot, take the bulbs out of the garden ridge base, tAke new bulbs off depot lights, assemble the new bulb, and replace in tree.  I did this for 5 hours today, guess what doesn't work.  Topper, the store will not give me a contact number for the manufacturer.  This tree cost 200+ a year ago, should last more than one season.  Last tree I had, bought at big lots lasted 10 years, and when bulbs burned out, they had them on hand.  what is wrong with garden ridge?  How do they stay in business?

I was repeatedly shocked trying to reassemble the bulbs as per Garden Ridge store recommendation.  This seems really unsafe.  In fact a niebor told me if I don't reassemble the bulbs right I can burn my house down.
justification: The incident involved repeated electric shocks and potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer stated her table lamp is a potential fire hazard. The consumer stated that she came into her bedroom and smelled a chemical plastic smell and found that the plastic dial switch was very hot to the touch. The consumer stated that the product never smoked or caught fire. The smell remained in her home for an hour. The switch panel melted but the consumer is unsure if the wires inside are melted. The consumer stated that was the only part of the lamp that was unusually hot. 
The product was on for 15 minutes at the time of the incident. The consumer noticed the night before that there was a delay when she attempted to shut off the lamp at the dial. The consumer stated that the firm and seller are one and the same. The consumer called the seller today and they offered no assistance because they could not find an order number. The consumer stated that the product did not damage to her and was not injured. The consumer did not call the fire department. The consumer had another product plugged in to the same outlet with the table lamp and that product appeared to be fine.
justification: The lamp showed signs of overheating and melting but did not cause injury or fire, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as similar incidents are possible given the described malfunction.

incident_description: Our 35 pound, 4 year old daughter was helping to put clothes into the bottom drawer of the Munire furniture Armoire. This piece was purchased as part of baby furniture set from the Baby Store in Michigan. This armoire weighs around 200 pounds. She put her weight on the bottom drawer and the entire armoire toppled over. Luckily it was caught at about a 45 degree angle on the bed so she was not injured. Had the bed not been there it would have fallen on our daughter. We have always been very cautious but could not foresee that a 35 pound child could pull over a 200 pound armoire. Upon further investigation, both the armoire and the book case from the set are extremely top heavy. We just want to make sure that something like this does not happen to anyone else.
justification: The armoire toppled over but the child was not injured due to the bed catching it, making it an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that the spiral fluorescent light bulb in the fixture of his sun room emitted a very foul odor. The consumer stated that the bulb is 23 watts. The fixture is accompanied by a hanging light shade. The consumer stated that the bulb contains mercury has a UL number of 15MA. The light was on at the time of the incident for undisclosed amount of time. The consumer came into the room to turn on the light and found that the switch was in the on position. The consumer has had the bulb in the fixture for 2 years.

 The consumer inhaled the odors and is unsure it is unhealthy for him. The consumer took the bulb outside of his home because the smell was so persistent. The light bulb did not crack but did in fact remain intact.  The consumer stated that there 24 hours later, the smell is still strong as ever. The consumer stated that the base of the bulb has a burn mark and there appears to be a singe mark in the inner base of the light bulb. 

The smell was so intense it made the consumer light headed and he needed to go outside. The consumer feels that the bulb is the source of the odor not the light fixture. The consumer purchased the bulb in a package of an unknown amount. The consumer stated that his light fixture is undamaged. The consumer stated that there has not been any property damage. The consumer has placed a common 60 watt incandescent light bulb in that light fixture.

The consumer has not contacted the retailer or the firm. The consumer was not harmed or injured by the product. The consumer has a heart condition and fears that this bulb's contents may afflict him if exposed to the inner material.
justification: The consumer experienced lightheadedness from inhaling foul odors but was not injured, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
On 12/3/2011, I was replacing unlit LED bulbs on my icicle lights.  Each set of 70-count LED strand has two in-line short cigar-shaped devices (perhaps ballasts?).  These ballasts were hard but I noticed some were hot and softer to the touch, distorted, and split exposing a green plastic.  At one point I squeezed-bent one and the unlit lights (half the strand) flickered.  On another in which I was replacing a few random bulbs that went out, I smelled plastic burning and looked and saw the ballast smoking and then split open exposing green plastic.  I then watched it for the next 20 minutes as it kept smoking and some of the lights kept working.  The board underneath the ballast was scorched black.  Although it was still smoking, I finally unplugged it.  It never caught fire, thankfully - and perhaps by design, but I was (and still am) a little scared that I had planned to attach that to my house.  I also noticed that the fuse never blew out.  In all, 9 of the 12 strands showed this damage to the ballasts.  The three that were undamaged were plugged in the middle of the series of strands in the garage (package says you can connect 43 sets to a single outlet).

On 12/4/2010, I purchased 12 boxes of Holiday Time 70-count LED icicle lights from Wal-Mart and they worked well after being hung from the roof and gutters by plastic hangers made for this purpose.  They were set by timer to turn on at dusk for 6 hours.  The weekend after Christmas I took them down and wrapped them loosely around wood pieces (poles) and stored them in the garage rafters.  The garage temperature is not controlled and this past year has ranged from (approximately) 0-110 degrees Fahrenheit.  Until 12/3/2011, I turned on the lights 3-4 times for no longer than 3-4 hours and do not recall that any lights had gone out until the weather began to cool.  

I took the lights back to Wal-Mart and got a refund but despite expressing my fear I saw no concern about the issue except to know whether to press Y or N on her screen for 'Product Defective?' That led me to be concerned that there was no process to identify or investigate this hazard.  The normal procedure would have been to mail the lights back to the manufacturer but that seems like mailing criminal evidence back to the criminal (I do not mean to suggest Holiday Time are criminal).  Also, given that the consumer is expected to pay to ship the lights back, there is a pretty fair guarantee that most people will not go through the trouble, which means the main indicator of a problem will be houses burning down.  After seeing the lack of concern, I wish I had taken them to the fire marshal first or at least taken pictures.  Thank you for your service.
justification: The incident involved smoking and scorched ballasts but no fire or injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as similar incidents are possible given the described conditions.

incident_description: The plastic thread used as the quilting on my son's Finding Nemo comfortor started to come off. While my son was sleeping the plastic thread became wrapped around one of his toes cutting off the circulation. He woke up because his toe hurt. The more he pulled the tighter the plastic thread got. I woke up to my son crying. His toe was purple and there was an indent from the thread. Becuase the thread was plastic and pulled tight from my son trying to get it off it was difficult to remove. I purchased this bedding approximately 6 years ago.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (purple toe and indent from the thread), but no death occurred.

incident_description: My 5-month-old son was sitting in his Bumbo infant seat when he arched his back and flipped out of it and onto the floor, hitting his head and landing on his back. He was not seriously injured in the incident, but it became evident that it is unsafe to leave a baby in the Bumbo seat without an adult hand on him or her at all times.
justification: The baby was not seriously injured but the incident highlights a clear safety risk with the Bumbo seat when unsupervised.

incident_description:
Purchased three pack of GE light bulbs (Product # 48695; 40G25W/RVL) on 11/27/11 at Home Depot.  Installed in bathroom fixture about 6:00pm.  

Used lights on/off over next few hours.  Shut light off for night about 9:30pm.  
About 10:30pm heard sound resembling popping noise followed by a shatter. It sounded like someone had bumped into a table, then a vase had fallen, breaking.  But no one was downstairs.

Wife and I went downstairs to discover one of the new bulbs was missing the glass globe portion.  We found the bulb shattered in the shower.  There was NO glass between the fixture and the shower.
It appears the bulb severed at base sending the globe portion over the shower curtain where it shattered when it hit the shower wall.

Only one bulb 'exploded', however I removed all.  I still have bulbs and can email photos if desired.
justification: The incident involved a bulb shattering without causing injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but have been reported.

incident_description: I put the batteries in the 6" long pre-lit Christmas Garland and it didn't turn on.  I tried the on-off button a few times and when the lights still didn't work, I thought to check to see if I had inserted the batteries properly.  When I took the cover off, the two center batteries were very hot and in fact the bottom battery cover was melting off of the battery.  I immediately took it outside, let it cool for five minutes and got the battery out.
justification: The incident involved overheating batteries and melting, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: Compact flourescent light bulb needed to be replaced as it was not lighting.  When I removed it I noticed that where the bulb and the plastic base meet, the plastic had melted.  I think this is a potential fire hazard.  The bulb was used in a standard bathroom light fixture.  It was an over the sink type fixture that has 5 other lights. No other lights seem to be damaged.  This fixture is about 8 years old and has had no problems with it or any other bulbs.  The bulb was not enclosed in a globe.  The fixture did have a glass "shade type" decorative enlosure that is open on the bottom.  The ones you see on a downward hanging light.   The bulb is from Commercial Electric sku #292-460  Model #EDXO-14  120 V  60Hz, 14 watt 200 A
justification: The melted plastic base indicates a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a leather sofa from our local furniture store.  A little while after having the sofa my husband started breaking out with what we thought was eczema.He was so itchy and could barely sleep at night.  Gradually over time the so called eczema turned into open sores they were not going away. Back and forth to the dermatologist with medicine and creams nothing would help the sores.   We had no idea what was going on never thinking it was the sofa. He had sores/ burns on the back of his arms, legs and lower back. The dermatologist gave him cortisone shots of no avail. Then in October 2010 I realized the only new thing it could be was the sofa. We decided to take the sofa out and put it in the garage.  My husbands skin started to clear up. He still has scars from the sores / burns.  We still have the sofa in the garage and if my husband goes in there he starts to scratch and his skin gets so irritated it takes days for it to go away.   

Had we not figured out that the sofa was causing this problem my husband would be in much worse shape. I have pictures of his open sores/burns. They are quite large on his body.  

The manufacture is Divani Chateau d'Ax
This sofa was assembled in China.
justification: The incident caused severe skin reactions, including open sores and burns, requiring medical treatment and leaving scars, indicating significant injury.

incident_description: A friend was over for Thanksgiving dinner and was sitting on a wooden folding chair when he noticed the chair he was sitting on started to give way below him. He weighs below 200 lbs. On closer inspection the wood around the bolt holding the legs together completely split away from the bolt. This is only the second time which these chairs have been used.
justification: The chair started to give way but no injury occurred, indicating a minor incident. The chairs have only been used twice, suggesting a possible defect.

incident_description: On November 25th at approx 12 noon, our 2 week old bunk bed broke and fell through with child lying on the bed. If my 3 year old had been on the bunk bed underneath at that time, it would have killed him. Child fell through and hit his head pretty hard.
justification: The child fell and hit his head, indicating an injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I was in my living room when I smelled something like it was burning. I followed the smell with my nose until I finally found it. I had to look up at my light in my bedroom to see a CFL light bulb melted. It had melted and had burn spots on it. The smell was pretty strong, so I opened the window. I'm lucky it didn't cause a fire, but it could very well have. Here is a link to the photo I took of it still attached to the socket: [REDACTED]
justification: The melted CFL bulb caused a strong burning smell but no injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I received my new wooden bunkbed for my guest room around 2nd week of October 2011 from K&A Furniture in Fairfield, CA. I could not find the Model# from the bunkbed but these are the informations the store owner gave me: BK458F-EXP and manufactured by Furniture of America. 
I googled online and it showed me the exact image of the furniture. The product was made in Vietnam with a manufacturing date of 08/2011. After a week of sleeping on it,  the wooden side rail at the bottom that run from the headboard to the footboard cracked. The cracked was about 8 inches long. Fortunately, no one was injured. I think the maximum capacity of EACH bed should not exceed 140lbs and so far my brother is not beyond the allowed weight capacity. 

I bought the bunkbed for $750.00. I called the store and they were so quick to fix the issue. They glued the cracked rail but after a night, it cracked again. The store called the manufacturing company and they are replacing the broken rail. And here's another problem, we are still waiting for the replacement part at this moment but the other side of the same rail (already damaged rail) got another cracked. I am thinking eventually this will cause the bunk bed to split and collapse.
We stop using the product for the main time or until it is fixed.

Thank you.
justification: The bunkbed rail cracked but no one was injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of recurrence is high (4) as the issue persisted after initial repair.

incident_description: I was three-hole punching papers over the weekend. As I was pressing my hand down on the handle of the puncher, I started to lift up to release the handle, and there is a white plastic piece between the handle and the front of the puncher. When I was releasing, my hand got caught between the white plastic piece and the handle. The force was so strong that my hand got stuck between and I had to press down the handle again in order to get my hand out. It cut my hand to the point of bleeding. I showed my fiance later on how this happened with a piece of paper and the force ripped the piece of paper instead of the paper slipping out between the handle and the white plastic piece. I am not sure what the white piece is suppose to do, but we even tried to remove it to prevent this from happening again.
justification: The incident resulted in a bleeding cut, indicating an injury, and the demonstration with paper suggests a possible recurrence under similar conditions.

incident_description:
Caller has been trying to work with store about a chair that collapsed while he was sitting in it but preparing to get up, thought he may be getting dizzy however learned that it was all three legs of the chair that gave way.

Weight limit for chairs is unknown, caller weighs between 275 lbs & 285 lbs and is approximately 5" 11"

This incident happened 3 - 4 weeks after caller had surgery to insert a pacemaker. 

Menard's, Inc. Model# Backyard Creations (model number is unknown) , swivel deck chair with three legs goes to a table and chair set.  
Chairs are aluminum round base with aluminum legs.

Caller's daughter purchased table and chair set at the Red Wing, MN Menards Store in [May] 2009.

Enclosed are three sets of photographs totaling 48 pictures. They represent three of the four-chair set in reference to the above referenced report. No defects were found on one of the four chairs.
Set No.1 shows total collapse of the three legs which resulted in my injuries.
Set No.2 shows the start of a crack on one of the legs.
Set No.3 is in reference to a factory-installed lock ring. Upon inspection, it was discovered that the lock ring was missing.

incident_description: Compact fluorescent bulb in enclosed ceiling fixture with 2 bulbs.  Bulb had blown out, but there was electrical burning smell.  The smell continued to get stronger until we realized the smell was coming from the fixture.  There was no smoke coming from the fixture.  I removed the bulb and found a burned area on the bulb.
justification: There was an electrical burning smell and visible damage to the bulb, but no injury or smoke occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a wooden twin/full futon bunk bed from the company, Atlantic Frame, in January of 2011. As my 2 year old, 4 year old, and I climbed in to bed the other night, we heard a loud CRACK, and the side of the full-sized futon bed that comprises the bottom bunk had dropped down a couple of inches. We immediately climbed off and looked down to see 2 large, horizontal splits in the wood, a little over a foot long, each. Now, I notice that there are similar splits in the wood on some of the rails on the underside of the twin-sized top bunk.
I've only had this bed for the past 10 months and paid $899 for it. I am VERY disappointed in the poor quality of this piece of furniture. I purchased it for use in my sons' room, hoping to use it for many years to come, but now I'm afraid that it will split with them on it and wake them in the night; or, worse yet, that the TOP bunk's rails will split, and one of the children will fall and the other will be crushed. It is NOT safe, and it is NOT functional, now. Can the CPSC do anything to help remedy this situation? I have contacted the manufacturer at contact@atlanticframe.com. That is their only contact information available online. The distributor who sold me the bed and delivered it to my house said to contact the company at the email address above (The distributor is [REDACTED] with Home Discounters, [REDACTED]) 
I contacted the company last week and have not heard back from them at all.
:(

 Thank you for your help.

incident_description:
My wife, who is disabled, was sitting in the family room.  I was in an other room.  All of a sudden smoke started rising from inside the shade of a floor lamp.  She called me.  I unplugged the lamp and discovered that the florescent light bulb which was installed in the lamp was chared and smoking.  The bulb was a "Lights of America" 30 W bulb with the label "E67590 Self-Ballasted Lamp 53SJ" writtten on it.   It was charred and smoking where one of the tube ends enters the base. There seems to be a plastic ring cover over the base at this point.  The bulb was very hot. 

This was very scary for us, particularly my wife who could not have dealt with the matter if she was alone, which she many times is.  We also leave this lamp on when no one is in the room and even when we are gone. I do not what would have resulted if I had not turned it off.  We were afraid the shade would have caught on fire which could  have led to a major fire. The smoke itself was very bad.    If this is at all to be expected from this type of bulb we consider it unsafe and completely unacceptable.  

We know that these type of bulbs are now being mandated over incadescent type bulbs.  We have never had a problem with an incadescent bulb. 

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a smoking and charred bulb, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a four piece conversation patio set made by Gardenline from Aldi in May of 2011.  Since May, both chairs and loveseat have broken.  The chair is made of rod-iron with plastic lattic patterned straps that hold the seat cushion. incident_description:
On October 22, 2011; my wife and I had several guests in our home. One of the guests was sitting in a "Swivel/Adj.Height" chair when the chair seat separated from the rollerbase and fell to the floor [with the lady].  What remained were three (3) separate pieces: an "Upper section" consisting of the seat, back,  arms, and an attached metal bracket with two (2) "holes" (this is a significant point); a "Lower section" consisting of the roller base w/pedestal and threaded "swivel collar [like inverted dixie cup]"; and a threaded metal support column [solid threaded metal shaft] with a "tapered end" (this is also a significant point).  Nothing appeared to have broken or malfunctioned to allow the chair to separate when I examined the components.  However, when I reassembled the complete chair (to match the other five (5) chairs), I discovered that when the chair is in its lowest position, the "thread engagement" between the "metal support column" and the "swivel collar" disengages [because the "metal support column" is allowed to travel completely through the "threaded collar" and "hang free"; held only by the frictional bond between the tapered end of the column and the holes in the bracket mounted to the seat assembly. NO FASTENER OR BONDING AGENTS SECURE THE METAL SUPPORT COLUMN TO THE SEAT BRACKET.  HOWEVER; AS LONG AS ENGAGEMENT EXISTS BETWEEN THE THREADED COLLAR AND THE THREADED SUPPORT COLUMN; THE COLUMN REMAINS IN PLACE.

The above situation becomes a serious issue when 1) the seat is in it's lowest position [meaning no engagement exists between the "threaded collar" and the "threaded support column", and 2) the seat is occupied and movement is occurring. This combination resulted in the "frictional bond" between the seat bracket and the "tapered support column" releasing; the support column falling to the floor; and the seat assembly (and occupant) also falling to the floor. All six (6) chairs have this exact potential. 

Each of the six (6) chairs have attached labels with names/addresses of both the "Manufacturing Firm" [DER CHENG WOODEN WORKS] and the "Selling Firm" [SHELBY WILLIAMS INDUSTRIES, Newport, TN].  I have talked to three different individuals at Shelby Williams Industries concerning the matter; and have be told "they" intend no action(s) in this matter.  

In my opinion, these chairs are "designed" to fail under certain "predictable" conditions. I am only grateful our guest did not suffer more serious injuries (She is in her mid-70's).  And I am extremely disappointed in the lack of concern/interest expressed by the personnel at Shelby Williams Industries.  I can provide pictures; or even a chair is necessary.      

Thank you very much for you time and interest.           [REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a guest due to chair failure, and the description indicates all six chairs have the same potential to fail under predictable conditions, making recurrence likely.

In October 2011 I purchased one of your ÃÂCandle of DoomÃÂ candles for our Halloween pumpkin.  The candle did not work as advertised-no smoke came out of the jack o lantern.  That issue seems trivial compared to the reason I am writing.

I gave them each a small cup of water to throw in the pumpkin to put the candle out.  What happened next shocked and terrified us.  A ball of flames erupted out of the pumpkin. incident_description:
Turned on lights and overhead fixture which used the FEIT Electric 100 Watt Compact Fluorescent Light and the light started to flicker and dim for about 30 seconds, then finally dimmed to a very dim glow.  Smoke started to come out of the light fixture.

After removing the electrical power to the light fixture, I investigated and discovered that the CFL (which was still significantly warm to the touch), while it was failing, was overheating to the extent that the sticker used around the socket of the light fixture appeared to have started to burn--it was a discolored brownish color.  I also examined the CFL and there appears to be some melting at the base of the CFL glass due to excessive heat.  I do not know for certain if the smoke was caused by the burning sticker or the melting CFL.  The wiring in the fixture was still intact and unaffected by the heat.  There was also a slight smell of electrical fire in the air.
justification: The incident involved smoke and overheating but no injury or death, and the wiring remained intact.

incident_description:
On Saturday, November 12, 2011, I turned on a bedside lamp with a Commercial Electric CFL bulb (SKU # 353-816, Model EDXO-23, 120V 60Hz, 23W .320A, V # 42836). The bulb began to flicker and, when I looked at the lamp, there was smoke streaming from the top of the shade. This smoke was accompanied by an acrid odor which was irritating to both the nose and eyes. After unplugging the lamp and allowing it to cool, I examined the bulb to find that the base was melted and charred black at the point of insertion of the fluorescent tube.

I contacted the customer service number on the bulb [REDACTED] and was connected to a company called TCP, Inc., which provided an email address to send product concerns. I sent an email detailing what had occurred with the bulb and a photograph of the charred bulb. I received this email in response:

You have experienced a non-passive failure. CFLs (compact fluorescent lamps) don't burn out the way incandescent light bulbs do. Instead, as they near the ends of their lives, they grow dimmer. While some CFL bulbs merely stop emitting light when they finally quit working, others may fail with a dramatic "pop!" sound and then vent a distinct odor. A few even release a bit of smoke at their termination. 

Sometimes the bases of the bulbs turn black and have some melting. This seemingly cataclysmic reaction has to do with the breakdown of the bulb's ballast, which is contained in the part of the bulb that is screwed into the socket. As the bulb ages and degrades, so does its ballast. Yet as scary as odors, smoke, and even blackening or melting of the base of the bulb might be, these lamps are fireproof and are meant to fail safely at the end of their lives.

If you would like, we can send a replacement. Please advise the SKU or TCP number that is on the bulb.


[REDACTED]

Needless to say, I find this explanation from the company less than satisfactory. The smoke and odor emitted by my bulb required the windows to be opened in the house and an exhaust fan used to remove the noxious fumes. And, regardless of what the company says in their response, I do feel this bulb posed a significant fire hazard and might very well have ignited the fabric shade on the lamp had I not been present to immediately unplug the light.
justification: The incident involved smoke and an acrid odor but no injury or death, and the company claims such failures are designed to be non-hazardous.

incident_description: I went to change a CFL bulb and when i touched the bulb it started to work. After i unscrewed it i noticed that it the plastic around the glass coil were melted and burned.
justification: The bulb malfunctioned but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My daughter went to sleep in a Halo sleepsack on Wednesday, November 9, 2011.  When I went in to wake her up on Thursday, November 10, 2011, the slider body and pull tab of the zipper were no longer attached.  The slider body piece was in her right ear and the pull tab was near her left hand.  One piece could have easily gotten lodged in her ear.  She could have choked on both.  I have contacted the company via email but have not gotten a response from them.
justification: The incident involved detached zipper parts near the child, posing a potential choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: The base of the compact florescent bulb melted.  It was screwed into a four year old light fixture.
justification: The bulb base melting is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I ordered the "twist a lite" from The Lakeside Collection.  After I used it about 10 times it shorted out and burned the back of my neck and my hair.  I actually had blisters on my neck.
justification: The incident resulted in blisters on the neck, indicating an injury, hence severity level 3. The likelihood is set to 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty electrical products.

incident_description: The bulb broke, releasing Mercury into the air and creating a broken glass hazard.  I purchased a ceiling mounted fixture at Lowes.  It came with a Good Earth Lighting, E300850 Lamp Adapter 61Y6 Model B2427-30-SP 120V 60Hz 27W 0.450A 3000K 82CRI, also labeled E300 Lamp Adapter 61Y6.  The lamp looks like a regular lamp base, but with 2 pins. However, when I tried to unscrew the bulb, it broke and sent glass everywhere. The lamp should be labeled as a non-screw-tpe bulb.   Even after it broke, I tried to unscrew the bulb from the 'adapter' because it is labeled as such.  It is not an adapter, but is integral with the bulb.
justification: The incident involved broken glass and mercury release, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We purchased a tri-bunk bed for our 6 year old son back in March of 2010. The bed started peeling paint and  both ladders fell off the unit. We reported this to the company where we bought the set from ( Affordable Fine Funiture located at (770) 898-6424
1557 Highway 20 W, McDonough, GA30253). The compnay got back with us a few months later and stated that the warranty company stated that the claim was denied due to child's wear. We asked for the company information ( warranty holder) and the comapny refused to provide us with it. On October 30, 2011 our son [redacted] got in his upper bed ( the one thats over his desk) and the entire bed collasped with him in it. both parents rushed into his room to find him on the floor screaming, and holding the back of his head. His knee was scraped up. 
The next morning after calling Affordable Fine Funiture serval times without getting an answer, I decided to drive by the store and inform them of what had happened. The store owner didnt show any concern, she was trying to rush me out the store, and claim she didnt have the warranrty company's number.
justification: The child suffered a head injury and scraped knee from the collapsed bed, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident was not fatal but highlights possible risks with the product.

incident_description:
The consumer is not aware of the  florescent compact bulb was purchased from and estimate s that it has been in the light fixture for approximately two.

The light was powered in the on position (the exact amount of time is unknown) when he walked into his garage he noticed a electrical burning smell. When he looked above in the ceiling he noticed that there was smoke coming from the light fixture. 

He powered the lights in the off position  and removed the bulb from the ceiling light fixture and noticed that it was glowing and burnt around the base of the bulb. 

The firm was contacted on 10/17/2011 and he was referred to another number (he isnÃÂt exactly sure who the other number belongs to) and no one answered it was just a voicemail so he did not leave a message. 

He then contacted his local Fire Department who advised him to replace the bulb and check the wiring in his home.
justification: The incident involved smoke and a burning smell from a light fixture, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
The light bulb was placed in a  ceiling fan light when powering the light switch in the on position she heard a pop sound followed with a electrical burning odor . The light switch was powered in the off position.

 After removing the light bulb from the light fixture she noticed that the  portion that screws into the base is brownish as if smoke came from it. The swivel portion of the bulb is blackened. 

She is not sure exactly where the light bulbs were purchased from and she thinks that the light bulbs have been in the light fixture  for approximately a year and a half.

She recalls that the failure occurred with one other light bulb in a different light fixture.  Since the failure occurred she has replaced all of the light bulbs in the home.
justification: The incident involved a light bulb failure with visible damage and odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The light bulb has been in my garage door opener for 2-3 years. Yesterday it began smoking and sparking. Now there is a brown burn mark on the outside of the white portion of the base of the bulb, and it left the light socket inoperable. The bulb is made by Sunbeam. The other information on the bulb are: 120V, 60Hz, 305mA, EST-18W, 18W, 93AF, E217504. This might pertain to the manufacture date: 2002.3.
justification: The bulb smoking and sparking caused damage to the socket but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
A portion of the office chairs' base supporting a caster boke off, while a relative sat in it.The chair must be supported by all five casters. The chair is a Gruga U.S.A. dba Novimex Fashion ltd. product that was purchased at Sam's Club. This chair's item number is 7950693-kN, SKU 751486. There is an additional number on the cushion tag A501180.  




  The CPSC announced a recall of chairs by this manufacturer sold at Staples years ago.
Sept. 21, 2004 Release # 04-218.
justification: The incident involved a chair breaking but no injury was reported, fitting severity level 2. Given the recall history, occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description:
A compact fluorescent light bulb I have been using for two or three years suddenly burst into flames.  Had I not be nearby and able to quickly put out the flames, the room and perhaps my entire house would have been engulfed.  As it was, an expensive brass desk lamp was destroyed and my home office where the bulb was used still reeks of the smell from the burned bulb.  Given the type of bulb it is likely that mercury vapor was released in my house. The bulb was in a modern lamp that was well within the 60 watt equivalent capacity of the bulb.  The lamp did not have a dimmer or other features that would make it incompatible with a compact fluorescent light bulb.

The brand name on the bulb is n:vision which is sold exclusively by Home Depot.  The SKU number was burned off but the lot number is 51Y6.

I have this same brand of bulbs, some of the same power, installed all over my house.  Based on this incident I believe these bulbs to be ticking time bombs and should be recalled.  I have saved the bulb and my lamp for inspection by a technical expert if that would be useful.
justification: The incident involved a bulb bursting into flames, causing property damage but no injury or death. The likelihood is possible given the description of similar bulbs installed elsewhere.

incident_description: I received a severe shock when I touched the pole of fluorescent torchiere light while also touching a grounded component on my laptop keyboard.   I isolated problem to the light using a voltmeter.    There is a 350V AC potential between the lamp pole and ground, likely from the fluorescent bulb power unit (built into torchiere and into which circular bulb is mounted).    There has been no damage or modification to lamp since I purchased it.  The shock was very painful - through dry hands across body.   It caused sharp muscle contraction and lingering pain.  Fortunately muscle contraction broke contact with lamp.
justification: The incident caused a severe shock with sharp muscle contraction and lingering pain, indicating an injury.

incident_description: While using Crayola tadoodles markers which are marked as appropriate for ages 18 months and yp, my granddaughter, age 20 months, was able to get the inner adjustable marker stick out by banging the markers together. I do not see anything broken on the marker, and when I attempted to remove the color stick from one of the other markers I was able to do so easily.
justification: The incident involved a child accessing a small part of a marker, but no injury or harm occurred.

incident_description:
I HAVE PURCHASED A DESK CHAIR FROM STAPLES ABOUT 7 MONTHS BEFORE.
AS I WENT TO SIT ON THIS CHAIR, ITS BASE BROKE IN HALF AND I FELL DOWN TO THE FLOOR.
I HURT MY KNEE AND SHOULDER.

PHOTOGRAPHS OF THE CHAIR WERE TAKEN AND SHOWN TO THE STAPLES SUPERVISOR, WHO
IMMEDIATELY GAVE ME A REPLACEMENT DESK CHAIR.

MY REPORTING OF THIS INCIDENT IS MAINLY TO HELP PROTECT OTHER CUSTOMERS FROM UNREASONABLE RISK OF INJURY RELATED TO THIS PRODUCT, WHICH IS MANUFACTURED BY "GLOBAL FURNITURE (ZHE JIANG) CO", ZHE JIANG PROVINCE, CHINA.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the knee and shoulder, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the reported frequency of similar incidents.

incident_description: This morning we noticed smoke coming from our kitchen light.  One of our GREENLITE 18W/ELS- M  2700K 120V 60Hz290mA was actually smoking / buring.  We immediately turned off the light and pulled the bulb once it had cooled down.  We were shocked to see the burn marks on the bulb where the glass enters into the fixture base.  Our entire home has these types of bulbs and we are now terrified that these bulbs are defective and may cause a major fire hazard in our home!
justification: The incident involved a smoking bulb with burn marks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A 13w CFL bulb malfunctioned and had the potential to start a catastrophic fire.  My 7 year old daughter said her light was flickering and smelt.  A awful acridic smell was coming from the bulb.  We swiched off the light and had to use a towel to unscrew the bulb from the socket.  It was so hot that it would have caught any nearby combustibles on fire if we didn't shut it off in time.  The unit was schorched where the glass tube enters the ballast area on the CFL. 
 The unit is made by Energeticlighting or Zhejiang Yankon Group Co. LTD  (as far as we could research a Company in China).
justification: The bulb malfunctioned and had the potential to start a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: I had turned on my heating pad and tossed it down on the bed. Sparks started flying and the cord was broken in half. Not sure if the cord broke which caused the sparks or if the sparks is what broke the cord. It caused a really bad smell. It broke where the controller was attached to the cord.
justification: The incident involved sparks and a broken cord, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a sofa from West Elm. Within days of its delivery, I developed an intense itch on the backs of my thighs, backs of my knees, and lower back and waist -- the precise area of contact with the new couch.  A few days later, I started breaking out with red sores in those areas.  I went to see a dermatologist who said it was an allergic reaction to an irritant or allergen.  When I mentioned the new sofa, thinking that perhaps I was allergic to the material, she said that many furniture manufacturers that ship from China currently use a chemical called dimethyl fumerate in the shipping process.  It is an anti-mold chemical, and it affects some people very strongly.  Indeed, the EU banned the use of this chemical many years ago, but it remains unregulated in the U.S.  The chemical is so potent, it was named "Allergen of the Year" by the American Contact Dermatitis Society in 2011.  My dermatologist gave me topical prescription creams and antihistimes to treat my reaction, but the condition did not get better.  In fact, it worsened.  So we did a biopsy, and the lab results showed conclusively that what I had was "contact dermatitis," a reaction to an irritant or allergen.  I got rid of the couch immediately, and am now trying to get some answers from West Elm about their use of this chemical, but as of the date of writing this complaint, they have not been able to provide me with a single answer, despite knowing about my issue for 3 weeks now.  I am now nearly 4 weeks after the delivery of the couch (and 2 weeks since the couch has been removed from my home), and my situation is getting progressively worse.  My itch is very intense, and the sores are continually spreading on my body.  I am VERY frustrated and angry by this situation, by the fact that a company can knowingly use such harsh chemicals, by the fact that the FDA and CPSC do not regulate the use of this in the US, and by West Elm's failure to treat this issue with any urgency or concern.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (contact dermatitis) requiring medical treatment, but the likelihood of such a reaction is unlikely given the specific chemical and individual sensitivity.

incident_description:
We have a light figure over our kitchen table which has five hanging fixtures in a circle, surrounding one in the middle.  We use regular light bulbs in it.  About a week or so ago the light fixture was on, and then, out of nowhere, the glass just exploded, and shattered all over the place...  I am not 100% that all the light bulbs in there came from the same box, but I am 90-95% sure that they might have. I believe that they say GE 67 Watt miser.  Many of the bulbs have the word MEXICO on them.

And the sad news was announced a few months back that the US is no longer going to be making their own lightbulbs anymore.  SAD/SAD/SAD.  There's no way Americans can get quality products if we keep buying [REDACTED] from foreign countries.  I'll bet the US light bulbs never had this kind of a safety problem.

Imagine if one of my children was sitting here eating, or doing their homework when that bulb exploded?

Thanks and regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a light fixture exploding, but no injuries were reported. The likelihood is possible given the description of the event.

incident_description: I had the GE bulb in my desk lamp.  I begin to smell an odor like burned rubber.  Then suddenly the black smoky gas blew out of the base of the bulb.  I became very, very, sick.  My eyes watering and I couldnÃÂt breathe.  I was then sick all day.  My eyes continued to hurt sinusly and my head began to throb.  My head still feels swollen.  I have sick spells.  This is the second bulb to explode.  The first time I thought to be a strange coincidence.  But two bulbs exploding in the same 7-month period isnÃÂt coincidence.
justification: The incident caused physical harm including breathing difficulties, eye irritation, and prolonged sickness, indicating an injury severity. The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a higher likelihood.

incident_description: I bought about 6 GE Hg Helical 15w light bulbs a couple of years ago to save money on energy costs, as the government recommends.  These light bulbs promise to last 5 years.  Since being installed, several of them have not only burned out, but they have started to arch and smoke just before they burn out.  They left a smoky smell in my apartment when they do burn out.  The base of these light bulbs indicate burned or smoke marks on them when I have removed them.  I wonder if fires have been started because of these defective bulbs?  I have noticed several other complaints about these bulbs posted online.
justification: The bulbs have caused smoke and burn marks, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no actual fire or injury has been reported.

incident_description: This chair was recalled in October 2009 b/c the bolts securing the back to the chair shear off causing a fall risk.  My son, an engineer, was nearly injured when he reclined in the chair and the back broke.  He got a repair kit after being routed to various departments at the manufacturer and submitting photos of the broken chair. The new back has four instead of two bolts and instructions to tighten them periodically and my son is satisfied with the new design, at least for now.  What disturbs me is that a) no one at the manufacturer recognized that the product had been recalled - since we have another Quantum chair, I did a little research and discovered the recall on my own and b) Office Depot seems to be holding up a negative review I tried to post indicating that the chair had been recalled and that you could get a replacement back by filling out an online form.  Furthermore, Office Depot does not have the recall notice posted on their site even though it's obvious from customer complaints that people are still being endangered by breaking chairs.
justification: The incident involved a near injury due to a chair defect, and the recall issue indicates ongoing risk to others.

incident_description:
We purchased 5 of the RSI bathroom medicine cabinets, model numbers 64136 (2 of these) and 64148 (3 of these) from Lowes on Nov 23, 2009 (3 that day and 2 a subequent day)  for our home remodel.

When taken out of the package my husband noticed one had glue that was not sticking well so he took it apart and reglued it. This one has not fallen apart.

The glass doors fell off one of the model 64148 we installed.  It was in our guest bathroom and when he opened the door to get something inside one glass door fell off and chipped the vanity. He quickly grabbed the door before if fell on the floor and that is when the glass cut his hands.  As he stood there (bare feet, bare hands, bleeding) another door fell off and he didn't have hands to grab it. The second glass door fell onto the vanity, shattered and sliced open his leg and foot.

My husband took a look at how the doors are held on and decided they were poorly designed and poorly made. To avert further injury he took took the 4 installed vanities out and threw them away. We have one that's never been installed still in the box. 

While shopping for replacement vanities at Lowes we told the salesman what happened and he said they were recalled. I called the recall number (888-774-8062) today and the person was not very open to discuss this issue since we did not purchase the product in their time frame of August 2007 to October 2007 per your alert #08-533. She basically told me told me that there was nothing they could or would do.

I am requesting that you expand the sold "to / from" dates to include additional products.  We are very fortunate that out daughter is a medical professonal and was there to help. Please contact me at [REDACTED] for questions / further details.  

Lowes Receipts (1) [REDACTED] (2) [REDACTED] (3) looking for 3rd receipt

Thanks -[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries including cuts to hands and a sliced leg and foot from falling glass doors.

incident_description: While using my twister light bulb it went "snap" and went off.  On investigation I found that it had cracked at the base.  At that time I did not know that it was filled with mercury vapors. As I examined it I assume I inhaled the vapers.  Now that [REDACTED] me off !!
justification: The incident involved exposure to mercury vapors, which can cause injury, but no immediate injury was reported.

incident_description:
CFL light bulb installed in standard tabletop lamp with lampshade, with CFL vertical, base down.  Light had been on for about 2 hours and suddenly went off without warning or noise.  Stayed off for about 30 seconds, then came back on for about 1 - 2 minutes.  Flickered and went off again, then came back on.  Slight odor noticed.  Looked into lamp from above and had strong odor of burnt plastic / hot material.  Turned light off.  Saw that base of CFL bulb was scorched and melted, base of CFL tube was burnt, very stong smell.  Unplugged lamp and took whole unit outside because I thought it was going to catch fire.  Opened doors and windows in house to clear the air.  Allowed light to cool fo 30 min before removing CFL bulb and taking photos.

Later that evening both my wife and I had severe headaches from the noxious fumes from the burnt plastics / electronics or other components of the light bulb.  Concerned about the long term health impact of these fumes and the apparently unsafe nature of these products.
justification: The incident caused severe headaches due to noxious fumes, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such events are not common but documented.

incident_description: Box springs dropped unexpectedly from side and mid beams hitting the floor and pinning the box spring tightly against the side of the bed frame.  Had children's fingers been near the side frame they would have easily been pinched, if not amputated.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard that could cause injury, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a Utilitech 100-Watt Equivalent Soft White Compact Fluorescent Light Bulb ENERGY COMPLIANT from Lowe's Hardware on the Internet Model#LBP23TDM  Store Item #340445 on Sep 09, 2011. After a week the bulb began flickering badly and kept turning off. I had to loosen the bulb by partly unscrewing and tightening it back up. About a week later I smelled an electrical odor and a smoky haze. The bulb then went out and the odor disipated. I removed the bulb and put it away. I contacted Lowe's about returning it and they have not bothered to reply. This bulb was highly recommended by a independent Consumer Magazine.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning light bulb causing flickering and an electrical odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Being an insurance agent, fire safety is a paramount concern at all times.  I have 2 cats - so burning candles with a flame was never going to happen in my home.  Thinking candle warmer on the stove was safer - I always opt for this.  I had a small 2-3" candle from Liganore Candles (Liganore, MD) on my candle warmer on the stove.  When I came into the kitchen - I saw hot wax had exploded onto the wall behind the stove, and on various parts of the stovetop also (I have cell phone pics for verification but do not have text capability.) The candle jar had also exploded.  Several days later a friend came over and showed me that my candle warmer had melted a hole in it where it was seamed together.  I have been in contact w Liganore Candle - thinking that was the main problem, because the glass jar they use is not as thick as the jars they sell at Walmart, etc.  Now I don't know which caused the potential fire hazard first.  I bought this candle warmer several years ago from Bed, Bath & Beyond.  Had someone not brought this to my attention, I would have continued to use this creating a more potential fire hazard.  I definitely believe that a recall should be established ASAP.   I live in a townhouse of 7 units together - including children, infants, pets.  This could have been a disastrous situation - and perhaps even deadly.  I am so terribly frightened at this point.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no actual injury or death, but significant property damage and risk to multiple units.

incident_description: We purchased 2 of these fans for use in a small space.  The fan blades are primary colors on one side and pastels on the other.  My daughter spray painted the blades white.  She installed one of the fans in my galley kitchen and the other in a reading nook I have in my living room.  They were installed on Saturday, October 8, 2011.  They both worked fine.  In the middle of the night last night, October 12, 2011, I heard a crash in my kitchen.  When I got up to investigate I noticed white glass on the floor. When I looked around to see where it came from I saw that the glass globe of the ceilng fan had basically exploded.  Neither the fan nor the light were on at that time.
justification: The incident involved property damage (exploded glass globe) but no injury or death, and such occurrences are unlikely given the context.

incident_description: About two years ago, I bought a "Drive" bedrail (model 15064) at Hayward Medical market to assist my elderly mother in getting in and out of bed. The bedrail is shaped like an "L" with the bottom part of the "L" sliding under the mattress. It is secured to the mattress by a one inch strap that goes around the matress. On February 5 of this year, my mother was reaching for the telephone on the bedside table and started to fall out of bed. Instead of keeping her from falling out of the bed, the strap slipped, causing her to fall between the bed and the bedrail. Her neck got caught on the bedrail, strangling her, and she suffocated to death. After her death, I contacted Hayward Medical Market, and they immediately removed that model from their shelves, but a bedrail with that kind of strap should not be sold anywhere.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of the user due to the bedrail's failure, indicating the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is considered rare based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: ProLume compact fluorescent light bulb cover/diffuser, which is part of the light bulb, fell off hitting the floor and shattering into many small and large shards of sharp glass. This is the second one to do this over a period of  3 months. The bulb still works, now it just doesn't have the diffuser/cover on it. The cover looks to have been poorly glued on so it fell off. Thank you for your help. [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a light bulb cover falling and shattering, but no injury was reported. It has happened twice in three months, indicating a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that his spiral fluorescent light bulb, inserted in a lamp burned up when switched off. The consumer is unsure if his bulb is similar to spiral bulbs that have been recalled and knows it has not been recalled. The bulb has cinge marks and blackening at the base. The bulb emitted a burning smell of a fire and had flames come out of the bulb's white ceramic that was a foot long. The flames went a foot above the lamp shade. The consumer heard a popping noise coming from the bulb and saw smoke and watched the bulb dim. The consumer decided not to call the fire department at the time of the incident. The bulb is 42 watts and 120 volts. The consumer cannot recall how he put out the fire.

The light bulb flickered just before the incident. The consumer mentioned that he had the bulb for 18 months and the bulb was on for 4-5 hours and burned up when switched off.  The bulb was purchased over the internet and the company is no longer in business, so consumer could not contact seller. The consumer has yet to call the retailer or the manufacturer since the incident took place.  The damage of the product did not spread to the structure of her home. The light bulb burned the light fixture in which in the bulb was inserted. The consumer was not harmed by the product. The consumer still has the light bulb a year after the incident.
justification: The incident involved flames and smoke but no injury or structural damage, fitting severity level 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated 3 as such incidents are possible but not common.

incident_description: Brand-new, out of box 100 Watt Fluorescent Light Bulb marketed by Whole Foods Market in the "365 Replacement Bulb Series" exploded and shattered 15 seconds after installation and being turned on; It had been installed in a standard 100 volt receptacle, and had shown no signs of damage or mistreatment before being installed.
justification: The bulb exploded but there was no mention of injury, so it's an incident without injury.

incident_description:
We have three sets of cabinets purchased from Lowe's - the first two sets were purchased in 2007 and the third set was purchased in 2008.  The mirrors are push open - push shut latches (push once to open, push again to close).  These are RSI cabinets listed in the recall number 08-533.
My husband pushed one open and the mirror hinges broke, causing the glass to fall out.  Luckily for us, he CAUGHT the mirror before it landed anywhere.
justification: The mirror fell out but was caught before causing injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: A "Bright Effects" compact fluorescent bulb failed in my kitchen. The bulb worked well prior to the problem with no diminishing of light that might indicate the end of life. The ballast in the bulb overheated, melting the plastic and causing the glass bulb to break. The overhead fixture had smoke damage from the incident although there does not seem to be any damage other than surface damage.
justification: The bulb failure caused smoke damage but no injuries or deaths, fitting severity level 2. Such incidents are possible but not common, warranting a likelihood of 3.

incident_description:
A GE Compact florescent bulb type FLE20HT3/2/SW was located in a lamp (inverted free standing bulb,) which was located in our living room. The lamp is a 120v and was plugged into a home outlet powered by 110v.   On the night of 10 Oct 11 at approx  11:30 pm, my wife had gone to the kitchen and noticed a strong " burning smell" and summoned me to the room.  A quick examination noted that the florescent bulb was smoking from its base and putting out light at approx 5% of its normal.  

I immediately reached down and unplugged the lamp.  The bulb continued to smoulder for several minutes.  Upon taking it out of the lamp, the base was noted to be very hot to the touch.

We later replaced the bulb with a conventional incandescent bulb. The lamp was plugged in and turned on and functioned without problem.

I have enclosed pictures of the bulb.  

I have no doubt that should this have continued it would have lead to a fire.
justification: The incident involved a smoking bulb with no injury or fire, indicating a minor incident with no harm. The likelihood is unlikely as it required specific conditions to occur.

incident_description:
Socket holding bulb melted, blackened; bulb corroded


Socket was supposed to take up to a 60 w  bulb; I had only a 6 or 9 w bulb so I did not overlamp the socket

If I had used the 40 w bulb, supplied with the fixture instead of much lower, it could have started a fire

The wires from the fixture to the outlet box were not burned and did not show any sign of damage  or improper installation

I have two other identical sconces, again with reduced wattage bulbs and neither of them has shown any sign of similar blackening/melting
justification: The socket melted and blackened, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased two of the Picchu dressers from an online retailer that are made by Argington a children's furniture company that bills itself as eco-friendly and 'safe'.

I purchased them in April and then in May of 2010 but did not start using them until my son was born in August of 2010. 

Last month (beginning of September 2011) I noticed that most of the fronts of the drawers were literally coming off the drawers themselves.  After further inspection, I saw that the fronts were glued on (no screws or dovetails or any other attachment) and the glue was in various states of failing.  Luckily the drawer front that was the worst and almost completely detached was at the top of one of the dressers so my son couldn't reach it.

However, when I pulled up that particular drawer (that I don't use that much because it's for his "future" clothes that are too big right now) it almost half off in my hand.  It totally freaked me out because my son likes to stand next to me when I am putting away his clothes and had he been right there and I pulled on the drawer just a little harder, it could have fallen right onto him (and it's heavy wood).  

I'm also concerned because he also likes to open and close the drawers and because the fronts are coming off, there are large gaps between the front and the drawer side where his fingers could and almost have easily been caught.  I understand the inherent dangers of opening and closing drawers, but this is more of a finger stuck in a crack that's not supposed to be there type of situation.
justification: The incident involves a potential hazard with the dresser drawers, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood of injury is possible given the described conditions.

I believe the weight limit was somewhere between 180-200lbs...but I'm not posiive. I remember the manual saying something about teenager to young adult, so i would assume at least a person of my size would be supported.
 So anyhoo, I was lying in the bed (BOTTOM BUNK) with my son both our heads at one end on his pillow. He sat up looking for a stuffed animal. I sat up so that I was on the edge of the bed (feet over the side), and he was looking for his animal leaning over the headboard. He reached over the side to get his animal (which was not on the floor but resting on some other stuff that was over the side, so he didn't have too far to reach), and I heard the board SNAP that was under the matress where his pillow rested; his pillow and his mattress sunk down a little bit. I pulled him off the bed. He was not hurt, thank goodness, but it scared him. I know now that the boards are weak and maybe my daughter didn't do anything wrong the first time.

incident_description:
Last week I purchased a fluorescent "shop light" from Menards, which operates a chain of home improvement stores in Wisconsin and elsewhere. It is a twin lamp fixture using T12 bulbs. The manufacturer is American Fluorescent Corporation, 2345 Ernie Krueger Circle, Waukegan, IL 60087, tel 1-800-873-2326, and the model # is ES1248HOCWXSE12.
When the factory installed plug was inserted into a GFCI protected circuit and the light was turned on (using the factory installed switch), the GFCI protection failed but did not "trip". The GFCI protection operates properly when the light fixture is switched-off. I tested the fixture on several GFCI circuits in my 8-year-old house (wired by a licensed technicin) and, in each case, the protection failed when the light was switched on.
I contacted American Fluirescent about this and was told that the electronics in units such as mine are not compatible with certain manufacturers' GFCI outlets. It was suggested tht I try using a [REDACTED] brand GFCI outlet.
There is no notice of this potential problem either on the packaging material or the loss of GFCI protection when using this product. It i unlikely that most consumers would become aware of the loss of GFCI protection when using this product. As I pointed out above, OPERATION APPEARS NORMAL unless one specifically tests the GFCI with the light switched on.
justification: The incident involves a failure of GFCI protection without injury or damage, but poses a potential safety risk if unnoticed.

The consumer stated that she just once she stepped on the switch and the unit caught fire. The consumer stated that the product was on for about 20-30 minutes before it caught fire. The extent of the damage to the product is the foot switch has melted and shorted out. The damage was mostly contained the foot switch. 

The consumer first noticed an electrical smell before she noticed it was her lamp. The consumer stated that damage to her home has been minor of where there was smoldering by the foot switch. The consumer would compare the diameter of the burns to her carpet to that of a cigarette burn. The consumer put out the fire by applying a wet towel on her carpet after powering off the lamp. The consumer never saw flames but saw sparks coming from the underside of the foot switch. 

The consumer did experience electric shock to her right hand when she picked the foot switch. The consumer did not experience any burns. The consumer opted not to call the fire department at the time of the incident. The consumer called the online retailer 2 weeks ago and was not given any information about the firm, therefore has not been able to call them. The consumer was referred by an attorney to call the CPSC.

The electric footswitch/electrical cord that is used in the manufacturing of this particular lamp model is specifically to blame for the incident. This same style of footswitch used to turn the lamp on/off can be found on hundreds of different lamp models. consumer believes that it is the manufacturer of this electric footswitch that needs to be notified.

incident_description: I installed a Philips Energy Saver Mini Twister 18W Soft White CFL bulb in a kitchen ceiling lamp.  About 10 seconds after installing it, the light burned out.  About 30 seconds to a minute after that, I tried to remove the bulb to replace it, and as I was twisting it off felt an extremely hot point and removed my hand.  I believe I was just touching the first few spirals of the tube, not the base, and the hot point seemed to be the lower spiral.  I don't believe I touched the base at all, but can't be sure.  After treating the burn I got from the bulb, several minutes later, I tried again carefully, cautiously just touching the topmost spiral, and succeed in removing the bulb.  After removal, I checked the bulb with my finger and found the base and bottom ring of the spiral tube was quite hot, but no longer enough to burn.  There was no smell of burned electronics or plastic, and the outside of the bulb appears normal.  I was surprised to see a burned out bulb hot enough to burn my finger.  I replaced the bulb with another one from the package and it worked fine.  It would be useful to either design the bulbs to not fail in this mode or warn consumers of the risk.  The box it is from is a 4 Bulb Value Pack, 4 Medium Base Mini Twister, Philips Energy Saver 18W Soft White, Ordering code EL/mdT2 18W 6/4.  I have the bulb available if someone wants to analyze the failure.  I reported this to Philips Lighting via their Contact web page today, October 2, 2011.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury from touching a hot bulb, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such failures are not common but have been reported.
