incident_description:
I would like to alert you of a very traumatic and troubling experience that we had with a Halo SleepSack Wearable Blanket.   I awoke to find our 9 month old son [redacted] screaming in pain Saturday morning in his crib.  I got out of bed to find the zipper of his Halo SleepSack stuck to his tooth.  He was in the fetal position and he must have been attracted to the flapping zipper pull and he put it in his mouth.  His lower front tooth quickly became "caught" in the eyelet of the zipper pull.  The baby panicked and tried to kick the zipper off of his tooth, which only led to more problems.  By the time that I entered the room, the zipper was completely stuck in his mouth. I could not tell exactly where it was stuck until it was too late.  I tried to keep his feet and head together but his absolute panic out of fear and pain caused him to kick harder and disgorge his whole tooth...root and all.  This was incredibly traumatic to everyone involved.  My wife and I had to deal with a large amount of blood, a child that now has barely slept for the past two days due to the pain and the fear of the situation.  I literally became physically sick after dealing with this event. I have experienced many traumatic injuries including help sew my finger tip back on, hit in the face with a baseball bat as well as being hit by two different cars while on my bike and I have never experienced this type of reaction before.  It was awful and an experience that I hope that I, nor any other parent, will have to experience.

I tried to put my son in another SleepSack last night and he refused to sleep in it (prior to putting it on, I have put tape over all of the zippers).   He has worked himself into such a state that he is completely sweating.   After staying up more than two hours past his bedtime, I finally took it off him and  have been forced to give him medication to calm his anxiety.  Once the SleepSack was off and the drugs took effect, he has now drifted to sleep out of pure exhaustion.

In order to save other children from this type of needless injury, I would hope that you would look at redesigning the product by putting a completely flat zipper (sans eyehole) or a rubber pull or other type of pull attachment that would help alleviate this type of needless injury.  The other solution is to have a flap over where the zipper resides so that the child does not see it...other children's brands currently have this solution.

I know this sounds like a freak injury, but it is very traumatic nonetheless and now my child will be walking around for the next 8-10 years without a front tooth and my family (along with our friends) will be constantly reminded of the result of your current product.    I would hope that we can put some sort of happy ending to this story.  As of now, I am searching for answers.

I have attached five  pictures:

1)      The extracted tooth from my 9 month old son

2)      The tag of the SleepSack (clearly identifying it as being a product of Halo Innovations) along with the deficient zipper that caused this gruesome injury.

3)      Picture of the SleepSack that caused the injury

4)      Picture of my son without his tooth due to your product

5)      Picture of my son with all of his teeth prior to the traumatic accident
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury (tooth loss) and trauma, but no death occurred. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such specific injuries are rare despite the product's widespread use.

Gentlemen:

incident_description:
I purchased 9-inch "deluxe" black steel bookends from Staples to hold up cookbooks on a shelf 6' high. I did not like the bookends, because they seemed very flimsy -- nothing like the sturdy old steel bookends we had around the house from years ago. In the middle of the night, one of the bookends completely collapsed (flattened), causing 3 cookbooks to fall off the shelf, damaging them. My concern is, what if a baby's highchair, etc., had been under the shelf when this happened? The sharp corners of a heavy book could cause a laceration, put out a child's eye, etc.

It was suggested by store management that my comments about the product were my "opinion" (I don't think it is my "opinion" that the product physically failed, creating a risk of injury). I went to the trouble to speak to the Office of the President at Staples, and was told, "It does show they're OK" (i.e., the website shows 3.3 "positive" reviews on a scale of 5, with 96 total reviews). But a number of the negative customer reviews are similar to my experience, and mention product failure. For example: "As a Teacher's Aide, I needed bookends to support two classroom textbooks which I use frequently. I thought these would do the trick. WRONG! The one textbook took down the bookend, flattening it! Solid steel? I think it was more like flimsy tin!!" Another customer wrote: "Bookends were just too flimsy to hold books upright...i was really surprised to find such a poor quality item in such a usually great store." (I agree with the comment about Staples usually being a great store, and hope they'll drop this product.)
Here's a link to all the reviews: http://www.staples.com/MMF-Industries-9-High-Black-Deluxe-Bookends/product_408682

I tried to explain to the Office of the President, this is different from a malfunctioning printer, etc., that causes consumer "frustration".......this is a product defect that can actually cause injury. Staples did ultimately advise they would "send an e-mail to the buyer" asking them to look into my comments. But I just thought that stronger action needed to be taken, and I told them I was going to write the CPSC. 

I think these bookends are a great example of products being cheapened to such an extent they cannot even function in their intended role. Consumers have a right to expect that bookends will be able to hold up books. And yes, the 9" Deluxe model should be expected to hold up relatively heavy books, like cookbooks and textbooks, without collapsing! But this product is of such extraordinarily poor quality, there is sure to be a failure at some point leading to a serious injury.

I have not gotten a refund yet from the store, and per the suggestion on your website I will keep the bookends for at least 30 days, in case you would like to examine them.
justification: The incident involved product failure causing property damage (cookbooks), but no injury was reported. Similar negative reviews suggest the issue is not isolated.

incident_description:
I was working with a Bello'O International AT-4203 audio system shelf/rack unit. The lower shelf supports on my rack gave way and crashed to the floor with my amplifier. The amp's cables pulled down every other shelf. My entire system collapsed on my arm. I could barely pull it out from under all the equipment. My equipment itself was damaged, and originally retailed for aroudn $3000. My arm was slightly injured but not seriously.

The actual failure spot is the clips that hold the shelves. They're made out of brittle cast metal and most of the ones on my rack are now broken or deformed. It seems that weight over time will cause them to bend and eventually fracture.

This problem is compounded by the fact the shelves aren't actually held into the clips by any positive means. It's a friction fit with a plastic setscrew. When the clips or screws go out of spec, the shelves are just free-floating with only about a 1/2" of support keeping them from falling.

The company didn't respond to my inquiries with much enthusiasm, and seemed to be of the opinion that they don't care if their products fail catastrophically outside of the warranty period.

If a child had been involved in such an incident, he/she could have easily been killed. I'm lucky I wasn't seriously injured. If any of the glass shelves had shattered I could have bled out, trapped under this pile of hardware.

I can provide photos.
justification: The incident resulted in slight injury to the arm and significant equipment damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is assessed as possible (3) due to the described design flaws and material weaknesses.

There is ample evidence that tight swaddling with the legs in full extension is major risk factor for hip dislocation and hip dysplasia. Kutlu, et.al. identified this association in Turkey almost twenty years ago, and the practice of tight swaddling was changed through public health efforts.[2] 
Kutlu, et.al. JPO 12:598-602, 1992

Although public health efforts were initiated in Turkey following that report, the association between swaddling and hip dislocation has not been completely eliminated. Hip dysplasia was identified at the time of ultrasound study in 21% of the 151 infants that had been swaddled. This was a greater risk factor than any other factor including breech delivery, gender, or family history. 
H. Dogruel, et.al. Intl. Orthop. (2008) 32:415ÃÂ419

 Clin. Orthop. Rel. Res. 184:34-40, 1984

Summary
Tight swaddling with the legs adducted and in extension is widely recognized by pediatric orthopedic surgeons as a risk factor for hip dislocation and hip dysplasia. Twenty of more years ago the lessons of correct swaddling were learned and implemented in countries that practiced incorrect swaddling methods. However, swaddling has recently gained popularity among parents in North America, most likely without knowledge of the risk of DDH. The benefits and risks of swaddling have recently been studied by pediatricians, and these benefits and risks are becoming more widely understood. However, there appears to be a need for greater awareness regarding the risk of hip dysplasia from incorrect swaddling so the lessons of the past will not be forgotten.

The frequency of hip dislocations has increased in Australia correlating with increased swaddling of infants. POSNA Health Alert Regarding Infant Swaddling

The Pediatric Orthopedic Society of North America supports the efforts of the International Hip Dysplasia Institute to educate caregivers and parents regarding the potential risks to hip development with certain swaddling techniques.

Infant swaddling is a technique used to promote comfort and quiet of infants. POSNA cautions parents and caregivers that numerous studies in the medical literature have identified an increased incidence of Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in infants swaddled with their hips in an extended and adducted position.

Although public health efforts were initiated in Turkey following that report, the association between swaddling and hip dislocation has not been completely eliminated. A prospective study of neonatal diagnosis in Turkey was published in 2007.[3] The authors reviewed 3,541 infants who had neonatal examination followed by routine Ultrasound screening at 4-6 weeks of age. Hip dysplasia was identified at the time of ultrasound study in 21% of the 151 infants that had been swaddled. Avoidance of forced or sustained passive hip extension and adduction in the first few months of life is essential for proper hip development.

justification: The incident involved a stapler ejecting staples towards a child's face but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The flawed design makes such incidents likely, especially for children.

incident_description: Lounge chair purchased at Sears in Salem, NH in May 2010 collapsed while a woman was seated in the chair. Chair is designed for outdoor/ patio use.
justification: The chair collapsed while in use, indicating an incident, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I had converted my son's Delta LOV crib (Model #4322, Order # 24030, made on 11 FEB 2004, in Indonesia) in to a youth bed, according to the instructions in step 4. My son, like many other kids, jumped on his bed on day and I heard a scream and him crying. I ran in the room to find him under the mattress and the mattress board. Evidently the whole thing had flipped over on him and he was trapped under the bed. I called the company to file a complaint, and/or receive at least a partial refund of what I had paid for the bed. They took my information and suggested that I not use the bed any more, but that was all they were willing to say to me. My son thankfully was not majorly harmed except for a scrape and some bruising, but with the crib recalls now from babies dying, I feel that the company should have paid more attention to this matter when it happened.
justification: The child suffered a scrape and bruising, indicating an injury, but no major harm or death occurred.

incident_description: My husband and I were awakened at 5am by a loud crash and went outside to find our Martha Steart patio table had shattered for no apparent reason.
justification: The patio table shattered, which is an incident, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: My concern is regarding the Palomar bed frame I purchase from Room Store in May 2011. The bed frame was not delivered until June 2011 and shortly thereafter, we realized that the bed frame is approximately 5 inches longer than the standard mattress length, leaving a large gap between the mattress and the foot board. Although there has been no incident, our concern is that our daughter who is 2 could fall into this gap and injure herself. We realize children fall off beds frequently. However, we feel that this design could potentially increase injuries to young children. We contacted the company and a technician was sent out. They reported that the bed was made to specifications and there was no problem. We also went by the store where the furniture was purchased and were told the same thing. They have not offered any solution to our problem. To summarize, we feel that the bed is unsafe due to the large discrepancy between the length of the bed frame versus the length of a standard mattress.
justification: No incident or injury has occurred yet, but there is a potential risk of injury to a child due to the bed frame design.

incident_description:
6/17/2011 I contacted Baccus Global to inform them that my Vector Model 191 had not been working correctly. The ser number of the VEC 191 is OFD20E201898.  When I plug the VEC 191 light into my 12 volt cigarette lighter in my 2005 [REDACTED], the radio and inside lights came on.  I plugged the 110 volt power adapter into my home to charge my light.  When the small red light is on it indicates itÃÂs charging.   When the charging is complete the red light blinks.  While charging, I noticed the red light had turned off.  When I went to remove the power source it was very hot to the touch.  I than plugged in another Vector 191 110 volt power adapter, it worked for a while and then quit working as the other.  There was also a smell of something electrical burning.  I contacted Baccus Global, 877-571-2391.  I was told that this model was no longer manufactured.  If I had a receipt to indicate when it was bought they would service the item if under warranty.  I donÃÂt have a receipt.  I said I would like to send it back to the company so they may look into why it is doing this.  After convincing the employee at Baccus how important it was that her company looks into this, she took my information.  I know the light is no longer manufactured, but there is others who may have the same concerns.  If I would have plugged this in my garage and walked away what may have been the outcome.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device that became very hot and emitted a burning smell, posing a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: A 23 watt CFL overheated,smoked and spewed brown liquid from two places at the top of ceramic base. Bulb  base got very hot. Fortunately I was in the room and immediately switched the light off,otherwise a fire would certainly  have started..
justification: The bulb overheated and could have caused a fire, but no injury or death occurred due to immediate action.

incident_description: A CFL light bulb began to smolder from its base and went out, alarming four adults. Similar to reports from Consumer Reports about Telstar and Electra CFL bulbs.
justification: The incident involved a CFL bulb smoldering but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. Similar reports suggest this is a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Purchased this bunk bed set early 2010.  It was setup using the instruction provided in packaging.  Over the course of time (Approximately 6-12 months  later) two of the 5 boards under each bed were cracked or  broken.

The items were used by children between ages 6-9 and therefore product should have been able to hold the weight of each child.
justification: The incident involved cracked or broken boards under the beds, but no injury was reported despite use by children.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the Glass table for the patio set exploded close to mid-day with a temperature of approximately 90 degrees on the deck.  She stated that the sun had not been on it for more than an hour, or posisbly 2 hours.

Consumer stated that the glass pieces were shattered into hundreds, if not thousands of tiny peices on the deck.
Consumer stated that she is concerned that this incident could have caused severe injury to someone standing close.

6/22/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer.  The manufacurer, Yotio Corp., apparently is Sears' current supplier.  Consumer's set was purchased in April, 1999.  

Consumer feels that this is an unsafe product.
justification: The glass table exploded but no injury was reported, though there was potential for severe injury.

incident_description: We have a ceiling light that caught on fire.  The light bulb in it burnt.  It burnt the sockets and the lamp is ruined.  Thank God someone noticed smoke and we cut the power.  The light bulb is a Phillips Soft White Plus  self ballasted lamp
justification: The ceiling light caught fire, causing damage to the lamp and sockets, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
While the consumerÃÂs nine year old son who weighs 100 pounds was attempting to climb down the ladder from the top of the bunk bed the bed caved in causing the safety board that supports the mattress to split.  A chunk of piece of wood broke off from the support board. 

It caused the mattress and child to fall into the bottom bunk. There were no injuries reported. The firm was contacted on 7/7/2011 and the representative (representative name unknown) that she spoke with advised the consumer to contact the retailer. 

She contacted the retailer and is currently awaiting a return. 

She is not sure if she will use the bed again in fear that her child could have been seriously injured.
justification: The incident caused the bed to collapse but no injuries were reported, indicating an incident with no injury. The likelihood is possible as the bed failed under normal use conditions.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that after using the mattress for the 1st night she and her spouse started experiencing headaches and sweating profusely, and were restless due to heat emitting from it.  

Less than 1 month later, she contacted the store and was advised to purchase new mattress pads to keep the mattress cool, but this did not resolve the problem.

Consumer and her spouse continued to experience health issues with this product, like numbness in hands and  feet and shortness of breath.  They visited their physician but the illness has not been diagnosed.  The physician advised that it could be related to some sort of toxin which had seeped into their bodies.

6/2011 Consumer contacted the retailer again and was advised to return the mattress pad, and they advise to use different sheets.  The retailer refuse to give them more information on the chemicals used in the product.

7/7/11 Consumer has removed the mattress from the room to see if this would alleviate their symptoms.  Within 2 days they noticed a difference in even the air quality of the bedroom.

Consumer is concerned that this product is a health hazard and feels that it should be reported.
justification: The incident describes health issues like headaches, numbness, and shortness of breath, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as the symptoms persisted and were linked to the mattress.

incident_description: I went in my daughter's room this evening to check on her before I went to bed (as I always do) and it smelled like something was burning. It was the lamp on her nightstand next to her bed. The top of the light bulb was black and literally burning the white off of the light bulb. I unplugged the lamp and took the light bulb out of the lamp once it had cooled. I have pictures of the light bulb and of the lamp. I looked online for recalls and saw that just 3 days ago, Target issued a recall for another type of Circo lamp (not the same model as the one I have) for what seems to be the exact same problem. I am absolutely mortified at this moment. Had I gone to bed without walking into my daughter's room, we could've woken up to a fire in our apartment- or worse- not woken up at all.
justification: The incident involved a burning lamp that could have led to a fire, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
A medicine cabinet mirror by RSI Home Products came crashing down when my wife closed it.
The metal hinge that was holding it broke.
I e-mailed the company asking if I could buy a replacement mirror and heard no response.
About two weeks later new mirrors arrived by Fedex, but two of the mirrors were broken.
I noticed that the new hinges were bigger and sturdier.
I was wondering why the company was so kind to me by giving me replacement mirrors for free, and decided to check the internet to see if there was a recall. There was.
Now I'm mad because they didn't tell me this and the potential for more mirrors to fall is still there.
justification: The incident involved a mirror falling due to a broken hinge, but no injury was reported. The likelihood is high as the company acknowledged the issue with a recall and sent replacements.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed online a recall (see Release 94-043) where the hazard was The bunk beds may develop cracks in the welds and collapse during use, and occupants may be injured. 

On one occassion the consumer's seven year old son whom weighs 55 pound was sitting on the bed when it suddenly collapsed. The beds were not in the bunk bed position but are placed side by side and used as two twin beds.  After taking a closer look at the bed it appears as if the weld broke.

She took a look at the other bed as well and noticed that the weld had broke on that bed as well. She did not contact the firm/retailer both are currently out of business. She has taken the bed apart and placed it on her porch. there were no injuries involved.
justification: The bed collapsed but no injuries were reported, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) as both beds showed weld failures.

incident_description:
The ceiling fan has two compact fluorescent light bulbs in it and was
operating for about 60 minutes when one of the light bulbs burned out. About 15 minutes later, I
smelled a terrible electrical burning smell and my husband and I determined it was coming from
the ceiling fan. He removed the globe and used gloves to remove the very hot fluorescent light
bulb. When the bulb cooled offwe noticed the spiral tubes were at an angle because the base
where they were connected had melted and had turned black. The air in the house smelled
horrible for several hours. There was a scorch mark on the housing of the globe.
If we hadn't been home, it could have caused a fire and our house could have burned down.
justification: The incident involved a burned-out light bulb causing a burning smell and potential fire hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: While working in my basement, I began to smell smoke, when i looked at the light  bulb just over my head (that recently had partially reached end of life) to find the bulb was smoking and extremely hot; this incident left burn marks on the light fixture.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and overheating light bulb causing burn marks on the fixture, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My 1-year-old son got his finger caught in the pullcord which operates the music box on the rocking chair (cord became wrapped tightly around his finger and he could not remove it himself).  He was not injured but just upset.  However, if I had not been right there to help him, he may have been injured.  

[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I purchased a 35" high cherrywood Bodilsen desk from Lowe's Hardware 07-03-2005.

I came one one day to find that the glass top on the desk had disintegrated.  There was glass on the floor, in the same room and the next room, and in the drawer of the desk.

The glass must have exploded as there was glass 18.5 feet from the desk and glass embedded in the laminate flooring by the desk.

No one was home at the time so fortunately no one was injured.  Had someone been near the desk I believe there would have been serious injury.
justification: The glass exploded, causing significant damage, but no one was present to be injured.

incident_description: The consumer says she smelled an electrical burning smell.  She went through the house and noticed the coil of the bulb melting at the base.  It was in a bathroom light.  The consumer says she quickly turned off the light.  She took it out of the socket.  the consumer says it is completely melted where the coils meet the base.  She says it is being held together by some wires there.  The consumer says she has experienced this at least three times with the same brand and type of bulb.  The consumer says the bulb may have been on for about 30 minutes.  The consumer says if she had not been home there would have been a fire.
justification: The incident involved a melting bulb with potential fire risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
While the victim was laying in her bed leaning  her body against the guard rail  that was securely attached to her twin bed within 10 minutes the  guard collapsed causing the victim to fall onto the floor 

The four year old 33 pound and 35 inches tall  victim hit her head on the wooden  floor receiving a bruise on the left side of her head and injured her left arm. She also had bruising to her legs. 

She was taken to see her Pediatrician (DoctorÃÂs name not provided) where he diagnosed her with a mild fracture to her left arm in which he placed in a sling. She had also fractured her collar bone. 

No cat scans were performed and the child was prescribed with medication and the victimÃÂs parents were advised to not allow her to use the arm for proper healing.

There are plastic pieces at the bottom of the guard real that broke off causing the guard rail to break and injuring the victim.  She noticed that the labeling on the product indicated  for ages 2-5.

 She has been using the rail for approximately 2 years. She has discontinued the use of the guard rail and will contact the firm to make them aware of the incident.
justification: The victim suffered a mild fracture to her left arm and a fractured collar bone, along with bruising, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the product's age indication and the fact that it broke after 2 years of use.

incident_description:
I bought two of these candles. They smelled lovely and looked ever so pretty. I brought them home and lit them. Here are a few observations.  

1) The flame gets wicked high, although trimming the wick helps.  I was worried the flame would set the wooden container on fire at the slightest draft.

2) When the candle finally burned down, I blew it out. When I picked it up, I noticed the wax had seeped through the wood and pooled on the kitchen counter. This isn't the sort of behavior I like in a candle.

3) With a lot of candles, you can take a minute to use the bathroom, make dinner, or fold the laundry while they burn--not this candle. I wouldn't take my eyes off this candle for a minute.

Maybe I'm just paranoid, but a candle where the wax seeps through the container doesn't strike me as being safe.  Maybe coconut shells are fireproof or something.
justification: The candle's high flame and wax seepage pose a fire hazard, but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: Our GTC compact fluorescent light bulb went out and immediately after, we saw smoke coming from the socket.  We quickly removed the light bulb to find that the bottom of the bulb had melted and turned black and was extremely hot.  We went around the house to find any other GTC fluorescents and found one other in a similar condition (not melted, but black on the bottom) and removed all GTC bulbs and threw them away to prevent any possible fires.
justification: The incident involved a potential fire hazard with no injury or death, and similar issues were found in other bulbs, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her computer lamp had broken on it's own while she was in another room. The consumer stated that she he heard a loud shattering from the next room and found that her computer lamp's glass covering had unhinged itself and shattered on her computer table. The consumer stated that the glass covering just unhinged itself and worries that she could have been injured; luckily she was not and the glass caused no damage, it only made a mess. 

At the time of the incident the product was not in use. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer; However, she did visit the retailer on May 26, 2011. The retailer explained to her that since the product only had a warranty of 90 days they could not assist her. The consumer found on that this is not the first time this exact product has been reported to the CPSC.
justification: The incident involved a broken lamp with no injury or damage, but the product has been reported before, indicating a possible recurring issue.

incident_description: The consumer says her son was on the seat on the dining room table.  He was reaching over and fell off of the table.  Consumer took son to the emergency room.  She says the daycare her son attends also had two incidents of children falling off of the bumbo seat.  The consumer says that both children at the daycare got skull fractures from the incident.  Her son was not seriously injured.  Consumer says that her son has a bruise on his forehead.  The product is recalled under Release # 08-046.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who offered a refund.
justification: The son fell off the table and sustained a bruise, indicating a minor injury, and there were previous incidents with more severe injuries at the daycare.

incident_description:
Consumer's son went to the back yard around noon and found out that the glass table shattered in thousand pieces (reason why unknown)

Consumer feels that the glass table could pose a laceration hazard.

Consumer called and explained incident to retail storeÃÂs rep. (name unknown) who said that they do not sale the glass table patio set any more.  Consumer would like manufacturers to know that this is dangerous.
justification: The glass table shattered but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the unknown cause of the breakage.

incident_description: I won a small votive style candle in a glass container hand made by [REDACTED] owner of Tranzformations a Center for Spirit [REDACTED] in a raffle.  The candle had a large piece of jet stone, which is a type of coal and it will and does burn.  When I used the candle it turned into a torch after a short while caused by the wax soaked jet.  It caused a nasty fire in my home while giving off billowing stinking black smoke. I was burned on my hands putting out the fire and some minor damage to done to the surroundings.  This could have been much worse if I had not been RIGHT there when it happened.   I called Tranzformations to complain about this and the owner, [REDACTED], ignored my phone calls for several weeks.  When I finally did speak with her, she told me it was my fault and that I should expect such things when burning her candles and that her customers know this. This is truly an out rage. Somebody is going to get hurt or killed by her carelessness.  I feel I have done everything I can do and I hope filing this report will help.
justification: The incident caused burns and minor property damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is high (4) due to the candle's design and the owner's disregard for safety.

incident_description:
Item: Sylvania LED retrofit bulb # LED8A/DIM/F/830 
Bulb burst into flames and also caught fixture on fire during normal use. I was nearby when the fire started so I was able to unscrew the bulb and put out the flame before the fire spread. After unscrewing the bulb, the flames continued burning and were being emitted from between the screw base and the heat sink portion of the bulb until I put them out.

incident_description: 5 month old girl was placed to sleep on her back in a velcro 'snuggle' or 'swaddle' wrap in her crib. Mother returned a few hours later to find infant lying unresponsive on her stomach. Infant was later pronounced dead at a local hospital. Cause and manner of death were listed by the pathologist as 'undetermined.'
justification: The infant was found unresponsive and later pronounced dead, indicating the highest severity level.

incident_description:
I purchased the RelaxRight toddler pillow for my daughter who is 21 months old. I purchased it from toys r us online. It's a "memory foam" pillow designed for toddlers. 

I woke up yesterday morning and walked into my daughter's bedroom to find foam bits in her hair, stuck to her lips, all over her, the crib, and a 2 ft radius around the crib. I found that she unzipped the cover and bit and gouged hunks of the pillow. Upon further inspection I found I could easily push the pillow apart myself with little to no effort. 

I called her pediatrician and they instructed me to also alert NJ poison control. They told me that if she is presenting normally and wasn't showing signs of choking she was okay. 

I feel lucky that she did not choke and I don't want anyone else to have that happen to them. I am very disappointed in that RelaxRight pillow.
justification: The incident involved a toddler biting and spreading foam bits from the pillow, but no injury occurred as confirmed by the pediatrician.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bedford Desk from Pottery Barn and noticed a chemical smell coming from it, especially when I open the desk drawer. I thought the odor would dissipate after time, but it has not. After sitting at the desk for long periods on some days, IÃÂve come away with an intense headache. I got a letter several days later ÃÂconfirming our agreement to send a Merchandise Card in the amount of $100.00ÃÂ. There was no agreement and she has not returned my calls. IÃÂm still waiting for Pottery Barn to refund the purchase price of this desk.

incident_description: The 14 watt energy efficient bulb in my lamp blew up, flames came out of it and fell all over my carpet burning holes in it  Thankfully the glass did not harm me as I was sitting next to the lamp although shards of glass were all over the room.  The explosion sound was so loud my ears rang for two days.
justification: The incident caused property damage (burned carpet) and loud noise affecting hearing, but no physical injury occurred.

incident_description:
One morning while getting ready for work, I was showering. I smelled a burning odor and upon opening the shower door I realized the bathroom had filled with a foul smelling smoke. It was coming from an overhead pendant light above my bathroom vanity. The fixture was equipped with a 13watt compact fluorescent light bulb from a company called Bright Effects. (Part # LBP13T2C2) I immediately turned off the power switch and opened windows and doors to allow the smoke to escape. After removing the bulb from the fixture, I noticed burn marks and evidence of overheating to the point of melting the plastic base. 
If I had not been in the immediate vicinity of this malfunction when it happened, I dare to imagine what might have happened.
justification: The incident involved a burning light fixture with no reported injury, but potential for harm if not addressed immediately.

incident_description: Light Bulb Caught Fire
justification: A light bulb catching fire is an incident with potential for harm but no injury was reported.

incident_description: We have a Bromley patio table that was purchased at Target in March 2011.  We use the table almost daily.  The table shattered completely.  This fortunatly happened when we were not near it.  We have two children and a dog.  We can not image what would have happened if we were sitting at the table.  The glass went everywhere.  It was stuck in between the boards on the deck, in the bushes and on the chairs.  After investigating online I found on Target's website this is very common with this table.  Safety is a risk  with this product.  Please do not wait until someone is severly hurt to have this product removed.
justification: The table shattered completely but no one was injured, indicating an incident without injury. Online reports suggest this is a common issue, making it likely to occur again.

incident_description: I purchased from Lowes Bright Effects Compact Fluorescent Lightbulbs 100Watt #210691 manufactured by FEC, 4901 Gregg Road, Pico Rivera, CA 90660 about 10 months ago. I place one in a table top light fixture in the living room. It was a standard table lamp, not a 3way, not on a timer. These bulbs are sold to last up to 7 years. My wife became startled and we started searching for the source.  We found the source blackened and smoking and unplugged it.  After awhile it was cool enough to remove and it had turned black.  I did a google search of this brand and found pages and pages of consumer complaints of the same situation.  This bulb needs to be alerted to the general public, recalled, and removed from use.  If we were not home I beleive that a fire would have certainly started.

incident_description:
Consumer feels that her mattress or foundation of her bed is safety concern because she canÃÂt sleep. The consumer stated that she wakes up drained and sometimes experiences headaches. The consumer feels that this may be derived from the fire retardant chemicals in the bed The consumer has had 2 similar mattresses and experiences similar difficulties. The consumer had this mattress for about 4 months before she got rid of the mattress in March of 2011. She contacted the manufacturer of the first mattress throughout December of 2010 and January 2011 who would not assist her referred her back to the retailer.
