The consumer is on her 4th foundation for her bed and the fourth one is a polymer and doesn't have the same odors of the other foundations she purchased.
justification: The consumer reports headaches and disrupted sleep, which are health impacts, but no severe injury or death.

incident_description:
On June 9, 2011 I bought this candle from Bath & Body Works. I bought it home and put it on my wooden dining room table on a large cork coaster that I put all candles I burn on. I work at this table in the evenings and burn candles almost year round at this location. The candle was sitting right next to me about a foor away. This is a small 1.6 oz candle in a plastic cylinder container.

When the candle had burned down a little more than halfway, I noticed that the plastic cylinder container had begun to melt and started to become disfigured. I carried into my kitchen on the cork coaster and doused it with water to extinguish it.

I made a couple of copies on a copier to try and show you the beginnings of the melt down. In the one picture that shows the label of the candle tou will start to see the degredation on the right-hand side. I also copied the bottom of the candle in question to give you further product information. Please remember that this began when I was seated right next to the candle so the degradation of the container is not that severe though it is evident more in the actual product than in the enclosed photo copy.

There was no injury involved with the beginnings of the melt down with this product in my experience. I attribute this to the fact that the candle was sitting so close to me. I don't think the average consumer sits this close to a burning candle prodcut for a period of time and therefore may miss seeing the potential for the melt down of this product which could be a potential fire hazard.

The moment after I doused the cande I called customer service line for Bath & Body Works. I expressed my safety concern about this product. the woman that took the call over the phone said she would have someone else from customer service call me back. I never did get that call back but I received a generic email several days later. I don't think Bath & Body Works expressed a level of concern with regard to their product that is a potential fire hazard.

It is my opinion that this candle product has the potential to melt down and start a fire.I am certain that the CPSC will investigate this safety concern. I have the product in question with me and two others of the same candles I purchased at the same time (have never been lit) if the CPSC wishes to see the product or investigate further.

Thank you for your concern.

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a melting candle container with no injury, but potential fire hazard was noted.

incident_description: while at the neighbors we were burning world market citronell votives while swimming the candle wax caught on fire and was smoking my 7yd old daughter put a hand full of water on it and it exploded causing flames 3 ft high this is from a small votive the wax flew on one of her feet and caused severe burns and she had to be rushed to the ER where she was treated for 1st and 2nd degree burns and released. When I went on the web and goggled water and citronell I was amazed of how may sever injuries and deaths this product ( not world maket) has caused I went to the store and looked at a few and the warnings about using water on these are very small and hardly noticable there are on the back below the directions. I want a larger warning on the front of these products and a public accouncment about these by these companies! Most everyone I have spoken to about this had never heard of this reaction and danger. I watched my child do this not thinking anything would happen if I had only known I would have never let this happen!
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns requiring emergency treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description:
I'm reporting this because I own the Outdoor Bromley Patio Table from Target Stores.  Mine hasn't broken yet, but a coworker of mine also had this table and hers has broken.  I have a 17 month old daughter so this concerns me of her safety eating at this table.  

My coworker had about 6-8 guests over to her house for dinner, and unprovoked, the table shattered into a million pieces causing injuries to some of her guests.  She said at least 2 of them received lacerations.

After hearing of this news, I went to Target.com to read the reviews on the Bromley items.  I discovered that within the past two months, from June 8, 2011-July 1, 2011, there have been 3 additional reports of this happening to other consumers on the Target website.  The item can be found at: http://www.target.com/dp/B003ZEUKKI?sortReviews=-rating&ref=pd_tab_grev_sort_HighestRatingFirst

and

http://www.target.com/Outdoor-Patio-Bromley-Rectangular-Dining/dp/B003ZTNFD2/ref=in_de_detail-item-display


Please read the aformentioned reports here:

----"DO NOT BUY - PIECE OF JUNK June 8, 2011 
Reviewer:  [REDACTED]
Sitting at dinner last night with six people seated and food on the plates, glass exploded into a million tiny pieces, cutting 5 of the 6 people at the table. I was wearing jeans, so I was spared. 

This was supposed to be a relaxing dinner after the death of a loved one and we ended up cleaning tiny pieces of glass for about an hour. 

This is a cheap piece of junk that is poorly made. I am going to Target and demanding they make this right. "

---"DANGEROUS PRODUCT! SHATTERED GLASS! July 1, 2011 
Reviewer:  [REDACTED] 

We purchased this table about a month ago and were really enjoying it until the glass on the table shattered for no reason; thankfully no one was hurt but it was difficult and time consuming to clean up. By this time there were no other tables available in the 3 closest Target stores. When I called Target they gave me the manufacturer's number and I said I had to deal with them. Seeing from the other reviews, I'm not the only person to whom this has happened. It could be very dangerous-Target should think about recalling this product and offering a refund/replacement as the item is still available online. "

---"Worthless June 20, 2011 
Reviewer:  [REDACTED]
Purchased this table a few months ago and only used it a few times, the heaviest thing to sit on this table was a glass of ice tea. Then last week I see the umbrella leaning to the side and when I go outside I discover that the table shattered into a million pieces! Only thing I can think of is that the Houston heat caused it to COMBUST, but it's patio furniture! Since we no longer have the reciept and paid cash, Target has brushed me off to the manufactor. Shame on Target for selling a worthless piece of merchandise and not standing behinde it!" 


Please please please look into this CPSC!!!  This table appears to have a defect and who knows how many more have experienced this with their Bromley table.

Thank you.
justification: The incident description reports multiple instances of the table shattering, causing lacerations to guests, which qualifies as injuries.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he started experiencing symptoms of shortness of breath approximately 1 month after he started sleeping on the pillow and mattress.  He stated that he was also nauseous when he got up in the mornings but this feeling would dissipate a few minutes later.  These items have caused him to also develop headaches, dry burning and itching eyes, sore throat, congestion, nose bleed, loss of energy, lower neck and back pain.

Consumer stated that he didnot smell any chemical odor.  He also stated that the company advised that a liner should be used with the mattress.

Consumer stated that he visted his physician with a rash on his left knee but there was no diagnosis for this. 

Consumer stated that he was advised by a friend to stop sleeping on the items, he discarded the bedding and started sleeping on his sofa and kept his bedroom closed.  Some of his symptoms has disappeared but he still has the shortness of breath.

Consumer stated that he has a report form to send in to Tempurpedic company.

Consumer feels that this product is a health hazard and should be reported.
justification: The consumer experienced multiple health symptoms including shortness of breath, nausea, headaches, and a rash, indicating injury but no death.

incident_description: I purchased a Colorado Kids Bunk Bed from My Bobs Furniture Discount Store. I also purchased insurance under Goof Proof for five years their name is Guardsman. There address is P.O. Box 88010 Grand Rapids, MI. 49518. The problem with the staircsase continues and is unsafe for children walking up and down stairs. I had two servicemen come to the house and repaired them. They also mentioned that the wood pieces are not sturdy enough to be walking up or down. The staircases are broken in various locations. They continue to crack one after the other. My son fell off the stairs and I immediately called them. I am concerned that this product should be listed to buyers and not go through with purchase due to continue breakage of stairway.
justification: The incident describes a child falling off the stairs due to structural issues, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: We have had a compact flourescent bulb manufactured by n:vision part number edxo-23 installed in our kitchen for the past 6-9 months. Today the bulb began to flicker like a tradition florescent bulb when either the starter was going bad or the bulb was going bad. The light was turned off for 15-20 min and restarted. Once power was reapplied the florescent buldb violently exploded over my wife's head, shattering the florescent bulb, sending glass flying around the kitchen and narrowly missing her eyes. The base of the compact florescent exploded apart as well. I have a second bulb  from the same manufacturer that has a burn hole on the side of the base of the bulb which I was going to return to Home Depot for disposal.
justification: The bulb exploded violently, sending glass flying, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Regarding the Dorel Pine finish bunk beds, I noticed in the recall that it was mentioned the side rails had a tendency to crack.  I have recently been given a brand-new bunk bed set, purchased from Kmart, which is a pine-finished set manufactured in Vietnam by Dorel.  It was made in December of 2010 and therefore is not included in the current recall; however, two days after assembling the set, I noticed that one of the upright support posts has cracked all the way from the bottom of the underside-top bunk down to where it adjoins with the bottom bunk.  Apparently Dorel has not corrected whatever flaw led their old bunk bed sets to crack, as their newer ones are also having the same problem.
justification: The incident describes a cracked support post in a bunk bed, which is a structural failure but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Greenlite compact fluorescent light bulb burned out by literally burning around its base. I saw actual sparks and small flames when it happened, and when it was done, the base was charred and there was a strong chemical smell permeating two floors of our house four hours.

I've actually seen this happen with several Greenlite CFL bulbs, but this was by far the worst case, so I decided to take pictures of the bulb and file this report, although it has taken me a while to find the time to do so.

I am concerned both about the potential for one of these bulbs to cause a fire when it burns out, and by the potential for toxic chemicals like mercury to be released into the air.
justification: The incident involved sparks, flames, and a strong chemical smell, indicating a potential fire hazard and release of toxic chemicals, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
Purchased a leather chesterfield sofa, manufactured by SpectraHome in China.  It was delivered on June 13, 2011. 

There is a strong chemical smell coming from this sofa which permeates the air in my home. When I sit on this sofa, my pulse rate increases immediately. When my clothing or any fabric comes in contact with this sofa, the odor is transferred to the fabric.

I wiped the entire sofa (including all 3 cushions) with a damp cloth (water) to remove any residue, flipped it over and vacuumed the fabric underside to remove any particles, left a HEPA air filtration unit on 24/7, and have the windows open as often as possible to air out the room.  

Today is July 7, 2011.  Three and a half weeks after this sofa was delivered and the dark, musty, heavy chemical smell is still prevalent throughout my home, the odor still transfers to fabrics, and my pulse rate still becomes elevated if I sit on the sofa.
justification: The incident describes physical symptoms (elevated pulse rate) and persistent chemical exposure, indicating potential health impact.

incident_description: You used this futon to sleep on and use as a couch. When someone went to sit on it one day the bar in front fell on my foot. The reason I believe this happened is because there was no extra support in the middle. Let's call a T-BAR. On all the other futons out there they this.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (foot being hit by the bar), and the likelihood is possible as it occurred due to a design flaw (lack of support).

incident_description: My Martha Stewart patio table top spontaneously shattered.  One day I simply walked outside and it was in thousands of pieces.  I had not idea what had happened until today I heard that this has happened to others as well and that it appears to be a manufacturing defect.  These tables should be recalled and customers' money refunded.
justification: The table shattered without causing injury, but it indicates a potential hazard.

incident_description:
I purchased two leather chairs.  I was allergic to the leather.  I believe the problem is that the chairs are likely to be contaminated with dimethyly fumarate (DMF).  This is an antifungal agent intended to prevent the leather from getting moldy during starage and shipment from overseas.  

Per the internet this problem showed up in England late 2006 to the present.  Also you can refer to a safety article by consumerreports.org dated May 19, 2009.

I returned the leather chairs for an exchange.  The store where I returned the chairs was great in exchanging them.

I have never been allergic to any leather product prior to this.  Apparently overseas leather manufactures are adding or exposing an unsafe product to the leather shipped to the USA.

Please investigate and advise.

Thank you
justification: The incident involved an allergic reaction to a chemical in the leather chairs, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) based on the description of similar incidents occurring overseas.

incident_description: I had purchased a Martha Stewart patio set some years ago from Kmart and I came home last night to find that my glass tabletop had exploded for no apparant reason.
justification: The glass tabletop exploded, which is an incident, but there was no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
Consumer feels that her mattress or foundation of her bed is safety concern because she canÃÂt sleep. The consumer stated that she wakes up drained and sometimes experiences headaches. The consumer feels that this may be derived from the fire retardant chemicals in the bed The consumer has had 2 similar mattresses and experiences similar difficulties. She purchased one in November of 2011 and the first night she woke up from a terrible dream and her heart was pounding. The consumer had this mattress for about 4 months before she got rid of the mattress in March of 2011. The second mattress the consumer bought was a different brand purchased on 2/24/2011 and was not delivered until March 11, 2011 The consumer has not experienced any rashes or markings from the mattresses.

 She contacted the manufacturer of the first mattress throughout December of 2010 and January 2011 who would not assist her referred her back to the retailer. The consumer contacted the retailer throughout December of 2010 and January 2011 and initially was not receiving any assistance. The consumer had called her credit card company who assisted her in eventually returning the mattress back to the retailer on the 3rd of April 2011. However, in March the mattress was removed from her home. 

The consumer called the retailer and manufacturer in May about her second mattress and both indicated they would not take it back because she had the product for longer than the time allotted to return the product. (consumer had the product for 3 months versus the one month permitted to return the mattress). The consumer feels that her first mattress "permeated" her home and the smell of her mattress in her home was evident. The consumer is on her 4th foundation for her bed and the fourth one is a polymer and doesn't have the same odors of the other foundations she purchased.
justification: The consumer reports headaches and sleep disturbances, which are health impacts, but no severe injury or death.

incident_description:
Regarding compact fluorescent bulbs (Sunbeam 13W #E217916 #53SJ).  Additional information on bulb 120V 60Hz 200mA FE-IIS-015W 15W 0504 Made in China.
_ _ _ _ _ _ _ _

On 6/26/11, a Sunbeam CFL began to smoke and was very close to starting on fire.  Fortunately, I was standing in the same room and noticed a burning plastic odor, looked up and saw the smoke coming from the bulb on the ceiling fan.  If I had not been in the room, or worse, had not been home and that light were left on, there would have been a fire in the house.  

I attempted to see if there were recalls for Sunbeam CFLs, but did not see any such information at sunbeam.com.  I have used CFLs for years but am now leery, especially with Sunbeam brand.
justification: The bulb smoked and nearly caught fire, but no injury or death occurred. The incident was noticed in time to prevent a fire.

incident_description:
Yesterday was the second time that a Greenlite flourescent light bulb started to catch fire in our home upon burning out.  Luckily, I was sitting under it when I heard it fizzle out.  My husband and I looked up and saw sparks and smoke coming from the bulb and socket, plus we could hear sizzling sounds.  

There was a strong odor that caused me to have an immediate negative reaction for which I had to take my asthma and allergy medicine.

My husband turned off the power and when the bulb had cooled, he removed it.  This is the second time a Greenlite bulb has caught fire upon burning out.  The bulbs are only 1 year old!
justification: The incident caused an asthma and allergy reaction requiring medication, indicating an injury, and it has occurred twice with the same bulbs.

incident_description:
I sat down into the chair,  the right arm rest snaped apart at the two lowest bolt holes at the seat.  The back of the chair collapest without warrning and the chair shot out from under me.  My left arm is badly cut, brused,  and the bone is badly brused and/or fractured.  My right leg was banged up pretty good,  with impact injuries includeing a smashed knee cap and loss off skin extending down below the knee for 7"...  This incedent caused me to fall into the typing table (arm injury),  and landed into the cpu knock it six inches out the back of the cabnet,  snaping off the front usb ports connecting the mouse and keybord(s) rendering them uselless.

I did a google search,  and looked at product reviews on this chair (walmart.com) ,  and just about every custermer review stated that this chair broke with out warning in less than two weeks of ownership,  and others were injured too...   By the way,  all of the chairs are braking at the same bolt locations,  left and right side of chair,  causing suddin collapes of the back to seperate completly from the seat.

This type of chair construction is also noted on other styles of chairs,  and are braking apart causing injuries and collateral property damage .

This chair is clear and present "DANGER' !,....  and recalled,  removed,  from the retail marked imideatly !,    ie;   Walmart,  and any other outlet.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries including a potentially fractured arm and a smashed kneecap, indicating a severity level of 3. The widespread reports of similar failures and injuries suggest a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
I purchased a Quoizel ceiling light fixture last year at a closeout sale.  Twice the glass globe on the fixture fell down on my bed.   I went and purchased a new fixture for obvious safety reasons.
To my shock, when examining the Quoizel fixture it showed that that the insulation in the fixture was actually burning and some aluminum sheet insulation was actually melting on a light bulb.
the fixture advises no larger than 60W, but I only had 40W bulbs. 
The glass globe falling could have created a serious injury had someone been sleeping at the time. However, the burning insulation could have resulted in a fire.
justification: The glass globe falling could have caused injury, and the burning insulation poses a fire hazard, though no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: I have a similar model to the bunkbeds recalled by Dorel Asia SRL previously. I own model WM2450 in Honey Pine and purchased the product in early spring of 2010. One of the cross support beams that hold up the mattress has split in half, the screw on one side splitting the support beam the runs beneath the rows of mattress cross supports. I have heard creaking from the remaining boards when I'm making the bed as well as when my children crawl into bed. No one was injured during the incident, but it does cause me worry, especially with the other recalls noted for the exact same issue.
justification: The incident involves a structural failure in the bunkbed but no injuries occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is high (4) due to the known recalls and ongoing creaking sounds indicating potential for further failure.

incident_description: Consumer stated that his fireplace lighter has no safety mechanism. The consumer stated that the lighter functions like a normal cigarette lighter with the exception of a long 8 inch tube where the flame comes out of. The consumer stated that this product has no safety mechanism to prevent children from using the product, though the packaging claims it has a "safety trigger". The consumer opened the packaging of the product and noticed the issue right away. The lighter is operated by fuel and the consumer was not hurt by the product. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer about the issue. The product has not caused any damage to the consumer's home nor appear to show any signs of damage.
justification: The incident involves a product defect (missing safety mechanism) but no injury or damage occurred.

incident_description:
Consumer feels the fluorescent light could poses a fire hazard.

Consumer stated that the light was on his phone ring consumer when to answer the phone -- while consumer was on the phone consumer saw the light was flicker then he saw smoke and flames coming out the light bulb then consumer turned the power off immediately the fire stopped.  Consumer opened the door and windows to air the smoke in his house.
justification: The incident involved visible flames and smoke from a light bulb, posing a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased at end of season a Martha Stewart table & 5 chairs at Bluefield K-Mart 2004. (Mftrd in 2003) The table has lazy susan that shattered on our enclosed screened patio room on Friday, May 27th. We were shocked the glass went everywhere; we had everyone at home earlier in the day including our grandchildren; thankfully it did not happen while they were in the room. It took us over 2 1/2 hours to clean up the pieces of glass. We attempted to call Martha Stewart # but could not be dialed from my phone.

I also called Kmart [REDACTED] in Bluefield, WV about this.  Talked to [REDACTED] (manager on duty) and she said they no longer carry Martha Stewart products and she advised me to call consumer protection agency and I called you. I couldn't find my receipt. I am sending you all the information I have on the Martha Stewart product I bought at Kmart. I also have copies.
justification: The glass shattered but no one was injured, classifying it as an incident without injury. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the nature of glass furniture.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the base of a his fluorescent light bulb burned out. The product had the plastic around light bulb and could have caused a potential fire. The product is a spiral light bulb and was plugged into a kitchen ceiling light fixture. The light bulb was in use for about 2 1/2 years and was on for about a half hour before burning. The damage has not spread to the structure of his home. The consumer removed the bulb by hand after allowing it to cool for about 5 minutes. 

The consumer decided not to call the fire department and was not injured by the bulb. The bulb is blackened at the base and one half of the base has melted away. The consumer called the manufacturer on May 30th of 2011 and sent him return material to send the product to them for analysis. The consumer has yet to call the retailer. The wattage is 14 watts and .2 amps.
justification: The incident involved a burned-out light bulb with potential fire risk but no actual injury or structural damage occurred.

incident_description:
Relax Right Toddler pillow specifically says for children ages 2-5.  I bought two for my 2 year old twins.  The pillow came with a zippered protective cover.  The store that I bought them at did not sell additional pillowcases.

I put my twins to bed with their new pillows.  In the morning, I discovered that they had unzipped the "protective cover" & had picked off several small pieces of the foam pillows.  They had the small pieces in their mouths, hair and ears as well as all over the bed.  They could have easily choked on the pieces of foam.

I e-mailed the manufacturer and received a standard response.  I replied that this product was not safe & did not carry the warnings on the box & label that he said it did.  I have not had a response back.
justification: The toddlers could have choked on the foam pieces, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My mother purchased a La-Z -Boy Lift Chair ( w/pw Reel/HE) and was unable to use it because of the hazardous design flaw at the base of the chair. (photos enclosed ) The upholstered portion ofthis La-Z-Boy lift chair is suspended 4" above the floor exposing the metal frame at the base of the chair. The metal frame flares out beyond the upholstered portion of the chair and at each end point of the support frame there are bolts sticking up 1 inch from the frame. I became aware of this frame problem when I hit my foot on one of the exposed bolts when I approached the chair to move it.
I am concerned not only about my mother getting injured using this lift chair, since she is 97 years old and a diabetic, but also about her health care giver when she approaches the chair to assist her.
justification: The exposed bolts pose a significant risk of injury, especially to elderly users and caregivers, as evidenced by the reporter hitting their foot on the bolt.

incident_description: My 10-month old son was sitting in the kristi g Go & Grow Chair manufactured by Kelsyus. He was secured in the chair with the 3-point harness. When he leaned forward the chair tipped forward and he fell to the ground, head first, bumping and scraping his forehead. In addition to the chair tipping, the harness clip gave away, allowing him to fall halfway out of the harness.
justification: The child suffered a head injury and scrapes from the fall, indicating a severity level of 3. The harness failure and chair tipping suggest this could happen again under similar conditions.

incident_description: This incident is regarding a patio set including 2 chairs and 1 table purchased 1 year ago at Sam's Club in Lewisville, TX.  Here is the information on the cushion...REG.UT1484(CN), Virginia Registry Number 20040, Certificate No: 66312.  Manufactured By: Sunjoy Industries, Jiashan Economy Dev. Zone, Phase 4, Zhejiang, 314100.China.  The incident occurred on June 25, 2011.  My father was sitting on one of the chairs and leaned back slightly when then the chair broke at the base.  He is a senior citizen, not overweight, and very shooken up.  The chair appears to be made of rod iron and I have pictures of the product.  Please contact me for the pictures.
justification: The chair broke while in use, causing the senior citizen to be very shaken up, indicating potential injury.

incident_description: In May a bunk bed by this company was recalled (Model #DA1026P) so I contacted the company for the repair kit. When we got it, all the pieces were mismatched but we tried to make the best of it. Once applying the kit though, we realized it was damaging the wood because they were ill-fitting or non-fitting. So, I contacted the company again and was asked to take pictures of the damage, which I did, and sent to them. I got a reply saying thanks for the pictures, please sent your contact info so we can better help you, and since, have heard nothing. I contacted them again, and have now been told they never received the pictures, even though in their reply emails it clearly stated they did. We are now left with beds that are even unsafer than before, and still absolutely no fix at all. I assume others are having the same issue so these unsafe bunks are still out there.
justification: The incident involves a recalled bunk bed with mismatched repair parts causing damage, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Consumer believes that her light weight glass ceramic table could pose a laceration hazard.

4:30 pm Consumer said that she was water up her plants when she heard a big crash when she looked back she saw her glass ceramic table shattered in thousand pieces.The wind apparently caught the umbrella knocking over the table. 

Consumer called and explained incident to Lowe's Customer Service Department. Consumer's attempts to write a product review on Lowe's website have been rejected. Consumer tried at least 4 times to alert other consumers to a possible injury.
justification: The incident involved a shattered table but no reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the described scenario of wind causing the table to break.

incident_description:
Caller had installed a new none enclosed ceiling fixture in kitchen area, put two CFL Bulb in the two available sockets, however one of the bulbs was not in the socket more than five minutes when it began chattering (rapid snapping sound) burned base of cfl bulb and the socket in the celing fixture TCP in NE Ohio who distributes to Home Depot.
Caller's wife turned light switch off, he examined fixture which checked out alright, he removed the two CFL bulbs noticing that one is fine and the other is burned at the base with the ceiling fixture socket being burned with melted contacts.
He contacted the manufacturer who advised him that the bulbs are created so that fire could not occur.
He has stated that he seriously doubts this because there was soot all over the end of the light bulb and it became hot enough to melt the contacts.
Caller is very qualified to make this statement and to perform this process due to his being an Biomedical Electronic Technician at *** and one of his duties was being responsible for the electric safety of the hospital.
He would very much like for this product to be investigated.
justification: The incident involved a burned bulb and socket, but no injury or death occurred. The caller's qualifications suggest a credible report of a potential fire hazard.

incident_description: The bed posts are getting vertical cracks in the wood on the upper bunk bed.  The bunk beds are made by Dorel Asia, model No.:WM2450 in honey pine color.
justification: Cracks in the bed posts indicate a potential structural issue, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: Wood rails cracking and causing the bunk beds to be unstable, I purchased 2 sets of these bunkbeds Model number WM2450 man. date 07-2009JYF made by Dorel Asia
justification: Cracking wood rails can lead to unstable bunk beds, posing a risk of collapse, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
Consumer had a smoking spiral fluorescent bulb in his dining room light fixture covered by glass a cover. The bulb was flickering and then the consumer turned off the light switch to power the bulb off. When the consumer turned the light switch back on, it started to smoke. The smoke and the smell of it persisted and the consumer turned off the switch and removed the bulb. There were 2 other fluorescent bulbs in the fixture at the time. 

The consumer stated that there was black smoke but no external flame and no damage to his fixture. The consumer feels if he wasn't there to observe the bulb there could have been a house fire. The consumer has yet to call the retailer or the manufacturer and opted not to call the fire department at the time because he felt no need to call them but did say the light bulb is blackened.
justification: The incident involved a smoking bulb with no injury or damage, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as such incidents are possible but not common.

incident_description: While taking a shower, consumer observed bathroom light flickering and then dimmed. Shortly thereafter, a short orange flame was observed shooting form the base of the bulb. Consumer shut off the light switch and needed to blow the flame out to extinguish. The incident bulb was removed and later submitted to the local fire department. The local fire official submitted to state fire marshal's offfice on or about 3/7/11. The incident bulb broke during transport and was received by CPSC investigator on 4/28/11.
justification: The incident involved a visible flame from a bulb, which was extinguished without injury, indicating a non-injury incident.

incident_description: We had a Phillip lightbulb - flouresnt energy saver flood R40 in our recessed lighting.  The lights were on and all of a sudden the glass part of the bulb crashed down to the floor and shattered.  The flouresent coils remained intact and were still lit until I turned off the switch.  If someone was standing under the bulb they could of been seriously injured.
justification: The incident involved a bulb shattering without injury, but with potential for harm if someone was underneath.

incident_description: My son was in his Bumbo chair and kicked back while in the chair and fell.  He suffered a concusion and a fractured skull.
justification: The child suffered a concussion and fractured skull, which are serious injuries.

incident_description:
I purchased a Tempurpedic mattress when I was 5-months pregnant almost 2 years ago.  When the mattress arrived, I was unable to sleep in it due to the terrible nausiating offgassing.  I slept on the couch for the remainder of my pregnancy hoping that the smell would dissipate with time.  After I brought my newborn baby home, I tried to sleep in my bed again with my baby.  The smell was still there.  I called the Tempurpedic company and asked if there were any toxic chemicals in the mattress, and I was told there were not.  I explained that I had a newborn and I was breastfeeding, so if there was anything toxic, I needed to know.  The Tempurpedic customer service rep. assured me that the bed was totally safe.  She said the smell was normal and would go away.  It has been almost 2 years, and the bed still smells terrible.  I need to know if this bed is toxic.  I do not want my family to continue sleeping on it if it is.  When I called again to report the smell, I was told that noone else had complained about the smell.  Meanwhile, I found several complaints online.

Moreover, when we purchased the Tempurpedic mattress, we purchased one for my in-laws, too.  My father-in-law was diagnosed with a rare form of cancer almost 6-months after purchasing the mattress for him.  I am not sure if the mattress is a factor, but I do not want the mattress to contribute to his failing health.  If the mattress is toxic, I do not want him sleeping on it any more.  He has been through a great deal of traumatic medical events.  He has had one health problem after another after another since then.  If this mattress is toxic, I need to know.

I greatly appreciate your investigation of this matter.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes prolonged exposure to a strong odor from the mattress and concerns about potential toxicity, but no direct injury or death is confirmed.

incident_description:
Fire
in house
Product description Costco Wireless Motion Sensor door/entry light
8 wide area led bulbs contains 3 duracell AA Batteries new

Wife and I were shopping for fathers day, daughter home alone with 2 dogs. She was ill and sleeping on couch with the dogs when she was wakend by the sound of a smoke alarm. Entire house filled with smoke. As she investiagted source of smoke she found on my bathroom vanity top the fire coming from the vanity top. She extinguished the fire which broke the mirrors, ruined the stone tops and cabinets and filled the entire house with soot.
Upon investigating further when I arrived home we found the motion light on the vanity top and it appears this is the source of the fire.
I lloved this light I turn it on at night and it is used as a motion light to find the bathroom at night and during the day turn it off. I t has never been hot and has always worked. Purchased new in Kendall Fl (Miami) from Costco and I have 2 more one in use by mother in law and one still in new package.
justification: The incident involved a fire causing property damage but no injuries or deaths.

incident_description: Last night we started noticing a burning electrical smell in our kitchen area. We did not know where it was coming from so I turned off the lights and the electrical breakers and called an electrician. While waiting for the electrician to come out turned the breakers on and still no smell. Then when I turned on the lights I started to smell the burning electrical smell. It turns out that inside one of my hanging light fixtures I started to see a small amount of smoke. Not sure if there are any safety recalls about this bulb but just wanted to let you know about it. I believe I purchased it a Ralphs Supermarket Mira Mesa (San Diego, CA) in 2007.The bulb says E176533 Greenlite 23W/ELS-M/Z 2700K 120V 60HZ 390 mA T33.
justification: The incident involved a burning smell and smoke from a light fixture, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: Had a Sylvania CFL that started smoking and was seconds away from erupting in flames. I have photos.
justification: The CFL started smoking and was close to erupting in flames, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Strathwood Anti-Gravity Adjustable Recliner Chair, Dark Brown with Champagne Frame (Lawn & Patio)  Widely available; I purchased from Amazon.com
The safety lock on this chair does not hold in locked position. After checking that the safety lock was in place on my new chair, I sat down and the chair immediately folded up on me, flipping me over backwards and throwing me onto my head, elbow and back on the cement floor. The lock does not fit firmly or hold in place. I weigh 122 pounds and it flipped me.
justification: The chair's safety lock failure caused the user to be thrown onto a cement floor, resulting in injuries to the head, elbow, and back.

incident_description:
The following Childs bunk bed. Manufactured by Ming Yih Furniture company, distributd by Home Elegance Inc.  Model number B27 Date of manufacture June 2010. 
Has an issue with the ladder rails splitting where the rungs attach.
justification: The incident involves a potential safety hazard with the bunk bed ladder, but no injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
The product is a HIKARI 20 Watt tubular Halogen Bulb repalcement used for under cabinet lighting.

The item was purchased from 1000bulbs.com. The part number is JCD 130V 20W G8 35MM.The country of origin is P.R.C.
The incident occurred on Saturday June 11th, 2011. The lights were on during a family event for some time. Suddenly one of the bulbs exploded, it blew the lamp cover off and sent glass materials in all directions. Fortunately, no one was hurt but some food had to be thrown out.
This is the first time I have ever had a bulb explode. I am removing all halogen lamps from use in my home as a result. 
I am concerned about the quality of this product as manufactured. I suspect these and all Halogen bulbs are being made outside of the US. I am very suspect of the quality controls to produce this product in the Peoples Republic of China. I don't believe these products are safe for use by anyone anylonger.
justification: The bulb exploded, causing property damage (lamp cover blown off, glass scattered, food ruined) but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:
While in the bathroom, I could smell something burning. I looked up at the light bar above the mirror to see one of the Sylvania compact fluorescent light bulbs smoking and the plastic housing melting profusely. 

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product and am in fear of my house burning down. About a year ago we replaced ALL of our light bulbs in the house with these thinking it'd be great for our house to be more energy efficient. After this incident I'm regretting investing all this money in this "upgrade" - fearing my house is now a fire hazard due to Sylvania's faulty design.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and melting light bulb, posing a potential fire hazard but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My son started screaming about 20 minutes after i stuck him to bed when i went to go check on him his head was stuck between the toddler mattress and the headboard of the bed. Apparently the wood slat closest to the headboard broke and the mattress fell and his head became trapped.
justification: The child's head was trapped but there is no mention of injury, indicating a severity level of 2.

incident_description: side matress support split and broke
justification: The mattress support breaking is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: I would like to report the following company: http://www.kuddlebundle.com/ . They are marketing pillows, loose blankets, and extra padding for young babies--all of which are proven to increase the risk of SIDS. I'm concerned that their product could cause additional infant deaths that would otherwise be preventable. Thank you.
justification: The products marketed are linked to increased risk of SIDS, which can lead to infant death.

incident_description: My husband, daughter, and I were standing on our deck next to our Whitley Oval Chaise lounge, purchased at Sam's Club and sold under the La-Z-Boy brand. There was a light breeze blowing, and we had the umbrella up for shade. Suddenly and without warning, the umbrella buckled and fell over, nearly striking us. The steel pole bent completely in half, and the top of the umbrella struck the ground in an instant. This is a heavy steel frame umbrella, and could easily have injured or even killed one of us had we been closer. I immediately contacted Sam's Club, La-Z-Boy, and BJI (the patio furniture subcontractor for La-Z-Boy), provided photos of the damage, and have not received a response. There is no visible wear or rust in the bent area - it appears to be strictly a poor design that placed too much stress on one point in the pole.
justification: The umbrella fell and nearly struck the family, indicating a potential for injury but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: Bromley rectangular dining table (patio table) bought at Target 1 year ago shattered into tiny pieces without anyone near it.  I have been on the phone with Target, they will not warranty the product because it is past 90 days, the mfg. of the product will not warranty the product because a different mfg. makes it now.  On the Target website, there are other reports of the same thing, with injuries being reported, in the customer review section on this product.  Thankfully no one in my family was injured, yet - the glass shattered all over the patio.  My concern is that no one at Target - the store, the corporate customer service dept., the mfg. seems to care, I hope someone is not sitting at this table the next time it happens.
justification: The table shattered without injury, but similar incidents have caused injuries, indicating potential risk.

incident_description:
The Emergency Ligthing is located in a an office building. On Saturday May 14,2011 The Orange County Fire Department received a phone call from the building's security personnal indicating that the emergency ligthing began to smoke and caught fire. The Security Personel was able to put the fire out prior to the Fire department . 

There was another fire in June of 2009 for the same emergency lighting at the same location in which they assumed it was just an electrical surge. Since the incident occurred reently he was able to link the two incidents together.

 While doing some further research online he noticed there was a Alert (see Alert #01-514) [a recall involving a different manufacturer] where the hazard The emergency lights have an internal electrical component that could overheat . He
justification: The incident involved a fire in emergency lighting, which was extinguished without injury, indicating an incident with no injury (severity 2). The recurrence of similar incidents suggests a possible likelihood (3).

incident_description: A flared and candle burned out of control.  The home owner moved the candle to her sink and attempted to extinguish the candle with water.  The flames reached the ceiling when the home owner applied water to the candle.  The home owner called the fire department.  Fire fighters responded and extinguished the candle.  There were no injuries.
justification: The incident involved uncontrolled flames and required fire department response, but there were no injuries.

incident_description:
I have purchased the same tea lights from the Bed Bath & Beyond store in Seattle ([REDACTED]) for almost four years.  However, in the past six months the tea lights are different: they have an odd, sweet/nauseous smell (even the "unscented" ones), and the "wax" looks different.  The main safety issue is that they do not burn properly.
The flame does not melt all the "wax," if you can even actually call this substance a safe form of wax.  The flame dies down just enough so you can't tell that it's still lit, even with very little light in the room.  Several times someone put their hand near or tried to pick up a hot (still burning) one, and almost burned themselves, because the tea light did not look like it was still lit.  The flame just gets very small and dim--but it's still burning!
Please examine these tea lights closely.  Someone should test what's being put in the "wax."  And please take them off the market before someone gets hurt.  Thank you.
justification: The tea lights pose a burn hazard as they do not burn properly and can mislead users into thinking they are extinguished, leading to near-burn incidents.

incident_description: My Homecrest glass patio table spontaneously exploded on June 6, 2011.  I heard a loud sound around 11am and looked out the window to see the glass table shattered into thousands of pieces.  It was still cracking and I made my way outside.  There was no outside trauma to the table and it is covered by a canvas canopy.
justification: The incident involved a glass table exploding, which could have caused injury but did not in this case.

incident_description:
I bought an "ANTIGRAVITY CHAIR" at Costco. During normal use it  tipped backwards and I sustained a concussion. The company asked me to send it back to them. I have not. I noticed they are still being sold at Costco. I believe they have an inherently dangerous design and can fall backwards and can cause serious head injury..

Item Anti-Gravity Chair  ITM/ART 536966
justification: The incident resulted in a concussion, which is an injury, and the product is still being sold with a potentially dangerous design.

incident_description:
On Friday, 06/03/2011 at approximately 7:00PM in the evening, my youngest daughter and I noticed the smell of "burning electronics" in our kitchen. I quickly turned off the stove, and a shout brought the rest of the family in to the kitchen to track downt he smells source.

We located the source. It was a CFL in our ceiling fan. We quickly turned off the ceiling fan lights and waited for everything to cool. I then inspected the lights and found that one of them had melted/burned at the point where the fluorescent tubes attach to the base. The base is normally an off white, but was now orange to purplish-brown, and clearly burned/melted.

The information printed on the base of the CFL is as follows:
GREENLITE
23W/ELS-M/A 2700K
120V 60Hz 330mA
E 176533
FLUORESCENT
SELF-BALLASTED
LAMP 61Y6

I inspected the other two CFLs in the ceiling fan. Anothe one of the same manufacturer/model was showing signs of burning/melting. The third CFL in the fan was a different manufacturer/model and had no signs of problems.

Inspecting the rest of the CFLs in the house, I found two other GREENLITE units (same mode) that were showing signs of discoloration at the base, turning orangish, but not the signs of melting yet.

The other CFLs in the (different manufacturers) did not have signs of this problem.


Additional Information:
-------------------
These CFLS are not new. They have probably been installed for more than a year.

3 of the 4 CFLS were installed in ceiling fixtures so they where inverted, with the base at the top and the 'bulb' at the bottom.

I have digital pictures of the units, and will hold on to them for a few weeks in the event that you wish to analyze them.
justification: The incident involved burning/melting of CFLs but no injury or death occurred, and the issue was promptly addressed.

incident_description: On or about January 2011, we purchased several Maxlite Compact Fluorescent 13-watt bulbs at Walgreens and other stores in the Hamden, Connecticut area.  Two of the bulbs failed and melted, exposing the electronics inside the base of the unit and emitting a noxious odor.  The first failed in February 6th in the light in our kitchen range vent, where it could have started a fire.  The second failed in June in a bathroom fixture, and my son and I both felt dizzy and lightheaded after just a few seconds near the melted bulb.  Even before the bulb popped and melted, I'd been feeling dizzy for hours after sitting in the bathroom with that light fixture on that day.  In one two-bulb fixture, the Maxlite bulb was completely melted, but the other bulb (a 13-watt Sylvania) was intact.
justification: The incident involved bulb failures causing dizziness and lightheadedness, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as it happened twice in a short period.

incident_description: CFL bulb started smoking. I removed bulb and noticed burned and blackened area where CFL tubes are connected to the base. The bulb was installed on November 17, 2010 and failed on May 12, 2011. This is not the first time I have had a problem with this brand and model of CFL. The bulbs are supposed to be long-lasting, with a 2 year warranty.
justification: The bulb smoking and showing signs of burning indicates an incident with potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: CFL light bulb made by Sunbeam started sparking out of the vents in the base of the light bulb and started on fire.
justification: The light bulb sparked and caught fire, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: I have Roman Shades which were installed in my home by 3 Day Blinds. I recently contacted them to inform them that the blinds were literally coming apart, the strings were becoming brittle and breaking and despite my efforts to fix them, they kept getting worse. Finally I called them to come out to evaluate them and repair them. 3 Day Blinds is coming out next week to get them and "fix them" but today I put my 2 year old granddaughter to sleep in the room and she choke herself in the cord. If my daughter didn't hear her choking and check on her, she would have died. I have the photos to prove it. So now the cords that kept breaking and the blinds that looked awful are now clearly potentially a fatal choking hazard for children. I had no idea that these blinds could be so dangerous or I would never have put my granddaughter anywhere near them.
justification: The incident involved a near-fatal choking hazard to a child due to faulty blinds, which could have resulted in death if not for immediate intervention.

incident_description: I smelled a burning odor and went to the living-room and found smoke coming from the top of the floor lamp. I immediately unplugged the floor lamp.  I then tilted the lamp to see what the problem was and noticed the base of the CFL bulb had a burnt appearance. I removed the bulb and, on closer inspection, found charring near the base of the helical tubes. It also appears that the base was starting to melt. I could not determine if the helical glass had broken.  I know CFL bulbs contain mercury, so I checked the bulb for a Hg (mercury) marking, which I found.  I am worried not only about the potential fire hazard these bulbs present, but that my wife and I may have either handled mercury or inhaled it's vapors. I did some research on the Internet and found numerous incidents where CFLs  had either "smoked or burned" exactly as mine (I could not see the bulb until after I unplugged the light and don't know if it was actually burning). I think these bulbs are both a fire hazard and a potential health risk.
justification: The incident involved a smoking CFL bulb with potential fire hazard and mercury exposure, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The mainstays pine wooden bunkbeds are having the same issues as the (another company) bunk beds.  The suppot slats and the side frame have broken during use.  The children using the beds weigh less than 50 pounds.  The support and frame should not be breaking in less than 6 months usage.
justification: The incident involves structural failure of bunk beds during use by children, but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
On April 11,2009, we purchased a La-Z-Boy glider-recliner and received delivery on May 30, 2009.  The chair began squeaking in November 2009.  The squeaking became progressively louder and began leaving a black dust that permanently stained our carpet.  In mid-May 2010, when the squeaking became unbearable, I telephoned the store where we had purchased the chair.  The salesman who answered the telephone refused to give me the telephone number for the service center, said this sometimes happens, and told me to put candle wax where it was squeaking.  My husband looked at the chair and could not ascertain where the salesman thought we should put the wax.  So, in early June 2010, I telephoned the store again.  This time a different salesman provided me with the telephone number for the service center.  When I spoke with the service center, they told me that the chair was just out of warranty and I would have to pay to have the chair repaired and for delivery.  They also told me the permanent black dust on my carpet was metal dust and would not come out.   The delivery service picked the chair up on June 25, 2010, and returned the repaired chair on July 2, 2010.

The night of December 6, 2010, while rocking my baby I heard a loud noise and nearly flipped over in the chair.  We discovered that the head of a bolt had been sheared off.  The next day, I telephoned the service center.  They advised me that the warranty on the repair had expired and I would be responsible for the cost fo the repair and delivery.  After speaking with the Customer Service Headquarters in Michigan, I was told that I would only need to pay for the chair to be delivered.  The delivery service picked up the chair on December 10, 2010, and returned it on December 17, 2010.  I was advised that the service center had completely replaced the internal components of the chair.

On May 31, 2011, while my husband was rocking our toddler, we heard another loud sound.  After inspecting the chair, we found that once again, the head of a bolt had been sheared off.  I believe that this chair is unsafe and that it could cause an injury.
justification: The chair's repeated mechanical failures and near-flip incidents indicate a potential for injury, though none have been reported yet.

incident_description: I purchased two Brookside Candles in glass jars from Anna's Linens. Upon arriving home and unwrapping the candles one of them shattered. I returned the next day to exchange the candle. After using once I went to remove the lid from the candle jar and the lip shattered shooting shards of glass at me and cutting my arm in two places. I believe these candles are made from inferior glass which causes them to shatter with nothing other than normal use.
justification: The incident resulted in cuts to the arm from glass shards, indicating injury (severity 3). The description suggests a pattern of glass shattering with normal use, making recurrence possible (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Purchased from their website a Sobakawa Cloud Pillow as seen on TV infomercial.  Nowhere on the TV ad or website or anywhere else prior to purchase is there any mention that there is a safety hazard with this product.  When I received the product, the label on the pillow and an insert in the package states that the pillow is made of highly flammable material that burns rapidly, depletes oxygen quickly, and releases hazardous gases when burning.  Both the pillow itself and the pillowcase are labeled as hazardous.  This is a product made for use by a sleeping person in a bedroom, so the safety hazard is unacceptable.  

Furthermore, the seller charges a high shipping/handling charge which is not refundable.  It seems clear that their sales strategy is to fail to disclose the unsafe condition of the product to encourage sales, while making the high cost of returns a deterrent to consumers to return the product.
justification: The product poses a significant safety hazard due to its highly flammable material, which could lead to severe injury or death if ignited, especially in a sleeping environment.

incident_description: consumer's friend purchased High power spotlight to use on the hunting trip. while charging the spotlight in the car The charger for the spotlight caught fire & burnt car seat, friend's hunting suit, destroyed the charger & spotlight. consumer sustained minor burns to hand.
justification: The incident resulted in minor burns to the consumer's hand, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the provided frequency data.

incident_description: My children's bunk bed was part of a repair kit recall. The repair kit I was sent does nothing to fix the problem. Some of the slats supporting the mattress broke in half. The repair kit only takes into account the corners of each bed. That is not where the problem is. I reported the problem when it originally occurred but do not remember when that was. I ordered the broken pieces and had my brother reinforce the bed with a solid mattress support. I think Jardine should recall all of these items and refund the customer's especially since most people wouldn't have someone who builds wood products be able to fix the bunks.
justification: The incident involves a product defect and repair kit failure, but no injury or death was reported.

incident_description: We have bought and broken two of extra long hideaway bed rails from Regalo in the past 6 months.  After the first one broke, I figured we must have put too much pressure on it or something.  But now that I have broken a second one, and I wasn't putting much pressure on it at all, I feel it is a defect in the product.  I have inspected how each one broke and it is right at the connection point between the bed rail and the rails that go under the mattress b/c there is only a small, thin metal disc holding it in place.  That is very poor quality construction and it really ought to be recalled immediately.  It doesn't break so much that it falls over, it breaks so that it pulls back from the mattress just far enough for a small child to get stuck.  That is way too dangerous.
justification: The incident involves a product defect that could lead to a child getting stuck, indicating potential for injury but no actual injury reported.

incident_description: Twice, my daughter's dresser has fallen over on her. It was made and installed by Ashley Furniture (store we purchased from was in Nashua, NH) and it sold as a children's bedroom set as well as just the dresser itself. It is the Creme Cottage model. I have attempted to contact the store as well as Ashley Furniture through their corporate website with no answer. The size and mass of the dresser could seriously injure or kill a child.
justification: The dresser has fallen over twice, posing a risk of serious injury or death to a child, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
We own a storkcraft bunkbed in the caribou style; product number 09720-129.

Our bed has cracked in the side rail that connects the head and footboards this damage is far beyond the capabilities of its 30 pound occupant. The damage is very similar to a recall you issued the 5th of this month from [another company]. Our damage was noticed this last weekend by my older son. The crack goes all the way through the wood and I have no apparent recourse in this matter. I have tried to contact the Storkcraft company and send them pictures of this damage but my emails are rejected due to the fact that they don't recieve messages with pictures. I want a new side rail from the company and our bed it right on the border of being covered by their 1 year warrenty. I have been unable to reach the company by phone at this point.
justification: The bunkbed has a significant crack, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
This safety concern deals with a Disney Tap Light that came with a sleeping bag set.  The light is about 5.5" in diameter.  The tap portion is located on top and is about the same diameter.  When replacing the batteries (4 x 1.5AA) the battery compartment was melted.  The compartment was so dis-formed that 4 new batteries couldn't be placed in the compartment securely.  The melted section also created a hole in the compartment that exposed some wires.  The wires were also melted.  I feel this could be a major problem that could be a fire hazard.

The information on the battery compartment cover is as follows:
Disney
Manufactured by Idea Nuova, Inc
Made in China
INI: 09101106622
justification: The incident involves a melted battery compartment and exposed wires, posing a potential fire hazard, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that yesterday his Westinghouse 35 watt lens flood halogen bulb exploded when his wife turned on the hood vent of the stove. He has had the bulb for almost 4 years and had two bulbs inserted and one exploded. His wife was not injured but she was startled. He has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer. He reported no further damage to the structure of his home and no fire ensued. He felt it was imperative to report this incident to the CPSC.
justification: The bulb exploded but no injury or damage occurred, only a startle, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 as bulb explosions are possible but not common.

incident_description: Light bulb had gone off and on several times.  When consumer went to change bulb, he noticed it had melted around the base of the bulb and at the top of the coil the glass had bubbled out.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning light bulb with visible damage but no reported injury.

incident_description: I purcced an eletric foot warmer from Cozy Winters, 4821 Golden Foothill Parkway, El Dorado, CA, 95762, and after about a month's use, the eletric cord came out of the blanket, exposing the wires. The blanket where the cord was attached is a flimsy cheesecloth like material. The wires were taped together with a paperlike tape. I was lucky not to get a severe electric shock, or electrocuted. I beleive this is a very unsafe and dangerous product that should be taken off the market unless improvements are made.. Thanl You [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved exposed wires which could have caused severe injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Kids Only Resin Chair, patio furniture, needs a labeled height recommendation beyond which the product is not safe. 
My grandson, 21 months of age, 30 lbs, 34.5 inches tall, while attempting to sit in the chair, fell backwards and hit his head on a hard ceramic tile floor.  
The chair's front legs are set wider than the rear legs which may favor a backward momentum. 
It seems prudent to label the chair with height and weight recommendations beyond which the product is not safe.
justification: The incident resulted in a child hitting his head on a hard floor, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I bought a foam mattress from Bobs discount furniture store. There was a warning of a possible smell coming from the mattress. It has been strong enough that i was getting a minor headache and we have not been able to sleep in the bedroom. My wife is pregnant and we have small pets. I am concerned that the fumes emanating could be dangerous. Although the fumes are going away, I am worried if there are any short or long term effects from the chemicals used in the foam?
justification: The fumes caused a minor headache and disrupted sleep, indicating a health impact, but no severe injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
Compact Flourecent Light Bulb Burn Out, Melt, Smoke

Feit Electric: 75W Equivalent CFLs, Item No: ESL18TM/18 purchased at Costco, Hillsboro, OR USA

2 of these bulbs have created hazard when they failed.

1) Plastic base housing turned brown from heat and completely melted hole in the housing
2) Smoke from the melting

Why are these bulbs safe? Feit said this is "normal" burn out. That is absurd. 

I consider these unsafe and have put my house in fire danger.
justification: The incident involved melting and smoke from the bulbs, indicating a potential fire hazard but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We had an incident involving our 4 daughters, ages 8, 6, 5, and 3, and a FEIT CFL light bulb.This bulb is not older than a year at best.  It is hard to describe accurately without being an electrical engineer, exactly what happened. After our girls were playing in our guest room with the lights on, then moving to another area to play, my wife, [REDACTED], noticed a peculiar smell coming from the room. It smelled of electrical burning/overheating. This smell led her to the guest room where she found a particular lamp flickering.  She immediately turned off the power to the lamp, and unplugged it. The fumes were so potent as to overwhelm her and give her chest pains. She immediately opened the windows to ventilate and stepped outside for her own safety. Thankfully our children had moved to another floor in the home.  She found the source of the fumes to be emanating from the base of the CFL. Upon further inspection, she noticed an area of the bulb housing that was burnt. She asked our children about it, if they noticed anything, and our oldest daughter stated she heard a funny sound coming from that lamp. My wife Goggled, "FEIT Electric" and found several incidents of reported bulbs exploding, and house fires. Feel free to Google this information yourself
justification: The incident involved potent fumes causing chest pains, indicating injury, and there are reports of similar incidents with the bulb model.

incident_description:
I have several Philips Marathon light bulbs in my house. About a year ago, the outer covering over the florescent part dropped off. Today, another did the same. Apparently, I'm not alone: http://www.saferproducts.gov/ViewIncident/1171552

Philips told me they'd send a check for all the light bulbs I had in my house. They asked that I mail them back and would provide shipping labels, though not boxes or money to cover the packaging.

When I asked if this was a common problem, a known one, they said there had been incidents reported but nothing widespread enough to think a recall should be issued.
justification: The incident involves the outer covering of light bulbs falling off, with no reported injuries or deaths, and Philips acknowledges some incidents but not widespread enough for a recall.

incident_description:
My wife and I have repeatedly cut ourselves on the thin sheet metal "corner protectors" on our Sealy Posturepedic box springs.They are probably 20 gauge steel, or perhaps even thinner, without any sort of rolled edge. They are vertical, so if you put your foot down too close to the corner of the bed, you risk a nasty cut.

The date below is only the latest of at least 5 incidents. Although no injuries needed more than first aid, several I was cut through the thick skin of my heel, and my wife was cut through the skin under the ball of the big toe.
justification: The description mentions repeated cuts requiring first aid, indicating injury (severity 3) and a high likelihood of recurrence (likelihood 4) based on the frequency of incidents.

incident_description:
We had just put this bunk bed together a week or so before my 10-year-old daughter fell through the top bunk.  Luckily, my 5-year-old son was on the other end of the bottom bed because a slat of wood broke in half with very sharp edges, ripping from the side.  No one was hurt, but it is not very comforting to know that the bed could break that easily.  My daughter weighs about 80 pounds, so she was well under the weight limit and this should not have happened.  

At least in our case, I believe the accident happened because the boards do not fit flush with the full width of the bed so the screws were too close to the edge instead of further back into the meat of the wood.  I also do not see how the spacing of these boards is safe, but the company assured me it is up to standards and would not send any extra slats to fill in the big gaps.
justification: No one was hurt, but the incident involved a structural failure of the bunk bed, indicating a potential safety hazard.

incident_description: CFL lightbulb burned in lamp. Lamp did not seem to be on, then started flashing and flickering in bright yellow and orange and there was a strong odor of electronics burning. Lamp was a floor lamp with basic on-off switch. shade/diffuser was a wide translucent white cone completely open at the top. I turned the lamp off, unplugged the lamp then unscrewed the very hot bulb. There appears to be burned material in the center of the top of the base, surrounded by the CFL tube. Some of this burned material may be dust or insect remains. Bulb: Lights of America 2414-T Self-Ballasted Lamp, 120V 60Hz 14W 230umA(394) We have no record of where or when this bulb was purchased.
justification: The incident involved a burning CFL bulb with no reported injury, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated 3 (possible) as such electrical incidents can occur but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
The unit was a Duro-Test Spiralux 26W 5500K fluorescent bulb.  Rated at 10,000 hours and made in China.  FCC ID: N6AFJEEJL0898.  It has labels "C", the UL listing logo, and "US".  Other text include "Listed 22KJ" and "Self-Ballasted Lamp".

The bulb was in our bird aviary room (a bedroom) in our house.  This morning, my wife saw that the bulb began to catch fire and smoke.  The smoke came out of where the bulb connects to the top of the ballast.  She unscrewed it (still smoking) and went outside and sprayed water on it with the hose.

Our birds (100-150 canaries) may have died from the fumes.  This is breeding season and the babies certainly would have been harmed.  Going further, the house may have burned down if the plastic shell around the ballast incinerated and caught nearby combustibles.

The unit was purchased about two years ago and ran approximately 12 hours/day.
justification: The bulb caught fire and smoke, potentially causing the death of birds and risking a house fire, indicating a high severity with a low likelihood based on the description.

incident_description: I recently purchased four Aero-Tech 100W light bulbs (100A19) from Menards.  I was tired of replacing bulbs in my dinning room chandelier with bulbs that would last less than a year.  So I purchased these with the hope of it lasting 10x longer.  I've had them in for nine days, and tonight one of them exploded (literally)!  It showered glass all over the dinning room and really scared my little kids who were near it.  I have never had this happen before to any other bulb I've used.  They claim Superior Quality, but this is totally unacceptable.  Please let me know how you will be handling this...

The other night, after my wife and I had gone to sleep, the lamp came on by itself, accompanied by an electrical buzzing noise and smoke. It took several clicks of the switch before it would turn off. I immediately unplugged the lamp and removed it from the bedroom. The lamp has two bulbs operated by a 3-way switch; the base contains a 3 watt night light and the main bulb is a 40 watt max standard light bulb. We had a 14 watt CFL installed in the main fixture and a 7 watt night light bulb that came packaged with the lamp installed in the base. I tested the CFL in another known good fixture and it operates normally with no buzzing or smoke. The lamp base has an electrical burned smell to it.

After talking to Sealy on the phone, it was determined that the common product was visco elastic, which is the memory foam.  The spring mattress also contained a layer of memory foam, or visco elastic. Took a few minutes to figure out where the smell was originating from, and came across the lamp, with smoke steaming up from the top. I was able to safely unplug the lamp, and unscrew the bulb before any serious damage or injury occurred, however, while unscrewing the bulb, I noticed that the entire hard plastic base of the bulb was really hot.

incident_description:
I purchased a string of outdoor patio lights at a Menard's store in Coon Rapids, Minnesota.  The set cost $29.99, plus tax. The product is called "40 ct. Globe Light Set," by Enchanted Garden.  The box carries the UL emblem.  The lighting set is comprised of 40 small Christmas-style lamp bulbs, each encased within a 1.5 inch diameter clear glass globe.  The lamps are attached at approximately 1 foot intervals along the 41 foot long cord.  The light set is designed to be plugged into a standard 120 volt outlet.

When I removed the product from its packaging, I noticed that a few of the glass globes were broken.  The glass globes are extremely thin, and while gently grasping one in my hand, it broke into shards of thin glass.  Fortunately, I was not injured. I carefully set the lights down on the lawn in front of my house and observed that several more globes shattered.  I had to pick up the shards of glass due to concerns that someone may step on it.

I made no further effort to use the lighting set and returned it to its box.  I plan to return the set to Menard's for a refund.

incident_description: Late April 2011.  Purchased Eclipse thermaback blackout curtains from Target Annapolis, MD.  Smell from curtains induced nausea, vomiting and diarrhea in my 19 year old son and myself in 2 separate incidents.  Chemical odor coming from curtains.

incident_description: Bought counter-height dinette set from Mor Furniture in Glendale, AZ.  After it was delivered we didn't use it until the next day (May 6th) and at that time we noticed that the chairs were designed in such a way as to cause extreme tipping hazard backwards. It isn't.  Ours is model# WM1848R3C, manufactured 10-2009XGX.  However, the side rail of the top bunk is broken, and I have been quite concerned about it.

The broken pieces include the safety rail which runs from the top bunk's headboard to where the ladder joins the bed.  There should be a bar that holds it steady and secure half-way between the headboard and ladder, which screws vertically into the three horizontal boards.

When we put the bed together, this piece would not stay attached.  We kept it in place for a while, even though it kept breaking at the slightest touch.

Thankfully, there have been no injuries.  I intend to contact the company now, though, since similar models of the bed have been recalled due to the same type of problem.

Since I started using my pillow I have experienced frequent sinus infections, ear infections, sore throats, depression, fatique, dizziness, headaches, joint soreness, etc.  Until now, I got sick maybe once a year with a cold or cough.  I now am averaging 6-8 times a year with sinus/ear infection/flu/cold/coughs.  The worst has been these severe ear infection, which I had never had one, not even as a child...and this jaw pain I'm sure is somehow connected. The company recommended it and stated that it was specifically designed to relieve pressure for side sleeping.  This pillow may have helped with some neck pains, but if slept on incorrectly or it slides during the night, the neck and shoulder pain is way worse than if I would have just slept with a regular pillow.  Not sure if it is the chemicals or materials that I am obviously allergic to or our causing a baterial or viral infection in my immune system.  There should be a warning label on this pillow explaining all of the medical and health problems associated with using this product.
justification: The user reports multiple health issues including infections and pain, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issues are recurring but not universal for all users.
